title: Exploiting tea protein-chitosan nanoparticles stabilized Pickering emulsion to enhance the bioaccessibility of curcumin
abstract: Natural biopolymer-based nanoparticles are promising candidates for emulsion stabilization and delivery of hydrophobic compounds. In this study, tea protein (TP) and chitosan (CS) were employed to fabricate complex nanoparticles (NPs) using a pH-dependent method. At a mass ratio of 2:1 (TP:CS), the NPs exhibited favorable properties (206.62 nm, -30.86 mV, 85.41° contact angle) owing to electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, and hydrophobic interactions (binding energy of the complex was -5.40 kcal/mol). At a particle concentration of 2 % and an oil-phase volume fraction of 60 %, the Pickering emulsion stabilized by TP-CS 2:1 NPs remained physically stable. Compared with TP alone, TP-CS 2:1 NPs significantly enhanced the encapsulation efficiency and antioxidant capacity (DPPH/ABTS) of curcumin (Cur). In vitro digestion confirmed that the emulsions reduced gastric degradation of Cur, increasing its bioaccessibility by 17.4 %. Accordingly, this study provides a strategy for designing natural protein-polysaccharide NPs for functional emulsions and sustained delivery systems.

title: Effects of seven thermal processes on the structural properties, digestibility, in vitro hypolipidemic activity, and prebiotic potential of adlay polysaccharides
abstract: This study systematically evaluated seven thermal processing methods for their impact on the structure, digestibility, in vitro hypolipidemic activity, and prebiotic potential of adlay seed polysaccharides (ASPs). Structural analyses showed that explosion puffing, steam explosion, and extrusion significantly enhanced yield and altered weight-average molecular weight (Mw), monosaccharide composition, and thermal behavior. Steam explosion and extrusion produced high-Mw, uronic-acid-rich matrices with superior in vitro hypolipidemic effects, including bile acid sequestration and pancreatic lipase inhibition. Simulated digestion led to molecular degradation and sugar release, most prominently in explosion-puffed ASPs. All samples were fermentable by gut microbiota, increasing short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. Explosion-puffed ASPs enriched Megasphaera, Segatella, Bifidobacterium, and Faecalibacterium, while reducing Escherichia-Shigella, and generated the highest SCFA yields. These findings demonstrate that food-grade thermal treatments can tailor ASP structure to produce distinct bioactivity profiles: steam explosion and extrusion favor lipid-lowering functions, while explosion puffing enhances prebiotic potential. This work establishes a scalable strategy for designing multifunctional cereal-based nutraceuticals.

title: Flavor evolution of Pu-erh tea (ripe tea): Quantitative characterization of volatile dynamics during natural aging
abstract: This study investigated the flavor evolution of RPT during natural aging using GC-MS and metabolomics approaches. We identified 114 volatile compounds and performed quantitative analysis. Metabolic pathway analysis implicated three pathways caffeine metabolism, toluene degradation, naphthalene degradation as potential sources of methyl group precursors for the formation of methylated aroma compounds, particularly methoxybenzenes. These findings indicate that methylphenols serve as essential intermediates in the biochemical transformations that produce methylated compounds during aging. Additionally, three compounds are suggested as precursors for methylphenols compounds: 2,4,6-tritert-butylphenol, 2,5-ditert-butylphenol, and butylated hydroxytoluene. This study advances our understanding of aroma evolution in RPT during natural aging, highlighting the critical role of methylphenols as key intermediates in these chemical transformations. The identification of these phenolic compounds provides a foundation for targeted strategies to enhance flavor development in Pu-erh tea.

title: Detection of biosynthetic citric acid and sugar addition in Italian tomato passata using liquid chromatography–combustion–isotope ratio mass spectrometry
abstract: The citric acid is naturally present in tomatoes and can be added to tomato passatas (E330) with no restriction about its amount and origin. The additive E330 is mainly biosynthetically produced starting from the Aspergillus Niger fed on cheap materials. For the first time, an isotopic method for the detection of biosynthetic citric acid addition to Italian tomato passata was provided. Italian tomato passata samples without added citric acid (287 samples) were analysed through LC-co-IRMS to establish reference values for tomatoes citric acid carbon isotopic ratio ( δ 13 C CA ). The isotopic values of glucose ( δ 13 C G ) and fructose ( δ 13 C F ) have been considered to increase the method effectiveness and to be compared to the reference values provided by the AIJN (European Fruit Juice Association). The method showed good repeatability, with intra-day and inter-day standard deviations below 1.1 ‰ for citric acid, glucose, and fructose. The ratios between the isotopic values R CA/G ( δ 13 C CA / δ 13 C G ) and R CA/F ( δ 13 C CA / δ 13 C F ) were more effective in the detection of biosynthetic citric acid addition than the δ 13 C CA alone. • Citric acid (E330) added to tomato passata can be both biosynthetic and natural. • Carbon stable isotopes can discriminate between natural and biosynthetic citric acid. • LC-co-IRMS can simultaneously measure the δ 13 C of citric acid, glucose and fructose.

title: Optimization of extraction methods, component identification of bound polyphenols from sea-buckthorn pomace, and its ameliorative effects on oxidative stress in sleep-deprived mice
abstract: Sea-buckthorn pomace, rich in various bioactive polyphenols, is often discarded as a by-product of Sea-buckthorn juice processing. Studies indicate that plant-bound polyphenols exhibit greater bioactivity than free polyphenols. The study innovatively used six hydrolysis methods to release sea-buckthorn pomace bound polyphenols (SBP), and clarified their composition and biological activities. The results found that the extraction yield and antioxidant capacity of the microwave-assisted base hydrolysis (MBH) method were higher than others. And the highest extraction yield of 2.09 % occurred with 4 min, 350 W, and solid-liquid ratio of 1:30 (g: mL). Compositional analysis revealed that SBP obtained by the MBH method primarily consisted of ellagic acid, kaempferol, rutin, salvianolic acid A, and isorhamnetin. Furthermore, SBP ameliorated oxidative stress, inflammation, and depressive-like behaviors in sleep-deprived mice through modulation of the Nrf2/Keap1 pathway. These results offered new support for the extraction and composition of SBP and its feasibility for use in retarding oxidative stress.

title: Quantitative analysis of corn adulteration in sweet potato starch using a CNN-LSTM hybrid model
abstract: Starch, as a primary storage carbohydrate, serves as a key energy source in the human diet. It is often difficult to distinguish between different starch types visually due to their similar appearance. Traditional starch detection methods suffer from several limitations like low accuracy, complex pretreatment processes, and sample damage. Therefore, to achieve a rapid and accurate quantification of starch adulteration, terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) was utilized. First, time-domain spectral data were obtained from a series of adulterated samples. Then, four pretreatment methods were applied to process the original spectra. Both the full spectra and SPA-selected spectral features were used as inputs to develop traditional regression models, and a deep learning model based on a hybrid convolutional neural network and long short-term memory network (CNN-LSTM) model. The results demonstrate that the CNN-LSTM model achieved the best performance (Rp = 0.9765, RMSEP = 4.85 %), indicating its potential for rapid and non-destructive monitoring of starch quality.

title: Dynamic changes in reducing sugars, amino acids, volatiles of Lanxangia tsao-ko and prediction of their potential precursors during constant and variable temperature drying
abstract: We examined the dynamic evolution of reducing sugars, amino acids, and volatiles in Lanxangia tsao-ko (LT) during constant temperature drying at 50 °C (CT) and variable temperature drying (VT). The study shows that VT shortened drying time, reduced total sugar consumption and energy consumption, and promoted release of volatiles (such as terpenes, esters, and aldehydes) during the pre-drying period. Terpenoids and esters constitute the predominant volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in VT. During the drying process, VT significantly elevated the concentrations of 114 VOCs, reaching 4.56 times that of CT. The 17 volatile substances mainly composed of 1-nonen-3-one are the main sources of the aroma of LT. Fourier transform near infrared spectroscopy showed that LT drying process concentration was the main cause of metabolite fluctuations, not type. Further combination with a partial least squares regression model achieved efficient prediction of 9 key substrates with residual predictive deviation ranging from 1.9 to 3.0.

title: Correlation analysis of monosaccharide composition and in vitro antioxidant and hypoglycemic activities of Tremella fuciformis spore polysaccharides
abstract: Tremella fuciformis polysaccharides have diverse bioactivities and beneficial physicochemical properties, enabling broad use in pharmaceuticals and food. This study analyzed intracellular and extracellular polysaccharides (IPs and EPs) from three T. fuciformis spores, assessing their monosaccharide composition and in vitro antioxidant and hypoglycemic effects. Results showed that TWW01-AX and TWW02-TMS had significantly higher biomass and polysaccharide yields than TYH-SD1. IPs were predominantly composed of Glc, exceeding 60 mol%, whereas EPs were primarily composed of Man, accounting for over 64 mol%. Monosaccharide percentages served as key discriminators between IPs and EPs. EPs exhibited stronger DPPH, hydroxyl radical scavenging, CUPRAC, as well as α-glucosidase and α-amylase inhibition, while IPs showed superior ABTS radical scavenging activities and FRAP. Ridge regression showed key monosaccharide percentage variations notably influence bioactivities. This study provided a theoretical basis for the functional evaluation of high-quality T. fuciformis polysaccharides and the efficient screening of superior strains.

title: Current developments in microextraction procedures for the extraction of antibiotics using deep eutectic solvents and ionic liquids: A review study
abstract: The presence of antibiotic residues in various matrices, such as food, environmental, and biological samples has been a growing concern in recent years. The extraction and analysis of antibiotics in various samples are essential due to their significant implications for human health. Liquid-liquid microextraction techniques, particularly those using ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents, have attracted special attention because of their high efficiency and selectivity. They show high selectivity, effective sample cleanup and preparation, high enrichment factors, excellent extraction recovery, and low consumption of solvent and samples. In this review, we also discuss the unique physicochemical properties of these solvents that make them ideal green solvents for the separation and preconcentration of antibiotics. We comprehensively review current advancements in ionic liquid and deep eutectic solvent-based microextraction methods, emphasizing and comparing their applications and results based on published studies.

title: Distinct response of components of food wastes to reaction time in hydrothermal carbonization
abstract: Herein, HTC of rice and potato, components of food waste (glucose, xylose, cellulose and lignin) and also willow wood for comparison were conducted. The results showed that, in terms of the yields of hydrochar, 4 h was enough to induce polymerization of the majority of intermediates from glucose and xylose; 2 h was enough for that of cellulose and cooked rice and potato as their sugar oligomer intermediates were more reactive towards polymerization. Extending the residence time from 2 h to 10 h made no marked difference in the oxygen content in the hydrochars from glucose, xylose, cellulose, but did result in slow aromatization of hydrochars from willow, potatoes and rice via deoxygenation. The in-situ IR characterization showed that conversion of alcoholic OH to phenolic OH and aromatization process with prolonged reaction time of 10 h. This, however, diminished polar functionalities that were essential for the adsorption of methyl blue.

title: Effects of ultrasound-assisted modification during freeze-thaw cycle on gel properties and conformation of myosin in EGCG-modified systems: Roles of ionic strength and ultrasound power
abstract: This study investigated effects of ultrasound power and ionic strength on conformation and gel properties of chicken myosin under freeze-thaw (FT) cycle in EGCG-mediated system. Ultrasound significantly increased solubility, α-helix content, and surface hydrophobicity, while reduced turbidity, particle size, sulfhydryl content, and intrinsic fluorescence (P < 0.05), indicating that mechanical forces induced by ultrasound promoted structural unfolding, which increased disulfide bonding and hydrophobic interactions, thereby enhancing myosin-myosin and myosin-EGCG interactions. Ultrasound significantly increased β-sheet, viscosity, gel strength, and ratio of immobile water, while reduced α-helix content and thawing loss of frozen myosin gel (P < 0.05). SEM, LF-NMR, and MRI analyses indicated that ultrasound facilitated formation of a compact network structure of myosin gel after FT cycle, significantly increasing water-holding capacity (WHC) of frozen myosin gel. WHC of myosin gel at 0.6 M NaCI was better than that at 0.3 M NaCI, resulting in higher gel strength and thawing loss.

title: Effects of ultrasound on zein-procyanidin composite nanoparticles: Interaction force, structure, emulsifying properties and interfacial behaviors
abstract: Given the growing demand for natural emulsifiers in the food and pharmaceutical industries, this study investigates how ultrasonic treatment affected the structural properties, emulsification performance and interfacial behavior of zein-procyanidin (PC) composite nanoparticles (Z/PC-NPs). The ultrasound-induced cavitation effect significantly enhanced the hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interaction between zein and PC. Spectroscopic analyses showed that ultrasound increased the β-sheet content to 21.90% and decreased the β-turn content to 49.0%, which enhanced the bonding stability between PC and zein. Compared with Z/PC-NPs, the emulsification activity and emulsification stability of the ultrasonically treated Z/PC-NPs-U were increased by 22.84% and 44.13%, respectively. After ultrasonic treatment, the elastic modulus rose 41% to 52.94 mN/m, while interfacial mass reached 350.09 ng/cm 2 , confirming improved interfacial layer thickness and elasticity. Ultrasound provides a new technical approach and theoretical support for the development of efficient functional emulsifiers by modulating the structure and interfacial behavior of nanoparticles.

title: Predicting heat-induced hazardous compounds in roasted almonds via browning index and moisture using machine learning
abstract: While roasting is essential for developing the characteristic flavor of almonds, it can also result in the formation of thermal contaminants that cause potential threats to human health. This study investigated the effects of roasting conditions (110-150 °C, 10-30 min) on precursor degradation, antioxidant activity, and formation of acrylamide (AA) and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) in almonds. Higher roasting intensity increased browning index (BI) and total phenolic content, while reducing sugars and asparagine declined. AA and 5-HMF contents peaked at 150 °C/30 min. A support vector regression (SVR) model using L*, a*, b*, BI, and moisture content accurately predicted the levels of AA and 5-HMF (R 2 > 0.94, RMSE < 10%). Moderate roasting conditions (≤ 130 °C for ≤15 min) are recommended to achieve an optimal balance between product safety and quality. These results suggested that machine learning is an effective method for food risk assessment.

title: Synergistic strategies of sulforaphane biosynthesis and functional properties in broccoli sprouts powder obtained from sucrose stress modulation coupled with vacuum freeze-drying
abstract: This study investigated methionine-sucrose stress treatments on glucoraphanin biosynthesis in broccoli sprouts and the impact of vacuum freeze-drying (VFD) on sprout powder quality. Results showed that sucrose treatment elevated glucoraphanin content by 316.30 % in 4-day sprouts compared to the control (9.72 mg/g), accompanied by increases of 42.65 % in total isothiocyanates (ITCs) and 70.00 % in anthocyanins. The treatment enhanced myrosinase activity and upregulated osmotic regulators. PCA confirmed that sucrose stress optimized the nutritional quality of broccoli sprouts and exhibited potential in sulforaphane enrichment. The VFD broccoli sprout powder exhibited high retention of sulforaphane (6.00 mg/g dw) and total ITCs (7.00 mg/g dw), with optimal water-holding capacity, oil-holding capacity, and swelling capacity. The sulforaphane extract exhibited significant antimicrobial activity against E. coli (16.00 mm inhibition zone) and Staphylococcus aureus (10.02 mm). The synergistic application of sucrose stress and VFD presents a promising approach for developing functional foods.

title: Synergy between chloride salts (Na+, K+, Ca2+) and ozonation in the simultaneous modification of pigmented rice starch
abstract: This study evaluated the dual chemical modification of red rice starch through a synergistic combination of ozonation and chloride salts (NaCl, KCl, and CaCl₂). A 2-h ozonation time (0.045 g/L and 50 g/h) and a fixed salt concentration of 200 mM were employed. The carbonyl and carboxyl contents increased with the addition of salt, as did the breakdown of starch chains, amylose, and larger branches of amylopectin, especially when using KCl. Crystallinity was reduced by 10.68 % of the starch granule, resulting in greater surface erosion and a reduction in the average diameter to 33.71 μm with KCl. The larger atomic radius of K + led to stronger electrostatic interactions, reducing the enthalpy to 7.33 J/g and producing textural properties similar (p > 0.05) to those obtained with CaCl 2 .

title: The impact of storage conditions on quality and shelf life of fresh-cut jackfruit: a metabolomics perspective
abstract: Jackfruit, valued for its unique flavor and rich nutrients, suffers from quality postharvest deterioration in fresh-cut products. This study links intact fruit storage duration to fresh-cut jackfruit shelf life and quality, defining four distinct states ('Lignification', 'Unripe', 'Perfectly-ripe', and 'Decay') via firmness and total soluble solids profiling. Through metabolomics analysis, we identified 1067 volatiles and 1571 non-volatiles, with relative odor activity value analysis pinpointing 2-phenylethyl 3-methylbutanoate as a key aroma marker varying across states. Fruits stored 3-6 days were optimal for fresh-cutting, exhibiting 'Perfectly-ripe' flavor through ester-phenylpropanoid metabolic synergy while retaining amino acids and phenolics. In contrast, 'Unripe' and 'Lignification' showed impaired flavor precursor conversion, while 'Decay' accumulated abnormal phospholipids, reducing nutritional and flavor quality. This study provides a metabolomic basis for optimizing fresh-cut jackfruit processing timing and preservation, supporting commercial circulation, quality control, and the standardized large-scale development of the jackfruit industry.

title: Induced fluorescence derivatization (IFD) determination of monosodium glutamate (MSG) in broths
abstract: In this work, we conducted a study on the analysis of monosodium glutamate (MSG) in broths by the induced fluorescence derivatization (IFD) method. The method was based on the derivatization of naturally non-fluorescent MSG to form a fluorescent structure when reacting with orthophthalaldehyde (OPA). The chemical reaction parameters were optimized in an aqueous medium. The calibration curve was subsequently established under optimal conditions, and its linearity was assessed using variance analysis, which indicated a significant regression. The low LOD (0.006 ng mL -1 ) and LOQ (0.018 ng mL -1 ) values, compared with reference values, reveal the high sensitivity of the IFD method. The quantity of MSG contained in the kg of broth was determined, with values ranging from 2.5 to 20 g. The daily dose obtained ranged from 17 to 137 mg person -1 day -1 . The mean recovery close to 100 % shows the accuracy of the method.

title: Effects of fatty acid positional rearrangement on palm-based oils properties during enzymatic glycerolysis modification
abstract: This study utilized palm oil (POL) as the raw material to investigate the impact of fatty acid positional rearrangement on the characteristics of glycerolysis products. The POL was enzymatic interesterification (EIE) modified to obtain a modified sample (IEPOL) with a rearranged fatty acid distribution. Both POL and IEPOL were subjected to glycerolysis to produce diacylglycerol (DAG) and triacylglycerol (TAG). The results showed that the sn-2 fatty acid distribution differences significantly affected both fatty acid migration and DAG composition during glycerolysis. EIE was shown to alter the fatty acid distribution at the sn-2 position, thereby stabilizing saturated fatty acids at this site. This stabilization is hypothesized to have reduced their migration during reaction. Furthermore, the DAG fraction derived from IEPOL exhibited superior crystallization behavior and thermal stability compared to POL. This work provides a theoretical foundation and a practical approach for designing functional lipids by modulating the fatty acid positions.

title: Quantification of oil/water emulsion stability kinetics using image analysis: ImageScan method
abstract: The objective of this study was to develop and validate a kinetic and cost-effective image-based method (ImageScan), for the quantitative assessment of oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion stability. O/W emulsions were prepared using commercial emulsifiers, and images of the emulsions were captured using a desktop scanner over time. The relative gravitational volume (rGV) was measured along the tube containing the O/W emulsions to calculate the Image Stability Index (ISI). The half-life time (HLT i ) was determined from the ISI over time using ImageScan EM , a program developed in Google Colab. The ImageScan method was validated by measuring the stability of the O/W emulsions using kinetic and turbidimetric methods to evaluate the half-life time (HLT t ). The HLT t and HLT i values demonstrated a strong correlation (r = 0.9019, p < 0.05) and exhibited a 95 % agreement limit according to the Bland-Altman analysis. The ImageScan method facilitates the quantification and identification of instability layers in emulsion stability.

title: Copper ions modulated growth of TiO2/Bi2S3 heterojunction in-situ: An enhanced photoelectrochemical immunosensor coupled with headspace strategy for chloramphenicol determination
abstract: In this study, CuO functions as a signaling modulator that precisely regulates the formation and concentration of H 2 S through the release of Cu 2+ under acidic conditions. The mechanism involves the reaction between Cu 2+ and S 2- to form CuS, which consumes part of the S 2- introduced via Na 2 S. This process effectively modulates the in situ deposition of dark brown Bi 2 S 3 on the surface of TiO 2 /Bi 3+ electrodes. Owing to the well-matched band structures of Bi 2 S 3 and TiO 2 , the resulting heterojunction exhibits excellent photoelectric performance. The photocurrent intensity of the TiO 2 /Bi 2 S 3 heterojunction shows a concentration-dependent relationship with the level of Cu 2+ . Based on this principle, we developed a novel photoelectrochemical (PEC) immunosensor integrated with a headspace strategy for the detection of chloramphenicol (CAP), using CuO as an immunomarker. The detection range extended from 1.0 to 5000 pg/mL, and the detection limit was as low as 0.57 pg/mL. This innovative sensor leverages the in situ generation of colored Bi 2 S 3 -sensitized TiO 2 , enabling both qualitative photocurrent-based detection and semi-quantitative visual analysis by the naked eye.

title: Effect of pH shift on the formation and structural properties of Inca peanut albumin–Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide composite gels
abstract: Herein, we investigated the effects of different pH conditions (pH 2-10) on the formation, structure, and properties of heat-induced composite gels composed of Inca peanut albumin (IPA) and Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide (DOP). Results indicated that under acidic conditions (pH 2 and 4), the gelation process of IPA-DOP gels were slow (2530 s) and the resulting composite gels exhibited a rough, porous structure dominated by hydrophobic interactions. By contrast, at pH 6 and 8, the composite gels formed a denser network structure with higher β-sheet content (26.8 % and 26.0 %) and the dominant intermolecular forces were hydrogen bonds. At pH 6, the optimal hardness and water-holding capacity were observed to be 84.608 g force (gf) and 85.92 %, respectively. These findings indicate that the combination of DOP along with pH modulation can effectively influence the structural and functional characteristics of IPA gel, offering a promising strategy to enhance its performance.

title: Distinguishing plant and milk proteins and their interactions in hybrid cheese using confocal Raman microscopy with machine learning
abstract: The increasing demand for plant-based alternatives to milk protein has led to the development of hybrid processed cheese analogues (HPCAs) combining plant proteins and casein. However, their complex microstructure and molecular interactions remain poorly understood. This study integrated confocal Raman spectroscopy with advanced machine learning for high-resolution spatial mapping and molecular characterization of HPCAs containing mung bean protein isolate (MPI) or hemp protein isolate (HPI) with casein. This integration helped distinguish between protein sources and elucidate structural changes. The addition of casein changed the HPI structure, promoting structural disorder, disulfide bond rearrangement, and a sharp decrease in the tyrosine doublet ratio from 4.5 in HPI100 to 1.2 in HPI50. Conversely, casein interaction with MPI led to microstructural segregation and changes of β-sheet content (from 53 % in MPI100 to 20 % in MPI30). This integrated method represents a powerful tool for analysing protein structure and interactions in complex food systems. • Raman imaging reveals the physical and chemical distribution of cheese components. • Machine Learning allowed protein type recognition in hybrid cheese. • Plant protein secondary structure is altered by cheese-making processing. • Hemp–casein mixtures showed high structural disorder and disulfide rearrangement. • Mung bean–casein mixtures led to pronounced phase separation.

title: Fabrication and characterization of high internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs) of ω-3 algal oil stabilized with seaweed-derived particles
abstract: This study investigated HIPPEs of algal oil stabilized with novel protein-rich particles from red seaweed, featuring a favorable contact angle (81.5°), 43.2% β-sheet and 30.4% β-turn content, and irregular amorphous morphology with rough surfaces. HIPPEs were prepared using 0.5-2.0% particle concentrations. All formulations had highly negative zeta potentials (~ -70 to -74 mV). Droplet size decreased significantly with increasing concentration (p<0.05), plateauing between 1.5% and 2.0% with D(3,2) values of 2.68±0.04 and 2.72±0.24 on day 1. Emulsions E-1.5 and E-2.0 exhibited improved physical stability (TSI: 3.63 and 2.12) and dominant elastic behavior (G′>G′′). Higher concentrations enhanced zero-/infinite-shear viscosity, microstructural resistance, and interfacial coverage. Oxidative stability improved, with E-2.0 maintaining the lowest peroxide value (21.06 meq/kg oil). Higher particle loads reduced α-tocopherol degradation and oxidation volatiles butanal, 2-ethylfuran, 1-penten-3-ol, and (E,E)-2,4-heptadienal. These findings support seaweed-derived particles as natural Pickering stabilizers in ω-3-rich functional food emulsions.

title: Sn-integrated NiFe-layered double hydroxide with cation and oxygen vacancy engineering for simultaneous electrochemical detection of carbamate pesticides in foods and environmental samples
abstract: Carbamate pesticides, including carbofuran (CF) and methiocarb (MTC), are highly toxic, inhibiting acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase, which causes neurotoxicity in animals and endocrine and reproductive disorders in humans. CF bioaccumulates, severely affecting the nervous system and aquatic life. Therefore, rapid and cost-effective detection methods are crucial for monitoring and controlling these toxic compounds in food and environmental systems. Therefore, in this work, cation and anion vacancies in NiFe layered double hydroxide (LDH) were engineered to enhance electrocatalytic oxidation performance. By integrating metal and oxygen vacancies, we modified NiFeSn-LDH for highly sensitive simultaneous detection of CF and MTC. X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed the presence of cation and oxygen vacancies from Sn Integration. The modified NiFeSn-LDH exhibited ultra-low detection limits of 9.31 nM (CF) and 10.71 nM (MTC) individually, and 7.37 nM (CF) and 8.54 nM (MTC) for simultaneous detection, with recoveries above 96 % in real samples.

title: An intelligent bilayer film incorporating anthocyanin sensitized TiO2 and salicylic acid with ethylene scavenging and antibacterial properties for perishable food preservation
abstract: The bilayer films incorporating sensitized titanium dioxide (BA@TiO 2 NPs) and salicylic acid (SA) were developed based on cassava starch/xanthan gum and sodium alginate. The sensitization of TiO 2 NPs improved photocatalytic activity to inhibit E. coli (from 14.94 % to 86.82 %) under visible light. The films incorporating BA@TiO 2 NPs and SA effectively improved mechanical properties (increased by 25.6 %), swelling behavior, light shielding and oxygen barrier properties. Additionally, the films displayed antioxidant activities (>75 %), antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (≥ 99 %) and pH-response sensitivity. The hemolysis rate (0.53 %) and migration rate (0.57 μg/kg), cell viability (>95 %), bean sprout germination rate (100 %) and soil degradation (3 months) demonstrated film biosafety and environmental compatibility. The intelligent films decreased the ethylene production by 35 % and delayed ripening of cherry tomatoes, and effectively monitored color changes of shrimp spoilage. These results demonstrated that intelligent films showed the application potential for preservation and monitoring perishable food.

title: Development of a novel activity-based ratiometric electrochemical probe for real-time detection of Listeria monocytogenes in human blood and milk samples
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (LM) is a prevalent food-borne pathogen that causes listeriosis, life-threatening disease. Current methods for detecting LM in turbid samples require multistep and complex-liquid extraction. Thus, an alternative tool is needed. A typical enzyme-biomarker for LM, PI-PLC, is secreted by LM. This study, we designed and prepared a PI-PLC (Phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C) activity-targeted-electrochemical probe, termed PL-AFc, for detecting LM in turbid samples. PI-PLC catalyzes the hydrolysis of the phosphoether linkage between phosphatidylinositol and the phenol moiety in PL-AFc, inducing a reaction cascade that releases the unmasked signaling molecule, aminoferrocene. PL-AFc exhibits a wide linear detection range against PI-PLC (0.00001-0.1 unit/ml) and LM (3 × 10 6 -1 × 10 8 cfu/ml), with detection limit of 2.703 ng/ml and 1.44 × 10 5 cfu/ml. Practical application, PL-AFc demonstrated the ability to sense LM in human blood and milk samples with a simple dilution procedure, suggesting the platform has significant potential for detecting LM.

title: Sensitive SERS sensor for convenient and rapid determination of vanillin in foods
abstract: Sensitive food additive detection is vital for food safety. We developed a flexible nitrocellulose membrane-based SERS substrate modified with silver nanoparticles, enabling additive detection through analyte separation/enrichment and SERS signal enhancement. Integrated with the novel probe 4-(methylthio)benzohydrazide (4-MTBH), the sensor selectively captured vanillin (VA) and ethyl vanillin (EVA) via specific aldehyde-hydrazide interactions, enabling highly sensitive detection. The substrate demonstrated exceptional performance with an enhancement factor of 2.62 × 10 6 , RSD of 3.98 %, and stability maintaining SERS activity for over 30 days with nitrogen protection. It achieved a detection limit of 10 -7 mol L -1 for both vanillin flavors, meeting practical requirements, and reliably quantified total vanillin flavorants in diverse real food samples. This work establishes a portable, rapid-response SERS platform for ultrasensitive vanillin detection and introduces a new probe system to the SERS methodology, demonstrating significant potential for analyzing diverse analytes in complex matrices.

title: Fat content of milk modulates colloidal properties of sea buckthorn: In situ flavonol dissolution and migration
abstract: This study innovatively employs milk as a natural dissolution medium to achieve in situ solubilization and stabilization of hydrophobic flavonols in sea buckthorn, circumventing the conventional two-step process (organic solvent extraction and synthetic carriers delivery) and realizing a one-step functionalization with the juice matrix. Milk incorporation significantly enhanced juice's physical stability, inducing shear-thinning and gelation behaviors. Efficient in situ dissolution of total flavonoids and flavonols was achieved, with dissolution kinetics fitting first-order and Korsmeyer-Peppas models (Fickian diffusion coupled with slight matrix expansion and erosion). High DPPH radical scavenging activity (92.56 %) and T-AOC confirmed the effective bioactive release. Milk fat content regulated long-term flavonol dissolution with maximum migration in low-fat milk at 14 d (quercetin, 19.10 %) and 21 d (kaempferol, 10.61 %; isorhamnetin, 15.64 %). This work presents a streamlined strategy for functional factor delivery, utilizing natural food substrate to enable extraction-free, carrier-free, one-step in situ solubilization and stabilization of sea buckthorn flavonols.

title: Functional protein-based emulsions for dysphagia management in the elderly: stability mechanisms, rheological design, and translational prospects
abstract: As the global population ages, the demand for safe, nutritious, and palatable foods for elderly individuals with dysphagia has become increasingly critical. Protein-based emulsions have emerged as a prominent area of research due to their tunable mesoscopic structures and swallowing adaptability. This review systematically examines the design principles and applications of various protein-based emulsions in swallowing-friendly foods, assesses the advantages and limitations of different emulsion preparation techniques, and evaluates the methods used to characterize swallowing-friendly foods. On this basis, it further identifies key challenges that require urgent attention, including the difficulty in harmonizing emulsion stability, functionality, and palatability; the gap between standardization and personalization; the insufficiency of clinical validation, and the limitation of cultural adaptability. Future research should be guided by the coupling mechanism of "Interface-Rheology-Swallowing", highlighting multidisciplinary innovation, advancing the specialized medical food industry and providing personalized nutritional solutions for elderly individuals with dysphagia.

title: Interfacial perspective: Modulation of fat crystallization behavior and stability of yeast proteins ice cream by sucrose esters with tailored HLB values
abstract: This study investigated the effects of sucrose esters with varying hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB) values on the fat crystallization behavior and stability of yeast proteins (YPs)-based ice cream from an interfacial perspective. The results demonstrated that sucrose esters with low HLB values (HLB max and γ ∞ of the pre-whipped emulsion interface gradually decreased, whereas the RS increased. The fat crystallization behavior analysis of aged pre-whipped emulsions revealed that samples containing sucrose esters with higher HLB values exhibited lower T cr , P 1 , P 2 and n, along with a higher k, resulting in the formation of smaller and more uniformly distributed fat crystals. The overrun in the YPs-S1570 ice cream increased from 70.76 % to 96.63 %, while the hardness decreased from 1644.25 g to 731.25 g. Therefore, when YPs are combined with appropriate HLB values (HLB=15) of sucrose esters, high-quality ice cream can be produced. This provides a new reference for alternative protein-based frozen desserts.

title: Self-supported cobalt-nickel phosphide Nanoflower/carbon cloth electrode for highly selective and sensitive nitrite detection at low reduction potential in food and water via transition metal-phosphide synergy
abstract: Nitrite, a common food additive and environmental pollutant, demands rapid detection for food safety and ecological protection. Its oxidizing nature usually requires electrochemical sensors at high potentials. Highly catalytic phosphides can reduce overpotential issues, but single-metal phosphide electrodes often have electron localization, causing overlapping reduction potentials for NO₂ - and NO₃ - ions and reducing selectivity. In this study, we used one-step electrodeposition to make a cobalt‑nickel phosphide nanowire/carbon cloth composite electrode (CoNiP/CC). By controlling the potential window, we achieved low-potential detection (-0.15 V vs. Hg/HgO) with high selectivity. Electrochemical tests and DFT calculations show the electrode has a sensitivity up to 6110 μA mM -1 cm -2 and a detection limit as low as 0.087 μM (S/N = 3). It also resists interference well and excels in food and environmental water sample analysis. This study reveals the synergistic catalytic mechanisms of transition metal phosphide alloys, offering new insights for low-potential nitrite sensor development.

title: Unlocking extra virgin olive oil identification: predicting ethyl esters with explainable AI on IR spectra
abstract: Extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) is susceptible to adulteration and degradation, making the assessment of its authenticity and quality essential. Fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEE), formed through fermentative processes, are regulated by EU legislation as key markers of EVOO quality, with acceptable levels up to 35 mg/kg. In this study, a rapid, non-destructive, and cost-effective alternative based on infrared spectroscopy combined with traditional statistical methods (i.e., Partial Least Square - PLS), machine learning (ML) and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is proposed. A dataset of 170 olive oil samples with FAEE concentrations ranging from 1.81 mg/kg to 109.00 mg/kg were analyzed using Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy. Spectral data were preprocessed and used to train various regression models. The best performance was obtained with an XGBoost model (R2 = 0.90, RMSE = 9.41 mg/kg). XAI techniques enabled interpretation of the model and identification of spectral regions mostly associated with FAEE content.

title: Integrating machine learning with lateral flow immunoassay for ultrafast and sensitive tadalafil detection
abstract: Tadalafil, a phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor frequently detected in functional foods and dietary supplements, poses significant risks. To enable sensitive on-site detection, an anti-tadalafil monoclonal antibody (3C5) with an IC₅₀ of 0.32 ng mL -1 was prepared. Antibody-antigen binding kinetics revealed distinct variations in the early detection stage, prompting the integration of lateral flow immunoassay with machine learning (LFIA@ML) to further speed up testing. A Random Forest model trained on multi-dimensional signal features achieved fast detection and high accuracy, with a coefficient of determination of 0.995 and a mean absolute error of 0.038. For 140 samples, the LFIA@ML demonstrated a 94.3 % prediction accuracy and significantly reduced detection time to 3 min. The assay exhibited a strong correlation with LC-MS/MS, with recoveries ranging from 92.3 % to 112 % (coefficient variations ≤15.37 %). The LFIA@ML showcased the ability to reduce detection time by using the Random Forest algorithm and was validated in wine samples.

title: Polymer encapsulation of Cynara Scolymus L. extract using supercritical fluid expansion into an aqueous solution (ESSAS): Optimization of conditions, identification of compounds using LC-HRMS, and investigation of antioxidant properties
abstract: This study deals with preparation of polymeric nanoparticles (PNPs) containing Cynara Scolymus L. extract. The effective compounds were initially extracted using supercritical fluid extraction, with their antioxidant activity determined. Subsequently, PNPs were synthesized using the green ESSAS method, an innovative evolution of the RESS technique. The ESSAS process was engineered to maintain the secondary pressure above the CO 2 critical point during the pressure drop, inducing formation of smaller particles that were collected directly in an aqueous solution. Under the optimal BBD conditions (24.9 MPa, 67 °C, 24 min), the PNPs achieved a minimal particle size (84 ± 25 nm) and high encapsulation efficiency (87 ± 1.3 %). The encapsulated artichoke extract exhibited enhanced antioxidant activity and good stability over 28 days. LC-HRMS confirmed the presence of components (Cynarine, Cynara saponin F/E). The green ESSAS technique establishes a sustainable approach for developing advanced nanomedicines and targeted drug delivery systems for natural extracts.

title: Cross-modal saltiness perception in MRPs derived from hydrolyzed Coprinus comatus protein: linking sulfur-containing volatiles to saltiness-enhancing capacities
abstract: Thermally processed edible mushroom protein hydrolysates exhibit saltiness-enhancing properties. Previous studies have primarily attributed this effect to either an increased content of umami substances or basic taste interactions; however, the potential contribution of odor-induced saltiness enhancement (OISE) through olfactory participation remains underexplored. This study investigated the accumulation of flavor compounds throughout thermal processing of a Coprinus comatus peptide-xylose-cysteine model system. Potential odorants with OISE capacities were screened by correlating the concentrations of sulfur-containing volatiles with the perceived saltiness intensities of Maillard reaction products (MRPs) obtained under different processing conditions. The impact of reaction time on flavor development exhibited distinct phase-dependent characteristics. The consumption of free amino acids primarily happened during the initial stage (0-60 min), while extended processing (90-150 min) promoted the controlled generation of sulfur-containing volatiles with meaty flavors, such as 2-methylthiophene, 2-pentylthiophene, 5-methyl-2-thiophenecarboxaldehyde, and bis(2-methyl-3-furyl) disulfide. Correlation analyses further revealed that sulfur-containing species, particularly thiophenes (2,3-dimethylthiophene and 2-pentylthiophene) and thiols (2-methyl-3-furanthiol), showed strong associations with perceived saltiness intensity (r > 0.9), underlying their cross-modal taste modulation capacities through OISE. This chemosensory mapping enables targeted sodium reduction while decoding OISE mechanisms in thermo-processing systems.

title: Colloidal gold-based immunochromatographic assay for β-lactoglobulin variants A and B in dairy products and insights into antibody recognition mechanisms
abstract: Food fraud practices, such as milk adulteration, exacerbate allergy risks by introducing undeclared allergens, primarily β-lactoglobulin (β-Lg). Therefore, the effective detection of β-Lg in food is crucial for ensuring consumer safety. In this study, we screened hybridoma cell lines 11F10 and 4G1, which recognized β-Lg variants A (β-Lg A) and B (β-Lg B). Genes of these hybridoma cell lines were extracted, amplified, and cloned into expression vectors to produce recombinant antibodies (rAbs). Using rAbs 11F10 and 4G1, colloidal gold immunochromatographic strips were developed for detecting β-Lg A and B in dairy products. The strips exhibited a visual limit of detection of 200 μg/kg in cheese and amino acid formulas, and 200 ng/mL in raw milk. The results of molecular docking indicated that the critical amino acid residues for 11F10 were Asp57, Tyr32, and Arg49, whereas those for 4G1 included Tyr101, Tyr106, and Tyr49.

title: Influence of pea protein-κ-carrageenan composite microgel particle interfacial structure on lipid digestibility in O/W Pickering emulsions
abstract: The impact of interfacial structure on lipid digestion of emulsions remains controversial, presenting a key limitation in developing technologies for precise regulation of nutritional characteristics through rational food structure design. This study employed pea protein isolate (PPI) microgel particle (PPM) and PPI-κ-carrageenan (κ-CG) composite microgel particle (PPCM) as a model system. The mixing ratio of these macromolecules was adjusted, which changed the interaction of protein and polysaccharide molecules, as well as the interfacial structure of PPCM. Subsequent analysis of structural changes and emulsion digestion in an in vitro simulated digestion model elucidated the regulatory mechanism of interfacial structure on lipid digestion of Pickering emulsions (PPM-E and PPCM-E). The results demonstrated that free sulfhydryl and hydrophobic groups embedded in PPI became exposed during the heat-shearing process of microgel preparation, facilitating disulfide bond formation. The κ-CG gel associated with PPI gel through non-covalent bonds, effectively shielding the exposed hydrophobic groups of PPI. Based on the thickness of the interface, the amount of adsorbed protein, and the protein concentration at the interface, and the surface dilatational modulus, it was found that the deformability of microgel particles at the interface varies. This variation leads to differences in the interfacial structure: PPM formed thick but sparsely distributed interfacial layers due to its limited interfacial deformability; PPCM1 and PPCM2 formed thinner and denser interfacial layers with exposed κ-CG gels on the surface owing to because of their greater deformability compared to PPM; PPCM3, PPCM4, and PPCM5 exhibited the thinnest and densest interfacial layers among the microgel particles, with the exposed κ-CG interconnected to form a polysaccharide network surrounding the oil droplets. Compared with PPM-E, the κ-CG outside the interfacial layer of PPCM1-E and PPCM2-E promoted the expansion of the interfacial microgel in the simulated intestinal fluid and enhanced the hydrolysis by trypsin and lipase, resulting in higher free fatty acid (FFA) release than PPM. In contrast, the κ-CG network outside the interfacial layer of PPCM3-E, PPCM4-E, and PPCM5-E impeded the trypsin and lipase activity, thereby inhibiting the lipid digestion and resulting in lower FFA release than PPM.

title: Protein-stabilized gold nanoclusters for colorimetric/fluorescence dual-mode detection of organophosphorus pesticides
abstract: The residue of organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) poses a serious threat to the environment and human health. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop sensitive, accurate, and environmentally friendly detection methods for OPs. Herein, we constructed a colorimetric/fluorescent dual-mode detection platform based on natural protein human serum albumin (HSA)-stabilized gold nanoclusters (HSA-Au NCs), combining the intrinsic fluorescence properties and peroxidase-like activity for OPs detection. The dual-mode detection strategy enhanced the accuracy and reliability of detection by mutual verification of signals. Moreover, benefiting from the biocompatibility of protein materials, HSA-Au NCs were environmentally friendly, allowing OPs detection in real samples. By integrating acetylcholinesterase, choline oxidase, and HSA-Au NCs on a cellulose acetylation membrane, a smartphone-assisted sensor with high sensitivity, low limit of detection, and environmental friendliness was developed. The sensor demonstrated a low detection limit of 0.476 ng·mL -1 for parathion methyl, which was suitable for real fruit and vegetable detection.

title: Visible light-triggered oxidase-mimicking activity of covalent organic frameworks for colorimetric assessment of total antioxidant capacity in food
abstract: Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) is a key indicator of the quality and nutritional value of foods. Conventional methods for TAC detection, however, are often time-consuming and complex, hindering the applicability for rapid screening. Herein, we synthesized a visible light-responsive imine-linked COFs incorporating bipyridine moieties (TpBpy-COF). The synergistic interaction between pyridinic N and imine bonds can enhance the oxidase-mimicking activity of TpBpy-COF, enabling it to effectively catalyze the oxidation of TMB and resulting in a distinct color transition from colorless to blue. However, the involvement of antioxidants generate fading of the blue color as the antioxidants have the ability to scavenge reactive oxygen species. We develop thus an effective colorimetric sensing platform based on oxidase-mimicking activity of TpBpy-COF for accurate, rapid and sensitive evaluation of TAC. This work not only establishes a novel strategy for developing visible light-responsive COFs-based nanozymes but also provides a practical tool for reliable food quality assessment.

title: One-class modeling for the authentication of a geographically certified Brazilian coffee based on atomic-molecular data fusion
abstract: Coffee is among the most consumed beverages worldwide and holds great economic importance for Brazil. Cerrado Mineiro region has gained prominence for its green coffee beans, certified with the Protected Designation of Origin (PDO), ensuring their quality and uniqueness. This study developed classification models to characterize these beans using total reflection X-ray fluorescence (TXRF), mid-infrared spectroscopy (MIRS), and paper-spray mass spectrometry (PS-MS). SIMCA (soft independent modeling of class analogy) one-class modeling was applied to individual techniques and fused data. The data fusion model combining MIR, PS-MS, and TXRF achieved 97 % accuracy. The interpretation of this model allowed the detection of the variables that contribute most to the authentication, related to chlorogenic acids and alkaloids, alongside the elements Cu, Rb, and Cl. The soft foodomics strategy proposed in this study enabled the detailed chemical characterization of this food matrix and the classification of distinctive, high-quality coffees, thus assuring their geographical indication.

title: Development of high-purity pyrethrins certified reference material
abstract: Certified reference materials (CRMs) are essential for reliable pesticide residue analyses. For this study, we hypothesised that stable and high-purity pyrethrins CRM containing six target compounds could be developed through the chromatographic purification of pyrethrum and argon-purged packaging. The purities of total and individual pyrethrins were determined using mass balance and external calibration methods. The CRM properties were evaluated using an ISO-guided approach. The candidate CRM exhibited excellent homogeneity, stability, and metrological traceability. Certified values of purity and expanded uncertainty were as follows: total pyrethrins (98.6 ± 0.9 %), pyrethrin 2 (44.6 ± 0.9 %), pyrethrin 1 (27.5 ± 0.5 %), jasmolin 2 (9.1 ± 0.8 %), jasmolin 1 (7.0 ± 0.4 %), cinerin 2 (5.1 ± 0.4 %), and cinerin 1 (5.4 ± 0.3 %). These findings demonstrate the successful development of a stable and high-purity pyrethrins CRM that ensures the reliability and quality of pyrethrin residue analysis.

title: Ethanol-mediated synthesis of size-controlled γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic frameworks: Mechanistic insights into clove oil encapsulation, release and pork preservation
abstract: Clove essential oil (CEO) possesses potent antioxidant and antimicrobial properties but suffers from high volatility and instability, limiting its application in food systems. A green, ethanol-mediated ultrasonic method was developed to synthesize biocompatible γ-cyclodextrin metal-organic frameworks (γ-CD-MOFs) with tunable particle size. Compared to conventional hydrothermal synthesis (3-5 μm), the ultrasonic approach yielded smaller, more uniform γ-CD-MOFs crystals (1-2 μm), which enhanced CEO loading (121 mg/g, +26 %) and improved structural stability. CEO encapsulation stabilized the framework through hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces, and pore confinement, enabling sustained release at 4 °C and 25 °C. A clear size-dependent effect was observed, with smaller frameworks exhibiting superior loading efficiency and controlled release behavior. Molecular dynamics simulations elucidated the binding mechanism between CEO and the framework. CEO-loaded composites effectively inhibited microbial growth, extended pork shelf life, and exhibited good biocompatibility, offering a promising strategy for food preservation and controlled delivery of volatile bioactives.

title: Edible oils as bio-plasticisers for sustainable additive manufacturing: comparative electrochemical performance and sensing of ascorbic acid in juices
abstract: We report the production of five separate high-performance conductive filament, using different edible oils (coconut oil, olive oil, a vegetable oil blend, sunflower oil, and rapeseed oil) as bio-plasticising compounds alongside recycled PLA and carbon black (CB) for additive manufacturing electrochemistry. Each filament was assessed through TGA, SEM, XPS, Raman and electrochemical scan rate studies, showing comparable electrochemical behaviour towards conventional redox probes, however, the materials containing coconut oil and olive oil exhibited distinct morphologies (as observed via SEM) and superior electroanalytical performance for the detection of ascorbic acid. These electrodes achieved detection limits of 2.45 and 2.14 μmol L −1 , respectively. The electrode incorporating coconut oil was applied to the determination of ascorbic acid in real juice samples, yielding satisfactory recovery rates without the need for complex sample preparation. This study highlights the use edible, bio-based plasticisers in fabricating sustainable, high-performance filaments for sensing applications in food monitoring field. • We report the first range of conductive additive manufacturing filaments made from edible supermarket oils. • The use of bio-based oils alongside recycled PLA offers excellent sustainable practices throughout this work. • Key analysis on the effect the different oils have on both the physicochemical and electrochemical properties of the filament and printed parts are discussed. • Through linking the characteristics of each oil, the performance of the final filament can be tailored to the required application. • Using edible oils as a plasticiser it was possible to detect ascorbic acid within complex juice drinks.

title: Integrated surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and machine learning for identification and quantification of multi-target pesticide residues in fruit juices
abstract: This study developed a novel SERS platform integrated with machine learning for rapid, sensitive, and discriminative analysis of multi-target pesticide residues in fruit juices. The core-shell Au@AgCNCs nanostructure markedly amplifies Raman signals through localized surface plasmon resonance and calcium-ion-induced aggregation, enabling ultrahigh-sensitivity detection of five pesticides with a limit of detection as low as 2.7 pM. When the Machine Learning (ML) algorithm was applied to multi-target pesticide residue analysis in juice, 99.56 % accuracy in identifying pesticide types within a complex juice matrix was achieved. Notably, the model was trained on pure pesticide spectra and tested on spiked juice samples. Using Support Vector Regression (SVR), recoveries for individual and mixed pesticides ranged from 94.2 % to 106.1 %, enabling quantitative analysis of multi-component pesticide residues. The integration of SERS with ML not only enhanced detection precision but also simplified analytical workflows, demonstrating significant potential for food safety monitoring and sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Tissue-specific metabolite profiling of alkaloids and flavonoids in lotus cultivated in China enables rational resource utilization
abstract: Various tissues of lotus are widely utilized in functional foods owing to their abundant bioactive compounds. However, comprehensive comparisons of metabolite profiles among different tissues remain limited. Elucidating these differences is essential for rational resource utilization. Here, a widely-targeted metabolomic approach was applied to characterize plumules, leaves, and flowers of three lotus cultivars using UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS. A total of 81 metabolites (46 alkaloids, 35 flavonoids) were identified across all tissues, including 14 newly reported in lotus. Quantitative analysis, based on available standards, revealed abundant total content across tissues (21,806.16-26,631.81 μg g -1 DW), with distinct metabolites showing marked tissue-specific accumulation. Plumules were enriched in bisbenzylisoquinoline alkaloids, alkaloid glycosides, and flavonoid C-glycosides. In contrast, leaves and flowers contained higher levels of aporphine alkaloids and flavonoid O-glycosides, with quercetin glycosides accounting for ∼50 % of total flavonoids in leaves. This study overviews lotus tissue-specific metabolite distribution, laying a biochemical basis for targeted functional food development.

title: Enhanced quality retention and flavor integrity of Camellia oleifera C.Abel seeds oil: Ultrasound-assisted moderate refining strategy
abstract: This study examined the influence of ultrasound treatment on the non-volatile components and volatile compounds of Camellia oleifera C.Abel seeds oil (COO) during moderate refining to improve its quality. The results revealed that compared to the moderate refining group (MR), ultrasound-assisted moderate refining group (UAMR) reduced acid value and phospholipid while increasing α-tocopherol (23.27 %), squalene (10.38 %), and phytosterols (9.14 %). Among 66 volatile compounds of the COO, 15 key flavor compounds (VIP > 1, P 1) were identified. Cluster analysis revealed four refining phases, with PCA showing UAMR group better preserved key flavor compounds than MR group. Ultrasound treatment reduced aldehydes and acids content in the refined COO by suppressing hydroperoxide (POV) decomposition. These compositional changes mitigated greasiness and significantly improved sensory acceptability. In summary, ultrasound treatment may be a promising approach to improve the quality of the refined COO.

title: A novel carbazole-based polymer and its hydrogel-assisted probe for portable detection of nitrite in food and water environment
abstract: Nitrite is an extensively used food additive that is essential for preventing spoilage. However, its excessive residues in food pose significant threats to food safety and human health, necessitating portable and rapid tools for effective on-site monitoring. Herein, a novel carbazole-based polymer (Cz-P) with green fluorescence as the response signal under strongly acidic conditions was synthesized via Suzuki cross-coupling. Cz-P exhibits a green fluorescence quenching response to nitrite with excellent selectivity, high sensitivity (limit of detection: 0.07 μM), and rapid response (3 min). Moreover, Cz-P was successfully applied to quantify nitrite in real samples (including pickled vegetables, cured meats, and water samples). The detection mechanism of nitrite by Cz-P revealed that nitrite-induced fluorescence quenching occurs primarily via an electron transfer mechanism and hydrogen bonding interactions. Notably, a smartphone-assisted Cz-P/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel-based sensor was constructed for portable and visual nitrite monitoring in food, offering a point-of-care testing tool for food safety.

title: Enhanced functionalities of cassava starch-based films incorporating berberine nanoparticles for sustainable food packaging
abstract: Cassava starch is a biodegradable polymer with limited functional properties for packaging. To enhance its performance, cassava starch was complexed with berberine to form a nano-berberine-starch complex and cast into active films. Modeling indicated favorable binding (score 23.88) via hydrogen bonding and π-π interactions. The complex showed a bimodal size distribution (81 nm, 44.3 %; 318 nm, 32.7 %). Incorporation at suitable loadings improved film surface uniformity, mechanics, and bioactivity: antioxidant capacity reached 63.12 % and 56.4 % for both radicals, antibacterial efficacy increased, and biodegradation reached 57.2 % after 30 days versus native starch films. In a sausage model, the films suppressed microbial growth and lipid/protein spoilage, maintaining Thiobarbituric Acid Reactive Substances (TBARS) at 1.7 mg MDA/kg and Total Volatile Basic Nitrogen (TVB-N) at 8.50 mg/100 g over 15 days at 4 °C, outperforming commercial packaging. These findings highlight nano-berberine-starch as a promising strategy for multifunctional, biodegradable films that extend meat shelf life.

title: Medium effects of polysaccharides: bidirectional regulation of invertase activity by sodium alginate and fenugreek gum
abstract: Sodium alginate enhanced invertase activity, whereas fenugreek gum suppressed it. Further investigation into the physicochemical properties of the medium revealed a bidirectional regulatory mechanism. Sodium alginate, characterized by a positive logarithm of the crowding factor (ln Γ), a smaller excluded volume (Vₑₓ), and improved hydration, interacted with invertase via enthalpy-driven hydrogen bonding. This interaction stabilized the α-helix and β-sheet structures of the enzyme, thereby increasing its activity. In contrast, fenugreek gum exhibited a negative ln Γ, a larger excluded volume, and lower hydration capacity. It perturbed the enzyme through entropy-driven hydrophobic interactions, leading to a reduction in β-sheet content and a consequent decrease in enzymatic activity. The overall influence of the medium-comprising viscosity, macromolecular crowding, and soft interactions-enables quantitative assessment of how polysaccharides affect invertase activity. This study offers valuable insights for the rational selection of polysaccharides in dietary formulations aimed at modulating digestive enzyme activity.

title: Ultrasonic cavitation pretreatment of batter: A mechanism for optimizing dough properties
abstract: In this study, a novel ultrasonic pretreatment of batter (UPB) was investigated prior to dough mixing to enhance bread dough quality through the effects of ultrasound-induced cavitation in liquids. The findings demonstrated that UPB increased protein hydration and significantly influenced the transformation of disordered structural β-folding (characterized by weak hydrogen bonding) into more ordered structures (inter- and intramolecular β-folding). Additionally, UPB enhanced disulfide bonding within the dough. Mechanistic investigations revealed that the cavitation effect of UPB intensified over time, leading to increased iodine release and protein aggregation. UPB facilitated the formation of additional peptide chains composed of amino acid residues containing oxygen and nitrogen, enabling the sulfhydryl groups of cysteine side chains to react with more free radicals and form additional disulfide bonds. These findings suggest that UPB holds significant promise as a green physical modification technology for improving wheat flour products, warranting further exploration for industrial-scale application.

title: Preparation of methyl salicylate nanoemulsion and its application in sprouting inhibition on potato tubers
abstract: Sprouting of potato tubers is accompanied by the accumulation of toxic solanine. In this study, a methyl salicylate (MeSA) nanoemulsion was prepared using ultrasonic emulsification, and its effect on potato tuber sprouting was investigated. Results showed that the optimum preparation conditions of MeSA nanoemulsion were as follows: surfactant concentration, 5.02 %; MeSA concentration, 9.79 %; ultrasonic power, 428.03 W; and ultrasonic time, 3.79 min. The results of Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and rheological properties of the emulsion showed that MeSA was successfully embedded in the nanoemulsion with a good stability. After treatment with MeSA nanoemulsion at 25 °C, the initial sprouting time of potato (Favorita) was effectively delayed for 9 d, with sprouting rate of 20.95 %, whereas other treatments had sprouting rate of 100 %. In addition, the MeSA nanoemulsion maintained the quality of potato tubers. This indicated that the preparation of the nanoemulsion enhanced the sprouting inhibition effect of MeSA.

title: Portable and in situ rapid detection of benzo[a]pyrene: a review
abstract: Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), a typical polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) pollutant, is widely present in water, atmosphere, soil, as well as smoked, baked, and fried foods. It exhibits carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic properties. This paper systematically reviews the research progress of portable and in situ detection technologies for BaP, focusing on its sources and hazards, the recognition elements and detection principles of in situ and portable detection technologies, and the pretreatment methods and applicable technical strategies for different matrices. Addressing limitations such as insufficient recognition element performance and the lack of real-time monitoring methods for biological samples, this paper proposes development directions, including the development of new high-affinity recognition elements and the integration of multiple technologies. The paper provides a theoretical reference for developing portable and user-friendly BaP detection technologies. This will improve prevention and control systems for environmental pollutants and ensure food safety and public health.

title: Quantitative proteomics analysis to identify potential biomarkers associated with promoted quality profiles of frankfurters by ultrasound treatment combined with κ-carrageenan
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effects of various ultrasound (US) treatments coupled with κ-carrageenan (KC) on the quality profiles of frankfurters. Label-free quantitative proteomics was employed to establish the associations between quality indicators and proteomic profiles. Compared with the control and exclusive KC inclusion, the US treatment (600, 800 and 1000 W) considerably diminished cooking loss and strengthened the textural features of the frankfurters, resulting in the forming of a more compact protein network. Similarly, US treatment facilitated α-helix-to-β-sheet conversion in meat protein. Furthermore, principal component analysis was used to develop a quality evaluation model, which indicated that the KC + US800 group exhibited the highest comprehensive scores. Moreover, 13 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) considerably correlated with the quality profiles of frankfurters, and myosin light chain 3, tropomyosin alpha-1 chain, β-enolase, ATP synthase subunit alpha, fructose-bisphosphate aldolase, creatine kinase were identified as potential biomarkers for determining the final quality of frankfurters.

title: Food surface characterization by scanning electron microscopy and fractal analysis: A review
abstract: Surface characterization of food products is critical for understanding their physical, chemical, and biological properties, which have a direct impact on quality, safety, and consumer acceptability. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) paired with "fractal analysis" has developed as an effective method for studying food surfaces at the micro- and nanoscales. This review investigated the use of SEM to examine the topographical features of various food items, such as fruits, vegetables, grains, and processed foods, emphasizing the importance of surface morphology in determining texture, moisture retention, and overall product quality during consumption and storage. Fractal analysis, together with SEM, is a quantitative approach for describing the complexity of foods surface structures. Fractal and multifractal analysis using SEM images yields a numerical description of surface roughness, complexity, and heterogenicity. The combination of SEM with fractal analysis not only allows for a more in-depth study of food surface characteristics, but it also helps to optimize food processing procedures. Positive correlations between processing (drying, frying, freezing) time, fractal dimension, and surface openings have been established. Fractal dimension of various food items (fruit, vegetable, crispy product, powder, extrudate product, puffed food, frozen product, fish, etc.) and their characteristics quality attributes have been found expressively interlined. The outcomes of multifractal analysis (Singularity and Rényi spectra) successfully characterized heterogenicity in foods surface micro-structure. SEM image-based fractal analysis, which reveals the subtle links between surface morphology and food attributes, showed potential to significantly expand food science and technology, paving the door for advances in food processing and quality management.

title: Moisture dynamics and flavor evolution in green Sichuan pepper during processing: An LF-NMR/MRI approach
abstract: This study hypothesized that specific moisture migration patterns during the dehydration-rehydration processes are intrinsically linked to the flavor profile evolution of green Sichuan pepper (Zanthoxylum armatum DC.). To test this, the study systematically evaluated the impacts of three dehydration methods - conveyor belt (WD), parallel-flow (PD), and natural drying (ZD) - and subsequent rehydration on the flavor profile, employing low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) to elucidate water mobility. Findings revealed that all treatments significantly reduced L ⁎ , a ⁎ , and b ⁎ values compared to fresh samples (P parallel-flow drying for 10 h (P10) > conveyor belt drying for 13 h (W13) and rehydrated samples ranking P60 > Z60 > W60. A total of 161 volatile aroma compounds were identified by GC-MS, comprising 22 shared and 139 unique compounds, accounting for the distinct aroma profiles across samples. The P10 dehydrated sample exhibited remarkable aroma similarity to fresh material. LF-NMR revealed progressive leftward T 2 peak migration during dehydration, while rehydration induced initial rightward shifts followed by leftward trends. MRI visualization confirmed superior water distribution uniformity in P60 rehydrated samples. Strong correlations (P ⁎ ), moisture content, volatile oils, and numbing compounds. Principal component analysis demonstrated parallel-flow dehydration (PD) as the optimal method for flavor preservation. These results confirm our initial hypothesis, establishing critical structure-function relationships between water dynamics and flavor evolution in Z. armatum during dehydration-rehydration processes, and provide a theoretical foundation for optimizing industrial processing protocols.

title: Foliar ZnSe co-biofortification in wheat grains: Proteomic insights into nutritional enhancement and molecular responses
abstract: Human deficiencies of zinc (Zn) and selenium (Se) primarily originate from their low concentrations in staple crops. We hypothesized that optimizing foliar ZnSe application would achieve ZnSe co-biofortification. This hypothesis was tested through field and soil culture experiments with proteomic analysis. Co-application induced antagonistic interactions between Zn and Se, but optimization of foliar concentration (0.4 % ZnSO 4 ·7H 2 O + 0.0021 %-0.0024 % Na 2 SeO 3 ) compensated for this antagonism, enhancing grain Zn and Se accumulation while maintaining Se concentration below the toxic threshold ( -1 ). This approach shifted Se speciation to 96.7 % organic forms, met daily Zn and Se intake requirements for adults from both flour and whole grain consumption. Proteomic analysis identified differentially expressed proteins involved in selenium, sulfur, and amino acid metabolism in response to ZnSe accumulation. Therefore, we established a field-validated, cost-effective ZnSe co-biofortification strategy readily integrated into conventional wheat production systems, offering a practical solution to alleviate human micronutrient deficiencies.

title: Dual-recognition biomimetic imprinted electrochemical aptasensor based on MXene/AuNPs composite for ultrasensitive detection of trace streptomycin residue in milk
abstract: An innovative streptomycin-specific electrochemical sensor was successfully established using a dual-recognition model based on the integration of molecular imprinting technology with aptamer affinity recognition. The functional interface was fabricated with a MXene/AuNPs composite covered by the specific aptamer and electropolymerized dopamine-imprinted film. Under the optimized conditions, the electrochemical sensor demonstrated a wide linear range from 1.0 × 10 -12 mol/L to 1.0 × 10 -4 mol/L with a detection limit of 0.0316 pmol/L for streptomycin. With the developed sensor, specific, rapid and accurate monitoring of streptomycin residues in milk samples was successfully achieved. The recoveries varied from 88.0 % to 105.8 % with relative standard deviations ranging from 1.7 % to 2.3 %. Overall, with the remarkable performance, the integration of MIPs with aptamer offers a novel approach to prepare the dual-recognition sensing interface and exhibits extensive adaptability and broad application prospects for the measurement, inspection and control of hazardous chemical substances in the complex matrices.

title: Application of LC-MS/MS for the analysis of highly polar contaminants in infant formulas: occurrence, exposure assessment, and unknown analysis
abstract: This study presents a method for analyzing nine highly polar contaminants in infant formulas, combining ultrasound, low temperature, and dispersive solid-phase extraction, followed by LC-MS/MS. Validation according to SANTE 11312/2021 v2 guidelines were performed showing good linearity (R 2 = 0.99), precision (RSD ≤20 %), and appropriate limits of quantification (10–30 μg/kg). Recoveries ranged from 70 % to 103.1 % except for perchlorate (54.4 % at 250 μg/kg) and glufosinate (63.7 % at 150 μg/kg). The method was applied to 30 liquid and powder samples based on soy, rice, cow, and goat milk, and phosphonic acid, chlorate, perchlorate, fosetyl-Al, and glufosinate were detected in 33 % of the samples. Perchlorate showed the highest concentration (139.88 μg/kg), with intake values exceeding the EFSA limit (0.00003 mg/kg body weight/day). For other compounds, daily intakes were within legal limits. An untargeted analysis using LC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS tentatively identified 39 additional compounds. • A novel stationary phase was tested for the separation of polar pesticides. • Glufosinate was the most prevalent compound detected in the samples. • Perchlorate presented the highest concentration in one sample. • The estimated daily intake was calculated for five quantified compounds. • Thirty-nine compounds were tentatively identified through unknown analysis by HRMS.

title: Preparation of a novel fluorescent material ZIF-8@ZIF-8 and its application strategy in the detection and stripping of the tetracyclines residue in food
abstract: The substantial presence of tetracyclines (TCs) and their resistant degradation properties have rendered them prevalent residues in animal-sourced foods. This paper introduced a novel metal-organic framework (AuNCs@ZIF-8@CDs@ZIF-8) that encapsulated carbon dots (CDs) and gold nanoclusters (AuNCs). This framework synergistically combined fluorescence emission with the porous characteristics of multi-shell metal-organic frameworks, facilitating the development of sensors and adsorbents specifically designed for tetracycline antibiotics. The fluorescence intensity ratio (F 0 /F) showed a good linear relationship with the concentration of TCs in the range of 0-100 μmolL -1 , with a detection limit of 0.0903 μmolL -1 . Additionally, AuNCs@ZIF-8@CDs@ZIF-8@SA/CMC hydrogel sensors were constructed and visualized for TC detection using a smartphone. The hydrogel demonstrated a TC loading capacity as high as 551.137 mg/g. The research provided a new strategy for developing the integrated technology of quantitative detection, rapid visualization detection, and adsorption removal of pollutant residues in food.

title: Sensory-metabolomics insights into quality alteration of dried jujube (Ziziphus jujuba ‘Huizao’) fruit in prolonged storage
abstract: Dried jujube, a medicinal-food homologous fruit, has seen significant industrial advancements. However, a comprehensive timeline for quality alteration during storage remains absent. Here, an integrated approach combining bionic sensory analysis and multi-omics techniques was applied to study prolonged storage. Visual marketability loss occurred after two-year storage for browning, while peak shifts in olfactory and gustatory profiles occurred after one-year and three-year storage, respectively. Although bionic sensing revealed multidimensional patterns, integrative omics pinpointed one-year as the critical phase, jointly supported by GC-IMS and LC-MS/MS. Non-volatile metabolite analysis revealed 281 metabolites exhibited significant changes within the first year of storage. Most metabolites exhibited limited abundance changes during storage; only 86 metabolites exhibited large abundance changes, including the typical functional components of jujube, cAMP and cGMP. Furthermore, candidate metabolites, with storage-tracing and nutraceutical/safety risk potential were preliminarily screened. The results provide critical insights for quality tracking, shelf-life assessment and biomarker discovery.

title: ROS-mediated oxidation of egg white proteins accelerates egg quality deterioration
