The signal amplification mechanisms of MOFs in NE-ECSs are systematically discussed, focusing on their roles as direct catalysts, support platforms, signal carriers, and signal probes. In addition, we investigate and review the applications of MOFs-NE-ECSs in food pollution analysis, encompassing the detection of pesticides, antibiotics, food additives, heavy metal ions, and other common substances. Finally, we prospect the current challenges and outline future prospects of MOFs as signal amplification materials for NE-ECSs from aspects such as material structure design and intelligent integration.

title: Systematic identification of novel glycosidic aromatic precursors in winemaking grapes via preparative LC fractionation, target GC and non-targeted UHPLC-MS analysis
abstract: Grapes used in winemaking contain non-volatile precursors that, through chemical reactions and rearrangements, release key aromatic compounds essential to wine aroma. This study aims to identify aroma precursors in extracts from 'Garnacha' grapes combining sequential C18, semi-preparative chromatographies (size exclusion + normal phase), target SPME-GC-MS analysis of the hydrolysed fractions and untargeted UHPLC-MS of the original fractions. Ninety-nine fractions were obtained, 92 of which released aroma upon hydrolysis. Targeted aroma compounds (terpenes, norisoprenoids, volatile phenols, vanillins and ethyl cinnamates) were detected in the hydrolysates of 55 fractions. Identification of precursors was based on: a) exact molecular mass, b) MS/MS spectrum, and c) correlation between the precursor and aroma signals in UHPLC-MS and GC-MS in the original and hydrolysed fractions, respectively. Overall, 185 precursors were identified, 98 for the first time, including 94 disaccharides, 57 trisaccharides and 34 monosaccharides from: terpenes (83), volatile phenols (30), cinnamic acid derivatives (22), norisoprenoids (21), vanillins (19), ethyl leucate (6) and furaneol (4). This work represents a significant advancement in the evaluation of the potential aromatic quality of winemaking grapes using UHPLC-MS.

title: Corrigendum to “Construction of covalent organic framework electrospun composite nanofiber membranes for the efficient extraction and detection of phenylurea herbicides” [Food Chem. 496(Part 2) (2025) 146787]
Flavor characteristics of traditional and mechanically processed base baijiu of sauce-flavor baijiu revealed by GC-IMS and GC-MS
abstract: Mechanized production of baijiu has attracted widespread attention; however, the differences in flavor characteristics between base baijiu produced by mechanized and traditional methods have yet to be elucidated. This study compares base baijiu samples of sauce-flavor baijiu produced over 7 rounds using traditional and mechanized fermentation processes. Fourteen samples were analyzed using GC-IMS and GC-MS, identifying 38 and 104 volatile organic compounds (VOCs).The traditional process produced higher and more consistent levels of volatiles, especially alcohols and ketones. Esters were dominant in both methods.Multivariate analysis (PCA, PLS-DA) revealed clear differences in volatile profiles with 18 and 34 differential compounds identified by GC-IMS and GC-MS, respectively. While both techniques produced similar types of volatiles, differences in concentration significantly influenced the aroma. These findings enhance the understanding of how production methods impact flavor and provide guidance for optimizing mechanized baijiu production and quality control.

title: An upgrade in cocoa alkalization: Functional changes, chemistry and new perspectives
abstract: Cocoa powder is a globally appreciated commodity with recognized health benefits. Alkalization is an optional process in cocoa powder production intended to enhance its sensory and technological properties. However, it can also have drawbacks, such as reduced nutritional value and altered physical and chemical properties. This review aims to update the literature from the past five years on the effects of alkalization in relation to the conditions applied, the matrix used (nibs, cake or powder), and the quality parameters of the final product. Many studies focus on process optimization, but given the variability in the origin of raw materials and the range of alkali that can be used, standardizing conditions is difficult. Advanced metabolomics studies are useful for providing information on chemical changes induced by alkalization. Regarding future challenges, particular attention is given to pioneering studies that aim to replace the conventional alkalizing process with a more sustainable alternative.

title: Sustainable extraction and bioconversion of tea stems using NADES: Dual benefits in polyphenolic recovery and carbohydrates enzymatic hydrolysis
abstract: This study presents a novel and sustainable strategy for valorizing tea stems, an abundant agricultural by-product, using natural deep eutectic solvents (NADESs) composed of choline chloride as the hydrogen bond acceptor and levulinic acid, acetic acid, glycerol, lactic acid, or urea as hydrogen bond donors. The NADES system enabled efficient extraction of polyphenolic and flavonoid compounds, with total flavonoid content (83.49 ± 0.40 mg/g) significantly exceeding that obtained using ethanol (61.65 mg/g). The extracts exhibited enhanced stability under thermal and light stress and demonstrated strong antioxidant activity and inhibitory effects against α-amylase and pancreatic lipase. Importantly, the solid residues remaining after extraction were further enzymatically hydrolyzed to release monosaccharides, supporting complete biomass utilization. This dual-phase NADES-based approach not only maximizes recovery and stability of bioactive compounds but also enables integrated valorization of tea stem residues, highlighting both scientific novelty and practical applicability in functional foods, nutraceuticals, and renewable energy.

title: Modulating fatty acid profile of clarified butterfat (ghee) through multi-stage dry fractionation to improve the functional lipid composition and thermal characteristics
abstract: Evolving across time, modern dietary guidelines for holistic nutrition in many countries place more emphasis on kind of fat ingested than on limiting overall fat consumption. Herein, multi-stage fractionation is demonstrated as a clean, catalyst-free approach that enables targeted concentration of PUFA-rich clarified butterfat (CB) fractions. Fractionation yielded four solid (S40, S30, S20, S10) and four liquid (L40, L30, L20, L10) fat fractions at different temperatures (40, 30, 20, 10 °C). Among the yielded fractions and pure CB, L10 and L20 exhibit most favorable health benefits with lowest atherogenic index, highest health-promoting index, and desirable fatty acids, attributed to their elevated PUFA concentration. Similarly, lowest apparent viscosity (0.076 Pa.s at 0.1 s -1 ), T onset (9.82 °C), T endset (21.01 °C), and highest FFA release (1.05 %) in L20, confirm enhanced bioaccessibility. PUFA-enriched CB fraction contributes to enhanced nutritional value and provides significant health benefits, thereby increasing its applications across food, beverage, and oil industries.

title: A novel Lu(III)-based rare-earth metal-organic frameworks for rapid detection of phosphate with triple-signal output
abstract: Accurate detection of phosphate is vital for food safety, health, and environmental monitoring. This work presents a rectangular plate-like lutetium(III)-based metal-organic frameworks (Lu-MOFs) utilizing Lu(III) ions as metal centers and TCPP as the ligand. Phosphate selectively disrupts the ligand-to-metal charge transfer within Lu-MOFs via host-guest interactions, inducing dual optical responses of enhanced magenta fluorescence and brown chromogenic transition. A portable sensing platform was developed using Lu-MOFs nanoprobe for on-site detection of phosphate, which integrates triple-signal readouts including fluorescent, colorimetric, and smartphone-based RGB analysis, providing respective LOD of 0.44, 2.05, and 4.08 μM. Importantly, this method showed high accuracy and reliability in detecting phosphate in complex samples including chilled foods, instant foods, beverages and water sample, matching well with the standard molybdenum blue method. These findings highlight the promising application potential of Lu-MOFs nanoprobe in the fields of food safety and environmental monitoring.

title: Preparation of mesoporous polydopamine/thyme essential oil/fish scale gelatin photothermal antibacterial film and its application on cherry tomato preservation
abstract: This study synthesized mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles (MPDA) through emulsion-induced interfacial polymerization method to encapsulate thyme essential oil (TEO). The resulting mesoporous polydopamine-thyme essential oil composite (MT) was incorporated into tannic acid-fish scale gelatin (TF) matrix. Upon near-infrared irradiation, the MT-TF composite film achieved a temperature increase of up to 70.1 °C and exhibited sustained as well as tunable release of TEO. The released TEO acted synergistically with the photothermal effect, endowing the MT-TF film with strong antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, achieving a kill rate exceeding 99 %. Additionally, the film demonstrated antifungal efficacy against Botrytis cinerea. In cherry tomato preservation experiments, the 0.3 % MT-TF film effectively maintained fruit quality upon near-infrared activation, thereby demonstrating potential for shelf-life extension. This work thus provides a new strategy for developing sustained-release essential oil-based photo-thermoactive packaging systems.

title: Integrated metabolomics and lipidomics for in-depth understanding of dynamic metabolic changes in passion fruit with different ripeness
abstract: The metabolic and lipidomic profiles of passion fruit at different ripeness stages were systematically investigated using integrated approaches. A total of 558 metabolites across 12 classes and 568 lipids spanning 6 classes were annotated, revealing distinct dynamic changes during both pre- and post-harvest ripening. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis indicated that pre-harvest ripening was associated with the upregulation of pathways such as linoleic acid metabolism, facilitating fatty acid accumulation for cell growth and energy metabolism. In contrast, post-harvest ripening predominantly enhanced the biosynthesis of plant secondary metabolites, notably functional compounds such as 4-Aminobutyric acid and L-(+)-Ergothioneine. Targeted quantification of these two key metabolites using UPLC-QQQ-MS validated the trends observed in untargeted metabolomics. These findings provide in-depth insights into the dynamic metabolic reprogramming during passion fruit ripening and highlight potential applications for functional compound extraction and the valorization of passion fruit by-products.

title: The characteristic roasted peanut flavor of fragrant peanut oil is controlled by non-lipids components in peanuts while the sweet aroma attribute is affected by the variation of fatty acids
abstract: The contribution of lipid and non-lipid components in peanuts to the formation of the flavor profile during roasting was investigated using defatted peanut protein meal (DPPM) and lipid recombination model. The results revealed that the non-lipid fraction of peanuts is primarily responsible for the characteristic roasted peanut flavor and the generation of related compounds, such as pyrazines and cyclic enolones. In contrast, lipids do not play a decisive role in determining the roasted flavor of fragrant peanut oils (FPOs). Notably, the type of lipid can influence the sweet intensity by altering the levels of benzeneacetaldehyde (BA). Model experiments demonstrated that, unlike saturated fatty acids and triglycerides, unsaturated fatty acids can significantly promote the occurrence of the Strecker degradation reaction. Specifically, linoleic acid undergoes this degradation 3.05 times faster than oleic acid. Four oxidative aldehydes derived from linoleic acid can act as α‑carbonyl compounds, significantly enhancing the accumulation of Strecker degradation products through carbonyl-amine reactions, decarboxylation, and hydrolysis. Their primary product is benzaldehyde, which markedly differs from the BA produced when glucose serves as the α‑carbonyl compounds. The study will help enhance our understanding of flavor development in food systems and strategies for optimizing flavor profiles.

title: Untargeted metabolomics elucidates the enhanced protective effects of blackberry juice fermented with Lacticaseibacillus paracasei on hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis neuronal dysfunction
abstract: In this study, lactic acid bacteria (LAB) fermentation was employed to improve the neuroprotective characteristics of blackberry juice (BJ). The underlying mode of action of fermented (F) and unfermented (UF) BJs protecting against corticosterone (CORT)-induced neuronal injury was clarified by multiple techniques. The total viable count of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC18 reached 9.58 log CFU/mL at approximately 30 h fermentation. FBJ markedly increased PC12 cell viability and MMP, and alleviated ROS and cell death, compared to UFBJ. The exogenous apoptosis-related signaling pathways showed lowered Bax and elevated Bcl-2, BDNF, and CREB levels in CORT-injured cells, corroborating the neuroprotection of FBJ. Untargeted metabolomics, which identified 1757 metabolites in BJ groups, revealed that most differentially-accumulated metabolites (DAMs) were mainly associated with amino acid metabolism, biosynthesis of other secondary metabolites, nucleotide metabolism, and membrane transport. This study explored potential of BJ as probiotic carrier with enriched small neuroactive compounds to protect against neuronal dysfunction.

title: Food quality surveillance: A smart fluorescent probe for viscosity-based spoilage detection
abstract: Viscosity is a key indicator reflecting food quality. In this study, we designed a powerful near-infrared-emitting viscosity-sensitive fluorescent probe (DCYM), which exhibited high selectivity and viscosity sensitivity (R 2 = 0.96), broad pH tolerance (pH 4.0-10), excellent photostability (retaining >95 % intensity after 9000 s illumination). Utilizing its superior properties, DCYM was applied to delineate spoilage-specific viscosity signatures across 12 food matrices, including liquid beverages, meat, and vegetables, mechanistically linking rheological changes to pectin hydrolysis and protein denaturation. By establishing precise correlations between molecular-scale viscosity changes and food deterioration pathways, we provided a paradigm-shifting framework for intelligent food monitoring. Hence, this research fundamentally advances the field of food quality control by developing novel analytical approaches, creating a groundbreaking framework for future intelligent food monitoring technologies.

title: Safety assessment of aloe vera produced in the Canary Islands: contamination by pesticide residues
abstract: Although native to the Arabian Peninsula and Africa, aloe vera is significantly cultivated in the Canary Islands, where mild climate and volcanic soils favour its growth. Despite its natural resistance to pest attacks, pesticide contamination can occur due to nearby agricultural practices. In this work, pesticide residue analysis in aloe vera has been carried out for the first time using the QuEChERS extraction method, followed by gas chromatography combined with tandem mass spectrometry analysis. Analytical performance was proved by calibration with R 2 ≥0.9924, recovery in the range 97–114 %, and limits of quantification between 1.744 μg/kg and 2.124 μg/kg. Cadusafos, chlorpyrifos, permethrin, and deltamethrin were found in at least one sample of the 15 aloe vera leaves analysed, all within European legal limits. These results suggested that the evaluated samples of Canary aloe vera can be incorporated into pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, or food products without posing immediate safety risks.

title: Photocatalytic ethylene scavenging by chitosan/gelatin packaging films loaded with TiO2-functionalized bismuth metal organic frameworks for postharvest preservation of fruits
abstract: This study reports the development of eco-friendly active packaging films based on chitosan/gelatin (CS/Gel) matrix reinforced with titanium dioxide-functionalized bismuth metal-organic frameworks (TiO 2 @BMOF) to extend the shelf life of climacteric fruits. TiO 2 @BMOF particles were prepared via the solvothermal method followed by mechanical agitation. The CS/Gel matrix incorporated with 2 and 4 wt% of TiO 2 @BMOF exhibited excellent UV-blocking efficiency (up to 99 %), strong antibacterial activity, improved surface hydrophobicity (79.9°), and increased tensile strength. Importantly, the TiO 2 functionalization promoted the photocatalytic decomposition of ethylene gas, contributing to the delayed ripening of fruits. In practical application, the CS/Gel/TiO 2 @BMOF films significantly preserved banana quality by maintaining firmness, delaying browning, reducing weight loss, and maintaining freshness for up to 10 days under cold storage conditions. These results suggest that the developed film provides an effective approach to extending the shelf life of climacteric fruits by actively alleviating ethylene accumulation and its associated ripening effects.

title: An investigative study into the suitability of the Bradford assay for rapid protein determination in whey
abstract: The gold-standard method to calculate protein content is to determine nitrogen levels, through Kjeldahl or Dumas, and subsequently convert this to protein using a conversion factor. However, this is slow, expensive and requires specialist equipment. This has led to the widespread use of colorimetric assays, principally the Bradford assay, as a rapid protein determination method. Limited research exists quantifying the accuracy of these methods for whey protein, using bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a quantifiable standard. To this end, standardised solutions were made of whey protein and BSA and protein content confirmed using Dumas. When tested with Bradford reagent, it was shown that standard solutions of whey protein were significantly less reactive than equivalent concentrations of BSA: thus, the use of BSA substantially underestimated the amount of protein present within a whey protein sample. This highlights that different proteins vary in their affinity for the reagent, indicating the need for researchers to create a sample-specific standard curve. Bradford data was shown to vary significantly from the reported protein concentration for a range of commercial whey proteins. Dumas was accurate only within a limited range, with higher margins of error being seen than commonly reported. The authors suggest against the use of BSA standard curves in the determination of protein within whey due to the varying protein-reagent affinities and recommend the use of any colorimetric assays with caution for heterogenous mixtures. It is hoped that highlighting these limitations will assist the development of more accurate protein determination methodologies, improving scientific quality.

title: Ultrasound-assisted one-step extraction of safflower red and yellow pigments by natural ternary deep eutectic solvents: Extraction optimization and mechanism, separation and biological activities of pigments
abstract: This study explores a green and sustainable approach based on natural ternary deep eutectic solvents (NATDES) and synergistic ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) of pigments from safflower florets. Choline chloride-ethylene glycol-acetamide (ChCl-EG-AM, 1:3:1) was successfully synthesized and characterized as the most effective NATDES for the one-step extraction of safflower red and yellow pigments. The optimal conditions for ChCl-EG-AM-UAE were as follows: solid-to-liquid ratio of 50.5 mg/mL, extraction temperature at 48 °C, extraction time of 21 min, and water content of 12.8 %. Moreover, this NATDES system could efficiently be recovered and reused in safflower pigments extraction. Safflower pigments also exhibit greater stability in ChCl-EG-AM under dark conditions at 4 °C. The AGREE, AGREEprep, and BAGI tools were used to evaluate this extraction process, suggestive of greenness. The Fourier transform infrared results showed that ChCl-EG-AM was mainly bonded by hydrogen bonding. Scanning electron microscope results revealed that ChCl-EG-AM disrupted the safflower florets' surface structure, facilitating the release of red and yellow pigments. Electrostatic potential, reduced density gradient, and molecular dynamic simulations were applied to reveal the extraction mechanism of ChCl-EG-AM-UAE, which demonstrated that hydrogen-bonding interactions were the key factor underlying its high performance. The isolated pigments (hydroxysafflor yellow A, anhydrosafflor yellow B, and carthamin) exhibit good antioxidant activity and cardioprotective effects in vitro. Overall, ultrasonic-assisted NATDES extraction is an eco-friendly method for the one-step recovery of safflower red and yellow pigments, which reduces resource waste and simplifies the process of extraction.

title: Development of moisture-responsive H2O2-releasing composite films for antimicrobial food packaging applications
abstract: This study introduces H 2 O 2 -releasing films by incorporating CaO 2 into poly(lactic acid)/polyethylene glycol (PLA/PEG) composites by melt extrusion and establishes a practical composition window that correlates PEG concentration with H 2 O 2 -release performance and shelf-life extension. To our knowledge, melt-extruded CaO 2 -containing films have been rarely investigated for antimicrobial packaging applications. PEG acts as a plasticizer and hydrophilic agent, enhancing film flexibility and moisture uptake, thereby facilitating CaO 2 hydrolysis and H 2 O 2 release. Composite films containing ≥ 20 wt% PEG released 67 ppm of H 2 O 2 within 12 h and achieved 99.999% bacterial reduction against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Storage tests with cherry tomatoes demonstrated that PLA/PEG/CaO₂ films delayed fruit deterioration and extended shelf life to 13 d. Migration test confirmed that films with ≤ 20 wt% PEG comply with the European Union regulatory limit. Within this compliant range, the developed PLA/PEG/CaO 2 composite films are safe and effective antimicrobial packaging materials, especially for fresh produce.

title: Glycyrrhizic acid encapsulated in zein/Astragalus polysaccharides nanoparticle: enhanced stability, bioactivity and sustained release
abstract: Glycyrrhizic acid (GA) exhibits potent antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective activities. However, its bioactivity is constrained by low stability under varying conditions, including pH and temperature. To improve its stability, GA was loaded into zein-Astragalus polysaccharides (APS) nanoparticles (zein-APS-GA NPs). The optimized nanoparticles had a diameter of 101.10 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.092, and an encapsulation rate of 91.70 %. Simulated digestion experiments revealed a bioaccessibility of 72.84 % for nanoparticles, compared to 30.70 % for free GA. The radical scavenging rates of the nanoparticles ranged from 66.23 % to 73.34 %, and retained over 40 % after 48 h at room temperature. Stability assays confirmed their robustness across a range of ionic strength, pH values, temperatures, and storage durations. Furthermore, zein-APS-GA NPs increased the viability of alcohol-injured AML-12 cells to 95.50 % at 100 μg/mL (containing 91.7 μg/mL GA), significantly surpassing that of free GA (63.29 %, 100 μg/mL), highlighting their enhanced stability and cytoprotective efficacy.

title: Magnetic dual-dummy-template molecularly imprinted polymer synthesized from plant's phenolic acid–derived deep eutectic solvents for the enrichment of organophosphorus pesticides from rice samples before LC–MS/MS analysis
abstract: A novel magnetic molecularly imprinted polymer (MDMIP) is synthesized using deep eutectic solvents (DESs) derived from choline chloride, plant phenolic acids, and formic acid as green binary functional monomers. Choline chloride-2-naphthol and choline chloride-thymol-ethanol DESs are used as a dual-dummy template. The MDMIP is applied in magnetic solid phase extraction coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to determine seven organophosphorus pesticides in rice samples. The adsorption behavior follows the pseudo-second-order (R 2 > 0.999) and Freundlich (R 2 > 0.987) models, with an imprinting factor of 2.02, indicating high selectivity. The method exhibits a wide linear range (0.0010-5 μg L -1 ), low detection limits (0.00050-0.010 μg L -1 ), and satisfactory recovery rates (80.64 %-112.2 %, relative standard deviations <7.7 %). The incorporation of plant phenolic acid-based DESs offers a sustainable synthetic route while enhancing the adsorption efficiency and analytical performance of the magnetic adsorbent.

title: Anthocyanins loaded bilayer films based on polysaccharides assisted by machine learning for fish freshness monitoring
abstract: Novel multifunctional packaging for monitoring and maintaining food freshness has been developed. Bilayer films based on polysaccharides incorporating red cabbage anthocyanins were prepared. Anthocyanins were encapsulated in the inner layer based on κ-carrageenan or alginate hydrogel, while the chitosan hydrogel was used as a protective outer layer. Carrageenan-anthocyanin-chitosan films demonstrated homogeneity, and fast pH and NH 3 responsiveness. The film exhibited significant antimicrobial activity and excellent antioxidant activity (87 %). To establish a quantitative relationship between film color and fish freshness using machine learning models, the films were exposed to different ammonia concentrations, and the corresponding color responses were recorded. The artificial neural network demonstrated the best performance, achieving a R 2 score of 0.984. Finally, storage of trout fillets was monitored for 12 days at 4 °C. The results confirmed the excellent potential of the bilayer films, which could be, in combination with machine learning models, effectively applied for monitoring food safety.

title: Unlocking the potential of waxy wheat: a comprehensive study on nutritional flavor, structural collapse, and practical blending strategies
abstract: Waxy wheat possesses unique functional properties but often leads to severe structural collapse in starch-based foods, especially steamed bread. The underlying mechanism remains poorly understood, and comprehensive data on its nutritional profile are still limited. This study first compared the nutritional and flavor components between waxy and normal wheat, and further investigated the collapse mechanism in both steamed and baked bread, focusing on starch properties and non-starch constituents. Waxy wheat demonstrated nutritional advantages, including higher levels of β-glucan, resistant starch, flavonoids, and unsaturated fatty acids, along with a distinct flavor profile. The high viscosity starch gel caused by unique waxy starch and elevated non-starch components, combined with high moisture and pressure during steaming, resulted in more severe collapse in steamed bread than in baked bread. Blending waxy wheat into normal wheat flour at ≤20 % effectively reduced steamed bread collapse, offering a practical utilization strategy.

title: Coffee beverage sedimentation: From roasting effects to storage stability
abstract: Ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee products often experience sedimentation that compromises product quality and consumer acceptance. This study investigated sedimentation mechanisms in RTD coffee under varying roasting conditions, extraction temperatures, and product formulations through molecular weight and compositional analyses. Two mechanisms were identified: galactomannan crystallization and protein-polyphenol interactions. Low-temperature extraction favored protein-polyphenol aggregation with higher protein proportions in sediments, while high-temperature extraction promoted galactomannan crystallization with mannose enrichment in the sediments. Commercial RTD exhibited distinct mechanisms of sedimentation patterns: black coffee showed carbohydrate-dominated sediments, while latte formulations exhibited protein-mediated aggregation. Prototype RTD revealed that formulation variables influenced both sediment quantity and aggregate molecular weight, while milk proteins increased both sediment quantity and molecular weight, indicating enhanced aggregation behavior. This framework supports targeted strategies such as enzymatic polysaccharide control for black coffee and protein ratio optimization for milk-based RTDs, providing a foundation for improving more stable RTD coffee.

title: Lipidomics-based evaluation of gender and monthly age on the quality of Congling Tibetan chicken
abstract: Congling Tibetan chicken is a geographical indication product of Chinese agricultural products. However, the effects of gender and monthly age on the chicken quality remain unclear. In this study, 4-month-old Congling Tibetan rooster (4CTR), 6-month-old Congling Tibetan rooster (6CTR) and 6-month-old Congling Tibetan hen (6CTH) were used to analyze the differences in their nutritional and lipid composition. Results indicated that 6CTH showed firmer meat with richer fatty acids and flavor compounds, while 6CTR exhibited deeper redness and higher minerals (Ca, Se, Zn). 4CTR had superior moisture and essential amino acids, but a simpler flavor. Additionally, rooster soup showed high triglycerides and diglycerides expression, while hen soup had low levels. 4CTR soup contained unique antioxidant phospholipids, while 6CTR and 6CTH soups were rich in digestible short-chain triglycerides. KEGG pathway analysis identified glycerolipid metabolism and ferroptosis as the key pathways.

title: Closed-loop biorefining of Moringa oleifera branches: unlocking nutraceutical polyphenols and fermentable sugars via NADES-mediated Cascade processing
Effects of ferulic acid additions on pasting properties, quality and in vitro starch digestion of extruded buckwheat noodles
abstract: The preparation of buckwheat noodles with excellent quality holds importance in food industry. The aim of study was to evaluate the effects of different ferulic acid additions on the pasting properties, quality and in vitro starch digestion of extruded buckwheat noodles. The overall viscosity of buckwheat/ferulic acid blends reduced by the ferulic acid addition. Ferulic acid reduced degree of ordered starch structure, corresponded to the decreased relative crystallinity in X-ray diffraction results. The stickiness of extruded buckwheat noodles markedly decreased from 2.333 N to 1.518 N with ferulic acid additions, corresponded to the lowering cooking loss. The noodle with 0.5 % ferulic acid addition is most acceptable by panelists. Ferulic acid decreased in vitro starch digestibility of noodles from 56.53 % to 50.61 %. The findings confirmed appropriate ferulic acid additions improved the quality and inhibited in vitro starch digestion of noodles, providing theoretical guide in the development of high-quality starchy foods.

title: A potential approach for targeting change of metabolic characteristics of the tiger nut (Cyperus esculentus L.) via different probiotics fermentation
abstract: This study applied six types of probiotics for investing their impact on metabolic characteristics of fermented tiger nut meal. There were 57 commonly shared metabolites to be identified. Metabolic pathway analysis showed that metabolites of different probiotic fermentation were mainly involved in amino acid metabolism, purine metabolism, pyrimidine metabolism, terpene, piperidine and pyridine alkaloids biosynthesis. Compared with control, Pediococcus pentasaceus, Lactobacillus brevis and Lactobacillus plantarum fermentation increased formation of alcohols and lipid-related compounds. Furthermore, a smaller number of ketones were also detected after Lactobacillus rhamnosus and Pediococcus pentasaceus fermentation. In contrast, Lactobacillus plantarum fermentation increased content of phenols and aldehydes. Although all the fermented samples demonstrated an increased number of volatile compounds, different pathway for synthesis of non-volatile and volatile compounds in the metabolites following different probiotics fermentation was also revealed, indicating their unique regulation pattern on the changes in the sensory and nutritional properties of fermented tiger nut meals.

title: Modification of polysaccharides with octenyl succinic anhydride (OSA): Reaction, effect on their functional properties and applications
abstract: The use of biopolymers, particularly polysaccharides like cellulose, starch, chitosan, and gums, has seen a significant rise in the pharmaceutical, cosmetics and food industries, due to their biodegradable and non-toxic nature. However, their hydrophilic properties limit their functional versatility. To address this limitation, the modification of these biopolymers with hydrophobic substituents, such as OSA, has become a topic of great interest. This review summarizes recent advances in OSA modification of natural carbohydrates, focusing on key parameters such as reaction medium, mechanism, temperature, pH, time, polymer concentration, and OSA-to-polymer ratio. The impact of OSA modification on the physicochemical and functional properties of polysaccharides is discussed, emphasizing on their potential applications as emulsifiers, gelling and foaming agents and film-forming materials. Notably, OSA-modification has reported to enhance the emulsifying capacity of polysaccharides by 40-100 % and the foaming capacity by 20-100 %, thereby enabling their application as stabilizers in beverages, cosmetic products and pharmaceutical formulations.

title: Insights into honey powder production: Key factors, production methods, physicochemical characterization, and applications
abstract: Honey powder is a free-flowing, dry form of natural honey produced through various drying techniques that aim to preserve its nutritional and functional properties while enhancing its shelf life and usability. However, challenges such as crystallization, stickiness, and thermal sensitivity during processing hinder its large-scale commercialization. This review explores the physicochemical, bioactive, and antibacterial properties of honey and dried honey, focusing on drying techniques such as spray drying, freeze drying, vacuum drying, microwave drying, and vacuum foam drying. Among these, spray drying stands out for its industrial feasibility, while techniques such as freeze-drying and vacuum foam drying offer advantages in nutrient retention and solubility, respectively. Applications range from bakery and dairy products to nutraceuticals, where honey powder functions as a natural sweetener, antioxidant, and preservative. Future research should prioritize predictive models for drying optimization, hybrid drying methods, and eco-friendly carrier systems. The paper also assesses the commercial potential of honey powder, highlighting its relevance in clean-label product development.

title: Antisolvent sequence as a tunable switch for zein-naringin-D-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol 1000 succinate (TPGS) nanoparticles: interfacial dynamics and bioactivity enhancement
abstract: Naringin (NRG), despite their demonstrated health benefits as natural bioactive compounds, are hampered by intrinsic hydrophobicity, which consequently impedes processability in aqueous systems and severely constrains oral bioavailability. The aim of this study was to form different type nanoparticles by Zein, TPGS and NRG, nanoparticles were obtained by the anti-solvent method, and to analyze the internal interaction forces, stability and antioxidative. The sequence of the antisolvents used becomes the primary factor influencing the properties of the nanoparticles. Nanoparticles were characterized by multimodal analysis, as spectroscopy, molecular docking, SEM, XRD, FTIR, TGA, and ITC. NRG is stabilized within the Zein matrix through hydrogen bonding involving Gln residues and hydroxyl or carbonyl groups, coupled with hydrophobic sequestration of its aglycone moiety in Pro-rich nonpolar cavities. The encapsulation efficiency of NRG increased up to 72.71 % at (Z-N)-T, which is the highest stability among different types of nanoparticles. The nanoparticles average size below 105 nm, and the zeta potential is 25.48 mV, and also exhibits significant antioxidant activity. This study architected Zein-based nanoparticles to methodically assess the interaction force and stability, pioneering a formulation approach for engineered carriers in food and drug delivery matrices.

title: Fluorescent sensor array based on emission enhanced gold nanoclusters for detecting and discriminating pesticides in vegetables
abstract: Fluorescence metal nanocluster (FMNC) sensor arrays have demonstrated high potential in simultaneously detecting multiple pesticides. However, the available FMNC arrays commonly depend on single interactions, which limits their application potential. In this study, a four-channel fluorescence sensor array consisting of enhanced Au-ATT/Tb, Au-ATT/CB[7], Au-ATT/Sc, and Au-ATT/Arg NCs was constructed based on multiple interactions of cucurbit[7]uril (CB[7]), Sc 3+ , Tb 3+ , and arginine (Arg) with gold-6-aza-2-thiothymine NCs (Au-ATT NCs). The sensor array simultaneously and distinctly discriminated four pesticides through various interactions, including charge transfer, hydrophobic, and metal complexation. Based on the differential fluorescence quenching degrees, the pesticides were quantitatively and qualitatively detected with detection limits of 0.174, 0.140, 0.120, and 0.819 μM for diquat, thiram, paraquat, and thiophanate-methyl, respectively. The array demonstrated excellent selectivity, high discrimination ability for pesticide mixtures, and 100 % identification accuracy in carrot, cucumber, and lake water samples at low concentrations, signifying the potential practical application of the proposed method.

title: pH-driven polyphenol-polysaccharide co-assembly for constructing curcumin-carrageenan complexes: Intestinal targeted, pH-responsive controlled release, and bioaccessibility enhancement in functional beverages
abstract: In this study, a simple, green, and efficient pH-driven polyphenol- polysaccharide co-assembly strategy was adopted to prepare curcumin-carrageenan complexes for enhanced encapsulation, intestinal targeting delivery, controlled release, and bioaccessibility of curcumin in functional beverages. Results showed that stable complexes (355.7 nm, -39.5 mV) were formed at a curcumin to carrageenan mass ratio of 1:10, achieving efficient curcumin loading (encapsulation efficiency: 76.0 %, loading capacity: 6.9 %). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), enhanced sampling molecular dynamics simulation (ESMDS), and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) confirmed that curcumin was mainly bound to carrageenan through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions to form a uniformly dispersed amorphous granular morphology with high tolerance to ion strength (0-500 mM) and pH (3-8). Carrageenan encapsulation significantly enhanced the DPPH and ABTS + free radical scavenging activities of curcumin. The complexes aggregated during simulated gastric fluid digestion and degraded during simulated intestinal fluid digestion, thus inhibiting the release and decomposition of curcumin in the gastric fluid and significantly increasing curcumin bioaccessibility from 36.1 % to 52.2 % (p inf of 64.498; k of 0.450). Current study will provide a theoretical basis for the green and efficient preparation of polysaccharide-based polyphenol delivery systems and their application in functional beverages.

title: Dietary components cooperate with intestinal flora to regulate food allergy
abstract: Global prevalence of food allergies is rising, which results from a combination of genetic, environmental, immune, and dietary factors. This paper systematically reviews mechanisms of food allergy, including the effects of intestinal mucosal immunity and gut microbiota. We also summarize the role of dietary components in the development of food allergies. Studies have shown that dietary components can modulate allergic diseases through the host, gut microbiota, and metabolites, thereby exerting a bidirectional regulatory effect on allergic outcomes. Specifically, certain dietary ingredients, such as carbohydrates, unsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, plant compounds, and probiotics, have been shown to significantly improve allergy symptoms. However, current research on synergistic effects between dietary components and intestinal microbiota remains limited. Therefore, in-depth exploration needs to provide a scientific basis for dietary interventions targeting microbiota regulation. Such research would hold significant scientific value and clinical relevance for the prevention and treatment of food allergies.

title: Signature aroma compounds and precursors in Chinese indigenous pork: Characterization via OAV-weighted GC-O-MS and lipidomic profiling
abstract: Chinese indigenous pigs exhibit distinct aroma characteristics compared to commercial pig breeds due to their unique fatty acid composition and lipid properties. This research conducted gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS) and liquid chromatography mass spectrometer (LC-MS) to conduct a multidimensional analysis of three geographically representative indigenous pig breeds in China. A total of 21 aroma compounds were identified as the primary contributors to pork aroma. Among these, nonanal, octanal, 2,3-octadione, dodecanal and thiazole were identified as signature aroma compounds of indigenous pig breeds; cis-3-nonen-1-ol and 3,5-octadien-2-one can be used as biomarkers for the identification of Bama and Shenxian pork breeds. Correlation analysis further revealed that C18:3 (n3), C20:4 (n6), and C18:2, cis (n6) are key fatty acids contributing to major aroma compound formation. Additionally, TGs and PEs containing C18:1 and C18:2 were the core precursor substances for the formation of indigenous pig aroma characteristics.

title: Sodium substitutes synergizing with dietary fiber: Effect on the textural, sensory, digestive, and storage properties of emulsified sausages
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of sodium substitutes (KCl, MgCl 2 , and CaCl 2 ) and soybean dietary fiber (SDF) on the textural, sensory, digestive, and storage properties of emulsion sausages. Replacing 25 % of NaCl with KCl or MgCl 2 minimally affected the physiochemical and texture properties of emulsified sausages. Notably, MgCl 2 increased the sensory score and degree of hydrolysis of the emulsified sausage. In contrast, CaCl 2 led to irregular microstructure, decreasing hardness, increased cooking loss, lower sensory scores, and lower degree of hydrolysis. SDF shortened water relaxation time and caused denser structure of sausages. It mitigated the negative impacts of CaCl 2 by increasing hardness and decreasing cooking loss, though SDF did not increase the sensory scores. However, SDF reduced the degree of hydrolysis to 35.1 %-41.1 %, and decreased the sensory scores. And SDF did not change the storage properties of the sausages, and sodium substitutes were favorable for it.

title: Structure-function modulation of protein-rich pumpkin seed flour via microfluidization processing for plant-based applications
abstract: The growing global demand for dietary proteins necessitates the search for novel and sustainable protein sources. As a byproduct of pumpkin processing, protein-rich pumpkin seed flour (PSF) holds significant potential. Yet, it is underutilized and limited research has been conducted on improving its functionality without prior protein extraction. This study examined microfluidization to enhance PSF's functional properties without protein extraction. Microfluidization reduced particle size and induced protein unfolding, producing a more irregular and porous surface. These changes increased free sulfhydryl content and surface hydrophobicity, improving foaming capacity by up to 7.5-fold, while also improving emulsifying properties. Changes in surface morphology also promoted interactions between the proteins and water or oil, increasing solubility (up to 710 %), water-holding capacity (up to 246 %), and oil-holding capacity (up to 400 %). Overall, the findings demonstrate that microfluidization is an effective strategy for the valorization of PSF, significantly enhancing its functional properties without requiring protein isolation.

title: Effect of extrusion parameters on the quality of extruded reconstituted konjac glucomannan Rice
abstract: This study investigated the effects of screw speed (175-250 rpm), feed rate (900-1900 g/h), and barrel temperatures of zones III (80-130 °C) and IV (70-120 °C) on starch-protein-konjac glucomannan (KGM) extruded complexes and reconstituted KGM rice (RKR). Results showed that these parameters influenced RKR quality primarily by modulating starch degradation. Degradation increased with higher barrel temperatures but exhibited a nonlinear pattern with increasing screw speed and feed rate, reaching a maximum at 220-235 rpm and 1100 g/h, respectively. Their influence on RKR quality follows a cascade framework in which extrusion parameters regulate starch degradation, thereby driving structural evolution and ultimately determining product quality. Stickiness and redness were sensitive to all three parameters. Hardness was sensitive to feed rate and barrel temperature. Optimal cooking time was sensitive only to feed rate, whereas total color difference and lightness were sensitive exclusively to barrel temperature. Findings provide guidance for producing high-quality reconstituted rice.

title: Machine learning-assisted dual-mode immunochromatography for high signal-to-noise ratio detection of aristolochic acid-I
abstract: Developing high signal-to-noise ratio strategies for immunochromatography remains challenging yet highly desirable. Here, we developed a "off-on" dual-mode immunochromatographic assay (ICA) enabling both sensitive on-field colorimetric detection (CICA) and accurate fluorescence quantification (FQICA) of aristolochic acid-I. The assay utilized porous coordination network (PCN) as colorimetric signal, fluorescence quencher, and antibody carrier, paired with europium-based metal-organic frameworks (Eu-BTEC) as fluorescence donor. Benefiting from its porous architecture and tunable absorption wavelengths, PCN exhibited favorable antibody coupling ability, remarkable colorimetric intensity and near complete excitation and emission quenching of Eu-BTEC. The ICA showed limits of detection (LOD) at 0.45 ng/mL (CICA) and 0.08 ng/mL (FQICA), representing 12- and 65-fold improvements over the LOD of AuNPs-ICA. Furthermore, machine learning integration enabled precise contamination classification and quantification. This work not only established an efficient strategy for aristolochic acid-I rapid detection also paved the way for integration immunoassays with machine learning in food monitoring.

title: Artificial intelligence revolutionize food detection? Vision, olfaction and taste integrated with machine learning/deep learning in food detection
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming the theoretical framework and technological paradigm of food detection. The study focuses on elucidating the underlying mechanisms of machine learning (ML)- and deep learning (DL)-based AI in feature extraction, pattern recognition, and decision feedback. AI algorithms have enabled perception systems such as computer vision, electronic nose, and electronic tongue to overcome their dependence on handcrafted features, achieving automatic learning and high-dimensional representation of complex signals, thereby significantly enhancing detection accuracy and robustness. In addition, this paper systematically analyzes the advantages and limitations of AI-empowered perception technologies and presents prospects for the potential applications of multimodal data fusion and large language models (LLMs). Finally, the study summarizes the major challenges that AI still faces in food detection and outlines potential directions for future development.

title: Cereals: a source of allergenic proteins and their characterization by proteomics
abstract: Cereals are sources of essential carbohydrates, nutrients and proteins. The most consumed cereals are wheat, rice and maize. However, cereals cause various allergic reactions which are associated with presence of gluten-based and non-gluten-based allergenic proteins. In addition to traditional methods used for detection of allergenic proteins such as ELISA, Western blotting and 2D immunoblotting, mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomic approaches are applied for identification of cereal proteomes and to distinguish among highly similar peptide sequences of cereal gluten proteins. Using MS-based proteomics, identification/quantitation of allergenic proteins and discovery of novel epitopes responsible for allergic reactions are possible with high accuracy. This allows for development of precise diagnostic tools and therapy. In this review, the proteins of wheat, barley, rye, rice and maize are described with main focus on their association with IgE-mediated allergy. The methods for cereal protein characterization are discussed and examples of proteomic studies on cereal allergenicity are included.

title: Enhanced bioaccessibility of a hesperidin-rich blood orange extract after encapsulation in alginate/chitosan microcapsules
abstract: Blood orange pulp extract was encapsulated using the ionic gelation method with an alginate/chitosan polymeric matrix to enhance the bioaccessibility of its bioactive compounds. The extract exhibited strong free radical scavenging activity (FRAP, ABTS, ORAC) and had a significant inhibitory effect on intestinal disaccharidases, with 55.9 % inhibition of sucrase, suggesting its potential application as a natural agent for postprandial glycemic control. Hesperidin was quantified as the main flavonoid in the extract (18.87 mg/g) and encapsulation efficiency was 70.07 %, indicating good retention of this compound in the biopolymeric matrix. Simulated digestion revealed that encapsulation provided significant protection from gastric degradation, with an increase in the hesperidin bioaccessibility index from 2.96 in the extract to 26.2 l% in the microcapsules (p < 0.001). These results demonstrate that encapsulation is an effective strategy for improving the stability and bioaccessibility of hesperidin, supporting its use in functional and health-promoting products.

title: Impact of cooking methods on the flavor profile of fresh-pressed and dry-pressed green huajiao (Zanthoxylum schinifolium Siebold & Zucc.) original pulp oil
abstract: Flavor alterations induced by various cooking methods have hindered the broader application of green huajiao original pulp oil in the food industry. This study evaluated the effects of six cooking methods on the flavor characteristics of dry-pressed and fresh-pressed oils. Overall, cooking generally reduced numbing and aromatic compounds, corresponding to decreased sensory numbing and aroma. Conversely, bitterness and rancidity increased in some samples, notably rancidity after microwaving and bitterness after high-pressure cooking. GC-MS identified alkenes and alcohols as the main VOCs, the types (69 in dry-pressed, 79 in fresh-pressed) and content differences are the reasons for the significant differences in VOCs between the two oils (p < 0.05). Finally, correlation analysis further identified the relationships between VOCs and aroma characteristics. The results showed that the reduction of linalool and nerolidol correlated with a weaker floral aroma, and that of d-limonene, myrcene, and linalyl acetate with a diminished citrus fragrance.

title: Chemical modification of microbial exopolysaccharides toward enhanced application in prepared pasta products
abstract: Microbial exopolysaccharides (EPS) are high-molecular-weight polysaccharides secreted by environmental microorganisms. Their unique physicochemical properties and bioactivities offer significant application potential in the food industry. However, the inherent limitations of native EPS restrict their use in prepared pasta products. Chemical modification, therefore, offers an effective strategy to alter the structure of EPS, enhance their physicochemical and bioactive properties, and improve their functionality in food systems, particularly in prepared pasta products. Although nearly one hundred related studies have been published since the 20th century, comprehensive summaries and critical evaluations in this area remain limited. This review summarizes recent advances in the chemical modification of EPS, focusing on how these alterations affect their functions. It also highlights relevant case studies of modified EPS in prepared pasta products and discusses associated safety considerations, aiming to provide a theoretical foundation and practical guidance for the development and application of EPS in the food industry.

title: Comparative assessment of infrared/microwave-induced structural and physico-chemical transformations in Canadian pulses: Implications for cooking, milling, and nutritional quality
abstract: Infrared (IR) and microwave (MW) processing are rapidly emerging as energy-efficient and clean-label thermal technologies for industrial-scale pulse utilization. This study explored how IR/MW-induced microstructural modifications influence physico-chemical attributes and starch-protein interactions of chickpeas (CP), yellow peas (YP), green lentils (GL), and fava beans (FB) under varying exposure times (60-120 s). Porosity of IR and MW-treated grains was increased as 1.3 %-12.2 % and 3.3 %-26.4 %, respectively. YP showed the highest reduction in cooking time for both IR (62.5 %) and MW (73.2 %). Both IR/MW induced starch gelatinization and protein denaturation, as confirmed by FTIR and correlation analyses. Uniform intermediate peaks in particle size distribution signified better milling quality of thermal-treated grains. YP was responsive to both IR/MW, while CP/FB responded effectively to MW, and GL showed better response to IR. In conclusion, the study underscores the efficacy of IR and MW in modifying pulse microstructure to enhance cooking and nutritional quality for better utilization of pulses.

title: Effect of free fatty acids with different chain lengths and unsaturation degrees on hazardous compounds in canola oil cooking fumes
abstract: This work investigated how the structure and content of free fatty acids (FFAs) in canola oil affect the characteristic pollutants in oil fumes. Results showed that higher FFA concentrations induced a maximum 18.3-fold rise in particulate matter concentrations in heated oil fumes, with chain length exerting a larger effect than the degree of unsaturation. For carbonyl compounds (CCs), increases in unsaturation and FFA content could increase their total concentration and associated carcinogenic risk, up to 590.2 μg/m 3 and 1.1 × 10 -5 , respectively. Regarding polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), chain length and FFA content affected their concentrations and health risks more significantly than unsaturation. As FFA content increased, the types of PAHs shifted from low-ring to high-ring structures. Moreover, changes in free radicals in heated oil were crucial for variations in oil fume components influenced by FFAs. This study provides targeted theoretical support for reducing harmful emissions from cooking oil.

title: Aerogel-based oil sorbents derived from pomelo (Citrus grandis L.) peel powder as fat replacers: effects on physicochemical properties and volatile profiles of semi-dried chicken sausages
abstract: Traditional oleogels require thermal treatment, which promotes lipid oxidation and diminishes health benefits in meat products. This study developed aerogels containing 5-6 % pomelo (Citrus grandis L.) peel powder (125 or 250 μm), which were converted into aerogel-based oleogel-like sorbents (ABOS) by immersion in rice bran oil at room temperature. ABOS were used to replace 20 % pork fat in semi-dried chicken sausages over four days of drying. The reformulated sausages maintained desirable pH (∼5.3) and water activity (∼0.93), while showing 33-46 % reduction in lipid content and 2.8-3.9-fold increase in dietary fibre. Volatile profiling (SPME-GC-MS) revealed PP-derived terpenes and esters may imparting fruity-meaty notes, in contrast to lipid-derived aldehydes and ketones in the control. Microstructural analysis indicated that 125 μm ABOS enhanced water retention and porosity, whereas 250 μm ABOS reinforced texture. These findings demonstrate ABOS as a sustainable, non-thermal alternative to traditional oleogels for healthier, fibre-enriched meat products.

title: Deciphering the butylated hydroxytoluene dissolution behavior in solid-liquid systems through coupled experimental and molecular dynamic simulation approaches
abstract: The insight of dissolution behavior at solid-liquid equilibrium systems offers a guideline for crystallization design, development, and further desired products preparation, while it is restricted in understanding the dissolution behavior. In this work, butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is chosen as the model substance due to the flake crystal shape, inducing the difficulty in filtering and washing, to study its dissolution behavior by joint experiments and molecular simulation approaches. Solubility determined by the gravimetric method increases with temperature. The modified Apelblat model shows the best predictability. Thermodynamic analysis reveals that the dissolution is endothermic and entropy increase process, and enthalpy acts as the key contributor to Gibbs free energy in the dissolution process. Crystal structure and molecular simulations show that the BHT is more easily dissolved in solvents with stronger solute-solvent interaction energy. This study offers the information for the crystallization design, operation, and the understanding of dissolution at the molecular level.

title: Enzymatic extrusion processing of oat protein concentrates: Structural, functional, and nutritional properties
abstract: This study produced oat protein concentrates (OPCs) from pregelatinized whole oat flour via enzymatic extrusion hydrolysis and evaluated their composition, structure, and functionality. OPCs obtained by high thermal α-amylase (Thr-NDFOPC) exhibited the highest protein content (58.78 %), followed by medium α-amylase (Med-NDFOPC) (52.02 %) and conventional enzymatic hydrolysis (Con-NDFOPC) (44.08 %). Structural analyses (FTIR, CD, SEM) showed significant alterations in secondary conformation, surface roughness, and porosity, particularly in Thr-NDFOPC, indicating partial unfolding and disruption of protein networks. Functionally, OPCs displayed limited solubility at neutral and acidic pH but improved values under alkaline conditions, with Con-NDFOPC reaching nearly 60 % solubility at pH 9. Water- and oil-holding capacities ranged from 1.90 to 2.97 g/g and 2.48-2.57 g/g, respectively, while emulsifying activity and stability ranged from 21.27 and 26.89 m 2 /g and 37.09-47.36 min, respectively. Subsequent ethanolic defatting at 65 °C further increased the protein concentration to 64.69 % in Con-DFOPC, 72.55 % in Med-DFOPC, and 74.88 % in Thr-DFOPC, and intensified structural disintegration, resulting in reduced solubility but enhanced hydration (3.19-3.75 g/g), oil-holding capacity (3.28-3.82 g/g), and emulsification capacity (25.27-34.55 m 2 /g). These results highlight enzymatic extrusion hydrolysis as a scalable method for producing OPCs with tailored structural and functional properties for food applications.

title: Comprehensive flavoromics and lipidomics analyses elucidate the mechanism of star anise in flavor improvement during braised duck leg processing
abstract: This study systematically investigated the mechanism of star anise in modulating the aroma of braised duck leg (BDL) using flavoromics and lipidomics. Six key volatile flavor compounds (d-limonene, linalool, eucalyptol, α-terpineol, anethole, and estragole) derived from star anise were found to impart floral, fruity, herbal, and anise-like notes to the BDL. Four potential off-odorants (hexanal, heptanal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 2-pentyl-furan) with rancid, metallic, bloody, and earthy odors in the BDL showed significant positive correlations with oxidation markers, while exhibiting negative correlations with n-9/n-6 unsaturated fatty acids. Non-targeted lipidomics analysis identified polyunsaturated triglycerides (TG), phosphatidylserine (PS), phosphatidylcholine (PC), and cardiolipin (CL) as key differential lipids distinguishing star anise-treated braised duck legs from control samples. Star anise may improve the flavor profile of BDL by inhibiting the thermal oxidation of key lipid precursors, thereby reducing the excessive accumulation of lipid-derived off-odorants.

title: Temperature-controlled steam explosion modulates structural and functional characteristics of Porphyra haitanensis dietary fiber
abstract: Developing efficient modification methods for seaweed dietary fiber (DF) is hindered by its sulfated galactan backbone, which differs fundamentally from terrestrial lignocellulosic matrices. In this study, temperature-controlled steam explosion (SE) was employed to modulate the structural and functional characteristics of Porphyra haitanensis TDF. Moderate SE (140 °C) promoted an effective IDF-to-SDF conversion, evidenced by pronounced increases in SDF (127.67 %), galactose (37.71 %), and uronic acids (22.73 %-25.65 %), accompanied by reductions in IDF (17.95 %), acid-insoluble residue (28.54 %), and sulfate groups (47.40 %) (p < 0.05). Multiscale characterization revealed the formation of a honeycomb-like porous network, strengthened hydroxyl/carboxyl signals, elevated crystallinity, and enhanced thermal stability. Correspondingly, hydration capacity, lipid adsorption, cholesterol binding, and inhibition of α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and pancreatic lipase increased significantly. Excessive SE (180 °C) led to structural densification and diminished functionality. These findings suggest that controlled SE may restructure sulfated seaweed DF, offering a green strategy for its functional utilization.

title: Impact of wheat postharvest maturation on gluten conformational and molecular properties
abstract: This study systematically explored the impacts of wheat postharvest maturation on gluten conformational and molecular properties. Results showed that postharvest maturation improved the viscosity and elasticity of dough. The analysis of gluten particle size, molecular chain morphology, and SE-HPLC demonstrated that postharvest maturation promoted gluten polymerization. Postharvest maturation induced a more hydrophobic microenvironment for tryptophan residues in gluten, and promoted the adoption of the gauche-gauche-gauche conformation in disulfide bridges. Furthermore, postharvest maturation increased the contents of ω5- (by 0.12 %), ω1,2- (by 1.76 %), and α-gliadin (by 4.41 %), with slight increases of 0.04 % and 0.96 % for D-type and B/C-type LMW-GS (low-molecular-weight glutenin subunits), respectively. Simultaneously, the intermolecular forces of gluten have been strengthened, including disulfide bonds, ionic bonds, and hydrophobic interactions. Thus, the increased gluten composition contributed to glutenin-gliadin and glutenin-glutenin polymerization via disulfide bonds, ionic bonds, and hydrophobic interactions, altered the gluten conformation, and thereby enhanced dough viscoelasticity.

title: Suppression of sensory bitterness of beverages via nanoscale complex coacervation
abstract: Bitterness suppression plays a crucial role in enhancing the flavor profiles of food and beverages. In this study, we developed a novel bitterness suppression strategy via selectively sequestering bitter compounds in solutions based on spontaneously generated nanoscale coacervates of small-molecular polyions with opposite charge, e.g., phytic acid (PA) and chitosan oligosaccharides (COS). The PA/COS coacervates exhibit universal bitterness suppression to different bitter beverages, like coffee, green tea, limonin and corn peptides solutions. Temporal dominance of sensations (TDS) showed addition of small amounts of coacervates effectively suppressed the bitterness of dark roasted coffee (30 % reduction). Untargeted metabolomics indicated the coacervates reduced coffee bitterness mainly via sequestering bitter compounds detected at higher levels in coffee, e.g., caffeine (29 % reduction), and di-esterified quinic acids (73 % reduction). This finding suggests that coacervates could provide a potent tool for enhancing the flavor profiles of food and beverages through the selective sequestration of bitter compounds.

title: Proteomics and peptidomics of variations in protein profiles of UHT milk following non-enzymatic compared to enzymatic processes
abstract: Ultra high temperature (UHT) milk may develop age gelation during storage; nevertheless, the variations in protein composition remain unexplained. This study employed proteomics to investigate the variations in proteins in milk under non-enzymatic and enzymatic settings. Findings showed Fresh UHT milk, Nearing expiration date (NED) UHT milk, and age-gelated UHT milk had 2616, 2685, and 3295 proteins, respectively. The proteins in Age gelation, enzymatically produced by plasmin, demonstrated a 140-fold up-regulation and a 143-fold down-regulation. β-Casein, as the primary hydrolyzed substrate, diminished in Age gelation to 29.72 % of its abundance in Fresh UHT milk. Nucleobindin-2 and bone bridging proteins were markedly diminished. The peptides in Age gelation were predominantly sourced from casein, with peptide function annotations indicated in Biological process, and it was postulated that the differential proteins primarily originated from cellular proteins. These findings offer novel insights into the mechanisms underlying age gelation in milk.

title: Corrigendum to “Interfacial performance of gallic acid and methyl gallate accompanied by lecithin in inhibiting bulk phase oil peroxidation” [Food Chem. 328 (2020) 127128]
Anti-inflammatory effect of high-abundance Core oligopeptides from white tea via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling pathway
abstract: White tea exhibits remarkable anti-inflammatory activity. Its unique prolonged withering process promotes protein hydrolysis, enriching oligopeptides whose bioactivity is governed by specific constituent amino acid sequences. However, the core anti-inflammatory sequences and their mechanisms remain unclear. To address this, an integrated multi-omics and experimental strategy was employed. Forty-eight high-abundance oligopeptides were identified, with network pharmacology revealing their interaction with key inflammatory targets via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway. Four core candidates-LCAY, SGFGG, SGGFG, and HHMCC-were selected based on binding affinity. Validations in LPS-induced RAW264.7 cells confirmed these peptides significantly suppressed NO, IL-1β, and TNF-α. Furthermore, Western blot analysis demonstrated that these oligopeptides exert anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting the phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and IKK, and blocked the nuclear translocation of NF-κB. These findings elucidate the material basis of white tea's anti-inflammatory properties and highlight the therapeutic potential of its bioactive oligopeptides.

title: Controllable oxidase-mimic activity of magnetic Fe3O4@metal-organic framework core-shell heterogeneous nanozyme aroused by chlorpyrifos for monitoring chlorpyrifos residue in foods and bioaccumulation in rice
abstract: The extensive use of poisonous chlorpyrifos in agriculture has created an urgent need for reliable detection methods. In this study, a rationally designed heterogeneous metal-organic framework (MOF) nanozyme was developed, consisting of an Fe 3 O 4 core and a Cu II -centered zeolitic imidazolate framework shell (Fe@CuZIF) for chlorpyrifos analysis. The hybrid exhibited synergistic properties, including strong adsorption capacity, magnetic separation for chlorpyrifos enrichment, and enhanced oxidase-mimicking activity compared with Fe 3 O 4 without H 2 O 2 . Leveraging the inhibitory effect of chlorpyrifos on the acetylcholinesterase- regulated collapse of Cu II -centered MOF shell, the Fe@CuZIF-based sensing platform produced chlorpyrifos-triggered oxidase-mimicking activity. The system achieved a detection limit of 0.35 ng mL -1 , along with excellent selectivity, anti-interference resistance, and capability for time-dependent kinetic monitoring of chlorpyrifos bioaccumulation in rice. Overall, this work establishes a promising paradigm for nanozyme-based sensors in pesticide residue analysis for food safety and provides a new strategy for designing hybrids capable of target pesticide-activated recognition.

title: Smartphone-assisted curcumin-based fluorescence sensing platform for alcohol content in Chinese liquor via hydrogen bond manipulation
abstract: Alcohol content is one of the most important quality control metrics in Chinese liquor production, and its accurate determination is highly desired in safeguarding product quality, consumer health, and tax assessment. This study presents an innovative fluorescence sensing platform for alcohol content determination. Curcumin was used as a fluorescent indicator, which demonstrated distinct fluorescence responses to hydrogen bonding interaction with ethanol and water. Experimental results demonstrated an excellent linear correlation between fluorescence intensity changes and alcohol content (20-80 %, vol%) with a strong correlation coefficient (R 2 = 0.991), excellent precision (relative standard deviation <1.67 %) and accuracy (recovery rate 96.78-102.79 %, relative error ± 3.22 %). Further integrated with smartphone technology, a portable fluorescence sensing platform was developed, which enables accurate alcohol content determination through RGB analysis of fluorescent images. This novel method demonstrates promising potential in practical applications, offering a portable and user-friendly solution for alcohol content determination in food and beverage industries.

title: Integration of UHPLC/QTOF-MS and GC–MS to decipher the subtle component difference between raw and bran-roasted Myristica fragrans (nutmeg)
abstract: To decipher subtle chemical variation of both non-volatile and volatile components during bran-roasting of nutmeg (Myristica fragrans), we innovatively established a "three-source comparison" approach (raw nutmeg, RN; bran-roasted nutmeg in lab, BN-L; bran-roasted nutmeg from market, BN-M) and developed chemometrics/machine learning (ML) models to identify processing-related markers. Untargeted high-resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based metabolomic analysis of the RN and BN-L samples unveiled 57 differential metabolites, and five thereof (involving increased 5-hydroxymaltol, maltol, dipterine, fragransin B2, and decreased adipic acid) were selected as processing-associated markers. These five markers achieved 90 % accuracy in identifying the BN-M samples in the external validation, much better than that gained by seven potential volatile markers recorded by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Conclusively, integration of chemometrics and ML reveals the subtle chemical changes during the processing of nutmeg, and it is the first study reporting robust markers that are diagnostic to discriminate between the raw nutmeg and processed products.

title: X-ray-mediated vitamin D synthesis
abstract: Vitamin D synthesis is traditionally linked to ultraviolet B (UVB) light exposure of its precursors 7-dehydrocholesterol and ergosterol. This study investigated whether ionizing X-ray irradiation can also induce the conversion of sterol precursors into vitamin D. At a dose of 25 kGy, X-rays produced 94 μg/g vitamin D 3 from crystalline 7-dehydrocholesterol and 74 μg/g vitamin D 2 from crystalline ergosterol. When the precursors were dissolved in oil (50 μg/ml), X-ray exposure yielded 70 ng/g vitamin D 3 and 45 ng/g vitamin D 2 . Similar increases were also observed in mushrooms, yeast, and rodent feed. Compared with UVB irradiation, X-ray exposure produced vitamin D amounts comparable to those obtained with 20 mJ/cm 2 UVB. High-dose UVB (200 mJ/cm 2 ) yielded substantially more - 151 μg/g vitamin D 3 and 188 μg/g vitamin D 2 from crystalline precursors. These results demonstrate that X-ray irradiation can generate vitamin D, an unexpected and unrecognized pathway of vitamin D formation.

title: Synergistic effects of endogenous protein components and starch molecular structure on physicochemical, rheological and digestive properties in rice
abstract: Developing rice cultivars with low-glutelin and high-resistant starch is beneficial for health management in diabetes and chronic kidney disease. This study systematically investigated the structural, physicochemical and digestive properties of four isogenic rice mutant cultivars with graduated prolamin-to-glutelin (P/G) ratios and identical macronutrient compositions. Molecular structure analysis revealed similar whole starch molecular size distributions but different amylopectin chain length distributions among samples with varying P/G ratios. The isolated starch with shorter and fewer amylopectin short-medium chains exhibited more disordered crystalline structures, resulting in reduced gelatinization enthalpies, peak viscosities and gel viscoelasticity, thereby promoting enzymatic hydrolysis. Critically, the prolamin-rich matrix exhibits stronger hydrophobic interactions, which inhibit starch granule swelling and promote starch-starch interactions, resulting in a stronger gel structure and resistant starch content increases by 8.73 % to 13.48 %. These findings reveal new insights into cultivating functional rice tailored for patients with diabetes and kidney disease by regulating the prolamin-to-glutelin ratios.

title: Tertiary enzyme synergistic network-mediated starch-directed transformation into resistant starch
abstract: Pea starch was modified with different combinations of α-amylase, 4-α-glucanotransferase, and pullulanase, to produce eight types of resistant starch. The results showed that, compared to pea starch, the triple-enzyme-modified starch showed a 37.51 % reduction in branching degree after gelatinization. Moreover, its crystal structure transformed from C-type to B-type, with crystallinity increasing to 37.21 %. Enzymatic modification increased the proportions of B1 and B2 chains. This structural reorganization significantly increased the resistant starch content and reduced the glycemic index. The maximum resistant starch content reached 56.77 %, while the glycemic index decreased by 9.43 %. After cooking, the resistant starch content declined. However, the resistant starch content of the starch that underwent gelatinization and triple-enzyme treatment remained above 30 %. After cooking, the glycemic index remained at a medium level, with the lowest value recorded at 62.78. This study provides a theoretical basis for the development of functional starch.

title: The significant reduction of extraction time using high-pressurized microwave extraction method for arsenic species from rice
abstract: To address the challenges of traditional extraction methods like time-consuming and insufficient extraction efficiency, this work integrated high pressure to microwave-assisted extraction. The proposed extraction way only required 3 min for achieving a great increase of extraction efficiency (1-2.5 times) of nine arsenic species from rice, compared to ultrasonic, heat-assisted, and microwave-assisted methods under the same conditions (solvent, temperature, and time). After the significant promotion of high pressure for extracting arsenic species was proved, other factors including extraction solvent, temperature and time were optimized. For 0.50 g of rice sample, the efficient extraction of nine arsenic species was accomplished in 5 mL of hydrochloric acid (0.023 mol L -1 ), under 45 bar, 90 °C and 3 min. Coupled with HPLC-ICP-MS, an analytical method was established in 0.2-500 μg kg -1 , and it exhibited better sensitivity (LODs, 0.04-0.12 μg kg -1 ) than other methods. Then some rice samples were analyzed, inorganic arsenic pollutants (sum of As(III) and As(V), 56.0-127.8 μg kg -1 ) and some organic arsenic targets containing DMA, MMA, ASC and ASB were found. The spiked recovery was ranged from 88.6 % to 103.1 % in rice samples, with relative standard deviations less than 4.55 %. These indicated the analytical method was suitable for the rapid determination of trace arsenic species in rice.

title: Elucidating microbial succession dynamics and flavor metabolite formation during two rounds of natural fermentation of Qingxiangxing baijiu: integration of flavoromics and genomics
abstract: Microbial succession in Jiupei (fermented grains) critically shapes Qingxiangxing Baijiu (QXB) flavor during two rounds of fermentation (Dacha and Ercha). To explore flavor differences between Dacha and Ercha, this study used multi-omics approaches to analyze the dynamic changes in volatile profiles and microbial communities. Reducing sugars accumulated in Dacha but declined in Ercha. A total of 433 (Dacha) and 560 (Ercha) volatile compounds were identified, with 69 volatiles (OAV > 1) as important flavor contributors, including ethyl acetate, ethyl lactate and 1-propanol. Ercha's microbial community structure differed significantly from Dacha's. Lactobacillus and Staphylococcus were core bacteria in both rounds. Saccharomycopsis dominated Dacha fungi, while Issatchenkia prevailed in Ercha. Correlation analysis showed that Lactobacillus and Pediococcus were positively associated with ester biosynthesis in Dacha, while Thermoascus and Wickerhamomyces showed significant correlations with volatile compounds in Ercha. This study enhances understanding of QXB's two-round fermentation process and provides a theoretical foundation for quality optimization.

title: Supramolecular calix[6]arene-COF with pocket-like cavities for host-guest recognition-based SERS detection of tryptamine and seafood freshness monitoring
abstract: Monitoring seafood freshness is critical for ensuring nutritional value and food quality, but targeted analysis in complex matrices remains challenging. Herein, a thiol-functionalized calix[6]arene covalent organic framework grafted with AuNPs, denoted as CX6-SCOF-AuNPs, was strategically designed for rapid, sensitive and selective detection of tryptamine in seafood by surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). CX6-SCOF-AuNPs featured extensive pocket-like hydrophobic cavities integrated within an ordered porous structure, enabling specific capture of tryptamine with exceptional enrichment capacity (203.4 mg/g) and rapid adsorption kinetics (within 2 min).
