We compared an aqueous soluble lignin (SLg) with two less soluble fractions produced by thermal (Lg-200) or alkali-thermal treatment (Lg10-200) processing using an in vitro batch fermentation model. SLg produced modestly higher total short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) than the other lignin fractions (from ∼7.80 to ∼8.72 mM), with relatively greater acetate (from ∼3.01 to ～4.24 mM) and propionate (from ∼2.71 to ∼3.50 mM), and a pH decrease from 6.60 to 6.15. It also increased microbial diversity and enrichment of taxa linked to carbohydrate fermentation (e.g., Ruminococcus torques, Megamonas), alongside reduced pro-inflammatory Collinsella. Moreover, SLg significantly decreased the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota (F/B) ratio relative to the blank (from ∼44.02 to ∼30.59, p < 0.05). These results suggest that soluble lignin may influence gut microbial composition and could be further explored as a potential functional ingredient.

title: Comparative non-volatile composition, sensory quality, and ferroptosis-targeted anti-inflammatory activity of instant green tea powders from green- and purple-leaf cultivars
abstract: Instant tea powder is a convenient, shelf-stable product with growing global popularity, yet the impact of cultivar type on its composition and functionality remains underexplored. This study compared two instant green tea powders from green-leaf (ZYQ) and purple-leaf (ZY) cultivars in terms of metabolite profiles, sensory attributes, and anti-inflammatory effects. Metabolomics and sensory evaluation revealed distinct characteristics: ZYQ contained higher levels of epicatechin, proanthocyanidins, total flavonoids, etc., while ZY was enriched in anthocyanin glycosides and EGCG. ZYQ showed greater umami, sweetness, and harmony, whereas ZY exhibited stronger bitterness, astringency, and a purplish-red infusion. Both powders significantly alleviated LPS-induced inflammation in RAW 264.7 macrophages by inhibiting NF-κB and ferroptosis-related oxidative stress, reducing ROS, MDA, iron, and inflammatory mediators. ZY induced stronger upregulation of Nrf2, Gpx4, and Txnrd1, indicating enhanced antioxidant defense. These findings demonstrate that cultivar selection shapes instant tea's flavour and bioactivity, with purple-leaf products offering distinctive functional advantages.

title: Reveal the flavor quality changes of soy sauce during shelf life through metabolomics
abstract: Soy sauce contains abundant flavor compounds, which are prone to change during storage. This leads to a decline in amino acid nitrogen content, accompanied by undesirable flavor shifts, including increased sourness and bitterness, as well as aroma deterioration. Using three metabolomics approaches, the compounds of 12 kinds of soy sauce were analyzed before and after accelerated shelf life testing (ASLT), identifying a total of 132 volatiles and 44 non-volatiles. Multivariate data analysis (OAV, TAV, OPLS-DA, FC and significance difference) pinpointed 9 key aroma and 15 key taste compounds in the shelf life of soy sauce, which were further verified by constructing a metabolite model and conducting sensory validation experiments. The sensory changes observed in soy sauce shelf life was explained at the metabolite level. This study conducted a comprehensive analysis of soy sauce quality changes during storage, which will be of significant theoretical value for the soy sauce industry development.

title: The flavor-related metabolites and sensory quality of white tea produced by exogenous methyl jasmonate treated tea leaves
abstract: Methyl jasmonate (MeJA) is a well-established plant hormone utilized for flavor enhancement in agricultural products. This study systematically investigated its effects on white tea flavor by integrating analyses of both volatile and non-volatile compounds. Results indicated that MeJA treatment increased soluble sugar content and decreased tea polyphenol level, and also altered the composition of catechins and amino acids, particularly glutamic acid, affecting the overall taste profile of white tea. The content of the grassy-scented compounds (1-octen-3-ol, limonene, butanal, and (Z)-3-Hexen-1-ol acetate) was significantly decreased, while the content of pleasant aroma compounds (α-terpineol, α-ionone, phenylacetaldehyde) was significantly increased with MeJA treatment. A total of eight key compounds were identified as key contributors to the aroma of white tea. Our results systematically reveal the effect of MeJA on the flavor and quality of white tea, providing a scientific basis for the application of MeJA in tea.

title: Targeted lipidomics reveals the impact of processing units on fatty acids and oxidized lipids in nutritionally complete food for special medical purposes
abstract: Lipids serve as crucial functional components in nutritionally complete foods for special medical purposes (nc-FSMP). However, potential impacts of processing units on lipids remain poorly understood in nc-FSMP. Therefore, this study investigated the influence of homogenization, sterilization, and spray drying on the lipids using targeted lipidomics. A total of 49 fatty acids and 20 oxidized lipids were identified and quantified. The results showed that spray drying led to the most pronounced increase in lipid oxidation and the highest accumulation of oxidized lipids. Fatty acids significantly reduced across the processing units, and both homogenization and spray drying resulted in larger losses compared to sterilization. Among the identified oxidized lipids, trans-EKODE-(E)-Ib and 9(S)-HpOTrE can be considered as specific markers for distinguishing different oxidation levels across the processing units. Overall, these findings elucidate the changes in lipids across the processing units and provide novel insights for quality control in the nc-FSMP manufacture.

title: Monitoring of protein oxidation, fat oxidation and flavor of Tan sheep during postmortem aging: formation and relationship
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the changes in protein oxidation, lipid oxidation, and volatile compounds in the longissimus dorsi muscle of Tan sheep during postmortem aging over a period of 0-144 h. The results indicated that as the aging time increased, the protein carbonyl content significantly rose from 0.005 μmol/g to 0.036 μmol/g, while the total sulfhydryl content decreased from 2.10 μmol/g to 1.14 μmol/g. Furthermore, malondialdehyde (MDA) levels increased from 0.03 mg/kg to 0.13 mg/kg. There was an increase in saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and a decrease in unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs). A total of 56 volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were identified, with notable changes in aldehydes, alcohols, and esters, which peaked at 48 h. These results demonstrate a strong relationship between oxidative changes and flavor development, offering a theoretical foundation for enhancing meat aging methods.

title: Enhancing high-fibre cereal food quality through microbial-enzymatic processing: Mechanisms, applications, and prospects
abstract: Microbial-enzymatic processing, a novel biological regulation method, combines enzymatic hydrolysis with microbial fermentation, showing significant potential for improving the quality of high-fibre cereal foods. However, current research has insufficiently explored the systematic mechanisms and quantitative analysis of its regulatory quality. This review summarises commonly used microorganisms and enzymes, process principles, and key influencing factors, providing an in-depth analysis of their regulation mechanisms on cereals. Results indicate a 34 % reduction in cellulose content and modifications in the molecular structure of starches and proteins. Anti-nutritional factors decrease by 20-40 %, total phenolic acids and flavonoids increase by 46.56 % and 57.28 % respectively. Water-holding capacity increases by 79.87 % and gel properties are enhanced. Antioxidant capacity increases by 48.98 %, while mineral bioavailability and macromolecular absorption rates improved. Furthermore, the flavour and texture of food are enhanced. Finally, this review summarises the applications and prospects for integrating this technology with novel methods to facilitate industrial development.

title: Mechanisms of aroma compound formation in traditional Japanese sake brewing by natural lactic acid fermentation: Insights from solvent-assisted stir bar sorptive extraction with GC–MS and bacterial flora analysis
abstract: Yamahai-brewed sake, a traditional Japanese rice wine fermented with naturally occurring lactic acid bacteria, has been understudied regarding its aroma compound profiles and bacterial dynamics during brewing. This study aimed to clarify the relationship between aroma compounds and bacterial communities throughout the sake brewing process, using solvent-assisted stir bar sorptive extraction with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (SA-SBSE-GC-MS) and 16S rRNA sequencing. Seventy-four aroma compounds were detected, and comprehensive analysis revealed key aroma compounds characteristic of Yamahai brewing. Spearman's rank correlation analysis demonstrated that lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus sakei and Lactococcus raffinolactis contribute to the production of characteristic aroma compounds. Quantitative analysis revealed that γ-6-(Z)-dodecenolactone reached 1.0-1.4 μg/L in Yamahai samples, whereas it was below the quantification limit in Sokujo samples. SA-SBSE-GC-MS enabled high-sensitivity detection of polar compounds, offering a powerful tool for investigating aroma formation mechanisms during the brewing of alcoholic beverages.

title: Sustainable ultrasound-assisted extraction of carotenoids from the seaweed Ulva lactuca: Performance of the green biosolvents 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran (2-methyl oxolane) and ethyl lactate and optimization using response surface methodology
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the efficiency of ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) combined with green solvents for recovering carotenoids from dehydrated Ulva lactuca . Two green solvents (ethyl lactate and 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF) were compared with conventional food-grade solvents (acetone, ethyl acetate, ethanol, and hexane). UAE significantly outperformed conventional maceration in carotenoid yield, depending on the solvent and compound. Ethanol and 2-MeTHF showed the highest total carotenoid content (TCC), with 2-MeTHF demonstrating high extraction efficiency across multiple carotenoids, including (all -E )-lutein and (9 Z )-fucoxanthin. Response surface methodology identified amplitude, extraction time, and solvent-to-sample ratio as key variables. Under optimal conditions (64.7 % amplitude, 10 min, 70 mL/g), the TCC reached 37.79 μg/g dw (dry weight)—3.4 times higher than the lowest tested condition. The comparative greenness assessment highlighted 2-MeTHF as a sustainable and effective alternative to petroleum-based solvents for carotenoid extraction using UAE. • Ultrasound-assisted extraction of carotenoids from Ulva lactuca was optimized. • Novel green solvents and conventional food-grade solvents were compared. • 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran proved to be efficient for carotenoid extraction. • Response surface methodology effectively optimized the extraction parameters. • The method applies green chemistry and promotes the valorization of U. lactuca.

title: Changes in the structure and thermal properties of feather keratin induced by L-Cys extraction followed by enzymatic hydrolysis
abstract: Feather waste was valorised into bioactive peptides by extracting high-purity L-Cys–urea solution, followed by enzymatic hydrolysis with commercial proteases selected for their catalytic efficiency. The extraction reduced the α-helix content in favor of the β-sheet leading to less ordered crystal structures as ATR FT-IR and the XRD analyses revealed. These structural changes decreased keratin's thermal stability, resulting in its slower yet more gradual decomposition, as TGA and DSC results showed. The hydrolysis with trypsin, chymotrypsin, pepsin and subtilisin altered the secondary structure and thermal stability of extracted keratin, with changes depending on enzyme specificity. All hydrolysates showed the preserved amide features but reduced α-helix and β-sheet content and crystallinity. Subtilisin induced the most profound structural and molecular transformations, including the secondary structure loss, carboxylate group formation, and short peptide fragment generation, resulting in reduced structural order but enhanced thermal stability attributed to the stabilizing effect of sodium carboxylates. • Keratin extraction disrupts S S and H-bonds, largely preserving peptide bonds. • Keratin extraction lowers α-helix in favor of β-sheet and reduces thermal stability. • Hydrolysis by trypsin, chymotrypsin and pepsin does not affect keratin structure much. • Enzymatic hydrolysis reduces keratin crystallinity and thermal stability. • Subtilisin hydrolysate is the most thermally stable despite secondary structure loss.

title: Vacuum frying of low-fat hairtail: process optimization, physicochemical dynamics, and volatile compounds characterization
abstract: This study aimed to develop a visually appealing, low-oil vacuum-fried hairtail product by optimizing processing parameters through Response Surface Methodology (RSM). The synergistic effects of frying time, de-oiling duration, and frying temperature on the physicochemical properties, textural attributes, and volatile flavor profiles of low-fat hairtail were systematically investigated. Optimal conditions, including a frying time of 40 min, a de-oiling time of 6 min, and a frying temperature of 80 °C, were identified using single-factor experiments and a Box-Behnken design. Volatile compounds in both raw and vacuum-fried samples were characterized using Gas Chromatography-Ion Mobility Spectrometry (GC-IMS), revealing 43 volatile organic compounds. Among them, hexanal, ethyl butyrate, and nonanal were notably abundant and likely contributed to the overall aroma profile. Glycine, aspartic acid, alanine, and glutamic acid impart a unique taste to vacuum-fried hairtail. This optimized approach overcame limitations associated with conventional single-factor experimentation, minimized energy consumption, and established precise control parameters suitable for automated production.

title: Mechanism of physicochemical changes in potato starch gel induced by citric acid-autoclaving for texture improvement and resistant starch formation
abstract: Potato starch readily forms gels with high hardness and viscosity, which limits its practical application. In this study, a citric acid-autoclaving treatment was employed to reduce gel hardness and viscosity while increasing the resistant starch content of potato starch. The results demonstrated significant reductions in crystallinity, setback viscosity (from 1285.33 ± 37.89 mPa·s to 91.67 ± 6.11 mPa·s), and gel hardness (from 4165.13 ± 123.94 mN to 7.48 ± 1.49 mN) after modification. Kinetic digestion simulations further revealed a slower digestion rate for the citric acid-autoclaving starch, which was attributed to the formation of a highly sterically hindered cross-linked structure and increased contents of resistant starch (from 8.55 ± 0.71 % to 12.81 ± 0.63 %) and slowly digestible starch. This dual-modification approach significantly improved the textural properties of the starch gels, offering a promising strategy for the deep processing and high-value utilization of potatoes.

title: Enzyme pretreatment combined with ultrasound-assisted aqueous biphasic extraction of flavonoids from Abelmoschus manihot (L.) leaves: Process optimization, antioxidant activity, and molecular docking
abstract: In this study, we developed a comprehensive strategy involving enzyme pretreatment combined with ultrasound-assisted aqueous biphasic extraction (EPUAABE) for extracting flavonoids from Abelmoschus manihot (L.) leaves (AMLF). Under optimized conditions (2.4 % enzyme concentration, 1:3 cellulase-to-xylanase ratio, pH 5.0, 37.5 °C, 2.5 h, 1:40 solid-liquid ratio, ultrasonic treatment of 180 W, 16 min, and (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 mass fraction of 20 %), the maximum recovery of flavonoids recorded was 66.81 %. The yield was 30.90 mg/g in the top phase. HPLC analysis revealed significantly higher contents of myricetin and quercetin with EPUAABE than with 80 % ethanol solvent extraction (SE). The EPUAABE extracts presented better radical-scavenging activity, which was strongly correlated with quercetin, myricetin, and quercetin-3-O-glucoside. Elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) activities, alongside reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels in the serum, were detected in the mice treated with AMLF. Molecular docking demonstrated high binding affinities of these flavonoids to SOD and CAT. Overall, this study highlights that EPUAABE, a green, scalable process, effectively enhances flavonoid yield and has strong antioxidant activity in enriched flavonoid fractions, indicating promising application in developing functional foods and nutraceuticals.

title: Molecular docking and fluorescence spectroscopy analysis of the interaction of different polyphenols with salivary mucin and proline-rich protein toward the astringency mechanism
abstract: Molecular docking, fluorescence spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), and circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy were used to systematically analyze the interactions between saliva mucin (MUC) or basic proline-rich proteins (bPRPs) and five typical polyphenols, including catechin (C), gallic acid (GA), epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), proanthocyanidin (PC), and tannic acid (TA), aiming to explore the key roles of two saliva proteins in the generation of astringency. Molecular docking results revealed that the binding energies of the polyphenols with MUC were generally lower than those with bPRPs, following the order of binding affinity TA > PC > EGCG > C > GA. Higher content of phenolic hydroxyl groups and degree of gallate acylation of polyphenols resulted in stronger interaction and more binding sites with the salivary proteins. Fluorescence quenching and synchronous, FTIR, and CD spectra confirmed that the polyphenols bound more strongly to MUC than to bPRPs, and MUC demonstrated more unfolded conformation and ordered secondary structure change.

title: Determination of beta-lactoglobulin in foods via colorimetric paper-based aptasensor using bimetallic MOFzyme
abstract: This study developed a paper-based colorimetric aptasensor for the detection of β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) in foods, using copper‑cobalt metal-organic framework (CuCo-MOF) as the core catalyst. The sensor achieved a detection limit as low as 0.102 mg/L. and a wide linear range (0.39-1250 mg/L). It offered a simple detection procedure with less than 20 min detection time, making it more suitable for on-site food safety screening. Validation with commercial ELISA confirmed its suitability for analyzing real-food samples, such as milk and infant formula. The developed paper-based RGB colorimetric aptasensor emerges as a user-friendly and economical assay for high-throughput, visual, and accurate determination of β-LG in foods.

title: Preparation and characterization of modified sunflower meal protein–quercetin nanoparticles: Shelf–life study of seasoned lamb kebabs
abstract: This study developed a quercetin (Que) nanoencapsulation system (PU-SMP-Que) using phosphorylated and ultrasonicated sunflower meal protein (PU-SMP) as the carrier. At a protein-polyphenol mass ratio of 15:1, the spherical PU-SMP-Que nanoparticles exhibited an average diameter of 175.3 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.351, and a high encapsulation efficiency of 98.09 %. Spectroscopic and X-ray diffraction analyses confirmed the incorporation of Que into amorphous PU-SMP matrices through hydrogen bonding, electrostatic, hydrophobic, and van der Waals interactions. Nanoencapsulation significantly enhanced the antioxidant capacity and antibacterial efficacy of Que, along with favorable sustained-release characteristics. Furthermore, the application of PU-SMP-Que nanoparticles to seasoned lamb skewers significantly reduced lipid oxidation and microbial proliferation, maintained pH, water-holding capacity, and delayed color and texture deterioration, extending the shelf life from 4-5 to 10 d. These findings indicate that PU-SMP-Que nanoparticles are a simple and promising composite transport system with a strong potential for meat preservation.

title: O2-switched catalysis direction of catalase-like nanozymes: a universal approach for enhancing the sensitivity of H2O2 electrochemical sensor in water-soaked foods
abstract: To improve sensitivity of electrochemical sensor based on nanozymes in food analysis, conventional strategies often focus on modifying the properties of nanozymes, which lack universality. Here, to conveniently obtain low-cost Co 3 O 4 nanozymes, a biomineralization strategy was proposed using freely available crop wastes (maize husks) as bio-templates. Co 3 O 4 nanozymes exhibited excellent catalase-like activity. Interestingly, increasing the O₂ concentration significantly inhibited the oxidative half-reaction of catalase-like activity, thereby enhancing the reductive half-reaction. Further, an O 2 -enhanced electrochemical sensor was constructed for the detection of H 2 O 2 at negative potential, which demonstrated low limit of detection (0.2 μM), wide linear range (1 μM - 9 mM), excellent anti-interference performance and acceptable detection reliability for water-soaked foods. Notably, this work improves sensitivity by manipulating O₂ concentration rather than modifying nanomaterials, offering a universal approach for enhancing the performance of electrochemical sensors. Furthermore, this strategy has been successfully extended to portable electrochemical test strips with plug-and-play USB workstations.

title: Evaluation of a copper(I)-Biquinoline complex modified electrode for electrochemical detection of nitrite in water
abstract: Glassy carbon electrodes were modified with a small amount of Nafion and a novel copper (I)-biquinoline coordination compound. Their electrochemical properties were evaluated for the detection and quantification of nitrite in aqueous media. The surface of the resulting stable and reproducible electrodes was characterized by Raman spectroscopy and atomic force spectroscopy (AFM). Electrochemical measurements in Britton-Robinson buffer revealed an increased current response and a decrease in onset potential for nitrite reduction compared with bare glassy carbon electrode. The modified electrode exhibited a linear response (R 2 = 0.998) a detection limit of ca 0.04 μM and recovery values of 88.9 ± 0.05 % in model water, 43.2 ± 0.04 % in drinking water and 23.9 ± 0.31 % in well water. Chronoamperometric measurements at -0.86 V (vs Ag/AgCl) demonstrated that no other ions interfered with the electrochemical response of Cu(I)-biquinoline modified electrodes.

title: Characterization of volatile components and identification of aroma precursors in different types of pork by multi-omics
abstract: Indigenous Chinese pork is highly favored by consumers due to its distinctive aroma. However, the lipid precursors responsible for its characteristic aroma compounds require further investigation. This study focused on four types of pork, including Ningxiang (NX), Duroc×Wujin hybrids (DW), Rongchang (RC), and Duroc×Landrace×Yorkshire hybrids (DLY). The relationship between phospholipids (PLs) and characteristic aroma components was explored using lipidomics and flavoromics. The results indicated that PLs enriched with linoleic acid (C18:2n-6), arachidonic acid (C20:4n-6), and oleic acid (C18:1) significantly promote the formation of aroma compounds such as (E,E)-2,4-nonadienal and 1-octen-3-ol through thermal oxidation. Additionally, correlation analysis revealed that hexanoic acid and 3-octanone were negatively correlated with intramuscular fat content but positively correlated with specific PLs. This study elucidates the aroma profiles and their phospholipid precursors in indigenous Chinese pork, providing a scientific foundation for understanding the mechanisms of flavor formation and molecular breeding.

title: Umami characterization and molecular simulation of novel peptides from Pleurotus citrinopileatus Singer bromelain hydrolysate
abstract: Pleurotus citrinopileatus Singer is the promising precursor of umami peptides. This study aimed to isolate P. citrinopileatus Singer-derived umami peptides, and then explore their taste characteristics and umami mechanism. Four novel umami peptides (LLVTVEDELRV, LDDWR, ELFEPT, and ENLLEK) were separated and identified from bromelain hydrolysate, and then predicted their umami potentials through umami fragment frequencies and T1R1/T1R3 receptor docking. Their umami characteristics were subsequently confirmed in sensory evaluation and electronic tongue verification. Particularly, LLVTVEDELRV (0.0625 mg/mL) and LDDWR (0.1250 mg/mL) exhibited potent umami taste, with significant lower thresholds than monosodium glutamate. Molecular docking analysis revealed that all four peptides could bind to T1R1/T1R3 receptor, and hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions were the dominant interaction forces. Asp219 and Glu148 residues were of great significance in the interactions of peptides ligand to T1R3. Furthermore, all of them exhibited umami enhancement in simulated broth solutions.

title: Multifunctional electrospun nanofiber films towards efficient deodorization and preservation of crayfish meat (Procambarus clarkii) via a triple-synergistic strategy
abstract: Although aquatic products are nutritious, they are highly perishable and tend to develop undesirable odors. Traditional methods of preservation and deodorization often suffer from limitations including inadequate efficacy and safety issues. Here, we propose a triple-synergistic strategy that integrates host-guest complexation by β-cyclodextrin, physical adsorption enabled by a highly porous nanofiber film, and the bioactivity of grape seed extract. The multifunctional nanofiber film, composed of polyvinyl alcohol, β-cyclodextrin, and grape seed extract, was prepared via electrospinning. At a 10 % grape seed extract loading level, the triple-synergistic strategy endowed the film with the remarkable adsorption rate (74.08 %), along with excellent antibacterial and antioxidant performance. This multi-mechanism action effectively extended the shelf life of crayfish meat (Procambarus clarkii) and minimized the production of undesirable odors during storage. Ultimately, the underlying mechanism of these excellent performances was expected to inspire the design of other aquatic products packaging films.

title: Unveiling the basis of metabolite accumulation and stress adaptation in Chinese kale: Metabolic divergence and environmental regulation of glucosinolates and anthocyanins
abstract: This study elucidated the biochemical and molecular basis of nutritional and flavor quality in Chinese kale, and investigated the effects of environmental factors on its characteristic metabolites. Field comparison revealed that Longjiang (LJ) accumulated higher soluble sugars, phenols, anthocyanins, and glucosinolates but lower vitamin C and flavonoids than Qiusheng (QS). Multi-omics integration identified 1774 differential metabolites and 7356 differentially expressed genes in LJ vs. QS group, identifying glucosinolate and anthocyanin metabolism as core differential pathways. Environmental response studies showed that temperature extremes differentially regulated glucosinolate and anthocyanin metabolism. High temperature significantly remodeled glucosinolate metabolism, characterized by a reduction in bitter-tasting glucosinolates and a 9.5-fold increase in sulforaphane. Low temperature triggered a 5.9-fold elevation in anthocyanin via upregulated synthetic genes and transcription factors. Drought and salt stress had minor impacts. Additionally, indole glucosinolate (1-sulfo-4-methyl-indol-3-yl)methyl glucosinolate accumulated under all stresses. These findings enable targeted environmental strategies for quality improvement in Chinese kale.

title: Unraveling the flavor formation of White King pigeon eggs: Identification of signature volatile compounds and their lipid- and water-soluble precursors
abstract: This study presents the first systematic integration of gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS), lipidomics, and metabolomics to investigate the flavor profile and precursors of White King (WK) pigeon eggs. A total of 30 volatile compounds were identified, and a flavor wheel for WK eggs was constructed based on 20 key compounds. For the first time, hexadecanal (fabric- and wax-like) and allyl methyl sulfide (onion- and garlic-like) were identified as signature volatile compounds distinguishing WK eggs from Hy-Line Brown (HL) eggs. Integrated lipidomic and metabolomic analyses revealed lipid- and water-soluble precursors associated with these key volatile compounds. Correlation analysis between flavor compounds and precursors revealed the multidimensional basis of WK egg flavor formation. These findings provide a scientific foundation for the sensory evaluation of pigeon egg flavor quality and offer theoretical support for the development and industrial application of flavor modulation strategies in specialty poultry egg products.

title: Development of rapid-cooking red kidney beans via combined pretreatments: Insights into starch-driven mechanisms
abstract: This study investigated the development of rapid-cooking red kidney beans using a combination of pretreatments, including soaking, freezing, steaming, and microwave vacuum drying, with a focus on the starch-related mechanisms responsible for the reduced cooking time. The results revealed that freezing prior to microwave vacuum drying induced the formation of a uniform porous surface structure, which significantly improved water absorption during cooking and increased the degree of starch gelatinization from 9.58 % to 84.32 %. Starch structural analysis showed that the combined pretreatments caused more extensive disruption to starch granules than microwave vacuum drying alone, including the breakdown of crystalline and short-range ordered structures, exposure of hydrophilic groups, and enhanced water-holding capacity. These structural changes led to a significant reduction in gelatinization enthalpy (ΔH), making the cooking time of red kidney bean comparable to that of rice. This study raises valuable insights for the development of quality instant coarse grains.

title: Ultrasonic-assisted betalain extraction from red dragon fruit pulp (Hylocereus polyrhizus) using response surface methodology
abstract: Ultrasonic-assisted extraction (UAE) was employed for the maximum recovery of betalain pigment from red dragon fruit pulp using response surface variables as temperature (25-65 °C), extraction time (5-25 min), number of extractions (1-5), and solid/mass ratio (1:5-1:15 v/v). UAE at 25 kHz increased the betacyanin yield by 32 % i.e. 15.18-20.03 mg/100 ml and betaxanthin by 30 % i.e. 6.39-8.31 mg/100 ml in fresh dragon fruit pulp respectively. The central composite rotatable design was found to be best fitted with data having a higher R 2 (91 and 97 %), lower value of standard error and scattered plot. Maximum recovery of betalain pigment from pulp was obtained at 55 °C, 20 min, four extractions and 1:12.5 v/v because at higher temperature breakdown of compact tissues of fruit lead to the release of pigments and further increase in temperature (55 °C) can cause degradation of pigment. This study provides sustainable data for process design and industrial scale-up operations.

title: Identification of novel umami peptides with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects in spent hen protein hydrolysate
abstract: Spent hens, a major byproduct of the laying hen industry, were used to prepare umami peptides with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Among nine hydrolysates, the Protex 6 L-Thermoase product (SPH-6 L-T, 2 mg/mL) showed the strongest umami intensity, comparable to 10 mM monosodium glutamate. In HEK293 cells expressing the type I taste receptor TAS1R1, SPH-6 L-T, at 2 mg/mL, significantly increased intracellular Ca 2+ mobilization; in tumor necrosis factor α (TNFα)-stimulated endothelial cells, SPH-6 L-T, at 500 μg/mL, significantly reduced cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2) ( p = 0.0058) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) ( p = 0.0031). Peptidomics identified 1318 di−/tripeptides and 170 oligopeptides. Four peptides (AR, AQ, SKEGGKVT, ELEEEIEAE), all derived from myosin heavy chain, showed strong umami taste (0.2 mg/mL) and favorable docking to the TAS1R1 Venus flytrap domain. Two oligopeptides (5 mM) induced sustained Ca 2+ responses (> 5 min), and all four reduced ROS ( p < 0.0001); SKEGGKVT (50 μM) also significantly inhibited COX2 expression ( p = 0.018). These findings highlight spent hens as a good source of multifunctional umami peptides. • Spent hen hydrolysate (SPH-6 L-T), produced using Protex 6 L and Thermoase, exhibits both umami taste and bioactive properties. • SPH-6 L-T activates TAS1R1- and CaSR-mediated Ca 2+ mobilization. • Four peptides (AR, AQ, SKEGGKVT, and ELEEEIEAE) identified through peptidomics and molecular docking, demonstrated umami taste and antioxidant activity. • All four peptides triggered TAS1R1-mediated Ca 2+ mobilization.

title: Rice bran extract with α-glucosidase inhibitory activity: Preparation, in vitro evaluation and molecular mechanism
abstract: Rice bran peptides, effective against type 2 diabetes via α-glucosidase inhibition, face scalability challenges due to complex, costly preparation processes. Rice bran extract (RBE) with enhanced protein yield and α-glucosidase inhibitory activity was prepared by directly hydrolyzing defatted rice bran. The optimized conditions achieved a protein extraction yield of 53.52 ± 0.65 % and an IC₅₀ value of 3.45 ± 0.17 mg/mL. RBE exhibited competitive inhibition of α-glucosidase, with binding to the enzyme's active site. Fluorescence spectroscopy and infrared spectral analysis revealed that RBE induced static fluorescence quenching and altered the secondary structure of α-glucosidase, decreasing α-helix (9.684 %) and increasing β-sheet (45.377 %) content. Peptides GK-6 and KK-8 with low binding energy (-10.249 and -9.277 kcal/mol). Molecular docking revealed that GK-6 and KK-8 interacted with the active site of α-glucosidase through hydrogen bonding, inhibiting the glycosylation process between the enzyme and its substrate complexes. These findings highlight the potential of RBE as a natural α-glucosidase inhibitor, providing a theoretical basis for the development of RBE-based functional foods for regulating carbohydrate metabolism.

title: Cultured meat protein has significantly higher digestibility and more potential bioactive peptides than traditional animal and plant proteins
abstract: This study examined the protein digestion characteristics of cultured pork compared to traditional pork, soy, egg, whey, and casein. The results indicated that the cultured pork had higher protein digestibility during gastric stage (76.77 %) and intestinal stage (88.33 %) than other proteins. The proportion of peptides smaller than 3 kDa in the digestive products was the highest, confirming its efficient enzymatic hydrolysis characteristics. LC-MS/MS analysis identified 3626 peptides in gastric digesta and 1734 peptides in gastrointestinal digesta, exceeding the numbers of peptides in egg white, whey, and casein digesta. Importantly, more and higher abundance of bioactive peptides, total amino acid and essential amino acids were observed in cultured pork digesta. These differences were synergistically influenced by changes in the digestive system microenvironment and the structural characteristics of the proteins, which enhanced the accessibility of enzyme cleavage sites. The results may provide a theoretical foundation for precision nutrition design and industrial applications.

title: A new detection method for the long residual herbicide fomesafen based on the anti-immune complex peptide
abstract: Fomesafen, a diphenyl ether herbicide widely used for broadleaf weed control in soybean fields. Herbicide causes persistent soil pollution, damaging microorganisms and threatening agricultural products safety, necessitating rapid detection methods. This study employed phage display to identify 14 anti-immune complex peptides (AIcPs) targeting Fomesafen. The optimal peptide, AIcP-F21, enabled a highly sensitive noncompetitive enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) with an SC 50 of 0.45 ng/mL-3.5 times more sensitive than competitive ELISA. A phage-free AIcP-F21 was synthesized for noncompetitive lateral flow immunoassay (NLFIA) test strips, achieving a visual detection limit (vLOD) of 0.31 ng/mL. This represents an eight-fold sensitivity improvement over competitive methods. The assays demonstrated excellent specificity with no cross-reactivity to analogous compounds. Validation using spiked samples and real samples analysis yielded results consistent with UPLC-MS/MS, confirming reliability. The new noncompetitive immunoassay method developed in this study is of great significance for monitoring and evaluating the residues of fomesafen in the environment and agricultural products.

title: The effects of freshwater immersion on muscle qualities and the evaluation of water addition in Amphioctopus fangsiao (Mollusca: Cephalopoda) from the seafood market
abstract: Amphioctopus fangsiao is widely favored by Asian consumers for its high nutritional value and delicious taste, yet fraudulent water addition practices often dissatisfy consumers. This study evaluated its nutritional value, established baseline data for the moisture (80.33 ± 5.28 g/100 g) and protein content (16.47 ± 2.95 g/100 g) of raw samples, and elucidated the effects of freshwater immersion. The muscle of A. fangsiao contained abundant taurine. However, freshwater immersion stress increased the octopus's weight, with 5-h exposure identified as a critical point for weight change. Moreover, it induced severe oxidative stress, enhanced protein oxidation, and disrupted metabolites related to amino acid metabolism and glycolysis, thereby deteriorating key muscle quality indices, including pH level, water-holding capacity, and texture. Based on the baseline data, we further investigated and assessed water addition practices in market samples, highlighting the need to strengthen market supervision.

title: Multi-omics analyses unveil the molecular mechanism involving flavonoid-mediated color changes of different mango varieties
abstract: Mango, as a major tropical fruit, is deeply loved by consumers due to its unique color and flavor. Fruit color is one of the important quality traits that determine its nutritional and commercial value. There are significant differences in the peel color of mango germplasm resources. However, the reason for the color difference in fruits is still unclear. In this study, we selected 43 representative mango varieties from the National Mango Germplasm Resources Nursery. Through the evaluation of germplasm resources fruit peels of 43 mango varieties, combined with transcriptomics and metabolomics, it was found that flavonoids play a decisive role in the color changes of mango peel. Overexpression of MiMYB33 can alter the color of tomato fruits by promoting an increase in flavonoid content. This study provides important theoretical basis for the subsequent research on mango fruit color and the cultivation of mango varieties that meet market demand. • Color evaluation of 43 mango germplasm cultivars. • Flavonoids are responsible for the color differences of mango fruits. • Coumaroyl-CoA plays a decisive role in the color change of mango fruits. • MiMYB33 modulates tomato fruit coloration by regulating flavonoid content.

title: Development and application of fluorescent immunoassay lateral flow Technology for the Detection of Prolamins in food
abstract: Lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) are well-suited for large-scale screening and on-site testing due to their simplicity and low cost. However, most current prolamin LFIAs primarily detect gliadins, exhibit limited broad-spectrum detection of hordeins and secalins, and lack validation in processed barley and rye foods, raising concerns about their practical reliability. To address these issues, thermally stable prolamin fractions were screened under simulated thermal processing conditions for antibody production. Using quantum dot carbodiimide random labelling, a sandwich LFIA was established with visual detection limits of 0.5, 1, and 0.5 μg/mL for gliadins, hordeins, and secalins, respectively. The LFIA detected flour contamination as low as 5 mg/kg in all three model food matrices. These findings demonstrate that the developed LFIA serves as a practical tool for rapid on-site detection of gluten prolamins in processed and commercial food products.

title: Mechanistic insights into the improved emulsifying properties of sunflower meal protein following high-pressure processing-assisted limited enzymatic hydrolysis
abstract: Sunflower meal protein (SMP) has high nutritional value and application potential, but its natural form exhibits poor emulsification. This research examined the effect and mechanism of high-pressure processing-assisted limited enzymatic hydrolysis (HPP-LEH) treatment on SMP emulsification. The results showed that, compared to untreated SMP (control) and LEH-treated SMP, HPP 500-LEH-treated SMP exhibited smaller particle size, more exposed hydrophobic groups, a less rigid and more flexible structure, significantly increased contact angle, and lower interfacial tension, collectively contributing to a more viscoelastic interfacial film. Furthermore, HPP 500-LEH-treated SMP demonstrated enhanced emulsification capacity and emulsion stability, producing smaller and more uniform emulsions. Pearson correlation analyses revealed emulsification was positively correlated with conformational flexibility and contact angle, and negatively correlated with interfacial tension. In summary, moderate HPP-LEH treatment enhances the flexibility of SMP, increases the contact angle, and reduces interfacial tension, thereby improving its emulsification properties. This study provides new ideas for SMP application in food.

title: Spatial lipidomics profiling of Bottarga (Mugil cephalus) by LC–HRMS using a QTOF platform: A comprehensive characterization of complex lipid
abstract: Bottarga from Mugil cephalus , a traditional salted and cured roe, holds significant cultural and culinary value, yet detailed studies on lipid composition remain limited. This work provides an untargeted lipidomic analysis, comparing lipid distribution between inner and outer layers of bottarga. Using an LC–HRMS platform and advanced annotation tools, 592 complex lipids were identified. The inner layer showed higher levels of cardiolipins, phosphatidylcholines, phosphatidylethanolamines, and triacylglycerols, reflecting greater nutritional value and oxidative stability. In contrast, the outer layer contained more lysophospholipids, free fatty acids, and lipid degradation products, indicating oxidative processes likely caused by environmental exposure during salting and drying. These findings reveal how biological structure and traditional processing influence lipid profiles. Recognizing such spatial variations can support improved processing strategies, helping preserve nutritional and sensory properties while enhancing the valorization and standardization of this artisanal product. • UHPLC-QTOF-MS analysis revealed significant lipid differences in bottarga layers. • The inner layer showed high levels of complex phospholipids. • The outer layer showed lipid hydrolysis products such as FFAs and lysophospholipids.

title: Improving rice quality by enhancing key amylose and amylopectin and their complexation with fatty acids
abstract: Lower quality of Chinese rice didn't meet societal demand for high-quality rice. Optimizing starch characteristics (including complexation) enhances rice quality, but the impact of starch-fatty acid complexation remains unclear. Therefore, we used molecular dynamics simulations to explore amylose/amylopectin-fatty acids complexation to elucidate rice quality impact. Results showed that Northeast/East China rice achieved first-grade quality, whereas Central/South/Southwest China rice achieved second-grade. Further analysis revealed 10-40 degrees of polymerization (DP) amylose and 3/2 of A/B 1 -chains (3A2B 1 -type) amylopectin enhance structural stability (lower energy/root mean square fluctuation (RMSF)) by forming more compact structures (amylose ends/center, amylopectin 2B 1 -region), increasing head rice rate and breakdown value, and reducing chalkiness and retrogradation value. These starch structures preferentially complex with specific fatty acids (palmitic/stearic/oleic acid for 10-40 DP amylose, linoleic acid for 3A2B 1 -type amylopectin), further tightening their structures. Therefore, boosting 10-40 DP amylose, 3A2B 1 -type amylopectin, and their fatty acid complexes improves rice quality, providing a basis for optimization.

title: Elucidating the aging mechanism of Fuyu-flavor Baijiu mediated by metal ions via GC–MS, spectroscopy, electrochemistry, and SEM-EDS
abstract: Metal ions can promote the aging of Baijiu and improve its sensory quality. However, the aging mechanism mediated by metal ions remains unclear. The content of esters, alcohols, and pH decreased while the acids content, viscosity, and conductivity increased after adding metal ions. 20 kinds of aroma components were identified in Baijiu including esters, acids, alcohols, and aldehydes by Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Spectroscopy and electrochemical analysis demonstrated that Fe 3+ has a higher affinity than Cu 2+ for the flavor compounds, and both Fe 3+ and Cu 2+ exhibit stronger affinity with acids than corresponding esters. Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) demonstratesd that Baijiu can form lamellar, spherical, flower-like, and crystal-like morphology during aging. The colloidal particles exhibit different elemental composition according to Energy Dispersive Spectrometer (EDS). These results indicated Baijiu aging is regulated by transition metal ions, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for Baijiu aging by selecting appropriate aging medium and storage conditions.

title: Mechanisms of sweetness enhancement by sweet aroma compounds in black tea: More than just cross-modal interactions
abstract: Black tea contains sweet aroma compounds (SACs) with sweetening potential. However, a systematic understanding of their composition, enhancing effects, and underlying mechanisms is lacking. This study identified 14 key SACs in global sweet-aroma black teas using headspace solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Electronic tongue and sensory validation confirmed their sweetness-enhancing effects in a sugar-free black tea beverage and revealed their inherent taste properties (sweetness, astringency, pungency, and cooling). Molecular docking and dynamics simulation elucidated the stable bindings of T1R2/T1R3-benzeneacetaldehyde/β-damascenone, α-amylase-benzeneacetaldehyde, TRPV1-geraniol, and TRPM8-methyl salicylate, mediated by hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. These protein-ligand complexes were proposed to modulate sweetness, sweet aftertaste, heat-evoked sweetness, and cooling-enhanced sweetness, respectively. Consequently, this study demonstrates that SACs enhance sweetness through cross-modal interactions and inherent taste properties, providing novel mechanistic insights and actionable strategies for flavor optimization in tea beverages and other food products.

title: Light-exclusion bagging modulates phenylpropanoid metabolism to balance preharvest quality and postharvest granulation in ‘Sanhongmiyou’ pomelo
abstract: Light-exclusion bagging is a common practice for improving the appearance of fruit, however, its effects on internal quality and postharvest texture remain poorly understood. Using integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we demonstrated that bagging 'Sanhongmiyou' pomelo promoted sucrose and citric acid accumulation during development but suppressed key phenylpropanoid pathway genes. The pathway was activated postharvest, resulting in a 42.2 % increase in lignin content and severe juice sac granulation. We identified the MYB78/bHLH25/NUP58 transcriptional module as a putative regulator of lignin synthesis, with co-expression and promoter analyses suggesting its potential action through the synergistic regulation of cinnamate-4-hydroxylase and phenylalanine ammonia lyase genes. The present study provides mechanistic insights into how bagging affects fruit quality and proposes that the identified MYB78/bHLH25/NUP58 module could be a target for mitigating granulation by fine-tuning phenylpropanoid flux.

title: Applying superheated steam stabilized rice bran for improving physicochemical and quality properties of frozen dough and steamed bread
abstract: This study aims to reveal the influences of applying superheated steam stabilized rice bran (SRB) to improve the physicochemical characteristics of frozen dough and the quality of steamed bread. Adding SRB can increase the conversion of free water to bound water by up to 8.64 % and enhance the viscoelasticity of frozen dough. Adding 5 % of SRB increased the level of disulfide bonds therefore partially protect the integrity of the gluten network. Increasing of the added amount improved the water retention of the steamed bread during storage. In addition, the addition of SRB could substantially enhance the antioxidant properties of frozen dough and steamed bread, with a maximum improvement of 49.92 %. Results of this study elucidate the effects of adding highly stabilized rice bran on frozen dough and steamed bread quality and provide scientific information for quantifying the standardized amount of stabilized rice bran added into frozen dough.

title: Changes in rheological properties, gluten network, and protein fractions of dough induced by soy proteins-Glutenins crosslinking
abstract: Soy proteins are used as nutritional fortifiers in wheat flour to enhance the protein content of wheat-based products. This study found soy protein isolate (SPI), soy protein concentrate (SPC), and textured soy protein (TSP) increased dough development time, stability time, and viscoelastic modulus, yet disrupted the gluten network integrity. Disulfide bond-mediated interactions between soy proteins and glutenins competed with native gluten-gluten crosslinking, thereby weakening the gluten matrix. Notably, TSP exhibited minor gluten weakening, supported by fewer voids in dough microstructure, increased gluten contents and unextractable polymeric protein (40.9 %). A mechanistic model is proposed: SPI/SPC likely form intermolecular disulfide bonds that fragment the HMW-GS backbone and reduce molecular weight. Conversely, TSP may primarily undergo disulfide exchange with intramolecular bonds in HMW-GS, attaching as branched chains to the linear backbone and enhancing secondary structure stability. These findings advance the understanding of how different soy proteins interact with glutenins and influence dough properties.

title: Different polyphenols improve the gel properties by altering the crystal density of short- and long-chain acyl triacylglycerols oleogels
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of loaded natural polyphenols on the structure of short- and long-chain acyl triacylglycerols oleogels. In this study, five representative polyphenolic compounds, gallic acid (hydroxycinnamic acid), tannic acid (tannins), dihydromyricetin (dihydroflavonols), kaempferol (flavonols) and luteolin (flavones) were selected. The microstructural and macroscopic effects of different polyphenols on the oleogels were examined by polarized light microscopy, infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and rheometry. Oleogels loaded with the flavonol or the flavone showed increased oil binding capacity (2.12 % and 2.3 %, respectively) and hardness (0.23 N and 0.25 N, respectively), which corresponded to the formation of the strongest crystalline network structure with the highest crystal density and thermal stability. Additionally, all five polyphenols significantly improved the oxidative stability of the oleogels. Overall, flavones or flavonols were most effective in enhancing the properties of SLCT oleogels by increasing their crystal density and strengthening hydrogen bond forces.

title: Effects and mechanisms of colour protectants combined with ultrasound treatment on colour enhancement in hot-air-dried green peppers (Piper nigrum L.)
abstract: The effects and influence mechanisms of l-ascorbic acid (AsA), L-glutathione (GSH), and their combination with ultrasound (US) treatment on the colour of hot-air-dried green peppers were investigated. The 0.10 %AsA - US (180 W) treatment resulted in the most favourable appearance, with a ⁎ , ΔE ⁎ , and BD values significantly decreasing by 145.3 %, 85.1 %, and 32.2 %, respectively. Additionally, the retention rates of AsA and total polyphenols in this group reached 134.53 % and 115.63 %, significantly higher than those of the control. Moreover, 5,7-dihydroxy-3,4,5-trimethoxyflavone was the monophenol most strongly negatively correlated with ΔE ⁎ (R = -0.94), contributing to a colour more closely resembling that of fresh green peppers. Importantly, AsA reacts with oxygen to inhibit polyphenol autoxidation and acts as a reducing agent to decrease quinone accumulation, while GSH inhibits browning by forming stable adducts with quinones. These results provide a theoretical basis and technical support for the processing of green peppers.

title: Comparative analysis of degumming effects on the structural profiles and physicochemical properties of Idesia polycarpa phospholipids
abstract: Idesia polycarpa (I. polycarpa) oil by-products are rich in phospholipids (PLs), yet research on their composition and functionality remains limited. This study compared six degumming methods-hydration degumming (HD), acid degumming (AD), phospholipase A 1 degumming (PLA 1 D), simple phospholipase C degumming (SPLCD), deep phospholipase C degumming (DPLCD), and compound degumming (CD) -to evaluate their effects on PL characteristics. The results showed that enzymatic degumming methods, particularly CD, achieved the highest degumming rate of 94.7 %, significantly outperforming non-enzymatic methods. Lipidomic profiling revealed that all treatments resulted in phospholipids enriched with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), especially linoleic acid (C18:2). Enzymatic treatments produced PLs enriched in lysophosphatides, while non-enzymatic methods retained mostly intact phospholipids. These findings suggest that I. polycarpa oil by-products, particularly those treated by enzymatic degumming, can be a valuable and sustainable source of PUFA-rich phospholipids, with potential applications in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries.

title: Portable SERS-based lateral flow strip for simultaneous rapid detection of three typical corn mycotoxins
abstract: The co-occurrence of multiple mycotoxins in corn is prevalent, with synergistic toxicity exacerbating health risks for humans and animals. Three typical mycotoxins-aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), zearalenone (ZEN), and deoxynivalenol (DON)-require stringent monitoring due to their widespread contamination. A novel SERS-LFIA detection platform was developed employing Au-Ag core-shell nanostructures loaded with dual-layer Raman reporter molecules (Au MBA @Ag MBA NPs) as signal probes, combined with Au-IgG indicator probes. This platform achieved simultaneous detection of three mycotoxins in corn samples, with linear detection ranges of 0.5-30 μg/kg (AFB1), 10-1000 μg/kg (ZEN), and 50-2000 μg/kg (DON), respectively. Additionally, it showed 87.18 %-93.60 % coincidence rates with HPLC results in naturally contaminated corn samples. The developed SERS-LFIA strip exhibited superior performance characteristics, including rapid detection (20 min completion), enhanced sensitivity, and method accuracy, establishing its potential as an effective on-site screening tool for corn safety assurance.

title: A novel strategy for sodium reduction in salted goose: Employing basic amino acids to mitigate oxidation and improve sensory quality
abstract: High sodium intake poses health risks, highlighting the necessity for effective sodium reduction in meat processing. This study investigated the impact of basic amino acids (l-lysine, L-arginine, L-histidine) as flavor enhancers on the flavor of low-sodium salted goose. The combined use of KCl and basic amino acids achieved a sodium reduction of 36.51 %. Basic amino acids significantly inhibited lipid oxidation, reducing TBARS by up to 40.60 %, likely due to suppressed lipoxygenase activity (from 186.05 to 113.78 U/(min·g)). GC-MS analysis revealed that aldehydes and alcohols, the dominant volatile compounds, decreased by 15.07 % and 12.64 %, respectively, thereby mitigating undesirable odors. Intelligent sensory and quantitative descriptive analyses confirmed that basic amino acids effectively masked KCl-induced bitterness and astringency while enhancing saltiness and umami perception. This study demonstrates the flavor-improving effects of basic amino acids in low-sodium salted goose, providing a practical strategy for developing healthier, low-sodium meat products.

title: Decoding aroma perception of grilled lamb skewers: an EEG-MambaFusionNet framework integrating TDS and GC-IMS
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic evolution of aroma perception in grilled lamb skewers from raw to well-done stages and its corresponding neural signatures. Temporal Dominance of Sensations (TDS) and Gas Chromatography-Ion Mobility Spectrometry (GC-IMS) were integrated to capture sensory transitions from 'mutton-distinctive' to 'charcoal-roasted', 'fatty', 'grilling-meat' and finally 'burnt' aromas, along with associated volatile compound profiles. Concurrent electroencephalography (EEG) recordings showed that these aroma variations elicit distinct and progressively stronger neural responses. A critical time window was identified at 8-10 s post-inhalation, during which neural activity exhibited the highest discriminability across grilling stages. EEG-MambaFusionNet, a deep learning framework fusing neural, sensory, and chemical data, was developed to quantify this process, achieving a predictive accuracy of 0.925. Interpretation analysis indicated that prefrontal and parietal electrodes function as key hubs for hedonic and integrative aroma processing. These findings reveal the processing mechanism of brain for the aroma of grilled lamb skewers.

title: Selection of appropriate pore size covalent organic frameworks for efficient extraction bisphenol compounds in water and food samples
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with larger pore sizes will exhibit greater bisphenol adsorption capacity and faster adsorption rates than COFs with smaller pore sizes. Different por size will offer different binding affinity between magnetic COFs and BPs. Herein, four different pore sizes of magnetic COFs were prepared by grafting trialdehyde monomers with different numbers of benzene rings. The Fe 3 O 4 @TBrAPT-Dt-COF (3.0 nm) exhibited the best extraction effect towards BPs, which can be attributed to the larger pore of magnetic COFs eliminated the diffusion obstruction associated with small-pore molecules, leading to the enhanced absorption (141 mg g -1 ). Further increase in pore size weakened the binding affinity of magnetic COFs (32 mg g -1 ). The Fe 3 O 4 @TBrAPT-Dt-COF achieved 8 recycles in the process of absorption and desorption. This work first predictes the appropriate magnetic COFs pore size for BPs extraction and concurrently presents a new strategy for COF design for BPs removal.

title: Multi-network crosslinked plant-based hydrogels with enhanced mechanical performance for 3D-printed edible cartilage analogues
abstract: Biomimicking plant-based cartilage structures is essential for improving the texture of plant-based meat. This study developed a triple-crosslinked hydrogel using soy protein isolate (SPI), sodium alginate (SA), and curdlan (Cur) via transglutaminase (TGase) covalent crosslinking, Ca 2+ ionic crosslinking, and Cur thermal gelation. The optimized formulation (20 % SPI + 0.5 % SA + 2 % Cur) exhibited excellent rheological properties and 3D printing for precise fabrication of stable 3D structures. In this system, TGase catalyzed the formation of a flexible and stable covalent network, SA and Ca 2+ created a rigid ionic network for energy dissipation, and Cur formed triple helices upon heating, improving mechanical strength through hydrophobic interactions. SEM revealed a denser and more ordered microstructure compared to single-crosslinked hydrogels, supporting the synergistic reinforcement. These networks improved mechanical strength, texture, water retention, and freeze-thaw (FT) stability. The triple-crosslinked hydrogel showed significantly higher compressive modulus (339.7 ± 24.5 kPa), toughness (78.92 ± 4.24 mJ), hardness (60.8 ± 0.5 N), and chewiness (100 ± 7.2 mJ), closely resembling the structure and texture of chicken cartilage. This work provides a novel strategy combining multi-network crosslinking and 3D printing to develop functional cartilage analogues, offering theoretical and practical support for the design of plant-based connective tissues.

title: Selenium-enriched chickpea beverage powders: How particle size shapes composition and functionality
abstract: Sifting of extrudates powders obtained from germinated chickpea flour, with or without selenium biofortification, and with or without the addition of commercial fish oil increased the protein content and solubility. The fine powder with the highest protein content (23.63 g/100 g DW) was that of non-selenized germinated chickpea and fish oil. This formulation had a water solubility index (WSI) of 18.76 % that increased to 37.71 % after sifting. This formulation also had a lower content of rapid digestible starch (29 g/100 g) compared to germinated chickpea powders (33-36 g/100 g), except when selenized yeast (28 g/100 g) was used in the formulation. Only the germinated selenium-biofortified chickpea formulation without fish oil (SSWW) contained linoleic (C18:2 n-6) and linolenic acids (C18:3 n-3). Fine fractions had higher levels of glutamic (15.9 g/100 g DW) and aspartic acids (11.3 g/100 g DW), and arginine (8.2 g/100 g DW) that improved water solubility index.

title: Encapsulation of vitexin using calcium carbonate microparticles enhances stability, release, and anti-inflammatory activity in a plant-based food matrix
abstract: Vitexin, a C-glycosylated flavonoid with poor aqueous solubility and low bioaccessibility, was incorporated into a plant-based protein-rich matrix in free and encapsulated forms to evaluate its stability, release, and bioactivity. Calcium carbonate microparticles were used as encapsulation carriers. Formulations containing free vitexin, encapsulated vitexin, or wall material were assessed for their physical properties, phenolic profile changes during simulated digestion, and anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-induced HepG2 cells. Both free and encapsulated vitexin improved water retention and cohesiveness without significantly affecting shear force. Free vitexin increased yellowness and browning index. UHPLC-MS/MS analysis revealed changes in phenolic composition during digestion, with encapsulation significantly enhancing vitexin stability. The encapsulated vitexin formulation reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species and downregulated IL6, TNFα, and IL1β gene expression more effectively than free vitexin. These findings highlight the potential of calcium carbonate microparticle encapsulation to improve the digestive stability and functional efficacy of vitexin in complex food matrices.

title: Peel color as a predictive marker of phytochemical and metabolic diversity in Ficus carica L.
abstract: This study examines how peel color relates to fruit quality and metabolic diversity in 20 fig cultivars grown in arid northern Xinjiang, China. Morphological traits, physicochemical indicators, and untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-MS/MS) were integrated using multivariate statistical analyses (PCA and OPLS-DA) to assess chromatic-group differences. Purple cultivars had the highest antioxidant capacity (DPPH: 863.6μg TE/g; FRAP: 19.0μmol Fe 2+ /g), which showed a significant positive correlation with flavonoid accumulation (r>0.63,p 1, p<0.05), including Phe-Pro. Peel color was found to be strongly associated with distinct phytochemical profiles, highlighting coordinated pigment and secondary metabolism regulation. These results support breeding strategies for nutrient-enriched figs adapted to arid environments. Future research should verify postharvest stability and key biosynthetic pathways for functional applications.

title: A miniaturized emission spectrometer coupled with headspace injection for rapid and sensitive determination of nitrite in food samples
abstract: Nitrite (NO 2 - ) is widely present in foods and their production processes, and yet excessive intake can pose a serious threat to human health. Thus, it is crucial to develop sensitive methods for NO 2 - analysis, preferably offering low cost and on-site analytical capabilities. In this study, a miniaturized emission spectrometer was developed to determine NO 2 - by detecting the characteristic molecular emission spectrometry (MES) of N-containing NO at 237.0 nm, which was generated from the reaction between NO 2 - and potassium iodide. To improve sensitivity, an automated headspace injection sampling strategy was designed and coupled to the MES detection unit. The gaseous analyte of NO was produced and accumulated in the headspace bottle and then rapidly transported to the subsequent miniature array microplasma excitation source for emission spectrometric determination. Thus, the sensitivity of NO 2 - analysis was considerably improved, while the complex pretreatment steps and analytical time were reduced. Under optimal experimental conditions, the limit of detection was 3 μg L -1 , and the relative standard deviation was 3.8 % (for 0.1 mg L -1 , n = 9). The proposed method successfully detected NO 2 - in certified reference materials and real food samples, demonstrating its accuracy and reliability. Furthermore, the constructed device offers the additional advantages of compact size and structure, making it highly promising for rapid, on-site analysis of nitrite in food field.

title: Magnetic solid-phase extraction of organophosphorus pesticides in fruits and fruit juices using imidazolium-based poly(ionic liquid) modified montmorillonite
abstract: A novel magnetic imidazolium-based poly(ionic liquid)-modified homoionic montmorillonite (Fe 3 O 4 -ImPIL@MMT) adsorbent was synthesized and applied in magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) for detecting organophosphorus pesticides (OPPs) in fruit and fruit juice samples. Key extraction parameters were optimized to achieve excellent linearity (0.5-500 ng g -1 , R 2 = 0.995-0.999), low detection and quantification limits (0.01-0.73 and 0.04-2.28 ng g -1 ), and acceptable recoveries (69.0-111.9 %) with precision ranging from 0.3 % to 13.7 %. High enrichment factors (75-412) and minimal matrix effects (≤3 %) demonstrated strong selectivity toward OPPs. Tolclofos-methyl was detected in grape and grape juice samples (7.8 ng g -1 and 7.5-8.7 ng g -1 , respectively), while ethion was found in orange and grape juice samples (2.4 ng g -1 and 9.1-17.3 ng g -1 , respectively). The developed Fe 3 O 4 -ImPIL@MMT material exhibited significant potential as a simple, efficient, and green sorbent for sample pretreatment and pesticide residue monitoring.

title: Purification, characterization and membrane-disruptive antibacterial mechanism of a novel bacteriocin SCAY10 from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SCAY10
abstract: A novel bacteriocin SCAY10, was obtained from L.Plantarum through macroporous resin adsorption, cation exchange chromatography, gel filtration, and reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC). The molecular weight was determined to be 1763 Da, and the amino acid sequence was identified as ALIMTVVPLGQTQHAQA. SCAY10 retained 60 % activity at 120 °C, 65 % at pH 7 and 80 % of activity was preserved with protease treament. SCAY10 exhibited significant antibacterial activity against Micrococcus luteus, with the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) of 0.25 mg/mL. Scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM and TEM) revealed SCAY10 caused surface wrinkling and membrane perforations in M. luteus., Membrane potential measurements indicated membrane disruption, as evidenced by the exposure of a DisC2(5) fluorescent probe. Additionally, SCAY10 depleted intracellular ATP and induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, ultimately leading to bacterial cell death. These findings underscore SCAY10 as a promising antibacterial agent with potential for controlling spoilage in fermented foods.

title: Exploring the mechanism of dough mixing characteristics from the perspectives of protein content, solvent retention capacity, and protein interactions based on genotype, irrigation, storage, and mill streams
abstract: This study examined wheat protein properties and dough rheology across genotypes ('2 + 12' vs '5 + 10'), irrigation, storage, and mill streams. '5 + 10' genotype, no irrigation, and break flour showed higher protein and disulfide (SS) bonds but lower solvent retention capacity and gluten water holding capacity (WHC), reflecting enhanced pre-harvest covalent crosslinking. Storage at 4 °C without oxygen increased hydrogen bonds and gluten WHC while decreasing SS bonds compared to ambient storage with oxygen, indicating post-harvest non-covalent reassembly. Negative correlation was observed between hydrogen bonds and SS bonds. The S-S/hydrogen bonds ratio positively correlated with dough peak consistency/protein content (P < 0.01), while gluten WHC negatively correlated with mixing energy/dry gluten. The ratio of S-S/hydrogen bonds could characterize protein aggregation degree, offering mesoscale insights to explain dough rheology using protein interactions.

title: Single-molecule fluorescent probes for metal ion detection in food: From coordination mechanisms to real-world testing
abstract: Metal ion contamination in food poses severe health risks, necessitating rapid, sensitive, and selective detection strategies. Fluorescent probes have emerged as powerful tools for on-site monitoring due to their high sensitivity, structural tunability, and compatibility with complex food matrices. This review critically analyzes recent advances in fluorescent probes for food safety, focusing on photophysical modulation mechanisms such as photoinduced electron transfer (PET), intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), and chelation-enhanced fluorescence (CHEF). Detailed studies highlight probes for toxic (Ag + , Pb 2+ , Hg 2+ , Cd 2+ , Cr 6+ , Cu 2+ ) and essential (Zn 2+ , Fe 2+ , Al 3+ ) ions, incorporating DFT-based structural insights, binding stoichiometry, and practical applications in diverse food samples. Comparative evaluations identify structure relationships, synthetic design strategies, and performance determinants, concluding with a discussion on the most efficient and least effective systems. The review further outlines emerging trends, including smartphone-assisted sensing, NIR-emissive probes, and multi-analyte platforms, providing a roadmap for translating molecular designs into industrial-scale food safety solutions.

title: Green CuNA@Arg-Ce BioMOF with multi enzyme-like catalytic activities for self-cascade one-step colorimetric detection of zearalenone
abstract: Biomimetic cascade systems have emerged as effective tools for signal amplification in sensing. In this work, a self-cascade one-step operation biosensor for colorimetric detection of zearalenone (ZEN) was constructed based on a biological metal-organic framework (BioMOF) CuNA@Arg-Ce, which was synthesized via a green self-assembly strategy using natural molecules as eco-friendly ligands. CuNA@Arg-Ce exhibits integrated phosphatase-, laccase-, and catalase-like activities as a self-cascade catalyst that hydrolyzed disodium phenyl phosphate (PPDS) to phenol, followed by the oxidation with O 2 decomposed from H 2 O 2 and coupling with 4-aminoantipyrine to form red quinoneimine. ZEN selectively inhibited the phosphatase-like activity that generated a "signal-off" response. The rapid cascade biosensor exhibits a detection limit of 0.1568 μg L -1 with high selectivity and good performance in multiple grain samples. Additionally, a smartphone-based RGB analysis enables rapid on-site detection. This study provides a strategy for designing BioMOF composites as self-cascade catalysts and offers an green platform for practical mycotoxin monitoring.

title: Fabrication of pea protein isolate-folic acid conjugates via free radical grafting: Formation mechanism, stability, and curcumin delivery potential evaluation
abstract: Plant proteins are increasingly used to encapsulate hydrophobic nutrients to formulate functional foods. A major challenge for plant protein-based nanocarriers is to improve the solubility and stability, thereby enhancing the absorption efficiency and bioavailability of hydrophobic nutrients within them. To address this issue, a free radical grafting strategy of folic acid (FA) modified pea protein isolate (PPI) was developed. The FA loading capacity of PPI-FA conjugates was 2.1-fold higher than that of PPI-FA mixtures. Conjugation of FA improved the solubility, thermal stability and storage stability of PPI. The photostability of FA was also enhanced (retention rate increased from 75.76 % to 94.92 %). Complexation with PPI-FA conjugate elevated the solubility, anti-cancer activity and cellular uptake of curcumin (Cur). The bioavailability of PPI-FA-Cur was 63.27 %, far exceeding those of free Cur (6.95 %) and PPI-Cur (24.47 %). These findings expand PPI's application and provide new reference for the development of advanced food delivery systems.

title: Impact of storage and light exposure on the technological and phytochemical quality of yellow, black, and brown soybeans
abstract: Pigmented soybean varieties, such as black and brown, are rich in bioactive compounds, including isoflavones and phenolics, which exhibit antioxidant properties. This study evaluated yellow, brown, and black soybean grains stored for 12 months under light and dark conditions. During storage, acidity increased by up to 28 % and lipase activity by up to 45 % under light exposure, while soluble proteins decreased by 18-25 %, with smaller losses in black soybean. Free phenolics remained relatively stable across genotypes, but black soybean showed the highest levels of bound phenolics. Glycosylated isoflavones declined by 15-30 %, especially the malonyl derivatives, while aglycones, such as daidzein and genistein, remained stable and were detected only in black soybean. Genotype was the main determinant of compound stability, while storage time modulated losses, and light selectively accelerated degradation. Black soybean stands out as a promising source of bioactive compounds for functional foods.

title: Fractionation of plant proteins using deep eutectic solvents and high-pressure processing
abstract: Increasing demand for desirable plant protein ingredients necessitates efficient fractionation methods to process plant materials into functional fractions optimized for specific food applications. Deep eutectic solvents (DES) can interact with proteins and alter their physical characteristics for sub-fraction separation. Pea protein concentrate (PPC) was extracted using DES-water mixture (ChCl/glycerol, molar ratio of 1:2, 60 % hydration) with heat (100 °C, 15 min) or high-pressure processing (HPP) (600 MPa, 5 °C, 5 min). Proteins were precipitated using isoelectric or anti-solvent methods. The proteins extracted were characterized by their extraction efficiencies, structural and functional properties. DES caused pea proteins to separate into two fractions with distinct denaturation peaks. While protein content of most sub-fractions (58.27-97.60 %) were comparable or higher than that of conventional extraction methods, extraction yields were significantly lower. Anti-solvent precipitation yielded legumin-rich sub-fractions which could enhance specific food applications, such as meat and dairy alternatives.

title: Functional characterization of mpdh as a key dehydratase in citrinin biosynthesis in M. purpureus YY-1
abstract: Monascus spp., a traditional fermentation microorganism, produces natural pigments but also citrinin, a nephrotoxic mycotoxin. This study investigated the function of mpdh in M. purpureus YY-1, which encodes a dehydratase. Following fermentation, the Δmpdh strain exhibited increased biomass compared to the wild-type strain YY-1, along with a 79.3 % reduction in citrinin production and a 31.4 % decrease in Monascus azaphilone pigments (MonAzPs) yield. Transcriptomic analysis revealed downregulation of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) within the citrinin biosynthesis cluster, particularly those associated with polyketide synthase. The disruption of mpdh function altered key primary metabolic pathways, reducing acetyl-CoA levels and consequently impairing citrinin and MonAzPs biosynthesis. The redistribution of acetyl-CoA from secondary metabolism to energy metabolism for mycelial growth resulted in enhanced biomass in the Δmpdh strain. These results confirm that mpdh catalyzes the dehydration of Intermediate 6 to drive citrinin synthesis, establishing its pivotal role in the citrinin biosynthetic pathway.

title: Click chemistry-assisted hapten modification for enhanced immunoassay development: A promising strategy for clodinafop-propargyl detection in environmental and food samples
abstract: Clodinafop-propargyl (CP), a WHO Class III toxic herbicide, poses significant public health and environmental risks. This study presents a click chemistry-based hapten modification strategy to develop highly specific monoclonal antibody (mAb) for ultrasensitive CP immunoassay. Compared to conventional hapten synthesis methods, the click chemistry-derived hapten exhibited superior performance in indirect competitive ELISA (ic-ELISA), achieving a detection limit (LOD) of 5.6 pg mL -1 , an IC 50 of 171.4 pg mL -1 , and a broad dynamic range (IC 20 -IC 80 : 12.8 pg mL -1 -2.3 ng mL -1 ). The assay demonstrated high accuracy in detecting CP residues across water, soil, wheat, and meat samples, with intra- and inter-assay recoveries of 76.5-106.5 % and 75.5-109.5 %, respectively. Validation via HPLC-UV showed recoveries of 77.9-98.5 %, confirming method reliability. This approach highlights click chemistry as a robust tool for hapten design, enabling cost-effective, high-throughput, and ultrasensitive CP monitoring in environmental and food safety applications.
