title: Development of dimeric aptamers for highly specific recognition of patulin and a label-free fluorescence aptasensor with a thioflavin T probe
abstract: The directional design of multivalent aptamers significantly impacts the development of aptamer-mediated rapid detection methods. In this study, ten kinds of dimeric aptamers were designed using different flexible linkers. The dimeric aptamer of 1AS2 with the "A" base spacer demonstrated the best fluorescence activity and binding activity for patulin when combined with the fluorescence probe of thioflavin T (ThT). A label-free fluorescence aptasensor for patulin detection was developed based on the G-quadruplex/ThT platform using the dimeric aptamer of 1AS2. This fluorescence aptasensor had a wide detection range of 0.5-200.0 ng/mL for patulin within the operation time of 10 min and showed negligible cross-reactions with common mycotoxins. The assay exhibited good recoveries of 85.3 % ∼ 99.3 % in juice samples by the aptasensor, and the results were validated by HPLC analysis with good correlations. This study brings a new strategy for generating multivalent aptamers and label-free aptasensors for the accurate detection of food contaminants.

title: A smartphone-combined fluorescence sensor based on porous organic polymers for determination of nitrofurans in aquaculture system
abstract: In this study, a porous organic polymer (POP)-based fluorescent sensor (Tta-DHBTA) was synthesized from 4,4',4″-(1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl)triphenylamine (Tta) and 3,3'-dihydroxy-[1,1'-biphenyl]-4,4'-dialdehyde (DHBTA) for the detection of nitrofurans (NFs). The sensor operated via static quenching, exhibiting a fluorescence emission peak at 575 nm under 465 nm excitation, which decreased proportionally with increasing NF concentrations (0.5-50 mg/L), with a detection limit (LOD) of 0.302-0.524 mg/L. For real-time monitoring, the sensor was integrated with a smartphone application. Portability and field applicability were further enhanced using a DarkBoxUVAnalyzer to convert fluorescence changes into quantifiable signals, achieving LODs of 0.278-1.494 mg/L. Spiked recovery experiments in actual samples confirmed the reliability of both the Tta-DHBTA fluorescence method and the smartphone-assisted approach. This platform provides a promising strategy for rapid, on-site environmental monitoring and food safety screening.

title: Random forest-guided decoding of multiplex role of initial brine salinity in shaping dichotomous equilibrium of microbial assembly and flavor compound in liquid phase and solid phase of radish Paocai during fermentation
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of brine salinity (3 %, 6 %, 9 % and 18 %) on the dichotomous equilibrium of flavor compounds and microbial composition in the liquid and solid of radish Paocai during fermentation by incorporating non-metric multidimensional scaling analysis and random forest model. Results showed that salinity of 6 % and 9 % facilitated more balanced microbial distribution, whereas salinity of 3 % and 6 % promoted balanced accumulation of lactate, esters and aldehydes, and enhanced degradation of glucosinolates into sulfur-containing compounds. Random forest model indicated that diffusion of salt from liquid into solid drove microbial assembly via regulating response intensity of microbiota, especially dominant Kazachstania, Candida, Pediococcus and Lactiplantibacillus to salinity, contributing to divergent dichotomous equilibrium of flavor compounds of radish Paocai. This study provided understanding of the multiplex role of salinity in shaping the quality of fermented vegetable during dichotomous phase fermentation beyond regulating osmosis.

title: Effect of hydrocolloids on the textural, physicochemical and rheological properties of Bambara groundnut tofu
abstract: Bambara groundnut (BGN) is a protein-rich legume with potential for plant-based tofu production. This study explored the effects of coagulants (vinegar, lemon juice, and glucono delta-lactone [GDL]) and hydrocolloids (gum Arabic and sodium alginate at 0.3 %, 0.4 % and 0.5 %) on the quality of BGN tofu. Factorial design and response surface methodology identified the optimal formulation as 0.5 % gum Arabic and 0.5 % sodium alginate. Vinegar-tofu and GDL-tofu were lighter, firmer and more elastic, with vinegar-tofu exhibiting a smoother texture. Tofu containing hydrocolloids exhibited higher protein, ash, and carbohydrate content, and lower moisture. Microstructural analysis revealed uniform networks in vinegar-tofu and coarser textures in GDL-based samples. Rheological analysis showed shear-thickening behaviour, with the Power law model fitting the data adequately. Coagulant type and hydrocolloid addition significantly influenced texture, microstructure and physicochemical properties. These findings provide foundational data for future optimisation of BGN-based products and the role of hydrocolloids in improving tofu quality. • Bambara groundnut is a promising alternative for plant-based tofu. • Hydrocolloids enhance tofu's protein, ash and carbohydrates while reducing moisture. • Vinegar and gluconolactone coagulants improve colour and texture of tofu. • Coagulant and hydrocolloid types significantly affect tofu structure and properties.

title: Direct photoconjugation multi-wall carbon nanotube-based immunosensor platform for clenbuterol determination
abstract: This study reports the development of a carbon nanotube-based potentiometric sensor for the selective and cost-effective detection of clenbuterol. The sensor design depends on specific molecular recognition between clenbuterol and an anti-clenbuterol antibody covalently immobilized onto a photosensitive amino acid-modified multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) platform. This functional nanomaterial enabled the direct conjugation of the antibody-crosslinked electrode surface. An anti-clenbuterol antibody-bound MWCNT was used as the indicator electrode. An Ag/AgCl electrode was used as the reference electrode. The immunopotentiometric sensor exhibited a rapid response (1 min), a broad linear detection range from 1.0 × 10 -11 M to 1.0 × 10 -5 M, and an excellent low detection limit of 4.83 × 10 -12 M. The operational lifetime was extended to 36 weeks, with pH 6.0 identified as the optimal working condition. The proposed immunopotentiometric sensor offers high selectivity, low detection limits, cost-effectiveness, and label-free detection, making it a promising tool for clenbuterol monitoring.

title: Effects of adding L-cysteine on the accumulation of the main compounds and their new analogs in roasting Coffea arabica beans
abstract: Hazardous substances such as acrylamide (AA) are easily produced by the Maillard reaction during coffee roasting. By adding L-cysteine (L-Cys), the production of AA was inhibited whereas the profiles of the newly formed compounds remain unclear. To elucidate the influence of L-Cys addition on the main characteristic compounds of Yunnan Coffea arabica, investigations using LC-MSⁿ-IT-TOF, FTIR and assays of in vitro antioxidant and xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitory activities were carried out. The result revealed that the most characteristic compounds represented by the chlorogenic acid analogs (CGAs) were critical to hazards formation during the Maillard reaction. Adding L-Cys before roasting enhanced coffee quality by reducing harmful intermediates such as 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF) while increasing bio-potentials. New compound N6 which was formed by the addition of L-Cys and CGAs, together with the flavonoids generated through polymerization and simple phenols derived from thermal cleavage, were mainly contributed to the above potential.

title: Comprehensive review of fat replacers utilized in sausages: Classification, advantages, and applications
abstract: Sausages are a globally cherished food item due to their rich texture, distinctive flavor, and cultural significance. However, the high fat content in traditional sausages, particularly the elevated levels of saturated fatty acids, poses significant health risks, such as cardiovascular disease, obesity, and certain types of cancer. To address these challenges, fat replacers have been introduced as viable alternatives to maintain the sensory and structural properties of sausages while reducing fat and saturated fatty acid content. This review comprehensively examines the application of lipid-based, carbohydrate-based, and protein-based fat replacers in sausages, focusing on their physicochemical properties, sensory impact, antioxidant activity, microbiological safety, and biological effects. Recent advancements, including composite fat replacers and nanotechnology, have demonstrated promising potential in enhancing sausage quality and consumer acceptability. Despite these advancements, challenges remain in replicating the flavor and texture of traditional sausages and optimizing storage stability. This review provides theoretical insights and practical guidance for developing healthier sausage products, addressing the growing demands for low-fat and health-oriented foods.

title: Oxidative stability of flaxseed oil: effects of tocopherols, phytosterols and extraction conditions
abstract: Flaxseed oil is rich in α-linolenic acid and bioactive compounds but highly susceptible to oxidation. This study evaluated the oxidative stability of flaxseed oil obtained by different cold-pressing methods and supplemented with natural antioxidants-tocopherols and phytosterols. Preheating flaxseeds (80 °C, 2 h) and double pressing improved oil yield and stability through a synergistic interaction between γ-tocopherol and co-extracted phenolics. γ-Tocopherol scavenges lipid peroxyl radicals, while phenolics donate hydrogen atoms and regenerate active γ-tocopherol, enhancing antioxidant capacity. TP supplementation exhibited a temperature-dependent behavior: high α-tocopherol levels showed a transient pro-oxidant effect at low temperatures but contributed to stabilization at moderate and high temperatures through γ-tocopherol persistence. Conversely, PS consistently improved oxidative stability by disrupting the autoxidation chain and stabilizing lipid radicals. The combined use of tocopherols and phytosterols achieved the most effective protection, providing mechanistic insight for developing stable PUFA-rich formulations.

title: Insight into the shell discoloration on black tiger shrimp (Penaeus monodon) induced by water change under frozen storage
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the shell discoloration on Penaeus monodon during frozen storage. The results showed that the L* and b* values increased significantly during frozen storage, while the color difference decreased significantly. After 30 days of frozen storage, the water content decreased significantly from initial 55.65 % ± 1.19 to 37.04 % ± 1.50, and the centrifugal loss increased significantly to 22.64 % ± 0.78. The relaxation time of bound water and free water increased, and the content of immobilized water and free water fluctuated. In addition, the activity of polyphenol oxidase, the total sulfhydryl content, and the Ca 2+ -ATPase activity decreased significantly after frozen storage, whereas the MDA and carbonyl contents increased significantly. There was a significant correlation between the change in shell color difference and water content. Hence, the water change is identified as the key factor contributing to shell discoloration.

title: Insight into the antioxidant mechanism of astaxanthin geometric isomers by quantum chemical calculations and molecular simulations
abstract: Astaxanthin (Asta) demonstrates structure-dependent antioxidant efficacy, with geometric isomers differing significantly. This study elucidated the antioxidant mechanisms of three Asta isomers and proposed a novel 1 O 2 quenching mechanism. 9-cis Asta outperformed 13-cis Asta in free radical scavenging, with both outperforming the all-trans Asta. Density functional theory analysis confirmed stronger chemical activity of 9-cis and 13-cis Asta by ΔE LUMO-HOMO , which were 22.01 % and 15.92 % lower than that of all-trans Asta, respectively. Bond length and reduced density gradient analyses confirmed these findings. The cis isomers also demonstrated a stronger single-electron transfer capability. The 1 O 2 quenching ability of 9-cis Asta was 1.27 and 1.49 times than those of 13-cis and all-trans Asta, and it had doubled binding sites for 1 O 2 and higher lowest unoccupied molecular orbital electron density. Especially, it formed a unique hydrogen bond with Arg483 of Keap1. These findings comprehensively explain Asta's antioxidant mechanism based on its geometric isomers.

title: Unlocking the impact of fusarium isolates in infected potato tubers by biochemical profiling, volatile emissions and elemental shifts
abstract: A study was conducted to explore the effect of fusarium infection in potato through physical, biochemical, and phytochemical profiling. For this, potato tubers were inoculated with Fusarium spp. and analyzed after 30 d for physical and phytochemical changes using standard biochemical assays and colorimetric measurements. Results revealed a decrease in total solids and density with increasing physiological weight loss with time. Infected tubers exhibited lower lightness, increased redness, and greater yellowness. Titrable acidity total soluble sugars and reducing sugars increased too. Starch content declined while polyphenolic, flavonoids, carotenoids total antioxidant activity, and free amino acids increased. FTIR and GC-MS/MS analysis showed potential shifts in chemical bonds and volatile components due to infection. Moreover, the correlation analysis revealed strong associations among physical and biochemical parameters, highlighting the metabolic adjustments in response to Fusarium infection. The findings offer potential biomarkers for early detection and management of Fusarium-induced tuber dry rot in potato storage and supply chains.

title: Surface-active ionic liquid/SDS-based supramolecular solvent microextraction for separation and enrichment of sulfonylurea hypoglycemic drugs prohibited in health food
abstract: The illegal addition of drugs to health foods posed significant risks to consumer safety, prompting an urgent need for reliable monitoring methods. A simple, green, efficient dual-surfactant supramolecular solvent dispersion liquid-liquid microextraction coupled with high performance liquid chromatography (SUPRAS-DLLME-HPLC) method was developed to determine four sulfonylurea hypoglycemic drugs (glibenclamide, gliclazide, glimepiride, gliquidone) in health food. A low-viscosity, high-density supramolecular solvent (SUPRAS) was prepared from 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) by vortex-assisted two-step self-assembly. The incorporation of SDS into [BMIM][TFSI] significantly enhanced the SUPRAS extraction efficiency, and the surface morphology, microstructure, and physicochemical properties of SUPRAS were subsequently characterized. The four analytes showed good linearity (R 2 > 0.9994) in the range of 7.8-2000 μg kg -1 , with limits of detection and limits of quantification of 1.14-2.40 μg kg -1 and 3.82-8.03 μg kg -1 , respectively. The present method provided a practical and green solution for identifying illegal additives in health food.

title: Effect of grape ripeness, alcohol content, and maceration duration on phenolic content and composition of cabernet sauvignon wines
abstract: Cabernet Sauvignon grapes were harvested at three different maturities (unripe, ripe, overripe, represented by Harvest 1, 2 and 3) and used for winemaking, adjusting total soluble solids of each harvest to three concentrations (~11 %, 14 %, and 16.5 % alcohol) and then subjected to either 10 or 240 days extended maceration (Control and EM). Phenolic compounds in both wines and grapes were measured with multiple methods (protein precipitation, phloroglucinolysis, UHPLC-MS-Q-ToF). Protein precipitable tannins significantly increased with the EM treatment, while alcohol only increased their extraction in the EM wines. Both Harvest 1 and EM wines showed higher seed extraction according to tannin size and composition. Harvest 1 presented higher protein precipitable tannin content in the grape seeds and skins, but did not increase the tannin content in the wine. Anthocyanins and Tannin-Anthocyanin Adducts were characteristic of the Control wines, while Flavanyl pyranoanthocyanins and aldehyde-bridged flavan-3-ol-anthocyanins were prevalent in the EM wines. • Maceration time and alcohol were crucial factors to alter tannin concentration. • Grape ripeness altered wine tannin size and composition, but not tannin content. • There was no relationship between grape and wine tannin content and composition.

title: Construction of a multilayer perceptron based intelligent platform for dynamic quality monitoring and shelf-life prediction of bivalves
abstract: Bivalves, due to their high water and protein content, are prone to spoilage reactions. Traditional shelf-life prediction methods have the drawbacks of being destructive and time-consuming. This study measured total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARs), total viable count (TVC), and color and electronic nose changes of five types of bivalves (Ostreidae, Ruditapes philippinarum, Farrer's Scallop, Sinonovacula constricta, Mytilus galloprovincialis) under different storage temperatures (25 °C, 4 °C, -18 °C). This study established: (1) a shelf-life prediction model, with the above indicators as input and the shelf life as output; (2) quality prediction models, focusing on TBARs and TVB-N. Particularly, TVB-N could be directly output by inputting the electronic nose. All models demonstrated excellent performance, with R 2 values exceeding 0.90 and average absolute error less than 0.50. This study aims to provide scientific basis for water product quality control and reduction of supply chain losses.

title: Constructing rice grain–dotted accordion-like TB–COF@NH₂–MXene to promote the simultaneous efficient elimination and sensitive detection of benzophenones
abstract: The excessive accumulation of benzophenone (BP) endocrine disruptors highlights the need to develop novel materials capable of efficient removal and precise, simultaneous monitoring of multiple BPs. Based on the characteristics of BPs, an accordion-like NH 2 -MXene-based composite material with rice grain-like 1,3,5-tris(4-aminophenyl)-benzene-1,3,5-benzenetricarbaldehyde covalent organic frameworks (TB-COF) on its surface after modification (TB-COF@NH 2 -MXene) was developed. The obtained TB-COF@NH 2 -MXene exhibited rich functional groups, an appropriate pore structure and suitable surface properties. Moreover, it exhibited a high saturation adsorption capacity (292.47-316.23 mg g -1 ), rapid kinetics (25 min) and excellent dynamic adsorption ability (1359-2548 BV). It demonstrated good selectivity and an excellent ability to capture BPs at low concentrations. Notably, dispersive solid-phase extraction based on TB-COF@NH 2 -MXene in combination with high-performance liquid chromatography-diode array detector enabled the simultaneous detection of trace BPs in river water, cookies, vermicelli, milk, coffee, tea and infant formula samples. This study provided practical guidance on environmental and food safety solutions.

title: Partially gelatinized extruded yam starch improves wheat dough rheology and microstructure through enhanced interactions with the gluten network
abstract: Although previous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of extrusion in starch modification, the mechanism by which changes in the degree of gelatinization (DG) influence the physicochemical properties of starch and its subsequent functionality in the dough system remains poorly understood. This study produced yam starches with different DGs (10.47 %, 35.79 %, 69.58 %, 96.58 %) using a twin-screw extruder under different temperatures (80, 90, and 100 °C), and water contents (30 %, 45 %, and 60 %), and systematically investigated the effect of DG on the microstructure and rheological properties of wheat dough. Results showed that increasing DG improved the hydration properties of yam starch, as evidenced by a higher water absorption index, water solubility index, and swelling power. These improvements were attributed to the disruption of the long- and short-range ordered structures of starch, leading to reduced relative crystallinity. Concurrently, structural modifications led to an increase in the mean particle size (D 4,3 ) and accelerated thermal decomposition. When incorporated into wheat dough, the functional effect of yam starch depended on its DG. Partially gelatinized starch (DG = 69.58 %) significantly increased the storage and loss modulus, indicating improved dough viscoelasticity. SEM and CLSM observations revealed that partially gelatinized starch granules integrated tightly within the gluten matrix, forming a continuous composite network that enhanced the dough's resistance to deformation. However, fully gelatinized starch (DG = 96.58 %) disrupted gluten network continuity through intense water competition, resulting in a significant decrease in dough stability time. Overall, this study elucidates the mechanism by which extrusion-induced changes in the DG of yam starch affect its physicochemical characteristics and functional performance in wheat dough, providing theoretical guidance for developing yam starch as a functional ingredient for improving dough quality through extrusion technology.

title: Hetero-molecular junction promoted electrochemiluminescence of porphyrin-based hydrogen-bonded organic framework for antibiotic resistance gene assay
abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) pose a significant threat to food safety and human health, underscoring the urgent need for their sensitive and convenient detection. Herein, a "switch-on" electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor is fabricated based on the heterogenized porphyrinic hydrogen-bonded organic framework (PFC-45) as the ECL luminophor and ZnO as the co-reactant accelerator for tetracycline resistant gene (tetA) assay. The hetero-ligand PFC-45 effectively performs an intrareticular charge transfer and suppresses aggregation-caused quenching, showing 2.5- and 101.5-fold higher ECL intensity in aqueous solution than that of mono-ligand 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-carboxyphenyl) porphine (TCPP) and 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-pyridyl) porphine (TPyP)-based HOF. Combined with Exonuclease III-assisted target recycling amplification, the proposed biosensor achieves a good specificity and sensitivity for tetA detection with a low detection limit of 65.02 fM. This work expands the application of mixed-ligand porphyrin-based HOFs in ECL sensing and establishes a generalizable paradigm for monitoring antibiotic resistance through target-driven nucleic acid signal amplification.

title: Triple cascade response mediated “transparent-tough” protein-polysaccharide gel network: Focusing on optical characteristics and mechanical properties
abstract: This study constructed transparent soy protein isolate (SPI) - hyaluronic acid (HA) gels through a triple-cascade strategy involving fermentation, deamidation, and decolorization, while elucidating the intrinsic relationship between transparency and mechanical strength. Characterization of SPI transparency revealed that the triple-cascade treated SPI achieved a decolorization efficiency of 89.53 % and reduced crystallinity to 11.26 %, with the <10 kDa fraction increasing from 8.20 % to 19.62 %. Upon thermal gelation, the 2.0 % SPIHA gel (FSH-2.0) exhibited a hardness surge (4.83 to 11.71). Rheological analysis demonstrated that FSH-2.0 reached the highest critical strain, with viscosity sharply increasing from 193.5 Pa·s to 402.4 Pa·s and yield stress peaking at 638.3 Pa. Microstructural quantification further confirmed FSH-2.0's high crosslinking density and low topological defects, evidenced by its elevated fractal dimension and reduced lacunarity. This work will provide critical theoretical insights for the rational design of plant protein-polysaccharide gels simultaneously achieving high transparency and mechanical robustness.

title: Photochemical glyoxylic acid production in white wine: Impact of light sources and ethanol concentrations
abstract: Exposing wine to light can cause photooxidation of tartaric acid to form glyoxylic acid, leading to detrimental wine development. The impacts of different light sources and the presence of ethanol on photochemical glyoxylic acid production in wine are unknown. A tartrate-buffer solution and commercially de-alcoholised Chardonnay, adjusted to different ethanol concentrations (0-12 % (v/v)), were exposed to three commonly used light sources for 1-2 weeks. The highest glyoxylic acid accumulation occurred under cool-white fluorescent lighting, followed by cool-white light-emitting diode (LED) and then yellow LED, which is consistent with increased emission intensities at wavelengths below 500 nm, especially those nearest to 340 nm. The presence of ethanol accelerated glyoxylic acid production but lowered the contribution of glyoxylic acid-derived spoilage pigments to wine colour. Of the light sources studied, yellow LED lighting produced the least photooxidative production of glyoxylic acid in white wine.

title: Provenance profiling: SN- and LA-ICP-MS based authentication of strawberries
abstract: Depending on their origin, strawberries can vary greatly in price. For example, fruit from Germany may be costly compared to imported goods, encouraging financially motivated food fraud. In this study, two different sample preparation techniques - acid digestion and laser ablation - were applied to determine the provenance of strawberries using ICP-MS and multivariate data analysis. 403 samples from six countries (Egypt, Germany, Greece, the Netherlands, Poland and Spain) were used to develop classification models. German and imported strawberries were distinguished with an accuracy of 91.7 % using solution nebulization. Strawberry seeds were identified as optimal matrix for the alternative laser ablation method. With laser ablation, a two-class classification model with an accuracy of 88.0 ± 12.1 % provided the best result. The classical SN-ICP-MS provides a very good classification result; however, it requires more reagents and time compared to the innovative and resource-efficient LA-ICP-MS, making it a realistic tool for food fraud detection.

title: Analysis of phenomics, metabolomics and transcriptomics reveals the differences in fruit quality between on-tree bagged and non-bagged apples
abstract: This study systematically elucidated the differences in fruit quality between bagged and non-bagged apples by integrating phenomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics. Significant variations were observed between the two groups in peel color, single fruit weight, epidermal cells, collenchyma, cuticular wax, peel hardness, peel toughness, flesh hardness, and flavor. The content of volatile compounds, represented by 26 key aroma metabolites, was significantly higher in non-bagged fruits than in bagged ones. Compared to bagged fruits, non-bagged fruits exhibited elevated soluble sugar levels (e.g., sorbitol), accompanied by a minor increase in organic acids. In contrast, bagged fruits accumulated higher levels of free amino acids (e.g., asparagine) and their metabolites. Spatial distribution maps for L-asparagine, L-aspartate, L-glutamine, L-glutamate, sorbitol, sucrose, fructose, glucose, and malic acid in fruits were generated via mass spectrometry imaging. Furthermore, key candidate genes potentially responsible for the differential accumulation of amino acids, sugars, volatile compounds, wax, and cellulose were screened.

title: AI for food chemistry: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled efficient analysis methods and applications in food chemistry
Optimizing oxidative stability of Camellia oleifera seed oil: Multimodal analysis of antioxidant efficacy, tocopherol loss, benzo[a]pyrene suppression, and kinetic mechanisms
abstract: Camellia oleifera seed oil (COSO) is highly susceptible to thermo-oxidative degradation due to its high content of unsaturated fatty acids, leading to nutrient loss and carcinogenic benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) formation. In this study, we employed a multimodal approach (Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, FTIR; electron paramagnetic resonance, EPR; oxidation kinetics, α-tocopherol and BaP monitoring) to systematically compare four antioxidants (PG, TBHQ, BHT, VE) at industrially relevant concentrations. Results showed that TBHQ (0.2 g/kg) and PG (0.1 g/kg) optimally preserved α-tocopherols (6.70/4.58 mg/kg) and minimized BaP (1.40/1.46 μg/kg) during 15-day oxidation. FTIR revealed preferential stabilization of CH, cis-C=C, and CO bonds, while EPR confirmed superoxide radical (•O₂ - ) quenching via HAT/SET mechanisms. Kinetic analysis indicated higher activation energies for TBHQ (126.60 kJ/mol) and PG (92.63 kJ/mol), confirming enhanced stability. Mechanistically, TBHQ and PG function via phenolic hydroxyl H-transfer and quinonoid transformation. PG is a low-toxicity alternative to TBHQ for COSO stabilization.

title: Solvent-free one-step mechanochemical synthesis of magnetic graphene composite adsorbent for efficient removal of multiple aflatoxins in vegetable oils
abstract: Aflatoxin-contaminated vegetable oils pose severe threats to human health. Although magnetic graphene-based materials can be used for aflatoxins (AFs) removal, their current preparation methods involve complex, multi-step procedures and are time-consuming. Herein, we proposed a simple, efficient and solvent-free mechanochemical approach for one-step synthesis of magnetic graphene composite (MGC) directly from graphite and Fe 3 O 4 . The MGC was used as an adsorbent to remove four AFs from vegetable oils, and the adsorption mechanism was further explored by conducting batch adsorption experiments. The results demonstrated that MGC could simultaneously remove 85.8-100 % of AFs from 13 types of oils within 60 min at 30 °C. The detoxification process exhibited low cytotoxicity towards HepG2 cells, and has little effect on the quality of oils. Thus, MGC exhibited promising application potential for vegetable oil detoxification in food industry due to its facile scalable production, efficient detoxification capability, good biosafety, and easy recovery and regeneration.

title: Metabolomic insights into the impact of cooking technologies on plant-based burger composition
abstract: This study evaluated the impact of different cooking methods (air frying, grilling, oven baking, and microwave cooking) on the metabolite profile of chickpea-based burgers using untargeted metabolomics. The results revealed that the primary source of variation was the thermal treatment, with raw samples clearly separating from cooked ones. Notably, heat-sensitive compounds such as lipids and several flavonoids were degraded across all cooking methods. In contrast, some phenolic acids (caffeic acid and hydroxycinnamic acid) and flavonoids (apigenin, luteolin, apigenin-7-apioglucoside, and apigenin-7-O-glucoside) increased after cooking. Among the evaluated techniques, grilling induced the most pronounced metabolic alterations compared to raw samples, whereas microwave cooking had the least impact, showing better preservation of certain lipids and phenolic compounds. These findings demonstrate that cooking methods can significantly modulate the metabolomic composition of plant-based products, with microwave cooking standing out as the gentlest approach for maintaining nutritional quality.

title: Comparative evaluation of nutritional quality and flavor characteristics for Acrossocheilus fasciatus muscle in different aquaculture systems
abstract: This study comparatively evaluated the effects of four aquaculture systems pond (PD), rice field (RF), round bucket (RB) and water trough (WT) on the flesh quality, gut microbiota and metabolites of Acrossocheilus fasciatus. Compared with the other three groups, texture analysis revealed that the RF group exhibited significantly higher hardness and chewiness (P < 0.05), the highest content of umami amino acids, relatively high levels of flavor compounds (alcohols and esters), and significantly higher polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content, particularly rich in eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA). Additionally, metabolomics and gut microbiota analyses showed that compared with the other three groups, the RF group had significantly higher contents of beneficial metabolites and bacterial genera, enhancing flavor and nutritional value by regulating amino acids, fatty acids, and volatile flavor compounds.These findings highlight the potential of RF in improving fish quality and elucidating metabolomic and microbial mechanisms, providing theoretical support for ecological aquaculture.

title: Identification of protein markers of muscle fibre type and ageing progress in beef cutaneous trunci and masseter
abstract: This study aimed to identify protein markers for fibre type, and extent of post-mortem proteolysis, in bovine cutaneous trunci and masseter , which represent very different muscles types. We applied mass-spectrometry-based proteomic techniques to analysis of muscle fibre type and, examined temporal proteolysis changes with post-mortem ageing. Global proteomic analysis was performed on fresh beef masseter (high type-I fibres) and cutaneous trunci (high type-II fibres). The profile of semi-tryptic peptides, before and after ageing, was analysed to quantify protein degradation extent. Progression of proteolysis in type-I and type-II muscles was indicated by semi-tryptic peptides derived from heat-shock-protein 27, and troponin T fast skeletal muscle, respectively. The content of type I fibres in beef could be estimated using the abundance of myosin light chain-3, and enzymes involved in glycolysis could indicate the content of type II fibres. These markers could be used in the supply chain to monitor and improve beef quality. • Muscle type influenced the proteolysis in beef during postmortem ageing. • Heat-shock proteins indicate proteolysis progression in beef high in type I fibres. • Troponin T indicates proteolysis progression in beef high in type II fibres. • Beef proteome varied extensively with fibre-type composition. • Myosin light chain-3 could indicate the content of type I fibres in beef.

title: Molecular modifications of myofibrillar proteins in structural transitions induced by plasma-activated water rinsing: A proteomic insight
abstract: Plasma-activated water (PAW) was generated by cold plasma treatment for 2 to 10 min and used to rinse bighead carp mince replacing deionized water during surimi preparation. The effects of PAW rinsing on myofibrillar proteins (MP) were investigated across three structural states: native MP, salt solubilized MP (MP sols), and thermal MP gels. In native MP, PAW rinsing induced oxidative modifications, as shown by a 39.13 % increase in carbonyl content and a decrease in sulfhydryl groups (P < 0.05). Proteomic analysis revealed myosin heavy chain as the principal oxidation target (48.84 %), particularly in the C-terminal region, with mono-oxidized Lys and Arg residues. In MP sols, PAW increased surface hydrophobicity (27.14 %) and reduced sulfhydryl content, enhancing protein rigidity and gel stability. The reduction of sulfhydryl groups restricted chain flexibility but promoted tail-region aggregation, contributing to a stable gel network in MP gels. These findings demonstrate PAW's potential to improve surimi production.

title: Sensitive detection of pyrethroid pesticides in vegetables using COF-functionalized magnetic nanocomposites: Enrichment, mechanism, and quantification
abstract: In this work, covalent organic framework (COF)-derived magnetic nanocomposites (Fe 3 O 4 @PDA@COF TABP ), comprising Fe 3 O 4 as the magnetic core, polydopamine (PDA) as the hydrophilic interlayer, and COF TABP as the outer shell, were first constructed and utilized as the powerful adsorbents for the magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) of pyrethroids (PYRs). The introduction of the PDA coating facilitated the growth of the COF TABP shell and simultaneously provided additional adsorption sites, thereby enhancing the extraction efficiency. Molecular docking simulations revealed that Fe 3 O 4 @PDA@COF TABP exhibited excellent affinity toward PYRs through synergistic π-π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and hydrophobic interactions. The developed MSPE method coupled with GC-μECD exhibited excellent linearity (R 2 ≥ 0.9988), low limits of detection (0.025-0.064 μg kg -1 ), satisfactory recoveries (82.4 %-106.8 %), and low relative standard deviations (RSDs <7.1 %). Finally, the established method was successfully applied to the quantification of trace PYRs in vegetable samples, demonstrating its strong potential for routine pesticide residue monitoring in vegetables.

title: Phytochemical profiling and antioxidant activity of ethanolic extracts from thinned immature ‘Shiranuhi’ mandarin peels and their effects on rapeseed oil stability
abstract: Phenolic composition and antioxidant activity of ethanol extracts from peels of 'Shiranuhi' mandarin at seven maturity stages were analyzed. Non-targeted UHPLC-MS/MS identified 1492 compounds, with phenolics accounting for 75.90 %-86.62 % of metabolites. Antioxidant capacity increased with fruit maturity, peaking at YF2, and then declined. Flavonoids were the dominant phenolic compounds, and lipophilic flavonoids such as hesperetin, naringenin, and demethylnobiletin showed strong correlations with oxidative stability (R > 0.50, p < 0.05). At 28 days of accelerated storage, TOTOX inhibition by YF2 extract reached 18.79 %, indicating high oxidative suppression. Lipophilic flavonoids played a key role in enhancing oil stability by inhibiting lipid peroxidation. Although TBHQ exhibited stronger protection, natural extracts offered safety advantages. Increasing concentration or purity, or combining with synthetic antioxidants, may optimize their application. Thinned immature citrus peel is rich in antioxidant compounds, highlighting its potential as a natural antioxidant source and a sustainable strategy for by-product utilization.

title: Synthetic biology for sustainable food colourant production: Innovations and opportunities
abstract: Natural healthy food colourants are increasingly demanded to replace synthetic ones which are linked to public health concerns. Although nature provides a rich palette of colours, producing food colourants from food crops or specific agricultural products can exacerbate food security issues and environmental challenges, such as deforestation driven by the expansion of farmland. Synthetic biology offers promising solutions to address the supply limitations of natural food colourants through developing colour-enriched plant varieties and particularly, high-yield microbial cell factories for production through precision fermentation. For the efficient translation of microbial fermentation solutions, it is important to integrate interdisciplinary synthetic/engineering biology research platforms, ranging from AI-assisted biological design to streamlined strain engineering workflows, and systems biology facilities, to address production challenges for scaling up. Bridging the lab-to-market gap through innovative economics and legality mechanism can accelerates the industrialisation of sustainable natural food colourants.

title: Functional characterisation of traditional Andean freeze-sun dried potato derivatives, Chuño and Tunta: Resistant starch, probiotic fermentation, and production of SCFA and GABA as bioactive metabolites
abstract: Chuño (black) and tunta (white) are two ancient potato derivatives traditionally produced in the high-altitude Andean region through a natural freezing, pressing, washing, and sun-drying process that preserves the tubers for long-term storage. The present study investigates the resistant starch (RS) content, antioxidant capacity, and bioactive metabolites produced by fermentation with probiotic bacteria. The RS content in dry matter chuño (52.63 g/100 g) and tunta (46.39 g/100 g) was found to be higher than that in native potatoes (36.66 g/100 g). The fermentation with Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus, Lacticaseibacillus casei, Levilactobacillus brevis, and Propionibacterium freudenreichii resulted in the production of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). The chuño fermentation process was found to yield higher levels of SCFA and GABA. These properties provide an additional functional property to chuño, which also has an interesting amino acid profile and protein content. These findings establish a foundation for incorporating Andean potato derivatives into functional food formulations. • Freeze and sun-drying processes increase the resistant starch content in chuño and tunta. • The high levels of RS suggest a high prebiotic potential of chuño and tunta samples. • First evaluation of SCFA and GABA production after probiotic fermentation. • Chuño and tunta are promising ingredients for the development of functional foods.

title: Comprehensive investigation of matrine and oxymatrine in Chinese jujube honey: a study on their conversion
abstract: The contents of matrine (MT) and oxymatrine (OMT) in 112 jujube honey samples were determined using an isotope-dilution-LC-MS/MS method. The detection rate was 62.5 %, with a concentration range of ND - 319.3 μg/kg. The average content of MT was higher than that of OMT, which differs from the previously reported pattern in acacia honey (AH). One-year dynamic monitoring revealed that OMT was transformed to MT in jujube honey, with the transformation rate of Ziziphus jujuba Mill. honey (JH) significantly higher than that of wild Ziziphus jujuba Mill. var. spinosa honey (WJSH). The DPPH assay demonstrated that the antioxidant activities of three kinds of honey were JH > WJSH > AH, and the SC 50 values showed a negative correlation with the transformation rate constant k. The results indicate that the transformation of OMT to MT in jujube honey is related to its antioxidant activity and furthered by its high phenolic content.

title: Identifying factors influencing Hydroxytyrosol in wines: Varietal selection, organic management, and yeast strategies in rosé and white wine production
abstract: Hydroxytyrosol (HT) is a low-toxic antioxidant with relevant biological properties. The objective of this study is to analyze natural HT production during rosé and white winemaking using various grape cultivars (including an organic one) and different yeast inoculation strategies. The UPLC-MS/MS method was validated to determine HT and related compounds. Six red and seven white grape varieties were harvested in southern Spain. Commercial yeasts ( Saccharomyces cerevisiae ) and wild yeasts were tested. As key findings, Rosé wines (Rome Variety) showed higher HT levels (1800 ng/mL) than white wines (Mantuo de Pilas variety) (300 ng/mL). Organic grapes produce up to five times more HT than conventional ones. Moreover, HT production was enhanced in wild yeasts compared with commercial yeasts (CY). In addition, wine lees and pomace retained considerable amounts of HT. To conclude, the formation of natural HT during winemaking varies by grape type and fermentation method. • Rosé wines showed higher HT levels than white: 1.4 mg/L compared to 0.6 mg/L. • Organic grape musts produced up to five times more HT than conventional musts. • Autochthonous yeasts resulted in more HT than commercial yeast inoculations. • Wine lees retained significant amounts of hydroxytyrosol (HT) after fermentation.

title: Development of a hydrophobic chain linker MIL-53(Al) as a sorbent in pipette tip-μSPE method for the determination of bisphenols in food packaging
abstract: Pristine aluminum-based metal-organic framework (MIL-53(Al)) as a sorbent shows limited affinity toward bisphenols due to the lack of hydrophobicity in its framework. To overcome this limitation, a dual-linker MIL-53(Al) with a hydrophobic carbon chain linker was synthesized for the first time and integrated into a pipette tip-micro solid-phase extraction (PT-μSPE) method for bisphenol determination. The parameters affecting the extraction process were optimized by implementing a response surface methodology (RSM) model using central composite design (CCD). Brunauer-Emmett-Teller analysis confirmed substantial increases in pore volume and pore width for the dual-linker MIL-53(Al) (0.74 cm 3 /g; 5.3 nm) compared with pristine MIL-53(Al) (0.17 cm 3 /g; 1.22 nm). This modification boosted the extraction efficiency of dual-linker MIL-53(Al) for bisphenols determination, resulting in low detection limits (0.01-0.1 μg/L), wide linearity (0.033-200.0 μg/L), high enrichment factors (up to 209), and good precision (RSD ≤ 7.0 %) in tea, disposable cups and containers, instant noodles, PET water bottles.

title: Fabrication of food-grade lipid nanodisc-based delivery systems: Structural characterization and self-assembly process
abstract: This study prepares food-grade nanodiscs using Tween 80 and lecithin. Initially, the formation process of the nanodiscs was observed, starting with the transformation of the hollow vesicle structure of lecithin into a notched vesicle structure, followed by the development of solid core nanodiscs, and ultimately into a cylindrical structure. The results from ITC indicated that hydrophobic interaction was the primary driving force behind the self-assembly of the nanodiscs with the binding ratio of lecithin to Tween 80 being 10:1. Owing to curvature effects, lecithin self-assembled into planar regions, while Tween 80 self-assembled into the edge regions. In comparison to hydrated liposomes, nanodiscs exhibited a smaller size, along with significant changes in molecular ordering, surface hydrophobicity, and microenvironment polarity of the phospholipid bilayers. Additionally, nanodiscs demonstrated superior encapsulation properties. This study elucidated the self-assembly process and structure of nanodiscs using food-grade ingredients, emphasizing their potential as delivery systems for food applications.

title: Structural interactions and transcriptional regulation by caffeic acid against multidrug-resistant Vibrio species: Mechanistic insights and efficacy in shrimp
abstract: This study aimed to investigate antimicrobial effects of caffeic acid (CA) against multidrug-resistant Vibrio parahaemolyticus and Vibrio cholerae both in vitro and in shrimp (Penaeus vannamei). CA at concentrations of 0.47-0.94 mg/mL disrupted bacterial membrane integrity, resulting in increased nucleic acid leakage and decreased intracellular DNA content. At 1 × minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), CA inhibited biofilm formation, with maximum reductions of 76.4 % and 68.3 % for V. parahaemolyticus and V. cholerae, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed stable binding between CA and critical bacterial proteins except for ompW, with binding energies of -6.6 to -5.8 kcal/mol. RT-qPCR further confirmed downregulation of related gene expression. In shrimp, CA treatment (6 × MIC, 4 h) reduced both Vibrio species by >4.4 log CFU/g. These results demonstrate the potent anti-Vibrio activity of CA, underscoring its potential as a plant-derived antimicrobial agent for ensuring microbial safety in seafood processing industry.

title: Impact of sucrose and NaCl Co-pickling on the flavor profile and digestive properties of salted egg yolks
abstract: This study investigated the effects of sucrose/NaCl co-pickling on lipid oxidation, flavor formation, and nutritional characteristics of salted egg yolks. Co-pickling established a dynamic balance between lipid hydrolysis and oxidation, generating moderate free fatty acids (FFA) and a stable flavor system. Yolks co-pickled at 45 °C exhibited higher PUFA and DPA contents than 25 °C, stronger umami and sweetness after baking, and a flavor profile similar to commercial yolks. GC-MS revealed that sucrose/NaCl co-pickling increased total volatiles (including alcohols, aldehydes, and hydrocarbons) by 42.1 %, reduced lipid oxidation by 22 %(based on TBA values), and enhanced digestibility by approximately 4.59 % (P < 0.05). The essential/non-essential amino acids was the highest (0.69), indicating improved nutritional balance. Overall, co-pickling at 45 °C effectively balanced oxidation and hydrolysis, promoted flavor compounds formation, and improves digestibility. These findings reveal coupling among lipid oxidation, amino acid transformation, and protein digestion, offering a practical route for producing low-salt, high-quality salted egg yolks.

title: Development of Salmon bone steak protein-based emulsion gels: Effects of fish oil volume fraction on gelation and structural properties
abstract: The influences of varying fish oil content (35 %-60 %) on the characteristics of Salmon bone steak protein (SP) emulsion gels were investigated. Results demonstrated that the emulsifying activity, emulsifying stability, and interfacial adsorbed protein content of SP emulsions reached their peak at 50 % oil, accompanied by the formation of small and uniformly dispersed oil droplets. Consequently, the emulsion gel containing 50 % oil exhibited the most favorable gelling properties, including gel strength, water-holding ability, whiteness, G' and G". Appropriate oil concentrations, especially 50 %, promoted the unfolding of SP and increased the β-sheet content, facilitating the formation of a more ordered and compact gel network. However, an oil fraction exceeding 50 % led to insufficient coverage of the oil-water interfaces, causing oil droplets leakage and subsequent decline in the performance of emulsions and emulsion gels. This study establishes a theoretical foundation for the development of SP-based emulsion gel products, with potential fat replacement applications.

title: Effect of the non-covalent complex of anthocyanins and whey protein on fish oil emulsions: Evaluation of stability, antioxidant properties, and bioaccessibility
abstract: The nutritional efficacy of fish oil is significantly limited by its high susceptibility to oxidative degradation and low bioavailability. In this study, a non-covalent complex composed of anthocyanins (ANC) and whey protein (WP), was rationally designed and utilized to develop a fish oil emulsion system aimed at enhancing oxidative stability and bioaccessibility. The fluorescence spectroscopy (INF), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and Far UV circular dichroism (CD) demonstrated specific molecular interactions were generated between ANC and WP. Upon emulsification, the WP-ANC complex at 0.4 wt% acted as an effective emulsifier, yielding emulsions with reduced droplet size and enhanced antioxidative stability. Comparative analysis revealed that WP-ANC stabilized emulsions exhibited superior inhibition of lipid oxidation compared to those stabilized solely by WP, thereby significantly enhancing the stability of fish oil. Under simulated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion, the emulsion formulated with 0.4 % ANC and WP promoted lipid droplet breakdown, suppressed oxidative degradation during digestion, decreased the release rate of free fatty acids, and consequently enhanced the bioavailability of fish oil.

title: Dietary lipid droplet size and phospholipids modulate lipid digestion and absorption in early life nutrition, an in vitro study
abstract: Lipid droplet structure differs in infant nutrition and may impact lipid digestion and absorption. Human milk (HM) contains large milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) coated lipid droplets, while standard infant formula (sIF) and sIF with added MFGM (sIFM) contains small protein coated droplets. Concept infant formula (cIF, Nuturis®) mimics HM's structure. Digestion of the infant formulae (IFs) and HM was simulated under infant conditions. Digests were sampled in time and free fatty acids (FFA) were analyzed to determine lipolysis rates. Lipid absorption was tested by digest incubation on Caco2-TC7 transwells for 6 and 16 h. sIF and sIFM had higher lipolysis rates than cIF and HM. FFA release patterns differed between the IFs and HM. sIFM showed increased triglyceride secretion and larger intracellular lipid droplets compared to sIF. The sIF and sIFM had higher lipolysis rates, while cIF was closer to breast milk in lipolysis and absorption rate. • • Lipolysis and absorption of IFs with small or large droplets vs HM was tested. • • Small droplets (sIF and sIF + MFGM) showed faster lipolysis rates vs large (cIF and HM). • • HM lipolysis resulted in more unsaturated FFA (OA, LA) and less free PA vs IFs. • • MFGM added to sIF increased TG secretion, cIF and HM secretion was not different. • • Lipid structure affects lipid availability; cIF is more similar to HM than sIF.

title: Dual-readout digital colorimetric assay for zearalenone in corn based on alkaline phosphatase mediated growth of Prussian blue nanoparticles
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEN) poses a substantial threat to global cereal grain security. Herein, a dual-readout biotin-avidin amplified nanozyme-linked immunosorbent assay (BA-ELISA) based on absorbance and blue intensity was established for detecting ZEN residues in corn. The method utilized alkaline phosphatase (ALP), which hydrolyzes ascorbic acid 2-phosphate (AAP) to generate ascorbic acid (AA). The resulting AA reduced K₃[Fe(CN)₆] to K₄[Fe(CN)₆], subsequently reacting with FeCl₃ to form blue Prussian blue nanoparticles (PBNPs). Concurrently, AAP reacted with FeCl₃ to yield a brown AAP-Fe 3+ complex, enabling dual-readout detection via PBNPs and AAP-Fe 3+ . The assay exhibited a linear detection range of 0.625-10 ng/mL, a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.022 ng/mL via absorbance and 0.00447 ng/mL via digital colorimetry, and spiked recovery rates of 104.63 %-118.64 % in corn samples. This dual-readout digital colorimetric detection provided a convenient, sensitive platform for on-site toxin monitoring, offering new perspectives for food safety inspection.

title: Taurine as a functional ingredient: Dietary sources, non-thermal extraction technologies, purification, potential health benefits and its applications
abstract: Taurine is a sulfur-containing amino acid derivative with diverse physiological benefits. This review provides comprehensive insights into its dietary sources, extraction and purification methods, processing effects, and applications in the food industry, highlighting seafood, meat, and organ meats as rich sources with variable content. Emerging non-thermal extraction techniques (e.g., ultrasound-assisted extraction, enzymatic hydrolysis, pulse-electric field) offer improved recovery, while purification ensures high-quality functional taurine, yet thermal and mechanical processing can cause significant losses. Taurine supports antioxidant defense, glucose and lipid metabolism, cardiovascular and liver health, and exhibits modest ergogenic effects. Despite growing demand for taurine-enriched foods in human and pet nutrition, challenges remain in selecting suitable raw materials, and developing diverse, demographic-specific products. Addressing these issues through optimized extraction, targeted product innovation, and well-designed, large scale clinical trial to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and identify populations most likely to benefit represents a key pathway for expanding its functional food applications.

title: Insights into ultrasound-modified soy protein isolate-inulin hydrogels: Focus on binding mechanisms, stability, and riboflavin controlled-release behavior
abstract: The loose structure of natural soy protein isolate (SPI) gels limits their application in food nutrient delivery systems. This study investigated the effects of varying inulin (INU) concentrations combined with ultrasound treatment on the structural characteristics, stability, and riboflavin digestion and release of SPI-based hydrogels. Increasing INU concentration enhanced the textural properties and water-holding capacity (WHC) of the composite gels, converting free water into immobilized water. The addition of 2 % INU with ultrasound treatment (SU-2) markedly improved rheological properties, yielding a smoother, denser microstructure and increasing protein disorder. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the SPI-INU gel structure was stabilized primarily through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. The modified gels improved riboflavin loading and stability, with SU-2 exhibiting the highest bioaccessibility (85.82 %) and chemical stability (76.01 %). This study contributes to the development of natural protein/polysaccharide gel carriers for targeted slow release of hydrophilic bioactives.

title: Intelligent evaluation of black tea withering quality via image-spectrum fusion using a multimodal attention network with contrastive learning
abstract: Withering is a critical process that significantly impacts the final quality of black tea. Traditional assessment methods, which rely on manual evaluation, are often subjective and time-consuming. To overcome this limitation, we proposed a multimodal evaluation approach based on computer vision (CV) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRs), integrating both qualitative classification and quantitative prediction during the black tea withering process. For withering degree classification, we developed a multimodal attention fusion network that combines a CV feature extraction module (pyramid CNN), an NIRs feature extraction module (attention-enhanced CNN and gated recurrent unit), and a cross-modal fusion mechanism using contrastive learning, achieving an accuracy of 95.56 %. For quantitative assessment, we constructed a squeeze-and-excitation enhanced ResNet18 model to fuse CV and NIRs features for predicting moisture and soluble sugar content, yielding test set correlation coefficients of 0.9151 and 0.9023, respectively. These innovations provide a comprehensive strategy for intelligent withering evaluation in black tea withering.

title: Incorporation of carminic acid in gelatin/chitosan nanoparticles for stabilizing high internal phase Pickering emulsions and its functional 3D/4D printing
abstract: Gelatin/chitosan nanoparticles loaded with carminic acid were adopted to construct and stabilize high internal phase Pickering emulsions for 3D/4D printing. Carminic acid was incorporated into gelatin/chitosan nanoparticles with excellent compatibility via interactions like hydrogen bonding and bridging flocculation. These gelatin/chitosan/carminic acid complex nanoparticles exhibited outstanding emulsifying ability, due to the fact that nanoparticle's amphiphilicity (hydrophilic-lipophilic balance) and interfacial wettability (contact angle) promoted its adsorption at the oil-water interface. The optimal high internal phase Pickering emulsion with proper-content carminic acid illustrated uniform droplets, excellent emulsion appearance, high viscosity, great thixotropy, high yield stress, high mechanical strength and outstanding thermal stability. The optimal emulsions also presented excellent 3D/4D printability with high shape maintainability, as well as potential usage in dysphagia diets. This study provides important implications for stabilizing emulsions with carminic acid-loaded nanoparticles and constructing creative, high-quality and functional food products via 3D/4D printing.

title: Solvent dielectric constant as a predictor of polyphenol yield and antioxidant activity in extracts from moringa
abstract: Polyphenol extraction is strongly influenced by solvent characteristics. This study investigated the effect of solvent dielectric constant on polyphenols recovery and antioxidant activity, using ultrasound-assisted extraction of moringa as a model system. Solvent mixtures of methanol, ethanol, and acetone with water were prepared to achieve a wide dielectric constant range. Extracts were analysed via liquid chromatograph mass spectrometry. Polynomial regression modelling was employed to evaluate the predictive power of dielectric constant on extract yield, total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), and antioxidant capacity. Results showed strong correlations between dielectric constant and extract yield, TPC, and antioxidant activity. TFC was highest in low-polarity solvents. Multivariate analysis revealed distinct polyphenol profiles associated with solvent polarity. This is the first study to model extraction performance using dielectric constant, offering a scalable framework for solvent selection. These findings provide practical insights for optimising polyphenol recovery in food and nutraceutical applications.

title: Responses of sugar metabolism to nitrogen fertilization in Lonicera caerulea: insights from integrated targeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and molecular docking
abstract: This study assessed 26 varieties of Lonicera caerulea, which exhibited significant genetic variation in sugar and acid profiles at the green fruit, veraison, and ripe stages. Nitrogen treatment in high-sugar cultivars led to a notable reduction in fructose and glucose concentrations. The sugar content differences between high- and low-sugar cultivars were primarily attributed to variations in fructose and glucose levels. At maturity, glucose and fructose concentrations ranged from 58.0 to 135.7 mg/g and 43.5 to 115.8 mg/g, respectively, reflecting genetic differences prior to nitrogen treatments. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed key gene modules associated with sugar metabolism. Molecular docking showed strong binding between fructose-1,6-bisphosphate and fructose-bisphosphate aldolase (-7.95 kcal/mol), as well as a biologically relevant but weak interaction between oxaloacetate and phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (-4.0 kcal/mol). These findings offer valuable molecular understanding of the control of sugar metabolism in blue honeysuckle, offering insights into improving fruit quality and functional food.

title: Smartphone-assisted paper biosensor based on MIL-100(Fe)@Hemin@CDs mimetic nanozyme for freshness monitoring of pork
abstract: In order to improve catalytic activity, MIL-100(Fe) was functionalized with Hemin and corncob carbon dots (CDs) to mimic the pocket-like structure of natural enzymes, and the resulting nanozyme was integrated into a paper-based biosensor coupled with a smartphone platform for accurate hypoxanthine detection and freshness evaluation of pork. The results showed that the MIL-100(Fe)-based nanozyme integrated with Hemin and CDs effectively mimicked the pocket-like structure of natural enzymes, exhibiting high catalytic activity along with enhanced K m , V max , thermal stability, and anti-interference performance. The developed biosensing platform displayed excellent linearity over the range of 2-160 μM and a low detection limit of 1.13 μM. These findings demonstrate that MIL-100(Fe)@Hemin@CDs, when combined with a smartphone-assisted paper-based biosensor, offers a reliable strategy for real-time freshness evaluation of pork.

title: Adsorbent resin technology for flavour removal in canola protein isolate processing
abstract: Bitter flavors, pigments, and odorants limit the application of canola protein isolate (CPI). This study combined Alkaline Extraction–Isoelectric Precipitation with resin washing (XAD-16N, HP-20, SP-207) to reduce volatile and non-volatile compounds. Resin treatments removed >95 % of non-volatiles, including sinapine and glucosinolates ( 1 H NMR, p ≤ 0.05). HS-GC/MS and ROAV analysis showed XAD-16N significantly reduced VOCs (p ≤ 0.05), confirmed by E-nose profiling. Functional properties improved: solubility increased >20 % between pH 4–8, with HP-20 showing the highest solubility across all pH and enhanced lightness (L* = 67.87). Emulsifying activity index (EAI) improved by >35 %, while foaming capacity remained unchanged; foam stability increased by >3 %. Resin-assisted purification effectively mitigates odorants and enhances CPI functionality. This approach supports CPI's use as a high-quality plant protein ingredient in food formulations, addressing flavour and odor challenges in plant-based systems.

title: Identification of the chili powder with illegal additive Sudan I by shifted-excitation Raman difference spectroscopy system
abstract: This study developed a Shifted-Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS) system integrated with a microscopic Raman system (μRaman) to reduce background interference in Raman spectroscopy. By using slightly shifted excitation laser wavelengths, two spectra are captured consecutively at the same sample position, allowing background noise to be subtracted and leaving only the Raman peaks. The reconstructed spectra showed a significant improvement in signal-to-noise ratio, effectively removing both broadband and ambient light interference. The system was applied to identify chili powder containing the illegal additive Sudan I, demonstrating enhanced performance in both Raman and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS).

title: Dual-mode optical nanoprobe based on red-emissive carbon dots for sensitive detection of positively charged nanoplastics
abstract: The large-scale production and use of plastics have led to the widespread distribution of nanoplastics (NPs) in environmental media and the food chain. Among various NPs, positively charged nanoplastics (pNPs) generated through aging processes exhibit enhanced bioaccumulation in living organisms and significantly increased biotoxicity. To achieve rapid detection of pNPs in food and environmental samples, this study synthesized red-emissive fluorescent carbon dots (CAT-RCDs) using 3,4-diaminobenzenesulfonic acid and catechol as precursors. Based on this, a sensing platform capable of fluorescence/colorimetric dual-mode detection of positively charged polystyrene nanoplastics (pPS-NPs) was constructed. The sensor exhibited a linear response from 1 to 50 mg/L (fluorescence) and 5-60 mg/L (colorimetric), with detection limits of 0.58 and 1.04 mg/L, respectively. Recovery rates of 90.91-104.80 % confirmed its accuracy. This dual-mode strategy allows visual detection and cross-validation of pPS-NPs, providing a rapid screening tool and a foundation for advanced nanoplastic sensing technologies.

title: Oxidation stability and kinetics of Camellia oil under thermal treatment: A non-isothermal differential scanning calorimetry analysis
abstract: The oxidation stability and kinetics of Camellia oil (CO) under thermal treatment were investigated using non-isothermal differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Oxidation kinetic parameters were determined using the Ozawa-Flynn-Wall and Kissinger methods. The results indicated that the oxidation activation energy (E a ) serves as a pertinent parameter for characterizing the oxidation stability of CO in the initial oxidation stage. A gradual decline in E a was observed as the heating time increased. Conversely, during the initial oxidation phase, the oxidation rate constant (k) rose with prolonged heating. Based on compositional analysis, this trend is primarily ascribed to the progressive destruction of endogenous tocopherols in oil. Furthermore, spearman correlation analysis reveal that E a was positively correlated with OSI (ρ = 1, p < 0.01) and negatively correlated with POV (ρ = -1, p < 0.01). The non-isothermal DSC coupled with chemical composition analysis offers a new approach to identifying industrial applications for edible oils.

title: Comparison of the structural characteristics, pH-sensitivity, antioxidant activity and thermal stability of different dialdehyde polysaccharides grafted with purple sweet potato anthocyanins
abstract: Three dialdehyde polysaccharides including dialdehyde chitosan (DACS), dialdehyde guar gum (DAGG) and dialdehyde pectin (DAPT) were grafted with purple sweet potato anthocyanins (PSPA) through acid-catalyzed grafting reaction, yielding PSPA-g-DACS, PSPA-g-DAGG and PSPA-g-DAPT, respectively. The structural characteristics, pH-sensitivity, antioxidant activity and thermal stability of PSPA-g-DACS, PSPA-g-DAGG and PSPA-g-DAPT were compared. PSPA-g-dialdehyde polysaccharides presented visible absorption peaks at 526-537 nm, infrared bands at 1517 and 1283/1289 cm -1 , and proton signals at 6.78, 2.67 and 1.28/1.36 ppm, corresponding to the grafted PSPA. PSPA-g-dialdehyde polysaccharides displayed similar pH-sensitivity with PSPA. PSPA-g-dialdehyde polysaccharides also had 193.69-359.76 μmol Trolox equivalents/g of free radical scavenging activity. The thermal stability of samples was in the order of PSPA-g-DAGG > PSPA-g-DAPT > PSPA-g-DACS > PSPA. Molecular docking analysis verified PSPA-g-DAGG possessed the most diverse inter-/intra-molecular interactions. Results revealed the characteristics of PSPA-g-dialdehyde polysaccharides were affected by the type of dialdehyde polysaccharides.

title: Special issue related to the 3rd NIZO Plant Protein Conference
In silico-predicted characteristic fragment ions database (CFID) for in-depth regiospecific analysis of triacylglycerol regioisomers based on UPLC-EIEIO-MS/MS
abstract: The regiospecific analysis of triacylglycerols (TGs) remains a critical challenge due to their structural complexity, particularly in distinguishing regioisomers like AAB/ABA and ABC/ACB types. In this study, a novel strategy combining electron impact excitation of ions from organics (EIEIO) tandem mass spectrometry with a curated characteristic fragment ion database (CFID) containing 160,000 theoretical EIEIO-MS/MS spectra was developed to rapidly determine precise TG structures and resolve complicated positional regioisomers. Applied to vegetable oils, this strategy led to preliminary identification of 59, 35, 30, and 45 regiospecific TG structures in rapeseed, linseed, perilla, and evening primrose oils, respectively, and discovery of 15, 3, 4, and 4 co-eluting regioisomeric pairs, which elucidate the nutritionally relevant fine structure of TGs. Furthermore, this strategy provides a more straightforward and expedient analytical method for determining fatty acid distribution in vegetable oils. Applying this method, we have elucidated the detailed distribution profiles of fatty acids at the sn-2 and sn-1/3 positions across four distinct vegetable oil samples. The proposed strategy enables rapid TG regiospecific analysis as well as fatty acid distribution determination, advancing insights into TG structure-function relationships for food nutrition research.

title: The study of functional properties of kiwifruit peel dietary fiber and the bioactivity as well as synergetic prebiotic effects of bound phenolics in it during in vitro gastrointestinal digestion and colonic fermentation
abstract: The structure, functional performance of soluble and insoluble Kiwifruit (Actinidia chinensis Planch) peel dietary fiber (KPDF) as well as abundant bound phenolics (BPs) in them were systematically investigated. It turned out that KPDF conserved outstanding capacities in adsorption and cation exchange. 23 BPs were identified in KPDF, most of which were inaccessible during in vitro gastrointestinal digestion but up to 27.10 % and 57.89 % BPs were released form insoluble and soluble KPDF after 24 h and 12 h colonic fermentation, respectively. Meanwhile, KPDF promoted the reproduction of beneficial bacteria such as Prevotella, Dialister, Faecalibacterium, while reducing the abundances of harmful bacteria such as Collinsella, Dorea, and Gemmiger with BPs contributing to such features. Such results reflected the promoting effects of BPs in the prebiotic effects of functional KPDF, providing theoretical foundation for the further exploration of KPDF as functional nutritional factors in health promotion.

title: Tannase-catalysed gallic acid release for clean-label inhibition of green tea auto-oxidative browning
abstract: Ready-to-drink (RTD) green tea is rich in flavan-3-ols, which readily undergo auto-oxidation, causing browning. Conventional browning inhibitors can induce undesirable ingredient interactions, flavour changes, and health concerns. Here, we explored a clean-label strategy to inhibit RTD green tea browning by releasing gallic acid from naturally present galloylated compounds using the enzyme tannase (from Aspergillus ficuum ). In-depth analysis of green tea by a combination of UHPLC-HRMS, NMR, and enzymatic hydrolysis led to the (tentative) identification of 75 galloylated compounds with four scaffold types. Hydrolysis of these galloylated compounds by tannase was affected by the scaffold type, scaffold stereo configuration, position of gallate attachment, and number of gallate moieties. Tannase treatment resulted in a substantial reduction in auto-oxidative browning of green tea. These results demonstrate that tannase treatment has the potential to decrease reliance on additives for maintaining the colour of RTD green tea and other phenolic-rich beverages. • A large number of galloylated compounds were (tentatively) identified in green tea. • Tannase was able to release more than 90 % of naturally present bound gallic acid. • Hydrolysis by tannase was affected by scaffold type and position of galloylation. • Tannase-catalysed gallic acid release reduced auto-oxidative browning of green tea. • Tannase treatment can decrease reliance on additives to control undesired browning.

title: Editorial Board
Effects of cold plasma on volatile organic compounds in foods: fundamentals, mechanisms, and applications
abstract: Cold plasma (CP) is an emerging non-thermal, environmentally friendly, and cost-effective food processing technology that has shown promise in microbial inactivation and food quality improvement. However, its high chemical reactivity can also negatively affect food quality, particularly through changes in volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which are key indicators of chemical reactions and sensory attributes. This review fills a current research gap by summarizing how CP influences VOCs across different food systems. After introducing plasma principles, chemistry, and discharge types, it examines VOC generation pathways-including lipid and protein oxidation and Strecker degradation-and analyses the transformation of VOCs under CP treatment. It then reviews the impact of CP on VOCs in various food matrices, highlighting both benefits and adverse effects. Finally, based on a decade of research, it proposes optimization strategies to mitigate negative impacts and improve process performance, offering practical guidance and future research directions.

title: Unraveling the impact of repeated and continuous heat-moisture treatment on WEAX-corn starch compounds: new insights into structure and digestibility
abstract: To assess the impacts of repeated heat-moisture treatment (RHMT) and continuous heat-moisture treatment (CHMT) on the structural and functional properties of water-extractable arabinoxylans (WEAX)-corn starch (CS) compounds (WEAX-CS), this study investigated the interaction mechanism of WEAX-CS with high- and low- molecular weight WEAX (HWEAX, LWEAX). The results demonstrated that prolonged HMT increased water adsorption capacity from 1.50 to 2.16 g/g, and the crystallinity of CS, HWEAX-CS (CS/H), LWEAX-CS compounds (CS/L) treated by 6 repetitions of RHMT (RHM-6) decreased by 8 %, 14 %, and 12 %, respectively. in vitro digestibility results showed a decrease in the final hydrolysis rate following HMT. For RHM-3, the hydrolysis rates of CS/H and CS/L were decreased by 4 % and 6 %, and 72.67 % of the reduced rapidly digestible starch of CS was converted to slowly digestible starch, while 27.33 % to resistant starch (RS). The RS increased by 12 %-16 % after HMT for 12 h, peaking at 58.78 % in RHM-6-CS/L.

title: Multi-channel spectral sensor–based instrument as an alternative to the Agtron for predicting coffee roast degree using classical chemometric and machine learning approaches
abstract: This study developed a new alternative Agtron detection system using a low-cost multichannel spectral sensor (410-940 nm) combined with classical and modern chemometric regression methods, and implemented the selected model in an embedded system to produce a portable, affordable, and field-ready device. Spectral data were collected from Arabica and Robusta samples (from different origins) at various roast degrees. Modelling was performed using quantitative chemometrics ranging from classical (Multiple Linear Regression-MLR and Partial Least Squares Regression-PLSR) to modern, including three machine learning (ML) algorithms (Random Forest-RF, Support Vector Regression-SVR, Artificial Neural Networks-ANN). All approaches and scenarios yielded high prediction accuracy (R 2 v 0.983-0.994, RMSEV 7.7), even with 50 % of the selected wavelengths. Furthermore, the selected model was successfully embedded into a stand-alone microcontroller device and delivered reliable results (R 2 0.965-0.967 and RMSE <3), even when tested on new samples from different coffee types (Liberica and Excelsa).

title: Development of an immunoassay with an immunomagnetic bead-based sample extraction procedure for detecting zearalenone in food products
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEN) is a mycotoxin produced by Fusarium fungi, commonly found in food and animal feed, posing a threat to public and animal health. For rapid ZEN detection in food samples, a monoclonal antibody (mAb) 5G3 was developed in this study and used to create the immunomagnetic bead (IMB)-based immunoassay, which can be used for the enrichment, purification, and detection of ZEN in multiple foods. Molecular recognition revealed a broad specificity of mAb 5G3 for ZEN and its five metabolites. Under optimal working conditions, the sensitivity (IC 50 ) of indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ic-ELISA) was 0.37 ± 0.04 ng/mL, and the limit of detection (LOD, IC 15 ) was 0.05 ± 0.01 ng/mL. Employing ZEN IMBs for purification demonstrated superior performance in 11 food matrices, achieving 1.42- to 50-fold lower detection limits than conventional dilution methods, with particularly significant sensitivity improvements observed in hominy grits (50-fold reduction).

title: Metabolomic analysis reveals stepwise metabolic adaptation to extended photoperiods in developing pea sprouts
abstract: Photoperiod strongly influences early seedling metabolism; however, its role during initial development remains unclear. We analysed 100 primary and secondary metabolites and phytohormones in pea sprouts grown under short-day (SD; 8 h light), long-day (LD; 16 h light), and all-day (AD; 24 h light) conditions. Principal component analysis revealed distinct photoperiod-dependent clustering, indicating stepwise metabolic reprogramming from SD to AD. SD enhanced amino acid accumulation and auxin conjugation by 1.01-6.50-fold and 0.99-2.66-fold over LD/AD, suggesting reduced carbon flux due to limited photosynthesis and a compensatory shift toward nitrogen metabolism to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Conversely, LD/AD increased sugars and stress-related hormones by 1.20-7.51-fold and 1.25-14.91-fold relative to SD. Notably, LD elevated abscisic acid (1.39-fold) and salicylic acid (14.91-fold) over SD, reflecting photooxidative stress.
