abstract: Protein-bioactive compounds interactions, including protein-glycoside, protein-triterpene, and protein-polyphenol binding, influence protein stability, gelation, and oxidative behavior; however, their impact on myofibrillar proteins (MPs) remains insufficiently clarified. To supplement existing knowledge, this work investigated MP with selected bioactive compounds, focusing on how glycosides, triterpenes, and polyphenols on affect functional and structural properties. The aim was to determine whether asiatic acid, madecassic acid, asiaticoside, madecassoside, quercetin, and chlorogenic acid modulate MPs' antioxidant activity, rheological behavior/structure, and thermal stability. Using rheological tests and viscosity analysis, SDS-PAGE, antioxidant assays, as well as scanning electron microscopy, their effects on MP gelation and oxidation resistance were assessed. Results showed that the pentacyclic triterpenes (asiatic acid, madecassic acid) disrupted the MP network, reduced thermal stability and increased gel heterogeneity, whereas the triterpene glycosides (asiaticoside, madecassoside improved gel uniformity and thermal resistance. Madecassic acid increased the storage modulus (G') and helped maintain, while both quercetin and chlorogenic acid weakened protein-protein interactions, resulting in reducted gel stiffness and viscosity. Quercetin and chlorogenic acid also showed stronger reducing power, whereas asiatic acid and chlorogenic acid exhibited higher radical-scavenging capacity than the remaining compounds. Overall, these observations suggested that the tested bioactive compounds can be used to fine-tune MPs gelation behavior and oxidative stability.

title: Construction, improved chelating activity and bioavailability of mercapto pea protein peptide‑zinc chelate via dithiothreitol mediated reduction and enzymatic hydrolysis treatment: optimization, structure and uptake mechanism
abstract: Pea protein peptides are rich in cysteine and exhibit potential as zinc carriers; however, the presence of disulfide bonds and hydrophobic proline clusters limits their zinc-chelation capacity. Dithiothreitol (DTT) was used to reduce disulfide bonds, and a composite protease was used for hydrolysis to obtain mercapto pea protein peptide (CMP) with a lower molecular-weight distribution ( 4 . This study establishes a foundation for developing CMP-Zn as a high-chelation, bioavailable zinc supplement.

title: Uncovering cryoprotective mechanism of natural deep eutectic solvents for highly efficient cryopreservation of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
abstract: The role of probiotics in human health has been increasingly emphasized. However, for cryopreserving stock cells of probiotics, the cytotoxicity and limited cryoprotective efficiency of traditional cryoprotectants always cause cell viability decline and loss of superior biological traits. To address the problems, in this study, three types of NADESs (Pro-Suc, Pro-Tre, and Bet-Pro-Suc) were prepared and used as green cryoprotectants for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum cryopreservation. Cytotoxicity analysis showed that NADESs could be more biocompatible than glycerol, and NADESs-cryopreserved cells were found to exhibit significantly higher post-thaw viability (84.5 % ∼ 94.6 %) than the glycerol-protected ones (75.7 %). Further mechanism investigation indicated that the high cryoprotective efficiency of NADESs was predominantly thanks to their superior ice regulation capacities and ice recrystallization inhibition activities, which can contribute to less and smaller ice crystals (67.2 % ∼ 86.3 % < ϕ10 μm) than glycerol (37.2 % < ϕ10 μm), hence alleviating possible mechanical damage induced by the ice growth.

title: Chitosan-ε-polylysine‑sodium tripolyphosphate based Pickering emulsions for co-encapsulation of cinnamaldehyde and linalool: An effective sustained-release system against toxigenic fungi
abstract: Chitosan-ε-polylysine‑sodium tripolyphosphate (CS-εPL-STPP) ternary solid particles were fabricated to stabilize Pickering emulsions for co-encapsulating cinnamaldehyde (CN) and linalool (LN). The incorporation of ε-PL into the CS-STPP system enhanced structural stability via hydrogen bonding and van der Waals-mediated crosslinking, as confirmed by FT-IR, XPS, and molecular docking, concurrently improving thermal stability. The optimized CN-LN-PE (oil fraction 4 %, CN: LN = 4:2) exhibited not only high encapsulation efficiency (86.67 ± 0.61 %) and temperature-responsive release properties but also favorable interfacial adsorption behaviors, collectively contributing to its superior antifungal activity. CN-LN-PE effectively inhibited the growth of Aspergillus flavus, suppressed aflatoxin B1 production by 78.63 %, and exerted antifungal action by disrupting membrane integrity and inducing oxidative stress. Beyond addressing the solubility limitations, the CN-LN co-delivery Pickering emulsion offered a sustainable functional strategy for effective mycotoxin mitigation during post-harvest storage of peanuts, showcasing great potential for broader application in preserving various agricultural products and processed foods.

title: From bamboo shoot to suansun: A comprehensive review of fermentation mechanisms, metabolic pathways, and potential health implications
abstract: Suansun, a traditional fermented bamboo shoot product, holds notable culinary importance in southern China and Southeast Asia, particularly as a defining component of regional dishes such as luosifen (river snail rice noodles). This review presents a comprehensive examination of suansun fermentation, encompassing raw material processing, physicochemical transformations, microbial succession, flavor compound biosynthesis, nutritional composition, and potential health implications. Suansun's characteristic aroma arises mainly from microbial metabolism of carbohydrates and amino acids, leading to the production of diverse flavors. The degradation of aromatic amino acids plays a pivotal role in odor formation, with recent studies clarifying the underlying metabolic pathways. Fermentation further enhances suansun's functional profile by increasing bioactive compounds such as polyphenols and flavonoids, boosting antioxidant activity, and enriching lactic acid bacteria with probiotic potential. By synthesizing recent findings, this review provides a scientific foundation for optimizing suansun production and promoting its application in the development of high-value functional foods.

title: Preparation of linalool microcapsules and its application on preservation and antifungal protection in postharvest sweet cherry
abstract: In this study, linalool microcapsules (LMs) were prepared through ionic gelation using linalool as the core material and sodium alginate as the wall material. The efficacy of LMs in cherry preservation and their inhibitory mechanism against brown rot (caused by Monilinia fructicola) were investigated. The optimal preparation process conditions for LMs were determined, while encapsulation efficiency could reach 88.44 %. Scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis confirmed the successful encapsulation of linalool in microcapsules, which exhibited good thermal stability and sustained-release properties. LMs enhanced the antioxidant capacity, disease resistance, and storage quality of cherries. The linalool significantly inhibited the mycelial growth and spore germination of M. fructicola by disrupting cell membranes, inhibiting ergosterol synthesis, and inducing reactive oxygen species accumulation, thereby suppressing the development of brown rot. These findings indicate that LMs can extend the shelf life of cherries and hold broad application prospects in fruit preservation.

title: Amylopectin chain length distribution shows limited explanatory power for cooked rice digestibility: A comparative analysis using SEC-DRI-MALS, FACE, and HPAEC
abstract: In this study, 28 rice starches with varying amylose contents ranging between 0.64 % ∼ 41.19 % were analyzed using size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), fluorophore-assisted carbohydrate electrophoresis (FACE), and high-performance anion-exchange chromatography (HPAEC). All methods reproduced canonical multi-modal chain length distribution (CLD) but differed in reliability: SEC was limited by band broadening, HPAEC resolved medium chains but became noisy at very high degree of polymerization above ∼68. In contrast, FACE combined high resolution of short and long chains with mild processing, providing the most robust and reproducible profiles, which is further confirmed by the analysis of compact, short-chain-rich topologies in low-amylose starches. Importantly, no statistically significant correlations were detected between FACE-derived CLD parameters and the in vitro digestion parameters of freshly cooked rice under the present sample size, highlighting the need for integrated approaches to link starch molecular structure with functional properties.

title: Study on the mechanism of flavor development in ultrasound-assisted microwave vacuum drying of shiitake mushrooms: Dosage effect of ultrasonic amplitude
abstract: In this study, the regulatory pathways of aroma formation in dried shiitake mushrooms under different ultrasound amplitudes (50 %, 70 %, and 90 %) were elucidated using GC-MS and non-targeted metabolomics combined with dynamic analysis of γ-GT and CS lyase activities. The results revealed that multiple metabolic pathways including cysteine and methionine metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, and cofactor biosynthesis exhibited amplitude-dependent responses. These pathways collectively influenced aroma compound production through coordinated resource allocation and signal regulation. Specifically, low and medium ultrasound amplitudes (50 % and 70 %) significantly enhanced cysteine and methionine metabolism, resulting in an increase of volatile sulfide content (up to 33.88 ng/g). Notably, ultrasound at 70 % amplitude markedly promoted sulfur metabolism and methylation processes, which contributed to a more complex and intense aroma characteristic of shiitake mushrooms. However, high-amplitude ultrasound induced metabolic offset, activating energy and nucleic acid metabolism to sustain basic cellular functions under stress, which limited the flavor development. Besides, ultrasound at 70 % amplitude was found to facilitate the release of enzymes in cells, increasing the activity of CS lyase by 134 % compared to the MVD group, which enhanced the formation of volatile sulfur such as lenthionine. These findings provide theoretical support for aroma regulation in dried edible mushrooms and offer new insights for optimizing high-quality drying processes in shiitake mushroom production.

title: The extraction, purification, and application of capsaicin in alleviating obesity: A comprehensive review
abstract: The anti-obesity effects of capsaicin have been widely verified in cell and animal models and human trials. Notably, the effects of these actions may be influenced by external factors, such as the type of capsaicin, intake method, and dosage, as well as by the host's inherent physiological conditions and gut microbiota responses. Additionally, the insufficient safety evaluation of capsaicin remains a bottleneck restricting the current development of functional foods. In response to these issues, this review summarizes the extraction and purification strategies for capsaicin, as well as the mechanisms by which it alleviates obesity. Furthermore, it discusses the factors that influence the physiological functions of capsaicin and provides corresponding suggestions. This review aimed to offer new strategies and a theoretical basis for the value-added utilization of capsaicin.

title: Scalable production of antioxidant ‘sandwich’ films from all-natural composites for inhibiting fruit browning
abstract: Bio-based films are emerging as promising sustainable materials, aligning with the principles of green chemistry. However, most studies on bio-based films rarely address scalable production. Herein, we address the challenge of scalable production in bio-based films by developing continuously fabricated, self-assembled sandwich-structured films composed of natural materials. Films with chitosan quaternary ammonium salt (QCS) as outer layer, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as middle layer and tannic acid (TA) as functional core, were manufactured efficiently using automatic coating machines. This structure significantly improves mechanical strength and preserves the bioactivity of TA. Films exhibit exceptional radical scavenging activity (>95 %), high antibacterial efficacy (>98 % against both S. aureus and E. coli) and UV blocking (100 %). Fruit preservation tests under both static and dynamic conditions confirmed its ability to inhibit oxidative browning and extend shelf life. The film is biodegradable, promoting plant growth within a closed-loop cycle and supports green chemistry and sustainable design.

title: Covalent organic framework-based solid-phase microextraction coupled with electrospray ionization mass spectrometry for in vivo determination of furanocoumarins in citrus fruits
abstract: Furanocoumarins (FCMs) are a group of organic compounds abundantly found in citrus fruits. Excessive intake is closely associated with increased incidence of skin cancer. Consequently, the development of an efficient approach for in vivo determination of FCMs in citrus fruits is of critical importance. In this study, 1,3,5-tris (4-aminophenyl) benzene (TAPB) and 2,4-dihydroxybenzene-1,3,5-tricarbaldehyde (DHTA) were used to synthesize covalent organic framework (COF) as a solid phase microextraction (SPME) probe. The probe showed highly ordered porosity (1.49 nm), outstanding stability, and hydrophobicity. With respect to these superiorities, it was coupled with electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI/MS) to achieve the detection of six FCMs with high enrichment factors (71.3-108.5), and low detection limits (0.003-0.160 μg L -1 ). The platform was used with great success for the in vivo analysis of FCMs in four citrus fruits, indicating that this platform had good prospects as a powerful instrument for in vivo monitoring fruits.

title: Effects of protein-glutaminase on structural and functional properties and the interaction mechanism in casein micelle suspensions: convergence of multiscale experiments and molecular dynamics simulations
abstract: Understanding protein glutaminase (PGase)-driven structural and functional remodeling of micellar casein suspensions is critical. Deamidation (0-40 min) increased the surface charge (ζ potential: -22.2 to -29.8 mV), reduced the particle size (403 nm to 179 nm; transmission electron microscopy verified fragmentation to 50-250 nm nanoparticles), and decreased the surface hydrophobicity to achieve complete solubility (93.49 %). Secondary structure reorganization increased the α-helix (from 20 % to 23 %) and β-sheet (from 14 % to 25 %) contents, increasing the thermal denaturation temperature (106.6 °C), emulsifying activity (from 52 m 2 /g to 108 m 2 /g), and oil-binding capacity (from 15.95 % to 38.99 %), and improved proteolytic digestibility. Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) peptide mapping revealed isoform-resolved PGase-susceptible glutaminyl residues, consistent with glutamine-to-glutamic acid conversion (Gln to Glu), revealing distinct deamidation site distributions across αs1-, αs2-, β-, and κ-casein. Molecular dynamics simulations and docking studies elucidated isoform-specific interactions of PGase with αs1-, αs2-, β-, and κ-casein, revealing conserved energetic hotspots.

title: Impact of pitaya peel powder particle size on bread quality and functional properties: a sustainable strategy for agro-industrial waste upcycling
abstract: This study investigated the valorization of pitaya peel powder (PPP), an agro-industrial byproduct, as a functional ingredient to enhance bread's nutritional quality and reduce food waste. PPP of varying particle sizes (D 50 )-large (415.8 μm), medium (183.7 μm), and small (60.3 μm)-was incorporated into bread at 5 % and 10 % levels. Particle size reduction significantly influenced PPP composition, leading to reduced bread specific volume and increased hardness, while maintaining consumer acceptability. Finer PPP particles increased bread's total phenolic and dietary fiber contents, as well as resistant starch, while reducing rapidly digestible starch, thereby lowering the estimated glycemic index. Microstructural analysis revealed that smaller PPP particles weakened gluten network by disrupting protein aggregation, consequently modifying starch digestibility and textural properties. These results highlight the potential of finer PPP particles to improve bread's nutritional profile and glycemic response, offering a sustainable strategy for developing healthier bakery products through agricultural waste upcycling.

title: Molecularly imprinted polymer-based field-effect transistor for real-time, highly selective, and sensitive aflatoxin B1 monitoring in food
abstract: In food, the simple and on-site quantitative detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), a known human carcinogen, remains a significant challenge. Shelf-stable detection methods compatible with portable electronics are scarce. This study proposes a cost-effective and promising field-effect transistor (FET) sensor technology as a potential solution. In tandem with a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) biomimetic antibody, we fabricated an FET-type sensor that uses poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) as a semiconductor to detect AFB1. The developed FET sensor exhibited high selectivity against structurally similar mycotoxins, such as zearalenone, ochratoxin A, aflatoxin G1, aflatoxin G2, and aflatoxin B2, while showing high response to low-level concentrations of AFB1 at 1 and 10 ppb. Moreover, the sensor enabled AFB1 detection across 0.35-100 ppb range. To the best of our knowledge, this study marks the first successful real-time direct sensing of a mycotoxin using MIP and FET technology, a breakthrough that could lead to new detection strategies.

title: Enhancement of color stability of cyanidin-3-O-glucoside by copigmentation with punicalagin: multispectral analysis and computer simulation
abstract: This study investigated the copigmentation mechanism between punicalagin (PUN) and cyanidin-3-O-glucoside (C3G) using spectroscopic analysis, thermodynamic evaluation, and quantum chemical modeling. UV-VIS spectra revealed enhanced absorbance and red shifts upon increasing PUN concentration to the C3G solution, indicating intensified color. Copigmentation was most effective at acidic pH (3-6) and declined at higher temperatures. Thermodynamic parameters indicated a spontaneous, exothermic interaction between PUN and C3G, involving hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking. FT-IR, 1 H NMR, and IGMH analyses confirmed these interactions and revealed that α-PUN formed more stable complexes with C3G than β-PUN, due to cooperative aromatic-polar interactions and more favorable stacking geometry. Quantum calculations supported the greater stability of α-C3G/PUN complexes. Furthermore, PUN significantly improved the thermal, light, and storage stability of C3G. These findings provide molecular-level insights into anthocyanin-ellagitannin copigmentation and demonstrate the potential of PUN as a natural copigment for improving color stability in food systems.

title: Insights into the microbial diversity of Xinjiang naan sourdough and its contributions to the production of volatile compounds
abstract: Naan, a traditional leavened flatbread, exhibits typical regional variations in flavor and texture. In this study, sourdough samples of Naan were collected from nine households across the Xinjiang region of China. Through the application of 16S rRNA and ITS rRNA high-throughput sequencing, a total of 921 bacterial genera and 441 fungal genera were identified. Among these, Fructilactobacillus, Lactiplantibacillus, Levilactobacillus, and Saccharomyces were recognized as the core microorganisms in Naan sourdough. Employing electronic nose technology and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, 166 distinct flavor compounds were detected. Of these, 29 were identified as key flavor compounds (odor activity value >1), with three specific compounds, 3-methyl-1-butanol acetate, 3-methyl-1-butanol, and 1-octen-3-ol, being particularly influential. Spearman's correlation analysis indicated that Levilactobacillus, Lactococcus, Pediococcus, Lactobacillus, Fructilactobacillus, Subdoligranulum, unclassified Basidiomycota and Sporidiobolus were critical microbial factors underlying the regional flavor differences in sourdough. Overall, the findings of this study provide theoretical support for the industrialization of Naan, which has traditionally been produced at a household scale.

title: Ultrasound-assisted extraction of peptidoglycan from Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: Structural characterization, anti-browning enhancement, and immunomodulatory effects
abstract: Bacterial peptidoglycan (PG) exhibits diverse bioactive properties and application potential, but efficient extraction and modification methods are lacking. This study optimized ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) to obtain PG from the cell walls of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum A736. Ultrasound treatment significantly increased cell wall yield and improved the physical properties of PG, including surface porosity and reduced particle size. The modified PG demonstrated anti-browning and anti-inflammatory activities, effectively reducing browning in apple, pear, and lotus root juices and modulating inflammation in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Cell assays further confirmed that PG exhibited no cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. These results indicate that UAE is an efficient method for producing multifunctional PG and highlight its potential as a natural anti-browning agent and functional ingredient, contributing to sustainable and clean-label solutions in the food industry.

title: Ultrasound-driven structural remodeling of coconut protein isolate: mechanisms of aggregation control and gel network reinforcement
abstract: Coconut protein isolate (CPI) exhibits weak thermogel properties, limiting its industrial development. In this study, we investigated the use of ultrasonic-assisted modification (100-500 W, 10-30 min) to regulate the structure, aggregation, and gel characteristics of coconut protein isolate. Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (LF-NMR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and rheological techniques revealed that ultrasonication optimized the order of β-sheets and α-helices, increased water retention capacity, and enhanced ionic and hydrophobic interactions (75.50 %). At 300 W and 20 min, the gel exhibited uniformly dense pores, 37 % increased water retention, and a storage modulus (G') of 91,006.211 Pa. Excessive power (>300 W) or duration (>20 min) caused protein over-aggregation, leading to network collapse. These findings demonstrate that ultrasound can enhance CPI gels and provide insights for structural design in plant-based foods.

title: Physically crosslinked polyphenol-chitosan edible coating for the application of walnut kernels during roasting
abstract: This study developed an edible chitosan-based coating incorporating the main polyphenols from walnut kernel seed coats (gallic acid, ferulic acid, and ellagic acid) to enhance the oxidative stability and sensory quality of fresh walnut kernels during roasting. SEM and AFM analysis revealed that gallic acid-loaded chitosan films exhibited a uniform yet rough morphology, while zeta potential measurements (36-41 mV) confirmed improved film stability. The gallic acid-loaded film demonstrated superior wettability (contact angle: 21.45°) and low water vapor permeability (2.87 × 10 -3 g/(mm∙h∙kPa)), ensuring strong adhesion. FTIR and UV-Vis analyses confirmed hydrogen-bonded crosslinking between polyphenols and chitosan. Thermal stability increased, with DSC and TGA peaks at 181.97 °C and 343 °C for the gallic acid-loaded film. Coated kernels exhibited significantly lower oxidation, with peroxide and acid values (0.04 g/100 g, 0.5 mg/g) outperforming uncoated samples. These findings suggested that gallic acid-loaded chitosan coatings effectively improve walnut kernel quality during roasting.

title: Exploration of complex-based probe for pesticide residue detection: Specific recognition achieved via the synergistic effect of coordination water and supramolecular chains
abstract: The rational design of molecular fluorescent probes from transition metal complexes is a promising chemical strategy, yet its deployment for detection pesticide residues remains largely unexplored. Herein, a novel fluorescent probe for the pesticide PDM is fabricated from the Salen-Zn complex [Zn(3,5-Cl-Salnptn) (H 2 O)] (Zn-3,5-Cl-Salnptn). Experimental results demonstrated that Zn-3,5-Cl-Salnptn possesses exceptional selectivity, a high Stern-Volmer fluorescence quenching constant (Ksv = 4.2 × 10 4 M -1 ) and a low detection limit (1.13 μM) for PDM, and to the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of the complex-based probe for PDM detection. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that the axial coordination water, which forms a supramolecular chain structure through intermolecular hydrogen bonds, is essential for the specific recognition capability of the probe. This study not only provides a novel probe model for PDM pollution monitoring but also demonstrates the significant role of crystal engineering in optimizing the performance of pesticide residue probes.

title: Cold plasma pretreatment enhances oil yield and quality in perilla seeds by reprogramming the Shikimate–phenylpropanoid–glycerophospholipid metabolic Axis
abstract: Perilla seeds are a valuable source of functional oils owing to their rich nutrient profile. Herein, perilla seeds were treated with cold plasma (CP) technology, and metabolomic and lipidomic techniques were used to analyze the post-treatment metabolite and lipid profiles, respectively. Optimized CP treatment (120 W, 9 min) increased oil yield by 8.1 % (P 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis indicated alterations in the molecular environment and distribution of lipids, suggesting physical reorganization of acyl chains. Untargeted metabolomic analysis identified 7242 metabolites, and lipidomic analysis identified 684 lipid species, including fatty acids, glycerides, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids, and sterol lipids. Differentially expressed metabolites were significantly enriched in the Shikimate-phenylpropanoid pathway (core pathway), driving the formation of an "amino acid-polysaccharide-lipid" synergistic network. Differentially expressed lipids were mainly enriched in glycerophospholipids, suggesting simultaneous remodeling of cell membrane lipids and enhancement of antioxidant capacity. Overall, this study indicates that CP treatment regulates the Shikimate-phenylpropanoid-glycerophospholipid metabolic axis, thereby optimizing the quality and functional activity of perilla seed oil. These findings provide a key molecular mechanistic basis for the application of CP technology in the green processing of oil crops and the development of functional oils.

title: Multilayered characterization of sour cream fermentation: Effects of cream origin and fermentation time on microbiota, lipid transformation, and aroma compounds
abstract: This study investigated how cream origin and fermentation time impact sour cream flavor by integrating microbial dynamics, fatty acid profiles, and volatile formation under pilot-scale conditions. Korean sour cream (KRS; produced from in-house cream) and Italian sour cream (ITS; produced from frozen cream) samples were fermented with Lactobacillus delbrueckii and Streptococcus thermophilus for 24 h. KRS exhibited greater lipid degradation, with palmitic acid decreasing by 7.8 %, and showed more dynamic volatile shifts, particularly at 12-18 h. Ethanol increased 1.35-fold and butanoic acid was 2.2-fold higher in KRS than in ITS. In contrast, ITS generated higher levels of sweeter volatiles, particularly 2-methyl-1-butanol, which was 7.6-fold higher than in KRS. L. delbrueckii was associated with late-stage, lipid-derived volatiles, and S. thermophilus was associated with early-stage compounds. Associations between fatty acids and volatiles suggested lipid metabolism contributes to flavor. These results guide cream selection and fermentation control to achieve consistent sour cream flavor.

title: Core-shell Cu@Pt nanoparticles and L-cysteine synergistically boosted electrochemical detection for wide-range melatonin detection in biological and food samples
abstract: An electrochemical detection method was proposed for the detection of Melatonin (MT) based on the synergistic signal amplification of L-Cys and core-shell Cu@Pt bimetallic nanoparticles (Cu@PtNPs). The successful fabrication of the PL-Cys/Cu@PtNPs/GCE was confirmed by characterization techniques including SEM, XRD, and TEM. The method exhibited excellent analytical performance, with a low detection limit of 0.03 μmol/L and a wide linear range across two concentration intervals: 0.1-100.0 μmol/L and 100.0-900.0 μmol/L. The method's practical applicability was successfully validated in human serum and various food samples, achieving satisfactory recovery rates of 98.73 %-99.67 % and 99.49 %-108.57 %, respectively, with relative standard deviations below 6.85 %. The novelty of this work lies in the synergistic amplification effect of the Cu@PtNPs and L-Cys and the application of density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the MT electrooxidation mechanism, confirming a 2-electron, 1-proton transfer process.

title: Apple pomace flour fractions as functional ingredients: compositional and bioactivity profiling
abstract: The growing volume of fruit juice industry waste has driven interest in apple pomace valorization. This study explores the chemical composition and bioactive potential of apple pomace, emphasizing its antioxidant and anti-aging properties. Metabolites were characterized by using advanced chromatographic techniques, showing high contents of flavonoids (1030 mg/100 g dw), carotenoids (to 50 mg/100 g dw), tocopherols and tocotrienols (to 886 μg/100 g dw), and 21 amino acids. Despite moderate antioxidant capacity (7 mmol Trolox/100 g dw), selected fractions demonstrated notable inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase (24–31 %). This highlights the potential of apple pomace for nutraceutical and food applications, supporting sustainability and circular economy. This study provides novel insight into the fraction-specific bioactive potential of apple pomace, revealing its richness in essential amino acids, vitamin E isoforms, and phenolics. Notably, certain fractions exhibited cholinesterase inhibitory activity, suggesting neuroprotective applications and highlighting apple pomace as a promising functional ingredient. • Apple pomace fractions differ in bioactive and nutritional compound content. • All vitamin E isoforms and essential amino acids were identified in apple pomace flour. • Selected fractions showed cholinesterase inhibition with neuroprotective potential. • Phenolics, carotenoids, and tocols contribute to antioxidant activity correlations. • Apple pomace offers a targeted valorization path for functional food applications.

title: Mid-infrared spectroscopy combined with chemometrics for the detection of ciprofloxacin and Bronopol® residues in milk
authors: Cleidiane Pereira da Silva dos Santos
abstract: The presence of antibiotic residues in milk poses a critical challenge to public health and food safety due to the risks of adverse reactions, disruptions in intestinal microbiota, and especially the spread of antimicrobial resistance. Although conventional detection methods such as chromatography are effective, they have limitations including high cost, lengthy analysis time, and the need for specialized labor. This study investigated the application of mid-infrared Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR-MIR), combined with chemometrics, as a rapid and effective alternative to detect ciprofloxacin residues and to evaluate the impact of the preservative Bronopol® in milk samples. In the first experiment, Bronopol® induced subtle yet consistent spectral modifications, enabling a clear distinction between sample groups through PCA across all preprocessing techniques (LBC, MSC, SNV, and SGD). Among them, the LBC approach exhibited the best performance, with PC1 and PC2 explaining 74.2 % and 18.5 % of the total variance, respectively. For classification purposes, the PLS model preprocessed with LBC achieved a sensitivity of 98.4 %, a specificity of 97.5 %, and an overall accuracy of 97.8 %, successfully discriminating all milk samples with and without Bronopol®. In the second experiment, distinct spectral variations were observed as a function of ciprofloxacin exposure time. PCA results showed that PC1 and PC2 accounted for 43.76 % and 35.67 % of the total variance, respectively, representing 79.43 % overall.The results confirm that FTIR-MIR combined with chemometric techniques is a promising, non-destructive, and efficient approach for monitoring milk contaminants and ensuring quality control and food safety compliance.

title: Exploring the chemical profile of Greek honey varieties via Liquid Chromatography coupled to Trapped Ion Mobility Spectrometry and High-Resolution Mass Spectrometry: from metabolomic fingerprint to varietal discrimination
abstract: In the present study, trapped ion mobility spectrometry (TIMS) coupled to liquid chromatography (LC) and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) was employed for the first time to determine the metabolomic composition of Greek honey. A total of 282 samples from 13 different botanical origins were analyzed, and 38 compounds were identified and quantified following target screening, like chrysin, hesperetin and pinobanksin. The application of suspect screening and the development of a novel semi-quantitative model expanded the comprehensive quantitative chemical characterization with 53 additional compounds, such as astragalin, dehydrovomifoliol and methyl syringate. A developed XGBoost classifier model, with 100 % classification in the validation set and 89 % in the test set, enabled the extraction of key authenticity markers, such as gallic acid and taxifolin for oak and pine varieties, respectively. The findings of this study provide a comprehensive investigation into honey's chemical composition, contributing to its authenticity assessment and accurate labelling. • LC-TIMS-HRMS was applied for the first time to determine honey's chemical profile. • A total of 282 Greek honey samples belonging to 13 varieties were analyzed. • Following target and suspect screening, 91 compounds were identified and quantified. • The correct classification of samples was achieved via advanced chemometrics. • Characteristic authenticity markers for each botanical origin were revealed.

title: Chitosan/gelatin-based film activated by Pickering emulsion of citrus essential oil stabilized by esterified starch/whey protein isolate fibrils: Application in preserving freshness of blueberry
abstract: This study used chitosan (CS) and gelatin (GL) as base materials and employed emulsion encapsulation technology to prepare films with citrus essential oil (CEO) as an antimicrobial agent. The results showed that the CEO emulsion was uniformly distributed throughout the interior and surface of the film, promoting the formation of a thicker and rougher layered porous structure, which significantly improved the film's elongation at break and water resistance. Additionally, the addition of the CEO emulsion significantly improved the film's thermal stability, enhanced its UV resistance, antioxidant properties, and antibacterial performance. In practical applications, the CG/WO-7 % composite film inhibited the respiration of blueberries, reduced weight loss and nutrient loss, enhanced their antioxidant enzyme activity, and suppressed the excessive accumulation of ROS. Compared with the control group, the treatment with CG/WO-7 % film extended the shelf life of blueberries by 3 days, from 5 days to 8 days.

title: Recent progress in typical foodborne spore-forming bacteria detection
abstract: Spore-forming bacteria are common foodborne pathogens known for their heat resistance and ability to form spores, making them difficult to eliminate. Their persistence poses risks to food safety and shelf life. Traditional detection methods are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and have insufficient sensitivity. Therefore, the development of rapid, accurate, and practical detection strategies is essential for food industry applications. This review summarizes recent advances in the rapid detection of four representative spore-forming bacteria: Bacillus subtilis, Bacillus cereus, Clostridium perfringens, and Clostridium botulinum. Five detection strategies were evaluated: gene amplification-based, protein-based, physicochemical property-based, multiple, and AI-enhanced detection systems. The commonalities between the various rapid tests are also analyzed, including specific molecular recognition, signal amplification, visualization of results, matrix effects, and sample pretreatment. These detection methods have broad application potential in food safety monitoring and may help guide the development of next-generation detection platforms for spore-forming bacteria.

title: Comparative effects of ultra-high pressure, ultra-high temperature, and thermal pasteurization processing on the flavor characteristics and nutritional components of freshly squeezed Hami melon juice
abstract: Conventional thermal processing causes substantial deterioration of melon juice. This study compared thermal pasteurization (TP, 65 °C/30 min), ultra-high temperature (UHT, 115 °C/5 s), and ultra-high pressure (UHP, 600 MPa/2 min) treatments on microorganisms, physicochemical parameters, bioactive compounds, and flavor characteristics of freshly squeezed Hami melon juice (FHJ). Results demonstrated that TP and UHT induced a color shift toward bright yellow, reduced soluble solids and acidity, lowered fructose content, and degraded carotenoids (β-carotene decreased by 25.7 % under UHT). In contrast, UHP preserved the original color, physicochemical properties, and sugar profile while ensuring microbial safety. Notably, UHP enhanced β-carotene content by 15.6 % and achieved a high sensory score of 16.63, retaining key aroma esters. Conversely, TP and UHT reduced total esters by 25.43 % and 31.39 %, respectively, and generated undesirable off-flavor compounds. Thus, UHP is a superior non-thermal technology for producing high-quality melon juice with minimal quality loss.

title: Trehalose substitution for sucrose improves freeze-thaw stability of Penaeus vannamei surimi: Focus on molecular interactions and cross-linking properties
abstract: This study investigated the substitution of sucrose with trehalose (2 %, 3 %, 4 %) to enhance the freeze-thaw stability of Penaeus vannamei surimi. Results exhibited a dose-dependent improvement in freeze-thaw stability with increasing trehalose concentration. Following five freeze-thaw cycles, 4 % trehalose outperformed 4 % sucrose in protecting myofibrillar protein, reflected in 5.3 % higher salt solubility and 7.8 % higher total sulfhydryl content. The improved protein stability enhanced gel cross-linking, evidenced by a 15.1 % higher gel strength and a denser microstructure. Molecular docking revealed that trehalose formed seven bonds within the myosin pocket, whereas sucrose formed only four superficial bonds and a steric hindrance. The stronger trehalose-protein interactions contributed to cryoprotection by both protecting protein structure and inhibiting ice crystal growth, thereby facilitating the formation of a superior gel network. This study provides a foundation for developing high-quality frozen shrimp surimi.

title: Aging of Citra®, Cascade, and Centennial hops under commercial storage and the discrepancies between sensory quality and HSI classification
abstract: The evolution and potential degradation of aroma quality during hop storage remain key concerns for brewers relying on year-round access to high-performing aroma varieties. This study evaluated the impact of post-pelleting/packaging aging under commercial storage on the chemical and sensory profiles of Citra®, Cascade, and Centennial hops. Across 1- to 6-year-old samples, we assessed oil composition, thiol content, hop storage index (HSI), and sensory attributes in both hops and beers brewed with fresh versus aged samples. Cascade consistently showed aging-related changes chemically and sensorially. Centennial displayed subtler chemical shifts, yet sensory analysis still revealed significant differences. In contrast, Citra proved highly resilient, with minimal changes. Thiol content, free and oxidized, was not markedly affected by aging or oxygen exposure but varied by lot and year, with hop variety being the dominant factor. These findings highlight the variety-dependent nature of hop aging and suggest that HSI may not reliably predict sensory performance.

title: Chemical composition of lettuce following root-application of osmolytes in hydroponic cultivation
abstract: Hydroponically produced lettuce ( Lactuca sativa L.,) naturally accumulates high amounts of nitrate in its leaves, and this compound is harmful for human health. Osmolytes affect the osmotic potential of plant cells and can potentially reduce the accumulation of nitrate. The potential of osmolytes mannitol and glycerol was compared to glycinebetaine —which is known to decrease the nitrate content of lettuce— in two hydroponic experiments. Plant samples were collected at various time points and analyzed for minerals, free- and hydrolyzed amino acids, soluble sugars, osmolality, and nitrate. All three osmolytes reduced the nitrate content in lettuce leaves and increased the contents of dry matter, soluble sugars, and some amino acids. The effect of mannitol and glycerol on lettuce nitrate content and quality were similar to those induced by glycinebetaine. Thus, the quality of hydroponically grown lettuce can be controlled with diverse types of root-applied osmolytes. • Edible quality of lettuce can be improved with osmolytes. • Osmolytes decrease the nitrate content in lettuce. • Osmolytes increase the sugar content in lettuce. • Osmolytes increase the total content of hydrolyzed amino acids in lettuce.

title: Aroma enhancement in clay jar-aged wine: 2-acetyl-1H-pyrrole at subthreshold modulates perception of fruity esters
abstract: The aroma modulation of Cabernet Sauvignon wine aged in Chinese clay jars was systematically studied, in comparison with stainless steel tank-aged controls. Integrated chemical and sensory analyses showed a significant enhancement of fruity aromas and a reduction of green pepper notes in clay jar-aged wine. Chemical profiling revealed decreased concentrations of off-flavor compounds (e.g., 3-methylthiopropanal from 13.2 to 5.59 μg/L), which is proposed to result from selective adsorption by the porous clay, and the exclusive presence of subthreshold 2-acetyl-1H-pyrrole (1.59 μg/L), which enhanced key fruity esters by lowering their detection thresholds by up to 4-fold (e.g., ethyl pentanoate, p < 0.001) in controlled sensory tests. Thus, clay jar aging refines wine aroma not only by removing negative attributes but also by enhancing positive ones through perceptual modulation, providing a scientific basis for its use as an alternative aging vessel.

title: Volatile evolutions during solid-state fermentation of oats by mono- and co-cultures: A Flavoromic approach using classical chemometric and machine learning techniques
abstract: While solid-state fermentation (SSF) can enhance the bioactive potential of oats, the temporal dynamics of volatile compound formation, particularly in mixed microbial systems, remain poorly characterized. Such volatiles contribute not only to sensory attributes but also reflect underlying metabolic interactions during fermentation. This study investigated volatile evolution in oat SSF with Rhizopus oligosporus in mono-culture and co-culture with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum over 120 h. Fifty-five volatile compounds spanning ten chemical classes were identified. With the exception of aldehydes, most classes increased over time, with the co-culture producing higher levels of alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, and ketones. Branched-chain, Strecker aldehyde peaks decreased during SSF in the co-culture system, indicating complementary metabolic exchange. Non-linear random forest regression better captured volatile trajectories than linear partial least squares regression. Together, these results provide a SSF system-level fingerprint of how mono- and co-culture SSF differentially shape oat volatile profiles, informing future development of fermented oat products.

title: Unraveling the flavor evolution mechanism in liquid-smoked rainbow trout through integrated lipidomics and flavoromics
abstract: Liquid-smoked rainbow trout (LSRT) is prized for its distinctive flavor, yet its flavor formation mechanism remains unclear. In this study, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and lipid profiles were dynamically monitored in fresh rainbow trout, salted rainbow trout, and different stages of LSRT (LSRT1-LSRT3) through integrated lipidomics and flavoromics. Results showed that lipid hydrolysis (acid value increased from 0.84 to 2.98 mg KOH/g) and oxidation (thiobarbituric acid reactive substance value increased from 0.28 to 3.94 mg/kg) were intensified throughout the salting and smoking stages. Lipidomics identified 1389 lipid molecular species, with triglycerides and phospholipids decreasing significantly. Flavoromics revealed 8 VOCs as potential flavor markers, including heptanal, 2-methoxy-phenol, hexanal, 1-nonen-4-ol, 2-methyl-pentanoic acid, 3,5,5-trimethyl-2-hexene, octanal, and 2,3-octanedione. Correlation analysis demonstrated significant negative correlations between differential VOCs and lipid molecules (glyceride and phospholipid) mainly containing C16:0, C18:0, C18:1, C18:2 and C18:3 fatty acids. Ultimately, a potential lipid-mediated flavor mechanism of LSRT was firstly proposed.

title: Oxidized hyaluronic acid-based biodegradable hydrogels loaded with potassium cinnamate: A sustainable coating for postharvest grape preservation
abstract: Fruit preservation materials are crucial for inhibiting post-harvest spoilage and extending fruit shelf life. However, a notable limitation of existing preservation materials is their frequent failure to simultaneously exhibit robust antibacterial activity, excellent biocompatibility, and effective shelf-life extension. Based on this, the present study intends to develop a potassium cinnamate-loaded hydrogel (PC@OHA-cl-SD gel ) for addressing the aforementioned challenges in post-harvest grape preservation. Primarily, potassium cinnamate (PC) was used as an antibacterial agent to prepare PC@OHA-cl-SD gel . The low cytotoxicity, high biocompatibility, and potent antibacterial activity endow PC@OHA-cl-SD gel with an application in post-harvest grape preservation. Storage experiments demonstrated that coating grapes with PC@OHA-cl-SD gel inhibited pH fluctuations, weight loss, and spoilage over a 10-day storage. PC@OHA-cl-SD gel effectively maintained the quality of post-harvest grapes and extended their shelf-life. Therefore, PC@OHA-cl-SD gel holds great promise as a novel preservation material for post-harvest grapes, with potential extensibility to other perishable fruits that face similar post-harvest quality deterioration issues.

title: Heat-induced conformational transitions and self-assembly of millet prolamin: Multiscale structural analyses
abstract: Heat-induced structural transitions and assembly of millet prolamin (25-100 °C, 30 min) were profiled across scales. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed minimal thermal stability around 50 °C (peak temperature 65.7 °C; enthalpy change 114.6 J/g), consistent with a perturbed conformational state. At 70 °C, thermal parameters partially recovered and the particle size distribution narrowed, indicating a restructuring regime with strengthened intermolecular associations. At 90-100 °C, fibrillar aggregates formed, as evidenced by enhanced thioflavin T fluorescence, low polydispersity, increased zeta-potential magnitude and β-sheet enrichment in FT-IR spectra, while amino acid composition remained unchanged. Across these temperatures, aggregation was closely associated with hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding. Overall, the data delineate three temperature-dependent structural regimes for millet prolamin-perturbation, restructuring and stabilization of compact aggregates-providing a practical framework for designing thermal processes to tailor the structure of plant proteins.

title: Determination of pesticides, antibiotics, PAHs, PCBs, and plasticizers in honeybees, honey, and other bee products – modified QuEChERS method. Method review for 2018–2024
abstract: Interest in the safety of bee products such as honey, beeswax, bee bread, pollen, and royal jelly continues to grow. Although valued for their nutritional and therapeutic properties, these matrices may accumulate pesticides, antibiotics, PAHs, PCBs, and plasticizers from environmental and apicultural sources. Given their complex composition, reliable contaminant analysis requires efficient sample-preparation strategies. This review critically evaluates 50 studies published between 2018 and 2024 that applied standard or modified QuEChERS protocols to bee-derived matrices. Key trends include the predominant use of acidified acetonitrile, increasing reliance on advanced sorbents such as C18, Z-Sep, EMR-Lipid, and graphene, and a shift toward multi-residue LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS workflows offering high sensitivity across diverse analytes. Greenness assessment using AGREE revealed considerable methodological variability. Overall, the findings highlight both the versatility and limitations of modified QuEChERS methods and identify future needs, including greener extraction solutions and the analytical monitoring of emerging contaminants.

title: Corrigendum to “Smartphone-based digital image colorimetry for rapid benzoyl peroxide detection in wheat flour” [Food Chem. 496(Part 2) (2025) 146796]
Pressure-driven depolymerization of Antarctic krill aggregates: Structural reconfiguration and gelation-enhanced functionality
abstract: This study investigated the effects of ultra-high pressure (UHP) technology as a non-thermal method on the depolymerization, structure, and functional properties of Antarctic krill protein (AKP) aggregates. UHP treatment significantly improved AKP functionality. Solubility notably increased from 91.4 % (Control) to 97.1 % at 600 MPa, concomitant with a pressure-dependent decrease in turbidity. Particle size analysis confirmed a depolymerization effect, with the main particle size peak shifting from 232.8 nm (Control) to 72.25 nm (600 MPa). Structural analysis revealed UHP-induced protein unfolding, evidenced by a 29.8 % increase in surface hydrophobicity (at 400 MPa), a decrease in total sulfhydryl content, and a conformational transition from α-helix (32.50 % in control) to β-sheet (30.40 % at 600 MPa). These structural modifications significantly enhanced gelation functionality; the storage modulus peaked at 600 MPa, corresponding to the formation of a dense and uniform microscopic network.

title: Unraveling the aromatic essence of baked green tea using sensomics: insights from three representative cultivars
abstract: Tea cultivars significantly influence aroma, yet essential odorants linked to specific cultivars remain underexplored. In this study, an integrated sensomics approach identified 57, 50, and 59 odorants in three representative baked green tea cultivars using sequential stir-bar sorptive extraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry/olfactometry, ultimately pinpointing eight key cultivar-specific odorants. The "sweet/green" notes in 'Zhongcha 108' were primarily attributed to cedrol (18.52 ng/mL, enhancing aroma by up to 176 % compared to the blank matrix). Indole, methyl salicylate, geraniol, and γ-dodecalactone were closely associated with the "floral" character of 'Zhongcha 302' (1.30-895.86 ng/mL, increasing aroma by up to 510 %). Viridiflorol, theaspirane B, and α-ionone contributed to the "sweet/floral" notes in 'Fuding Dabaicha' (trace levels to 12.47 ng/mL, enhancing aroma by up to 163 %). Furthermore, the aroma profile of 'Zhongcha 302' was successfully reconstructed based on its quantified odorants, achieving >90 % similarity to the original tea.

title: Construction of correlation networks and metabolic pathways reveals the self-gel and flavor formation mechanisms of silver carp surimi during natural fermentation based on volatile and non-volatile metabonomics
abstract: Poor gel and flavor of freshwater fish surimi are not conductive to high-quality product development. In this study, fermentation was used to improve the gel and flavor of silver carp surimi, followed by mechanism clarification. The gel strength, hardness, and chewiness significantly increased after fermentation. Metabonomics showed that most of core volatile and non-volatile metabolites were obviously improved after fermentation. Correlation analysis revealed that the burst of Lactococcus and Lactobacillus led to the self-gel without heating and improvement of flavor metabolites. Metabolic pathways showed that the oxidation of fatty acids and metabolisms of glucose and amino acids by Lactococcus and Lactobacillus contributed the most to the volatile flavor formation, while the free amino acids and peptides were responsible for the taste formation. The lactic acid bacteria including Lactococcus and Lactobacillus can be isolated as starters to further improve the flavor and safety of silver carp surimi in the future.

title: Impact of oil extraction pretreatments on biodegradable food packaging foam fabricated from Tigernut starch: Sustainable valorization of Tigernut oil production by-products
abstract: The severe environmental challenges posed by the production of synthetic plastics urgently demand addressing. This study innovatively utilizes cake remaining after oil extraction from tigernut, a non-grain novel starch resource, to develop biodegradable starch-based foam. Based on this, the study systematically analyzed impacts of oil extraction pretreatments (roasting, microwave and extrusion) on the physicochemical and biodegradable properties of tigernut starch-based foam (TSF). The results showed that compared to untreated TSF, microwaved and extruded TSF exhibited compact network structures. Compared to degree of short-range ordered structures (0.98) of untreated TSF, pretreated samples showed enhanced short-range order (1.16-1.56). Compared to untreated TSF (thermal stability (50 % residual mass): 310.48 °C; springiness: 44.91; water absorption: 705.28 %), microwave improved thermal stability (312.98 °C), while roasting enhanced springiness (48.11) and reduced water absorption (627.40 %). Notably, all TSF exhibited excellent biodegradability (residual mass: 28.45 %-50.56 %), especially extruded TSF (28.45 %). These findings showed that TSF as biodegradable material with promising applications in food packaging and protective transport. Furthermore, this provides theoretical basis for sustainable valorization of tigernut by-products.

title: Polysaccharide structure–activity mechanisms regulating SPI-PP composite hydrogels
abstract: This study systematically investigated three anionic polysaccharides to modulate the structure and functionalities of soy protein isolate (SPI)-potato protein (PP) composite hydrogels. Results demonstrated that sodium alginate (SA) significantly enhanced hardness, elasticity, and adhesiveness via Ca 2+ -mediated "egg-box" crosslinking and strong electrostatic interactions with both SPI and PP. SA also increased the loss modulus (G") and reached optimal network compactness at 10 % concentration, yielding a water-holding capacity (WHC) of 99.94 %. Conversely, κ-carrageenan (KC) improved adhesiveness through hydrogen bonding and helical aggregation but reduced pore integrity via charge neutralization and phase separation, forming uniformly micro-scaled particulate structures with near-identical densification at 10 % and 15 %. Xanthan gum (XG) substantially elevated the storage modulus (G') via its rigid helical backbones, forming interpenetrating networks with SPI and PP, which conferred exceptional elasticity and shear resistance. Collectively, SPI served as the primary gel matrix, PP enhanced network homogeneity and interactions, and anionic polysaccharides acted as structure-directing agents that precisely modulated gel properties through specific binding mechanisms.

title: Construction and textural modification of soft surimi gel from spanish mackerel (Scomberomorus niphonius) by polysaccharides
abstract: The effects and mechanisms of four polysaccharides (xanthan gum (XG), pectin (PE), curdlan (CUR), and chitosan (CS)) at 2 % (w/w) concentrations on the gelation of Spanish mackerel surimi were investigated. The gel strength, hardness and chewiness of surimi added with XG and PE decreased by 33.6 %-84.9 %, while those of the CUR and CS groups increased by 6.2 % to 38.9 %. Additionally, the incorporation of PE reduced water holding capacity and increased cooking loss. According to the International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative framework, gels supplemented with XG and PE met levels 5 and 6 standards, respectively. Through strong electrostatic repulsion and steric hindrance, XG and PE impeded the approach and cross-linking of myofibrillar proteins and competed for water binding, which collectively weakened hydrophobic interactions, inhibited the formation of a dense gel network, and resulted in a soft and porous weak gel structure. This research provides insights into the development of dysphagia-friendly foods.

title: Development of a targeted mass spectrometry method for porcine pancreas marker peptides detection in protein hydrolysates
abstract: Protein hydrolysates are widely used in health foods, but undisclosed enzymatic sources, particularly porcine pancreas, raising concerns regarding food safety, allergenicity, and dietary restrictions. To address this issue, this study comprehensively characterized the porcine pancreas proteome, identifying 418 proteins and establishing 50 °C autolysis to ensure consistent peptide profiles. Three homologous highly specific α-amylase-derived marker peptides, VTNPSRPW, VVTNPSRPW, and IVVTNPSRPW, were selected and validated, and a targeted LC-MS/MS assay was established with porcine pancreas detection limits of 0.5 %, 1 %, and 5 % (w/w), respectively. Application of this method to commercial products revealed the presence of porcine peptides in samples labeled as "animal-free" which was further proved by on-site investigation. This study provides a robust and practical approach for verifying the species origin of enzymatic preparations in protein hydrolysates, enhancing traceability, food safety, and regulatory compliance. To our knowledge, it represents the first systematic investigation into enzyme source authenticity in such products.

title: Analysis of aroma and flavor changes in hawthorn during heat treatment by electronic sensory systems and GC-IMS
abstract: Hawthorn is valued for its pleasant flavor and health benefits. Heat treatment is commonly used to enhance its nutritional quality, but it significantly alters the aroma and taste of the fruit. Sensory evaluation of these changes remains limited, and the underlying mechanisms are not fully understood. This study employed electronic tongue, electronic nose, liquid chromatography, and GC-IMS to analyze sensory and compositional changes in hawthorn during heat treatment. Results showed a significant increase in 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), a Maillard reaction product, which correlated strongly with bitterness measured by the electronic tongue. Odor changes detected by the electronic nose were closely associated with differential volatile components identified via GC-IMS. Among these, 2-methyl-1-pentanol showed strong correlations with multiple electronic nose sensors, indicating its notable influence on odor changes. This work provides sensory and compositional insights into flavor changes during heat treatment and offers technical references for optimizing processing techniques and developing high-quality products.

title: Facile construction of bifunctional and stable covalent organic frameworks for efficient extraction and ultrasensitive determination of neonicotinoid insecticides
abstract: Efficient extraction and sensitive determination of neonicotinoid insecticides in intricate matrix remain a challenge due to their high-water solubility and trace level. Herein, an irreversible 4-carboxyl-quinoline linked COF, named CQ-COF TAPB-DHTA/DMTA , was synthesized via a one-pot multicomponent Doebner reaction. The CQ-COF TAPB-DHTA/DMTA incorporated abundant bifunctional hydroxyl and carboxyl groups while exhibiting enhanced hydrophilicity and excellent chemical stability. Then, solid-phase microextraction (SPME) fiber based on CQ-COF TAPB-DHTA/DMTA was prepared and exhibited exceptional durability and remarkable extraction performance for eight neonicotinoids. After coupling with ultra-high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), an ultrasensitive analytical method was developed with low limits of detection (0.51-3.5 ng L -1 ), wide linear range, and satisfactory correlation coefficients (R 2 ≥ 0.9910), and was successfully used for analysis of neonicotinoids in water and honey samples. This work highlights the potential of multifunctional and stable COFs for the extraction and analysis of polar pollutants from intricate matrices.

title: Synergistic antenna-effect-driven multi-channel ratiometric wearable sensor for visual on-site detection and accurate discrimination of fluoroquinolone analogs
abstract: The misuse and overuse of fluoroquinolone antibiotics (FQs) pose a global threat, driving the need for effective detection methods. This study developed a multi-channel ratiometric sensor by integrating cadmium telluride quantum dots (CdTe QDs) and terbium-based coordination polymers for the detection and discrimination of FQs. The addition of enrofloxacin (ENR) triggers an antenna effect, enhancing green Tb(III) emission and reducing red CdTe QDs fluorescence, resulting in a distinct color change. Furthermore, a point-of-care testing system, comprising a smartphone detector and a wearable fingertip sensor, was constructed for rapid and real-time ENR detection, achieving high sensitivity with detection limits of 4.7 nM and 13.1 nM for spectrometer- and paper-based sensors, respectively. The practical applicability was demonstrated through satisfactory recoveries (91.7 %-110.7 %) in food samples, confirming its anti-interference capability. Finally, by expanding this platform into an array format, the sensor successfully differentiated ENR analogs, highlighting its broad potential for contaminant monitoring.

title: Development of a fluorescence imaging system for real-time assessment and monitoring of the quality deterioration in Lapins cherries during refrigerated storage
abstract: This study presents a novel fluorescence imaging approach for non-destructive quality monitoring of Lapins cherries during refrigerated storage. Seven quality indices-including soluble solids content (SSC), titratable acidity (TA), pH, firmness, and color parameters (L ⁎ , a ⁎ , b ⁎ )-were analyzed to evaluate their dynamic changes. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to integrate these indices into a comprehensive quality indicator. Chlorophyll fluorescence characteristics exhibited a strong correlation with cherry quality deterioration during storage. Accordingly, a fluorescence imaging system (440 nm excitation/690 nm emission) was developed to capture chlorophyll fluorescence images at different storage intervals. Regression and classification models were then established using the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to predict quality indices and assess freshness. The comprehensive indicator model provided satisfactory results, with R c 2 and R p 2 of 0.925 and 0.838. The classification model achieved high accuracy in detecting fresh and spoiled cherries, with calibration and prediction accuracies of 100 % and 96.6 %, respectively.

title: Kapok-fiber-supported liquid–liquid extraction enables rapid and convenient determination of five phenoxycarboxylic acid herbicide residues in beverages and oral liquids
abstract: In this study, a novel green and miniaturized sample preparation method, named tributyl phosphate (TBP)-based kapok-fiber-supported liquid microextraction (TBP-KF-SLME), was developed to determine five phenoxycarboxylic acid herbicides in beverages and oral liquids. The extraction of phenoxycarboxylic acid herbicides was achieved using natural kapok-fiber and tributyl phosphate. A unique in-syringe platform, in which the kapok fiber was packed within the needle tip, facilitated the integration of extraction and enrichment through straightforward push-pull movements with 6 min. This method demonstrated excellent linearity (R 2 ≥ 0.999), sensitivity (limits of detection: 0.006-0.024 μg/mL), recovery (92.3-104.6%), stability (relative standard deviation <6.63%), and enrichment factor (9.36-13.47). The validated in-syringe TBP-KF-SLME method was successfully applied to real samples, showcasing high accuracy and precision. A rigorous evaluation using six green assessment tools revealed that, TBP-KF-SLME offers a sustainable and efficient strategy for the analysis of herbicide residues.

title: Discovery of novel metabolites in Colombian specialty coffee via multiplatform untargeted metabolomics during solid-state fermentation
abstract: The metabolite composition of Arabica coffee during solid-state fermentation remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined changes in mucilage and endosperm metabolites on a Colombian smallholder farm using gas and liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (GC-QTOF-MS and LC-QTOF-MS). Across three batches, more than 600 compounds were detected in both matrices. Samples were collected at 0, 5 and 10 h, with depth-resolved sampling in one batch. Among 63 GC-QTOF-MS library-identified compounds, 42 discriminated between endosperm and mucilage, while 11 and 2 differentiated fermentation time in mucilage and endosperm, respectively. From 557 LC-QTOF-MS(+) features, 206 were discriminant and annotated at varying confidence levels. More discriminant metabolites were found in mucilage than in endosperm, although endosperm showed the highest number at the end of fermentation. In total, 269 compounds were identified, including 193 newly reported in coffee fermentation. The findings highlight distinct metabolite fingerprints, and novel metabolites of potential importance.

title: Thermal aging treatment of starch-based straws: The role of temperature-time effects on structure and functional performance
abstract: Starch-based straws are susceptible to retrogradation during storage, which reduces their practical value. This study aimed to investigate the effects of thermal aging temperature and duration on the structure and properties of starch-based straws prepared by twin-screw extrusion. Straws treated at 90 °C for 4 h and at 30 °C for 7 days exhibited the highest short-range order and degree of double-helix structure, respectively. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that thermal aging at 30 °C facilitated the formation of more complete orthorhombic crystal structure. However, relative crystallinity decreased to 9.80% and 9.22% after treatment at 30 °C and 90 °C, respectively, due to hydrogen bond disruption and starch chain rearrangement. Moreover, after 32 h of thermal aging at 90 °C, the dissolution rate decreased by 5.16% when immersed in water at 70 °C. This study provides potential for performance improvement and industrial production of starch-based straws.

title: Unravelling the role of pueraria nanofiber in emulsion formation and potential in stabilizing emulsion gels: A focus on structural-physicochemical properties
abstract: Pueraria nanofibers (PNFs) derived from high-yield, renewable processing residues can exhibit a favorable hydrophilic-lipophilic balance under mild processing. This research explored the impact of NaOH and H₂SO₄ concentrations during the extraction process on the structure and emulsifying performance of PNFs. On this basis, the influence of oil phase fraction (Φ) and PNF concentration (w) on the gelation properties of the resulting Pickering emulsion gels (EGs) was further examined. The PNFs were filamentous nanocellulose of cellulose type I. The crystallinity of the PNF 0.5-1-60 reached 73.32 %, the Zeta potential was -32.01 mV, and the contact angle reached 38.88°. Emul 0.5-1-60 showed no detectable oil separation during long-term storage or centrifugation, while its apparent viscosity at low shear rates was approximately 16-fold higher than that of the poorest-performing sample. EG 0.4-2 exhibited the smallest droplet size (D₄,₃ ≈ 19.63 μm) and the greatest stability, showing only 2.3 % reduction in emulsification index after 180 days of storage.

title: Flavor perception in the oral processing of mixed grain foods: Flavor release and AI
abstract: Despite the growing demand for nutritious dietary options, grain-based products remain underused in the marketplace, primarily owing to their coarse texture and unpalatable taste. This paper investigates the flavor perception of mixed grains during oral processing by elucidating the formation and release mechanisms of mixed grain flavors. The perception of flavor is mediated by the synergistic interaction of multiple senses, including sight, touch, smell, hearing, and taste. These senses not only independently shape the perception of food flavor but also modulate flavor perception through cross-modal sensory interactions. Furthermore, a flavor prediction conceptual framework is develop by combining flavoromics and artificial intelligence(AI) technologies to assist in the design of higher quality mixed grain foods. The combined application of flavoromics technology and AI technology can systematic fusion of multidimensional chemical and sensory data, with the aim of providing a powerful assistant for research in the field of flavor engineering.

title: A comprehensive review on inhibitory effects and mechanisms of plant polyphenols on acrylamide and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural formation in heat-processed foods
abstract: Thermal processing is widely used in food manufacturing to enhance flavor and extend shelf life. However, it also facilitates the formation of hazardous substances such as acrylamide (AA) and 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF). The incorporation of materials rich in plant polyphenols as a promising strategy for mitigating these hazardous substances in heat-processed foods. This review provides an evaluation of the inhibitory effects of different plant polyphenol sources (plant raw materials, plant extracts, polyphenol compounds) on the formation of AA and 5-HMF. It further analyzes key factors influencing their inhibitory efficacy and elucidates the underlying mechanisms involved by plant polyphenols. On this basis, potential strategies to enhance the inhibitory efficacy of plant polyphenols on AA and 5-HMF are discussed. This review aims to provide valuable insights into the current studies, and further guide the subsequent research and application of plant polyphenols in inhibiting AA and 5-HMF in heat-processed foods.

title: Photothermal mediated bionanocomposite films with pasteurization-like activity for tangerine preservation
abstract: Herein, we propose a composite packaging film with pasteurization-like activity by doping the MnO x /MoO x into chitosan film (CMM). The prepared CMM films exhibited excellent photothermal activity, which was inherited from the material. Under near infrared (NIR) irradiation, CMM films showed pasteurization-like activity due to the photothermal performance, in which CMM 0.1 was able to kill 99.15 % of E. coli and 99.39 % of S. aureus. CMM 0.1 film also showed good light transmittance (T 660 = 69.2 %), tensile strength (TS = 41.4 MPa) and UV-light/water vapor/ oxygen barrier ability. Less than 4.28 % of hemolysis rate and more than 92.89 % of cell survival rate after being treated with MnO x /MoO x demonstrated the biosafety of the CMM films. The shelf life of tangerines treated with CMM 0.1 + NIR can be extended from 9 days to 21 days, in which the nutrients can be retained well during storage. Our work provides a new perspective on the combination of pasteurization and packaging technology.

title: Strain-specific metabolic endpoints and predictive phase classification in gnotobiotic kimchi fermentation
abstract: Fermentation is driven by dynamic interactions between substrates and microbial communities. However, the complexity of natural consortia limits their predictive control. To address this problem, we developed a gnotobiotic kimchi model via inoculation with defined lactic acid bacterial (LAB) consortia and individual strains under controlled temperatures. Consortium fermentations exhibited temperature-dependent growth and acidification, with stable proliferation under 6 °C and 10 °C, whereas 15 °C induced a rapid shift in community structure. Phase normalisation revealed convergence of microbial and metabolite profiles along a shared successional pattern. Machine learning identified a nine-metabolite signature (lactate, sucrose, fructose, glycine, glucose, succinate, threonine, choline, and glutamate) that accurately classified the fermentation phases with robust performance across internal and external datasets. Network analyses highlighted Leuconostoc mesenteroides and Lactococcus lactis as keystone metabolic species, whereas mono-association fermentation uncovered strain-specific metabolic endpoints and strategies. These findings established a predictive framework for LAB-driven kimchi fermentation. • Gnotobiotic kimchi models reveal temperature-dependent LAB growth and acidification. • Phase-resolved analysis uncovered robust LAB-driven fermentation dynamics. • Machine learning identified nine key metabolites for accurate phase classification. • Leuconostoc mesenteroides and Lactococcus lactis as metabolic keystone species. • Mono-association fermentations defined strain-specific metabolic endpoints and strategies.

title: Investigation of browning and antioxidant degradation in peach pulp: metabolomics insights and quality improvement strategies
abstract: This study elucidated the impact of traditional pulping (TP, 0 MPa) on the quality and metabolomes of peach pulp, and evaluated vacuum pulping (VP, -0.1 MPa) and nitrogen-assisted pulping (NP, 0 MPa) as strategies for quality enhancement. Metabolomics revealed that TP inhibited the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites and accelerated the degradation of amino acids and flavonoids. VP and NP reduced browning by 76.44-85.31 % and limited the increase in color difference (ΔE) by 9.52-87.61 %. Antioxidant retention was 48.95-93.79 % in TP, 78.88-98.65 % in VP, and 75.18-97.26 % in NP. Soluble protein increased by 56.38-250.63 %, 21.37-191.61 %, and 21.52-189.71 %, while reactive oxygen species rose by 18.01-288.20 %, 1.62-54.43 %, and 4.38-65.47 % in TP, VP, and NP, respectively. Radical-scavenging capacities were highest in VP (85.39-96.97 %) and NP (76.60-94.26 %), compared to TP (39.53-80.88 %). Overall, VP and NP effectively mitigated TP-induced quality degradation, and the findings provide valuable metabolomic and oxidative-stress insights that are crucial for improving pulping processes.

title: Effect of roasting on the chemical profiles of white and black sesame seeds during accelerated storage
abstract: Roasted sesame seeds are highly valued for their distinctive flavor; however, their quality is affected by roasting temperature and storage. Herein, we examined the effects of roasting (160 °C-200 °C) on the chemical profiles of black and white sesame seeds during 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 days of accelerated storage. Results revealed the same trends in both white and black sesame seeds. Specifically, at a roasting temperature of >160 °C, the acid and peroxide values were the highest after 20 days of storage, whereas tocopherol content decreased significantly (p < 0.05). Pyrazines and phenols were identified as the two most abundant volatile compounds, and their contents significantly decreased during accelerated storage. After 15 days of storage, the intensity of nutty, smoky, and caramel aromas significantly decreased (p < 0.05), whereas that of green aroma notably increased (p < 0.05). These findings provide important insights for maintaining the quality of roasted white and black sesame seeds.

title: Current advances in LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS coupled with chemometrics for integrated food analysis and quality control
abstract: The continuous evolution of food analysis is being pushed by the integration of cutting-edge liquid and gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS), which have transcended the limitations of traditional analytical techniques through their exceptional sensitivity, specificity, and throughput. This review presents a critical and forward-looking overview of recent advancements in LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS technologies, emphasizing their pivotal roles in addressing contemporary challenges in food safety surveillance, fraud detection, nutritional profiling, and overall quality assurance. In parallel, the emergence of advanced chemometric strategies spanning multivariate statistics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence has redefined how complex datasets are processed, interpreted, and visualized, enabling more robust, high-resolution insights into food composition and integrity. By synthesizing the latest developments in both instrumentation and data science, this review highlights the synergistic potential of analytical chemistry and chemometrics to set new standards in foodomics, traceability, and risk assessment. Ultimately, these innovations contribute to greater transparency, regulatory compliance, and consumer trust in the global food supply chain.

title: Advancement of a hen-free approach for highly efficient zinc enrichment of eggs through the shell: investigate the effect of UV exposure
abstract: Eggs are a vital source of high-quality protein and essential micronutrients; however, global zinc deficiencies persist as a widespread public health concern. Conventional zinc fortification methods, which rely on dietary supplementation for hens, are often inefficient, costly, and environmentally unsustainable. This study introduces an innovative hen-free approach to zinc enrichment by utilizing UV modification of eggshells to enhance permeability and facilitate zinc enrichment.
