Under combined homogenization-sterilization conditions, elevated homogenization pressure and cycle numbers reduced oil droplet size and increased interfacial protein content, leading to enhanced absolute zeta potential, emulsifying activity, and stability. However, excessive homogenization (e.g., 2-3 cycles under high pressure) triggered droplet aggregation, reduced interfacial protein coverage, and intensified protein-lipid co-oxidation, as demonstrated by elevated concentrations of N'-formyl-l-kynurenine, di-tyrosine, and malondialdehyde. Curve fitting and correlation analysis identified significant relationships between homogenization cycles number/pressure, emulsifying activity/stability indices, and co-oxidation levels. A predictive regression model (R 2 = 0.967, p < 0.05) successfully quantified the effects of homogenization parameters and interfacial characteristics on oxidative stability (malondialdehyde content). Hierarchical clustering identified the S-2-40 sample demonstrated optimal emulsifying performance with minimal co-oxidation products. These findings establish theoretical and technological foundations for engineering high-stability preterm infant formulas.

title: Avocado ripeness classification using handheld Raman spectroscopy: addressing data imbalance with machine learning and resampling techniques
abstract: Food waste is a global concern, partially caused by destructive testing and inaccurate visual inspections that misclassify quality. This study developed a machine learning-assisted handheld Raman spectroscopy for non-destructive classification of avocado ripeness. A total of 1274 Raman spectra were collected alongside firmness and internal quality measurements for model training. Characteristic peaks reflected chlorophyll decline and anthocyanin increase during ripening. A two-layer one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) outperformed models wither more layers (i.e., 4 and 6 layers) on the original imbalanced dataset, achieving a receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.831. In practice, ripeness stages often have uneven sample sizes, challenging classification. The synthetic minority oversampling technique improved the performance of traditional models, with support vector machine and random forest achieving ROC-AUC values ≥0.786. The 1D-CNN, however, performed best on the original dataset. These results highlight a rapid, non-destructive, in-field approach to food ripeness assessment, offering a practical tool to reduce food waste.

title: Fe-Cu bimetal/N-doped carbon nanotubes with oxygen vacancies and multivalent redox cycling for ultrasensitive electrochemical detection of benomyl in fruit samples
abstract: Valence cycling in metal-carbon composites is critical for electrochemical pesticide detection, yet conventional single-metal systems often suffer from limited electron transfer and poor active site utilization. To address this, a Fe-Cu bimetallic catalyst embedded in oxygen vacancy-rich N-doped carbon nanotubes (FeCu-DMSC) was developed for ultrasensitive detection of benomyl (BN). The incorporation of Cu induces lattice distortion around Fe-N coordination centers, generating abundant oxygen vacancies within metal oxides that facilitate charge migration and strengthen BN adsorption. The Fe 3+ /Cu 2+ ↔ Fe 2+ /Cu + redox cycling promotes reversible electron exchange, enhancing catalytic responsiveness. Additionally, a bamboo-like carbon matrix encapsulates Fe-Cu nanoparticles, stabilizing active sites and preventing aggregation. This synergistic structure yields excellent analytical performance: a low detection limit of 0.012 nM, broad linear range (0.05 nM-10 μM), and high reproducibility (RSD < 1.23%). Application in spiked fruit samples (recovery 93.01-103.04%) confirms its practical utility for pesticide residue monitoring in food matrices.

title: Development of a pomelo pectin–based microencapsulation system for Akkermansia muciniphila
abstract: Pomelo (Citrus maxima) is rich in polyphenolic compounds. Pectin extracted from pomelo peel offers various health benefits. This study evaluated the properties of pomelo pulp extracts and pectin at different ratios. Microencapsulation was employed to enhance stability and assess protective effects on next-generation probiotics. Naringin, the primary active compound, was quantified at 2.58 mg/mL in pulp extract and 1.66 mg/mL in pectin. The pectin was classified as low-methoxyl pectin (LM), with a degree of esterification (DE) of 35.0%, equivalent weight (EW) of 323 mg/mol, methoxyl content (MeO) of 5.16%, and total anhydrogalacturonic acid of 83.79% in this study. Microcapsules were prepared using 1%, 2%, and 3% sodium alginate, achieving encapsulation efficiencies of 24.4%, 40.5%, and 66.7%, respectively. Stability tests confirmed that 3% sodium alginate microcapsules exhibited optimal encapsulation efficiency and stability. In probiotic culture experiments, Akkermansia muciniphila growth and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production were significantly enhanced by microcapsules containing pomelo pulp extract and pectin. These findings suggest that pomelo-based microcapsules may promote gut health by supporting next-generation probiotics.

title: Temperature-driven metabolic reprogramming in starter cultures impairs rheological properties and flavor release in fermented milk: A multi-omics approach
abstract: This study demonstrates the critical impact of starter culture storage temperature (-20 °C to 37 °C) on fermented milk quality. Extended storage at 37 °C severely compromised microbial viability, increasing fermentation time by 134%, while reducing lactic acid production by 7.6% and impairing water-holding capacity and texture. Rheological analyses confirmed structural deterioration through reduced G', G", and viscosity, indicating a collapse of the gel network. High temperatures reduced the umami and increase bitterness of samples. Metatranscriptomic profiling revealed temperature-dependent microbial community shifts, while integrated omics identified suppressed metabolic networks. Glycolysis (galU, pdhA) and TCA cycle genes were downregulated, diminishing flavor compound production; protease (pepF) and amino acid transporter (livM) inhibition caused nitrogen limitation; while impaired lipid metabolism (reduced accA expression and phospholipid content) destabilized milk fat globules and promoted aldehyde off-flavor formation. These findings establish ≤ 4 °C as the optimal storage condition for maintaining starter culture viability and fermented milk quality.

title: Highly sensitive niclosamide detection using the multifunctional carbon nanoflowers@halloysite nanotubes@graphene nanoplates nanocomposite modified electrochemical sensor
abstract: In this study, the glassy carbon electrode (GCE) was embellished with carbon nanoflowers (CNF)@halloysite nanotubes (Hal)@graphene nanoplates (Gr) nanocomposite to fabricate the CNF@Hal@Gr/GCE sensor for the sensitive determination of niclosamide (NA). CNF with unique petal-shaped structure had good conductivity and abundant active sites, which could accelerate the rate of electron transfer and provide large specific surface area. Hal with outstanding physical adsorption capacity could enrich NA molecules on the working electrode surface. Gr with nano-plates structure exhibited superior electrical conductivity and larger specific surface area. The CNF@Hal@Gr nanocomposite not only increased the contact area of working electrode with NA molecules but also possessed excellent electrical conductivity and adsorption properties. The CNF@Hal@Gr/GCE sensor exhibited ultrasensitive NA detection performance, including wide linear range (0.01-20 μM) and low limit of detection (5.83 nM). Moreover, the CNF@Hal@Gr/GCE sensor presented superior practical applicability with relative standard deviations of 0.87-4.71% and recoveries of 95.18-103.1%.

title: Comparative yak and Simmental rumen microbiome-metabolome across lactation stages: Implications for milk nutritional superiority
abstract: Both yaks and Simmental are dual-purpose highland varieties, but the mechanisms behind the differences in their milk production are not yet fully understood. This study compared milk composition, rumen microbial communities, and metabolomes across a range of lactation stages for both breeds. Yak milk yields were lower and it had higher levels of fat, protein, long-chain and polyunsaturated fatty acids, key amino acids, and essential minerals than Simmental milk. The microbial community of yak rumen exhibited unique characteristics, with the Family_XIII_AD3011_group persistently enriched and positively correlated with rumen fermentation parameters and milk quality, and the content of glutamate and glutamine in yak rumen was higher than in Simmental and positively correlated with milk quality. Therefore, key microorganisms and metabolites in yak rumen are crucial factors for high-yield dairy production, providing new insights to enhance milk production in ruminant dairy cattle.

title: Influence of extraction conditions on self-assembled colloidal particle formation in ginseng aqueous extract
abstract: During the processing of ginseng beverages, the formation of colloidal complexes occurs readily, which severely compromises the sensory quality of the final product and concurrently reduces the bioavailability of its functional components. Extraction conditions significantly influence the formation of self-assembled colloidal particles in ginseng water extracts. This study analyzed the main chemical composition and rheological properties of ginseng water extracts under different extraction conditions, identified the structure of the self-assembled colloidal particles, and further investigated the microstructure of these colloidal particles at different temperatures. The results clarified that both reversible and irreversible sedimentation tend to decrease with increasing extraction temperature, with a high temperature (80 °C) reducing the amount of colloidal precipitate by over 30%. Utilizing proteomics technology, protein molecules highly associated with carbohydrate binding were screened. Through molecular dynamics simulations, the binding mechanism of the colloidal particles was systematically elucidated. It was found that protein A0A5E6M5Y3 exhibits a stronger binding affinity for ginsenoside Rb1 (-10.26 kcal/mol) than for glucose (-6.816 kcal/mol), and the ternary complex demonstrated superior stability.

title: Catalytic activity and Conformaitonal stability of polyphenol oxidase in variousphysical states and concentrations under high pressure freezing
abstract: This study investigates the effects of high-pressure freezing (HPF) at 0.1-400 MPa and -20oC for 30 min on polyphenol oxidase (PPO) in both solid crystal (S-PPO) and liquid forms at high and low concentrations (HL/LL-PPO). The effects were ranked according to enzyme activity and structural changes in the following order: physical state > concentration > pressure > crystallization path. Notably, LL-PPO exhibited greater stability than both HL-PPO and S-PPO, under HPF conditions, low temperatures provide a protective effect against the pressure-induced denaturation of S-PPO. Additionally, the sulfhydryl content and the high concentration state are crucial for maintaining the structural stability of L-PPO. By altering the physical state of PPO (Liquid and Solid), the enzyme's activity can be effectively regulated through activation and inhibition. Furthermore, the back propagation artificial neural network model demonstrates a precise fit for the correlation between spatial structure and enzyme activity.

title: Vitamin C in fruits and vegetables: stability, processing effects, analytical detection, nutrient interactions, bioavailability, and health implications
abstract: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid and dehydroascorbic acid), crucial water-soluble micronutrient with strong antioxidant properties, serves as a co-factor for multiple enzymes. Its significant role in immune-regulation, collagen-synthesis, and iron-absorption makes it an essential diet component. Fresh fruits and vegetables are primary dietary sources of vitamin C, but its content is highly variable and sensitive to environmental and processing conditions.This review explores vitamin C in fruits and vegetables, discussing stability, analytical detection techniques, nutrient interactions, bioavailability, and public health implications. Advanced analytical techniques have improved the sensitivity and specificity of detecting ascorbic acid in food matrices, vitamin C is highly susceptible to degradation. Bioavailability of Vitamin C is influenced by food matrix and interactions with other nutrients, notably enhancing non-heme iron absorption and working synergistically with other antioxidants. Improved nutrient detection and understanding can aid in accurate nutritional assessment and public health strategies like food-to-food fortification, maximizing the health benefits of vitamin C-rich fruits and vegetables.

title: Multi-omics chemical and biochemical profiling reveals ellagic acid enhances insulin sensitivity via gut microbiota–tryptophan–indole signaling mechanism
abstract: Ellagic acid (EA) is a dietary polyphenol with limited systemic bioavailability, resulting in substantial intestinal exposure. However, the biochemical mechanisms by which EA modulates gut microbiota and metabolism remain unclear. Here, EA improved glucose tolerance and enhanced insulin sensitivity, with histology confirming reduced lipid accumulation and restored tissue architecture in liver, skeletal muscle, brown adipose tissue, and mesenteric fat. Consistently, metagenomic analysis showed that EA enriched Akkermansia muciniphila, Muribaculum intestinale, and Duncaniella dubosii, while reducing Lachnoclostridium phocaeense. These microbial shifts were accompanied by elevated levels of tryptophan-derived metabolites-indole-3-propionic acid, indole, and indole-3-acrylic acid-known to enhance insulin sensitivity. Lipidomics revealed EA decreased triacylglycerols and ceramides, along with restored phosphatidylcholine, phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylserine levels. Transcriptomics revealed EA suppressed hepatic lipogenesis, inhibited MAPK signaling in skeletal muscle, activated thermogenic and oxidative phosphorylation in adipose tissues. Our findings highlight EA, a food-derived polyphenol, might alleviate insulin resistance through a gut microbiota-indole metabolite-multi-tissue axis.

title: Preparation of indicator cards for freshness detection of rice with four different processing degrees during storage based on olfactory visualization technology
abstract: Rice deteriorates during storage by producing volatile amines and aldehydes. Based on olfactory visualization technology, this study prepared a chitosan-carboxymethylcellulose-Congo red (CS/CMC-CR) indicator card, which can specifically detect changes in the main deteriorative flavor substances in rice, thereby realizing the visual determination of rice freshness. This indicator card also possesses the characteristics of environmental friendliness, cost-effectiveness, and convenient operation. Experiments show that hexanal is the main characteristic flavor compound for rice deterioration during storage, and Congo red exhibits the highest sensitivity to hexanal-with a significant color change observed when the hexanal concentration reaches 2.24 mg/kg. The interference of other volatile flavor compounds on the color of the Congo red indicator card was eliminated. Furthermore, the CS/CMC-CR composite indicator card has a denser structure and better crystallinity than single materials, with improved mechanical properties (maximum tensile strength of 37.10 MPa) and barrier properties, achieving nearly 100% accuracy in rice freshness detection.

title: Impact of defatting processes on lipidomic markers and flavor in camelina and pennycress flours: advancing clean food production
abstract: The growing demand for plant-based products has increased interest in underutilized oilseeds such as camelina and pennycress as sustainable protein sources. As defatting is essential prior to protein extraction, this study examined the effects of solvent-based (hexane) and flammable solvent free (supercritical CO₂ (SCO₂)) defatting on lipid oxidation and flavor development in flours. Fatty acid profiles were analyzed by GC-FID, oxylipins by LC-MS/MS, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by HS-SPME-GC-MS. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) accounted for 53% in camelina and 32% in pennycress. SCO₂ defatting more effectively reduced total lipid content and esterified oxylipins. A total of 58 VOCs were identified, 36 of which were associated with lipid oxidation or lipoxygenase pathways. SCO₂-treated flours showed lower levels of oxidation-derived volatiles compared to hexane-treated samples. Significant correlations were observed among fatty acids, oxylipins, and VOCs. These results highlight the potential of SCO₂ extraction to improve the oxidative stability and flavor of camelina and pennycress ingredients.

title: Roles of saliva on the rheology and lubrication properties of phytosterol-stabilized water-in-oil high internal phase emulsions
abstract: Water-in-oil high internal phase emulsions (W/O HIPEs) can function as fat-like structures, but their interactions with saliva remain unclear. In this study, phytosterol (PS)-stabilized HIPEs were mixed with artificial saliva to examine saliva-driven changes across scales. Low-PS emulsions (0-0.25%) showed droplet aggregation and rapid water release, whereas high-PS emulsions (0.5-1%) exhibited mucin adsorption and penetration into particle layers. These mechanisms weakened viscoelastic moduli, increased structural rearrangement under strain 0.1%-1%. Saliva also reduced boundary friction of emulsions from 0.06-0.12 to 0.01-0.03. Quick lubrication in low-PS emulsions (lowest friction at 60 s) and slower but more persistent lubrication in high-PS emulsions (lowest friction at 120 s) were observed. The contrasting lubrication behaviors translated into faster-thinning sensations in low-PS emulsions and thicker, more sustained creaminess in high-PS emulsions. These findings established PS concentration-dependent pathways linking microstructure, rheology, and lubrication, offering guidance for designing stable and fat-reduced foods with tunable mouthfeel.

title: Synergistic mechanism of hydrophobic and hydrophilic antioxidants in the interface of tree peony seed oil bilayer emulsion
abstract: Interplay between hydrophobic and hydrophilic antioxidants in bilayer emulsions remains unclear, especially within the unique, thicker interface of layer-by-layer assembled systems. This study investigates the antioxidant behavior and interaction mechanism of α-tocopherol (hydrophobic) and l-ascorbic acid (hydrophilic) in tree peony seed oil (TPSO) bilayer emulsions stabilized by whey protein isolate and sodium alginate. At equivalent concentrations, α-tocopherol exhibited stronger antioxidant activity than l-ascorbic acid. When combined, α-tocopherol and l-ascorbic acid yielded a synergistic effect (Q value = 1.3-1.6). In combined treatments, the proportion of l-ascorbic acid distributed in the aqueous phase decreased compared to its individual use, while its presence at interfacial layer increased correspondingly. This distribution significantly enhanced the oxidative stability of the bilayer emulsion and effectively slowed TPSO degradation. Mechanistically, the close proximity of l-ascorbic acid and α-tocopherol at interface facilitated electron transfer, allowing l-ascorbic acid to regenerate α-tocopherol from its radical form and synergistically enhance oxidative stability.

title: Performance of unpublished commercial yeasts in alcoholic fermentation, phenolic compounds, volatiles, and free amino acids profiles of cv. ‘Rosa’ mango wine
abstract: Wine production is an alternative process for adding value to mangoes, and the search for yeasts to obtain exclusive products has been growing. In this study, wines were produced from mangoes of the 'Rosa' cultivar, evaluating the novel yeasts Lachancea thermotolerans CVE-7, Brettanomyces claussenii, and Saccharomyces pastorianus, in comparison with the standard Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The performance of fermentation was evaluated by analyzing metabolites, including acids, alcohols, amino acids, and volatiles. The Lachancea thermotolerans CVE-7 proved to be suitable for complete alcoholic fermentation, producing high levels of ethanol (70 g/L), lactic acid (12.9 g/L), and glycerol (7.9 g/L). Saccharomyces pastorianus and Brettanomyces claussenii exhibited moderate and low fermentative powers, respectively, but produced higher levels of volatiles typical of mango (β-caryophyllene, humulene, and β-pinene). All yeasts studied exhibited normal amino acid consumption, metabolic behavior, and a preference for glutamine and arginine. The yeasts evaluated showed potential for obtaining unique fermented products.

title: Chiral plasmonic rhombic dodecahedral gold nanoparticles for photodynamic antibacterial films in food preservation
abstract: Chiral inorganic nanomaterials have emerged as potential antibacterial agents due to their biocompatibility, facile surface modification, and superior optical properties. This paper investigates the preparation and application of chiral plasmonic rhombic dodecahedral gold nanoparticles (L/D-Au NPs), synthesized by inducing chirality through the chiral molecule cysteine. The chiral architecture substantially amplifies the antibacterial potency of Au NPs. Films composed of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and L/D-Au NPs demonstrated potent antimicrobial effects against both Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) under ambient light. DAu NPs, in particular, showed superior antimicrobial activity, reducing the viability of E. coli by 97.4%, much higher than Au NPs. Preservation experiment with blueberries revealed that PVA/D-Au NPs films effectively inhibited microbial contamination, retarded nutrient loss, and markedly extended the shelf life of blueberries at room temperature. This study pioneers the application of chiral inorganic nano-antimicrobial agents in food preservation films, offering innovative perspectives in the field of food preservation.

title: Design and synthesis of novel 2,3,4-trisubstituted thiazole derivatives as preservative agents by in vitro and in silico approaches
abstract: Today, there is an urgent need for new molecules because of the increasing development of fungal resistance. Here, novel phenol-thiazole-hydrazone hybrids were designed and synthesized using a mimic-to approach referenced from azole antifungals. After structural confirmation, the compounds were tested against fungi and further evaluated against the NIH/3T3 cells to determine their selectivity index as well as potential genotoxicity. All compounds have inhibitory activity against C. glabrata except 3a, while 3o inhibits C. albicans among others. Inhibition effects on NIH/3T3 cells indicated that 3o had the strongest cytotoxic effect, while 3 h had the least significant toxicity. Scanning-electron-microscope (SEM) analyses indicated that active compounds compromise cell integrity, thereby leading to cell death. The binding modes of lanestrol-demethylase (LDM)-3o/-3j complexes were investigated through in silico analysis, and structure-activity relationships (SAR) were established. Compounds 3b, 3g, 3i, 3j, 3k, and 3o are identified as potential preservative agents.

title: Anthocyanins-quercetin copigmentation enhances liposomal encapsulation: Mechanisms, bilayer interactions, and sustained release performance
abstract: Conventional liposome preparation techniques often show poor encapsulation efficiency (EE) for hydrophilic compounds. In this study, copigmentation was employed as a hydrophobic modification strategy to improve the liposomal delivery of anthocyanins (ACNs). ACNs formed stable copigmentation complexes with quercetin (QTI), primarily through π-π stacking and hydrophobic interactions. These interactions enhanced the hydrophobicity of ACNs and promoted their redistribution from the aqueous phase toward the bilayer interfacial region. Liposomes prepared by the polyol dilution method encapsulated ACNs@QTI complexes more efficiently than free ACNs, achieving an EE of 81.5 ± 0.6% and a particle size of 166.4 ± 7.9 nm. FTIR, DSC, and fluorescence analyses confirmed stronger interactions between ACNs@QTI complexes and phospholipid membranes, while in-vitro release experiments demonstrated its superior sustained-release performance. These findings highlight copigmentation as a practical non-covalent strategy to enhance liposomal encapsulation of hydrophilic bioactives, offering a basis for enhancing the stability and delivery of ACNs and other water-soluble compounds in food and pharmaceutical applications.

title: Multi-scale analysis of thermal processing-induced textural changes in fish muscle with distinct ecological characteristics: Integration of structural and proteomic perspectives
abstract: This study compared three fish species with distinct ecological habits-freshwater silver carp (HM), skipjack tuna (KP), and Pacific mackerel (SJ) to elucidate species-specific mechanisms of texture change during thermal processing. Multi-scale analyses integrating texture measurements, microstructural observation, and proteomics revealed divergent thermal responses. The results showed that the shear force of KP increased 7.62-fold to 960.77 g after heating, leading to thick filament aggregation, increased abundance of glycolytic enzymes, and enhanced protein cross-linking, resulting in a hardened texture. SJ exhibited marked softening associated with thermal destabilization and solubilization of the collagen network and depolymerization of the actin cytoskeleton. Following thermal processing, HM displayed the highest muscle fiber density and the smallest average muscle fiber length. The differentially abundant proteins were significantly enriched in autophagy and mitochondrial function, maintaining the homeostasis of muscle cells. It facilitated buffering of heat-induced denaturation and regulation of texture flexibility.

title: Drying methods impact bioactive compounds in Siraitia grosvenorii fruit: Metabolomic insights
abstract: Siraitia grosvenorii is widely used in functional foods, and drying is essential for long-term preservation. Drying methods significantly impact the fruit quality. Here, we evaluated how hot air drying (HAD), heat pump drying (HPD), microwave vacuum drying (MVD), and vacuum freeze drying (VFD) affect bioactive compounds in S. grosvenorii fruit. HAD-treated fruit showed elevated phenolic, flavonoid, and sugar contents, together with strong ·OH scavenging capacity. In contrast, VFD better preserved green color and native flavor of fresh fruit and yielded higher ascorbic acid and mogroside V contents than thermal drying. Under HAD and HPD, differentially accumulated metabolites (DAMs) were mainly enriched in linoleic acid, tryptophan, and purine metabolism. Under VFD, luteolin-7-O-glucoside was positively correlated with mogroside IV, mogroside V, and 11-oxomogroside V, whereas under HAD and HPD, protocatechualdehyde and vanillin (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde) were positively correlated with mogroside IV. These findings provide a theoretical basis for selecting appropriate processing strategies for S. grosvenorii fruit. • Different drying methods shaped bioactive compounds of Siraitia grosvenorii fruit. • Vacuum freeze drying (VFD) preserved green color and retained fresh, original flavor. • Hot air drying (HAD) enhanced flavonoid content and ·OH scavenging activity. • VFD maintained higher ascorbic acid and mogroside V contents than thermal drying. • Luteolin-7-O-glucoside in VFD samples positively correlated with mogroside content.

title: Ultra-sensitive SERS-ICA for carbofuran detection in complex food matrices: a smart signal averaging strategy overcoming matrix interference
abstract: The accurate detection of pesticide residues in complex food matrices is significantly hindered by interference from sample components. To address this challenge, we developed a novel surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy-based immunochromatographic assay (SERS-ICA) for the ultrasensitive and on-site detection of carbofuran. The method employs antibody-conjugated Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles (Au@Ag NPs) as SERS probes, introducing the Raman reporter molecule 4-mercaptobenzoic acid (4MBA) with stable and easily identifiable characteristic peaks. A competitive immunoassay format was established, leveraging antigen-antibody specificity for selective carbofuran recognition. To maximize detection reliability, we systematically evaluated signal-averaging strategies for SERS-ICA by comparing Raman signals collected at 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 test-line positions. We identified an eight-point averaging scheme that balances precision (R 2 = 0.9934) and practicality (average recovery = 99.39%). The assay demonstrates remarkable sensitivity with a Raman detection limit of 1 pg/kg (10 -6 mg/kg) and a visual cutoff of 10 μg/kg (10 -5 mg/kg). Validation with three agriculturally relevant vegetables (celery, cowpea, and cucumber) showed excellent performance, with linear correlations (R 2 > 0.99) and near-quantitative recoveries (99.09-99.39%). Blind spike-recovery tests (95.47-101.65%) further confirmed the robustness of the method for real-world applications. This work establishes SERS-ICA as a next-generation platform for field-deployable, matrix-resistant pesticide monitoring with unmatched sensitivity.

title: Elemental fingerprinting and regional verification of Pakistani basmati and non-basmati rice varieties using ICP-MS and multivariate analysis
abstract: This study investigates the elemental composition of Basmati and non-Basmati rice cultivars grown across five different regions in Punjab, Pakistan using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Distinct cultivar and regional variations in elemental concentrations were observed, with twelve key elements identified as regional classifiers. Basmati rice exhibited higher accumulation of essential macro and trace elements compared to non-Basmati varieties. Supervised classification methods (LDA) accurately separated rice cultivars and successfully classified their geographical origins with high accuracy. Environmental factors, including sunshine, precipitation, and temperature exhibited positive correlations with several elements, highlighting the influence of climate on nutrient distribution in rice grains. The spatial distribution of elements was heavily influenced by geographic location, reflecting distinct geochemical patterns for Basmati and non-Basmati growing zones. This comprehensive elemental fingerprinting approach provides a robust tool for rice cultivar discrimination and regional origin authentication, supporting efforts in food quality control and traceability of premium Pakistani Basmati rice.

title: Updated insights into designing bioactive compounds-loaded protein-based nanoparticles using pH-driven method: Positive impacts of technical evolutions based on existing theoretical framework
abstract: Consumer demand for bioactive compounds (BACs) with potential health benefits in functional foods is growing. However, their application must overcome poor bioavailability owing to low solubility and instability under harsh conditions. Therefore, pH-driven method (PDM) has emerged as a green and facile platform for preparing protein-based nanoparticle (NP) carriers by leveraging pH-responsiveness of proteins and BACs. Obtained products exhibit superior performance in colloidal properties, stabilization, and release. A systematic literature review revealed that, driven by recent technological innovations, this field has achieved multi-layered leaps since its invention. Encapsulation modalities gradually transformed from singularity to diversity. Then, fabrication details were optimized in acidification pathways, process customization, and auxiliary means. Finally, pseudo-dynamic characterization across pH gradients tracked self-assembly process for elucidating mechanisms. Besides, this review highlighted the positive role of above aspects in improving scalability, enhancing industrial feasibility, and developing future foods. Notably, remaining deficiencies and future trends were also pointed out.

title: Natural sources and bioactive mechanisms of anti-inflammatory peptides: from digestive metabolism to bioavailability enhancement strategies
abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs), a class of biologically active molecules with high specificity and low toxicity, demonstrate outstanding potential in replacing traditional anti-inflammatory drugs. In this review, the multiple natural sources of AIPs (including marine organisms, terrestrial plants and animals, and microorganisms) are comprehensively reviewed, and their core molecular mechanisms to inhibit inflammatory responses through the synergistic regulation of key signaling pathways such as NF-κB, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, JAK/STAT, and Keap1-Nrf2 are examined. To address the bioavailability bottlenecks of AIPs' oral delivery, such as gastrointestinal degradation and low intestinal permeability, this review systematically analyzes the mechanisms of action of enhancement strategies, including nanocarrier technologies and chemical modification methods. Finally, we propose cutting-edge future directions such as artificial intelligence-guided design and innovative combination therapies to accelerate their clinical translation. This work provides not only a solid theoretical foundation but also practical insights for the development of AIPs as next-generation anti-inflammatory ingredients.

title: Enhanced rehydration of egg white powder by high-pressure homogenization: A quantitative proteomic perspective
abstract: This study investigates how high-pressure homogenization (HPH) pretreatment influences the properties of spray-dried and freeze-dried egg white powder (EWP). HPH treatment significantly reduced particle size and increased surface charge, enhancing protein solubility and dispersibility. Structural analysis revealed HPH induced partial protein unfolding, evidenced by increased surface hydrophobicity and exposed sulfhydryl groups, while maintaining secondary structure stability. These modifications improved functional properties, notably increasing emulsifying activity by 20-59% and gel strength by 15-41%. HPH markedly enhanced powder rehydration, reducing turbidity by 32% and increasing solubility to 97-98%. Quantitative proteomics of rehydrated precipitates revealed that HPH selectively reduced aggregation-prone proteins while enriching structure-stabilizing ones. These findings demonstrate that HPH pretreatment optimizes fluid-solid transitions during drying through controlled protein modifications, offering new insights for improving protein powder processing.

title: Effects of blocking alcoholic fermentation at different residual sugar levels on sensory and chemical profiles of cabernet sauvignon fortified wines
abstract: Fortified wine has been gaining popularity in China. However, studies on non-aged fortified wines with different sugar levels remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the sensory and chemical profiles of Cabernet Sauvignon fortified wines produced by blocking alcoholic fermentation at approximate residual sugar levels of 110 g/L (HW), 70 g/L (MW), and 30 g/L (LW) of the must. A total of 49 anthocyanins and 52 volatile compounds were identified and quantified using anthocyanin-targeted metabolomics and HS-SPME-GC-MS, respectively. Distinct differences were observed in the profiles of anthocyanins and volatiles among the wines. Six key anthocyanins and fifteen key volatile compounds (VIP > 1) were identified as discriminant markers. Sensory analysis revealed that MW exhibited a well-balanced profile with moderate astringency, while LW exhibited the highest antioxidant capacity, an enhanced fruity aroma, and significant overall color differences (p < 0.05). All samples demonstrated distinct floral aromas and low alcohol aroma intensity.

title: Food Safety and quality of some Italian honey: Study of long-persistent contaminants (heavy metals and PFAS) in different production areas in southern Italy
abstract: In recent years, persistent environmental contaminants such as PFAS have emerged alongside traditional pollutants like heavy metals. Honey is a useful biomonitoring tool thanks to bees' foraging range, which reflects average pollution levels. The objective of this study was to determinate heavy metals and PFAS in honey from six areas of the Molise region (rural, industrial, and remote), to evaluate environmental impact on the matrix, verify if honey meets health standards, and assess potential consumer risks. 56 honey samples were collected over four months directly from honeycombs. Heavy metals were analyzed by ICP-AES; PFAS by SPE-LC-MS/MS. Aluminium, antimony, and selenium were the most detected metals; three PFAS (Bistriflimide, 6:2FTS, L-PFOS) were found at ultra-trace levels. Chemometric analysis identified arsenic, antimony, and selenium as area-specific markers. Risk assessment showed higher non-carcinogenic risk in areas A and E, and carcinogenic risk in C and D. Area B was the least impacted.

title: Aroma profile of oxidatively aged White and Tawny Port wines with different indication of age. Contribution of the non-rectified wine spirit
abstract: The aroma profiles of oxidatively aged White and Tawny Port wines with increasing indication of age were studied to understand differences in their ageing processes. Thirty-one and twenty-eight aroma compounds were quantified in Tawny and White Ports, respectively. Sotolon increased with age in both styles, contributing significantly to the aroma of older wines. Esters such as ethyl hexanoate, ethyl octanoate, and ethyl decanoate had odour activity values (OAVs) >1, especially in Tawny Ports, where their concentrations rose with age. In contrast, their levels declined in aged White Ports, reducing aromatic impact. 1,1,6-Trimethyl-1,2-dihydronaphthalene and β-damascenone also contributed to aroma due to their low odour thresholds. Differences in aroma evolution may be linked to differences in wine matrix composition. Wine spirit used for fortification influenced the initial aroma through its higher alcohols and esters. Over time, oxidation-derived compounds became dominant, enhancing aromatic complexity and differentiating styles. • Aroma evolution in White and Tawny Ports was studied throughout age indications. • Sotolon increases with age, enhancing aroma in both Port wine styles. • Key esters decrease in aged White Ports but increase in Tawny Ports. • Wine matrix affects aroma retention in Tawny and White Port wines. • Fortification and ageing volatiles together shape Port wine aroma.

title: Thyme polyphenols modulate myofibrillar protein-odorant interactions: Molecular mechanistic insights into mutton off-flavor release
abstract: The characteristic flavor of mutton, commonly described as "muttony" or "goaty", limits consumer acceptance and market potential. This study evaluated the effects of four thyme phenolics, including gallic acid (GA), rosmarinic acid (RA), scutellarin (SCU), and apigenin-7-O-glucuronide (A7G), on the interaction between myofibrillar protein (MP) and six key off-flavor compounds. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry showed that all four phenolics reduced MP binding with odorants and enhanced their release, with SCU and RA showing the strongest effects. Spectroscopic analyses demonstrated that phenolics induced MP conformational changes, such as decreased α-helix and β-sheet content, reduced surface hydrophobicity, and lower sulfhydryl levels. Docking and simulation confirmed that hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen bonding dominated phenolic-MP binding, and SCU exhibited the highest binding stability among tested phenolics and was likely to competitively displace 4-methyloctanoic acid. These findings provide molecular insights into how thyme phenolics promote off-flavor release and support their application in improving mutton sensory quality.

title: Ursolic acid nanoemulsion system for inhibition of goji berry black mold caused by Alternaria alternata
abstract: Ursolic acid (UA) possesses antifungal activity against A. alternata, however, its poor solubility poses a challenge for practical application. We prepared UA nanoemulsions consisting of ethyl oleate, Cremophor EL, and Transcutol HP. The particle size of the UA nanoemulsions ranged from 20.53 to 27.88 nm. Electron microscopy revealed a nearly spherical structure. Fourier-transform infrared analysis proved that UA was successfully encapsulated, and the encapsulation efficiency ranged from 82 to 84%. UA nanoemulsions showed stable characteristics for 15 days of storage. The minimum inhibitory concentration of UA nanoemulsions against A. alternata was 0.8 mg/mL. UA nanoemulsions suppressed hyphal growth, reduced the spore yield and germination rate, and shortened the length of germ tubes in A. alternata. In vivo experiments confirmed that UA nanoemulsions could inhibit the goji berries and apple fruits infected by A. alternata. Collectively, these results demonstrate that UA nanoemulsion shows strong antifungal potential for postharvest rot control.

title: Proanthocyanidins in food and health: structure–activity relationships, application challenges, and emerging strategies
abstract: Proanthocyanidins (PCs) are plant-derived polyphenols that exhibit diverse redox-related and protective functions intrinsically linked to their chemical structures. Key structural features, including degree of polymerization (DP), galloylation, and interflavan linkage type, critically govern the bioactivity, interaction behavior, and functional performance of PCs. This review summarizes recent advances in elucidating the structure-activity relationships (SAR) of PCs, with emphasis on the links between structural features and their bioactivity in food systems. Recent progress in depolymerization, structural modification, and stabilization strategies has enhanced the solubility, stability, and bioaccessibility of PCs through chemical catalysis, physical processing, and biotransformation. In addition, interactions between PCs and food matrix components play a critical role in preserving structural integrity and regulating retention during processing and gastrointestinal digestion. Future advancements in targeted delivery systems, multi-omics approaches, and computational modeling are expected to facilitate the rational design and translation of PCs into functional ingredients in food and health systems.

title: Essential oil-based intelligent packaging with controlled release: A review on mechanisms, encapsulation, and molecular interactions
abstract: Essential oil (EO)-based intelligent packaging has emerged as a promising strategy for sustainable food preservation by leveraging the natural antibacterial and antioxidant properties of EOs. Encapsulation serves as a pivotal approach to overcome inherent limitations of EOs, such as high volatility and poor stability, enabling the design of stimuli-responsive controlled-release systems sensitive to environmental cues like pH and humidity. This review systematically investigates the integration mechanisms between intelligent packaging and EO-controlled release systems, providing an in-depth analysis of the antibacterial principles of EOs, advanced encapsulation strategies, and operational mechanisms of intelligent indicators. Particular emphasis is placed on the molecular-level interactions (including both covalent and non-covalent bonds) within the packaging matrix that govern EO stability and release behavior - an aspect frequently overlooked in current research. Future advancements should focus on developing high-performance composites with integrated sensing capabilities, while concurrently addressing the scale-up and cost-effectiveness for widespread commercialization.

title: Enzymatic synthesis of N-propionyl phenylalanine: enhancement of umami and salty taste and decoding of its taste mechanism
abstract: This study investigated the enzymatic synthesis of N-propionyl phenylalanine (PP) and its potential as a novel taste enhancer. PP obtained 89.64% and 79.33% yield using FP-G and pancreatic enzymes under optimized conditions (pH 7.0, 50 °C). At a dosage of 100 mg/L, PP demonstrated exceptional dual taste-enhancing qualities, increasing umami by 176% and saltiness intensity by 132.5%. Time-intensity analysis revealed PP prolonged taste perception by 42.5-64 s. Molecular docking showed strong binding (-6.6 to -7.3 kcal/mol) with human taste receptors hTAS1R1/hTAS1R3 and hTMC4 through hydrophobic interactions. In neutral-alkaline conditions, the enzymatic process remained stable, exhibiting synthetic activity for pancreatin enzymes (345.15 U/g) and FP-G (488.45 U/g). These findings highlight PP's potential as a taste enhancer, enabling approximately 49% sodium and 48% MSG reduction in food products while preserving taste quality. The work provides valuable insights into enzymatic N-acylation and the molecular basis of taste modulation, offering promising strategies for healthier food formulation.

title: Gliadin hydrolysate-chitosan bilayer nanoparticles for berberine delivery: Controlled release, enhanced antioxidant activity, and lipid digestion regulation
abstract: Berberine (BBR) is a natural isoquinoline alkaloid with poor water solubility and chemical instability, which limits its application in functional foods. Here, food-grade bilayer nanoparticles based on gliadin hydrolysates (GLH) and chitosan (CS) were constructed via a green encapsulation strategy to improve BBR delivery. The resulting GLH-BBR-CS nanoparticles (GLH-BBR-CS NPs) exhibited high encapsulation efficiency, good storage stability, and controlled BBR release under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. FT-IR and XRD analyses suggested that BBR was stabilised within the nanoparticles through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. In vitro, GLH-BBR-CS NPs enhanced the antioxidant activity of BBR and inhibited pancreatic lipase in a dose-dependent manner, indicating potential for modulating lipid digestion. In vivo, oral administration of GLH-BBR-CS NPs improved antioxidant status and reduced fat absorption in rats. These findings highlight a scalable approach for designing food-compatible BBR delivery systems and support the development of BBR-enriched functional foods.

title: Dynamic evolution of ethanol clusters and solubility modulation of flavor esters during the aging of Soy sauce flavor Baijiu
abstract: This study elucidates the microstructural evolution of ethanol clusters and their regulatory role in flavor ester solubility during the aging of Soy sauce flavor Baijiu. Using integrated fluorescence and Raman spectroscopy, we show that Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation (LLPS) transforms ethanol clusters from hydrophilic to hydrophobic microdomains. Methodologically, we innovatively combined alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) activity assay with Nile Red fluorescence probing to distinguish ethanol molecular states. Mass spectrometry further reveals a Non-Monotonic dissolution pattern for four key long-chain fatty acid ethyl esters: initial solubility increase through hydrophobic microdomains is later reversed by steric hindrance due to excessive cluster densification during extended aging. In samples aged over 30 years, pronounced ethanol cluster aggregation triggers flavor precipitation, evidenced by decreased free ethanol and solid deposit formation. These findings uncover the microstructural mechanism linking phase separation to flavor stability, offering a theoretical basis for improving Baijiu colloidal properties and sensory quality.

title: Regulation of solubility and thermal stability for egg white proteins via alkaline heat treatment: A new insight into protein conformation and interactions at the nanoscale
abstract: Thermal aggregation limits the use of egg white proteins in heat processed, high protein systems. A microenvironment reconstruction strategy was developed by adjusting pH (9.5-10.5) and protein concentration (1-3%, w/v) during preheating. Alkaline thermal pretreated proteins showed improved clarity, solubility, and particle uniformity, forming 21.94 ± 0.11 nm nanoparticles. Spectroscopic analyses revealed a conformational shift from α-helix to β-sheet dominance, and increased sulfhydryl exposure favoring intramolecular over intermolecular disulfide formation. This rearrangement enhanced zeta potential (-29.83 ± 0.40 mV), reinforcing electrostatic repulsion and preventing large aggregate nucleation. Consequently, denaturation temperature increased by 33% (115.90 °C vs. 87.04 °C), and solubility was preserved at 98.5 ± 0.24% (2%) and 87.6 ± 0.44% (3%) after heating. This preconditioning enables heat stable egg white proteins for transparent beverages and thermally robust delivery systems.

title: Maintaining postharvest quality and extending the shelf life of bananas through integrated LED light exposure and packaging strategies
abstract: Given the importance of preserving and enhancing the quality of banana fruit during the postharvest period, this study examined the combined effects of LED light exposure (blue, red, green, and no light) and various packaging types (polyethylene, PVC, plastic films, and no packaging) on the chemical and physical properties of bananas stored at room temperature for seven days. Key parameters, including total phenolic content (TPC), flavonoids, antioxidant activity, titratable acidity, pH, Total Soluble Solids (TSS), and moisture, were measured at the end of the storage period. The results showed that blue LED light significantly increased total phenolic content by 1.78-fold (from 1.25 to 2.23 mg GAE/g FW) and antioxidant activity by 1.93-fold (from 38.7% to 74.7% DPPH inhibition) compared to the dark control. Among packaging types, PVC film yielded 1.53-fold higher phenolic content (1.97 vs. 1.29 mg GAE/g FW) and 1.37-fold greater flavonoid levels (1.10 vs. 0.80 mg QE/g FW) than unpackaged samples after 7 days. Two-way ANOVA confirmed that both light and packaging significantly affected key quality traits (p < 0.01), with a significant interaction effect for phenolic and flavonoid content (p < 0.05). Principal Component Analysis (PCA) further revealed that treatments involving blue light + PVC were distinctly separated from the control, with phenolics, flavonoids, antioxidant activity, and TSS serving as the primary drivers of quality differentiation (PC1 explained up to 97% of variance). These findings demonstrate that the integration of blue LED exposure with PVC packaging offers a practical, non-chemical strategy to maintain nutritional quality and extend the shelf life of banana fruit under ambient storage conditions.

title: Novel sea-urchin-like Pt Au nanoparticles enhanced electrochemiluminescence of nitrogen-vacancy carbon nitride for specific detection of Sudan III
abstract: A highly sensitive molecular imprinting electrochemiluminescence (MIP-ECL) sensor was developed for Sudan III detection in food. The sensor utilized nitrogen-vacancy carbon nitride (CNNV) as an efficient ECL emitter in the S 2 O 8 2- system, with sea-urchin-like PtAu nanoparticles (PtAu NPs) and Ti 3 CN MXene serving as co-reaction accelerators and support material respectively to enhance signal intensity. Molecular imprinting was achieved using O-phenylenediamine (O-PD) as functional monomer, creating specific recognition sites for Sudan III. The detection mechanism was based on target-induced ECL quenching through electron transfer inhibition. The sensor showed excellent analytical performance with a wide linear range from 1 × 10 -12 to 1 × 10 -6 mol L -1 and an ultralow detection limit of 3.3 × 10 -13 mol L -1 (S/N = 3). Real sample analysis demonstrated good accuracy and precision. The sensor maintained 87.5% of initial response after 20-day storage, indicating good stability. This method provides a reliable approach for monitoring Sudan III in food.

title: Biphasic-gelled W/O/W emulsion gel for co-delivering vitamins B12 and E: Preparation, characterization, and in vitro digestion
abstract: This study aimed to enhance the stability and functional properties of W/O/W emulsions through a biphasic gelation strategy. An emulsified gel system was constructed with soybean lipophilic protein-chitosan hydrochloride complex (SLP-CHC) as the emulsifier, beeswax as the oil-phase gelling agent, and curdlan/anhydrous calcium chloride as the aqueous-phase gelling agent. The microstructure and physicochemical properties were characterized, and in vitro digestion experiments were conducted to evaluate the protective and delivery capacities for vitamin B 12 (VB 12 ) and vitamin E (VE). The biphasic gel exhibited a dense network, high viscoelasticity (G' > G"), and superior water/oil-holding capacity. Encapsulation efficiencies reached 95.92% for VB 12 and 69.51% for VE, with enhanced stability under heat and pH stress compared to single-phase gels. In vitro digestion confirmed effective gastric protection and intestinal release, leading to high bioaccessibility for both vitamins. This study provides a novel approach for the co-delivery of polar and non-polar bioactive compounds.

title: Selenium bioenrichment and functional enhancement with antioxidants in Actinidia arguta juice by fermentation with selenium-enriched Tibetan kefir grains
abstract: Selenium is an essential trace element with critical roles in antioxidant defense, immune regulation, and metabolic health, yet its intake is insufficient in many populations. This study investigated the effects of fermenting Actinidia arguta juice with selenium-enriched Tibetan kefir grains to enhance its nutritional, sensory and functional. Selenium-enriched Tibetan kefir grains fermentation not only increased total Se content but also promoted the biotransformation of inorganic selenium into bioavailable organic selenium, supporting effective dietary biofortification. The fermented juice showed enhanced activities of antioxidant enzymes, including glutathione peroxidase, glutathione S-transferase, and thioredoxin reductase. Interestingly, selenium enrichment enhanced zinc bioaccumulation and co-regulation. The volatile compound analysis revealed selenium-driven shifts toward alcohols and esters, which contributed to enhanced floral, fruity, and balsamic aroma qualities. Metabolomics further revealed that selenium-enriched activated cysteine and methionine, and glutathione-related metabolism pathways. Thus, this study providing a promising approach for developing selenium-enriched functional beverages.

title: Enzymatic degradation of aflatoxin B1 by Bacillus species: Mechanistic insights and application potential in cereal detoxifications
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination remains a major food safety challenge, urging exploration of effective mitigation strategies. Screening of 135 samples on a coumarin-based medium yielded 26 aflatoxin B1 (AFB1)-degrading bacterial isolates. Bacillus subtilis C2 and S60, and Bacillus licheniformis C16 showed the highest activity, primarily via their cell-free supernatants (CFS). Proteinase K inhibition and SDS-PAGE of active fractions confirmed the role of proteins. The CFS activity was thermostable and worked optimally at pH 8.0; it was enhanced by Cu 2+ but inhibited by Zn 2+ . Proteomic analysis revealed extracellular proteins involved in oxidation-reduction. Critically, cytotoxicity assays confirmed that the degradation products from B. licheniformis C16 and B. subtilis S60 were significantly less toxic than intact AFB1. Furthermore, fermentation with these two strains significantly reduced AFB1 levels in contaminated cereals. These results demonstrate the potential of this method for the practical detoxification of food and feed.

title: Efficient extraction and detection of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in honey: A study on extraction mechanism
abstract: The efficient extraction of both short- and long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) from food remains a challenge. However, there are hardly any studies on extraction mechanism in food. This study first confirmed that the protein affinity is the key mechanism affecting efficient extraction of long-chain PFAS from honey by simulating sugaring-out liquid-liquid extraction (SULLE) in the presence of different honey matrix substances. Short-chain PFAS exhibited strong matrix effects under acidic environment of honey. 2% ammonium hydroxide-acetonitrile was used as extraction solvent to effectively releases the binding of PFAS-proteins and minimize matrices interference. By combining liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, a novel method for the determination of 22 PFAS from honey was developed, which showed low limit of quantification, satisfactory accuracy and precision. This work not only provides a highly-efficient and cost-effective approach for analyzing PFAS in honey, but also offers deep insights into the efficient extraction of PFAS from food.

title: Interfacial reorganization of egg yolk granules by ultrasound-assisted pH-shifting: concentration-dependent lecithin functionality from emulsion stabilizer to competitive displacer
abstract: The dense structure of egg yolk granules (EYG) limits their emulsification functionality. This study investigated interactions between EYG (1%) and egg lecithin (EL, 0-1%) under ultrasound-assisted pH-shifting. Results showed EL significantly enhanced complex solubility, increased negative Zeta potential, and reduced particle size (P < 0.05). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed increased β-sheet content and reduced random coils (P < 0.05), while intrinsic fluorescence indicated EL-induced quenching of EYG proteins. Molecular docking identified that EL bound to EYG proteins primarily by hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. At 0.5% EL, protein-phospholipid synergy formed viscoelastic interfacial layers and producing emulsions with small droplet size (9.55 μm), low creaming index (3.64%), and high interfacial protein coverage (57.13%). Conversely, exceeding 0.5% EL caused competitive adsorption, displacing proteins and weakening interfacial stability. This work provided novel mechanistic insights for rationally designing EYG-EL emulsifiers with tailored functionality.

title: Dynamic changes in umami and aroma compounds and transcriptome analysis of Pleurotus pulmonarius at different growth stages
abstract: Pleurotus pulmonarius is renowned for distinctive umami and aroma. However, accumulation patterns and regulatory mechanisms of these compounds during fruiting body development remain poorly understood. HPLC results showed umami 5'-nucleotides levels exhibited decreasing trends accompanying maturation. The contents of five flavor amino acids (AAs) and four sweet-tasting AAs at the immature stage peaked at 1.53 and 0.69 g/100 g, significantly surpassing that at other stage (P < 0.05). HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis revealed 1-octen-3-ol exhibited the highest relative odor activity value at primordial stage, while 3-octanone dominated in later stages. At over-mature stage, DEGs were predominantly enriched in the organonitrogen compound metabolic process, whereas at other stages they chiefly associated with small-molecule metabolic processes. Some umami AAs levels were correlated with aspB and OTC expression. This study explained how umami and aroma compounds built up and were controlled during the growth of P. Pulmonarius fruiting bodies, providing novel insights for optimizing harvest timing.

title: Eco-friendly and active carboxymethyl cellulose film integrated with eggshell powder and tea polyphenols for beef and apple preservation
abstract: The food waste resulting from by corruption not only causes huge economic losses to society, but also exacerbates global hunger. In the contemporary context of mounting global environmental awareness and concerns regarding food safety, the utilization of biodegradable active packaging has attracted a considerable attention. In this study, a novel and degradable CGP-ESP-TP film was prepared with wheat straw-based carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC, 2%), glycerol (30% w/w of CMC), eggshell powder (2.5%) obtained by superfine grinding and tea polyphenols, polymalate (0.9%), to the preservation of beef and apples. The 90% particle size of the eggshell powder particles obtained via superfine grinding was found to be less than 8.942 μm. When the concentration of tea polyphenols was 0.20%, the CGP-ESP5-TP4 film has excellent antioxidant and anti-UV properties, tensile strength, elongation at break, oxygen permeability, water vapor permeability and carbon dioxide permeability were 35.84 MPa, 100.96%, 1.44 *10 -14 kg·m·m -2 ·s -1 ·Pa -1 , 1.10 *10 -13 g·m·m -2 ·s -1 ·Pa -1 and 1.25 *10 -14 kg·m·m -2 ·s -1 ·Pa -1 , separately. According to scanning electron microscopy results, film components, except eggshell powder, had good solubility in the solution. It was also found that non-covalent bonds (eg: hydrogen bonds) were the mainly interaction force between the matrix of the film by the fourier transform infrared spectroscopy spectra. Preservation results indicated that the packaging film lowered the increase in pH, total volatile basic nitrogen and total viable count of beef, as well as the increase in pH and weight loss of apples, and the decrease in apple firmness, which were effectively maintained their quality. The study indicated the significant potential of eggshell powder from waste resources and its transformation into sustainable and biodegradable composites as a promising solution for food packaging applications.

title: A review of yellow Monascus pigments with recent updates: Separation and identification, biosynthesis, biological activities, production and application
abstract: The global demand for natural pigments continues to grow, with microbial-derived pigments gaining attention for their advantages over synthetic counterparts, including higher safety, lower production cost, and excellent stability. Yellow natural pigments constitute about 60% of the market; however, current options such as curcumin and gardenia yellow are limited by issues in solubility, stability, odor and cost. Yellow Monascus pigments (YMPs), as a major category of Monascus pigments, offer a promising alternative. Their distinct chemical structure confers not only superior stability but also a range of valuable biological activities. These properties greatly broaden the application prospects of YMPs in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals and other related fields. This review systematically outlines the separation and identification, biosynthetic pathways, biological activities, production and potential applications of YMPs, offering a comprehensive perspective on recent advances in this promising field.

title: Edible hydrogel coating films encapsulating α-lipoic acid and Chlamydomonas reinhardtii: A novel approach for blueberry preservation
abstract: In this study, α-lipoic acid (ALA) and Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (C.r.) were encapsulated in carboxymethyl chitosan/sodium alginate hydrogels to preserve blueberries. The composite films created a microclimate that effectively reduced fruit respiration and water vapor transmission rate. Specifically, the CSA-C.r.-2 coating significantly minimized weight loss to 10.9% after 6 days, compared to 39.8% in the control. It also more effectively maintained fruit brightness (L ⁎ value of 12.9 vs. 5.3 in the control) and firmness (84.67 g vs. 54.29 g in the control) Furthermore, the coating mitigated oxidative stress by lowering malondialdehyde and H₂O₂ levels while enhancing the activities of key antioxidant enzymes, including superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT). These results confirm that the specific ALA/C.r.-composite coating offers a potent strategy for maintaining quality and extending the shelf life of perishable fruits.

title: Chemical changes in the volatile composition associated to the anoxic and oxidative storages of red wines
abstract: Sixteen red wines were stored for one month at 35 °C under anoxic conditions and with 35 mg/L of O₂ (over the stoichiometric to total SO₂). Major and minor volatile compounds, including Strecker aldehydes, total acetaldehyde, and acetals, were analysed. Both storage conditions led to qualitatively similar changes, although oxidation caused more pronounced effects, involving eight chemical processes. Three were time-dependent (hydrolysis of glycosidic precursors, esterification equilibria, and molecular rearrangements in acidic media) and not related to oxygen. Two processes (acetalization and Strecker degradation) occurred under both conditions but were more intense with oxidation. Additional oxidative effects included the oxidation of terpenols and methionol, the degradation of phenols (likely ferulic and sinapic acids) into vanillin and syringaldehyde, and the loss of non-polar compounds, such as esters and higher fatty acids, due, possibly, to adsorption. The most sensory-relevant changes were the accumulation of Strecker aldehydes, free acetaldehyde, and diethyl acetal in oxidised samples. • Specific changes under anoxia are similar but less intense than under oxidation. • Wine volatile evolution is governed by eight distinct chemical processes. • Acetalization and Strecker degradation occur even under anoxic conditions. • Strecker aldehydes and acetals drive the main sensory changes in both aging modes. • Oxidation releases free acetaldehyde without increasing total acetaldehyde.

title: Cocoa bean shells as a source of functional fiber in a muffin model
abstract: Cocoa bean shells (CBSs), a by-product of cocoa production, are rich in dietary fiber (46.4–60.6%) and bioactive compounds, making them a promising functional ingredient for bakery applications. This study evaluated the incorporation of CBSs into muffins, using a 7% inclusion level as a model food system. Two control muffins were prepared: one with the basic recipe and another enriched with inulin as a standard fiber. CBSs-enriched muffins showed a significant increase in antioxidant activity (1.91 and 2.67 mg TE/g by DPPH • and ABTS •+ assays, respectively) and were positively evaluated for chocolate-like flavor and shape. In vitro digestion followed by colonic fermentation of the insoluble fraction led to a notable increase in butyric acid (from 1.86 to 5.66 mmol/L after 48 h), indicating prebiotic potential. However, whole digesta fermentation, possibly hindered by high sugar content, did not show similar effects. Overall, CBSs can potentially enhance nutritional quality in bakery products.

title: Efficient capillary electrophoretic analysis of anthraquinones and phenolic acids in functional foods using a novel deep eutectic solvent–in–deep eutectic solvent microemulsion
abstract: This study for the first time applies a deep eutectic solvent-in-deep eutectic solvent microemulsion system as the separation medium in microemulsion electrokinetic chromatography to effectively separate an detect multiple components in Cassia seeds. The optimal experimental conditions obtained via single-factor experiments and response surface methodology are as follows: The concentration of menthol-n-octanol was 0.30%, the concentration of choline chloride-ethylene glycol is 0.60%, and the pH value is 8.49. The microemulsion contains 2% SDS and 10 mM borax. The proposed method demonstrates an excellent linear relationship, with all correlation coefficients (R 2 ) above 0.999. The calculated detection limits and quantification limits are 0.5940-1.8987 μg/mL and 1.9802-6.3291 μg/mL, respectively. The recovery results are good, ranging from 90.68% to 107.07%. The proposed method enables the effective detection of anthraquinones and phenolic acids in food matrix, demonstrating its superior environmental friendliness and practical applicability.

title: Study of polyvinyl alcohol/starch-based hydrogel pads loaded with blueberry anthocyanin/citric acid/gardenia red/yellow/blue overlapping color system for monitoring beef freshness
abstract: In this study, a water-absorbent indicator pad with blueberry anthocyanins (BA), citric acid (CA), gardenia yellow (Y), gardenia red (R), gardenia blue (B) and their compound colors superimposed in a polyvinyl alcohol/starch-based hydrogel was prepared for dynamic monitoring of beef freshness at 4 °C. The addition of CA increased the redness of the pads compared to only BA, whereas the gardenia yellow/gardenia blue mixture significantly increased the range of color change of the indicator pads at pH 6-7 (brownish-red to light khaki to grassy-green) compared to the other colors. The initial color of the indicator pads was red, which gradually turned green with the volatilization of nitrogenous compounds from the beef and the leaching of the gravy. Combined with the correlation analysis between the color change of the indicator pads and the beef storage process, it was verified that the indicator pads could reflect the freshness of beef simply and accurately.

title: Study on the overall network structure and stability mechanism of food biomacromolecule based emulsion from the perspective of the interaction of interface and continuous
abstract: The emulsion consists of dispersed phase, oil-water interface and continuous phase. The interaction of interface and continuous phase (IICP) connect dispersed and continuous phase to form an overall network, which determines the emulsion stability. However, there is currently a lack of evaluation systems for IICP, as well as unclear mechanisms for their impact on the overall network and emulsion stability. Herein, an evaluation method for IICP was constructed via quartz crystal microbalance (QCM-D), investigated the influence mechanism of different gelatin and cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) interaction modes on IICP and overall network. Results displayed gelatin and CNCs were respectively adsorbed in the interface and continuous phase at pH = 7, formed gelatin-based interfacial film and dense cellulose-based network, contributed to enhancing IICP through intermolecular hydrogen bond, thus formed a stronger overall network and emulsion stability than pH = 4 and pH = 11. Therefore, this work can provide new ideas for the research on food emulsification systems.

title: Divergent temperature regulation of dough sheet extensibility driven by moisture threshold during mixing
abstract: Dough sheet extensibility is synergistically regulated by water addition and mixing temperature, yet their interaction mechanisms remain unclear. Employing water content (34%, 37%, 40%) and mixing temperature 4-45 °C, this study investigated dough sheet extensibility, water state and distribution homogeneity, glutenin-gliadin interactions, and gluten network structure. At 34% water content, extensibility first increased then decreased with mixing temperature, peaking at 25 °C. Conversely, at 40% condition, extensibility decreased monotonically by 29.66% from 4 °C to 45 °C. Mechanistically, mixing temperatures at 25 °C with 34% water condition optimized gluten network densification by increasing weakly bound water (increased 2.99% than 45 °C) and hydration homogeneity (reduced 30.94% CV than 45 °C). At 40%, low temperature (4 °C) suppressed free water surge (67.65% reduction) and protein depolymerization (25.08% LPP decrease), driving glutenin-gliadin crosslinking (23.81%/15.43% reduction in α/γ subunit extractability; 46.64% HMW-GS increase than 45 °C) to form hyper-branched networks. These insights establish quantitative processing windows: high-extensibility zone (40% water content + ≤15 °C), high-strength zone (34% water content + ≥35 °C), and balanced zone (37% moisture +4-35 °C).

title: A novel heteropeptide self-assembly-cascaded dual-enzyme (HSC-DE) system for cascade synthesis of enzymatically modified isoquercitrin (EMIQ) from rutin and sucrose
abstract: Enzymatically modified isoquercitrin (EMIQ), a natural compound known for its antioxidant, anti-proliferative, and anti-inflammatory properties, exhibits remarkable bioavailability and low toxicity, making it a promising therapeutic agent for diabetic kidney disease. However, conventional chemical synthesis of EMIQ is hampered by inefficiency, high reagent consumption, and substantial by-product formation. In this study, EMIQ was produced from rutin and sucrose using a novel Heteropeptide Self-Assembly-Cascaded Dual-Enzyme (HSC-DE) system, which co-immobilized α-L-rhamnosidase and amylosucrase via SpyTag/SpyCatcher pairs. This system significantly enhances reaction efficiency by adding the substrate and gradient temperature, achieving a sucrose conversion rate of 98.3% within 24 h, which was increased by 5.7% compared to previous (92.6%). Notably, the yield of quercetin-3-O-tetraglucoside, the form with optimal bioavailability, reached 62.1%, an increase of 12% over previous methods. This study presents a novel, sustainable, and highly effective bioengineering strategy for the synthesis of EMIQ, highlighting its potential for scalable and environmentally friendly production.

title: Smart evaluation of tea quality: machine learning-assisted SERS for white tea vintage authentication and grade classification
abstract: Traditional sensory evaluation methods for tea-relying on empirical experience, visual colorimetry, and subjective taste perception-suffer from irreproducible inter-rater variability and inability to quantify bioactive markers, thus failing to establish scientifically verifiable quality standards. To address this, we developed an intelligent platform integrating surface-enhanced Raman scattering with machine learning for rapid and quantitative white tea analysis, enabling detection within just 20 min. Utilizing silver nano-coral substrates for signal enhancement and a 785 nm portable Raman spectrometer for full-spectrum data acquisition, we constructed a hybrid machine learning architecture featuring Random Forest for vintage classification (96% accuracy) and Gradient Boosting Regressor for epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) quantification (R 2 = 0.98, the values of Root Mean Square Error, Mean Absolute Error, and Mean Square Error all approach zero). This approach established a definitive EGCG-content grading hierarchy: Yinzhen > Mudan > Gongmei > Shoumei, which is highly consistent with traditional sensory evaluation methods, while provides additional quantitative ability.

title: Pectin degradation during high-humidity hot air impingement blanching contributes to microstructure development of cell wall and drying rate increase of strawberry
abstract: This study investigated the effects of high-humidity hot air impingement blanching (HHAIB) at 110 °C for varying treatment time (0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 s) on the pectin properties, cell wall structure, moisture migration, and drying characteristics of strawberries. Compared to unlaunched samples, HHAIB reduced drying time at 60 °C by 27.80%-40.61% and enhanced moisture migration during the drying process. HHAIB induced the breakage of both the main and side chains of water-soluble pectin and the reduction of rhamnogalacturonan-I domain in chelator-soluble pectin. Furthermore, HHAIB reduced the molecular weight of pectin by 5.75-71.08% and raised the degree of esterification to 37.20-44.39% when compared to unblanched samples. Correspondingly, the changes in pectin primarily led to the formation of mesoporous structures (<50 nm) in cell wall. In conclusion, HHAIB treatment at 110 °C for 90 s was more effective at promoting moisture migration and accelerating drying rate at 60 °C.

title: Convergence of computer analysis and biological screening: Advanced immunoanalytical platform for ultra-sensitive oxyfluorfen detection
abstract: The common use of Oxyfluorfen (Oxy), a diphenyl ether herbicide, in agriculture, necessitates the development of rapid detection methods to ensure food safety, mitigate environmental risks, and enable on-site pesticide residue monitoring. In this study we developed a highly sensitive immunochromatographic strip for the detection of Oxy. Through computer-assisted hapten design, antibody screening, and system optimization, the method achieved rapid detection of Oxy residues in agricultural products. The optimized strip demonstrated calculated limits of detection (cLOD) of 9.96-14.71 ng/g in apples, cucumbers, cowpeas, and lettuce, significantly lower than the national standard limit. Method validation showed spike recovery rates of 95.2-98.8%, with high consistency to LC-MS/MS results (R 2 > 0.99). This technology offers advantages such as simplicity (results in 8 min), low cost, and resistance to matrix interference, making it suitable for on-site monitoring of agricultural product safety.

title: Dynamic light exposure from afternoon shading reveals aromatic plasticity in grapes and wines from a semi-arid region
abstract: To mitigate afternoon heat stress and improve aroma attributes in semi-arid regions, Cabernet Sauvignon grapevines were subjected to moderate (MD, 1.5 h) and strong shading (SD, 2.5 h) treatments over three vintages (2021-2023). Plant responses to diurnal light dynamics were assessed, berry and wine volatiles were analyzed, and wine sensory was evaluated. Results showed that photosynthetic assimilation of grapevines was suppressed by 50% during shading, while photosynthesis during exposure and leaf area were enhanced. Berry volatiles in MD and SD were 16% and 10% lower than CK at 2021 harvest, but were enhanced in the latter two years. Linalool, hexanal, β-damascenone, and 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one were key light-responsive biomarkers. Shaded wines exhibited elevated levels of terpenoids and norisoprenoids, contributing to improved fruity-floral aromas and sensory scores in 2022 and 2023. This study provides new insights into grapevine responses to light modulation and the volatile modification of grape and wine under semi-arid conditions.

title: Unveiling the bioactive potential of microalgae: Integrative analysis of nutritional composition and peptidomic signatures
abstract: This study aims to identify potential bioactive peptide in different microalgae species. Proteins were extracted by mechanical disruption, digested, and analyzed by LC-MS/MS. Bioactive peptides or motifs with previously reported bioactivities (antihypertensive, antidiabetic, and antioxidant potential) were successfully identified and quantified in Chlorella vulgaris, Phaeodactylum tricornutum, Dunaliella salina, Nannochloropsis oculata and Arthrospira platensis, respectively. Notably, the antidiabetic peptide IPR was detected in P. tricornutum. Additionally, the study presents a comprehensive biochemical characterization of five microalgae species. A. platensis contained the highest protein (71.6 g/100 g dry matter), while N. oculata and P. tricornutum were richest in lipids (∼17 g/100 g d.m.) enriched in ω-3 and ω-6 fatty acids. The amino acid profiles indicated favorable essential amino acid indices across all species. Distinct pigment signatures included C-phycocyanin in A. platensis, fucoxanthin in P. tricornutum, violaxanthin in N. oculata, lutein in D. salina and C. vulgaris, and β-carotene across species.
