It facilitated higher yields of polyphenols (≤ 35.5 g/100 g) in specific species with insignificant differences in radical scavenging activity compared to controls (p 90% viability in human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells. These findings evidence the potential of L. rhamnosus in conserving beneficial seaweed metabolites, thus underscoring their prospects as functional foods.

title: Machine learning-assisted carbon dot sensing for iron speciation in Auricularia auricula soaking solutions under various processing conditions
abstract: Accurate iron speciation in Auricularia auricula soaking solution is essential for evaluating nutritional quality, as bioavailability depends on its valence state (Fe 2+ / Fe 3+ ). Herein, a machine learning-assisted fluorescent sensing strategy based on bamboo-derived carbon quantum dots (CQDs) was developed for iron speciation analysis in Auricularia auricula soaking solutions. The CQDs, synthesized via a one-pot hydrothermal method, acted as a selective probe for Fe 3+ through static fluorescence quenching, while Fe 2+ was indirectly quantified following H 2 O 2 oxidation to Fe 3+ . The method exhibited a wide linear range of 1-500 μM with a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.30 μM. Application to soaking solutions showed iron predominantly existed as Fe 3+ , while the bioaccessible Fe 2+ fraction decreased to below 1% after 30 min at 100 °C. Furthermore, a random forest model revealed temperature- and origin-dependent iron leaching behavior, achieving excellent predictive performance with a coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.99) between measured and predicted values.

title: Artificial intelligence-based modeling and quality evaluation of turmeric under full-spectrum artificial sunlight drying
abstract: Full-spectrum artificial sunlight drying (FSASLD) was investigated as an innovative drying technology for turmeric dehydration, focusing on drying characteristics, quality preservation, and machine learning (ML)-based modeling. Turmeric slices were dried at power levels of 200-400 W using a controlled artificial sunlight drying system. Increasing power level accelerated moisture removal, with effective moisture diffusivity increasing from 2.54 × 10 -10 to 5.07 × 10 -10 m 2 s -1 . Color degradation kinetics varied with the evaluated color parameter and drying condition, and both zero-order and first-order models adequately described color changes during drying. Curcumin retention exceeded 85%, indicating effective preservation under FSASLD conditions. Five ML algorithms were employed to predict moisture ratio from drying variables. Among them, the Gaussian process regression model achieved the highest predictive performance with an average test coefficient of determination of 0.9879. These findings highlight the potential of FSASLD as a controllable alternative to traditional drying.

title: sweelin®, a novel sweet protein, does not affect blood glucose and insulin levels – a double-blind, crossover, randomized study
abstract: A novel hyper-sweet protein, sweelin®, enables sugar reduction without compromising taste. This double-blind, randomized, crossover study evaluated the effect of sweelin® on blood glucose, insulin and GLP-1 levels compared to stevia and dextrose in healthy adults. In this study, subjects consumed sweelin® (0.051 g), stevia Reb-M (0.225 g) or dextrose (75 g) in beverages matched for sweetness levels. Blood samples were collected at baseline and during 120-min post consumption. Each participant (n = 19) consumed each of the three beverages in a randomized order. At every time point after consumption, as well as iAUC, glucose and insulin levels were significantly lower following sweelin® consumption compared to dextrose (p < 0.0001), and not different from stevia. Overall, the findings indicate that sweelin®, is well tolerated and does not increase blood glucose, insulin or GLP-1 levels in healthy individuals, and suggest that sweelin® may serve as a metabolically neutral alternative for individuals seeking to reduce sugar intake. This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov (identifier code: NCT06520293).

title: Synergistic fermentation of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum 40 and 42 regulates browning in soybean paste and its mechanistic analysis
abstract: The color of soybean paste is a crucial sensory attribute for evaluating its quality, with light-colored and color-stable products being more favored in the market. The microbial community plays a significant role in determining color variations in soybean paste; however, the key strains and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, two lactic acid bacteria strains were isolated from light-colored soybean paste, and their combined application significantly improved the color of fermented soybean paste. Mechanistic investigations revealed that on the one hand, the lactic acid bacteria consumed reducing sugars, thereby decreasing the substrates available for Maillard and caramelization reactions and ultimately inhibiting non-enzymatic browning. On the other hand, the lactic acid bacteria decomposed proteins to produce antioxidant peptides capable of chelating metal ions and scavenging free radicals, thereby suppressing enzymatic browning. This dual-pathway mechanism elucidates how lactic acid bacteria regulate the color of soybean paste and provides theoretical support for the development of anti-browning fermentation agents and targeted color control strategies.

title: Effects of sustained release of tea polyphenols from a bacterial cellulose-based coating to prolong shelf-life of fresh walnuts
abstract: Fresh walnuts are highly perishable due to high moisture and unsaturated lipid contents. A multifunctional coating was developed by grafting glycerol onto oxidized bacterial cellulose to form a stable nanonetwork and incorporating tea polyphenols. Structural analyses revealed a compact network with improved crystallinity and barrier integrity, supporting sustained release of tea polyphenols. The coating exhibited strong antioxidant activity (72% scavenging) and broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy (inhibition rates up to 97.8%). Cytocompatibility assays using human gastric epithelial cells confirmed excellent biocompatibility. When applied to fresh walnuts, the coating reduced moisture loss (maintaining a moisture content of 23.4%), delayed lipid oxidation (suppressing acid value to 2.3 mg KOH·g -1 ), and preserved total phenolic content (3.52 mg/g) after 60 days. Furthermore, it effectively inhibited microbial growth, maintaining the total viable count at 3.8 log CFU/g, significantly below the safety threshold. These results demonstrate a green, effective strategy for sustainable preservation of perishable nuts.

title: The chelation mechanism, stability and calcium absorption activity of Ruditapes philippinarum peptide‑calcium chelate
abstract: This study optimized the preparation of peptide‑calcium chelates from Ruditapes philippinarum protein (RPP). Under optimal conditions, RPP's calcium-binding capacity reached 95.79 ± 2.09 mg/g. Structural characterization (FTIR, UV, SEM) and molecular docking revealed that chelation occurred via coordination bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and hydrogen bonds (binding energy: -5.74 kcal/mol, primarily involving carboxyl oxygen atoms in a bidentate pattern. RPP-Ca demonstrated high stability, maintaining an 80%-85% calcium retention rate at pH 6.0-10.0. Furthermore, calcium transport assays showed that RPP-Ca's transport capacity was 42.20 ± 1.54% higher than that of inorganic CaCl 2 . These findings indicate that RPP-Ca is a stable, high-affinity chelate with superior bioavailability, making it a promising candidate for functional calcium supplementation.

title: The differential effects of sodium chloride on the formation of amyloid-like fibrils derived from glutenin and gliadin
abstract: Although NaCl modulates gluten assembly, its component-specific effects on glutenin and gliadin amyloid-like fibrillation remain unclear. This study examined glutenin- and gliadin-derived amyloid-like fibrils (AFs) formed at 0-2.0% NaCl during 0-7 min heating. In glutenin, low-to-moderate ionic strength promoted electrostatic shielding and β-sheet stacking, which, together with hydrophobic interactions, favored relatively long and uniform fibrils. Gliadin showed a more rapid and salt-sensitive fibrillation response, indicating that ionic strength strongly influenced its early assembly behavior. Under high salt, gliadin fibrillation was rapidly initiated, whereas subsequent ThT fluorescence decline, broadened SE-HPLC profiles, irregular AFM fibrillar aggregates, and large H₀ variation suggested reduced ThT accessibility, increased molecular heterogeneity, and weakened structural stability. These results indicate that glutenin mainly forms a stable fibrillar scaffold, whereas gliadin acts as a salt-sensitive kinetic modulator. This study clarifies salt-mediated gluten fibrillation and supports targeted texture regulation in wheat-based products.

title: Editorial Board
Mechanisms of action of melatonin and salicylic acid in enhancing postharvest longevity of grapes
abstract: Postharvest senescence, pathogens, and chilling injury present major challenges in the grape industry. This review synthesizes evidence on the physiological and molecular mechanisms by which combined exogenous melatonin (MT) and salicylic acid (SA) preserve grape berries quality. During postharvest storage, the MT-SA crosstalk delays senescence by downregulating ethylene biosynthesis and respiration while bolstering antioxidant defenses to mitigate reactive oxygen species. This synergy preserves structural firmness, stimulates nutritional metabolites, and inhibits enzymatic browning. Additionally, the treatment enhances stress resistance through the activation of defense signaling pathways. Despite these theoretical benefits, empirical data remain inconsistent, with some studies showing individual treatments outperforming the combination. This review suggests these discrepancies stem from non-optimized concentration ratios rather than biochemical incompatibility. Future research must prioritize orthogonal experimental designs to identify the precise dose-dependent synergistic thresholds required to maximize the commercial efficacy of this dual-treatment strategy.

title: Mechanistic insights into the crisping of Nata-de-Coco: soluble polymer-induced swelling of bacterial cellulose and its use in microgel fabrication
abstract: Bacterial cellulose (BC) exhibits a densely entangled nanofibrillar network, limiting structural tunability and hindering both texture optimization in Nata-de-Coco and microscale fabrication of functional microgels. Despite widespread industrial use of polymer-assisted crisping, its underlying physicochemical mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we elucidate a temperature-dependent swelling-diffusion mechanism using carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). Dynamic light scattering shows reversible contraction of CMC coils from 2381 nm (30 °C) to 1099 nm (90 °C), enabling nanopore diffusion, followed by re-expansion upon cooling that loosens the BC network. By decoupling molecular weight (Mw), degree of substitution (DS), and concentration, we establish a unified regulatory framework. Optimal conditions (MW ≈ 325,600 Da, DS = 1.2, C = 0.9 wt%) increase specific surface area from 121.87 to 144.64 m 2 /g, enhance compressive modulus from 40 to 408 kPa, expand pore volume to 0.51 cm 3 /g, and reduce microgel size to 13.2 μm. This work provides a mechanistic basis for scalable polymer-mediated BC structural engineering.

title: Analysis of key aroma attributes and characteristic volatile compounds in multiple rice varieties
abstract: The aroma of rice was a critical determinant of its quality and significantly influences consumer acceptance. This study investigated 21 rice varieties. A total of 85 volatile compounds were identified using solid-phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. Quantitative descriptive analysisrevealed five distinct aroma attributes. Through the screening of differential compounds between the high and low-aroma groups and subsequent correlation analysis and gas chromatography-olfactometry verification, a total of 19 volatile compounds were identified. Further addition tests supported that: hexanal, 2-butylfuran, 3-octen-2-one, E-2-octenal, E-2-decenal, and 2-butyl-2-octenal might serve as characteristic volatiles for the grassy aroma; 2-ethylfuran and 2-heptylfuran were candidate contributors to the nutty aroma; 2-acetyl-1-pyrroline (2-AP) and indole were identified as the dominant volatiles responsible for the popcorn and floral aromas, respectively. No volatile compounds correlated significantly with sweet aroma. This study provided a scientific basis for the aroma regulation and sensory evaluation of cooked rice.

title: The mechanisms of freezing-induced meat-like layered fibrous structure formation and texture enhancement in mycoprotein products
abstract: This study systematically elucidated how freezing conditions regulate the formation of meat-like layered fibrous structures and quality development in mycoprotein products. For samples frozen at -10 °C and -20 °C, hardness, chewiness, and degree of organization increased with storage time, and at 19 d, the hardness of the -10 °C and -20 °C samples reached 2.29 and 1.88 times that of the unfrozen controls, respectively. Ice crystals induced hyphal aggregation and realignment through mechanical compression, forming layered fibrous structures at the macroscopic level and enhancing hyphal entanglement and network density, thereby promoting improvements in texture and structural performance. Meanwhile, slow freezing triggered protein conformational rearrangement and strengthened intermolecular interactions, including disulfide bonds, hydrogen bonds, and hydrophobic interactions. These molecular changes were closely associated with ice recrystallization and water redistribution, which regulated molecular mobility and facilitated stabilization of the three-dimensional protein-polysaccharide network.

title: Red pitaya peel as encapsulant for hybrid crude palm oil nanoparticles: Characterization and 60-day stability
abstract: The red pitaya peel (Hylocereus polyrhizus) is an underutilized agro-industrial by-product rich in functional compounds, while hybrid crude palm oil contains levels of carotenoids and tocopherols but is prone to oxidation. This study developed and characterized hybrid crude palm oil nanoparticles using freeze-dried pitaya peel as an encapsulant. Eight formulations were tested using a 2³ factorial design, and the one with 150 mg of oil and 150 mg of peel was selected. The nanoparticles exhibited high encapsulation efficiency (95.6 ± 2.6%), full carotenoid retention (1386.8 ± 21.2 µg/g), and betalain content (2.40 ± 0.01 mg/g). They exhibited particle sizes of 331.5–351.8 nm, PDI 0.35–0.36, and zeta potential near ±30 mV, with good stability at 4 ± 1 °C over 60 days. Despite some pigment degradation, antioxidant activity remained more stable than in free constituents. These results highlight the feasibility of using pitaya peel as an encapsulating matrix for functional applications.

title: Effect of starches on the preparation and properties of special low-protein scones
abstract: Special low-protein food development has attracted much attention in the medical and food community. Herein, low-protein scones (LPSs) were developed using a three-step baking method with five starches, sugar, baking powder, butter, whole egg liquid, and water. Key formulations required sugar/starch and butter/starch mass ratios of at least 0.1 and 0.3, respectively. The LPSs had low protein contents (0.38-0.56 g/100 g) and high energy values (1831-1876 kJ/100 g), which confirmed confirm their suitability to meet clinical dietary requirements. Gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry recognized 83 volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Moreover, the LPSs with tapioca starch, lotus rhizome starch, and low-protein powder exhibited 2, 3, and 12 characteristic VOCs, respectively. Their free fatty acid released percentages in in vitro digestion model depended on starch sources: low-protein powder (92.90%) > lotus rhizome starch (52.31%) > wheat starch (50.94%) > corn starch (45.98%) > tapioca starch (25.34%). These findings enhanced understanding of starch-food relationships.

title: Identification and evaluation of citrus peel-derived polymethoxyflavonoids as natural SIRT1 activators
abstract: • A non-fluorometric MS-based assay enables reliable SIRT1 evaluation. • Citrus peel extracts contain compounds that promote SIRT1 activity. • PMFs are identified as key activators of SIRT1 deacetylase activity. • Heptamethoxyflavone (HMF) shows the strongest SIRT1 activation among tested PMFs. • Citrus peels are a rich source of food-derived SIRT1 activators.

title: Comprehensive characterization of walnut oil processing by-products: biochemical composition, bioactive properties, and polyphenol in vitro bioaccessibility and bioavailability
abstract: Underutilized by-products from the walnut-oil industry, namely walnut oilcake (WOC) and walnut oil dregs (WOD), were evaluated for their nutritional composition, phenolic compound profile and digestive behaviour, as well as bioactive properties (antioxidant, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, cytotoxic and prebiotic activities). WOC was rich in protein (38.1 g/100 g) and dietary fiber (32.6 g/100 g), while WOD presented high fat (46.8 g/100 g) and carbohydrate content (20.9 g/100 g). Glansreginin A was the predominant phenolic compound in both matrices. Following in vitro digestion using the INFOGEST protocol, higher overall polyphenol bioaccessibility was noticed in WOD (78%) compared to WOC (15%). Bioaccessible fractions exhibited higher antioxidant activity than the undigested samples. Glansreginin A was detected only on the cellular apical compartment suggesting the absence of transport across Caco-2 cells. After in vitro digestion, the non-bioaccessible fractions enhanced the growth of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium strains, in some cases surpassing fructooligosaccharides, a standard prebiotic. These findings support the valorisation of walnut by-products as functional ingredients, also contributing to sustainable food systems.

title: Synergistic construction of heat-stable resistant starch by confined Retrogradation of short-chain amylose within calcium alginate beads
abstract: As a functional carbohydrate with dietary fiber-like properties, resistant starch (RS) has attracted attention for its potential to regulate blood glucose fluctuations. In this study, varying concentrations (10-40%) of short-chain amylose (SCA) were encapsulated within calcium alginate beads and subjected to retrogradation at 50 °C. The confined space within the beads facilitated molecular rearrangement and the formation of stable crystalline structures in the SCA. With increasing SCA concentration, the onset temperature (To) of the cooked beads increased up to 86.64 °C, and the enthalpy change (ΔH) gradually rose to 36.69 J·g -1 , indicating enhanced thermal resistance. The RS content in the cooked beads increased significantly, reaching 51.3% at 40% SCA, far exceeding the 8.0% observed in non-encapsulated samples. The estimated glycemic index (eGI) decreased from approximately 103 to about 73, suggesting a significant reduction in digestibility. This strategy provides a feasible approach for designing heat-resistant RS-based ingredients for thermally processed foods.

title: Preparation, antioxidant and antibacterial properties of PCL/APS composite nanofiber films embedded with CS/TPP-CV nanospheres for blueberry preservation
abstract: At present, active cling films for food preservation face a core bottleneck: the encapsulation materials for active substances have limited effectiveness, failing to achieve a balance between material safety and sustained-release performance. In this study, carvacrol (CV) was encapsulated in chitosan (CS)/sodium tripolyphosphate (TPP) ionic gelation nanospheres, with an encapsulation efficiency of 89.3 ± 1.1%. The gel nanospheres were integrated into polycaprolactone/astragalus polysaccharide (PCL/APS) nanofibers via electrospinning (ELS) technology to fabricate active cling films. Characterization results showed that increasing the chitosan/tripolyphosphate-carvacrol (CS/TPP-CV) loading enlarged the nanofiber diameter, reduced the water contact angle, and simultaneously increased the water vapor transmission rate. The packaging film exhibited significant antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli (96.5% inhibition rate) and Staphylococcus aureus (95.1% inhibition rate), along with excellent antioxidant capacity (DPPH radical scavenging rate of 60.2% and ABTS radical scavenging rate of 74.4%). In fruit preservation experiments, compared with the control group, the chitosan/tripolyphosphate-carvacrol-loaded nanofiber film reduced the weight loss of blueberries to approximately 3%, increased the retention of vitamin C (VC) content to around 40%, and extended the storage period of blueberries to 10 days. Blood compatibility tests confirmed that the material had an extremely low hemolysis rate, indicating high safety. This study pioneers the synergistic application of chitosan/tripolyphosphate gel nanosphere-encapsulated carvacrol and electrospun nanofibers, providing a scalable technical solution for next-generation food preservation.

title: Bio-inspired exosome mimetics as novel nanocarriers to enhance physicochemical stability and controlled release of linalool
abstract: Linalool, a widely used food flavoring with antioxidant activity, is limited by its volatility and poor physicochemical stability. In this study, a food-compatible exosome mimetic delivery system composed of cholesterol, ceramide, sphingomyelin, phosphatidylcholine, and phosphatidylserine was developed to improve linalool stabilization. Encapsulation conditions were optimized, achieving a maximum loading of 1% (w/w) at 150.10 ± 8.12 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.20 ± 0.01, and an encapsulation efficiency of 82.01 ± 1.50%. Physicochemical assessments demonstrated robust stability across varying pH levels, temperatures, and ionic strengths. The controlled release profile of linalool from L-EMs follows diffusion-driven kinetics consistent with the Higuchi model. The Korsmeyer-Peppas exponent (n = 0.55) revealed significant linalool-membrane interactions and anomalous transport. The antioxidant properties of the vesicles preserved linalool's radical-scavenging activity. Overall, this study demonstrates that exosome mimetics serve as simplified, food-compatible lipid carriers for stabilizing volatile bioactives, offering a promising strategy for functional food applications.

title: Formulation optimization of emulsifier-based hydrated gel cake improver for α-crystal stabilization using D-optimal mixture design
abstract: Cake gel is widely used in bakery systems, yet its functionality declines during storage due to polymorphic transition of fat crystals from the α to β' phase. This study investigated compositional control of polymorphic stability in a distilled monoglyceride-based hydrated gel using a D-optimal mixture design. Polyglycerol ester (0-10%) and polysorbate 80 (0-5%) were incorporated at varying water levels and evaluated over 1, 30, and 60 days of storage. Thermal transitions were analyzed by differential scanning calorimetry and crystalline organization by X-ray diffraction. Fresh samples exhibited a coagel index close to 1 and a characteristic α-phase spacing of approximately 4.1 Å. During storage, systems lacking polyglycerol ester showed enhanced polymorphic conversion, whereas ester-enriched formulations preserved α-phase lamellar structure. Optimization identified 10% polyglycerol ester, 3.294% polysorbate 80, and 50.206% water as the optimal composition, achieving a desirability of 0.969 at day 30.

title: Membrane-protected carboxylated COF-based micro-SPE coupled with HPLC-MS/MS for simultaneous determination of 16 heterocyclic aromatic amines in Cantonese bakery
abstract: Carcinogenic heterocyclic aromatic amines (HAAs) inevitably form during thermal processing, particularly in sugar- and meat-rich Cantonese baked products, making sensitive quantification of trace HAAs essential for food safety. Here, we synthesized a carboxyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) via post-modification, namely TpBD-COOH, and evaluated it as an adsorbent for HAA enrichment. Despite exhibiting a low surface area (96 m 2 ·g -1 ), TpBD-COOH exhibited high affinity and rapid adsorption (10-20 min) for 16 HAAs, with adsorption behavior well described by fitting pseudo-second-order and Freundlich models. Furthermore, a membrane-protected micro-solid-phase extraction (M-μSPE) method coupled with high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) analysis was developed, achieving low limits of detection (0.04-1.39 μg·kg -1 ), satisfactory recoveries (72.6-118.7%), and good analytical stability for profiling of multiple HAAs. These results indicate that the proposed M-μSPE-HPLC-MS/MS method shows strong potential for food safety monitoring of thermally processed bakery products.

title: Dietary fiber modification by cellulase-AP3 supplementation tailors oat digestion under elderly gastrointestinal conditions with attenuated starch hydrolysis and enhanced polyphenol bioaccessibility
abstract: The resilient fiber matrix of oats limits nutrient release and moderates glycemic response. This study employed a dynamic in vitro stomach-intestine model to investigate how Cellulase-AP3 enzyme supplementation alters oat digestion under simulated elderly conditions. Cellulase-AP3 supplementation caused significant oat matrix disintegration by enzymatically converting insoluble fiber (54.84% to 32.18%) into soluble fiber (50.56% to 59.63%), which in turn elevated digestive fluid viscosity and delayed gastric emptying. This modified physiological environment hindered amylase action, thereby substantially reducing starch hydrolysis from 33.59% to 23.88% and lowering the estimated glycemic index (eGI) from 64.29 to 53.72. Cellulase-AP3 supplementation also enhanced polyphenol bioaccessibility, increasing the release of key phenolic acids (caffeic, vanillic, chlorogenic) above adult-model levels. Factor analysis associated Cellulase-AP3 with a dual improvement in higher soluble fiber/attenuated glycemic impact (F1) and enhanced polyphenol release (F2). These findings establish a novel in situ fiber modification strategy to tailor oat digestion for the elderly.

title: From byproduct to bioresource: Antioxidant potential, flavor profile, and microbiological quality of recovered water from freeze-dried and rotary evaporation dried Muscat grapes
abstract: Grape drying generates substantial condensate (recovered water) containing soluble aroma and bioactive compounds, offering potential for value-added reutilization. This study characterized the antioxidant capacity, volatile profile, and microbiological quality of the water recovered during freeze-drying (FD) and rotary evaporation drying (RED) of Muscat grapes. Both condensates retained measurable grape-derived bioactives and volatiles (e.g., linalool, squalene). FD-recovered water exhibited peak total phenolic content (0.49 mg GAE/L) and flavonoid (0.42 mg RE/L) contents at 60 h, accompanied by increased DPPH (25.27%) and ABTS •+ (20.99%) radical scavenging activities. FD generally demonstrated higher antioxidant retention than RED, which induced greater thermal degradation. Notably, pathogenic indicators (E. coli and S. aureus) were absent across all samples. Although absolute antioxidant levels were relatively low, the retention of natural grape aromas alongside satisfactory hygiene indicators suggests the recovered water's potential as a clean-label flavoring base, though comprehensive safety and sensory evaluations remain necessary before industrial application.

title: Nanoencapsulation of bioactive compounds: recent advances in food systems for enhanced stability and bioavailability
abstract: Bioactive compounds from natural sources offer significant health benefits but face challenges including poor stability, low bioavailability, and degradation during processing and storage. Nanoencapsulation has emerged as a transformative technology to protect these sensitive compounds and enhance their functionality in food matrices. This review systematically examines recent advances (2022-2025) in nanoencapsulation strategies for bioactive compounds, organized as follows: (1) a methodology section detailing literature search strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria; (2) a comparative analysis of major nanocarrier platforms (lipid-based, biopolymer-based, and hybrid systems) organized by functional properties; (3) mechanisms of stability enhancement and controlled release; (4) bioavailability enhancement and gastrointestinal fate; (5) industrial applications, economic feasibility, and regulatory landscape; and (6) future perspectives including AI-driven design and personalized nutrition. Special attention is given to innovative encapsulation materials derived from food waste, plant-based proteins, and polysaccharides aligned with sustainability principles. The review highlights breakthrough findings in controlled release mechanisms, gastrointestinal stability, and cellular uptake pathways. Regulatory considerations, safety assessments, and industrial scalability are comprehensively discussed.

title: Inhibition of starch retrogradation in fermented rice cakes during simulated cold chain logistics
abstract: Starch retrogradation causes quality deterioration in fermented rice cakes (FRCs) during logistics storage, reducing shelf life and consumer acceptability. FRC was stored under four temperature conditions: stable refrigeration at -18 °C/4 °C (G1), temperature fluctuation protocols (G2 and G3), and ambient storage at 25 °C (G4). Refrigerated storage preserved moisture and limited hardness, whereas ambient storage and temperature fluctuations induced moisture loss and textual deterioration. LF-NMR revealed water redistribution from bound to free states, with refrigerated samples maintaining stable water distribution while ambient storage accelerated moisture migration. XRD showed crystallinity, increasing from 24% to 44% (G1), and 56% (G4). DSC showed increases in melting enthalpy, indicating ordered crystalline structures. SEM showed microstructural transformation from porous to dense structures, with severity correlating to storage temperature. Refrigeration maintains starch below critical rearrangement thresholds while elevated temperatures provide thermal activation for crystalline reconstruction. These findings provide theoretical basis for maintaining qualities of traditional fermented foods during logistics.

title: Rational fabrication of molecularly imprinted polymers based ratiometric fluorescence sensing platform with aggregation-induced emission effect for visual detection of 6PPD-Q in aquatic products
abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-benzoquinone (6PPD-Q) is ubiquitous in aquatic environments and poses big threats to food safety and public health. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop timely and effective methods to detect 6PPD-Q. In this work, the Zn-doped silicon quantum dots and Au nanoclusters were embedded in the molecularly imprinted polymers to form ratiometric fluorescence sensor for the detection of 6PPD-Q in the concentration ranging from 0.0099 to 1.0 μg·mL -1 with the detection limit of 3.0 ng·mL -1 . The imprinting factor was calculated as 2.56. Then, a 3D-printing device was developed to capture fluorescence for images digital image colorimetry of 6PPD-Q while YOLOv5 algorithm was employed to achieve a prediction accuracy of 99.6%. The recovery rates for real sample analysis ranged from 95.5% to 108.0%. This method offers a simple and rapid strategy for detecting 6PPD-Q in food samples.

title: Micro-aqueous hydration extraction for green and sustainable production of high-quality edible oils
abstract: Conventional edible oil extraction technologies suffer from low recovery, solvent residues, environmental pollution and nutrient degradation, while emerging aqueous-based methods face challenges such as higher water consumption, severe emulsification, and high costs, with the manifestations of these issues being highly dependent on raw material sources. Micro-aqueous hydration extraction (MAHE), a novel solvent-free, non-thermal green technology, achieves efficient oil separation via precise control of water addition and agitation intensity, leveraging the differential water affinity of oil and non-oil components under mild conditions. Core mechanisms include membrane protein rearrangement, storage protein aggregation-mediated system destabilization, and agitation-induced oil droplet coalescence. MAHE offers 90-95% recovery for most oilseeds, saves over 70% water vs. aqueous enzymatic extraction, avoids solvent residues, and preserves heat-sensitive nutrients. Limitations involve low efficiency for low-oil (<30%)/high-fiber materials, emulsification risk, and customized industrial equipment need. Future research should focus on intelligent optimization, hybrid pre-treatments, and industrial trials for commercialization.

title: Preparation and characterization of Tremella polysaccharide/corn glutelin-stabilized emulsion for quercetin delivery
abstract: Here, we present the design and characterization of Corn glutelin-Tremella polysaccharide (CG-TPs) complexes, highlighting their potential as novel natural emulsifiers for quercetin (Que) delivery. The formation of CG-TPs complexes was primarily mediated by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions, which induced conformational rearrangements in corn glutelin. These increased β-sheet and β-turn content, and optimized the hydrophilic-hydrophobic balance. CG-TPs exhibited outstanding emulsifying properties, with the emulsifying activity index (EAI) and emulsifying stability index (ESI) significantly increasing by 28.93% and 55.7%, respectively, compared to CG. Compared with corn glutelin alone, CG-TPs emulsions displayed reduced particle size, reduced Turbiscan Stability Index (TSI) values, and enhanced physical stability. Encapsulation of quercetin within the emulsions provided substantial protection against thermal and ultraviolet (UV) degradation. Moreover, quercetin loaded in CG-TPs emulsions demonstrated significantly greater antioxidant activity than quercetin dispersed in oil. Collectively, these findings indicate that CG-TPs emulsions represent a promising, biocompatible platform for stabilizing and efficiently delivering hydrophobic bioactive compounds.

title: Dynamic remodeling in lipophilic metabolites during Coffea canephora maturation: A lipidomic study
abstract: Lipids in coffee are involved in membrane structure, energy storage, stress response, and beverage quality. However, lipid metabolism during the maturation of Coffea species remains poorly understood. Here, we present the first comprehensive lipidomic analysis of Coffea canephora var. conilon beans across five maturation stages. Samples were analyzed using LC-Orbitrap, and data were processed using Compound Discoverer, MS-FINDER, and molecular networking, followed by multivariate statistical analysis. A total of 220 lipids were putatively annotated, representing 27 classes. Lipid profiles showed stage-specific changes throughout maturation. Stage M4 (45 weeks after flowering) emerged as a metabolic turning point characterized by widespread shifts in several lipid classes, including fatty amides, fatty acids, and hydroxytryptamides. These stage-specific lipid markers demonstrated the potential of lipidomics to guide optimal harvest time and develop predictive models linking lipid composition to coffee quality. These results fill an important gap in understanding C. canephora metabolism.

title: Fluorescent sensors and microdevices: a comprehensive review on real-time visual monitoring of freshness in meat and aquatic products
abstract: The rapid deterioration of meat and aquatic products demands advanced monitoring technologies. This review focuses on recent advances in fluorescent sensors for their freshness monitoring. It first analyzes and compares the signal providers, transduction mechanisms, and response patterns of these sensors. Next, it discusses how these sensors apply to key biochemical freshness indicators across the spoilage process. These indicators range from early autolytic metabolites (adenosine triphosphate and hypoxanthine) to later microbial spoilage markers (volatile amines, biogenic amines, pH, and sulfides), with a comparative analysis presented. Furthermore, a dedicated section evaluates the integration of these technologies into microdevices, including filter papers, polymeric membranes, gels, and bio-based membranes. Portability and real-time capability are identified as the primary bottlenecks for practical adoption. Finally, the review outlines the challenges and future directions for commercializing fluorescent sensors. Overall, this review aims to offer a holistic theoretical reference for developing practical freshness monitoring sensors.

title: Determination of micro/nanoplastics on the surface of polystyrene lunch boxes by pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry combined with efficient magnetic capture by Fe3O4 nanoparticles
abstract: In this study, 1 μm glass fiber membranes were used to enrich polystyrene microplastics (PS MPs), and then hydrophilic iron oxide nanoparticle (n-Fe 3 O 4 ) was used to capture the residual polystyrene nanoplastics (PS NPs), primarily through hydrogen bonding, coordination, and electrostatic interactions. MPs on membranes and NPs captured by n-Fe 3 O 4 were respectively determined by pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS). The method was verified by adding PS MNPs standard to ultrapure water. The detection limit of this method was 0.16 μg/cup for PS MPs and 0.03 μg/cup for PS NPs. The absolute recovery rates of MPs and NPs were 99 ± 2% and 89 ± 3%, respectively. The test results of three batches of PS lunch boxes showed that the content of PS MPs attached on surfaces was 6.79-12.30 μg/box, and the content of PS NPs was 0.51-0.96 μg/box. The migrated PS MPs and PS NPs were 4.71-5.19 μg/box and 1.27-1.40 μg/box respectively.

title: Analyzing the effect of dietary isoleucine on characterization of flesh flavor using a combination method of E-tongue, E-nose, and GC–MS
abstract: This experiment used combination of electronic tongue, electronic nose, and gas chromatography mass spectrometry methods to analyze the impact of dietary isoleucine (Ile) on the flavor in grass carp muscle. Key findings include: Ile improved the sweetness and umami and reduced sourness and bitterness of the flesh. Ile inhibited sulfide and the relative content of volatile compounds like nonanal and hexanal in muscle. Second, Ile enhanced the content of adenosine triphosphate, adenosine diphosphate, and adenosine monophosphate, and decreased the content of hypoxanthine. Furthermore, Ile raised the content of fatty acid (FA) and the enzymes related to FA synthesis. Based on the above results, it can be concluded that dietary Ile improved flesh flavor by reducing the relative content of volatile compounds like 1-octen-3-ol and increasing the content of FA and nucleotides, providing valuable insights into improving flesh quality.

title: Design of Photonic Crystal System for real-time monitoring of cold-chain transportation
abstract: Time-temperature indicator (TTI) has been widely used for real-time monitoring of perishable products during cold-chain transportation. However, the existing TTIs struggle to simultaneously achieve broad temperature monitoring ranges and high stability. Temperature-responsive photonic crystal (PC) materials can undergo obvious structural color changes through physical structural transformations. Herein, an ionic liquids (ILs) diffusion-type photonic crystal time-temperature indicator (PC-TTI) is developed. Duration of high-temperature exposure and quality of monitored product can be inferred based on the color change of the PC film. Leveraging the stability and environmental friendliness of polymer materials and ILs, this PC-TTI can achieve irreversible structural color changes. Moreover, by selecting ILs with different melting points, the PC-TTI can adapt to a wide temperature range. Featuring flexible design, simple preparation, high sensitivity, and robust stability, this kind of PC-TTI shows strong potential for real-time temperature monitoring applications in the food cold-chain industry.

title: Enzymatic modification of black bean dough: Mechanisms for enhancing physicochemical properties, noodle quality and frozen storage stability
abstract: In this study, the effects of transglutaminase (TGase) and glucose oxidase (GOD) on the quality of black bean dough, the starch hydrolysis kinetics and the stability of frozen storage of black bean noodles were investigated. The results of black bean dough research showed that TGase and GOD improved the structural order and thermal stability of black bean protein, especially the thermal stability increased from 105.07 J·g -1 to 874.70 J·g -1 . The results of black bean noodles showed that TGase and GOD inhibited the catalysis of amylase by forming a protein-starch complex, the predicted glycemic index (pGI) decreased from 88.09 to 66.85. During frozen storage, this stable protein structure prevented the deterioration of noodle quality caused by water migration and starch recrystallization, reduced noodles' cooking loss and deterioration of texture properties. This study provides data support for the development of black bean products with high quality, controlled glucose release and freezing stability.

title: In situ nanoencapsulation of curcumin in egg yolk low-density lipoprotein gels: Calcium-regulated protein network restructuring and stability enhancement
abstract: The structural compactness of egg yolk low-density lipoprotein (LDL) limits its application in protein-based hydrogels for hydrophobic bioactive delivery. In this study, calcium ion-regulated gelation was employed to induce LDL network restructuring and enable in situ nanoencapsulation of curcumin. Ca 2+ promoted LDL aggregation and gel network formation through electrostatic screening and charge bridging, accompanied by increased β-sheet content and enhanced hydrophobic interactions. As a result, a hierarchically interconnected protein network with hydrophobic microdomains and nanoscale confinement spaces was generated, allowing synchronous incorporation of curcumin during gel formation rather than post-gelation entrapment. Consequently, curcumin encapsulation efficiency increased from 63.3% to 93.2%, with markedly improved photothermal stability and digestion-responsive release behavior. The resulting gels exhibited elastic-dominant viscoelasticity and pronounced shear-thinning behavior. This study elucidates an ion-regulated lipoprotein gelation mechanism and provides a structurally tunable platform for functional bioactive encapsulation in food systems.

title: Investigation on the effects of drying methods on Amomum tsaoko in key odorants, in vitro antidiabetic, anticancer, and antioxidant activities
abstract: Amomum tsaoko (AT) is mainly dried through natural drying (ND), open fire drying (OFD), air-source drying (ASD), or hot-air drying (HAD). To investigate the effects of drying methods on AT odorants and bioactivity, sensory science and network pharmacology methods were employed. Results indicated that the numbers of alcohols in HAD AT and alkenes in ND AT were the highest; the odorant concentration in ASD AT was the highest, whereas that in OFD AT was the lowest. (Z)-2-Decenol, germacrene D, 4-terpineol and neral were identified as differential markers. The bioactivity research outcomes on AT essential oil (ATEO) indicated that both HAD and ASD ATEO exhibited greater α-amylase and α-glucosidase activity inhibitory capabilities; ASD ATEO showed the highest inhibition rate (>97%) to A549 cancer cell and the strongest total reducing power; HAD ATEO had the highest inhibition rate (>85%) against SW872 cancer cells; ND ATEO exhibited the highest radical-scavenging efficiencies.

title: The removal of gossypol from cottonseed oil by Chlorella pyrenoidosa modified with cetyltrimethylammonium bromide
abstract: We developed a novel composite adsorbent (CTAB-ACP), fabricated from cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) and Chlorella pyrenoidosa (CP) biomass, and applied it to gossypol removal from cottonseed oil. The synthesized adsorbent was characterized for its structural properties and adsorption capacity to elucidate the underlying behavior and mechanism. Under the determined optimum conditions (16 wt% adsorbent based on oil, 35 °C, 8 h), CTAB-ACP achieved a 90.80% gossypol removal efficiency and an adsorption capacity of 67.55 mg/g (calculated by mass balance), superior to the removal efficiency of raw CP. The detoxification process was found to minimally impact cottonseed oil quality while maintaining low cytotoxicity in the treated oil. The adsorption process was a spontaneous endothermic process involving physical and chemical interactions. The adsorbent maintained a removal efficiency of over 50% after four cycles, with good repeatability. These results suggest that CTAB-ACP is a promising material for gossypol removal from vegetable oils.

title: Effects of oil body addition on the structure and oxidative stability of soybean oil-beeswax-based margarine
abstract: Incorporating oil bodies (OBs) into soybean oil and beeswax-based margarine (MG) modulates the fat crystal network structure, thereby enhancing product performance while preserving natural nutrients. The effect of adding OB to margarine on the structure and properties of soybean oil beeswax based margarine was investigated. The results showed that although the addition of OBs did not alter the crystal polymorphs (remaining as β and β' forms), it optimized the crystal network morphology, resulting in a denser needle-like structure and a stable emulsion system. This directly improved the crystallization temperature, viscoelasticity, structural strength, and hardness of the system, while significantly enhancing oxidative stability and slightly lightening the color. This study suggests that OBs can serve as a functional ingredient to regulate the crystal network structure of soybean oil-beeswax-based margarine, thereby providing a theoretical basis for their application in solid fat products.

title: Mussel-inspired chitosan/alginate bilayer films with superior UV barrier and antibacterial activity for food preservation
abstract: Food spoilage during post-harvest storage underscores the critical need for sustainable active packaging, yet single-layer polysaccharide films suffer from limited functionality and conventional bilayer strategies lack molecular-level integration. Herein, we proposed a mussel-inspired bilayer composite system fabricated by layer-by-layer casting, which addresses these limitations through synergistic interfacial design. This design integrated the molecular-level functionalization of chitosan (CS) layer with polyphenols to impart enhanced adhesion and biological activity, combined with nano-reinforcement of alginate (ALG) layer using a metal-phenolic network (MPN) functionalized layered clay to achieve superior barrier function. The resultant bilayer composite system demonstrated outstanding antibacterial activities against E. coli (up to 98.8%) and S. aureus (up to 98.0%), excellent UV barrier capacity in the UVB (up to 99.99%) and UVA (up to 99.91%) regions, alongside improved hydrophobicity, antioxidant activity, and acceptable opacity. In addition, the tensile strength reached as high as 14.40 MPa, representing an improvement of 221.43% compared with pure ALG film. In the strawberry preservation experiment, the bilayer composite system effectively extended the shelf life of strawberries to seven days, owing to the structural complementarity and the high bioactivity of polyphenols. These results reveal that utilizing natural polysaccharides, polyphenols, and layered clay to construct a mussel-inspired bilayer composite system is a feasible strategy, providing a sustainable and promising approach for designing multifunctional packaging materials to mitigate food waste.

title: Effect of five selected flavonoids on the stability of anthocyanins: Kinetics, structural characterization, and interactional characteristics
abstract: To address the issue of poor stability of anthocyanins, this study conducted a comparative investigation into the intermolecular copigmentation characteristics between five different flavonoids (catechin, luteolin, quercetin, eriodictyol, and taxifolin) and cyanidin-3-o-glucoside (C3G). The experimental results revealed that the redshift occurred in the maximum absorption wavelength upon the formation of the copigmentation. The copigmentation system with the addition of quercetin exhibited a high absorbance (1.14 ± 0.02) (p ⁎ = 39.75). Further analysis demonstrated that the copigmentation reactions were all non-spontaneous endothermic reactions. The analysis of thermodynamic parameters indicated that structural differences among the flavonoids could influence the effectiveness of the copigmenting agents. Additionally, the incorporation of flavonoids enhanced the antioxidant capacity of C3G. Molecular interaction mechanism analysis indicates that hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking play key roles in the interaction between C3G and flavonoids, serving as the core driving forces of the copigmentation effect.

title: One-step method for modification of soy protein isolate and preparation of stable protein emulsions by industrial-scale high-energy fluidic microfluidizer
abstract: Current research methods remain confined to a model of modifying the protein first and then preparing the emulsion, requiring multiple steps and cycles. To address this challenge, a one-step strategy was developed using a high-energy fluidic microfluidizer (HEFM) to simultaneously solubilize the soy protein isolate and fabricate stable emulsions. The HEFM increased the solubility of the soy protein isolate from 30.9% to 92.3%, while reducing the particle diameter from 53.0 μm (D [4,3] ) to 0.4 μm. Structural analysis revealed that HEFM promoted a conversion of β-sheet to α-helix and exposed the hydrophobic residues. These changes facilitated rapid adsorption of the soy protein isolate to the oil-water interfaces, resulting in the formation of substantial and resilient interfacial films. The HEFM co-processing of protein-oil-water mixtures yielded emulsions exhibiting exceptional storage stability with no phase separation after 40 days. This research may establish a transformative technology for concurrent protein modification and emulsion fabrication.

title: Bovine milk fat globules containing probiotics enhance colonisation resistance, pathogen exclusion and macrophage modulation in simulated gut environments
abstract: Probiotics are widely used to manage gastrointestinal disorders; however, their therapeutic effects have been limited by rapid transit and degradation in the gut. Milk fat globules (MFGs) have recently gained attention as a bio-carrier that can shield probiotics and enhance their functionality under gastrointestinal stress. The present study hypothesises that MFGs enhance the survival and functionality of probiotics (e.g., L. fermentum, L. mesenteroides) by supporting colonisation resistance and modulating host immune responses. MFGs+L. fermentum exhibited significantly higher exclusion of enteric pathogens (e.g., E. coli, S. enterica, S. flexineri, K. pneumoniae, and P. aeruginosa) and synergistically attenuated oxidative stress. Mass spectrometric analysis revealed adaptive shifts in pathways of amino-acid biosynthesis, peptidoglycan assembly, transporters, and metabolism. Flow cytometry-based marker analysis showed that MFG-containing L. fermentum downregulated inflammatory markers (CD11b, CD14) in macrophages, promoting a more balanced immune state. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that MFGs enhance probiotic resilience, gut microbiome, and immune modulation.

title: Amaranth Fortification in Pasta: A Systematic Review of Nutritional Enhancement, Processing Parameters, and Sensory Attributes Across Wheat, Semolina, and Gluten-Free Formulations
abstract: Despite the growing demand, conventional pasta products remain nutritionally deficient, relying predominantly on refined starches with inadequate protein quality, limited bioavailable minerals, and reduced dietary fiber content. Amaranth, an ancient pseudocereal with superior nutritional characteristics, represents a promising biofortification ingredient; however, a systematic understanding of its technological integration and commercial viability remains fragmented. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence from 38 peer-reviewed studies (2001-2024) to establish evidence-based strategies for incorporating amaranth into wheat-based, semolina, and gluten-free pasta formulations. The results demonstrated that amaranth incorporation at optimal levels (10-25%) significantly enhanced the nutritional profiles through protein content improvement with superior lysine bioavailability, substantial mineral fortification, dietary fiber enrichment, and antioxidant enhancement. However, amaranth incorporation presents critical technological challenges, including compromised pasta texture (reduced firmness), elevated cooking loss, and unfavorable sensory characteristics, requiring strategic processing optimization. This review identifies evidence-based interventions, including controlled hydration protocols, strategic hydrocolloid incorporation, precise extrusion parameters, pre-gelatinization treatments, composite flour blending strategies (combinations with buckwheat, cassava, and legumes), and optimized high-temperature drying. Beyond nutritional and technological considerations, amaranth cultivation provides sustainability advantages, including drought tolerance, adaptation to poor soil conditions, efficient water utilization, and soil carbon sequestration potential. Critical research gaps have been identified in flavor masking technologies, color stabilization mechanisms, large-scale processing optimization, shelf-life stability, and cost-effectiveness analysis, representing priority areas for future investigation before widespread market implementation.

title: From protein structural reconfiguration to long-term emulsion stabilization: How ultrasound-microwave synergistic modulates no-added-salt myofibrillar protein-based emulsions through multiscale interfacial assembly
abstract: The application of native myofibrillar protein (MP)-stabilized emulsions is limited by salt dependence and poor stability. This study investigated the effects of ultrasound (U-MP), microwave (M-MP), and combined (UM-MP) treatments on MP under no-added-salt conditions. UM-MP significantly reduced particle size (to 537.76 nm), increased surface hydrophobicity (11.093 μg/mg), and shifted secondary structure from α-helix to β-sheet and random coil, resulting in high interfacial adsorption (92.37 ± 2.01%). The UM-MP emulsion showed excellent storage stability with no phase separation after 72 h. This stabilization was attributed to the synergistic effects of ultrasound-induced cavitation and microwave-induced unfolding, which generated restructured nanoscale MP aggregates capable of rapid interfacial coverage. A dual mechanism of mechanical barrier reinforcement and viscoelastic network formation effectively suppressed droplet coalescence. These findings provide an effective strategy for designing a no-added-salt and MP-stabilized emulsion suitable for functional food formulations.

title: Microwave-assisted guar gum conjugation improvement in stability of pea protein high internal phase Pickering emulsion and its application in zeaxanthin delivery
abstract: Glycation conjugate nanoparticles of pea protein isolate (PPI) and guar gum (GG) were prepared with microwave pre- and post-treatment for 4 and 6 min. Effect of microwave-assisted GG conjugation on stability and delivery function of high internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs) constructed by PPI nanoparticles were investigated. Microwave pre-treatment promoted covalent binding of GG to PPI with smaller particle size (99.02 nm) and higher interfacial stability. The secondary structure of conjugate nanoparticles was more flexible, and their tertiary conformation was looser. Microwave pre-treatment improved appearance, microstructure and rheological properties of conjugate HIPPEs, enhancing their physical, thermal, pH and ionic strength stability. Furthermore, encapsulation efficiency of conjugate HIPPEs with microwave pre-treatment for 4 min was 95.88%, and improved its controlled release effect, resulting in the highest bioaccessibility (62.79%). Therefore, microwave-assisted PPI-GG glycation modified physicochemical properties and structure of conjugate nanoparticles, which enhanced stability of HIPPEs and their delivery function for zeaxanthin.

title: Bimetallic Ce/Zr-MOF nanozyme for integrated colorimetric detection and degradation of tetracycline in foods
abstract: The development of simple and cost-effective technologies for the detection and degradation of tetracycline (TC) is essential to ensure food safety. In this study, a cerium/zirconium bimetallic metal-organic framework (Ce/Zr-MOF) was developed, which demonstrated enhanced peroxidase-like catalytic activity compared to monometallic Zr-MOF. The Ce/Zr-MOF effectively oxidized the colorless TMB to a light blue ox-TMB, and the presence of TC further amplified its activity, resulting in a deep blue ox-TMB. The absorbance of ox-TMB showed a linear relationship with TC concentrations in the range of 0-40 μM, with a detection limit of 0.368 μM, thereby establishing a rapid colorimetric method for TC detection in food samples. Additionally, TC adsorption on Ce/Zr-MOF surfaces facilitates electron transfer and generates a substantial amount of •OH radicals, promoting TC degradation. This study introduces an integrated Ce/Zr-MOF platform for TC detection and degradation, offering a comprehensive solution for monitoring and controlling TC residues in food.

title: Chemical modifications of polyphenols by plasma-treated water: oxidation, nitration, and adduct formation
abstract: Plasma-treated water (PTW) is increasingly explored in food processing, yet its oxidative and nitrosative impacts on the stability of phenolic compounds remain unclear. In this study, individual polyphenols (5 mM) and mixtures of polyphenols with amino acids were treated with PTW. PTW generated after 10 min plasma treatment caused up to 75% degradation of polyphenols, with stability decreasing in the order: p-coumaric acid > phloretic acid > protocatechuic acid > 4-hydroxybenzoic acid > chlorogenic acid. Multiple hydroxylated and nitrated derivatives were identified, including dihydrocaffeic acid and 3-(4-hydroxy-3-nitrophenyl)propanoic acid from phloretic acid, protocatechuic acid and 4-hydroxy-3-nitrobenzoic acid from 4-hydroxybenzoic acid, and 3-nitrocoumaric acid from p-coumaric acid, ranging from 40 μmol to 160 mmol per mol of precursor. Amino acids altered these pathways: cysteine yielded five distinct cysteine-polyphenol adducts, whereas lysine produced two. The results clarify how reactive plasma species modify phenolics and amino acids, underscoring the complexity of oxidation chemistry in PTW-treated systems.

title: Internal–external dual cross-linked alginate/gelatin composite hydrogel beads: Structure and pH-responsive gastrointestinal delivery of bioactives
abstract: This work presented a novel stimuli-responsive sodium alginate (SA)/gelatin (Gel) dual cross-linked composite hydrogel beads using Rana chensinensis ovum protein hydrolysate calcium chelates (RPH-Ca) as a unique internal cross-linker to synergize with external calcium. The optimal mass ratio of SA to RPH-Ca was determined at 1:0.5. FTIR and XRD analysis revealed that the beads were stabilized by hydrogen bonding and ligand coordination, forming an amorphous system. The beads exhibited significant pH-responsiveness, with minimal release in simulated gastric fluid ( 95%). High encapsulation efficiencies for curcumin (94.66% ± 0.05%) and rhodamine B (96.84% ± 0.03%) demonstrated capability for simultaneous delivery of lipophilic and hydrophilic bioactives. Release kinetics analysis showed that curcumin followed super Case-II transport, while rhodamine B exhibited composition-dependent release, near-zero-order release in SRGHB3 and non-Fickian transport in SRGHB4. By integrating dual cross-linking, this work demonstrated a promising strategy for constructing smart delivery vehicles for food bioactives.

title: Stage-dependent aroma evolution of Liupao tea during long-term storage revealed by molecular sensory science
abstract: Storage plays a critical yet insufficiently understood role in shaping the aroma quality of Liupao tea (LPT) during long-term aging. Here, a molecular sensory science strategy was used to investigate the evolution of odor-active compounds (OACs). Multivariate analysis revealed significant stage-dependent variation (PERMANOVA, R 2 = 0.516, p 2 = 0.996, RMSE = 0.22). With aging, aroma shifted from floral and fruity to stale and betelnut-like attributes, accompanied by decreased terpenoids and increased carbonyl and aromatic compounds. Representative OACs such as (E,E)-2,4-Heptadienal (OAV = 4333) and Linalool (OAV = 1740) contributed to these changes. Notably, aroma evolution was driven by reorganization of relative contributions among existing OACs rather than compositional turnover. Collectively, these findings provide a time-resolved perspective on LPT aging and a basis for quality evaluation of dark teas.

title: Screening of polyphenolic cathepsin B inhibitors and proteomic insights into muscle protection in grass carp during chilled storage
abstract: Endogenous cathepsin B is a key contributor to protein degradation and muscle softening in grass carp during chilled storage. In this study, proanthocyanidins (PC) were identified through targeted screening as an effective inhibitor of cathepsin B, with an IC 50 value of 84.10 μmol/L. PC treatment markedly suppressed endogenous proteolysis over a 16-day chilled storage period, as evidenced by reduced TCA-soluble peptide content and myofibrillar fragmentation, which was associated with the inhibition of cathepsins B and L. SDS-PAGE, texture, LF-NMR, OM, and TEM analyses further confirmed that PC preserved muscle integrity and delayed quality deterioration. Proteomic analysis identified 33 quality-related differentially abundant proteins mainly associated with tissue structure maintenance, protein phosphorylation, and protein turnover, with most of them being upregulated in fillets treated with 0.3% PC on day 12. Overall, PC mitigated endogenous enzyme-induced protein degradation and maintained muscle structural stability, providing mechanistic insight into polyphenol-mediated protection of fish muscle proteins.

title: Multiscale analysis of enzyme combinations and hydrolysis methods: Effects on bitterness, structure, functional properties, and peptide profile of soybean meal hydrolysates
abstract: To address bitterness in soybean meal hydrolysates, this study compared simultaneous and sequential hydrolysis using endopeptidases (Alcalase, Protamex, Papain, and Trypsin) with Flavourzyme, focusing on taste, structure, functional properties, and peptide profiles. Hydrolysis progressively degraded β-conglycinin and glycinin, enhanced peptides <5 kDa accumulation, and yielded DH values of 14.73 ± 0.63%-39.30 ± 1.69%. Bitterness initially increased and then decreased, with sequential hydrolysis producing lower bitterness. Structural changes included chromophore exposure, altered hydrogen bonding, increased β-turn content, reduced particle size, and decreased zeta potential, whereas enzyme specificity affected free sulfhydryl content, surface hydrophobicity, emulsifying properties, and antioxidant activity. Although nutritional improvements were limited, emulsifying and antioxidant activities were enhanced. Protamex-Flavourzyme provided the most favorable balance of debittering and functional improvement. Cleavage patterns and potential bitter peptide profiles indicated that Flavourzyme reduced N-terminal Val/Ile/Leu enrichment in Protamex-generated peptides, partly explaining its debittering effect and guiding functional soybean meal hydrolysate design.

title: Valorizing banana peel into carbon dots via pyrolysis: CCD optimization and machine learning prediction of fluorescent properties
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) derived from biomass waste represent a sustainable alternative to conventional fluorescent nanomaterials. In this study, highly fluorescent CDs were synthesized from banana peel by pyrolysis using an integrated approach combining Central Composite Design (CCD) and machine learning (ML). The workflow included precursor screening, CCD-based optimization, ML prediction of fluorescence intensity, and environmental stability evaluation. Among the tested precursors, urea was the most effective for enhancing fluorescence performance and quantum yield. CCD identified the key synthesis parameters affecting fluorescence, and the optimized conditions yielded a predicted fluorescence intensity of 16,696 a.u., with quantum yield approaching 40%. Among seven ML algorithms, Random Forest showed the best overall predictive performance, achieving the highest cross-validated R 2 of 0.97 with a low RMSE of 542.14. Feature importance analysis revealed that measured carbon content (C0) was the dominant predictor when elemental descriptors were included, while the precursor-to-banana-peel mass ratio (m_P2) was the most important controllable synthesis factor. Urea-derived BP-CDs retained approximately 97% fluorescence intensity at 1.0 M NaCl and maintained stable emission across pH 3–11. These findings demonstrate a data-guided strategy for producing high-performance, environmentally robust CDs from agricultural waste.

title: Co-fermentation of Ampelopsis grossedentata with Camellia sinensis reduces bitterness, enhances sweet aroma, and generates novel bioactive theaflavin analogues
abstract: This study developed a co-fermentation strategy to process the leaves of Ampelopsis grossedentata (vine tea) and Camellia sinensis (tea), which significantly improved the sensory quality of fermented vine tea by reducing its bitterness while enhancing sweet aroma. Untargeted metabolomics and GC-MS revealed significant metabolic changes, discovering two novel theaflavin analogues, dihydromyriflavin (1) and dihydromyriflavin-3'-gallate (2), (0.48 and 0.53 mg/g in co-fermented-vine-black tea (CVBT), respectively), formed via enzymatic oxidation. Compound 2 and the CVBT extract exhibited strong antioxidant (SC 50 = 42.91 μM and 227.05 μg/mL, respectively) and α-glucosidase inhibitory (IC 50 = 2.86 μM and 19.86 μg/mL, respectively) activities. Molecular docking confirms that 1 and 2 bind strongly (binding energies = -10.1 and - 10.9 kcal/mol) to α-glucosidase active sites. This work provides a foundation for developing high-value fermented tea products from underutilized resources and highlights the potential of co-fermentation to generate novel bioactive natural products.

title: A green and practical quadratic Box-Behnken design reverse micelle-assisted supramolecular solvent-based microextraction approach for the simultaneous determination of Cd and Pb in foodstuffs and cosmetics
abstract: The aim of this study is to provide a simple and environmentally friendly approach for the preconcentration and determination of Pb(II) and Cd(II) ions in complex matrices. A green and practical reverse micelle-assisted supramolecular solvent-based microextraction method was developed for the simultaneous determination of Cd(II) and Pb(II) in foodstuffs and cosmetics. Key experimental variables affecting extraction efficiency were optimized using Box-Behnken design. Under optimum conditions, the method showed good linearity in the ranges of 0.09-100 ng mL -1 for Cd(II) and 0.4-250 ng mL -1 for Pb(II). The limits of detection were 0.03 ng mL -1 for Cd(II) and 0.1 ng mL -1 for Pb(II), while the preconcentration factor was 100. Relative standard deviation values were below 2%. The method was successfully validated using certified reference materials and applied to real samples, demonstrating its reliability, applicability, and suitability for routine trace metal analysis.

title: High internal phase emulsions stabilised by amyloid fibrils from 7S/11S soybean protein at varying ratios: Study on interfacial behaviour, rheological properties and curcumin delivery potential
abstract: In response to the challenges associated with stabilising high-internal-phase emulsions (HIPE) using natural soy protein-namely, its weak surface activity and susceptibility to structural instability-as well as the poor water solubility and insufficient bioavailability of curcumin, this study utilised soy protein amyloid fibrils with varying 7S/11S ratios as emulsifiers to construct curcumin-loaded HIPE, elucidating the intrinsic relationship between fibril structural characterisation, HIPE interfacial and rheological properties, and curcumin delivery performance. The results indicate that fibrillation treatment significantly increased the β-sheet content and turbidity of the samples, with the 7S/11S = 2:1 group exhibiting the optimal comprehensive performance. Fibrils from this group form a more stable oil-water interfacial film; their HIPE exhibits the best resistance to deformation and structural stability, significantly improving curcumin encapsulation efficiency, thermal stability, antioxidant activity, and bioavailability. This study provides theoretical and technical support for the development of food-grade HIPE stabilisers and active substance delivery systems.

title: Multimodal calcium coordination and transport mechanisms of cod bone-derived novel peptides DYGGEY and GESGEAGDR
abstract: This study characterized two novel cod bone-derived peptides, DYGGEY and GESGEAGDR, revealing distinct Ca-binding architectures and transport routes. DYGGEY displayed a higher Ca-binding capacity (68.42 ± 3.15 mg/g) than GESGEAGDR (54.73 ± 2.96 mg/g), accompanied by secondary structural rearrangements after Ca chelation. Spectroscopy and NMR demonstrated that DYGGEY formed compact 1:1, 1:2, and 2:2 peptide-Ca complexes mainly via Asp/Glu/Tyr carboxyl coordination, whereas GESGEAGDR adopted more flexible 1:1 and 1:2 complexes involving Glu/Asp and protonated Arg. These structural differences led to divergent transport behaviors. DYGGEY (1.0 mg/mL) increased Ca transport from 26.95 ± 1.20 to 37.05 ± 5.63 μg/well and bioavailability from 33.45 ± 3.38% to 49.17 ± 6.43%, primarily through TRPV6 and L-type channel activation. In contrast, GESGEAGDR elicited modest transport enhancement but markedly promoted intracellular Ca retention via clathrin-dependent endocytosis. Proteomic analysis further revealed that DYGGEY and GESGEAGDR differentially modulated cellular Ca homeostasis.

title: Design of magnetic coral-like mesoporous carbon materials for highly effective solid-phase extraction of bisphenols in food samples
abstract: Efficient enrichment of trace bisphenols (BPs) is critical for food safety. Herein, a magnetic porous carbon (MPC) material (MPC-600) was prepared via controlled pyrolysis for extracting BPs from food. The three-dimensional coral-like framework and open surface mesopores in this material contributed to substantially reduced mass transfer resistance and abundant active sites. The adsorption of BPs by MPC-600 achieved rapid adsorption equilibrium within only 2 min along with high adsorption capacities (286.9-693.1 mg·g -1 ), attributed to π-π stacking, cation-π interactions, hydrophobic interaction, and the mesopore-filling effect. A method of magnetic solid-phase extraction coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography was established using MPC-600 as the adsorbent for the simultaneous detection of BPs. The method exhibited a wide linear range (0.06-200 ng·mL -1 ), high enrichment factors (383-425), and low limits of detection (0.02-0.03 ng·mL -1 ). Recoveries from food samples were in the range of 81.2%-114.9%, and the adsorbent was reusable for 20 cycles, demonstrating its high potential for practical usage.

title: Caffeic acid-grafted high-amylose maize starch for self-stabilizing emulsion gels: efficient encapsulation and protection of pterostilbene
abstract: Caffeic acid-grafted high-amylose maize starch (Cf-HAMS) with grafting degrees of 4%, 8%, and 12% was synthesized via esterification to address the limitations of native HAMS in emulsion-gel stabilization. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed covalent grafting at the C-6 hydroxyl groups. Due to the introduction of caffeic acid's phenolic hydroxyls and aromatic rings, Cf-HAMS exhibited markedly enhanced hydrophobicity (contact angle from 26.8° to 65.1°) together with strong antioxidant and antibacterial activities. Consequently, Cf-HAMS alone, without any added surfactants, stabilized emulsion gels with smaller droplets, reinforced interfacial films, and enhanced viscoelasticity. When applied as carriers for pterostilbene, Cf-HAMS achieved approximately 90% encapsulation efficiency, improved UV and thermal protection, suppressed lipid oxidation, and increased bioaccessibility by a factor of 2.5 compared with native HAMS. Overall, these findings demonstrate that phenolic-acid grafting effectively integrates interfacial stabilization with chemical protection for hydrophobic bioactives.

title: Intermolecular interaction of coreopsin with β-lactoglobulin at varied pH values: Experiment, dynamics simulation and IGM analysis
abstract: In this investigation, underlying intermolecular interaction of coreopsin and β-Lactoglobulin (β-Lg) under various pH values were explored using multiexperiments, dynamics simulation and independent gradient model (IGM). Fluorescence analysis indicated that coreopsin interacted with β-Lg mainly through hydrogen bonds and van der Waals forces, which were validated by IGM, and molecular mechanics poisson boltzmann surface area (mm-PBSA) results. Based on multispectral and zeta potential-particle size analyses, the binding of coreopsin to β-Lg induced significant alterations in the conformation, crystallinity, charge distribution and particle size. Molecular simulations revealed obvious differences in the binding sites of coreopsin toward monomer, dimer and tetramer, thereby resulting in diverse dynamics behaviors. The mm-PBSA analysis indicated that residues PRO38, GLN59 and LYS138 contributed greatly to electrostatic energy during the binding of coreopsin with monomer, dimer, and tetramer, respectively. Several amino acid residues maintained the stability of complexes by providing van der Waals energy.

title: Spatial metabolomic profiling of ripening pepper fruit (Capsicum annuum L.) by MALDI-MSI: Decoding metabolic heterogeneity and its role in quality attribute regulation
abstract: To decipher the metabolic regulation of pepper fruit (Capsicum annuum L.) quality, tissue-scale matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) was employed to systematically map 19 key metabolites across four developmental stages at a spatial resolution of 50 μm. Imaging revealed distinct spatiotemporal dynamics: capsaicinoids exhibited a localized "bimodal accumulation" in the placenta, while capsanthin precursors shifted from a uniform distribution to specific enrichment in the pericarp. Notably, a synthesis-distribution decoupling was observed in ascorbic acid metabolism, suggesting potential inter-tissue redistribution. Integration with high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) for the absolute quantification of four core metabolites (n = 3) provided complementary insights, distinguishing continuous bulk accumulation from dynamic, non-linear local metabolic activity. This study constructs a tissue-scale spatial metabolomic atlas, highlighting the synergistic value of combining spatial imaging with bulk quantification to unravel metabolic heterogeneity in food matrices.

title: Green-synthesized ε-polylysine/zein nanocomplexes as safe antimicrobials: Applications and metabolomic mechanisms in grape preservation
abstract: Microbial contamination is a major contributor to postharvest fruit losses, highlighting the need for effective and safe antimicrobial strategies. Herein, ε-polylysine (ε-PL)/zein nanocomplexes were fabricated via synergistic complexation using a flow-based flash nanoprecipitation (FNP) technique. The nanocomplexes showed negligible cytotoxicity and minimal surface residues after conventional washing. Additionally, the nanocomplexes exhibited uniform morphology, good storage stability over 14 days, and sustained release properties. More importantly, ε-PL/zein nanocomplexes demonstrated antimicrobial activity against both bacteria and fungi by disrupting cell integrity. As a proof-of-concept, grape preservation experiments showed that ε-PL/zein nanocomplexes significantly reduced decay rate (5.7%) compared with commercial ε-PL (10.5%) and the control (17.3%), while maintaining firmness and total soluble solids during storage (p < 0.05). Metabolomic analysis suggested nanocomplex treatment may be associated with changes in metabolic pathways related to stress resistance and quality maintenance. This work presents an innovative strategy for developing promising green antimicrobials for postharvest food preservation.

title: Fluorescence spectroscopy, 3D-QSAR, and molecular dynamics analyses reveal the interaction mechanisms of flavonoids with lysozyme
abstract: This research elucidates the mechanisms of non-covalent interactions between flavonoids and lysozyme. Binding constants were determined via fluorescence spectroscopy, and a Topomer CoMFA 3D-QSAR model was developed, effectively explaining the binding behavior. Detailed studies on rutin, naringenin, and hesperetin showed binding occurred via a static quenching mechanism with a 1:1 stoichiometry, and hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces were indicated as the primary drivers. Synchronous fluorescence revealed flavonoid binding disrupted the tryptophan microenvironment but left tyrosine relatively stable. IGM analysis of rutin glycosylation revealed a rigid intramolecular hydrogen-bond network, whereas the aglycones were less stable. Intermolecularly, rutin formed multiple hydrogen bonds and extensive hydrophobic interactions, while aglycone binding was simpler. MD simulations and free energy calculations yielded the following binding affinity: hesperetin > naringenin > rutin, underscoring the importance of solvation effects. This work provides molecular-level insights into the structure-activity relationship, aiding the design of flavonoid delivery systems.
