Drying was conducted until the samples reached the target moisture content, and drying characteristics, energy consumption, color parameters, and pesticide residues were determined. Among the tested methods, oven drying at 80 °C resulted in the shortest drying time and the highest energy efficiency. Greenhouse drying generally preserved product color more effectively than the other methods. Drying kinetics were best described by the Page model (R 2 = 0.9997). Both pesticides showed significant reductions during the drying process, with pyridaben exhibiting greater reduction than acetamiprid. Increasing drying temperature enhanced pesticide reduction across all drying methods. The highest residue reductions were obtained under oven and vacuum oven drying at 80 °C. While vacuum drying at 80 °C produced the greatest net residue reduction, oven drying at the same temperature provided a more favorable balance between drying time and energy efficiency. These findings demonstrate that drying, particularly at elevated temperatures, can serve as an effective postharvest strategy for reducing pesticide residues in peppers while maintaining acceptable product quality and process efficiency.

title: Molecular mechanism of hidden matrix-bound deoxynivalenol binding to proteins in wheat
abstract: Protein-bound hidden deoxynivalenol (DON) poses significant health risks during mycotoxin degradation in wheat matrices. This study combined spectroscopic analyses and molecular docking to elucidate DON-gliadin interaction mechanisms. DON induced static fluorescence quenching of gliadin (quenching constant: 0.98 × 10 3 L·mol -1 ) and formed a stable 1:1 complex through hydrogen bonding, van der Waals, and hydrophobic interactions (ΔG = -14.07 kJ·mol -1 ; binding constant = 0.289 × 10 3 L·mol -1 ). The interaction altered gliadin secondary structure, reducing α-helices (4.29%) and β-sheets (2.86%) while increasing β-turns (3.75%) and random coils (3.35%), and decreased surface hydrophobicity. These structural changes were confirmed by FTIR, synchronous fluorescence, and CD spectroscopy. Molecular docking further showed DON binds to residues in the gliadin domain, with Gln223 and Phe238 playing key roles (binding energy: -5.851 kcal/mol; binding distances: 1.81 Å and 5.41 Å). These findings support the development of targeted detoxification strategies for hidden DON, contributing to improved wheat safety and protection of human health.

title: Seasonal variation in the biochemical composition of fish discards and its impact on the production of mince, protein hydrolysates, and oil
abstract: Fish discards and fish processing by-products represent valuable but variable resources. This study investigates the seasonal effects on the composition of representative discarded species, blue whiting, mackerel, and Atlantic horse mackerel, alongside their impact on the production and characterization of their protein hydrolysates and oils. Proximate analysis of specimens fractionated into mince, heads, viscera, skin and bones reveals significant seasonal differences in lipid and protein content, autumn samples generally exhibiting higher lipid levels. Mince consistently proves a high-protein, low-lipid fraction suitable for human consumption, while viscera from all species generally exceed heavy metal thresholds. Enzymatic hydrolysis of each fraction effectively yields protein hydrolysates, often increasing the essential amino acid proportion. The recovered oils demonstrate healthy characteristics, notably high omega-3 fatty acid content, which vary seasonally. These findings underscore the importance of seasonal assessment for optimizing the integral valorization of diverse fish discards into high-value compounds.

title: Combined computational and spectroscopic analyses of the interactions between ginger compounds and bovine type I collagen
abstract: The stability of collagen is critical for meat quality; however, how ginger compounds act as collagen stabilizers is poorly understood. Molecular docking identified 24 compounds with binding affinities below -5.0 kcal/mol, involving Pro168, Tyr161, and Arg179 as key residues. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that collagen complexes with 3 major ginger compounds exhibited lower root mean square deviations than collagen, maintained by hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Given that 6-shogaol is a dehydration product of 6-gingerol (6-GOL), 6-GOL and gingerenone A (GGA) were selected for experimental validation. Ultraviolet-visible absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy showed 6-GOL and GGA interacted with collagen. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that both compounds altered the Amide bands, confirming strengthened hydrogen bonding. Furthermore, differential scanning calorimetry analysis demonstrated that both compounds enhanced the thermal stability of collagen. These findings demonstrate that 6-GOL and GGA stabilize bovine type I collagen, providing insights into their potential as collagen stabilizers.

title: WPI-SA-STE stabilized high-internal-phase emulsion filled κ-carrageenan/konjac glucomannan hydrogels: Structural properties and curcumin delivery
abstract: Existing studies predominantly use single proteins or polysaccharides to stabilize high-internal-phase emulsions (HIPEs), while κ-carrageenan/konjac glucomannan (κ-KC/KGM) hydrogels often suffer from poor mechanical properties. This study addresses both limitations by fabricating HIPEs stabilized by a ternary complex of whey protein isolate‑sodium alginate-steviol glycosides and incorporating them into hydrogels. Hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions between HIPEs and κ-KC/KGM promoted a more uniform and dense gel network. After filling with HIPEs, the hardness, elasticity, and chewiness of the gel decreased, while the water holding capacity increased significantly. After UV irradiation, the curcumin (Cur) retention rate in the filling gel reached 94.63%, significantly higher than that in the HIPEs system. In vitro digestion experiments have shown that an appropriate amount of HIPEs (20%) filling can effectively improve the bioaccessibility of Cur. The resulting HIPEs filled gels exhibited excellent 3D printability. This study supporting the developing functional fat replacers and lipophilic bioactive delivery systems.

title: Monitoring of non-systemic and systemic pesticides and date (Phoenix dactylifera L.) fruit metabolites using DESI–TOF MS
abstract: A desorption electrospray ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry (DESI-TOF MS) method was developed for monitoring eight non-systemic and systemic pesticides from five major chemical classes of organophosphates, along with their metabolites and major putative endogenous metabolites-including sugars, lipids, and polyphenols-in both the peel and flesh of Mazafati dates. The limits of detection were 0.10 for diazinon, 0.33 for chlorpyrifos, and 1.00 μg kg -1 for the other pesticides. LC-MS/MS combined with QuEChERS extraction was used for comparison with DESI-TOF MS and reduced solvent consumption and a significant decrease in total analysis time-from 90 min to 3 s-along with simultaneous determination of putative metabolites of pesticides and dates are key advantages of the proposed method. Also, the reduction of non-systemic pesticide residues by water washing was investigated. Water washing led to a residue reduction in the date peel in the following order: chlorpyrifos > diazinon > fenitrothion.

title: Effects of rapeseed (Brassica napus L.) ripening and post-harvest ripening duration on physicochemical properties and lipid concomitants of rapeseed oils
abstract: Rapeseed oil is a nutritious vegetable oil, obtained from Brassica napus L. plants. To explore the changes of physicochemical properties and lipid content of rapeseed in the process of growth and post-harvest ripening (PHR), this study evaluated the impact of ripening (1-18d) and PHR (1-5d) on cold-pressed oil. Results demonstrated that optimal maturity (R6) produced the most favorable fatty acid profile, achieving 92.54% unsaturated fatty acids. Extending PHR to 5d significantly enhanced the retention of key bioactive compounds: tocopherols reached 385.47 mg/kg, phytosterols accumulated to 1838.97 mg/kg, and phenolic content peaked at 599.95 mg/kg. Comprehensive lipidomics analysis revealed two processes during PHR: an initial hydrolysis phase marked by elevated free fatty acids and lysophospholipids, followed by a stabilization phase characterized by triacylglycerol re-synthesis and concomitant phospholipid degradation. These findings evidence that coordinated harvest timing and PHR duration improve the oxidative stability, functional composition, and nutritional quality of rapeseed oil.

title: A konjac glucomannan composite film embedding proanthocyanidin-grafted chitosan and carvacrol@ZIF-8 nanoparticles for synergistic antioxidant/antibacterial packaging
abstract: Few bio-based active packaging films simultaneously achieve sustained antioxidant and antibacterial functions, making a dual sustained-release system highly desirable. To extend postharvest fruit shelf life, this study developed an active packaging film based on konjac glucomannan (KGM). A dual-release antioxidant and antibacterial system was constructed by introducing proanthocyanidin-grafted chitosan (PACS) and carvacrol-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles (CV@ZIF-8). The resulting KPCZ-3 film exhibited a tensile strength of 34.36 MPa, a water vapor permeability of 2.72 g·mm·m -2 ·day -1 ·kPa, and an oxygen permeability of 1.27 × 10 -3 g·s -1 ·m -2 . In strawberry preservation tests at 25 °C, the film synergistically delayed quality deterioration and maintained optimal sensory and nutritional quality for over 4 days. In addition, the film showed good biodegradability and biocompatibility. These results indicate that KGM/PACS/CV@ZIF-8 films, as novel degradable active packaging, have promising application prospects.

title: Insights into the underlying mechanisms of foam instability in whipped cheese-enriched reduced-fat cream prepared from ultra-high temperature-treated emulsion
abstract: Ultra-high temperature (UHT) processing ensures dairy cream shelf-stability, yet its detrimental effects on foaming are often overlooked. This study characterized the interfacial evolution during the three foam formation stages (initial aeration, partial fat coalescence, and stabilization) of UHT-processed whipped cheese-enriched reduced-fat cream (WCRC), compared to the pasteurized (PU) control. UHT reduced the overrun (63.4% vs. 96.8% for PU) and fresh foam quality (hardness: 129.3 vs. 145.6 g; bubble diameter: 180 vs. 100 μm). This instability resulted from a sequential cascade effect. Initially, UHT-induced high viscosity and altered serum proteins impaired aeration and air-serum adsorption. This fragile state, combined with a thickened oil-water interfacial film, subsequently inhibited shear-induced partial fat coalescence. Ultimately, the lack of a robust fat network, alongside disrupted intermolecular interactions, weakened the final fat globule-serum film stability. Therefore, modulating serum properties, fat coalescence, and molecular interactions offers a pathway to enhance UHT-WCRC foam stability, providing new formulation insights.

title: Effects of complexation temperature on the helical structure and properties of amylose–α-linolenic acid complexes
abstract: Amylose is a promising drug delivery vehicle that can achieve the protection and controlled release of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) which play crucial roles in preventing type 2 diabetes, thereby improving their stability and bioavailability. Among PUFAs, α-linolenic acid (ALA) stands out because of its abundance in plant seed oils and its ability to serve as a biosynthetic precursor for other PUFAs. This study examined the effect of complexation temperature on the multiscale structure of amylose‒α-linolenic acid complexes. Amylose, obtained by debranching waxy maize starch, was complexed with ALA at temperatures of 30/50/70/90 °C. The solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance results indicated an increase in the single-helix content and a decrease in the double-helix content as the temperature decreased. The highest complexation rate (over 56%), smallest particle size (0.57 μm), optimal emulsion stability, and highest melting temperature (83.1 °C) were achieved with a complexation temperature of 30 °C. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that single helices formed at 30 °C and 90 °C, and elevated temperatures intensified both the amylose‒amylose interaction and the amylose‒ALA interaction. These findings confirm the hypothesis that the complexation temperature is crucial in controlling the single/double helical structures and complexation rates of amylose‒ALA complexes.

title: Fatty acid–incorporated resistant starch nanoparticles for enhanced rheology and syneresis control in set-style yogurt
abstract: This study introduces fatty acid-incorporated starch nanoparticles (FANP), fabricated via amylosucrase-mediated self-assembly, as a clean-label stabilizers for set-style yogurt. The incorporation of FANP significantly enhanced the yogurt's rheological properties, evidenced by a higher storage modulus, increased viscosity, and greater thixotropic recovery, indicating a more resilient and shear-recoverable get network. In particular, FANP reduced syneresis by approximately 40% over 28 days of refrigerated storage, demonstrating superior water retention and stability. These improvements were achieved without increasing gel firmness, a common drawback of traditional stabilizers. This suggests that FANP reinforces the matrix through enhanced particle-protein interactions and water immobilization, rather than by hardening the casein network, thereby preserving the yogurt's desirable soft texture while maintaining its characteristic shear-thinning behavior. Overall, FANP acts as a multifunctional ingredient that improves the quality of set-style yogurt while delivering the added nutritional benefits of resistant starch, positioning it as a promising stabilizer for functional dairy products.

title: Multifunctional gelatin-based sustainable films with humidity-responsive optical properties for visual monitoring and preservation of fresh products
abstract: Environmental humidity critically impacts the quality and shelf life of high-moisture foods, but conventional packaging lacks real-time monitoring. This study developed a multifunctional gelatin (GE)-based film with an amphiphilic hyperbranched polyetheramine (HBPA) for visual humidity monitoring and food preservation. The HBPA-GE film exhibited a reversible transparency transition in response to humidity variations, enabling direct and continuous visual indication without instrumentation. The HBPA-GE-40 film (containing 40 wt% HBPA relative to gelatin) showed high tensile strength (82.1 ± 3.6 MPa), excellent UV-blocking efficiency (94.5 ± 0.6%), and potential antioxidant (67.5 ± 1.4% DPPH scavenging) and antibacterial activity against E. coli (85.4 ± 5.6%) and S. aureus (91.3 ± 3.1%). It also demonstrated improved water vapor barrier properties, recyclability, and rapid biodegradability. Storage tests on Agaricus bisporus confirmed the film's effectiveness in reducing weight loss and browning, extending shelf life, and providing visible humidity feedback, offering a sustainable strategy for intelligent food packaging that integrates preservation, protection, and real-time visual monitoring of humidity-sensitive foods.

title: Active antioxidant packaging films from polyvinyl alcohol-corn starch and chilgoza pine nut shell extract: Characterization, release kinetics, and multi-criteria performance assessment
abstract: Chilgoza pine nut shells (CPNS), an underexploited agro-industrial waste, were utilized as a novel antioxidant source for developing active packaging films using polyvinyl alcohol-corn starch (PC). The addition of CPNS extract (CPNSE) reduced film's transparency, solubility (29.53%), and water vapor permeability (23.54%); improved tensile strength, antioxidant capability (83.62% DPPH scavenging activity and 24.95 mg TE/g FRAP activity) and UV-blocking ability compared to PC film. The FTIR revealed hydrogen bonding between matrix and CPNSE, while, XRD analysis showed increased crystallinity with no notable effect on thermal stability of films with addition of CPNSE. The polyphenols release fitted well to Korsmeyer-Peppas's model (R 2 > 0.95), indicating Fickian diffusion. Furthermore, pine nuts packed in PC-CPNSE films exhibited lower peroxide (40-70% reduction) and TBARS (15-70% reduction) value compared to PC film; highlighting their potential for extending the shelf-life of lipid-rich foods. The multi-criteria performance analysis revealed film with 10% CPNSE as the most suitable.

title: Tapioca starch-yeast protein 3D printing system for dysphagia: Different hydrocolloids regulate viscoelasticity and 3D printing accuracy through molecular interactions
abstract: To develop easy-to-swallow foods for dysphagic individuals, this study prepared yeast protein (YP) and tapioca starch (TS) composite gel, and explored the effects of four hydrocolloids (HCs): flaxseed gum (FG), locust bean gum (LBG), xanthan gum (XG), and sodium alginate (SA) on their viscoelasticity, swallowing and 3D printing performances. All gels satisfied International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative (IDDSI) Level 6 criteria. HCs raised 3D printing accuracy from 80.53% to 95.85%, correlating with increased viscoelasticity in the order: FG > XG > LBG > SA. Molecular analysis showed this stemmed from HCs' ability to increase hydrogen bond density in YP-TS gel. FG exhibited the highest hydrogen bond density due to abundant -OH and -COOH groups; XG had steric hindrance from side chains; LBG contained only -OH groups; SA had ionized -COO - groups. Thus, HC enhanced viscoelasticity and printability through hydrogen bonds in the order FG > XG > LBG > SA. This study offers a novel perspective for texture design of dysphagia foods.

title: Elucidating the chemical and perceptual basis of lychee-like aroma in grapes through multi-omics and molecular sensory analyses
abstract: Lychee-like aroma in grapes is a distinctive fruit trait with great market potential, yet its chemical composition and molecular basis remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics and sensory strategy, this study elucidated its chemical foundation, perceptual mechanism, and biosynthetic regulation. Metabolomic profiling identified cis-rose oxide and citronellol as key volatiles responsible for the lychee-like note. Electroencephalography (EEG) during grape consumption revealed neural activation associated with olfactory-gustatory integration, highlighting the role of cross-modal perception in flavor experience. Model solution assays and molecular docking suggested that these volatiles may enhance sweetness and sourness by modulating taste receptor-ligand interactions. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed sugar-acid-terpenoid metabolic networks and identified Vitvi037507 as a candidate gene for the biosynthesis of cis-rose oxide and citronellol. Overall, this work elucidates the chemical and perceptual mechanisms of lychee-like aroma in grapes, offering insights into flavor chemistry and a foundation for breeding and metabolic engineering.

title: Konjac glucomannan enhances the thermal and freeze-thaw stability of rennet-modified caseinate high internal phase emulsions via viscoelastic structuring and interfacial modulation
abstract: High internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) often exhibit limited resistance to thermal processing and freeze-thaw treatments, restricting their practical applications. This study demonstrated that konjac glucomannan (KGM) significantly enhanced the stability of rennet-modified sodium caseinate (RM-NaCas) HIPEs under heating (60-100 °C for 20 min) and repeated freeze-thaw cycles. Emulsions containing 0.8% KGM maintained structural integrity after heating at 100 °C and exhibited reduced crystallization temperature. KGM also increased the viscosity and viscoelasticity and promoted the formation of a denser droplet distribution and network structure. In addition, interfacial tension and contact angle measurements indicated improved interfacial properties, while FTIR analysis suggested the presence of intermolecular interactions between KGM and NaCas, such as hydrogen bonding. Overall, the enhanced stability is primarily attributed to viscoelastic structuring of the continuous phase and interfacial reinforcement. This study provides an effective and clean-label strategy for designing thermally and freeze-thaw stable HIPEs for food applications.

title: Comparative study of raw and solid-state fermented finger millet (Eleusine coracana L.) on the quality, microstructure and in vitro starch digestibility of wheat noodles
abstract: In this study, raw finger millet (FM) and solid-state fermented finger millet (FFM) were incorporated into composite noodles (FMN and FFMN respectively) by replacing wheat flour at 0%, 5%, 10%, and 15% substitution levels. The cooking quality, textural properties, tensile properties, sensory attributes and in vitro digestibility of noodles were evaluated. Results indicated that FM and FFM addition shortened the optimal cooking time of noodles, significantly enhanced free phenolic content (from 15.70 mg/g to 23.04 mg/g for FMN, and to 24.83 mg/g for FFMN), and reduced the extent of starch digestion (the estimated maximum starch hydrolysis extent decreased from 86.60% to 73.15% for FMN and 68.52% for FFMN). However, the hardness of FMN increased while that of FFMN decreased. Noticeably, FFMN exhibited superior performance to those with FMN, and FFMN with 10% substitution exhibited best sensory characteristics. This study offered a new strategy for the application of FFM in noodles.

title: Comparative effect of gum arabic and psyllium husk on alginate hydrogels for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum encapsulation
abstract: This study examined the effects of gum arabic (GA) and psyllium husk (PH) as functional co-polymers in alginate (ALG) encapsulation matrices for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, combined with inulin (IN), trehalose (TRE), or their mixture. Probiotic beads were produced by ionic cross-linking and evaluated during short-term refrigerated storage for morphology, metabolic activity, viability, membrane integrity, hydrophobicity, and intracellular trace-metal retention. PH-based hydrogels showed the highest viability, lowest membrane permeability, and improved retention of Mn, Fe, and Zn. These effects are consistent with the hydrated PH-rich network that may facilitate mass transfer and membrane stabilization under refrigerated storage. GA-based systems exhibited greater permeability and hydrophobicity but lower culturability, consistent with denser interfacial layers that may restrict diffusion. Microscopy supported visible morphological differences between hydrogel systems. A conceptual structure-function interpretation is proposed, and ALG-PH-IN and ALG-PH-IN/TRE emerged as the most effective formulations under the tested conditions.

title: Structure and antioxidant characteristics of diacylglycerol-based oleogels: A comparison with triacylglycerol systems
abstract: This study compared the effects of γ-oryzanol/β-sitosterol combined with monoglyceride (MAG) as composite gelators on soybean diacylglycerol (DAG) and triacylglycerol (TAG)-based oleogels. Results showed that TAG and DAG systems formed stable oleogels with high mechanical strength at γ-oryzanol/β-sitosterol concentrations of 4% and 8%, respectively. The subsequent addition of 1% MAG significantly reduced gel hardness (more pronounced in DAG), while the oil-binding capacity remained largely unaffected. Microstructural and FTIR analyses revealed that MAG transformed the crystal shape of DAG and TAG-based oleogels from a needle-like arrangement to clustered networks, and the intermolecular interactions were primarily driven by van der Waals forces. Accelerated oxidation demonstrated that while DAG exhibited higher oxidation rates than TAG in liquid and oleogels, the DAG composite gel displayed enhanced oxidative stability compared to γ-oryzanol/β-sitosterol only systems. These findings clarify the differences between DAG and TAG based oleogels, demonstrating the potential for MAG-phytosterol composite oleogels in functional foods.

title: In silico technologies for food-based gels: Molecular docking and molecular dynamic simulation
abstract: High biocompatibility and three-dimensional printability of gels make them highly promising for the food industries. Appropriateness of gels for the food industry depends heavily on their mechanical characteristics and molecular dynamics. For identifying dynamic molecular information at the atomic level, molecular docking (MD) and molecular dynamics simulation (MDS) are thought to be viable methods. They can be used as a tool in creating food gels because they may investigate chemical bonding, particular binding sites, changes in spatial structure, and binding energy between molecules, as well as assess the ideal conformation. MD techniques can reveal the biopolymer interactions. Promising methods include data-driven protein engineering, which designs proteins using computer techniques. The history and evolution of MD techniques are discussed in this article, with a focus on their uses in the food-based gel field. Lastly, research avenues for enhancing the quality attributes of food-based gels via MD and MDS are discussed.

title: Ultrasound processing induces mild protein oxidation and significant changes in physicochemical properties of milk proteins
abstract: Ultrasound (US) processing is a promising food technology to improve protein solubility, reduce particle size, and modify functional properties. However, concerns exist regarding US-induced protein oxidation due to reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation during treatment. This study evaluated the effects of US on physicochemical properties and oxidative modifications in raw milk (RM), skim milk powder (SMP), and milk protein concentrate (MPC). US treatment significantly reduced apparent viscosity and particle size, especially in MPC. Solubility decreased in RM but increased in MPC, with no major changes observed in SMP. LC-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis revealed low levels (μg/g range) of aromatic amino acid-derived oxidation products, including kynurenine, o-tyrosine, m-tyrosine, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine, and 5-hydroxytryptophan. UHPLC-based amino acid analysis showed minimal alterations in overall amino acid composition. These results indicate that while US processing substantially modifies the physicochemical properties of milk proteins, it induces only minor oxidative changes, with minor effects on amino acid stability.

title: Zr-functionalized hydrogen-bonded organic framework for magnetic solid-phase extraction and LC–MS/MS determination of fluoroquinolones in milk
abstract: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics (FQs) are frequently detected at trace levels in milk, complicating accurate quantification due to matrix interference and stringent regulatory limits. This study developed a zirconium-functionalized magnetic hydrogen-bonded organic framework (Zr@MHOF101) for selective magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) of six FQs prior to LC-MS/MS analysis. Three π-conjugated carboxylic acid-based HOFs were synthesized and compared. Magnetic functionalization enabled rapid phase separation and altered adsorption behavior, while Zr post-modification increased adsorption selectivity toward FQs in milk matrices. Optimized MSPE enabled rapid enrichment (2 min) using 3 mg adsorbent and 1 g milk, achieving LODs of 0.1-0.2 μg/kg, LOQs of 0.2-0.5 μg/kg, and recoveries of 77.17%-105.49%. Compared to MOF/COF sorbents, Zr@MHOF101 reduced resource use and improved FQs selectivity over other antibiotics, providing a practical tool for monitoring residues in complex food matrices.

title: Blending with quinoa flour enhances the quality of fish balls: A natural strategy for inhibiting freeze-thaw deterioration
abstract: This research assessed how the partial replacement of potato starch (PS) with quinoa flour (QF) affects the freeze-thaw stability of fish balls over five consecutive freeze-thaw cycles. At an optimal QF-to-PS substitution ratio of 1:3, the fish balls exhibited marked improvements in critical quality parameters-including whiteness, textural properties (TPA), thaw loss, water-holding capacity (WHC), and gel strength-over the control (0,1), even following repeated freeze-thaw cycles. The establishment of a gel network that is denser and more uniform in structure was facilitated by QF through enhanced water retention and the concurrent promotion of β-sheet structures. Moreover, QF effectively suppressed the growth and aggregation of ice crystals during freeze-thaw cycling, thereby mitigating microstructural damage and moisture migration, which improved freeze-thaw stability. Notably, sensory and cost analyses revealed that the 1:3 formulation achieved the highest overall consumer acceptability without imposing an economic burden.

title: Multi-platform metabolomics reveals lipid remodeling during fruit development and aroma emergence in ripening durian (Durio zibethinus L.)
abstract: Durian (Durio zibethinus L.) is prized for its distinctive aroma, yet lipid metabolism during ripening remains poorly understood. We profiled lipids in durian pulp across five stages of fruit development and ripening using untargeted LC-MS-based lipidomics and annotated 212 lipid species from 24 classes. Phosphatidylethanolamine increased during development, whereas triacylglycerol and digalactosyldiacylglycerol decreased from mature to ripe stages. Phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidic acid showed stagewise fluctuations, and sulfur-containing sulfoquinovosyldiacylglycerol was annotated in durian pulp. Complementary volatilomic profiling of ripe pulp using solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry/sulfur chemiluminescence detection annotated carbon disulfide among sulfur volatiles, with relative odor activity values indicating ethanethiol and hydrogen sulfide as major candidate odor-impact sulfur compounds. Phytosterols and β-amyrin were quantified using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. These data establish a multi-platform compositional reference showing ripening-associated lipid remodeling alongside sulfur- and ester-associated volatile signatures in durian pulp.

title: Chestnut porous starch loaded with curcumin: preparation, characterization and applications in 3D printing of chestnut flour
abstract: This study developed a sustainable delivery system by investigating curcumin (Cur) adsorption onto chestnut porous starch (CPS) through kinetic, isotherm, and thermodynamic analyses, subsequently evaluating the CPS/Cur complex as a functional ingredient in 3D-printed chestnut flour (CF) gels. Results indicated that CPS achieved an adsorption capacity of 6.82 mg/g at 25 °C within 300 min. The adsorption process conformed to the pseudo-first-order kinetic model and the Langmuir isotherm, revealing a spontaneous, exothermic monolayer adsorption primarily driven by physical entrapment and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Multispectral characterizations confirmed the successful formation of the CPS/Cur complex via this green strategy, evidenced by the masking of curcumin's characteristic peaks. Crucially, a 12.0% CF formulation optimized both extrudability and shape fidelity while strictly satisfying IDDSI Level 5 criteria for safe swallowing. Overall, this scalable approach demonstrates exceptional potential for the continuous, automated 3D printing of personalized, value-added functional foods tailored for dysphagia management.

title: Emulsion gels stabilized by freshwater fish-lotus seed dual-protein complexes: Rheological properties, microstructure, and stability
abstract: Dual-protein emulsions are gaining attention for their functional and nutritional complementarity. This study investigated how ratios (k = 6:1, 2:1, 1:1, 1:2, 1:6) of fish collagen peptides (FP; from grass carp or silver carp) to lotus seed protein (LSP) influenced physicochemical and emulsifying properties of FP-LSP complexes. Results revealed that formation involved electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonds, and hydrophobic interactions. As the k decreased to 1:6, the absolute ζ-potential values and surface hydrophobicity increased significantly. At Φ = 0.3, FP-LSP adsorbed at the droplet interface and formed a network structure, with droplet aggregation constructing a triple-network architecture that endowed the emulsion gels with excellent freeze-thaw stability. At Φ = 0.6, the FP-LSP-stabilized continuous phase enhanced gel viscoelasticity. LSP content and oil percentages significantly influenced the structural formation and stability. This study establishes theoretical framework of the formation of FP-LSP complexes, offering technical and theoretical insights for their applications in emulsion-based products.

title: A comparative study on cryoprotective and water-retaining effects of trehalose and sodium pyrophosphate on silver carp surimi during frozen storage
abstract: This study compared the cryoprotective and water-retaining effects of trehalose (TH), sodium pyrophosphate (SPP), sucrose (SC), and TH + SPP on silver carp (Hypophthalmichthys molitrix) surimi during frozen storage. Quality declined with time, but all additives mitigated the decrease in texture, breaking force and deformation, shear force, and water-holding capacity. Gel quality protection followed TH + SPP > TH > SC > SPP, as indicated by gel strength of 320.68 ± 21.73 for TH + SPP, 303.14 ± 14.56 for TH, 218.23 ± 11.53 for SC and 185.21 ± 26.03 g·cm for SPP after frozen storage for 180 d. Phosphate-containing additives (SPP and TH + SPP) showed advantages in maintaining water. Notably, TH demonstrated a significant antifreeze effect, while SPP showed an advantage in maintaining water. Overall, TH + SPP showed the best synergistic cryoprotective and water-retaining effects, which is beneficial for improving the quality of surimi during frozen storage.

title: Rapid detection of raw meat freshness using deep learning and colorimetric/fluorescent array
abstract: Effective monitoring of raw meat freshness is essential for food safety and reducing waste. This study presents a rapid freshness detection system combining a colorimetric fluorescent array (CFA) with deep learning (DL). The CFA, made by loading alizarin and fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) onto a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane, provides a sensitive response to amines produced during meat spoilage. A dataset of 8170 images was used to train convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Vision Transformer models. The CNN-based ResNet-152 model achieved the highest prediction accuracy, with 95.82% under natural light and 97.88% under ultraviolet light. The system can assess meat freshness from a single image in 130 ms. This CFA-DL approach offers a fast, non-destructive, and accurate method for real-time monitoring of meat freshness, potentially enhancing food safety and reducing waste without the need for specialized personnel or equipment.

title: Screening of umami peptides from shrimp juice based on molecular docking and kinetic modeling, and investigation of their interaction mechanisms with T1R1/T1R3 receptors
abstract: This study investigated three shrimp juices (ZG, TG, and 30d) to elucidate their flavor superiority and the underlying mechanisms of key umami peptides. Flavoromics revealed that 30d exhibited better flavor complexity and harmony, with umami amino acids accounting for 25%-27%. Ultrafiltration and sensory evaluation identified the 1-3 kDa fraction as the core taste-active components. Through machine learning and molecular docking, five umami peptides (RR-12, LD-11, GY-11, SM-14, and TL-14) with the lowest binding energies to the T1R1/T1R3 receptor were screened. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that four of them stably bound to the receptor through hydrogen bonds. This study provides molecular-level insights into the flavor superiority and umami mechanism of mixed-fermented shrimp juice, establishing a theoretical foundation for flavor-oriented design and quality enhancement of fermented aquatic seasonings.

title: Mechanism of α-amylase hydrolysis in maize and potato starches: Insight into outer shells and inner blocklets
abstract: In this study, outer shells and inner blocklets of maize and potato starches were prepared to reveal the influence of their molecular structure on α-amylase hydrolysis pattern of starch. Results showed that outer shell of maize starch had higher amylose (29.5%) and long amylopectin chain proportions (fb1, fb2, and fb3), while outer shell of potato starch showed lower amylose (13.5%) and fb1 proportion compared to their inner blocklets. Meanwhile, outer shell of maize starch had a lower α-amylase hydrolysis rate than inner blocklets, resulting in an "inside-out" hydrolysis pattern, while outer shell of potato starch showed a higher hydrolysis rate than inner blocklets, leading to an "outside-in" hydrolysis pattern. Additionally, outer shell and inner blocklets had different types and abundances of starch biosynthesis-related enzymes. Overall, the differential enzymes distribution during starch synthesis establishes distinct molecular structures in inner versus outer shells, which affect α-amylase susceptibility and hydrolysis patterns of starch.

title: Environmental factors drive rutin accumulation through a synergistic network promoting flavonoid biosynthesis and suppressing hydrolysis in tea plants (Camellia sinensis)
abstract: As an important glycosylated flavonoid, rutin contributes to the sensory quality and health benefits of tea. However, the relationship between rutin accumulation and environmental factors remains poorly characterised. Integration of meteorological, soil, and multi-omics data was used to assess rutin accumulation responses to environmental factors. The results showed that average daily rainfall, maximum temperature, and soil pH are key drivers, significantly affecting transcription and metabolite levels in basal metabolism, signal transduction, and flavonoid pathways. Specifically, the favourable environment enhances gene expression and precursor contents such as quercetin and isoquercitrin in the flavonoid pathway. Simultaneously, the hydrolysis genes CsGH1 and CsBGLU11 are downregulated, collectively promoting rutin accumulation. In summary, key environmental factors drive rutin accumulation through a combined network that enhances flavonoid biosynthesis and reduces hydrolysis. This study reveals the key environmental factors and regulatory mechanisms that drive rutin accumulation, providing a basis for improving the functional properties of tea products.

title: Increased polysaccharide molecular interaction improves foam template oil absorption behavior of egg white protein oleogel
abstract: To address trans saturated fats health risks, novel alkaline-heated egg white protein (AHEWP) with propylene glycol alginate (PGA) and sodium alginate (SA) composite oleogels were developed using the foam template method. In methodology, the effects of PGA:SA mass ratios on the physicochemistry, functionality, microstructure, oil absorption kinetics and thermal stability were evaluated. Results showed that the 1:1 (PGA:SA) oleogel formed stable 3D network structure through protein folding and polysaccharide electrostatic interactions. Accordingly, this exhibited moderate porosity, balanced oil retention, and enhanced dynamic rheology and thermal stability. In addition, polysaccharides synergistically improved foam stability, expansion rate and interfacial film strength, with raised SA exposing hydrophobic groups, increasing α-helix and reducing β-sheet/turn. Group 1:1 presented optimal oil absorption (OAC, 37.44 g/g) and holding capacity (OHC, 83.10%). Overall, this study introduces lyophilized AHEWP-PGA/SA foam templates filled with liquid oil as novel fat substitutes, paving way for developing functional food-grade oleogels with tailored textures.

title: CeVO₄-CNT-nafion modified glassy carbon electrode for voltammetric detection of 3-nitrotyrosine: a biomarker of protein nitration
abstract: 3-Nitrotyrosine (3-NT) is a recognized biomarker of protein nitration. In this study, an electrochemical nonenzymatic sensor was developed for 3-NT detection by modifying a glassy carbon electrode with a nanocomposite of CeVO 4 , carboxylated carbon nanotubes (CNT), and Nafion. Scanning electron microscopy revealed that flower-like CeVO 4 nanoparticles were uniformly embedded within the interconnected tubular network of CNT and Nafion. Under optimal conditions, the sensor exhibited a wide linear response to 3-NT in the range of 10 to 900 μM, with a detection limit of 1.20 μM. To validate its practical application, myofibrillar protein (MP) was extracted from pork and exposed to varying concentrations of nitrite at pH 6.0, leading to the formation of 3-NT. These nitrosative MP samples were then analyzed using the developed sensor, and the results were compared with those obtained by HPLC using split samples. The findings demonstrated no significant differences between the two methods.

title: An electrochemical index approach to assess the antioxidant capacity of olive oils extracts using a Sonogel-Carbon electrode
abstract: This study proposes a rapid and cost-effective electrochemical method for evaluating the antioxidant capacity of olive oil extracts by using differential pulse voltammetry. Fourteen commercial oils, including extra virgin olive oils (EVOO), a virgin olive oil (VOO), olive oils, olive pomace oils, and a sunflower oil, were analysed. The extraction of polyphenolic compounds from the oils was performed following the official International Olive Council method. The antioxidant capacity was assessed using the ABTS and DPPH spectrophotometric methods. Electrochemical measurements results showed EVOO and VOO with higher electrochemical index than the rest (≥2), with repeatability lower than 5%, strongly correlating with ABTS (% inhibition, R 2 = 0.9662) and DPPH (R 2 = 0.9319) results. No electrochemical response was observed in OPO and SO extracts. The first anodic peak (I 1 /E 1 ) correlated more closely with antioxidant activity, suggesting it reflects the contribution of polyphenols bearing ortho-dihydroxyl groups. Consequently, I 1 /E 1 , can be considered as a reliable indicator of antioxidant capacity in olive oils.

title: Cod protein modifications induced by lipid oxidation-derived aldehydes: Insights into multi-aldehydes environment
abstract: Cod and its products are particularly vulnerable to modifications caused by lipid oxidation products especially aldehydes. Most studies have focused on the effects of individual aldehydes. However, in real food systems, multiple aldehydes may interact competitively or synergistically to alter protein functionality. Here, a model system of a clickable probe, 4-(2-propyn-1-yloxy)-2-butenal (yne-ACR, 500 μM), with five reactive carbonyls (500 μM and 1000 μM): formaldehyde (FA), malondialdehyde (MDA), methylglyoxal (MGO), glyoxal (GO), and phenylacetaldehyde (PhA)-was used to simulate and visualize protein modifications. Results showed that FA and GO had no significant effect on yne-ACR-mediated modification, whereas MDA, MGO, and PhA significantly increased the modification levels and decreased intrinsic fluorescence, indicating conformational changes and increased binding availability. Physicochemical evaluations confirmed that aldehyde treatments markedly altered the microstructure, thermal stability, and volatile profile of cod protein. This work provides new insights into the mechanisms of multi-aldehydes co-modification of cod protein and offers a theoretical basis for controlling oxidation of foods.

title: Formation mechanism, detection methods and control strategies of warmed-over flavor in meat and meat products of livestock and poultry: A comprehensive review and future perspectives
abstract: Warmed-over flavor (WOF) represents a typical off-flavor in meat products, characterized by stale, cardboard-like, and metallic notes. Growing research efforts have increasingly focused on WOF of meat products, while comprehensive and systematic reviews remain scarce. This review systematically summarizes the WOF in meat products from three interconnected perspectives: Formation mechanisms, detection technologies, and control strategies. Current evidences indicate that lipid oxidation acts as the primary driver of WOF development, while protein oxidation and microbial metabolism synergistically accelerate flavor deterioration. In detection, conventional detection methods such as TBARS and GC-MS serve as foundational approaches, whereas emerging techniques including rapid colorimetric sensing, lipidomics and imaging mass spectrometry (IMS) offer novel molecular-level insights. For control strategies, a comprehensive prevention framework spanning the entire "rearing-storage-processing-packaging" chain is proposed. Future studies should prioritize elucidating the molecular interplay between lipid and protein oxidation, developing multi-scale real-time detection platforms, and establishing green, sustainable, full-chain flavor preservation strategies.

title: Identification, characterization, and molecular docking of immunomodulatory peptides from Capsicum annuum var. conoides seed protein hydrolysates
abstract: Plant-derived bioactive peptides offer an attractive strategy for developing immunomodulatory functional foods. This study investigated the structural characteristics and immunomodulatory potential of Capsicum annuum var. conoides seed protein hydrolysate (CSPH), prepared via simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Comparative structural analysis revealed significant conformational changes in CSPH relative to the native protein. CSPH significantly enhanced macrophage proliferation and phagocytosis, and increased NO and ROS production and pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion (IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α). Treatment with the TLR4 inhibitor (TAK-242) significantly suppressed this CSPH-induced immunostimulation, confirming TLR4 as a critical mediating receptor. LC-MS/MS analysis combined with molecular docking identified three novel TLR4-binding peptides from CSPH. All three synthesized peptides exhibited immunomodulatory activity without cytotoxicity, validating their immunomodulatory effect. These findings provide new insights into the immunomodulatory mechanism of CSPH and underscore the potential of Capsicum annuum var. conoides seeds as a valuable source for immunomodulatory functional food.

title: Effects of lycopene extract incorporation strategies on the quality attributes and protein digestibility of beef meatballs
abstract: This study examined the effects of lycopene incorporation strategies, direct addition (LM), dissolution in lard (LOM) and homogenization after dissolution (LOHM) on beef meatballs qualities. The LOHM treatment significantly improved oxidative stability (reduced TBARS and carbonyl values) but compromised protein network formation, increasing viscous modulus (G″) and deteriorating texture. In contrast, LOM enhanced elastic network structure (higher storage modulus G') and textural properties. During digestion, LOHM exhibited a "digestive dichotomy": it promoted initial gastric proteolysis, increasing peptide diversity and low-molecular- weight peptides, yet induced protein aggregation that resisted intestinal hydrolysis, limiting free amino acids release. These results demonstrate that the finely dispersed, lycopene-stabilized emulsion created by LOHM facilitates early pepsin-mediated cleavage but also promotes aggregation/reorganization that hinders later intestinal enzyme access, representing a stage-dependent digestibility trade-off. This work provides novel insights for designing precision-functionality meat products with tailored digestive behaviors.

title: Multi-scale analysis of brown seaweed fortified pasta on structural, functional, nutraceutical, sensorial and volatilomic attributes
abstract: Brown seaweed is an underutilised marine ingredient for cereal product fortification despite its nutritional and functional properties. In this study, we studied the multi-scale effect of brown seaweed fortification in pasta from structural to sensorial attributes. MixoLab analysis showed brown seaweed addition dose dependently increased gluten network strength by 19-22%. Seaweed fortified pasta exhibited increased hardness and chewiness by 32.8% and 41.0% of pasta along with reduced SDS extractability and increased gluten hydrophobicity. This indicates an enhanced gluten network, supported by increased starch order and β sheets content of up to 6.9% in FTIR as well as a more compact gluten network observed in microstructure analysis. Nutritionally, the total phenolic content and antioxidant activity increased dose dependently with the highest values observed at 2.5% seaweed inclusion level. Volatile profiling of cooked pasta showed increased presence marine or earthy odour compounds which caused decrease in sensory acceptance.

title: On-demand, thermally triggered burst release of essential oils via native complex coacervate-stabilized emulsion gels in instant beverages
abstract: The application of grapefruit essential oil (GEO) in acidic, high-sugar syrups is hindered by the release paradox: the need for structural confinement during storage versus rapid aroma liberation upon consumption. This study developed a marine-derived liquid encapsulation platform using fish gelatin-fucoidan complex coacervates (COA). Optimized at pH 3.3, the COA formed robust interfacial multilayers, achieving 96.1% encapsulation efficiency at 60% GEO content. Unlike conventional powders, GEO-COA maintained homogeneous dispersion and structural integrity, suppressing GEO release to <10.3% over 28 d in a real-food syrup matrix. A thermally triggered burst release is driven by a critical viscoelastic transition at 42.5 °C, where the loss of interfacial rigidity enables rapid GEO release. Consequently, dilution with 80 °C water induced 95.6% GEO release within 2 min with an immediate surge in headspace volatiles. This strategy ensures long-term storage stability in acidic syrups, while providing on-demand aroma release for instant hot-beverage applications.

title: Corrigendum to “Highly selective and sensitive colorimetric detection of nicosulfuron based on Cu-MOF nanozyme” [Food Chem. 518 (2026) 149573]
Synergistic texture enhancement of fibrous and amorphous fava bean protein fractions in reduced-phosphate myofibrillar protein gels: A concerted physical and chemical cross-linking mechanism
abstract: Reduced phosphate weakens myofibrillar protein (MP) gels, hindering healthier meat product development. This study used fibrillated fava bean protein (FFP), separated into fibrous (FF) and amorphous (AF) fractions, to restore gel properties. In low-/zero-phosphate MP gels, FF formed microporous structures via physical filling and hydrophobic interactions, which improved water immobilization but contributed limited rigidity. Conversely, AF enhanced gel strength through disulfide cross-linking and ionic bonding. The synergy between these fractions enabled FFP to restore key gel properties. At a 2% addition level, cooking yield exceeded 80%, gel strength recovered to 60-95%, and water-holding capacity reached 87-92% of the full-phosphate control, despite a 50-100% reduction in phosphate. This work elucidates a "physical filling-chemical cross-linking" mechanism, offering a viable strategy for producing phosphate-free, clean-label meat products with desirable texture.

title: Insight into the underlying mechanism of succinylation-ultrasound dual-modification in synergistically improving the physicochemical and functional properties of yeast proteins
abstract: The poor solubility of yeast proteins (YP) highly limited their application in food manufacturing. Herein, we present a succinylation-ultrasound dual-modification strategy to improve YP's physicochemical and functional properties with optimized parameters of succinylation pH 9.0, reagent/protein ratio 0.3, and ultrasonic power 400 W. This approach synergistically enhances dispersibility and colloidal stability, with solubility increased to 65.43% and particle size dramatically reduced to nanoscale. Additionally, the dual-modification alters YP's secondary and tertiary structures, accompanied by changes in surface properties, particularly surface hydrophobicity and zeta potential, thereby demonstrating a synergistic effect superior to individual treatments. Mechanistically, succinylation introduces negatively charged succinyl groups to enhance the electrostatic repulsion (V R (H)) and reduce the hydrophobic energy (V H (H)), thereby raising the energy barrier (V(H 0 )), while ultrasound facilitates the escape of particles from the energy well, inducing the transition from aggregation to dispersion. This study could promote the extensive application of YP in the food industry.

title: Enhancing the properties of Pleurotus ostreatus protein-konjac glucomannan gels through pH regulation: Gel formation mechanism and application in low-fat cheese sticks
abstract: Precise pH regulation of protein-polysaccharide interactions is essential. This study systematically investigated the effect of pH regulation (4.0-8.0) on the gel properties, structural characteristics, and molecular interactions of Pleurotus ostreatus protein (POP)-konjac glucomannan (KGM) composite gels. Results showed that the POP-KGM gels exhibited optimal gel properties at pH 6.0, with the highest water holding capacity (87.91%), gel strength (1.51 N), and thermal stability (T d = 84.82 °C). Microstructural analysis revealed that disulfide bonds were pivotal for POP-KGM gel formation, and pH regulation significantly enhanced the gel network structure by changing the protein conformation. Specifically, at pH 6.0, X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy revealed that POP-KGM gels formed more ordered crystalline structures and denser three-dimensional networks. Furthermore, the POP-KGM gels (pH 6.0) were successfully used as a substitute for cream cheese in low-fat cheese sticks, which exhibited superior physicochemical properties and protein digestibility to full-fat cheese sticks.

title: Effect of whey protein isolates on lipid-amylose complex structure and function in diacylglycerol oleogel cakes
abstract: In bakeries, margarines are often replaced by oleogels that contain less saturated and trans fatty acids, the latter are considered as harmful ingredients to health. However, oleogels increase starch digestibility of baked products, leading to high postprandial blood sugar. An option is to add whey proteins to reduce starch digestibility. When whey protein isolate was 1.8% (w/w) in cake batter, resistant starch increased from 42.86 to 51.24%, with the consequence of reduced starch digestibility. Reduced starch digestibility was resulted from the formation of lipid-amylose complexes, as evidenced by increases in the starch complex index (from 26.50 to 27.80%), relative crystallinity (from 34.63 to 37.85%), and enthalpy change (from 605.1 to 4311 J/g). Therefore, adding whey protein isolates is effective to adjust and design oleogel functions to address the issue of high postprandial blood sugar caused by oleogels.

title: Determination of benfuracarb residues in plant-derived foods using a modified QuEChERS method with UHPLC-MS/MS
abstract: An UHPLC-MS/MS method, combined with QuEChERS sample preparation, was developed and validated for the quantification of benfuracarb residues in 43 plant-derived foods. Silver nitrate (AgNO 3 ) solution was used as a protective agent, and an ammonia-ammonium chloride buffer solution (ACS) was employed to neutralize the pH in acidic samples. Calibration curves demonstrated excellent linearity (R > 0.9977) over the concentration range of 5-250 μg/kg. Recoveries of benfuracarb ranged from 80.67 to 113.33%, with relative standard deviations (RSDs) of 0.97-11.02%. The limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) were 0.01-0.93 μg/kg and 0.04-3.11 μg/kg, respectively. Cross-validation in six independent laboratories yielded recoveries of 78.3-106% and RSDs below 11%. The method was applied to analyze 50 plant-derived food samples, all containing pesticide residues below the established maximum residue limits (MRLs). These results confirm the method is accurate, sensitive, and universal for benfuracarb detection in plant-derived foods, with good stability, transferability, and suitability for routine monitoring.

title: Moderate roasting combined with low-aqueous extraction enables simultaneous improvement of quality and flavor of walnut oil
abstract: Moderate processing technologies that enhance flavor while preserving nutritional quality are increasingly demanded in the edible oil industry. This study systematically evaluated the effects of microwave (MR), oven (OR), and infrared (IR) roasting combined with low-aqueous extraction (LAE) on oil yield, physicochemical properties, flavor characteristics, and lipid composition of walnut oil. An oil yield of 79.08% was achieved under optimized conditions (liquid-to-material ratio 10%, 1 min, 50 °C), with MR and IR further enhancing the yield. Roasting had minimal effects on acid value, peroxide value, pigment content, and fatty acid composition, but significantly enhanced oxidative stability, which was attributed to increased levels of tocopherols, phytosterols, and phenolic compounds. HS-SPME-GC-MS identified aldehydes and heterocyclic compounds as key contributors to roasted aroma. Lipidomic analysis revealed that moderate roasting conditions, particularly IR, preserved triglycerides while limiting excessive oxidation. Overall, moderate roasting combined with LAE effectively improved walnut oil flavor while maintaining quality.

title: Insights into the potential contribution of glycosidic aroma precursors to the aroma and sensory profile of icewines
abstract: Grape glycosidic precursors are a significant potential source of volatile compounds that may contribute to icewine aroma. This study investigated the effects of glycosidic precursors from conventional and ice grape juices on the volatile composition and sensory profile of 'Beibinghong' and 'Vidal' wines using a conventional fermentation model. The addition of precursor extracts primarily increased the concentrations of various terpenes, C 13 -norisoprenoids, volatile phenols, lactones, and higher alcohols, with more pronounced effects from ice juice glycosides. Sensory descriptive analysis revealed that the addition of ice juice glycosides significantly enhanced the 'medicinal', 'smoky', and 'dried fruit' aromas in 'Beibinghong' wine, as well as 'citrus', 'floral' and 'honey' notes in 'Vidal' wine. However, significant differences in 'caramel', 'dried fruit', and 'honey' aroma intensities remained between authentic icewines and precursor-supplemented wines, suggesting that some key aroma contributors in icewine may originate from alternative metabolic pathways rather than from glycosidic precursors.

title: Preparation, isolation, purification and identification of ACE inhibitory fractions from yak casein fermented by Bacillus cereus (XBMU-13)
abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptides have been shown to contribute to blood pressure reduction. In this study, a protease-producing bacterial strain was isolated and identified for fermentation of yak milk casein to produce ACE inhibitory peptides. Subsequently, fermentation conditions were optimized, and the resulting peptides were purified, and identified. The results showed that a Bacillus cereus strain, designated XBMU-13, was isolated from naturally fermented bean curd and exhibited a protease activity of 86.27 ± 3.82 U/mL. Using response surface methodology, the optimal fermentation parameters were obtained as follows: substrate concentration of 63.2 g/L, sucrose concentration of 6 g/L, inorganic salt concentration of 6 g/L, initial pH of 7.87, and fermentation temperature of 34 °C. Fraction G-10-1 exhibiting the highest ACE inhibitory ability was isolated through sequential ultrafiltration, Sephadex gel chromatography, and preparative liquid chromatography. Furthermore, nine peptide sequences in fraction G-10-1 were identified by liquid chromatography-mass analysis.

title: Invisible plastic release from overlooked usage practices in microwaved food packaging
abstract: Plastic food packaging is an overlooked source of invisible contamination during microwaving. In this study, polyethylene (PE) residues released from microwaveable food packaging, including onigiri wrappers, porridge cartons, and milk cartons, were investigated under microwave conditions representative of routine consumer use. PE release increased markedly with heating duration. Nile Red fluorescence staining showed that microplastic size decreased from 3.88 ± 0.28 μm to 3.18 ± 0.23 μm during prolonged heating. Dynamic light scattering analysis revealed nanoplastic particles within 1-3 min of microwave heating, with sizes ranging from 40 to 240 nm. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy showed that polyethylene residues released from onigiri wrappers reached 1443.78 ± 5.28 μg/mL after 5 min of microwave exposure. Exposure to these residues decreased the viability of Clone 9 normal rat liver cells and increased oxidative stress. These findings suggest that neglected usage patterns may contribute to invisible plastic contamination, raising concerns about food safety.

title: Comparative analysis of flaxseed meal sources influences the functional properties of flaxseed globulin via protein structure
abstract: This study investigated variations in the structure and functional properties of flaxseed globulins (FGs) extracted from different flaxseed meal sources. The results indicated that S2 exhibited superior solubility (53.53 ± 2.25%) and emulsifying properties (38.24 ± 1.32 m 2 /g, 15.98 ± 1.02 min). This superiority was attributed to its smallest particle size and highest absolute value of zeta potential, which facilitated protein-water interactions. Conversely, S4 demonstrated a greater oil holding capacity (18.27 ± 0.58 g/g). Principal component analysis and Pearson correlation analysis confirmed the correlation between the structure and functional properties of FGs. Smaller protein particles demonstrated a less compact structure and higher fluorescence intensity. Higher α-helix combined with lower β-sheet contents contributed to the stability of emulsion interfacial film, thereby preventing emulsion aggregation. This research elucidated the influence of flaxseed meal source on the structure and functional attributes of FGs, offering valuable insights into functional properties of FGs.

title: Improving the structural and functional properties of soy protein amyloid fibrils through ohmic heating
abstract: The purpose of this study was to explore the effect of ohmic heating (OH) on the formation of soy amyloid fibrils (SAF) by self-assembly of soy protein isolate (SPI). Compared with traditional heating methods, OH technology can directly act on proteins, but the regulation of different electric field intensity (EFI) on fibrillation was still unclear. Therefore, this study induced SPI to form SAF by regulating the EFI of OH, and analyzed the conversion rate, spatial structure and functional characteristics. Results showed that appropriate EFI can accelerate fibrillation and improve functional properties. When the EFI was 7 V/cm, SAF-OH-7 had the fastest formation rate of fibril, the highest conversion rate (53.13%), β-sheet content (59.22%), solubility (32.01 mg/mL), emulsion property and thermal stability (166.41 °C). This study revealed the regulatory mechanism and advantages of OH in soy protein fibrillation for the first time, and provided a new strategy for plant protein fibrillation.

title: Enhancing polyphenol recovery from NaDES extracts of olive oil by-products through polymeric resin purification
abstract: Olive oil production generates large amounts of leaf waste rich in phenolic compounds. This study aimed to purify olive leaf extracts obtained with a choline chloride-glycerol green solvent using polymeric resins, while removing co-extracted sugars and solvent residues. Two non-functionalized polymeric resins were evaluated through adsorption, aqueous washing, and ethanol-water desorption. Phenolic compounds were monitored by high-performance liquid chromatography, and antioxidant capacity was assessed using the Ferric Reducing Antioxidant Power assay. Two sequential water washes removed solvent residues with minimal phenolic losses. Resin selectivity differed by compound polarity and size: one resin favored recovery of small polar compounds, whereas the other improved recovery of larger flavonoids. An ethanol-water mixture of 70:30 enabled effective elution of key olive leaf phenolics. The optimized workflow produced antioxidant-rich purified fractions and provides a reproducible laboratory-scale strategy for improving the quality of green-solvent extracts intended for further food and cosmetic applications.

title: Pickering emulsion gels stabilised by ultrasound-treated PSE-like myofibrillar protein microgel particles for age-friendly dysphagia foods: The structural changes, stability and texture-modified gel properties
abstract: To improve the processing suitability of pale, soft and exudative (PSE)-like myofibrillar protein (MP), ultrasound was applied to modulate heat-induced MP aggregates and prepare MP microgel particles (MMPs). The structural and interfacial properties of MMPs were compared with those of large gel particles without ultrasound treatment and native MP. The effects of different MMP concentrations on Pickering emulsion stability, gel texture and swallowing properties were evaluated. Results indicated that MMPs prepared using ultrasound treatment at 600 W for 15 min exhibited more favourable structural modifications and enhanced emulsification potential. Compared with native MP, their surface hydrophobicity and contact angle increased by 221.88% and 50.54%, respectively. Increasing the MMP concentration from 0.5% to 4.0% enhanced emulsion stability, with hardness and gumminess increasing by 75.82% and 96.73%, respectively. According to the International Dysphagia Diet Standardization Initiative, the emulsion gels were classified as Levels 4-5, highlighting their potential for developing dysphagia-friendly foods.

title: Artificially screened and rationally constructed lignocellulose-transforming microorganisms for producing food ingredients
abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass (LCB) constitutes a significant portion of terrestrial biomass, and the challenge of disposing of LCB cost-effectively and environmentally friendly is considerable. The food industry is experiencing increasing demand for sustainable, eco-friendly raw materials. There is growing interest in researching the microbial bioconversion of sugar-rich LCB into food ingredients. Utilizing LCB for food ingredient production increases economic value and aligns with diverse manufacturing concepts in the food sector. This review provides an overview of recent advancements in microorganisms capable of converting LCB into food ingredients through artificial screening. The application of rationally designed high-performance engineered strains and microbial consortia for producing food ingredients was investigated, thus offering a unique microbial technology perspective for the high-value utilization of LCB in sustainable food ingredient production. Additionally, the review discusses the current limitations and future directions concerning the microorganisms used for the bioconversion of LCB into food ingredients.

title: Unlocking the blue treasure: Marine-derived fungi and their metabolites for green preservation of fruits and vegetables
abstract: Postharvest losses of fruits and vegetables caused by pathogenic fungi and oxidative stress highlight the need for sustainable preservation strategies, and marine-derived fungi provide structurally diverse secondary metabolites with dual antifungal and antioxidant activities. These metabolites inhibit major pathogens through multitarget mechanisms, including cell membranes disruption, oxidative stress induction, and interference with energy and metabolic pathways, thereby reducing the likelihood of pathogen resistance. Incorporation of these compounds into biodegradable materials, such as composite films, enhance stability, enable controlled release, and provide dual-function preservation. Unlike previous reviews that mainly focus on individual aspects such as antimicrobial activity, antioxidant activity, or packaging applications, this review proposes the "full-chain" framework for marine-derived fungal applications in fruit and vegetable preservation, covering resource screening, bioactivity identification, mechanism analysis, safety evaluation, and material development. Future studies should focus on systematic resource exploration, functional integration of metabolites, and comprehensive safety evaluation to facilitate industrial applications.

title: Assessment of the enological potential of several strains of Lachancea thermotolerans. A proteomic approach
abstract: We evaluated five Lachancea thermotolerans strains (F108, F111, A54, L31-Blizz™, Laktia™) with divergent acidification capacities from an enological perspective, focusing on their ability to control wine pH through lactate production and sensory impact using quantitative label-free proteomics. A total of 3588 non-redundant proteins were identified. L. thermotolerans, known for its thermotolerance and environmental resilience, is a climate-change-tolerant non-Saccharomyces yeast valuable for winemaking in warmer conditions. The abundance of acidification enzymes (lactate and succinate dehydrogenases) varied among strains, influencing wine acidity and sensory attributes such as freshness/minerality. High acidification strains (A54, L31-Blizz™, Laktia™) showed elevated lactate dehydrogenase values (>78 units), whereas low-acidification strains (F108, F111) displayed low (48-49 units). Differences were also observed in succinic acid and aroma-related enzymes (β-lyases, β-glucosidases). These proteomic profiles provide innovative molecular insights into the enological potential and intraspecific variability of L.thermotolerans, offering useful guidance for biotechnological companies and winemakers adapting to global warming.

title: Polysaccharide-protein composite systems in dysphagia-oriented food design: interactions, applications, and additive manufacturing
abstract: Global population aging has made dysphagia a major public health concern, yet current dysphagia-friendly foods often lack texture variety, palatability, and nutritional balance. Polysaccharide-protein composites enable texture modulation and nutrient fortification through controllable interactions (e.g., electrostatic, hydrophobic, hydrogen, covalent). When combined with 3D printing, these systems can be fabricated into dysphagia-oriented foods with patient-adapted texture, nutritional composition, and structural form, thereby better matching individual swallowing needs. This review systematically examines formation mechanisms and key factors influencing polysaccharide-protein interactions, focuses on designing IDDSI-compliant composite gels and emulsions, and evaluates synergy between ink rheology and 3D printing parameters for printability and swallowing safety. Despite these advances, the practical translation of dysphagia foods remains constrained by an incomplete understanding of oral processing-related interactions, the lack of standardized design frameworks, and limited clinical validation. Future research should focus on dynamic interaction mechanisms under oral and gastrointestinal conditions, stimuli-responsive composite systems, and AI-assisted 3D printing strategies that connect formulation design with individual swallowing requirements.

title: Synergistic effects of organic salt curing and heating methods on quality and flavor preservation of large yellow croaker during frozen storage
abstract: This study systematically investigated the combined effects of organic salt curing with sodium acetate (SA), sodium citrate (SC), and sodium lactate (SL), and different heating methods on the quality and flavor stability of large yellow croaker during frozen storage. Organic salt treatments significantly enhanced the water-holding capacity of the fish fillets. After 8 weeks of frozen storage, the moisture content of the control group decreased to approximately 77%, while the SC and SL treated groups maintained approximately 84%, which was significantly higher than that of the control (P < 0.05). Microwave heating produced fillets with superior textural properties compared with steam heating. Microstructural analysis revealed that SC- and SL-treated samples preserved more intact muscle fibers with optimal inter-fiber spacing (40-80 μm). In addition, these treatments promoted the formation of desirable volatile compounds, resulting in flavor profiles closer to those of fresh fish. Overall, curing with SC or SL combined with microwave heating effectively mitigated quality and flavor deterioration during frozen storage, providing a scientific basis for developing low-sodium, high-quality frozen fish products.

title: Thermal stability and bioaccessibility of apple phenolics in starch systems are governed by their molecular motifs, plant cell walls, and cell wall pre-loading
abstract: Wheat starch (S), an apple cell wall analogue (aACW), and an apple pomace phenolic extract (PP) were formulated into blends-S-PP, S-aACW, S-aACW-PP, and phenolic pre-loaded wall composites S-(aACW:PP)-then hydrothermally processed and digested to elucidate the molecular determinants of phenolic thermal degradation and gastrointestinal bioaccessibility in starch-fibre systems. Processing-induced phenolic loss and bioaccessibility decreased with starch, declined further with aACW, and were most suppressed in S-(aACW:PP). Single-compound analysis revealed distinct lability clusters. Group-1 included heat-labile phenolics, slightly stabilized by starch but strongly protected by aACW, particularly when preloaded. Group-2 showed pronounced matrix dependence, with starch additionally exerting a stabilizing effect. A small group exhibited stochastic matrix effects. During digestion, small phenolics benefited from aACW retention. In contrast, larger flavanols were prone to precipitation by starch and aACW, reducing their bioaccesibility. Phenolic structure, interactions with S and aACW, and aACW pre-loading together determined thermal and digestive stability and gastrointestinal release.

title: Influence of whey isolate protein emulsion gels substitution ratio on structural, sensory and rheological properties of chicken paste and its suitability for 3D printing
abstract: Structure-tunable emulsion gels (EG) exhibit rheological properties similar to or better than those of solid/semi-solid fats, making them suitable for constructing solid fats with low saturated fatty acid content to replace animal fats. This approach can reduce the saturated fat content in meat products. In this study, emulsion gels made from whey protein isolate (WPI) and ĸ-carrageenan were added as fat substitutes to chicken paste. The effects of animal fat and WPI-KG emulsion gels on the rheological properties, 3D printing suitability, and quality characteristics of chicken paste were compared. The chicken paste samples containing emulsion gels exhibited higher apparent viscosity, G' values, hardness and elasticity, as well as stronger water-holding capacity and microstructure. Relative to the group treated exclusively with fat, the incorporation of emulsion gel elevated the initial apparent viscosity from 19,786.36 Pa•s to 25,636.85 Pa•s-43,253.21 Pa•s. This viscosity progressively diminished with increasing shear rate, thereby demonstrating shear-thinning behavior in the chicken paste. G' increased from 4742.36 to 13,002.3 Pa at 1-100 rad/s to 5612.84-14,443.28 Pa upon emulsion gel addition. Across all treatment groups, G' values consistently surpassed those of G", indicating a predominantly elastic gel structure within the chicken paste. This composition is more conducive to the formation of a three-dimensional network. This can be attributed to the addition of emulsion gel promoting cross-linking between proteins and polysaccharides within the gel matrix, forming a more compact network structure. The appearance of 3D-printed chicken paste products showed that the addition of emulsion gel imparted stronger viscoelasticity and structural recovery to the samples, significantly improving the printability of the chicken paste. Additionally, sensory evaluation results indicate that WPI-KG emulsion gel exhibits high overall acceptability (6.17 ± 0.49) as an animal fat substitute. In summary, WPI-KG emulsion gel significantly improves the 3D printability of chicken paste and validates its potential application as an animal fat substitute in meat products.

title: Auxiliary fermentation with Pediococcus acidilactici C1 reshapes flavor formation in sufu: An integrated metagenomic, flavoromic and non-targeted metabolomic deciphering
abstract: Sufu, a traditional Chinese fermented soybean product, relies on spontaneous microbial succession for flavor, leading to high variability. Starter-assisted fermentation improves flavor; this study explores sufu flavor differences and mechanisms between spontaneous and Pediococcus acidilactici C1-inoculated processes. The findings demonstrated that inoculation with P. acidilactici C1 markedly enhanced the diversity and concentration of flavor compounds in sufu. Notably, 12 key taste-active free amino acids were detected, with glutamate up by 14% and aspartic acid showing an approximate 20-fold increase. A total of 15 key volatile flavor compounds were characterized, among which 8 were newly uncovered, namely ethyl 2-methylbutanoate, ethyl acetate, ethyl butyrate, ethyl caprylate, ethyl 2-ethylhexanoate, ethyl propionate, isoamyl acetate and 3-octanol. Metagenomics revealed enrichment of genes related to carbohydrate transport, amino acid/lipid metabolism, while non-targeted metabolomics confirmed metabolic remodeling. Multi-omics analyses showed P. acidilactici C1 reprogrammed carbon flux and boosted amino acid/lipid-derived volatile biosynthesis, enabling flavor-enhancing starter development.

title: CRISPR-Cas12a-regulated photo-ATRP for ultrasensitive detection of lipopolysaccharide
abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), a primary virulence factor produced by Gram-negative bacteria, demands rapid and ultrasensitive detection for safeguarding food safety and supporting clinical diagnosis. This study developed a novel electrochemical biosensing platform by integrating the programmable recognition of CRISPR-Cas12a with the high-gain signal amplification of photoinduced ATRP. In this mechanism, the binding of LPS to its aptamer regulated Cas12a activity, which controlled an N 3 -DNA initiator probe.
