Flaxseed oil (FO), rich in unsaturated fatty acids, showed the highest emulsifying activity, stability, ζ-potential, and interfacial protein content, followed by Dongliao black pigs lard (DBPL) group, the Crossbred fattening pigs lard (CFPL) group, and the Hybrid fattening pigs lard (HFPL) group (P < 0.05). Compared to FO group, lard groups exhibited higher Turbiscan stability index and larger particle size, indicating poorer emulsion stability, confirmed by confocal laser scanning microscope. Interfacial kinetics revealed that MP rearrangement dominated interface film formation. FO achieved the highest interfacial pressure and rearrangement rate (P < 0.05), enhancing emulsion stability. Conversely, lard groups largely preserved the α-helix structure of interfacial MP, resulting in a compact, rigid molecular conformation. Consequently, the lard-formed interface film was inflexible and ineffective at resisting droplet aggregation.

title: Effects and mechanisms of natural deep eutectic solvents on the Decrystallization and quality of multifloral honey
abstract: This study proposes natural deep eutectic solvents (NADESs) to address the limitations of conventional honey decrystallization methods. Under mild conditions (30 °C), the decrystallization rate exceeded 70%. With a higher dosage, this rate approached approximately 90% (P < 0.05). NMR, IR, and DSC analyses revealed a stable hydrogen-bond network in NADESs. The spectra exhibited only shifts in peak intensity and position, with no new compounds detected. Cytotoxicity tests further demonstrated that these solvents are biocompatible. In multifloral honey, the addition of NADESs lowered the 5-hydroxymethylfurfural content from 13.81 μg/mL to about 7 μg/mL. This equals a roughly 40% reduction (P < 0.05). Moreover, the in vitro antioxidant activity of the honey was strengthened. Further analyses-including XRD, polarized light microscopy, and metabolomics-revealed decreased crystal content, stronger hydrogen bonding, and an enrichment of flavor-related metabolites. Collectively, these results demonstrate that NADESs provide a new strategy for honey decrystallization.

title: Sustainable utilization of rice wine cake: The integration of in vitro and in silico method for exploring antioxidant peptides
abstract: Rice wine cake was sustainable utilized for bioactive peptide development. Alkaline protease was verified optimal among selected industrial proteases based on the highest DH (15%), 77.4% content of peptide <1 kDa, and potent antioxidant activity of its hydrolysate (APH). APH reduced intracellular ROS by approximately 50% in the oxidant injury HaCaT cells. There were 703 peptides identified from APH by Nano-LC-Q-Orbitrap MS, and 57.0% of oligopeptides exhibited terminal amphiphilicity. The Keap1-binding potential were predicted. Among the ones with binding energy < -7.0 kcal/mol, GLPPEWY, QHSIVATPF, and WIDFPRAPQ with amphiphilic termini were chosen, and ATPFWQPATF and AAAPWPW with non-amphiphilic termini, for ROS scavenging. At 50 μM, QHSIVATPF and ATPFWQPATF respectively acted the highest (69.8%) and lowest ROS inhibition (40.1%). The molecular dynamics simulations well illustrated the mechanistic differences between the two. The three amphiphilic peptides were confirmed to promote nuclear Nrf2 accumulation. The findings suggested the significance of terminal amphiphilicity for antioxidant peptides.

title: The mechanism of egg yolk lecithin in improving the quality of chili oil during thermal processing: Integrated insights from lipid oxidation and flavoromics
abstract: Egg yolk lecithin was evaluated as a natural additive to improve chili oil during thermal processing. Lecithin (0-3.6%, w/w) significantly enhanced oxidative stability and reshaped the volatile profile. At 2.0% lecithin, acid value and TBARS decreased from 0.03344 to 0.00792 mg/g and from 0.022 to 0.012 mg/kg, respectively, while DPPH radical scavenging activity at 10 mg/mL rose from 63.77% to 86.48%. Although 3.6% lecithin exhibited the strongest antioxidant effect, 2.0% gave the highest sensory acceptability. GC-IMS and HS-SPME-GC-MS identified 38 and 83 volatiles, respectively. Lecithin reduced d-limonene and linalool but increased 5-hydroxymethylfurfural, furfuryl alcohol and 2-pentylfuran. Eight differential metabolites (VIP > 1, p 1. Overall, 2.0% lecithin offered the best balance of oxidative stability, sensory quality and aroma optimization.

title: Properties of MgO2NPs/CMCS composite paper and its application in ambient temperature preservation of cantaloupe
abstract: In this study, nano‑magnesium peroxide/carboxymethyl chitosan (MgO 2 NPs/CMCS) composite paper was fabricated by coating Xuan paper for energy-saving ambient-temperature preservation of cantaloupe. At a coating weight of 25 g/m 2 , the composite exhibited optimal mechanical strength, barrier properties, and antimicrobial activity; SEM, XRD, and inhibition assays confirmed uniform coating distribution and durable bacteriostasis. Preservation experiments showed it outperformed uncoated paper and single-layer CMCS-coated paper: it mitigated weight loss by 42%, retarded firmness deterioration, suppressed respiratory metabolism, retained pulp color, maintained higher total soluble solids (TSS) and lower titratable acidity (TA), and reduced rot index by 49%. The paper inhibited lipoxygenase (LOX) activity, restrained malondialdehyde (MDA) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) accumulation, and preserved superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, delaying senescence. It enabled 14-day ambient-temperature storage without excessive Mg 2+ migration into edible tissues. The ROS-releasing MgO 2 NPs/CMCS paper shows potential for cold-chain-free cantaloupe storage. Low-cost, scalable, biodegradable, it innovates preservation, enriching low-carbon packaging for carbon-neutral logistics.

title: Heat treatment effects on Jiuxiangchong sensory & components
Aroma deterioration during accelerated storage of sugar-free peach-flavored oolong tea: Key markers, degradation kinetics, and regulatory links between non-volatile and volatile components
abstract: Aroma deterioration critically limits the flavor stability of sugar-free fruit-flavored tea beverages, yet its chemical drivers remain poorly understood. In this study, a ready-to-drink oolong tea was subjected to accelerated storage at four temperatures and analyzed by headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), odor activity value (OAV), partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), kinetic modeling, correlation analysis, and Gaussian calculations. Ten key aroma deterioration markers were screened. After 90 d at 25 °C, tea polyphenols, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), and epicatechin gallate (ECG) retained 68.7%, 59.3%, and 64.5% of their initial levels, respectively. The Logistic kinetic models showed good fits (Radj 2 > 0.96) for all selected aroma markers, with cis-3-hexenyl acetate being the most temperature-sensitive marker. EGCG and ECG exhibited stronger independent associations with late-stage aroma modifiers than total polyphenols. Gaussian calculations further suggested EGCG forms thermodynamically favorable non-covalent interactions with representative aroma compounds. These findings provide marker-level evidence into flavor deterioration in sugar-free fruit-flavored teas.

title: Mycotoxins and plant alkaloids in plant-based protein foods and meat alternatives: Occurrence, exposure and risk assessment
abstract: Plant-based protein-rich foods and meat alternatives are increasingly used as substitutes or supplements to animal-based products. Despite their potential nutritional and environmental benefits, data on their contamination with natural toxins remain limited, particularly for plant alkaloids. In this study, 57 mycotoxins, 16 tropane alkaloids and 32 pyrrolizidine alkaloids were analysed in 101 plant-based protein samples, including protein isolates/concentrates, extruded products, veggie burgers and other meat alternatives, using U-HPLC-HRMS/MS. Twenty-five mycotoxins and eight alkaloids were quantified, with enniatins and Alternaria mycotoxins being the most prevalent. The highest concentrations reached 2800 μg/kg for tenuazonic acid and 890 μg/kg for deoxynivalenol. Atropine and scopolamine were most frequently detected plant alkaloids, with maximum levels in soybeans reaching 33 and 12 μg/kg, respectively. Risk assessment identified extruded soy-based products, veggie burger mixes and rice proteins as major contributors to natural toxin exposure, with elevated risks for aflatoxin B1, Alternaria toxins and atropine/scopolamine, particularly in children.

title: Glassy state physical stability versus vitamin B2 chemical stability in saccharide-modulated, freeze-dried corn starch matrices
abstract: This study examined saccharide effects on physical stability and vitamin B 2 retention in corn starch matrices with restricted glassy state mobility. Vitamin B 2 was selected for its susceptibility to light and moisture. Matrices containing glucose, sucrose, raffinose, or stachyose were gelatinized and freeze-dried. Water sorption isotherms and glass transition temperature (T g )-water relationships were modeled using Guggenheim-Anderson-de Boer (GAB) model and Gordon-Taylor equation, respectively. Among the saccharide-containing matrices, T g increased with saccharide molecular size, whereas the monolayer moisture content generally decreased from glucose to stachyose. Combined GAB and Gordon-Taylor analysis showed that raffinose- and stachyose-containing matrices remained glassy state over a wider water activity range at 25 °C than glucose- and sucrose-containing matrices, consistent with microscopy and X-ray diffraction results. Vitamin B 2 stability under humid and light stress did not strictly follow T g trends, indicating that T g predicts moisture-induced physical changes but not vitamin B 2 stability alone.

title: Ca2+-mediated free radical grafting of whey protein with ferulic acid: Physicochemical characterization and antagonistic effects on lead toxicity
abstract: Developing safe and effective dietary interventions to enhance lead (Pb) elimination and mitigate Pb-induced tissue damage is of considerable public health significance. This study prepared a calcium ion-mediated whey protein-ferulic acid (WP-FA) covalent complex via an ascorbic acid‑hydrogen peroxide radical-initiated system, aiming to improve FA stability and bioactivity and investigate its anti-Pb toxicity efficacy. Ca 2+ significantly regulated the grafting rate and structural characteristics of the complex. Optimal WP-FA covalent complex with the highest grafting amount, smallest particle size, and best stability was obtained under 4 mmol/L Ca 2+ supplementation. In vitro simulated digestion showed that the complex possesses satisfactory Pb-chelating capacity. Therefore, the optimized WP/FA-4 conjugate was chosen in vivo validations. Mice were exposed to Pb from day 1 to day 7, followed by a 14-day intervention period. The animals were euthanized on days 14 and 21 respectively for sampling. This covalent complex reduced Pb accumulation in blood, liver, kidneys, and brain, while mitigating Pb-induced weight loss, organ damage, and cognitive impairment. Mechanistically, these protective effects might be related to the alleviation of tissue oxidative stress and regulation of metal transporters expression by WP-FA. These findings highlight the important role that Ca 2+ plays in augmenting the WP-FA covalently binding properties, providing theoretical support for modifying protein-polyphenol complexes and preventing food-derived Pb toxicity.

title: An integrated strategy to obtain ready-to-use carotenoid extract from persimmon (Diospyros kaki Thunb.) using hydrophobic eutectic solvents: From virtual COSMO-SAC screening to atomistic level mechanism
abstract: Persimmon carotenoids are valuable, but the preparation suffers from the abuse of organic solvents, while the emergence of hydrophobic eutectic solvents (HESs) provides a feasible means to obtain ready-to-use extracts. This study developed an integrated strategy for the preparation and preservation of persimmon carotenoid extract using food-compatible HESs without solvent removal. Profiling identified 42 carotenoids (139.2 μg/g) in persimmon powder, with over 85% existing as esterified forms. Menthol and ethyl hexanoate (molar ratio of 1:1) were selected as the optimal HES via COSMO-SAC high-throughput virtual screening and experimental validation. The dissolution behavior of carotenoids in HESs was regulated by van der Waals interaction and hydrogen-bond anchoring, as evidenced by molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, the artificial neural network-genetic algorithm showed alternative potential to response surface methodology in the modeling and optimization of extraction process. The established strategy provides a referenceable means for the rational design and mechanistic analysis of phytochemical extraction.

title: Lattice-matched SnS/SnIn4S8 heterojunction-based molecularly imprinted photoelectrochemical sensor for tetracycline detection in milk
abstract: Tetracycline residues in milk pose potential food safety risks, highlighting the need for sensitive and selective analytical methods. In this work, we developed a molecularly imprinted photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor based on a lattice-matched SnS/SnIn 4 S 8 heterojunction. The ultralow lattice mismatch (0.33%) promotes efficient charge separation and migration, producing a markedly enhanced photocurrent response (2.81 μA·cm -2 ), up to 3.6 times the responses of the individual components. Coupling the heterojunction with molecular imprinting yielded a signal-off PEC sensing platform, and machine-learning-assisted optimization further improved its analytical performance. The sensor achieved a wide linear range (1 × 10 -4 - 1 × 10 2 μmol·L -1 ) and a low detection limit (2.43 × 10 -4 μmol·L -1 ), with reliable performance in real milk samples. These results identify lattice-matched heterointerface engineering as an effective strategy for regulating carrier transport and enhancing PEC signals, providing a general framework for high-performance analytical sensing.

title: Fermentation of Chlorella vulgaris by Stropharia rugosoannulata: An approach for improved aroma and bioactivity
abstract: Chlorella vulgaris is a nutrient-rich microalga whose broader application is limited by its undesirable aroma characteristics. To improve its sensory quality, commercial C. vulgaris powder was fermented with 20 edible Basidiomycota. Stropharia rugosoannulata was identified as the most effective strain for aroma improvement. Sensory evaluation revealed reduced green and earthy while enhanced fruity notes after submerged fermentation, which were associated with decreased pyrazines and the biosynthesis of ethyl esters, including ethyl 2-methylpropanoate, ethyl butanoate, ethyl 2-methylbutanoate, and ethyl hexanoate. In addition, fermented C. vulgaris exhibited enhanced anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)-stimulated vascular endothelial EA.hy926 cells. Peptidomic analysis suggested that these bioactivities are attributed to the formation of fermentation-specific bioactive peptides, along with increased abundance of pre-existing peptides. Further, fermented C. vulgaris showed no increased cytotoxicity in HepG2 cells. Overall, fermentation with S. rugosoannulata effectively improved the aroma and bioactivity of C. vulgaris without compromising cellular safety.

title: Synergistic pore size screening and dual time window kinetics: machine learning-based discrimination and concentration prediction of different types of preservatives in complex food matrices
abstract: Distinguishing between different preservatives is of great significance in quality control. Therefore, developing effective methods to distinguish between them is of great importance. This study overcomes the limitation of traditional sensor arrays that identify only a single analyte. Through the synergistic integration of pore size screening, metal doping, and machine learning, this system achieves multi-category discrimination of different preservatives, with a minimum discrimination concentration of 150 nM. With the optimal pore size effect of the ZIF-8 nanozyme and a dual-window reaction analysis strategy, its anti-interference capability and discrimination performance are significantly enhanced. Adsorption kinetics and electron paramagnetic resonance experiments reveal the mechanism underlying the discrimination between different preservatives. Furthermore, by integrating machine learning models, the system enables both concentration-independent identification and concentration regression through model switching. The proposed detection model exhibits good discrimination performance in real sample matrices.

title: From bioactive chemistry to packaging function: a structure-interaction-release framework for sustainable food packaging
abstract: Bioactive materials offer a promising route to sustainable food packaging with antimicrobial, antioxidant, enzymatic, probiotic, and sensing functions; however, their performance cannot be predicted from intrinsic bioactivity alone. This review establishes a Bioactive-Matrix-Structure-Release-Function (BMSRF) framework linking bioactive chemistry and molecular interactions with matrix architecture, transport behavior, functional efficacy, and food-preservation outcomes. Particular emphasis is placed on the transition from bioactivity to bioavailability and ultimately bioefficacy at the food-packaging interface. Across natural extracts, essential oils, probiotics, enzymes, and nanomaterials, the review identifies interconnected trade-offs among activity, stability, retention, release, mechanical integrity, and barrier performance, interpreting these relationships as design constraints rather than isolated limitations. Based on these relationships, rational design rules are proposed for matching bioactive chemistry, matrix architecture, and release kinetics to food environments and preservation targets. Emerging approaches including advanced encapsulation, stimuli-responsive systems, predictive modeling, and AI-assisted formulation are discussed toward predictive and scalable sustainable packaging design.

title: Integrated abundance analysis and artificial intelligence-assisted screening reveal novel antihypertensive milk-derived tripeptides
abstract: Milk consumption has been associated with reduced blood pressure, yet most studies have focused on a limited number of peptides, such as IPP and VPP. Here, we evaluated the antihypertensive effect of a single serving of milk in spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) and developed an integrated computational-experimental framework to identify milk-derived tripeptides with potential bioactivity. Major milk proteins were subjected to in silico gastrointestinal digestion to generate a virtual tripeptide library. Artificial intelligence-assisted structural modeling of angiotensin-converting enzyme-tripeptide interactions, combined with bioinformatic screening and peptide abundance analysis, was used to prioritize candidates with predicted bioactivity and physiological relevance. A total of seven selected tripeptides were further validated by molecular docking and in vivo assays. Several candidates significantly reduced systolic blood pressure in SHRs, with EIV, VAL, and SEE showing effects comparable to IPP. This approach provided an effective strategy for identifying physiologically relevant antihypertensive peptides from complex food proteins.

title: Compositional, structural, thermal, and microstructural modifications in black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens) proteins induced by alkaline pulsed electric field-assisted extraction
abstract: This study aimed to determine how alkaline pulsed electric field-assisted extraction modulates the compositional, molecular, colloidal, thermal, and microstructural properties of black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) proteins. Defatted BSFL powder was extracted under alkaline conditions and subjected to pulsed electric field treatments at electric field strengths of 1.25-3 kV/cm and 50-250 pulses. Protein fractions were characterised for composition, structure, colloidal behaviour, thermal properties, and microstructure using amino acid analysis, circular dichroism, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, zeta potential, differential scanning calorimetry, thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and particle size analysis. Crude protein content remained relatively stable, from 56.86 to 57.92 g/100 g. In contrast, pulsed electric-field treatment induced clear intensity-dependent changes in protein composition and structure. Thermal transitions shifted markedly, with onset temperatures ranging from 51.62 to 75.59 °C and enthalpy increasing from 0.65 to 1.17 J/g. Zeta potential remained negative, while circular dichroism, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction confirmed molecular reorganisation. Microstructural and particle-size changes further demonstrated the treatment effects. Alkaline pulsed electric field-assisted extraction can therefore generate black soldier fly larvae protein ingredients with distinct structural, colloidal, and thermal characteristics.

title: Heat-induced homogeneous dispersion–cold setting assembly strategy to construct tea polyphenols-starch functionalized hydrogel for encapsulation and controlled release of curcumin
abstract: In this study, guided by the enthalpy-entropy co-driven binding mechanism between amylose (AM) and tea polyphenols (TPs), a pH-enzyme dual-responsive controlled-release system, corn starch (CS)-TPs hydrogel-encapsulated curcumin (Cur@CS-TPs), was designed and constructed through a heat-induced homogeneous dispersion-cold setting assembly strategy. The direct use of gel precursor solution achieved a Cur embedding efficiency approaching 100% without organic solvents, ensuring operational simplicity and improved environmental sustainability. TPs and AM formed hydrophobic micro-regions through non-covalent interactions, inducing Cur self-assembly into an amorphous state, which significantly enhanced its encapsulation efficiency and solubility. In vitro release studies revealed minimal gastric release as well as sustained and targeted release in the small intestine, demonstrating pH-enzyme dual responsiveness. Furthermore, TPs endowed the hydrogel with antioxidant activity and retarded its digestion, contributing to a reduced glycemic index. The CS-TPs hydrogel represents a multifunctional delivery system that effectively stabilizes Cur and enhances its bioaccessibility.

title: Molecular interactions of gallic acid, epigallocatechin gallate, and tannic acid with pea protein during high-moisture extrusion: Impact on meat analogue quality
abstract: To provide a deep insight into the regulatory mechanism of polyphenols on the quality of plant-based meat analogues, molecular interactions between pea protein isolate and different phenolic compounds (gallic acid (GA), epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), and tannic acid (TA)) during high-moisture extrusion were investigated. TA led to the greatest reductions in surface hydrophobicity and highest increases in β-sheet structures, promoting the formation of the extrudate with highest chewiness (477.63 mJ) and anisotropy index (1.56). EGCG enhanced the disulfide bonding, leading to the highest springiness (3.46 mm) and cooking yield (174.47%). GA showed limited effects on protein structural changes and product qualities. Molecular docking revealed that these polyphenols mainly bound to PPI via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, with the binding affinity following the order of TA > EGCG > GA. These findings provide a scientific basis for the targeted selection of phenolic compounds as natural functional modifiers for meat analogues.

title: Albumin from bovine serum-prepared fluorescent hydrogel for real-time monitoring of H2S and food freshness
abstract: In this work, A fluorescent intelligent label (BE-P) was prepared for real-time monitoring of food freshness by grafting an H₂S-sensitive small-molecule fluorescent probe (NP-H₂S) onto a hydrogel cross-linked with bovine serum albumin (BSA) and ethylene glycol diglycidyl ether (EGDE). The results indicated that the addition of NP-H 2 S had no significant effect on the properties of BE-P, and the BE-P exhibited thermal stability and mechanical properties. Impressively, BE-P demonstrated good color stability, storage stability, and high sensitivity to H 2 S gas (LOD: 5.5 ppb). Additionally, BE-P was successfully used to monitor the freshness of pork, beef, and shrimp at 4°C and 25°C with satisfactory results. Moreover, the color changes in the BE-P correlated with changes in total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) and total viable count (TVC) in the food samples (R 2 > 0.97). Therefore, the developed intelligent label provides new insights for the development of multi-marker activated multicolor fluorescent intelligent labels.

title: Simultaneous determination of 13 thermo-induced endogenous contaminants in black and green tea based on a split-flow SPE strategy coupled with UPLC-MS/MS analysis
abstract: A rapid and sensitive UPLC-MS/MS method was developed for the simultaneous determination of 13 thermo-induced endogenous contaminants in black and green tea, including acrylamide, 4-methylimidazole, and 11 heterocyclic aromatic amines. To overcome matrix complexity and analyte differences, a two-step extraction combined with a split-flow polymeric cation-exchange (PCX) solid-phase extraction(SPE) procedure was optimised. The method achieved satisfactory linearity (R 2 > 0.9988), limits of quantitation (0.005-0.02 mg/kg), and recoveries (71.7%-118.7%) with acceptable intra-day and inter-day RSDs (<19.6%). The validated method was applied to analyse 20 commercial tea samples from China and Japan. The detection rates of 4-methylimidazole, acrylamide, harman, and norharman were 100.0%, 40.0%, 60.0%, and 70.0%, with detected levels ranging from 0.048 mg/kg to 1.449 mg/kg, 0.023 mg/kg to 0.671 mg/kg, 0.005 mg/kg to 0.167 mg/kg, and 0.006 to 0.243 mg/kg. This study provides an effective solution for monitoring multi-class TECs, supporting quality control and safety assurance in tea production.

title: Comprehensive profiling unveils insights into cultivar-depending correlations of volatile substances to postharvest quality resistance of fresh hot peppers by microbiomics integrated with metabomics
abstract: Hot peppers are much preferred for preparing cuisine or seasoning. However, decay poses considerable losses of fresh peppers after harvest. In this study, difference of resistance against postharvest decay of six cultivar fresh hot peppers was evaluated, and causing pathogenic fungi were identified. Epiphytic and endophytic fungal communities, and volatile organic compounds of pepper cultivars were characterized by microbiomics integrated with metabolomics. Results indicated that 'Xiaomijiao' and 'Erjingtiao', identified as disease-resistant cultivars, exhibit distinct microbial community compositions compared to susceptible cultivars, with differences in community evenness and co-occurrence patterns. Cultivar-depending correlation of key volatile substances to disease resistance of fresh peppers was comprehensively profiled. (E)-2-hexenal was proved highly associated with the resistance of cultivars, but negatively correlated the infections by Colletotrichum jasminigenum and Colletotrichum truncatum. The results association novel insights into understanding fruit resistance and would provide a promising approach for the control of postharvest decay of fresh hot peppers.

title: A comparative multi-omics dissection of alcoholic fermentation dynamics of island-grown and coast-grown Marselan wines
abstract: Islands and coasts exhibit distinct microclimatic characteristics that influence wine production; however, the differences in constituents produced during alcoholic fermentation under these specific microclimatic conditions remain unclear. To address this, the differences in inorganic and organic constituents between island-grown and coast-grown Marselan wines during alcoholic fermentation were investigated using a multi-omics approach. Among 32 volatile compounds with variable importance in projection (VIP) > 1, alcohols (15 compounds) were the primary discriminators. Potassium (VIP = 4.79) was strongly associated with coast-grown wine on day 3, whereas sodium (VIP = 1.26) was closely linked to island-grown wine at the same time point. Among the top 15 non-volatile metabolites with VIP > 1, eight were organic acids, which served as the primary discriminant metabolites. These findings highlight compositional differences between island-grown and coast-grown Marselan wines during alcoholic fermentation, providing a scientific basis for precise fermentation control and enhanced wine quality.

title: Monitoring tropane alkaloids in plant-based beverages using μSPEed® strong cation exchange ordered mesoporous silica cartridges
abstract: This study introduces a novel miniaturized method using μSPEed® and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS) for the extraction and purification of atropine and scopolamine in plant-based beverages. The approach employs a sorbent of SM-type ordered mesoporous silica functionalized with sulfonic acid groups, packaged for the first time in a miniaturized format. Validation followed Regulation (EU) 2023/2783, demonstrating excellent performance: recoveries (91–105%), precision (RSD ≤19%), linearity (R 2 ≥ 0.996), low quantification limits (0.06–0.4 μg/L), slight matrix effect, and proper selectivity. Analysis of 26 commercial samples purchased in Spain revealed contamination in 21 samples. Millet-based beverages, a previously unstudied matrix, showed the highest combined levels of atropine and scopolamine (1.2 μg/L), followed by oat-based (1.1 μg/L) and spelt-based beverages (0.83 μg/L). Maximum concentrations reached 0.80 μg/L for atropine and 1.03 μg/L for scopolamine, highlighting the need for legal limits to improve food safety.

title: LhSiase1-catalyzed transglycosylation: unlocking the bioactive potential of bird's nest fragments for sialylated oligosaccharides synthesis
abstract: Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) comprise a diverse array of structurally complex glycans, among which 3'-sialyllactose (3'-SL) is a predominant bioactive sialylated oligosaccharide. In this study, a novel sialidase LhSiase1 from Lactobacillus helsingborgensis was characterized and applied in a one-pot hydrolysis-transglycosylation process to produce 3'-SL from cost-effective glycoprotein sources. LhSiase1 showed optimal activity at 45 °C and pH 5.0, and demonstrated efficient transglycosylation with a hydrolysis/transglycosylation ratio (R H/T ) of 2.27, converting sialic acid from casein glycomacropeptide (cGMP) into 3'-SL with a yield of 4.17 mg/mL. Importantly, it also transformed high-molecular-weight sialylglycoproteins from edible bird's nest fragments into 3'-SL at a yield of 2.28 mg/mL, thereby enhancing their bioavailability and potential for nutritional uptake. Furthermore, a practical instant powder formulation was developed, enabling equipment-free, in-situ 3'-SL synthesis upon hydration. This ready-to-use strategy offers a scalable route to produce bioactive 3'-SL for functional foods and nutraceuticals aimed at improving human health.

title: Effects of seasoning matrices on umami peptides: molecular insights into mechanisms of umami perception
abstract: This study investigated how pH, salt, and sugar regulate the conformation and umami perception of LEADLVH using response surface optimization, sensory evaluation, spectroscopic analyses, and molecular dynamics simulations. Seasoning matrices enhanced umami perception by modulating peptide conformation, with the optimal combination of pH 7.01, 0.58% salt, and 0.40% sugar increasing umami intensity by 62.45%. Under these conditions, β-sheet content decreased from 45.45% to 36.12%, while α-helix and random coil contents increased from 17.61% and 13.58% to 23.05% and 17.75%, respectively, indicating a more extended and flexible conformation. This structural rearrangement was driven by pH-induced deprotonation, salt-mediated electrostatic shielding, and sugar-induced disruption of hydrogen-bond networks, thereby strengthening peptide-receptor interactions and improving binding free energy from -53.07 to -83.32 kcal/mol. In the ternary seasoning matrix (PSSu; pH 7.01, 0.58% salt, 0.40% sugar), Ser122, Asp144, Asp254, Tyr172, and Ser100 were the major favorable energetic contributors.

title: A sodium alginate-dual-protein double-network gel based on whey protein isolate and Tiger nut protein: Preparation, characterization and its sustained release properties of curcumin
abstract: This study developed a sodium alginate-tiger nut protein/whey protein isolate double-network gel, and its sustained-release properties for curcumin were investigated. A series of sodium alginate (SA) concentrations (0-0.3%) were screened, and 0.25% SA was determined as the optimal level, which yielded superior gel hardness (401.67 ± 16.04 g) and water-holding capacity (81.49 ± 1.96%). Structural characterizations verified a double-network structure formation: one relied on protein aggregation, while the secondary network was formed via calcium ions-mediated cross-linking of SA. Owing to the dual-crosslinked network structure, the optimized gel containing 0.25% SA achieved a high curcumin encapsulation efficiency of 93.08 ± 3.05%, and improved the stability of encapsulated curcumin against light, heat, and long-term storage. In vitro gastrointestinal digestion tests demonstrated that the composite gel effectively shielded curcumin from gastric degradation and realized sustained intestinal release. This double network gel exhibits great promise as a carrier for bioactive compound delivery.

title: Dietary zinc oxide nanoparticles alter tissue-specific shifts in fatty acid and amino acid profiles but do not affect meat quality or targeted rumen bacteria in Haemonchus contortus-infected lambs
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs; 99 mg/kg concentrate) on tissue fatty acid and amino acid profiles, zinc concentrations in meat and liver, meat quality, and selected rumen bacterial taxa in lambs experimentally infected with Haemonchus contortus. Twenty-four lambs were assigned in a factorial design based on infection status and ZnONP supplementation and fed experimental diets for 40 days. ZnONPs induced tissue- and infection-dependent changes in selected fatty acids and amino acids, particularly in rumen fluid, serum, liver, and adipose tissue, whereas muscle composition and physicochemical meat quality remained largely unchanged. ZnONPs did not increase total zinc concentrations in meat or liver tissues. Targeted qPCR revealed only small taxon-specific differences, without broad modulation of the targeted rumen bacterial populations. Overall, ZnONPs altered selected fatty acid and amino acid profiles across tissues without substantially affecting meat quality, tissue zinc concentration, or targeted rumen bacteria.

title: Integrated multi-sensor tracking and metabolomics uncover transport environmental stress and metabolic mechanisms in leopard coral grouper (Plectropomus leopardus)
abstract: Maintaining the quality and physiological stability of high-value live seafood during transport remains challenging. This study investigated the effects of transport time and temperature on water-quality dynamics, oxidative stress, and serum metabolism in leopard coral grouper (Plectropomus leopardus). Progressive acidification was a major environmental change during transport. Prolonged transport increased MDA and altered serum enzyme activities, whereas 16 °C alleviated oxidative stress and hepatic injury. Integration of continuous water-quality measurements with serum responses identified final-30-min pH and low-level dissolved oxygen (10th percentile) as complementary environmental indicators (R 2 = 0.749), while MDA, GSH-Px, and ALT were selected as representative serum indicators (R 2 = 0.817). Metabolomic analysis showed that low-temperature transport attenuated metabolic disturbances, whereas prolonged transport altered creatine, histamine, and palmitic acid, mainly involving arginine and proline metabolism and glycerophospholipid metabolism. These results provide a basis for characterizing transport stress and optimizing pre-slaughter handling of high-value live seafood.

title: Intelligent De novo Design of Multifunctional Taste Peptides via an integrated deep learning, conditional diffusion, and reinforcement learning platform
abstract: Taste peptides from dietary proteins elicit taste sensations and have reported bioactivities, but their rational prioritization remains hampered by the limited throughput of conventional screening. Here, we describe a multi-stage computational workflow for de novo prioritization of multifunctional taste peptides, combining multi-task benchmarking, conditional diffusion sequence generation, feature-space novelty filtering, and PPO-based sequence optimization. A multi-label dataset of 4801 experimentally reported peptides was assembled from BIOPEP-UWM, MBPDB, FermFooDb, and published taste-peptide benchmark sets. The best-performing classifiers achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values of 0.923 (umami), 0.872 (bitter), 0.828 (ACE-inhibitory), and 0.807 (antioxidant), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals estimated for each task. Conditional diffusion yielded 9401 unique candidates after validity filtering and deduplication. Novelty-aware filtering and an independently optimized PPO policy were compared using the same composite reward. The novelty score used for ranking is a Euclidean feature-space distance rather than a flow-matching likelihood. All outputs are presented as computational priorities for synthesis and experimental validation, not as measured activities.

title: Robust triazine-based COF membrane for efficient enrichment and ultrasensitive determination of veterinary antibiotics from complex animal-derived food
abstract: The cost-effective pretreatment and ultrasensitive determination of multiple antibiotic residues from complex animal-derived food are imperative, yet cumbersome. Herein, a novel triazine-based covalent organic framework (TpTAPT) film was assembled and employed as the robust solid phase microextraction (SPME) membrane for efficient enrichment of veterinary antibiotics, including sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, and macrolides. With multiple functional groups, distinct surface charge distribution and hydrophobicity, TpTAPT membrane demonstrated superior enrichment performance for representative antibiotics than commercial SPME fibers (6.1-213.1 times) and membranes (1.1-167.6 times), and exhibited excellent anti-interference capacity with recoveries of 80.6-110% in complex matrix. Therefore, it was integrated with LC-MS/MS to establish an ultrasensitive method for the trace analysis of antibiotics in milk and dried meat products, with detected concentration low to 5.7 ng/L, satisfactory recoveries (80.3-119.8%) and low RSDs < 9.4%. The developed TpTAPT membrane-SPME protocol provided a reliable and practical approach for veterinary antibiotic determination, highlighting its potential in food analysis.

title: Chain length-dependent antioxidant activity of phosphatidylcholine complexes of alkyl gallates in fish oil and emulsions: a reverse micelle interfacial mechanism
abstract: In bulk oils, phosphatidylcholine (PC) and trace water form reverse-micelle interfaces that concentrate hydroperoxides and pro-oxidant metals, promoting oxidation. PC complexes of gallic acid and selected C1-C16 alkyl gallates were evaluated in fish oil and emulsions. Activity peaked at C2 (ethyl gallate-PC, EG-PC) and C12 (dodecyl gallate-PC, DG-PC) rather than changing progressively with chain length. After accelerated oxidation, EG-PC and DG-PC showed the lowest peroxide values (25.27 and 24.53 mmol/kg oil) and TBARS values (7.00 and 6.89 mg MDA/kg oil), while preserving polyunsaturated fatty acids and suppressing aldehyde formation. Spectroscopy supported complexation, whereas cryo-TEM, CLSM, and SAXS supported reverse-micelle formation. We propose that PC anchors gallates at this interface, the short-chain EG-PC localizes near the hydrophilic region to quench aqueous-phase initiators, whereas the long-chain DG-PC partitions into the lipophilic region to intercept chain-propagating radicals. In emulsions, excess PC micelles further relocate DG-PC to the interface, enhancing its efficacy.

title: Tetramodal saccharin (SAC) sensing with a novel Ba-MOF: Leveraging SAC-induced PET effect and enhanced photocatalytic oxidase-mimicking activity
abstract: A tetramodal sensing method for the sensitive and selective detection of saccharin (SAC) was developed using a novel Ba-MOF. The fluorescent Ba-MOF was prepared via a solvothermal reaction between Ba 2+ and 5,5'-(anthracene-9,10-diyl)diisophthalic acid (H 4 ADIP), and its single-crystal structure was unambiguously determined. Upon addition of SAC, the fluorescence of Ba-MOF was remarkably quenched, while its oxidase-like catalytic activity was significantly enhanced. This dual-response behavior enabled the establishment of a tetramodal sensing platform integrating fluorescence, colorimetric, photothermal and electrochemical detection. The sensor exhibited wide linear ranges, a low detection limit (58.50 nM), high selectivity and stability. Real sample analysis of Sprite, Coca-Cola and whipped cream using the standard addition method yielded recoveries of 93.40%-106.55% and RSD of 0.67%-4.87%. Mechanistic studies revealed that coordination of SAC to the Ba center reduced the band gap, enhancing oxidase-like activity, while photoinduced electron transfer (PET) from H 4 ADIP to SAC quenched the fluorescence.

title: Optimized extraction, enrichment, identification and pancreatic lipase inhibition of triterpenic acids from Ziziphus jujuba Mill
abstract: Jujube (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) is rich in bioactive triterpenic acids, but their efficient extraction and pancreatic lipase (PL) inhibition mechanisms remain unclear. Cellulase-assisted ultrasonic extraction was optimized, and the enriched fraction was purified, identified by UPLC-MS/MS, and assessed for PL inhibition by docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD). It afforded a yield of 48.52 ± 0.4 mg/g and purified-fraction purity of 75.82% ± 1.11%, with 14 triterpenic acids identified and eight monomers quantified. The fraction was a reversible mixed-type PL inhibitor, acting dose-dependently (IC₅₀ = 113.47 μg/mL); corosolic and maslinic acids were the most potent monomers, whereas 3-oxo monomers were far less active. Docking indicated stable binding within the PL hydrophobic pocket via hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions, while MD simulations further revealed why: the C3 hydroxyl acts as a hydrogen-bond donor maintaining the planar A-ring trans-conformation (circular SD ∼6°, R ∼ 0.995), whereas 3-oxo oxidation induces torsional distortion (31-45°) and weakens binding in a skeleton-dependent manner. This work thus enables efficient high-purity enrichment and, for the first time, unravels the PL inhibitory mechanism at static and dynamic levels, establishing the C3 hydroxyl as the key structural determinant and supporting these compounds as natural lipid-lowering ingredients.

title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon formation in duck patties: A comparative study of thermal processing methods with nutrient degradation analysis
abstract: This study compares four thermal processing methods (pan-frying PF, oven baking OB, air frying AF, microwave MW) on nutrient degradation and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) formation in duck patties. The fundamental reason for differences lies in heating media and heat transfer methods. PF uses direct metal pan heating, triggering intense lipid oxidation; thus protein/fat loss is highest, polyunsaturated fatty acids production is significantly higher (P < 0.05), and PAH formation is highest. OB relies on hot air radiation with lower thermal conductivity than PF, producing the second-highest PAH levels. AF uses high-speed hot air circulation, offering uniform heat transfer and relatively controllable lipid oxidation. In contrast, MW uses electromagnetic waves generating heat via friction of polar molecules (water, fat) in a relatively closed environment, significantly inhibiting PAH cyclization. MW reduces fat content, moderately hydrolyzes protein, and retains higher amino acids. PAH4 (the sum of benzo[a]pyrene, chrysene, benzo[b]fluoranthene, and benzo[a]anthracene) content is reduced by 62.78% compared to PF, especially benzo[b]fluoranthene formation. Overall, MW demonstrates superior performance in preserving nutritional value while reducing high-temperature harmful substances, providing a reference for nutrient preservation and thermal processing selection.

title: The effects of epigallocatechin gallate and resveratrol water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) emulsion on the physicochemical, functional and sensory properties of yogurt
abstract: The water-in-oil-in-water emulsion loaded with epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and resveratrol (RES) was applied to a yogurt system for nutritional enhancement, and the effects of adding different concentrations of emulsion on thissystem were discussed. Compared with pure yogurt, the presence of emulsion significantly improved the water holding capacity, storage stability, texture and antioxidant capacity. The improvement effect of 1% emulsion was optimal. The retention rate analysis showed that the retention rates of EGCG and RES in yogurt with 1% emulsion were the highest, 48% and 51%, respectively. Microstructural data showed that with an increase emulsion, resulted in aggregation, indicating an the existance of an optimum of emulsion concentration. Electronic nose and electronic tongue data showed that the introduction of emulsion reduced unfavorable flavor while retaining its original taste.

title: Chemical composition vs. sensory reality: Investigating smoke phenol interactions in red wine matrices
abstract: Perception is shaped not only by individual compound concentrations but by interactions within the matrix. Traditional approaches to aroma prediction have relied on odor activity values (OAVs), which compare compound concentrations to detection thresholds, but are increasingly seen as insufficient. This study uses red wine and volatile smoke phenols as a model system to investigate both orthonasal and retronasal perceptual behavior within a complex matrix. Controlled mixtures explored how concentration ratios influenced perceptual outcomes. Syringols showed no significant direct sensory impact, reinforcing their role as exposure markers rather than aroma contributors. Mixtures with identical total concentration but differing individual compounds did not differ in aroma quality, suggesting aroma masking or blending interactions. These findings emphasize the importance of matrix interactions in predicting perceptual outcomes from chemical data. This understanding of volatile phenol interactions enhances interpretability of analytical results and supports more informed decision-making for winemakers facing smoke events.

title: Alterations of Fusarium venenatum mycelium upon sequential processing mediate the interfacial behavior and emulsion stability
abstract: As a promising sustainable source of mycoprotein, Fusarium venenatum (F. venenatum) offers high protein content, and a well-balanced amino acid profile. Prior to food application, F. venenatum mycelium requires nucleic acid removal and sterilization for safety concern, which might induce structural changes including protein loss, polysaccharide enrichment, and potential thermal denaturation, therefore compromising its interfacial performance. Accordingly, this work systematically evaluated the impact of sequential processing on the functionalities of F. venenatum, with the protein content consistently decreased from 50.96% in the untreated group to 43.47% in the sterilized group. Atomic force microscopy revealed that native mycelium (MB) exhibited a smooth, intact morphology with uniform nanomechanical properties, whereas processed samples showed progressive surface roughening, structural flattening, and an increased mechanical heterogeneity. These structural and mechanical alterations directly influenced the interfacial behavior, where MB demonstrated superior interfacial activity by rapidly adsorbing to form a robust elastic layer with an equilibrium tension as low as 19.12 mN/m, while sterilized samples exhibited insufficient interfacial activity (20.13 mM/m). Consequently, MB-stabilized emulsions maintained exceptional stability across diverse environmental challenges, including 28-d storage, thermal treatment (up to 120 °C), and ionic strengths (up to 400 mM). However, sterilized mycelium most susceptible to coalescence, while nucleic acid-removed mycelium retained adequate functionality at elevated concentrations, achieving a minimum droplet size of 1.03 μm at 3% concentration. The findings revealed the inherent balance between food safety requirements and functional performance, providing a rational framework for optimizing downstream conditions to preserve emulsifying functionality of F. venenatum, and for developing of mycelium with lower nucleic acid content.

title: Effects of grilling process on the formation pattern of heterocyclic amines and advanced glycation end products and physicochemical quality of premade grilled grass carp fish blocks
abstract: This study found a temperature-dependent pattern in heterocyclic amines (HAs) and advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) formation, as well as the physicochemical quality attributes of pre-made grilled grass carp. Raising the center temperature from 50 °C to 80 °C increased total HAs by 20% and total AGEs (CML + CEL) by 107%. At grilling temperatures of 220-280 °C, HAs formation dominated, with tryptophan, glyoxal, and creatine/creatinine as key precursors. In contrast, AGE formation prevailed at 310 °C, primarily involving lysine and methylglyoxal. Notably, grilled fish skin contained only 23-39% of total HAs and 36-65% of AGEs found in flesh. Prolonged grilling increased hardness, chewiness, gumminess, and yellowness (b*) but reduced lightness (L*) and moisture content, the latter showing strong negative correlation with HAs (r = -0.89) and moderate correlation with AGEs (r = -0.51). These findings provide science-based guidance for optimizing grilling conditions to balance safety and quality.

title: CD-MOF-assisted phase transfer combined with SERS for rapid and eco-friendly detection of zearalenone in edible oil
abstract: An eco-friendly phase-transfer method based on cyclodextrin-metal-organic framework (CD-MOF) was developed to extract zearalenone (ZEN) from edible oil into aqueous phase. Leveraging this green pretreatment approach, a rapid surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) sensing platform was established for ZEN detection. CD-MOF possesses an amphiphilic structure, whose hydrophobic cavities can encapsulate ZEN to form host-guest complexes. The gradual structural collapse of CD-MOF leads to the release of ZEN into the aqueous phase, achieving efficient oil-to-water transfer with an extraction efficiency of 80-90%. Following this extraction method, SERS detection was achieved using cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB)-capped gold nanorods (Au NRs). The CTAB bilayer on the Au NR surface facilitates the adsorption of hydrophobic ZEN toward the plasmonic hotspots, significantly enhancing the Raman signal. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of CD-MOF extraction and Au NRs-based SERS enhancement, rapid detection of ZEN in corn oil was achieved with performance comparable to that of conventional high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC).

title: From waste to structure: valorisation of agro-industrial byproducts as functional inducers of low-methoxyl pectin gelation
abstract: Low-methoxyl (LM) and amidated low-methoxyl (LMA) pectins are widely used as calcium-responsive hydrocolloids in reduced-sugar foods and edible materials. However, their gelation still relies largely on purified calcium salts and refined co-solutes, while the structuring potential of agro-industrial side streams remains poorly integrated within a unified mechanistic framework. This review proposed that these streams should be understood as multifunctional gelation inducers, co-inducers, or modifiers whose effects arise from their mineral, sugar, organic-acid, protein, polyphenol, and polysaccharide composition. Their functionality is examined through four principal mechanisms: ion donation and competition, regulation of pH and ionic strength, control of water activity and molecular crowding, and promotion of secondary interactions or co-gelation. Evidence from rheology, spectroscopy, microscopy, and molecular modelling is integrated to connect side-stream composition and processing history with junction-zone formation, network heterogeneity, viscoelasticity, water retention, and product performance. The review further examined how these composition-structure-property relationships can guide the selection and standardisation of molasses, vinasse, whey permeate, fruit-pomace extracts, and related streams for food structuring. Gelation performance is subsequently connected with safety, sensory acceptability, process scalability, life-cycle assessment, and techno-economic feasibility. This mechanism-driven framework will provide a basis for moving from empirical side-stream incorporation towards predictive formulation strategies for multifunctional and potentially lower-impact LM/LMA pectin systems.

title: Multi-omics and network pharmacology reveal aroma, metabolite, and antioxidant diversity in freeze-dried fruits
abstract: Despite the wide market diversity of freeze-dried fruit products, systematic multi-omics comparisons across different fruit types remain limited. Herein, integrated volatilomics and untargeted metabolomics were employed to systematically evaluate the chemical and functional diversity of eight representative freeze-dried fruits. Significant inter-specific differences were observed in volatile profiles, metabolite compositions, and antioxidant capacities. Green orange exhibited the highest diversity and total content of volatile compounds (∼1.4-7.0 times higher than others), whereas jackfruit displayed the highest ester abundance. Metabolomics identified 941 non-volatile metabolites, including 134 differential metabolites predominantly linked to lipid, amino acid, carbohydrate, and phenylpropanoid metabolism. All fruits demonstrated notable antioxidant capacities, with green orange exhibiting the strongest potential, which highly correlated with its abundant phenolic accumulation. Network pharmacology revealed 26 key antioxidants predicted to act synergistically, particularly targeting AKT1 and potentially regulating the PI3K/Akt pathway. These findings provide a comprehensive framework for evaluating freeze-dried fruit quality and offer valuable guidance for raw material selection, product development, and value-added utilization in the freeze-dried fruit industry.

title: Effect of hypobaric with nitric oxide fumigation on flavor compound retention in postharvest ‘Xiaobai’ apricots
abstract: This study explored the effects of hypobaric treatment combined with nitric oxide fumigation (HYT-NO) on apricot postharvest quality and flavor metabolism. HYT-NO tended to show better storage quality than the control and individual treatments. To further investigate the observed quality difference, electronic nose, HS-SPME-GC-MS, and GC-O-MS were employed to characterize sensory attributes and volatile profiles of control and HYT-NO treated fruit. HYT-NO treatment partially suppress sensor responses associated with undesirable volatiles. Among the 918 VOCs identified, terpenoids and esters predominated. HYT-NO also mitigated late-stage losses of key volatiles (eg. Linalool, d-limonene), and enrichment of monoterpenoid biosynthesis metabolites suggested a possible link to aroma retention, meriting further validation. GC-O-MS analysis further suggested linalool, hexanal, and 2-hexenal as potential core flavor contributors. Collectively, these findings suggest that HYT-NO may help preserve desirable apricot flavor during storage, highlighting its potential as a postharvest preservation strategy.

title: The synergistic evolution of structural characteristics and interfacial behavior in the Maillard reaction process regulated the emulsifying properties of flaxseed globulin-flaxseed gum conjugates
abstract: Flaxseed globulin (FG), the predominant protein in flaxseed, exhibits suboptimal emulsifying properties that limit its food applications. The Maillard-driven glycation with polysaccharides offers a promising strategy to enhance protein functionality. This study elucidated the dynamic structural changes, interfacial behavior, and emulsifying properties of flaxseed globulin (FG)-flaxseed gum (FSG) conjugates. Covalent grafting between FG and FSG was confirmed by grafting degree and SDS-PAGE. The conjugates exhibited reduced particle size (206.33 ± 3.86 nm), increased absolute zeta potential (25.53 ± 0.43 mV) and enhanced solubility (76.48 ± 0.58%). Protein unfolding introduced greater disorder (random coils increased by 47.20%) and conformational flexibility (57.99%). Decreased interfacial tension accelerated protein adsorption and rearrangement at the interface, promoting a thicker, more stable interfacial layer. Notably, FG-FSG-6 h demonstrated superior emulsifying properties (76.37 ± 0.93 m 2 /g, 20.16 ± 0.49 min). This study established a foundation for engineering high-performance flaxseed globulin-based emulsifiers.

title: Impact of proteolytic enzyme on the processing and sensory quality of dry-fermented hybrid analogs
abstract: Dry-fermented sausage analogs show low endogenous enzymatic activity compared to meat products, thus limiting their sensory quality. This study examined proteolysis, lipolysis and microbial interaction dynamics mediated by addition of exogenous proteases in analogs. Three hybrid analogs prepared using texturized pea protein and gelled sunflower oil, one without protease (OG) and two with protease at two levels (OGP, OGPP), were produced and compared to a control (C). OG sausages showed higher level of volatiles from amino acid degradation, carbohydrate fermentation and esters, with distinct umami and animal odor, and similar texture to C. Protease modified the matrix structure and fermentation, increasing proteolysis, reducing lipolysis, and decreasing lipid-derived volatiles, mainly aldehydes. Protease also caused gummy texture and increased volatiles derived from ile, leu, val and phe. Protease addition buffered fermentation, affecting microbial and sensory traits. Starter culture and protease combinations were essential to ensure analog quality.

title: New insights into modifying structure and techno-functional properties of sesame protein: high-pressure homogenization coupled with pH-shifting
abstract: High-pressure homogenization (HPH) was investigated as a strategy to modify sesame protein isolate (SMPI) combined with pH shifting. SMPI was adjusted to pH 2.0, 7.0, and 11.0 and processed at 50, 100, or 150 MPa (1 cycle, 25 °C). HPH induced pH-dependent structural rearrangements that affected the techno-functional properties of SMPI. At pH 2.0, HPH at 150 MPa increased Ho by 131% and promoted random-coil structures, accompanied by changes in solubility (135%), EAI (43%) and WHC (21%), relative to its respective control., At 50 MPa/pH 7.0, structural rearrangements were reflected by changes in zeta potential, fluorescence, and secondary structure, resulting in improved OHC (108%) and EAI (67%), compared to the control. 150 MPa/pH 11.0 promoted β-sheet structure, solubility (178%), EAI (5%) and OHC (19%) increase relative to the control. Overall, HPH combined with pH-shifting offers a condition-dependent strategy for tailoring SMPI functionality for specific food applications.

title: Chitosan-polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel films containing polyphenols-encapsulated ZIF-8 for pH-responsive freshness monitoring and preservation of pork
abstract: We developed a biodegradable hydrogel-based packaging film from chitosan and polyvinyl alcohol. The film was integrated with epigallocatechin gallate, curcumin, or anthocyanins encapsulated in zeolitic imidazolate framework-8. Due to the synergistic effects between ZIF-8 and polyphenols, the films had enhanced mechanical strength, thermal stability, and barrier properties against water vapor and oxygen. The films also exhibited antibacterial and antioxidant activities and could inhibit microbial growth and lipid/protein oxidation in fresh pork during 9-day storage at 4 °C. Moreover, the incorporated polyphenols confer pH-responsive yellow and purple-red color change and controlled release, enabling real-time visual monitoring of pork freshness. Among all film variants, the PVA-CS-Cur@ZIF-8 had the best preservation performance. It could extend the shelf life of pork by 2-4 days and had superior biocompatibility (>85%) and soil degradability (80%). Overall, this work presents a sustainable and intelligent packaging hydrogel film that can act as a preservative material and freshness indicator.

title: Native granular resistant starch from New Zealand-grown avocado seeds: Structural, physicochemical, and digestive properties
abstract: Physicochemical, structural, and digestive properties of seed starches from ten New Zealand-grown avocado varieties were compared with potato and normal maize starches. Samples were characterized by microscopy, particle sizing, X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, size-exclusion chromatography, rheology, and digestion. The avocado seed starches contained smooth, oval-to-elongated granules with B-type crystallinity. Their relative crystallinity ranged from 25.9% to 29.5%, true amylose content from 26.3% to 32.8%, and the infrared absorbance ratio associated with short-range molecular order from 0.595 to 0.618. After 4 h of enzymatic digestion, the resistant starch fraction ranged from 52.15% in Hass to 76.68% in Reed, compared with 45.62% in potato starch and 17.64% in normal maize starch. Resistant starch was not significantly correlated with amylose content, crystallinity, or granule size. These results identify Reed as a promising source of native granular resistant starch and show that resistance reflects the combined organization of the granule.

title: Ultrasound-assisted citric acid treatment mitigates oxidative deterioration of oysters during frozen storage
abstract: This study investigated the effects of ultrasound-assisted citric acid (US+CA) treatments on the quality stability of oysters during frozen storage. Results showed that freezing induced pronounced deterioration in color, texture, water-holding capacity, and freshness, accompanied by lipid and protein oxidation. CA pretreatment partially alleviated these changes, while ultrasound further enhanced preservation efficacy. Among the tested conditions, US200+CA exhibited the best protective effect, maintaining physicochemical properties and suppressing volatile off-flavor formation and TVB-N accumulation. Lipidomic analysis showed improved retention of membrane phospholipids and polyunsaturated fatty acids, alongside reduced lipid oxidation. Similarly, protein oxidation markers, including carbonyls, Schiff bases, dityrosine, and disulfide bonds, were significantly reduced. Proteomic analysis revealed reduced oxidation frequency and fragmentation of key myofibrillar and cytoskeletal proteins under US+CA treatment. Overall, moderate ultrasound enhanced the antioxidant effectiveness of CA by coordinately regulating lipid and protein stability, providing mechanistic insight into oxidative control strategies for frozen oyster preservation.

title: Electron beam-induced structural modification enhances pea protein emulsion gels formed by transglutaminase‑calcium dual crosslinking
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI) has limited use in the food industry due to its poor solubility and gelation. This study used electron beam irradiation (EBI, 5-30 kGy) to treat PPI, followed by dual crosslinking with transglutaminase (TG) and/or CaCl 2 to prepare oil-in-water emulsion gels, aiming to optimize processing conditions for improved gelation properties. Moderate EBI (10-15 kGy, with 15 kGy showing the greatest overall improvement) promoted protein unfolding and increased surface hydrophobicity, water solubility (10.6% → 11.2%), and emulsifying activity index (15.9 → 25.6 m 2 /g). Dual crosslinking (TG + 25 mM Ca 2+ ) generated stronger, more elastic networks than single crosslinking, with higher water-holding capacity (80.7%), superior freeze-thaw stability, and higher viscoelasticity. EBI-treated PPI produced softer yet more hydrated gels. Excessive Ca 2+ (≥50 mM) or irradiation (20-30 kGy) increased protein aggregation and weakened gel strength. This combined physical-enzymatic crosslinking strategy allows tailoring of plant-based emulsion gels for specific food applications.

title: Transfer learning-assisted snapshot multispectral imaging for robust prediction of chemical components during black tea fermentation under different processing conditions
abstract: Rapid and accurate monitoring of key chemical constituents during black tea fermentation is crucial for quality control and process optimization. However, chemical and spectral heterogeneity caused by different processing conditions compromises the robustness of conventional spectroscopic calibration models. This study developed a transfer learning (TL)-assisted snapshot multispectral imaging framework for robust prediction of catechins, theaflavins, theabrownins, and thearubigins under different processing conditions. Three progressive fine-tuning strategies based on pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were designed to improve feature transferability. These models were evaluated across two withering conditions and an independent batch for external validation. Results showed that TL models improved prediction performance, with R p values increased by 0.47%-3.15% over retrained CNN models on the target domain, and maintained robust prediction on the external validation set. This study provides a transferable strategy to improve the robustness of spectroscopic analysis, enabling reliable chemical quantification across varying processing conditions during black tea fermentation.

title: Phase-dependent antioxidant behavior in a synthetic C-α-glucogallin analogue library by photoredox-mediated α-ketonylation
abstract: Phenolic acid glycosyl esters like glucogallins are promising antioxidants but are often limited by hydrolytically labile O-glycosidic linkages. Here, twelve C-α-glucogallin analogues were synthesized in six steps from commercial peracylated sugars by combining four monosaccharides with three plant-derived phenolic acids. Photoredox-enabled C-α-ketonylation furnished C-ketonyl sugars in 70-88% yield with high α-selectivity and aqueous stability over 120 h. Chemical and food-relevant antioxidant assays identified the protocatechuic acid derivatives 4ac-dc as the most active subset (70-99% activity) with marked phase-dependent sugar effects. Specifically, the most hydrophilic glucoside 4ac performed best in aqueous systems yet remained less active than V C , whereas the less polar rhamnoside 4dc was most effective in lipophilic models, with activity exceeding BHT, as indicated by a 2.1-fold lower IC 50 in the lipid peroxidation assay and greater protection against canola oil oxidation at 120 °C. Collectively, these findings highlight C-α-glucogallins as structurally tunable and highly effective antioxidants for lipid-rich foods.

title: The effect of root-applied glycinebetaine and nutrient cutoff on the sweetness, bitterness, and nutrient content of hydroponically grown lettuce during storage
abstract: Root-applied glycinebetaine (GB) is a novel method to enhance the edible quality of hydroponically grown lettuce. However, the effect of root-applied GB on lettuce postharvest quality is unknown. Here we compare the effect of root-applied GB and nutrient cutoff treatment on postharvest quality of lettuce. In nutrient cutoff treatments, the fertigation solution was replaced with tap water with or without GB. Hyperspectral imaging technique was used to investigate the visual quality. The contents of sugars, sesquiterpene lactones, nitrate, minerals, vitamin C, and GB were analyzed. Plants treated with root-applied GB or nutrient cutoff treatment showed higher content of sugars and lower content of nitrate during storage compared to plants treated with fertigation alone. No significant changes in visual quality were observed. GB persisted in lettuce leaves over 13 days. In conclusion, root-applied GB as well as nutrient cutoff treatment coincided with improved quality attributes relevant to consumer and lettuce shelf life.

title: Identification of key aroma compounds underlying three distinct aroma types of longan (Dimocarpus longan Lour.) fruit via integrated GC–MS, GC-olfactometry, and molecular docking
abstract: Longan fruit is renowned for its sweet aromatic flavor and nutrition; however, the essence of its aroma formation remains unclear. This study employed three cultivars with distinct aroma profiles-'Shixia' (SX), 'Lidongben' (LDB), and 'Xiangcui' (XC)-for sensory evaluation and volatile profiling throughout fruit development. Terpenoids and esters rapidly accumulated and dominated during fruit expansion. Integrating multivariate analysis, odor activity value (OAV) and GC-olfactometry (GC-O), this study first identified 19 characteristic aroma compounds and elucidated their biosynthetic pathways. Seven key compounds defining aroma types were distinguished: (E)-β-ocimene as a common background aroma contributed to fresh green scent of SX, linalool and methyl salicylate provided floral notes in LDB, while four ethyl esters imparted a winy aroma to XC. Molecular docking revealed spontaneous binding (-2.57 to -5.35 kcal/mol) of all key compounds to olfactory receptors. These findings clarify the chemical basis underlying aroma diversity in longan and support flavor quality improvement.

title: Co-production of gelatin, hydroxyapatite and calcium-binding peptides from Tilapia scales: Structural characteristics and physicochemical properties
abstract: A novel co-production strategy was developed to valorize tilapia scale waste into gelatin (TSG), hydroxyapatite (TSHA), and calcium-binding peptides. TSG was obtained by hot-water extraction, and the residues were calcined at 700 °C for 3 h to produce TSHA, which served as a self-prepared affinity medium. Alkaline protease hydrolysis yielded the highest calcium-binding capacity (CBC, 4.86 μg/mg). After TSHA-based affinity purification, the recovered fraction (THAC) showed improved CBC (5.71 μg/mg). Isothermal titration calorimetry suggested spontaneous and exothermic calcium-binding (K a = 2.4 × 10 4 M -1 ; n = 2.26). Spectroscopic analyses demonstrated Ca 2+ coordination through carboxyl groups. The b and y fragments of the representative peptide (GDDGE, DVSGGYDE, GEPGDDGAK, and GDRGDEGPK) were analyzed. Molecular docking revealed distinct Ca²⁺-binding modes involving carboxylate and backbone carbonyl oxygens. This strategy provides a feasible route for converting aquaculture by-products into value-added calcium-binding peptide ingredients.

title: Reduction of cyanide compounds in Prunus mume syrup: Compositional profiling and the effects of ultrasonication and soaking treatments
abstract: Cyanogenic compounds in Prunus mume syrup may pose safety concerns; practical reduction strategies for fruit-based syrups are poorly defined. The ultrasonication and soaking pretreatments applied to raw fruit prior to syrup preparation were assessed and amygdalin, prunasin, mandelonitrile, and free cyanide were monitored using UHPLC–(ESI)QqQ–MS/MS. Both treatments substantially reduced the total cyanide content, with extended soaking (72 h) achieving the largest decrease, whereas ultrasonication was particularly effective in lowering free cyanide. Ultrasonication was associated with sustained β-glucosidase activity during aging. Neither pretreatment adversely affected the total phenolic content nor antioxidant activity. This study provides the first systematic, multi-compound evaluation of CN − reduction strategies in P. mume syrup during long-term aging and offers mechanistically-supported guidance for the practical mitigation of cyanogenic compounds in P. mume syrup production.

title: Metal chelating and radical scavenging activities of soybean protein hydrolysates for lipid oxidation inhibition: A cross-varietal experimental and bioinformatic approach
abstract: This study examined how soybean variety influences peptide composition, antioxidant activities, and lipid oxidation inhibition in soy protein hydrolysates (SPH). Protein isolates from eight varieties (SP1–SP8) were hydrolyzed with Alcalase (2% E/S, 2 h), yielding degrees of hydrolysis of 9.68–12.22% and peptide concentrations of 1.07–1.27 mmol NH₂/g. Size-exclusion chromatography and LC–MS/MS revealed distinct peptide and molecular-weight profiles, with SP1 and SP4 enriched in the 300–1000 Da. In silico analysis using AnOxPePred selected 20 peptides, among which His-Phe showed the highest predicted free radical–scavenging (0.488) and metal-chelating (0.311) potentials. SP1 and SP4 were enriched in His-Phe and Arg-Phe and displayed superior performance, including stronger DPPH scavenging, Cu 2+ chelation, and inhibition of lipid oxidation. By contrast, SP6 exhibited pronounced Fe 2+ chelation but comparatively weak overall antioxidant efficacy. The findings demonstrate that varietal selection can markedly modulate the lipid oxidation–mitigating properties of SPH.

title: Deamidated zein improves the rheological properties of gluten-free dough: insights from liquid lamella and interfacial mechanisms
abstract: Buckwheat, which is rich in flavonoids, serves as a high-quality protein source despite lacking gluten, leading to poor dough structure and fermentation performance. Therefore, we investigated the effects of moderately deamidated zein on the rheological properties of buckwheat gluten-free dough and the interfacial properties of dough liquor (DL). The results showed that zein treated with 30 U/g protein glutaminase (PG) significantly increased the fermentation height from 5.89 mm to 7.39 mm (p < 0.05), while enhancing the dough's resistance to deformation and the uniformity of its protein network. Moreover, moderate deamidation improved the structural and functional properties of zein, facilitating its rapid adsorption at the gas-water interface and leading to the formation of a viscoelastic interfacial network surrounding gas cells. Consequently, the interfacial tension of DL decreased, whereas the interfacial dilatational modulus increased. A correlation analysis revealed that foaming property and interfacial dilatational modulus of DL are key factors regulating the rheological properties of gluten-free dough. Therefore, moderately deamidated zein improves the quality of gluten-free dough through the enhancement of rheological and interfacial properties.

title: Enrichment of five fluoroquinolones from milk, pork and chicken samples with cyano-functionalized cationic porous polymer
abstract: Sensitive monitoring of trace fluoroquinolones (FQs) in animal-derived foods holds significant importance for safeguarding human health. Herein, an imidazolium cation and cyanogroup co-functionalized porous organic polymer (ICN-POP) was synthesized for the first time. Except that ICN-POP possess large specific area, the cationic imidazolium moieties and cyanogroups in ICN-POP can serve as electrostatic interaction sites and hydrogen bond acceptors, respectively, which may synergistically promote FQ capture. ICN-POP demonstrated excellent adsorption performance towards FQs, especially in neutral and alkaline environments, primarily through electrostatic attraction, π-π stacking and hydrogen bonding. Coupled with high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, solid-phase extraction employing ICN-POP as the adsorbent was applied to develop a sensitive method for detecting five FQs in milk, pork and chicken samples. This work not only provides a reliable alternative approach for FQs detection in complex food matrices, but also confirms the application potential of ICN-POP for high-efficiency capture of polar pollutants.

title: A universally automated and ultra-efficient pretreatment device for rapid assay of mycotoxins in grain and oil
abstract: Sample pretreatment is a critical step in mycotoxin detection and analysis for grain and oil. Conventional pretreatment processes are complex and time-consuming, while manual operations frequently lead to low detection specificity and efficiency. This study presents a universal, automated, and ultra-efficient pretreatment device (GOMAPD) and its method. Systematic elucidation of the direct sonication mechanism established the principle that probe immersion depth, intensity, and duration should be preset according to matrix type, providing a theoretical basis for adaptive parameter setting. The fully automated platform covers the entire pretreatment workflow, processing 24 samples per hour, producing extracts directly compatible with TRFIA and HPLC detection. The method achieved recoveries of 84.01%-110.15% with RSD below 5.73%, replacing manual operation with high-efficiency batch processing. This research offers technical support for practical, safe, and efficient detection across the entire food chain, providing an efficient and reliable solution for food safety monitoring.

title: Complex coacervation of eggshell membrane keratin and gelatin: Interaction mechanism, structural regulation, and functional properties
abstract: Eggshell membrane is an abundant agricultural by-product from the egg-processing industry, most of which is landfilled and thus deprived of high-value valorization. Herein, a mild one-step alkaline procedure was developed to simultaneously extract keratin and gelatin from waste eggshell membrane. Composite protein coacervates were prepared by adjusting pH, sodium chloride concentration and gelatin-to-keratin mass ratio. Their phase behavior, microstructure, molecular interactions and functional properties were characterized to elucidate protein synergistic mechanisms. Quantitative experiments determined the optimal conditions: pH 4.5, 50 mmol/L NaCl, and a gelatin/keratin mass ratio of 8:2. Electrostatic interactions triggered coacervation, while hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic forces and thiol interactions stabilized the network alongside protein conformational transitions and disulfide-bond rearrangement.
