The optimized 8:2 coacervate showed a compact microstructure, improved rheological and emulsifying performance, and 23.4% free-radical-scavenging activity. This facile green strategy achieves full-value recovery of egg-processing waste and promotes sustainable valorisation of agricultural by-products.

title: In vitro gastrointestinal release profiles and antioxidant capacity of bound polyphenols from soluble and insoluble dietary fiber of jackfruit pulp
abstract: Jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam.) pulp dietary fiber contains abundant bound polyphenols, but their gastrointestinal release remains unclear. This study examined polyphenol release, bioaccessibility, and antioxidant capacity of soluble dietary fiber (SDF) and insoluble dietary fiber (IDF) during simulated digestion. Total phenolic content showed phase-dependent changes: SDF peaked in the intestinal phase, whereas IDF peaked earlier in both gastric and intestinal phases. Phenolic bioaccessibility was higher in the gastric than intestinal phase for both fibers. DPPH scavenging activity and FRAP values were mainly enhanced during gastric digestion, while ABTS scavenging activity showed fiber-dependent changes, including higher intestinal-phase activity in SDF and a secondary rebound in IDF. Catechin was the dominant phenolic compound throughout digestion. Gaussian modeling captured the dynamic release profiles of total phenolics and catechin (R 2 = 0.69-0.99). These findings clarify the digestive behavior of jackfruit fiber-bound polyphenols and support their use in functional foods.

title: Artificial intelligence and in silico discovery of senolytic and senescence-associated food peptides
abstract: Cellular senescence, characterized by the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, is a primary driver of age-related tissue dysfunction. While synthetic senolytics have shown promise, concerns regarding systemic toxicity have shifted focus toward sustainable alternatives like food-derived bioactive peptides. This review evaluates AI and in silico methods in senolytic food peptide research, distinguishing discovery, prioritization, and unverified senescence relevance. We evaluate discovery pipelines across soy, dairy, legumes, and marine sources, addressing pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, senescence heterogeneity, gastrointestinal stability, bitterness, and the lack of standardized replicative and therapy-induced experimental senescence models. We further highlight that a substantial proportion of peptides discussed in the current literature are best characterized as senescence-associated candidates that await mechanistic validation, rather than as confirmed senolytics or senomorphics. Future research must prioritize bioengineered 3D human tissue models and long-term clinical validation.

title: Monitoring the crystallization process and polymorphism in cocoa-based products via solid-state 13C NMR
abstract: The crystallization time and polymorphic transitions of cocoa butter (CB), dark (DC) and milk (MC) chocolate samples, which underwent thermal pretreatment at 80 °C, 50 °C and 40 °C, were monitored via solid-state 13 C NMR spectroscopy. Measurements were performed alternating between low flip angle direct polarization (HPDEC pulse sequence) and cross-polarization (CPMAS pulse sequence) that were used to monitor the crystallization process (using solid fat content) and polymorphism, respectively. Hexagonal or orthorhombic forms were observed at the beginning of the process and converted into triclinic structures, for thermal pretreatment at 80 °C and 50 °C, except for MC after melting the sample at 80 °C. However, thermal pretreatment at 40 °C showed faster crystallization and direct formation of triclinic structures. When compared to X-ray diffraction, this approach is more selective to monitor CB crystallization present in chocolates, without interference of other solid components. The proposed method provides a framework for studying fat crystallization in other fat-rich foods.

title: Dual-mode colorimetric and fluorescent detection of Staphylococcus aureus using a bacteriophage-modified nanozyme with tetra-(4-aminophenyl) ethylene as a dual-functional substrate
abstract: Herein, a bacteriophage-modified nanozyme sensing platform was developed for dual-mode detection of Staphylococcus aureus in food samples. A peroxidase-like Fe/Ce metal-organic framework nanozyme was functionalized with bacteriophage SAYZU01 to obtain SAYZU01@Fe/Ce MOF, enabling specific recognition and capture of S. aureus. Tetra-(4-aminophenyl) ethylene (TPE-4A), an aggregation-induced emission-active molecule, was introduced as a dual-functional substrate to generate both colorimetric and fluorescent signals after catalytic oxidation. Compared with conventional TMB, TPE-4A provides complementary colorimetric and fluorescent readouts, allowing cross-checking of the sensing response. The captured bacteria inhibited the catalytic activity of SAYZU01@Fe/Ce MOF, resulting in concentration-dependent signal changes. Under optimized conditions, the platform achieved low detection limits of 1.48 × 10 1 CFU mL -1 for colorimetry and 1.27 × 10 1 CFU mL -1 for fluorometry, with a linear range of 2.43 × 10 1 -2.43 × 10 7 CFU mL -1 . This strategy provides a dual-mode approach for rapid pathogen detection in food safety monitoring.

title: Hydrophobic bioactive diaporthein B regulates supramolecular hydrogel formation for controlled release and postharvest fruit preservation
abstract: Low-molecular-weight hydrogels (LMWHs) show promise for bioactive delivery but are limited in food systems by high gelation thresholds and poor incorporation of hydrophobic compounds. Here, a food-grade supramolecular hydrogel based on glycyrrhizic acid (GA) was developed, in which a marine-derived natural product, diaporthein B (DTB), actively participated in network formation rather than acting as passive cargo. DTB enhanced non-covalent interactions, lowered the critical gelation concentration from 15 mM to 10 mM (a 33.0% reduction), and enabled stable network formation at low loading. The resulting hydrogel exhibited improved viscoelasticity, pH-responsive swelling, and sustained release behavior. It also showed enhanced antifungal activity against Botryosphaeria dothidea and prolonged efficacy compared to free DTB. In the postharvest apple model, the system effectively suppressed disease progression and preserved fruit quality. This work demonstrates a strategy for integrating hydrophobic bioactives into food-relevant networks without chemical modification or surfactants.

title: Mechanistic insights into graphene quantum dots-mediated regulation of single-atom nanozyme activity for homogeneous dual-mode detection of acetamiprid
abstract: A homogeneous colorimetric/ratiometric fluorescence biosensor was developed for acetamiprid (Ace) detection based on graphene quantum dots (GQDs)-regulated Fe/Mn-N-C single-atom nanozyme (SAzyme) activity. Aptamer-functionalized SAzymes with high peroxidase-like activity were hybridized with complementary DNA-modified GQDs (CS/GQDs) emitting fluorescence at 450 nm. Without Ace, the hybridized CS/GQDs suppressed SAzyme activity, likely through proposed substrate-access blocking and hydroxyl-radical scavenging mechanisms, while retaining intrinsic fluorescence. Upon Ace addition, the CS/GQDs are released from the SAzyme, restoring SAzyme activity. The reactivated SAzyme then catalyzes oxidation of OPD by H 2 O 2 to yellow DAP, which quenches GQDs fluorescence via inner filter effect and emits at 570 nm. This cascaded signal transduction enables robust visual colorimetric readout and ratiometric fluorescence (I 570 /I 450 ). The detection limits are 10.37 ng/mL and 3.79 ng/mL, respectively. Spiked food sample recoveries ranged from 93.65% to 103.05%, comparable to LC-MS/MS. These findings demonstrate a reliable, sensitive, and straightforward platform for Ace residue monitoring.

title: Dietary astaxanthin modulates heat-induced volatile flavor profiles across egg matrices by reshaping in vivo metabolic precursors: A multi-omics approach
abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary astaxanthin (0-60 mg/kg) on egg flavor and precursor alterations by combining GC-IMS volatilomics with UHPLC-Q-TOF untargeted metabolomics. Astaxanthin dose-dependently suppressed lipid autoxidation markers in raw yolk, such as 3-heptanone and 2-hexanone, while promoting the accumulation of fruity esters including isobutyl 3-methylbutyrate. During boiling, it inhibited secondary aldehydes, notably (E)-2-heptenal and pentanal, and reduced sulfurous dimethyl sulfide. Untargeted metabolomics revealed that astaxanthin enriched polyunsaturated LPE 22:6 while downregulating LPC 24:0 in raw white, and accumulated acylcarnitines (e.g., CAR 18:0;O) while attenuating peptides (e.g., leucylproline) in raw yolk. Correlation network analysis indicated that raw yolk acylcarnitines and phospholipids were positively associated with thermal aldehydes, whereas short peptides correlated with the Strecker aldehyde 2-methylbutanal. Relative odor activity values coupled with sensory evaluations identified 60 mg/kg as the optimal supplementation level. Overall, dietary astaxanthin modulates raw endogenous precursor pools, thereby stabilizing thermal volatiles and enhancing egg flavor quality.

title: Integration Boruta-SVM-RFE model with flavoromics: Unveiling the aroma enhancement mechanism of enzyme-microbe synergy in soymilk
abstract: Traditional methods for removing the beany flavor from soymilk often result in losing its original flavor, resulting in a bland flavor profile. So, this study proposes a synergistic aroma-enhancing strategy combining enzymolysis with fermentation. Flavoromics and machine learning techniques were utilized to elucidate the mechanisms by which enzymolysis co-fermentation impacts soymilk flavor. Results indicated that enzymolysis co-fermentation significantly enhances the functional and storage characteristics, with substantial increases in free fatty acids and free amino acids contents, providing abundant precursors for aromatic compounds formation. A 80 volatile and 76 non-volatile flavor compounds were detected by GC-IMS and LC-MS. To accurately identify key flavor compounds for the "soy aroma", a progressive machine learning selection strategy combining Boruta with SVM-RFE was employed. Key contributors identified include γ-linolenic acid, glutamic acid, 2,3-butanedione, and 3-hydroxy-2-butanone. Important pathways for aroma formation include Ehrlich pathway, Maillard reaction, lipid oxidation, and β-oxidation. This research provides theoretical insights and technical support for the development of high-quality soymilk.

title: Screening and identification of novel walnut-derived hypolipidemic peptides and evaluation of their hypolipidemic effects
abstract: Walnut peptides improve lipid metabolism by alleviating hyperlipidemia-related symptoms and regulating key genes, but their specific high-activity hypolipidemic sequences have not yet been identified, limiting their hypolipidemic potential. In the study, walnut protein hydrolysates were separated by ultrafiltration under optimized enzymatic hydrolysis conditions, and the molecular weight (Mw) < 3 kDa fraction exhibited the highest hypolipidemic potential (pancreatic lipase, PL: 51.35 ± 0.98%; cholesterol esterase, CE: 45.63 ± 1.50%). A hypolipidemic peptide prediction model was constructed using the designed PeptidasGAN model and the random forest (RF) method, and based on this model, three highly active hypolipidemic peptides (VLTL, LFL, and LVV) were screened and identified from the fraction with MW < 3 kDa. In vitro experimental results showed that these three peptides exhibited strong inhibitory activity against the key targets of hyperlipidemia, PL and CE, with IC₅₀ values of approximately 0.027 mg/mL and 0.070 mg/mL, respectively, comparable to those of the positive control. Molecular interaction and molecular dynamics simulation results indicated that the peptide-target complexes adopted stable conformations, and free energy analysis further demonstrated a clear energetic advantage. In addition, 3T3-L1 cell experiments showed that these peptides significantly improved lipid accumulation and lipid-related parameters (TC, TG, LDL-C, and HDL-C), thereby confirming their potential hypolipidemic activity. Overall, the three walnut-derived hypolipidemic peptides identified in this study exhibited effective hypolipidemic activity.

title: Deciphering competitive interactions in hyaluronic acid-wheat germ gliadin-EGCG ternary nanoparticles: Multi-spectroscopic and computational insights into encapsulation and release
abstract: This study investigated the relationships between intermolecular interactions, physicochemical properties, and EGCG release in ternary nanoparticles assembled from hyaluronic acid (HA), wheat germ gliadin (WGG), and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Multi-spectroscopic analyses, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested that HA and EGCG interact with WGG through hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, and π-π stacking and may occupy partially overlapping interaction regions. These competitive interactions were associated with composition-dependent changes in particle size and EGCG encapsulation efficiency. HWE-NPs also exhibited a faster EGCG release profile than WGG-EGCG nanoparticles (WE-NPs) under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. Overall, these findings suggest that competitive intermolecular interactions, in addition to cooperative associations, may represent an important factor regulating the encapsulation and release behavior of protein-polysaccharide-polyphenol ternary delivery systems.

title: Enzymatic synthesis of neotrehalose: Deciphering the β-1 catalytic promiscuity of transglycolytic starch-active enzymes
abstract: Neotrehalose is a naturally occurring, non-reducing, rare disaccharide with promising nutritional, medical, and synthetic applications, but its low natural abundance and complex chemical synthesis limit commercial production. This study evaluated starch-active enzymes as a sustainable route for its synthesis from renewable substrates. A one-step biocatalytic process using starch and/or maltose as glucosyl donors was developed with the hyperthermophilic α-amylase from Thermotoga maritima. Optimized conditions yielded up to 23.2 g neotrehalose/L (11.60 g neotrehalose/100 g initial maltose), among the most efficient enzymatic methods reported. Combining maltose and starch resulted in an additive effect, increasing productivity and reducing reaction time. Mechanistic analysis showed that neotrehalose is formed through β-anomer-specific transglycosylation at the reducing end of maltose or maltooligosaccharides, generating neotrehalose-core oligosaccharide intermediates. Structural studies with inositol scaffolds examined how the presence and orientation of hydroxyl groups in β-glucosyl acceptors influence enzyme-substrate recognition and the capacity of AmyA to synthesize neotrehalose.

title: A robust and recyclable magnetic three-dimensional nitrogen-doped graphene aerogel for magnetic solid-phase extraction of pyrethroid residues from vegetables
abstract: To suppress graphene restacking and enable diverse intermolecular interactions, a magnetic three-dimensional nitrogen-doped graphene aerogel was synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal approach and applied to magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) of pyrethroids. The aerogel exhibited synergistic properties, including strong magnetic response, good adsorption capacity, and excellent recyclability over ten consecutive extraction-regeneration cycles. Integrated analysis of adsorption isotherm/kinetic data and spectroscopic evidence revealed that π-π stacking, hydrophobic interactions, and hydrogen bonding were the predominant mechanisms governing the adsorption process. Moreover, the MSPE method with HPLC was employed for the determination of pyrethroid residues in vegetables. Under optimal conditions, this method exhibited excellent linearity (3.3-330 μg kg -1 , R 2 ≥ 0.9981), a low limit of detection (1.0 μg kg -1 ), high matrix effect tolerance (|ME| ≤ 2.79%), and outstanding precision (RSD ≤ 7.72%). Furthermore, satisfactory spiked recoveries (78.52%-116.64%) were obtained in vegetable samples. This study establishes a robust and matrix-compatible analytical method for the determination of pyrethroid residues in vegetable samples.

title: Enzymatically hydrolyzed soy protein nanoparticle–polysaccharide composite hydrogels for enhanced stability and pH-responsive release of fucoxanthin
abstract: Fucoxanthin (FX), a hydrophobic marine carotenoid, exhibits low stability and oral bioavailability under harsh conditions. A pH-responsive sodium alginate-xanthan gum (SA/XG) hydrogel incorporating soy protein nanoparticles (SPN) was fabricated for FX stabilization and intestinal-targeted release. SA/XG ratio and intermolecular interactions govern its physicochemical performance. The optimal hydrogel was formulated with SPN obtained after 1.5 h of enzymatic hydrolysis, 1.5% (w/v) sodium alginate, and 1.5% (w/v) xanthan gum at an SA/XG volume ratio of 2:1. It exhibited an encapsulation efficiency of 78.47 ± 2.11%. In vitro digestion resulted in minimal FX release in simulated gastric fluid, whereas 83.85 ± 1.01% of FX was released in simulated intestinal fluid. The Korsmeyer-Peppas model indicated that the release was primarily governed by hydrogel swelling and Fickian diffusion. SPN/FX/SA/XG hydrogel extract showed >90% HaCaT cell viability (negligible cytotoxicity), enabling efficient FX encapsulation and sustained release for oral-food use.

title: MoS2@Ag nanoflower-based SERS substrate coupled with transformer network for sensitive detection and intelligent classification of fluoroquinolone antibiotics in milk
abstract: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics (FQs) residues in dairy products pose a persistent challenge to food safety. This work establishes an integrated analytical platform combining a three-dimensional molybdenum disulfide‑silver nanoflower (MoS 2 @Ag NFs) SERS substrate with a transformer network based deep learning model for the sensitive detection and intelligent classification of FQs in milk. The prepared MoS 2 @Ag NFs substrate with a 1T/2H mixed-phase MoS 2 and a hierarchical structure densely decorated with silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs), exhibits a high enhancement factor and achieves nanomolar-level detection limits for four representative FQs. To overcome the discrimination challenge posed by the highly similar spectral signatures of different FQs, a transformer network is employed to automatically extract decisive spectral features via its self-attention mechanism, which results in an exceptional classification accuracy exceeding 99.82%. The integrated platform enables sensitive and intelligent monitoring of FQs in milk, providing a promising strategy for on-site detection of antibiotic residues in complex food matrices.

title: Electron-bridge mediated Z-scheme nanozyme with homologous heterostructured MOF-on-MOF architectures for simultaneous colorimetric detection and removal of aflatoxin B1
abstract: Mycotoxins are typical contaminants produced by various fungal species, showing significant risks to human health due to their wide distributions and high carcinogenicity. Herein, the homologous heterostructured MOF-on-MOF nanozyme with Z-scheme structure were constructed via surface-initiated strategy by encapsulation of Cu-BDC on HKUST-1 for simultaneous colorimetric analysis and removal of aflatoxin B 1 (AFB 1 ). The homologous Cu 2+ ion plays a pivotal "electronic bridge" role in shortening the electron transfer distance between Cu-BDC and HKUST-1 and enhancing interfacial coupling. The recombination of intrinsic electrons and holes within HKUST-1@Cu-BDC can be suppressed owing to typical Z-scheme structure. These leads to a significant enhancement in peroxidase (POD)-like activity, as confirmed by advanced characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Based on this enhanced homologous heterojunction, the indirect detection (HKUST-1@Cu-BDC/ssDNA biosensors) and direct removal (HKUST-1@Cu-BDC nanozyme) methods with limits of detection (LOD) of 0.87 μg/L and maximum removal rate of 79.6% for AFB 1 have been established. Finally, the homologous MOF-on-MOF nanozyme was successfully verified by both detection and removal process in complex food samples, while also demonstrating excellent repeatability and stability throughout the tests. This work provides a versatile strategy in designing and fabricating high-quality Z-scheme heterojunction nanozyme for mycotoxins governance.

title: Unlocking the molecular basis of the unique jujube aroma in white tea: pile-withering driven aroma formation
abstract: Jujube-aroma white tea (JWT) can be produced via pile-withering, yet the key compounds and mechanisms responsible for its characteristic aroma remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated the dynamic evolution of volatile and non-volatile compounds during JWT processing, identifying 107 volatile compounds and 421 differential metabolites. Pile-withering promoted the accumulation of alcohols, aldehydes, and ketones, while reducing hydrocarbons and esters. Through comparative analyses of samples from different processing stages, as well as red jujubes and aged white tea, seven key aroma-active compounds were identified. Among them, benzaldehyde, benzyl alcohol, and β-ionone showed strong positive correlations with jujube aroma intensity. Molecular docking revealed their high binding affinity and stability with olfactory receptors, and aroma addition experiments further confirmed their potential to enhance the jujube aroma. Overall, this study provides a theoretical foundation and key targets for flavor-oriented precision processing and quality control of white tea.

title: Development and characterization of chitosan-based edible films incorporating Erica manipuliflora extract for active food packaging applications
abstract: Biodegradable active packaging materials offer a sustainable alternative to conventional plastics. This study involved the development and evaluation of chitosan-based edible films containing Erica manipuliflora extract for use in food packaging. The extract exhibited high total phenolic (348.45 mg GAE/g) and flavonoid (56.19 mg CE/g) content. FTIR analysis revealed interactions between the extract and the chitosan matrix, and SEM showed concentration-dependent morphological changes. Incorporating the extract improved the films' properties by reducing their water vapor permeability, moisture content, and swelling degree. The Cs-EP2 formulation demonstrated enhanced mechanical performance, with tensile strength increasing from 11.7 to 23.7 MPa. The antioxidant activity was found to be 72.65% DPPH inhibition and the antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli exhibited inhibition zones of 20.68 mm and 21.61 mm, respectively. Applications of strawberry coating delayed deterioration and reduced decay from 96% to 30%, highlighting the potential of these films to extend the shelf life of perishable foods.

title: Six-year quantitative NMR profiling of polyfloral honey from a single beekeeping area in Okayama: harvest-season-associated variation in minor components
abstract: Forty-six polyfloral honey lots collected in 2018–2023 from four apiaries in one beekeeping area in Okayama, Japan (5 early-spring, 15 spring, 14 late-spring, and 12 summer) were profiled for 17 minor components by quantitative broadband-WET 1 H NMR; conventional 1 H NMR quantified major sugars in 2018–2019. Tryptophan, phenylalanine, and tyrosine were broadly spring-associated, whereas valine and ethanol were relatively high in summer; lactic acid was higher in spring and summer than in late spring. Each year included spring, late-spring, and summer lots, so year-aware validation used 41 lots; early-spring lots (2022−2023) were retained for component-wise comparisons. The harvest-season association persisted after adjustment for year and site (pseudo- F = 20.312, partial R 2 = 0.5672, P = 0.0001). Nested leave-one-year-out PLS-DA classified 39/41 correctly (balanced error rate = 0.0460; permutation P = 0.0001). These findings characterize harvest-season-associated patterns within this geographically restricted dataset without establishing causality or external predictive validity.

title: Informed manipulation of nanoliposome bilayer structure enhances the antioxidant activity and storage stability of curcumin
abstract: This study investigated the impacts of Cur loading level on bilayer structures, antioxidant activities, and physicochemical stabilities of Cur-loaded nanoliposomes (NLs-Cur). Particle size, encapsulation efficiency, and lipid bilayer architecture were monitored in parallel with fluorescence spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). The results suggested that at low loading (0.05 wt%), Cur were embedded in the hydrophobic core of the bilayer, reinforcing vesicle integrity and resulting in improved stability. Increased Cur loading (0.10-0.20 wt%) promoted its localisation at the lipid-water interface loosening phospholipid packing and increasing bilayer fluidity that leads to a substantial enhancement in antioxidant activity. Excessive Cur loading (0.40 wt%) disrupted the acyl-chain packing, inducing bilayer disorder and membrane dilation, thereby compromising stability. Meanwhile, the NLs-Cur was decorated with (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) to specify the role and contribution of EGCG in liposomal systems. The results indicated that the EGCG partial embedded into the bilayer, which increased stacking density and decreased bilayer fluidity, which improved antioxidant performance and stability of NLs-Cur during storage. However, its contribution was relatively limited compared with Cur, revealing that EGCG acts as a supplementary stabilising component. Collectively, these findings offer valuable guidance for advancing liposomes delivery systems and broadening their application in personalized nutrition.

title: Dual-component stimulated Raman scattering imaging reveals enhanced persistence of silicon-based nanocarrier-delivered pesticides in tea
abstract: Nanopesticides with improved utilization efficiency and reduced application rates have attracted increasing attention as promising pesticide delivery systems. However, the lack of in vivo visualization techniques in crops limits understanding of their transport behavior, controlled-release mechanisms, and efficacy. Here, we developed a dual-component imaging strategy for simultaneously tracking silicon nanocarriers and acetamiprid in tea leaves. By introducing cyano groups with distinct bioorthogonal Raman signals onto silicon nanocarriers and loading acetamiprid, a nanopesticide probe with distinguishable Raman fingerprints for both carrier and pesticide was constructed. Using stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) imaging combined with multilayer depth scanning, the penetration, migration, and spatial distribution of both components were dynamically monitored in situ. The silicon nanocarriers delivered acetamiprid into leaf tissues, reaching a depth of approximately 20 μm within 2 h. Although the nanopesticide exhibited slightly lower initial penetration than free acetamiprid, it significantly enhanced pesticide retention, resulting in greater accumulation in tea leaves after 24 h. This dual-component visualization approach provides direct evidence of nanocarrier-mediated pesticide transport and persistence in plant tissues. The findings advance the understanding of nanopesticide fate in crops and provide a valuable tool for optimizing pesticide delivery systems, improving pesticide utilization efficiency, and supporting more rational pesticide application strategies.

title: Sensory preference of unsweetened green tea beverage: Mechanistic insight into the role of nonvolatile components revealed by LC-MS metabolomics
abstract: Consumer satisfaction strongly affects unsweetened green tea beverage (USGTB) market performance. This study aimed to investigate the key compounds driving consumer preference in USGTBs by characterizing their flavor profiles and molecular features via an integrated approach of sensory evaluation, quantitative physicochemical analysis, and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based metabolomics. Hedonic ratings (9-point scale) of 26 commercial USGTBs were clustered into "liked" and "disliked" groups; four samples from each group were selected for in-depth analysis. Color, amino acids, and catechins emerged as primary drivers of hedonic perception. Orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) revealed 104 differential compounds - including flavanols, phenolic acids, flavonoid glycosides, and amino acids - between the two groups. Adding theanine and tryptophan significantly improved preference for a disliked sample (paired preference test). This study pinpoints critical acceptance drivers for USGTBs and informs quality assessment and process optimization in the tea industry.

title: A novel temperature-responsive biphasic deep eutectic solvent for one-step extraction and selective enrichment of multi-polarity bioactives from green tea
abstract: Green tea contains bioactive components with varying polarities. Single deep eutectic solvents (DESs) struggle to achieve simultaneous extraction of different polarity targets. This study developed a temperature-responsive biphasic DES (TRBDES) system for the selective extraction of six bioactive substances with distinct polarities from green tea. The system exhibited reversible biphasic-monophasic transition via temperature modulation. Under optimal conditions, the total extraction efficiency reached 158.24 ± 6.30 mg/g, significantly higher than conventional methods. Hydrophilic (e.g., EGCG) and hydrophobic (e.g., chlorophyll) components were almost completely partitioned into the lower and upper phases, respectively, while caffeine was distributed between both phases. Notably, the TRBDES extracts exhibited superior antioxidant activity (4.4-fold increase over ethanol extraction) and low melting points, confirming structural formation and functionality. Density functional theory calculations elucidated the interaction mechanisms. Demonstrating environmental friendliness, operational simplicity, and strong cell fiber structure disruption capability, this system provides a novel strategy for multi-polarity bioactive substance extraction.

title: Modulating the stability and rheological behavior of camellia oil body emulsions via pH regulation and different charged polysaccharide coatings
abstract: This study investigated the effects of chitosan (CTS), sodium alginate (SA), and methylcellulose (MC) on the physicochemical stability and rheological properties of camellia oil body (OB) emulsions across pH 3.0-9.0. A zeta-potential-derived charge descriptor was used to identify representative pH conditions (3.0, 4.5, 7.0, and 9.0) for further characterization. Uncoated OB emulsions showed pronounced destabilization near the isoelectric region, with particle sizes increasing to approximately 5000 nm at pH 4.5. CTS-coated emulsions showed improved dispersion under acidic conditions, maintaining particle sizes of approximately 1300-1800 nm, but exhibited increased aggregation at neutral and alkaline pH. SA-coated emulsions showed distinct pH-dependent stability and rheological responses, including high apparent viscosity (14.2 Pa.s) under acidic conditions. MC-coated emulsions exhibited comparatively low apparent viscosity across the tested pH range. Overall, these findings revealed distinct polysaccharide-dependent responses, providing comparative insights into the regulation of OB-emulsion properties under different pH and processing conditions.

title: Hansen-guided green recovery of non-extractable hesperidin from lemon by-products with antioxidant and cholinesterase inhibitory potential
abstract: Non-extractable phenolics (NEPs), including high-value flavonoids such as hesperidin, remain trapped in residues after conventional and advanced extraction processes, despite their recognized antioxidant and neuroprotective potential. Their sustainable recovery is key to fully valorizing citrus by-products. For the first time, a Box-Behnken experimental design was applied to optimize the recovery of extractable phenolics (EPPs) from lemon by-products using aqueous-organic pressurized liquid extraction (PLE), followed by the recovery of non-extractable hesperidin from the residual matrix using Hansen Solubility Parameter-guided green solvents and a mixture design optimization. Optimal PLE conditions (11.9 min, 100 °C, EtOH:H₂O 40:60 v/v) maximized EPP yield and bioactivity. Residual NEPs were efficiently recovered by PLE using benzyl alcohol:1,3-butanediol (67.6:32.4 v/v), enhancing non-extractable hesperidin content. HPLC-MS/MS analysis confirmed hesperidin as the main compound, while methyl naringenin rutinoside showed predictive bioavailability and blood-brain barrier permeability. Molecular docking highlighted their strong cholinesterase inhibitory potential, supporting their relevance as neuroprotective agents.

title: Effect of the ripening stage on the hot-air drying behavior of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.): Cell wall polysaccharides, ultrastructure, and mechanisms of bioactive and flavor evolution
abstract: Industrial tomato drying is strongly influenced by ripening stage. This study evaluated mature green, breaker, and red tomatoes for physicochemical traits, cell-wall polysaccharides, microstructure, drying behavior, bioactives, and volatiles. With ripening, polygalacturonase and pectin methylesterase activities increased, water- and chelator-soluble pectins accumulated, Na₂CO₃-soluble pectin and hemicellulose declined, and SEM/TEM observations showed apparent parenchyma loosening and middle-lamella blurring. Red ripe tomatoes had higher effective moisture diffusivity than mature green fruit (1.62 × 10 -9 vs 1.25 × 10 -9 m 2 /s) and 24.44% shorter drying time. Lycopene increased after ripening and drying, total phenolic equivalents rose with maturity on a dry-matter basis, and ascorbic acid declined after drying. Electronic-nose and HS-SPME-GC-MS analyses indicated maturity-dependent volatile fingerprints, with breaker tomatoes enriched in tentatively annotated aroma-related aldehydes and esters. These findings underscore maturity-based grading as a vital strategy to balance drying efficiency, nutritional quality, and flavor development.

title: Comprehensive analysis of the effects of storage temperature and period on physicochemical, microbial, and volatile profiles of chives (Allium tuberosum)
abstract: This study aimed to characterize the physicochemical, microbial, and volatile profiles of chives during storage. Chives were cut and stored at temperatures of 1 °C, 4 °C, and 20 °C. Samples stored at 20 °C showed a rapid increase in weight loss, microbial growth, and antioxidant capacity, accompanied by a decrease in chlorophyll content and textural properties, indicating accelerated deterioration of chives. Low storage temperatures maintained the initial quality attributes up to day 12 at 1 °C and day 9 at 4 °C. Among volatile organic compounds, sulfur-containing compounds were identified as key indicators of storage-related quality changes. Sulfides, disulfides, and trisulfides were strongly influenced by storage temperature than by storage period, and their alteration rates increased at the later stage of storage. These findings provide a comprehensive understanding of chive quality changes during storage and identify factors affecting storage stability, providing practical guidance for optimizing storage conditions.

title: Natural deep eutectic solvents-based pickering emulsion droplets as a robust and sustainable platform: Stability-activity trade-off on the interface for continuous-flow biocatalysis
abstract: The continuous-flow Pickering emulsion biocatalysis system present considerable potential for scale-up industrial applications. In this text, SiO 2 nanoparticles were hydrophobically modified using trimethylchlorosilane (TMCS) and subsequently utilized for the immobilization of Candida antarctica lipase B (CALB), resulting in the creation of a dual-functional material CALB@SiO 2 -TMCS, which functions both as an emulsifier and a biocatalyst. A novel natural deep eutectic solvents-in-oil (NADES/O) Pickering emulsion was developed. The catalytic efficiency of the NADES/O Pickering emulsion was 9.43-fold and 4.73-fold greater than those of the biphasic system and the O/NADES Pickering emulsion, respectively. Furthermore, the continuous-flow NADES/O Pickering emulsions demonstrated extensive substrate adaptability to crude oils, consistently achieving a catalysis efficiency exceeding 98% during continuous operation over a period of 888 h. Consequently, the innovative and effective continuous-flow NADES/O Pickering emulsion developed in this study represent a promising platform that facilitates advancements in Pickering interfacial biocatalysis.

title: Preserving Daifuku quality via static and pulsed magnetic freezing: Associations with water state and structural changes
abstract: This study investigated magnetic-field-assisted freezing (MF) to mitigate post-thaw quality deterioration in Daifuku. Static magnetic field (SMF, 4-8 mT) and pulsed magnetic field (PMF, 6 mT, 0.4-0.8 Hz) were compared with regular freezing (RF) at -20 °C. MF treatment shortened phase-transition time, with the greatest reduction reaching 32.08% under PMF. Compared with RF, MF-treated samples exhibited improved surface morphology, reduced starch short-range ordering, and better preservation of ordered protein secondary structures. RF caused severe post-thaw hardening relative to fresh Daifuku (+639.6%), whereas all MF treatments substantially alleviated this change. Among the frozen groups, PMF at 0.8 Hz showed the best overall texture retention, with a hardness increase of only 9.45% relative to fresh Daifuku. DSC and LF-NMR results further indicated that MF mitigated unfavorable water-state changes in Daifuku skin. Overall, MF-assisted freezing substantially alleviated freezing-induced quality deterioration, with SMF and PMF showing different quality-preserving advantages.

title: Soy sauce cake as novel flavour enhancer and salt-reducing agent and its application in bakery formulations
abstract: Soy sauce cake (SSC) is the underexploited co-product remaining after pressing of fermented soybeans. This study assessed the potential of SSC as flavour enhancer and salt-reducing agent. The nutritional, metabolomic and electronic tongue profiles of SSC were determined. Four bread and oatcake formulations were characterised by sensory and instrumental analyses: full salt (FS), full salt with SSC (FS-SSC), reduced salt (RS) and reduced salt with SSC (RS-SSC). SSC displayed high saltiness and medium umami taste scores. SSC proved suitable as salt-reducing agent in bread, with RS-SSC matching the saltiness, savouriness and acceptability of full-salt products, and as flavour enhancer in oatcake, with RS-SSC exhibiting lower saltiness but similar savouriness and taste intensity to FS. SSC showed high concentrations of flavour-enhancing compounds including aspartate, glutamate and carboxylic acids, which compensated for flavour loss at reduced salt level. This study demonstrated the potential to upcycle SSC as a novel sustainable flavouring ingredient.

title: Anti-swelling performance enhancement and underlying mechanism of noodles by gliadin coating constructed via local phase separation
abstract: This study developed a protein-based edible coating by depositing food-grade gliadin (GLA) from aqueous ethanol onto cooked noodles through moisture-triggered local phase separation. Effects of GLA concentration and contact time on swelling, texture, water distribution, microstructure, and sensory quality were evaluated. Treatment with 5% GLA for 30 s reduced swelling after 30 min in naturally cooling cooking liquor. The swelling ratio decreased from 41.78 ± 2.23% in untreated controls to 27.98 ± 0.93%, while hardness and springiness increased. MRI indicated altered spatial distributions of water-related proton signals. SEM and CLSM revealed a more continuous protein-related surface structure after coating. A 30 s water rinse reduced perceived alcoholic odor without impairing anti-swelling performance. The mean sensory score of rinsed 1% GLA noodles (8.44 ± 0.41) did not differ significantly from the control (8.24 ± 0.28). These findings support GLA coating for improving the holding quality of cooked noodles.

title: Upcycling pomegranate juice by-products into a new oenological tannin: wine color stabilization and sensory enhancement through pre-fermentation addition
abstract: Oenological tannins are widely used in winemaking to enhance clarification, stabilize color, modulate mouthfeel, and prevent oxidation. Among emerging sources, tannins extracted from pomegranate peel (PPE), a food industry by-product rich in ellagitannins characterized by the distinctive gallagyl group, represent a promising alternative. This study evaluated the effect of adding PPE during pre-fermentation of Sangiovese grapes, compared with commercial nutgall tannin (NGT), oak tannin (OKT), and control without tannins. Polyphenol content, antioxidant activity, and color parameters (including CIELab coordinates) were monitored throughout vinification and after six months of bottle aging, alongside sensory evaluation. PPE wines showed the highest polyphenol content (2585 mg/L) and enhanced antioxidant activity, comparable to NGT. PPE significantly increased color intensity and polymeric pigment concentration, improving long-term color stability. Bitterness was reduced and stabilized without affecting astringency or sourness. These findings highlight pomegranate tannin as an effective and sustainable oenological coadjutant, supporting circular economy approaches in winemaking.

title: Protein glutaminase–mediated deamidation enables soy protein isolate to act as a stable zinc carrier with improved gastrointestinal bioaccessibility
abstract: Poor gastrointestinal bioaccessibility limits the efficacy of conventional Zn supplements. Herein, protein glutaminase-mediated deamidation of soy protein isolate (SPI) was performed to develop a Zn delivery system. Deamidation increased the Zn-binding capacity of SPI to 29.8 mg/g protein through the formation of additional carboxyl-containing groups. Structural analyses of Zn-chelated proteins (ZCPs) revealed conformational changes characterized by reduced α-helix content, altered tertiary structure, increased surface hydrophobicity, and an increase in negative surface charges. These changes improved the antioxidant activity of the system and increased its foaming and water-holding capacities by 97.0% and 98.2%, respectively, while decreasing its emulsifying activity. During simulated gastrointestinal digestion, the SPI-Zn system exhibited higher Zn solubility than Zn sulfate and Zn gluconate, resulting in a 78.8% increase in bioaccessible Zn content. Overall, deamidation enhanced the Zn-binding capacity and gastrointestinal stability of SPI and improved Zn bioaccessibility, highlighting its potential for developing protein-based Zn fortification systems.

title: Determination of synthetic antioxidant tert-butylhydroquinone in food matrices using a DyVO4/SnO2/graphene oxide-based sensor
abstract: The widespread incorporation of tert-Butylhydroquinone (TBHQ) in food matrices necessitates the development of highly selective and ultrasensitive analytical platforms. Therefore, constructing synergistic heterointerfaces provides a pivotal means of driving next-generation electrochemical sensing technologies. In this work, a hierarchical DyVO 4 /SnO 2 /GO ternary nanocomposite has been developed and integrated onto GCE for ultrasensitive TBHQ detection. Structural analyses confirmed tetragonal DyVO 4 and SnO 2 phases uniformly anchored on graphene oxide (GO), forming defect-rich heterostructures with strong interfacial coupling. DyVO 4 /SnO 2 /GO architecture significantly improved charge transport, reducing charge-transfer resistance from 581.4 to 139.19 Ω·cm 2 and higher the electroactive surface area to 0.16 cm 2 . In addition, DPV revealed a linear range (0.01-278 μM), and a detection limit of 0.82 nM. Furthermore, it shows good selectivity, reproducibility, and long-term cyclic stability have been achieved. Importantly, real-sample analysis in noodles, chips, tap water and river water, samples yielded satisfactory recoveries ranging from ±96.5-99.5% with RSD values below 0.005-1.82%, validating its practical applicability. Therefore, the proposed DyVO 4 /SnO 2 /GO ternary nanocomposite demonstrates excellent sensitivity, stability, and reproducibility, and highlights its potential as a powerful platform for next-generation environment and food safety monitoring.

title: Protein-based emulsion systems: Potential and mechanisms for regulating lipid digestion
abstract: Lipid digestion in protein-based emulsions is governed by dynamic interfacial restructuring involving proteins, bile salts, and lipases. This review proposes a qualitative interfacial competition framework to integrate these processes and evaluate candidate rate-limiting processes. Protein interfacial stability (PIS), bile salt displacement capacity (BSDC), and lipase accessibility (LA) are introduced as three interrelated, condition-dependent mechanistic descriptors. Interfacial adsorption, diffusion barriers, physical shielding, and spatial confinement are evaluated as candidate rate-limiting processes whose importance may change during digestion. Lipid structure, interfacial composition, droplet size, and digestive-fluid properties are examined for their effects on interfacial organization, substrate hydrolysis, and product bioaccessibility. A mechanism-oriented methodological framework is also proposed to connect digestion models, interfacial measurements, structural characterization, and product analysis. This framework supports mechanistic comparison across protein-based emulsions and provides a basis for rationally designing foods with controlled lipid digestion.

title: High-loading and efficient immobilization of commercial CalA/CalB lipase blend onto tbo-COF for enhanced ester hydrolysis activity
abstract: Lipase-catalyzed hydrolysis is generally hampered by a narrow substrate scope, poor catalytic efficiency, and surfactants are often required to form emulsions to improve enzyme-substrate contact. Developing lipase immobilization supports that achieve efficient emulsifier-free hydrolysis while retaining high loading capacity and operational stability remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report a tbo covalent organic framework (COF) as a robust support for immobilizing a commercial CalA/CalB lipase blend. Through van der Waals interactions, the COF enables an ultrahigh lipase loading of 1900 wt%. The resulting Lipase@COF exhibits expanded substrate adaptability and excellent long-term storage stability. Moreover, it delivers enhanced catalytic performance, achieving over 90% hydrolysis conversion for three plant oils within 13 h. Meanwhile, the intrinsic microenvironment of the COF alleviates hydrolysis-induced inhibitory effects and strengthens catalytic stability. This work validates 3D COFs as multifunctional scaffolds for high-performance immobilized lipases, providing a feasible strategy for ester hydrolysis and lipid modification.

title: Development and application of resveratrol-encapsulated nanostructured lipid carriers for mulberry juice fortification
abstract: The physiological efficacy of resveratrol (Res) is limited by its inherent hydrophobicity and poor bioaccessibility. Nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) have been engineered to overcome these pharmacokinetic bottlenecks. In this study, Res-NLCs were developed, characterized byuniform spherical morphology and high encapsulation efficiency (99.07%). Res-NLCs maintained relatively stable physicochemical properties under the evaluated storage conditions and exhibited enhanced intestinal transport potential, with an apparent permeability coefficient of 4.84 × 10 -6 cm/s. In a food matrix application (mulberry juice), the Res-NLCs acted as a robust delivery vehicle and a stabilizer for endogenous anthocyanins. Notably, the Res-NLCs increased anthocyanin storage retention by 7.28% and reduced anthocyanin loss by 283.9 mg/L. Dynamic digestion further confirmed that Res-NLCs protected the anthocyanins during the intestinal phase and modulated their release, thereby improving their potential bioaccessibility. These findings highlight the potential of Res-NLCs as multifunctional ingredients to enhance the nutritional profile and chemical stability of functional beverages.

title: Combining molecular simulations and bitter receptor modelling reveals the bitter-taste mechanism of walnut protease hydrolysates
abstract: Walnut protein hydrolysates (WPHs) have attracted considerable attention owing to their functional properties. However, the enzymatic hydrolysis process frequently leads to the formation of bitter peptides, which impart an undesirable taste to the hydrolysates, consequently limiting their applications. To elucidate the mechanisms underlying bitterness perception, this study used a combined computational and experimental approach to systematically explore bitter peptides derived from walnut proteins and their interaction mechanisms with bitter-taste receptors (type 2 taste receptors, T2Rs). Initially, a computer-based prediction process was adopted to screen 596 potential bitter peptides from chymotrypsin hydrolysates. The screening led to the identification of T2R1, T2R14 and T2R41 as the primary candidate receptors. The combination of molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations showed that hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions between the peptides and receptors are crucial for stabilising the complex. Notably, three peptides-LHFR, KIVNKDGKPY (KIV10), and LIGEAAKNQ (LIG9)-exhibited stable binding with low energies. Further experiments confirmed that these three peptides markedly increased calcium flux in HEK293T cells overexpressing T2Rs (T2R1, T2R14 and T2R41). Transcriptome analysis revealed that KIV10 significantly activates the bitter-signal transduction cascade in HEK293T cells overexpressing T2R14. This study provides a theoretical model for understanding the generation of hydrolysed bitter taste in food proteins by systematically elucidating the bitter-taste mechanisms of walnut protein-derived bitter peptides.

title: Integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis of 3-phenyllactic acid variation across diverse kimchi types
abstract: 3-Phenyllactic acid (PLA) is a bioactive metabolite in kimchi with antifungal activity. We investigated PLA formation across kimchi types using targeted metabolomics and bacterial community profiling, including lactic acid bacteria (LAB) composition. Baechu, chonggak, and radish kimchi showed high PLA levels, whereas mustard and godeulppaegi showed lower levels associated with precursor imbalance. Watery kimchi types, including dongchimi and nabak, showed low PLA levels, likely due to high water content. Multivariate analysis based on metabolite profiles and microbial composition classified samples into four groups reflecting PLA levels, precursor balance, and ingredient origin. Random Forest and XGB classified the four groups with out-of-fold accuracies of 0.994 and 0.929, respectively, while comparisons with simpler linear and kernel-based models supported the robustness of predictive patterns. Integrated analysis indicated that PLA accumulation was associated with precursor availability, ingredient matrix, and LAB composition, providing an integrated assessment of factors associated with PLA distribution among kimchi types.

title: Nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots for turn-off fluorescence detection of Aflatoxin B1 and Fumonisin B1: FRET versus aggregation-caused quenching
abstract: Developing rapid and sensitive methods for monitoring of multiple mycotoxins is crucial for food safety. In this study, nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (N-CQDs) were synthesized via hydrothermal treatment of fumaronitrile and applied as a fluorescent "turn-off" probe for Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) and Fumonisin B1 (FB1). For AFB1, the sensor shows high sensitivity through a Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) mechanism, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.046 ng/mL and a linear range of 0.3-180 ng/mL. Meanwhile, the detection of FB1 follows an Aggregation-Caused Quenching (ACQ) mechanism with a working range of 40-250 ng/mL and a practical quantitation limit (PQL) of 50 ng/mL (RSD < 40%) for semi-quantitative screening. DFT calculations suggesting that N-CQDs may facilitate stronger π-π stacking and electrostatic interactions compared to O-CQDs. This work provides a promising analytical platform for ultra-trace mycotoxin detection and offers insights into tailoring carbon nanomaterials for sensing applications.

title: A novel whole-kernel defatting technology for simultaneous production of high-quality edible oil and protein-rich intact kernel
abstract: Conventional oilseed processing prioritizes oil extraction, relegating protein-rich meals to low-value by-products. Here we report a whole-kernel defatting (WKD) technology using n-pentane that simultaneously yields high-quality peanut oil and protein-rich intact kernels. After seven extraction cycles, WKD removed >99% oil and retained 98.8% kernel integrity, outperforming supercritical CO₂ and n-hexane. The oil contained higher levels of vitamin E, phytosterols, and resveratrol than conventional-pressed oils, with superior oxidative stability. The defatted kernel retained its native protein conformation, achieving a nitrogen solubility index of 86.6%. In mice fed isocaloric diets, mice consuming defatted kernels instead of raw peanuts exhibited over 2.4-fold lower body weight gain and significantly attenuated hepatic lipid deposition. The process yielded a gross profit of $633.7/ton of raw peanuts, 3.5- to 5.9-fold higher than conventional pressing, and also successfully applied to other oilseeds including camellia seeds and walnuts. This work presents a sustainable, high-value oilseed paradigm without low-value meal.

title: Application of Cu2+-chelated curcumin/chitosan coating in maintaining the storage quality of harvested passion fruit
abstract: Passion fruit is susceptible to postharvest spoilage, requiring innovative preservation strategies. This study developed a novel Cu 2+ -chelated curcumin/chitosan composite coating (CuCur-CS) via self-assembly. Under ambient temperature, CuCur-CS treatment was the most effective, exhibiting the lowest weight loss rate (only 5.6% on day 18), along with superior fruit shape and surface color retention. The coating stabilized sugar-acid balance by suppressing respiration and alleviating oxidative stress. By day 18, H 2 O 2 and MDA contents in the control increased by 53% and 28%, respectively, versus only 11% and 12% in CuCur-CS. Metabolomics revealed that CuCur-CS attenuated energy metabolism by stabilizing TCA cycle intermediates, while modulating phenylpropanoid and fatty acid pathways to suppress volatile alcohols, esters, and excessive phenolics and flavonoids. These actions delay aroma degradation and prevent antioxidant overactivation. Overall, CuCur-CS effectively retards senescence and postharvest losses, offering a promising preservation solution for passion fruit.

title: Ballpoint tip as an integrated tool for extraction and ionization: a dual-workflow for rapid screening and quantification of multiple mycotoxins in edible oils
abstract: This study developed a dual screening-quantification workflow based on ballpoint tip liquid-phase microextraction (BT-LPME) for the high-throughput analysis of multiple mycotoxins in edible oils. By integrating BT-LPME with ballpoint tip electrospray ionization (BP-ESI), the method enables the acquisition of high-resolution mass spectrometry data within 30 s per sample, achieving rapid broad-spectrum screening of 254 mycotoxins. For screen-positive samples, the extract from the tip can be retrieved for accurate quantification via LC-MS/MS. Systematic validation using 55 representative mycotoxins confirmed that the screening sensitivity meets regulatory requirements. The quantitative method demonstrated good linearity (r >0.9970) with limits of detection ranging from 0.01 to 10 μg/kg. In real edible oil samples, 78 mycotoxins were detected, most of which are not covered by current regulatory systems, highlighting potential food safety risks. This approach is green, rapid, and efficient, making it suitable for batch risk monitoring of edible oil safety.

title: Protein–polyphenol–polysaccharide ternary complex as a multifunctional pickering stabilizer for Lycium barbarum seed oil encapsulation: Antioxidant activity, stable delivery, and mechanisms based on interfacial behaviors
abstract: Pickering emulsions present an effective method for delivering functional oils while addressing their inherent water insolubility. However, the stability of these emulsions can be compromised by complex composition of functional oils and their susceptibility to oxidation. This study developed a composite stabilizer consisting of whey protein isolate (WPI), grape seed proanthocyanidins (OPCs), and Lycii fructus polysaccharides (LFP). Alkali-prepared WPI-OPCs were covalently modified with LFP via Maillard reaction, resulting in smaller particles with increased roughness. The conjugate exhibited strong scavenging capabilities, superior emulsifying properties, improved wettability and reduced surface tension, enabling faster adsorption and the formation of a thicker, denser interfacial film with improved resistance. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested hydrogen-bond-related hydration effects and van der Waals interactions may contribute to the superior film properties. Consequently, emulsion containing Lycium barbarum seed oil demonstrated improved stability and oil protection. This study highlights a protein-polyphenol-polysaccharide complex as an effective stabilization approach for food applications.

title: Stable isotope and multi-elemental fingerprinting for seafood authenticity: discriminating production type and geographical origin
abstract: Stable isotope and multi-element fingerprinting were applied to discriminate seafood by production method and geographical origin. A total of 222 samples were analysed, comprising 162 gilthead seabream ( Sparus aurata ) samples (112 farmed and 50 wild) collected from the Mediterranean, Adriatic, and Atlantic regions, and 60 Mediterranean mussel ( Mytilus galloprovincialis ) samples from Portugal (30 farmed and 30 wild). In addition, gill tissues from selected farmed seabream groups were analysed as an exploratory matrix. Stable isotope values ( δ 13 C, δ 15 N, δ 34 S, δ 2 H, δ 18 O and δ 18 O water ) were determined by IRMS while elemental concentrations were measured by ICP–MS, and the combined dataset was evaluated using chemometric modelling. For seabream, δ 13 C and δ 15 N showed clear differences between farmed and wild samples, while an OPLS-DA model based on stable isotope variables achieved 100% classification accuracy within the investigated dataset. δ 34 S provided additional discriminatory information for production type and geographical origin in seabream, and for production type in mussels. The highest classification performance for geographical origin was achieved by combining isotopic and elemental variables, reaching 95.5% overall accuracy for seabream. The DD-SIMCA model was used for class modelling and verification of Portuguese-origin samples, achieving 96% accuracy within the investigated dataset, with high sensitivity (93%) and specificity (98%). These findings demonstrate the potential of complementary isotopic and elemental fingerprints for seafood authenticity, while broader applicability requires validation using independent and geographically diverse datasets.

title: Non-monotonic concentration-dependent hydrogel formation of α-Lactalbumin induced by glycyrrhizin: Mechanistic insights from multi-spectroscopic and molecular dynamics approaches
abstract: The non-monotonic concentration-dependent formation mechanism of α-lactalbumin (α-La) and glycyrrhizin (Gy) composite hydrogels was systematically investigated using multi-technique approaches combined with molecular dynamics simulations. Phase diagrams showed that gelation occurred only within specific windows (α-La 0.1-1.0% w/v, Gy 3.0-15.0 mM), with Gy thresholds increasing from 3.0 to 15.0 mM as α-La rose, whereas no gel formed at α-La ≥2.0%. Hydrophobic interactions dominated network assembly (56-79% contribution), accompanied by conformational rearrangements. All gels exhibited shear-thinning rheology and enhanced bound water (LF-NMR). Simulations revealed Gy-dependent increases in H-bonds, and the solvent-accessible surface area of α-La peaked at an optimal Gy number then slightly decreased. Gy also reduced diffusion coefficients of both α-La and water. Overall, gelation relies on moderate hydrophobic exposure within a strict non-monotonic window, excess protein paradoxically inhibits gelation. This finding could provide a molecular foundation for designing green hydrogels with precisely tunable behavior.

title: A comprehensive biorefinery process for valorising brewers' spent grains using conventional and deep eutectic solvents
abstract: A holistic biorefinery concept integrating cell wall deconstruction, downstream separation and purification steps to convert brewers' spent grains (BSG) into high-value fractions was developed using alkali and deep eutectic solvents. Protein and arabinoxylan yields significantly increased with ultrasound (US) pretreatment, reaching 21% and 27% (w/w) of starting dry BSG, respectively. Protein purity reached 67% with 58% recovery efficiency, and arabinoxylans achieved 90% purity with 94% recovery efficiency using conventional sodium hydroxide (NaOH). Furthermore, the branched structure of arabinoxylans was preserved in NaOH biorefining with an arabinose/xylose ratio > 0.4. However, choline chloride maleic acid (CCM) selectively cleaved side-chain acyl substitutions, identified in phenolic fractions as 5-O-trans-p-coumaroyl-l-arabinofuranose and 5-O-trans-p-feruloyl-l-arabinofuranose. Consequently, linear monodispersed xylopyranose homopolymers and low molecular weight xylo-oligosaccharides were produced with higher phenolic yield than conventional biorefining. Holistic biorefinery concepts demonstrated the potential to extensively valorise BSG into a cascade of high-value products, promoting circular bio-economy principles through waste-to-value conversion.

title: LC-MS/MS quantification of egg allergens across eight avian species in foods: development, validation, and application
abstract: Validated analytical methods for egg allergen detection across multiple avian species remain scarce, posing risks for allergic consumers. This study developed and validated an LC-MS/MS method for simultaneous quantification of ovalbumin from eight avian species (chicken, duck, quail, goose, pigeon, turkey, ostrich, and guinea fowl) in processed foods. Species-specific and shared peptides were screened by high-resolution MS, with MRM transitions optimized and thermal stability assessed. Sample preparation included defatting, urea-assisted extraction, tryptic digestion, and SPE cleanup. Using matrix-matched calibration with stable isotope-labeled internal standards, the method achieved, for all eight species, LODs of 0.5-2 mg/kg, LOQs of 2-5 mg/kg, linearity (R 2 > 0.995), accuracy (80.3%-94.4%), and precision (RSD < 13.3%). Among 26 commercial products, egg allergens were detected in 22 (84.6%); seven (26.9%) were undeclared, exceeding the FAO/WHO reference dose per 100 g serving. This validated protocol provides a reliable tool for multi-species egg allergen surveillance and food labeling compliance.

title: Rapid detection of yam adulteration using portable NIRS combined with chemometrics
abstract: Yam is widely utilized for both culinary and medicinal purposes in China. However, it is frequently subject to adulteration in its powdered form. This study proposed a novel hierarchical modeling strategy integrating portable NIRS (900-1700 nm) for rapid detection of yam powder adulteration. First, 38 pure yam samples, 96 corn starch-adulterated and 96 cassava starch-adulterated samples were used to develop PLS-DA model, achieving 100% classification accuracy. Subsequently, two PLSR models were developed to predict the adulteration levels of corn starch and cassava starch, respectively. Through the spectral preprocessing and variable selection, the corn starch adulteration PLSR model yielded r val of 0.9979, RMSEP of 1.29% and RPD of 15.40; while the cassava starch adulteration PLSR model achieved r val of 0.9934, RMSEP of 1.83% and RPD of 8.74, both indicating excellent predictive capability. The results demonstrated that the portable NIRS combined with hierarchical modeling strategy successfully achieved rapid detection of yam adulteration.

title: Effect of the amorphous complexes of gelatin and quercetin on lutein ester emulsions: Evaluation of stability, interfacial properties and bioaccessibility
abstract: Lutein esters are carotenoid fatty acids esters with extensive physiological activities. However, susceptibility to oxidation and degradation significantly limits its application in food products. In this study, a novel delivery system based on gelatin-quercetin complex (GEL-QU) was developed to encapsulate and protect lutein esters in emulsions. X-ray diffraction (XRD), Intrinsic fluorescence spectrum and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) supported that the GEL-QU is an amorphous complex through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. GEL-QU improved interfacial activity and emulsion performance. The GEL-QU-based emulsion retained up to 92.50% lutein esters after 14 days storage. The after in vitro digestion retention of increased from 69.45% for GEL to 96.19% for GEL-0.1QU, while bioaccessibility increased from 57.74% to 88.69% for GEL-0.05QU. This study provides a novel strategy for protecting lutein esters from degradation in emulsion delivery systems and could potentially expand the application of hydrophobic bioactive ingredients in functional food design.

title: Modulating the flavor quality of black tea by exogenous enzymes: Insights from intelligent sensory technologies and metabolomics
abstract: This study employed intelligent sensory technologies combining with metabolomics to elucidate the effects of four exogenous enzymes on black tea flavor quality. Sensory assessment demonstrated that α-galactosidase treatment yielded the highest overall quality score with a notable emphasis on aroma, whereas cellulase optimally enhanced the taste profile. Utilizing GC-MS/MS and UHPLC-Q-Exactive/MS platforms, 72 volatile and 131 non-volatile metabolites were characterized. In aroma development, glycosidase treatments were most effective in elevating glycosidically bound volatile (GDV) levels. α-Galactosidase, in particular, exhibited the greatest efficacy in modulating the GDV profile, imparting distinct sweet and floral notes. Regarding non-volatile metabolites, cellulase treatment stimulated the accumulation of key differential metabolites, such as amino acids, nucleotides, and carbohydrates, which collectively underpin the development of a brisk, mellow, and well-rounded taste profile. These findings unravel the flavor modulation at the metabolite level by exogenous enzymes, offering a theoretical basis for targeted quality enhancement in tea manufacturing.

title: Modulation of calcium chelation and intestinal transport by acidic residue arrangement in cod bone-derived peptides: Insights from sequence redesign and quantum chemical analysis
abstract: Acidic residues are widely recognized as key structural motifs for calcium coordination in calcium-chelating peptides, yet how their spatial arrangement modulates calcium chelation and intestinal transport remains poorly defined. In this study, LTVEDKD and GPDGEEGK were selected from cod bone hydrolysate based on their structural characteristics, and two derivatives, GPDGEGEK and GPAGAAGK, were rationally designed to evaluate the roles of acidic-residue presence and arrangement. Calcium-chelating capacity followed the order LTVEDKD > GPDGEEGK > GPDGEGEK > GPAGAAGK, indicating that the presence and local arrangement of acidic residues are crucial determinants of calcium chelation. UV-Vis, FT-IR, Raman spectroscopy, and quantum chemical calculations revealed that carboxyl and amide groups served as major coordination sites, while electrostatic attraction and coordination bonds contributed to the stabilization of peptide-calcium chelates. Caco-2 cell assays demonstrated that stronger calcium chelation promoted calcium uptake and transepithelial transport. These findings provide mechanistic insights for designing peptide-based calcium delivery systems.

title: Comparing polysaccharides in microfluidic-fabricated Zein-based lutein ternary composite nanoparticles: enhanced stability, bioaccessibility and assembly mechanisms
abstract: Lutein's (Lut) food application is hindered by poor aqueous solubility, low stability, and limited bioaccessibility. In this study, Zein-based Lut-loaded nanoparticles (Lut-NPs) were fabricated via an intelligent microfluidic platform using four polysaccharides: sodium alginate (ALG), pectin (PEC), sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), and chondroitin sulfate (CHS), to systematically compare delivery performance. Lut-PEC-NPs and Lut-CHS-NPs presented optimal comprehensive performance, with small particle sizes (<104 nm), low PDI (<0.25), high encapsulation efficiency, and excellent antioxidant capacity (DPPH: 97.12%; ABTS: 92.28%). Both exhibited uniform spherical morphology and robust environmental stability. Simulated digestion confirmed sustained Lut release and prominently improved bioaccessibility (65.88% for PEC, 82.38% for CHS), nearly three-fold higher than free Lut. Molecular simulations revealed that hydrophobic, electrostatic, and hydrogen-bonding interactions synergistically drove nanoparticle assembly and stability. This study identifies PEC and CHS as ideal coating materials and provides a reliable microfluidic strategy for Lut delivery in the food industry.

title: Bioaccessibility and epithelial transport of chlorogenic acid extracts from Ilex paraguariensis by-product: Effect of encapsulation
authors: José Eduardo Pedroso Gomes do Amaral
abstract: Ilex paraguariensis is a rich source of phenolic compounds, particularly chlorogenic acids; however, its by-products (IPC) are typically discarded and remain underutilized for value-added applications. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the in vivo toxicity of a chlorogenic acid-rich non-encapsulated extract (IPCE), as well as to evaluate the bioaccessibility and epithelial transport of both the encapsulated extract (IPCEE, formulated with zein) and IPCE. Simulated bioaccessibility was assessed using the standardized INFOGEST protocol, while epithelial transport studies in Caco-2 cells included cytotoxicity evaluation and transport assays. The in vivo toxicity assessment demonstrated that IPCE exhibited no systemic toxicity. These results indicate that encapsulation improves the bioaccessibility of chlorogenic acids, whereas IPCE showed higher epithelial transport, highlighting a trade-off between bioaccessibility and transport. These findings highlight the potential of IPC extracts as sources of bioaccessible phenolic compounds. Further optimization of encapsulation and controlled release may improve epithelial transport under in vitro conditions.

title: Targeted reduction of bitterness in infant extensively hydrolyzed formula by engineering a chymotrypsin from Metarhizium
abstract: This study investigated the reduction of bitterness in extensively hydrolyzed formula (EHF) for milk-allergic infants by engineering chymotrypsin CHY1 through molecular simulation and mutagenesis. Molecular docking identified key mutation sites (Ser201, Pro309, Gly345) for enhancing binding to bitter peptides. Virtual mutation analysis predicted stable interactions. Mutant enzymes were expressed in Pichia pastoris GS115, with expression levels increased to 86.24-112.17 mg/L. The P309W mutant exhibited more than twice higher activity than CHY1. Optimized enzyme combinations, particularly P309F with flavor protease, were applied to milk protein hydrolysis. Results demonstrated significant reductions in hydrophobic amino acid content and bitterness, alongside improved peptide distribution below 500 Da. Sensory evaluation and electronic tongue confirmed near-zero bitterness, while antigenicity was substantially reduced. These enhancements were attributed to the mutant's efficient cleavage and synergistic exopeptidase action. The findings provide a strategic basis for industrial low-bitterness EHF production using microbial chymotrypsin.

title: Exogenous 3-Hydroxy-4-methoxycinnamic acid inhibits browning in fresh-cut pear flesh
Deep eutectic solvent extraction of Camellia oleifera seed meal protein: Functional properties, antioxidant hydrolysate production and molecular mechanism compared with alkaline extraction
abstract: Conventional alkaline extraction of Camellia oleifera seed meal (COSM) protein is not satisfactory in extraction effects and co-extraction of antinutritional saponins. This study compared five choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The choline chloride/1,4-butanediol system (DES-5) showed the most favorable balance. In detail, it increased protein content from 33.91% to 50.84% while maintaining a comparable extraction rate (33.12% vs. 30.11%) and reduced saponin-equivalent levels versus alkaline extraction. DES-5-extracted protein (DES5-P) showed higher α-helix content, lower free sulfhydryl content, and significantly improved emulsifying and foaming stability. Density functional theory indicated the DES-5 system is stabilized primarily by hydrogen bonds and supplemented by van der Waals. Molecular dynamics revealed that DES-5 achieved protein extraction mainly through hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions. Enzymatic hydrolysates of DES5-P and their <3 kDa fractions showed greater radical-scavenging activity than alkaline-extracted protein. These findings support DES-5 as an effective extraction method for COSM protein valorization.

title: Trends in microextraction-based sample pretreatment for food flavonoids
abstract: Flavonoids are widely distributed in plant bodies and possess multiple biological activities such as antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects, making them crucial components in the development of food, pharmaceuticals, and health supplements. Their content in natural samples is unevenly distributed, and they are often present in complex matrices with numerous coexisting interferents. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop efficient and selective miniaturized extraction techniques to achieve precise separation, enrichment, and accurate quantification of target flavonoids. This paper systematically reviews recent applications and research progress of two core microextraction technologies-liquid-phase microextraction and solid-phase microextraction-in flavonoid analysis. It highlights innovations including green solvents in DLLME, functionalized materials in HF-LPME, and novel adsorbents like MOFs and MIPs in SPME variants. By comparing techniques' principles and performance, this paper guides method selection and outlines future trends toward green, automated, and material-driven approaches.

title: Surfactant-amplified interfacial migration difference during emulsification enables efficient DAG enrichment
abstract: Diacylglycerol (DAG) has broad application potential in food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics, yet its mild separation from triacylglycerol (TAG) remains challenging due to their highly similar molecular structures. Herein, we propose a phase-separation-driven emulsion strategy for DAG enrichment. With Span 20 as surfactant, DAG content in the upper phase increased by 26%. DAG enrichment also occurred in the absence of surfactant, indicating that intrinsic structural differences drive partitioning, which added surfactants can synergistically amplify. Interfacial tension measurements, ATR-FTIR and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that DAG preferentially adsorbs at the oil-water interface and forms an organized interfacial layer, which promotes its selective accumulation in the upper emulsion phase. This strategy was successfully applied to DAG enrichment from corn, soybean, peanut and rapeseed oils. Overall, this study transforms emulsion phase separation into a controllable enrichment strategy, providing a green platform for separating structurally similar compounds.

title: Construction and characterization of a ternary composite emulsion based on hydrolyzed soy protein isolate
abstract: Achieving long-term stability of oil-in-water emulsions through robust interfacial films remains challenging. This study aimed to address this challenge by using hydrolyzed soy protein isolate-tannic acid-citrus pectin (HSPI-TA-CP) ternary complexes as stabilizers and investigating the effects of complex concentration (1%-3%, w/w) on emulsion microstructure and physicochemical properties. The complexes adsorbed at the oil-water interface via hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions, forming a dense interfacial film. As the concentration increased from 1% to 3%, the droplet size significantly decreased from 24.87 to 12.27 μm, the zeta potential shifted from -40.65 to -57.91 mV, and the emulsion stability index increased from 52.23% to 91.47%. All emulsions exhibited a strong gel network structure (G' > G″). At 2.5% concentration, interfacial adsorption approached saturation, and the emulsions showed optimal storage stability and good pH and temperature tolerance. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of HSPI-TA-CP ternary complexes as emulsion stabilizers.

title: Caffeoylquinic acid-mediated modification of a soybean β-conglycinin fraction under alkaline conditions: structural and functional properties
abstract: This study compared the structural and functional properties of a soybean 7S-enriched β-conglycinin fraction treated with chlorogenic acid (CA) or isochlorogenic acid C (IAC) under alkaline conditions. CA exhibited higher apparent binding efficiency than IAC, with maxima of 93.48 ± 1.23% and 62.95 ± 0.76%, respectively. Compared with CA-treated samples, IAC-treated samples showed greater increases in α-helix content and decreases in β-sheet content, generally smaller particles, more negative ζ-potentials, and higher emulsifying indices, radical-scavenging activities, and thermal transition temperatures. At a protein-to-polyphenol mass ratio of 5:1, solubility reached 76.45 ± 9.37% with IAC and 67.32 ± 7.84% with CA, while DPPH radical-scavenging activity reached 76.42 ± 8.63% with IAC. Higher apparent binding efficiency did not consistently correspond to better functional performance.
