These findings inform polyphenol selection for improving ingredient functionality in soy protein processing.

title: Dual-ligand engineering of copper nanoclusters enables “turn-on” fluorescence label for pH-responsive freshness monitoring of shrimp
abstract: With increasing consumer demand for food safety, conventional freshness detection methods remain limited by subjectivity and operational complexity. Herein, highly emissive green fluorescent copper nanoclusters (CuNCs) were developed as intelligent packaging labels via dual-ligand engineering of kojic acid (KA)-stabilized CuNCs with D-penicillamine (DPA). DPA markedly improved the fluorescence quantum yield from 1.2% to 11.4% by promoting ultrasmall cluster formation (∼2 nm), enhancing quantum confinement, and passivating surface defects. The obtained DPA-KA-CuNCs exhibited a pH-responsive fluorescence "turn-on" behaviour toward volatile basic nitrogen compounds (VBNs). Fluorescence quenched under acidic conditions was efficiently restored upon exposure to ammonia, dimethylamine, and trimethylamine through ligand deprotonation and enhanced ligand-to-metal charge transfer. Detection limits reached 0.23, 0.19, and 0.18 ppm, respectively. A paper-based fluorescent label further enabled visual monitoring of shrimp freshness, showing excellent correlation with TVB-N values (R 2 = 0.9835). This work provides a sensitive and visual strategy for non-destructive aquatic product freshness evaluation.

title: Regional prevalence of aflatoxin M1 in milk and milk-based products (2021–2025): Contamination drivers, detection advances, and mitigation strategies
abstract: Aflatoxin M1 (AFM1), a hydroxylated metabolite of aflatoxin B1, is a heat-stable mycotoxin commonly detected in milk and dairy products, posing a significant food safety concern. This review synthesizes data from 98 studies across 53 countries (2021-2025) to evaluate the global occurrence of AFM1 in milk, cheese, and yogurt relative to regulatory limits. Contamination patterns show marked regional variability, with higher exceedances in South Asia and Africa than in Europe and East Asia. Key drivers include contaminated feed, climatic conditions, and seasonal variability. From a food chemistry perspective, AFM1 exhibits strong casein-binding affinity and thermal stability, enabling persistence during processing and concentration in cheese. Recent advances in detection (immunoassays, chromatography, biosensors) and mitigation strategies, including lactic acid bacteria and non-thermal processing, are critically discussed. The review highlights the need for integrated monitoring and improved control strategies to reduce AFM1 exposure.

title: Comparative proteomics and metabolomics of milk digesta during simulated infant gastrointestinal digestion: Novel insights into quantitative differences among bovine, sheep, and goat milks
abstract: This study compared the digestion behavior, protein composition, and metabolite profiles of bovine (B), sheep (S), and goat (G) milk digesta following simulated in vitro infant gastrointestinal digestion. Microstructural analysis indicated that goat milk underwent slower digestive progression during the gastric phase relative to bovine milk. Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics and untargeted metabolomics were applied to characterize differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) and metabolites (DAMs). A total of 107 DAPs were identified across all samples, including CSN1S1, CNDP2, GP2, FLOT2, etc. G and S exhibited accumulation of sugar-nucleotide and precursors. B was richer in DAG and oxidized fatty acids (OFAs). Integrated proteome-metabolome analysis pinpointed glycerophospholipid metabolism as the core pathway that distinguishes the species' digesta. This work provides scientific support for the application of featured milk in the field of functional foods.

title: MCOF-assisted and MnO2 nanozyme-triggered cascade dual-mode aptasensor for intelligent detection of Salmonella Typhimurium
abstract: Conventional methods for detecting Salmonella Typhimurium in food often require lengthy procedures or specialized instrumentation. We developed a dual-mode aptasensor based on magnetic covalent organic frameworks (MCOFs) and MnO 2 nanozymes. MCOF-AuNPs@apt captures bacteria, followed by MnO 2 @apt binding to form sandwich complexes. The retained MnO 2 @apt promotes TMB oxidation without added H 2 O 2 . Subsequent acidification produces yellow TMB 2+ , which etches gold nanorods. Etching shifts the longitudinal plasmon resonance to shorter wavelengths and decreases the photothermal response under 808 nm irradiation, providing complementary multicolor and photothermal readouts. Calculated detection limits were 6.6 and 3.2 CFU/mL for the colorimetric and photothermal modes, respectively. The assay was evaluated in spiked milk and meat infusion. Smartphone-assisted linear discriminant analysis classified independently prepared blinded samples by bacterial concentration with 97.14% accuracy. These results support the platform as a proof-of-concept approach combining complementary dual-mode detection and smartphone-assisted concentration classification.

title: Phenolic acid-grafted chitin nanofibers improve frozen quality of frozen Litopenaeus vannamei: myofibrillar protein preservation and ice crystal control
abstract: Frozen storage of Litopenaeus vannamei causes ice crystal-induced tissue damage and myofibrillar protein (MP) denaturation. Ferulic acid (FA), sinapic acid (SA), and caffeic acid (CA) were grafted onto chitin nanofibers (ChNFs) to prepare cryoprotective phenolic acid-grafted ChNFs (PC) conjugates. During 12 weeks of frozen storage. PC treatment significantly inhibited quality deterioration. SA-g-ChNF reduced TVB-N (8.07 vs 10.81 mg/100 g) and TBARS (0.23 vs 0.36 mg/kg) at 12 weeks; CA-g-ChNF maintained higher MP water-holding capacity (12.59 vs 6.69 g/g) and Ca 2+ -ATPase activity (2.20 vs 1.31 U/mg). PC conjugates preserved sulfhydryl content, limited surface hydrophobicity, and maintained α-helix content, indicating reduced MP unfolding. Smaller ice-crystal areas and better water distribution were observed. A working model is proposed: the ChNFs backbone mainly limits ice-crystal growth and mechanical damage, while grafted phenolic acids mainly inhibit oxidative denaturation and stabilize MP conformation, providing synergistic protection. These conjugates are promising bio-based cryoprotectants for frozen aquatic products.

title: Walnut and peanut protein microgel particles: production, characterization, and application in stabilizing emulsions and gels
abstract: The functional differences between peanut protein (PPI) and walnut protein (WPC) in constructing microgel particles and the structure-property regulation mechanism in stabilizing emulsions and forming gels were investigated in this study. The results revealed that superior stability was exhibited by the high internal phase emulsions (HIPPEs) prepared therefrom due to the stronger hydrophobicity possessed by walnut protein microgel particles (WPC-MPs). In contrast, enhanced gel-forming ability and higher gel strength were observed in HIPPEs prepared from peanut protein microgel particles (PPI-MPs). Furthermore, the apparent viscosity and gel stability of emulsion gels were increased by the introduction of salt ions. The performance of emulsion gels was improved significantly by the SO 4 2- . This study gap in the structure-property mechanism of walnut protein based microgels was filled. And a theoretical basis and data support for selecting plant protein resources to develop emulsion-based foods or solid gel foods were provided.

title: Atmospheric air DBD plasma treatment of rapeseed (Brassica napus L.): balancing growth enhancement and fatty acid content
abstract: The effects of atmospheric-pressure plasma on rapeseed (Brassica napus L.), a major oilseed crop, remain largely unexplored despite growing interest in plasma-based seed technologies. This study investigated the influence of atmospheric air dielectric barrier discharge plasma (10-120 s) on seed surface properties, germination, seedling development, and fatty acid composition. Plasma treatment markedly improved seed wettability, reducing the water contact angle from 123.7° to 28.6°, and enhanced germination and early growth. Notably, plasma exposure produced a duration-dependent response in seed lipids. Moderate treatments (10-60 s) increased the mass-normalized values of several major fatty acids, while prolonged treatment (120 s) reduced the recovered FAME yield, suggesting possible plasma-induced lipid modification. These findings demonstrate, for the first time, that atmospheric air plasma can simultaneously influence seed performance and lipid composition in rapeseed, revealing a critical treatment window that maximizes biological benefits while preserving oil quality.

title: Next-generation non-Saccharomyces yeast derivatives: Fine tuning antioxidant capacity through inactivation process
abstract: Inactivated non-Saccharomyces yeasts offer a promising way to exploit their unique metabolic features, already valued in their active state for bioprotection or bioacidification in winemaking. Producing efficient yeast derivatives at industrial scale requires precise characterization, for which metabolomics provides a powerful analytical framework. This study investigates how biomass nutrition and inactivation by high-pressure or heat affected the composition and antioxidant capacity of derivatives prepared from three non-Saccharomyces strains. Although strain specificity remained the dominant factor for antioxidant capacity, non-thermal inactivation consistently improved score for all strains, with increases up to +57.7%. This enhancement was not linked to greater abundance or diversity of nucleophiles, as fewer than 10% were unique to high-pressure treatment, but rather to the preservation of thermolabile metabolites with redox activity. High-pressure inactivation also promoted the release of low-molecular-weight compounds potentially contributing to antioxidant function. Overall, metabolomics emerges as a valuable tool for guiding precision biotechnology in enology.

title: A RCA-based signal amplification and machine learning-assisted sandwich-type dual-mode split aptamers sensor for the simultaneous detection of diarrhetic shellfish toxins
abstract: Sensitive detection of diarrhetic shellfish toxins (DSTs) is vital for ensuring marine food safety. In this study, a novel sandwich-type dual-mode split aptamers sensor (DMSAS) was constructed for the ultrasensitive simultaneous detection of DSTs by integrating rolling circle amplification (RCA)-based signal enhancement, fluorescent/colorimetric dual-mode output, and machine learning (ML)-based intelligent data analysis. Under the optimal conditions, DMSAS displayed limits of detection of 4.510 fg/mL and 4.859 fg/mL for fluorescent and colorimetric detection modes, which were improved to 3.383 fg/mL after ML-based dual-signal fusion. An intelligent recognition model for DSTs concentrations that was established using ML could achieve 100% classification accuracy for DSTs in simulated natural shellfish samples. Spiked recovery experiments yielded recovery rates ranging from 88.9% to 103.1%, with relative standard deviations below 12%, indicating the satisfactory accuracy, repeatability, and matrix adaptability of DMSAS. This work provides a new strategy for monitoring marine food safety.

title: EMS-induced variability in phytochemical and antioxidant traits of Withania somnifera varieties (NMITLI-118 and CIM-Pushti) across the generation
abstract: Withania somnifera is an important medicinal plant in which induced mutagenesis can generate biochemical variability. This study evaluated the effects of ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) on two cultivars, NM-118 and CIM-Pushti, using five EMS doses (0.2-1.0%) and a control. EMS treatment was associated with variation in chlorophyll pigments, carotenoids, total phenolic and flavonoid contents, total antioxidant capacity, reducing power, DPPH· scavenging activity, and protein content. Moderate EMS doses (0.4-0.8%) generally increased pigment accumulation and several biochemical traits, whereas higher doses reduced pigment content. DPPH· scavenging activity generally decreased with increasing EMS dose, while other biochemical responses varied with dose, cultivar, tissue, and generation. CIM-Pushti exhibited greater variation in several parameters than NM-118. Differences between M₁ and M₂ indicated generation-dependent responses. Overall, EMS treatment was associated with measurable biochemical variability, providing a preliminary screening of EMS-associated responses.

title: DmcFlavor: Compound–informed prediction and interpretation of integrated multi–flavor profiles in foods and herbs
abstract: Food flavor is inherently multidimensional and arises from the complex combined effects of diverse compounds; however, dedicated computational tools for predicting integrated multi-flavor profiles of foods are still lacking. In this study, DmcFlavor was developed as the first framework for predicting and interpreting integrated multi-flavor profiles of foods. DmcFlavor employs Transformer-based modeling to perform both compound-level and mixture-level flavor prediction across five flavor attributes: bitter, pungent, salty, sour, and sweet. DmcFlavor was applied to tomato ripening analysis, revealing dynamic changes in integrated flavor profiles during ripening and quantitatively identifying major contributors to sourness and sweetness. It was further applied to characterize integrated flavor patterns across 18 food categories, including fishes, fruits, herbs and spices, and vegetables, and to explore potential flavor-health effect associations. This framework may facilitate integrated food multi-flavor evaluation, support flavor optimization in the food industry, and promote the systematic exploration of food therapy.

title: Sex-specific lipidomic profiling of the marine mussel Mytilus coruscus: A comparative analysis of male and female lipid metabolism
abstract: Sex-dependent lipid metabolism plays a pivotal role in physiological adaptation and reproduction in marine bivalves, yet its molecular basis remains poorly understood. Here, UPLC-HRMS-based lipidomics was applied to characterize sex-specific lipid profiles in mussels. Females showed higher levels of glycerophospholipids, particularly phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine enriched with polyunsaturated fatty acids, whereas males contained more glycerolipids, especially saturated fatty acid-rich triacylglycerols. Principal component analysis and orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis revealed clear metabolic separation between sexes. A total of 140 differential lipids were identified, with glycerophospholipids mainly enriched in females, while glycerolipids exhibited bidirectional regulation in males. Pathway analysis indicated coordinated remodeling of glycerophospholipid metabolism, glycerolipid turnover, and polyunsaturated fatty acid-related pathways. Females also accumulated higher ceramide levels, suggesting altered sphingolipid metabolism and potential differences in lipid remodeling between sexes. These findings reveal distinct sex-dependent lipid metabolic strategies and provide insights into nutritional evaluation and precision mussel aquaculture.

title: Metabolomic dynamics and health-related properties of red radish (Raphanus sativus var. sativus) through lactic acid fermentation and storage
abstract: Untargeted UHPLC-HRMS metabolomics coupled with HPTLC/HPLC bioautography revealed that lactic fermentation and subsequent storage profoundly remodelled the metabolome of red radish (Raphanus sativus var. sativus) and shifted bioactivity-relevant compound pools. Fermentation induced pronounced class-specific changes: organic acids increased approximately 10-fold, phenolic compounds 8-fold and flavonoids 4-fold, whereas glucosinolates decreased to 16% of their initial levels. Discriminant biomarkers of fermentation included phenyllactic acid, hydroxyphenyllactic acid, chlorogenic acid isomers and isorhamnetin derivatives. Antioxidants profiling showed a restructuring of the antioxidant pool - shifting from anthocyanins toward flavonols and phenolic acids, with kaempferol-3-O-rhamnoside, quercetin, and oxygenated lipids emerging as novel antioxidant contributors. α-Amylase inhibitory activity increased throughout fermentation and storage, peaking at 4.08 ± 0.08 mg acarbose equivalents/g DW after storage at 18 °C and correlating with increased flavonoid availability, supporting fermented red radish as a promising functional ingredient with antioxidant and antidiabetic potential.

title: Anthocyanin-rich extract from grape pomace enhances the quality and yield of hydroponic lettuce by modulating carbon–nitrogen metabolism
abstract: Anthocyanins are regarded as natural biostimulants with significant potential in agricultural production. We investigated the effects of an anthocyanin-rich extract from grape pomace (ACNs) on the yield and quality of hydroponic lettuce. The most balanced improvements in growth and quality were achieved with 2 g L -1 ACNs. ACNs significantly increased shoot biomass, elevated the levels of total phenolics, flavonoids, anthocyanins, and antioxidant activity, while concurrently reducing nitrate accumulation. These changes were accompanied by upregulated enzyme activities and transcript levels in phenolic biosynthesis and nitrogen assimilation pathways, together with enhanced photosynthetic performance. Metabolomic analysis further revealed that ACNs modulated carbon and nitrogen metabolism, promoting a shift in metabolic profiles toward the accumulation of health-promoting phenolic compounds. Therefore, grape pomace-derived anthocyanins can serve as an effective elicitor to improve both the yield and nutritional quality of lettuce, offering a promising strategy for the valorization of winery byproducts into functional vegetables.

title: Covalent conjugation of catechin monomers to corn bran arabinoxylan via DBD plasma and its impact on structural reconstruction and conformational evolution
abstract: A green, non-thermal dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma protocol was established to covalently graft four structurally distinct catechin monomers, epicatechin, epicatechin gallate (ECG), epigallocatechin, and epigallocatechin gallate, onto corn bran arabinoxylan (CAX). Among the synthesized conjugates, ECG-CAX showed the highest grafting yield (72.66 mg/g). Fourier transform infrared spectrum (FT-IR) and ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy analyses verified phenolic incorporation while preserving the primary polysaccharide skeleton. Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance (2D-NMR), supported by gradient acid hydrolysis, indicated a free-radical-mediated, heterogeneous multi-site conjugation network, with the B- and D-rings of ECG predominantly anchored to the inner xylan backbone. Plasma treatment contracted native CAX from flexible random coils into compact coil conformations, whereas phenolic grafting partially reversed this transition by introducing steric hindrance and promoting chain re-expansion into semiflexible coils. This conformational evolution reduced apparent viscosity and shifted the micromorphology from lamellar sheets to interconnected porous fibrous networks, providing mechanistic insight into plasma-mediated polysaccharide-polyphenol conjugation.

title: Design of a pH-switchable supramolecular deep eutectic solvent for the extraction of flavonoids from citrus peel waste and Rutaceae herbs
abstract: The rising demand for natural ingredients across the food, cosmetics, healthcare industries has driven the broader utilization of agricultural and food industry waste as valuable sources of bioactive compounds. A pH-switchable supramolecular deep eutectic solvent (SS-DES) based on geraniol and octanoic acid was first prepared for the simple, rapid, and efficient extraction of flavonoids from citrus peel waste and Rutaceae herbs. In this system, geraniol acted as a hydrophobic building block to construct the hydrophobic SS-DES, thereby effectively resolving the poor compatibility between conventional hydrophilic DESs and lipophilic flavonoids. Furthermore, the application of SS-DES overcame the drawbacks of difficult phase separation, excessive solvent consumption, and low reusability. A series of DESs were successfully prepared, and the key experimental parameters affecting enrichment were systematically investigated and optimized. Among these DESs, the geraniol/octanoic acid (1,1) system containing (2,6-di-O-methyl)-β-cyclodextrin showed the highest enrichment for flavonoids and was successfully applied to citrus peel wastes and Rutaceae medicinal herb samples. The prepared SS-DES was characterized using FT-IR and 1 H NMR. Meanwhile, the extraction mechanism of target compounds using the SS-DES were investigated via molecular docking and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Furthermore, following an evaluation of the environmental impact of the proposed method, the biocompatibility of the SS-DES was further evaluated by in vitro cytotoxicity assays in GES-1 and HK2 cell lines, as well as in vivo acute oral toxicity test. After five adsorption-desorption cycles using AB-8 macroporous resin, the extraction performance of the regenerated SS-DES remained above 91.72%, indicating had satisfactory stability reusability. As a result, the designed SS-DES may hold great potential to replace traditional organic solvents for extracting flavonoids from diverse and complex matrices.

title: Signal-amplified detection of sodium pentachlorophenate using a radical-enhanced electrochemiluminescence strategy
abstract: A molecularly imprinted signal-on electrochemiluminescence (MIECL) sensor based on molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) and the Ru(bpy) 3 2+ luminescence system was developed for rapid and highly sensitive detection of pentachlorophenol (PCP) and its sodium salt (PCP-Na). In this design, PCP-Na acts as both the imprinting template and the ECL co-reaction accelerator, enabling target-driven signal amplification. Enhanced dual-channel electron transfer provides highly sensitive and selective detection of trace PCP-Na under experimental conditions. Under optimized parameters, the ECL signal exhibited a linear relationship (R 2 = 0.9990, LOD = 0.0060 μg/L) with the logarithm of PCP-Na concentration from 0.010 μg/L to 50.0 μg/L. Recoveries for seawater and three biological samples ranged from 85.0% to 114.0%, and relative standard deviations did not exceed 2.9%. The proposed MIECL sensor demonstrated high selectivity in real-sample analysis and shows strong potential for rapid determination of PCP and PCP-Na in environmental matrices.

title: Cross-scale study of aging-driven colloidal transformations in Qingxiangxing baijiu via EEM-guided multi-technique integration
abstract: Qingxiangxing baijiu (QXB) aging involves dynamic colloidal evolution, yet its underlying mechanisms remain underexplored. This study integrated excitation-emission matrix spectroscopy (EEM), Tyndall imaging, atomic force microscopy (AFM), and dynamic light scattering (DLS) to investigate aging-induced colloidal dynamics in QXB. EEM identified characteristic peaks (excitation/emission wavelengths of 250/310 and 310/340 nm) and effectively distinguished aroma types and aging years. Tyndall intensity fluctuated periodically (129.5-193.3) with aging. AFM visualized colloidal self-assembly and ripening, while DLS showed predominant particles sized 0.3-5.0 nm alongside growing larger particles exceeding 1 μm. These results reveal a periodic "dispersion-assembly-ripening" cycle driven by colloidal self-assembly and Ostwald ripening. The multi-scale approach elucidates QXB aging mechanisms and supports EEM's potential for rapid vintage authentication.

title: Bioactive compounds from coffee husk (Coffea arabica) obtained by green extraction methods: Characterisation, antioxidant capacity and inhibition of lipid peroxidation
abstract: Coffee husk, the principal by-product of wet coffee processing, is an underutilized agro-industrial residue with significant potential as a source of bioactive antioxidant compounds. In the present study, four green extraction methods were evaluated: aqueous extraction (AQU), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) and enzyme-assisted extraction (EAE), for the recovery of bioactive compounds from the husk of two Coffea arabica varieties (var. caturra chiroso from Tolima and var. castillo from Antioquia, Colombia). Antioxidant capacity was determined by ABTS, DPPH, FRAP and ORAC assays. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to evaluate varietal differentiation. Selected extracts were assessed in an accelerated oxidation model using linseed oil. AQU yielded the highest total polyphenol content (831.63 mg GAE/100 g) and antioxidant capacity (14,036.27 μmol Trolox/100 g by ABTS). MAE generated the most enriched profiles in hydroxycinnamic acids and condensed tannins. UAE showed greater extractive efficiency with hydroalcoholic solvents. EAE was the least efficient method, attributed to the lignocellulosic recalcitrance of the matrix. PCA explained 88.1% of the total variance, separating varieties by bioactive profile; the caturra chiroso variety exhibited higher antioxidant capacity. AQU extracts at 250 mg/L delayed hydroperoxide formation in linseed oil by up to 37.3%, whilst MAE extracts showed pro-oxidant behavior towards peroxide formation but retarded the appearance of polar compounds at 250 mg/L (29.0%). These results demonstrate that coffee husk is a valuable source of natural antioxidants recoverable through green chemistry principles, with potential application in functional foods and cosmetic products.

title: Dual pH-responsive packaging film based on modified bacterial cellulose Pickering emulsion: impact of anthocyanin content
abstract: In this study, bacterial cellulose (BC) was functionally modified to obtain BC-COOH nanoparticles, which were used to prepare Pickering emulsions (5-25%, v/v). The 10% oil emulsion showed optimal stability with a droplet size of 6.67 μm, a zeta potential of -45.16 mV, and pronounced pH sensitivity. The dual pH-responsive packaging films, featuring both triggered-release and indicator functions, were prepared by incorporating different anthocyanin (Ant) concentrations (0-0.1 mg/mL) into emulsion/sodium alginate composite (EC) (10%, v/v). The composite film with 0.02 mg/mL Ant (0.02Ant/EC) showed enhanced tensile strength and elongation at break, reaching 16.43 MPa and 84.12%. The film also showed good light barrier, hydrophilicity, and antioxidant activity, and was therefore selected for dual pH-responsive analysis. This film showed reversible visible color changes across pH 2-13. The cumulative release of essential oil reached 0.254 μL/mg over 36 h at pH 10.0, representing a 37.79% increase compared to release at pH 7.2.

title: Effects of extraction method and flour type on nutritional, antioxidant, antinutritional, volatile, and proteomic profiles of navy bean protein extracts
abstract: The effects of extraction method and flour type on the digestibility, antinutritional factors, proteome composition, and volatile profiles of navy bean protein (NBP) remain insufficiently studied. Whole and dehulled flours were processed by aqueous, enzyme-assisted, and homogenization-enzyme-assisted extraction. Dehulled enzyme-assisted extract showed the highest ABTS radical scavenging activity, ferric reducing antioxidant power, total essential amino acids, essential amino acid index, and biological value. Among NBP extracts, dehulled homogenization-enzyme-assisted and dehulled enzyme-assisted extracts had the highest in vitro protein digestibility (98.38% and 98.32%), whereas whole homogenization-enzyme-assisted extract had the highest protein digestibility-corrected amino acid score (PDCAAS; 0.983), lowest lipoxygenase activity, and lowest phytic acid content. Dehulled enzyme-treated extracts had the lowest trypsin inhibitor activity. Proteomic profiling showed phaseolin-dominated profiles, and volatile profiles showed compound-specific differences among extracts. These results indicate that processing method selection influences the nutritional and quality characteristics of NBP ingredients.

title: Dual modification of rice bran protein by enzymatic hydrolysis and tannic acid: Impacts on structural characteristics and emulsifying properties
abstract: Rice bran protein (RBP) exhibits limited functional properties because of its compact structure, which reduces its interfacial adsorption capacity and consequently constrains its food applications. This study combined moderate enzymatic hydrolysis and non-covalent complexation with tannic acid (TA) to improve RBP functionality. Moderate hydrolysis combined with TA induced protein unfolding via hydrophobic forces and hydrogen bonding. This effectively enhanced the structural flexibility of RBP and improved its interfacial properties, significantly enhancing its emulsifying and foaming capacity. At a mass ratio of 1:0.2 for TA to rice bran protein hydrolysate (RBPH, at a degree of hydrolysis of 4.39%), the emulsifying activity index (EAI) reached 263.42 ± 5.60 m 2 /g, and foaming capacity (FC) 205.33 ± 6.25%. The RBPH-TA complexes effectively stabilized oil-in-water emulsions. TA improved emulsion viscoelasticity and inhibited droplet coalescence. This study introduces a viable strategy to improve RBP functionality and offers mechanistic insights into its emulsion stabilization behavior.

title: Ultrasound-assisted enzymatic synthesis of medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols from tricaprylin and algal oil
abstract: Medium and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs) are functional lipids, but their efficient synthesis in various systems remains challenging. An ultrasound-assisted enzymatic interesterification process was developed using tricaprylin and algal oil as substrates. The optimized enzymatic conditions were obtained by artificial neural network modeling. The structure of enzyme and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of enzymatic process were both evaluated. The results showed that the MLCT yield reached 69.16%, with Cy-Cy-DHA as the predominant product (28.99%). Only slight structural changes were observed in the enzyme after ultrasound treatment, while the apparent reaction rate constant increased by nearly 2.8-fold and the activation energy decreased. CFD showed that ultrasound improved substrate diffusion and mixing with a lower maximum static pressure than stirring (178 vs. 259 Pa), suggesting MLCT synthesis was enhanced mainly by mass transfer intensification. This study provides valuable insights into mechanisms underlying ultrasound-enhanced enzymatic processes and guides their further scale-up and industrial application.

title: 1H NMR fingerprint and chemometric analysis of biochemical stability in fresh cheeses enriched with corn silk, grape seed, and tangerine peel extracts
abstract: This study applied proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR)-based metabolomic and lipidomic profiling to evaluate biochemical stability in ricotta, cottage, and curd cheeses formulated with plant-derived extracts from tangerine peel ( Citrus reticulata ), grape seed ( Vitis vinifera L.), and corn silk ( Stigma maydis ). Cheeses were stored at 4 °C and 12 °C for 14 days, and polar and lipophilic extracts were analyzed. PCA indicated that cheese matrix and storage temperature were the main sources of compositional variation, whereas PLS-DA provided useful predictive discrimination only for cheese type. Corn silk and grape seed extracts were associated with greater preservation of residual carbohydrates and unsaturated lipid signals and lower accumulation of acidogenic and oxidation-related metabolites, whereas tangerine peel showed a weaker protective trend. These findings support 1 H NMR fingerprinting as a useful approach for monitoring freshness-related biochemical changes in fresh cheeses and indicate that selected agro-industrial by-product extracts show potential as ingredients for clean-label preservation strategies. Further chemical characterisation of the extracts and targeted microbiological, physicochemical, sensory, and dose-response studies are required to establish their preservative efficacy and technological applicability.

title: Composition-dependent amorphous matrix formation controls vitamin C stability in reconstituted freeze-dried lactose–whey protein isolate systems
abstract: This study examined how freezing history and matrix composition affected the solid-state structure and post-reconstitution stability of vitamin C in freeze-dried lactose-whey protein isolate (WPI) matrices (lactose:WPI = 4:0, 3:1, 0:4, w/w). The samples were freeze-dried after one- or two-step freezing and characterized using X-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. WPI suppressed lactose crystallization and produced amorphous hydrogen-bonded matrices, whereas lactose-dominant matrices remained highly crystalline. After reconstitution, vitamin C degradation under dark and light storage for 72 h followed a two-parameter Weibull model, which outperformed the first-order kinetics. Matrix composition affected stability more than freezing history: WPI-only matrices had the longest half-lives and retained most of their stability advantage under light, whereas lactose-dominant matrices degraded rapidly under light. These results indicate that protein-rich amorphous matrices improve vitamin C stability, specifically in the reconstituted aqueous state, a condition not captured by evaluating the dry powder alone.

title: Thermal pretreatment-assisted dual-enzyme hydrolysis of steamed skipjack tuna dark muscle for safety-controlled bioactive hydrolysate production
abstract: Steamed skipjack tuna dark muscle (STDM), a protein-rich by-product of tuna canning, is underutilized because of microbial contamination and histamine-related safety concerns. This study developed a safety-controlled hydrolysate through heat pretreatment and sequential Alcalase (AL)-Flavourzyme (FL) hydrolysis. An AL:FL ratio of 4:1 (w/w), 20 mg total enzyme, and sequential addition yielded 56.38% hydrolysis after 5 h. Heat treatment reduced total aerobic bacteria, coliforms, and Escherichia coli below detection limits and was associated with lower relative histamine-forming bacteria-associated DNA signals. It limited further histamine and biogenic amine accumulation during room-temperature exposure without removing preformed amines. Hydrolysis increased total and free amino acids approximately 2.5- and 5.6-fold, respectively, in the resulting hydrolysates. Hydrolysates exhibited over 93% in vitro ABTS radical scavenging activity and 92.42-92.76% in vitro ACE inhibitory activity, alongside altered taste and aroma profiles. These findings support potential use of STDM hydrolysates as protein-based food ingredients for food applications.

title: Using lipidomics to reveal the changes in lipid composition during soymilk processing
abstract: Soybeans are rich in lipids, but the changes in lipids during soymilk processing are not fully understood. In the present study, the changes in different lipid fractions during soymilk processing were detected by nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometry, and the changes in lipid profiles were monitored using ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometry. The results demonstrated that soaking decreased the contents of phospholipids (PL), along with the increases of PL hydrolysis products, whereas cooking decreased the contents of neutral lipids (NL), along with the increases of NL hydrolysis products. Subsequently, the lipidomic profiles confirmed that soaking could increase the abundances of most of triglyceride molecules, while cooking could decrease them; both soaking and cooking could decrease the abundances of most of PL molecules. This finding provides useful insight into lipid changes and the control of beany odor generation during soymilk processing.

title: Changes in antioxidant capacity, flavor, and physicochemical properties during pilot-scale natural fermentation of green plums
abstract: Green plum has nutritional and medicinal value, but its composition changes during long-term natural fermentation. Green plum liquids fermented for 1-4 y were characterized for physicochemical composition, sensory properties, volatile and metabolite profiles, and in vitro antioxidant capacity. The composite in vitro antioxidant index and total flavonoid and polyphenol contents reached minima at 3y and partially recovered at 4y. From 1y to 4y, total acid content decreased by 14.9%, total sugar content peaked at 3y before declining, and total free amino acids increased continuously, nearly doubling by 4y. Sensory profiles varied with fermentation duration, and HS-SPME-GC-MS revealed duration-associated shifts in volatile composition. Non-targeted LC-MS metabolomics identified 147 candidate metabolite annotations that varied among durations after excluding probable exogenous contaminants and pesticide-related annotations. Collectively, this integrated analysis reveals multidimensional quality remodeling during long-term green plum fermentation, offering a basis for process monitoring and quality control.

title: Electrochemical sensing of rutin using MoS₂@f-CB nanocomposite a facile strategy for enhanced sensitivity and selectivity toward real-time detection in natural food samples
abstract: Rutin (RT), a bioactive flavonoid with strong antioxidant properties, is commonly found in various foods. To facilitate its sensitive and portable detection, a novel sensor was developed using a Molybdenum disulfide@functionalized carbon black (MoS₂@f-CB)-modified GCE. The MoS₂@f-CB nanocomposite was synthesized via a hydrothermal process, followed by ultrasonic functionalization of CB with carboxylic acid groups. Characterization using FTIR, XRD, XPS, FE-SEM and HR-TEM confirmed successful integration. Electrochemical techniques, EIS, CV and chronoamperometry, were employed to assess sensor performance. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a LOD of 0.42 μM (S/N = 3), a wide linear range (0.02-8808 μM) and a sensitivity of 0.02 μA μM -1 cm -2 . It also exhibited good selectivity and stability. The sensor's practical utility was validated through the successful detection of RT in foods, with acceptable recovery. These findings underscore the potential of the MoS₂@f-CB nanocomposite as a robust platform for electrochemical sensing in food quality monitoring.

title: An interpretable CNN–grad-CAM framework for detection and quantification of cow milk adulteration in goat milk using excitation–emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopy.
abstract: Cow milk adulteration in goat milk is difficult to detect because of subtle compositional differences. A rapid, non-destructive method combining excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy with a convolutional neural network (CNN) was developed for the detection and quantification of cow milk adulteration. The CNN directly processed raw EEM matrices as image-like inputs without prior fluorescence decomposition. For binary classification, it achieved 98.65% accuracy, with precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score exceeding 98%, whereas it outperformed SVM in seven-class classification. For quantitative prediction, CNN yielded marginally better results than SVR, with an RMSEP of 4.84% and an R P 2 of 0.91, compared with 4.88% and 0.90 for SVR, respectively. Grad-CAM and PARAFAC showed partial overlap between CNN-discriminative and protein-related regions, indicating that protein signals contributed to, but did not solely determine, the model decisions. This EEM-CNN framework enables rapid, interpretable screening of cow milk adulteration in goat milk under controlled conditions.

title: Editorial Board
Apigenin modifies the structure and function of Lactoferrin through non-covalent and covalent binding: Antioxidant, antibacterial, and anticancer activities
abstract: In the food industry, the addition of polyphenols to enhance functional protein performance is a research direction of great interest. In this study, non-covalent (LF + AP) and covalent (LF-AP) complexes of lactoferrin (LF) with apigenin (AP) were prepared and characterized by gel electrophoresis. Fluorescence analysis indicated that hydrophobic interactions were the main driving force for non-covalent binding, whereas the covalent complex exhibited stronger binding affinity. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, circular dichroism, dynamic light scattering, and differential scanning calorimetry analyses showed that covalent binding exerted a more pronounced effect on the particle size, surface hydrophobicity, secondary structure, and thermal stability of LF. Furthermore, both complexes modulated the gastrointestinal digestion behavior and exhibited enhanced in vitro antioxidant, antibacterial, and anticancer activities, with the LF-AP complex demonstrating more pronounced effects. This study presents a novel approach for improving the antibacterial and anticancer potency of LF and potential application as bioactive food ingredients.

title: Fabrication of a high internal phase emulsion stabilized with Pleurotus eryngii protein modified by ultra-high pressure combined with glutamine transaminase treatment as a potential fat substitute in pork patty formulations
abstract: Plant protein-stabilized high internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPEs) represent a promising strategy to replace animal fat in meat products, yet their performance depends critically on protein modification. Pleurotus eryngii protein (PEP) was modified by ultra-high pressure-assisted transglutaminase (TG) crosslinking. This treatment significantly enhanced PEP's emulsifying activity, induced secondary structural rearrangement, increased surface hydrophobicity, and reduced its particle size. The modified PEP successfully stabilized a high internal phase Pickering emulsion (HIPE, 75% oil phase, 4% protein), which exhibited a gel-like network, excellent stability, and an average droplet size of 1.72 μm. In pork patties, substituting 50% animal fat with this HIPE reduced cooking loss and fat exudation by 22.7% and 27.2%, respectively, while simultaneously improving texture, rheology, and sensory acceptability. This study demonstrates that modified PEP-stabilized HIPEs serve as high-performance fat mimics, offering a practical and scalable approach to develop healthier meat products with reduced saturated fat and improved technological properties.

title: Foam-templated dual-network oleogels based on soybean protein isolate-κ-carrageenan and glycerol monostearate for partial cocoa butter replacement in a model chocolate
abstract: Reducing saturated fat while preserving chocolate structure remains a key challenge in fat reformulation. This study developed soybean protein isolate (SPI)-κ-carrageenan (KC)-glycerol monostearate (GMS) dual-network oleogels for partial cocoa butter replacement in a model chocolate. SPI-KC foams prepared at pH 7.0 were lyophilized and infused with soybean oil containing GMS, forming an interconnected polymer-crystal network. The 2.0% SPI-0.6% KC template showed balanced foaming stability, porosity, oil absorption, and oil holding, while 9.0% GMS strengthened oleogel texture and oxidative stability. Replacing 50% cocoa butter reduced saturated fatty acids by >20% and increased unsaturated fatty acids by >25%. Compared with the cocoa-butter control, the oleogel model chocolate retained solid appearance, β(V)-dominant polymorphism, processable Casson parameters, and improved bloom resistance, although it had lower hardness and melting enthalpy. These results support SPI-KC-GMS oleogels as promising partial cocoa butter alternatives, while further refinement of texture, sensory properties, and industrial scalability is still required.

title: Concentration-dependent structural transition and thermoreversible behavior in WPI oleogels containing glyceryl monostearate
abstract: In this study, 2 wt% whey protein isolate (WPI)-based oleogels were constructed using glyceryl monostearate (GMS). The effects of GMS concentration on the microstructure, rheological properties, thermal behavior, crystallinity, oil-holding capacity, and structural recovery of the oleogels were systematically investigated. Increasing GMS concentration progressively transformed the structure from a loose WPI-based matrix to a denser structure with developed crystalline domains. At 3 wt% GMS, a detectable crystalline phase emerged, accompanied by the onset of thermoreversible behavior. Increasing GMS concentration to 5-7 wt% enhanced oil-holding capacity, viscoelasticity, and structural recovery. At 9 wt% GMS, the oleogel exhibited the highest viscosity and crystallinity, but its structural recovery was markedly lower than that of the intermediate-concentration systems. These results demonstrate that the functional properties of low-protein WPI oleogels depend on the concentration-dependent evolution of the crystalline phase rather than on structural reinforcement alone. The findings provide a theoretical basis for regulating the structural and thermal behavior of WPI-based oleogels through GMS concentration.

title: Pulsed electric field pre-treatment of sweet potato: cultivar-dependent effects on phytochemical stability and bioaccessibility
abstract: Pulsed electric field (PEF) pre-treatment is proposed to improve drying and phytochemical bioaccessibility, but its effect in starch-rich matrices is unclear. Three sweet potato cultivars differing in flesh pigmentation were processed into flour under the same nominal PEF treatment (3.1 kV cm −1 ; mean 10.4 kJ kg −1 ) in aqueous medium. PEF did not shorten drying at 75 °C and raised moisture and water activity. It reduced phenolics reaching the intestinal phase in two cultivars, and the purple-fleshed cultivar lost ≈83% of anthocyanins before digestion; without an immersion-only control, this loss most plausibly reflects combined aqueous immersion and electroporation, possibly with oxidative or pH-mediated contributions. Fractionation recovered 87–95% of carotenoids and anthocyanins in an insoluble fibre-, starch-associated fraction. Cultivar dominated colour, composition, and most digestion outcomes (η 2 ≥ 0.52), except anthocyanins, for which PEF and its interaction with cultivar exceeded cultivar; PEF dominated moisture and water activity (η 2 = 0.70–0.74).

title: Hydrolyzed rice glutelin assemblies: how interfacial microstructure and rheology contribute to Pickering emulsion stabilization
abstract: Pickering emulsions stabilized by protein assemblies have attracted increasing attention. However, how protein architectures regulate interfacial and bulk properties to determine emulsion stability remains unclear. In this study, fibrils, particulates, and amorphous assemblies of hydrolyzed rice glutelin (HRG) were prepared. Their interfacial films were evaluated using dilatational rheology, Lissajous curves, and general stress decomposition, while emulsion rheological properties were characterized by mechanical and micro-rheological measurements. HRG fibrils exhibited faster adsorption (0.72 mN/m/s 1/2 ) and penetration rates (3.03 × 10 4 s -1 ), whereas HRG particles showed higher rearrangement rates (9.19 × 10 4 s -1 ). HRG fibrils generated the most stable emulsions by forming elastic interfacial films and dense networks, exhibiting enhanced viscoelasticity, as evidenced by higher storage modulus and complex viscosity. These findings reveal the synergistic roles of interfacial microstructure and rheology in protein-based Pickering emulsion stabilization.

title: Fingerprint spectrum construction for Chinese wolfberry (CW) origin tracing and key element prediction via multi-source data fusion and intelligent algorithms
abstract: Chinese wolfberry (CW), an essential traditional functional food in China, faces challenges like market confusion about its origin and counterfeiting. A multimodal workflow integrating computer vision and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was applied to 120 CW batches from four regions. Chromaticity, visible-light response, Gabor texture, and elemental data were combined to construct a fingerprint for origin discrimination and elemental prediction. Multivariate statistical analysis identified As, Zn, Fe, Energy, yellow-light response, CIE Z, and b ⁎ as key variables with variable importance in projection (VIP) scores greater than 1. After VIP screening, convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved 100.0% training and held-out test accuracy, with a five-fold cross-validation balanced accuracy of 0.988 ± 0.018 and a test Macro-F1 of 1.000; processing time decreased by 31.5%. Temporal Convolutional Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (TCN-GRU) yielded test R 2 values of 0.967-0.977 and RPDp values of 5.52-6.59 for As, Zn, and Fe, outperforming conventional regressors. These findings support multimodal CW evaluation, while broader validation will further improve model robustness.

title: Molecular mechanism of SIRT1 activation by polymethoxyflavonoids derived from citrus peels
abstract: Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) activation by small molecules is linked to aging-related health benefits. We investigated how citrus peel–derived polymethoxyflavonoids (PMFs), 3,5,6,7,8,3′,4′-heptamethoxyflavone (HMF) and 5,6,7,8,3′,4′-hexamethoxyflavone (nobiletin), activate SIRT1. Both compounds modestly but reproducibly increased deacetylase activity toward acetylated p53 and PGC-1α peptides. HMF and nobiletin significantly increased catalytic efficiency ( k cat / K m ) toward both substrates, whereas K m decreased significantly only for the PGC-1α peptide. Residue-resolved NMR analyses localized the PMF-responsive surface to the α2–loop–α3 region of the SIRT1 N-terminal domain (NTD), with overlapping perturbations at T209, E214, L220, I223, and V224. Tryptophan fluorescence-quenching measurements provided complementary evidence. Docking and molecular-dynamics simulations showed that both PMFs remained on this NTD surface while adopting multiple binding modes. Integrative models combining AlphaFold 3–derived SIRT1–substrate complexes with MD-derived PMF poses suggest that NTD-bound PMFs may stabilize a catalytically favorable SIRT1–substrate state, providing molecular insight into SIRT1 activation by citrus-derived PMFs.

title: Perilla essential oil-loaded gelatin–hyaluronic acid films for kiwiberry preservation: Effects of dual crosslinking on film properties and proteomic responses
abstract: A dual-crosslinked gelatin-hyaluronic acid (HA) film loaded with perilla essential oil was developed for Actinidia arguta preservation. Ca 2+ and gallic acid reinforced the film network, giving GH/Ca/A₃ high tensile strength (40.39 MPa), low water vapor permeability (3.34 g/m 2 ·day), improved hydrophobicity, and enhanced thermal stability. During 12 days of storage, the essential oil-free gelatin-HA film (GH-K) reduced fruit weight loss from 40.01% to 17.98%, confirming its physical barrier-based preservation effect under ambient storage conditions. Perilla essential oil further enhanced preservation, reducing weight loss to 10.00%, maintaining firmness at 27.6 N, and lowering total colony and yeast/mold counts to 4.26 and 2.19 log CFU/g, respectively. Proteomics showed that GH/P-K modulated antioxidant defense, glutathione metabolism, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, redox regulation, and cell wall-related pathways, linking film performance with delayed kiwiberry deterioration.

title: Comparative metabolic profiling of different cherry tomato cultivars reveals phytochemical diversity through widely targeted UPLC-MS/MS metabolomics
abstract: Cherry tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L. var. cerasiforme syn. Lycopersicon esculentum var. cerasiforme) is prized for its sensory quality and nutritional value, yet the biochemical networks driving their phenotypic diversity remain incompletely characterized. Widely targeted ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) metabolomic analysis of seven specialty and commercial cherry tomato cultivars quantified 1690 metabolites in this research, uncovering extensive nutritional diversity. Through specific variations in organic acids and umami-enhancing amino acids, differential fluxes in primary carbon and nitrogen metabolism fundamentally reshaped the sensory baseline across the evaluated germplasm. Most strikingly, cultivar 'HF' emerged as a profound metabolic outlier, defined by the exponential hyperaccumulation of highly decorated anthocyanins and flavonols. This superior antioxidant chemotype was mechanistically coupled with an extreme depletion of its absolute upstream precursor, L-phenylalanine. Such an inverse accumulation pattern indicates highly efficient metabolic routing targeted toward the phenylpropanoid pathway, a systemic shift further corroborated by Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. The profiling also captured the unique presence of trace health-promoting constituents, including specific glucosinolates and steroidal alkaloids. Ultimately, this comprehensive metabolomic blueprint elucidates the fundamental biochemical drivers of tomato quality, offering invaluable metabolic markers for evaluating and developing novel functional horticultural foods.

title: Rapid determination of reducing sugars in demerara sugar using a sustainable smartphone-based digital colorimetry approach
abstract: This study presents a novel, eco-friendly, and rapid method for determining low levels of reducing sugars in Demerara sugar using smartphone-assisted digital image colorimetry with the Benedict reaction (DIC-Benedict). Designed as a practical alternative for regulatory analyses, the method emphasizes simplicity, low cost, and on-site applicability. Optimized reagent volume and image acquisition distance ensured robust performance, with adequate linearity (R 2 > 99.8%) and detection and quantification limits of 0.04% and 0.20% ( w / v ), respectively. Matrix effects were minimized by standard addition calibration, ensuring high accuracy (recoveries: 94.9–104.9%) and precision (RSD < 2.0%). Reducing sugar levels in 20 commercial samples ranged from 0.29 to 0.74%, mainly influenced by processing conditions rather than origin. Green metrics (AGREE: 0.6; BAGI: 72.5) confirmed environmental compatibility. Overall, the DIC-Benedict method demonstrates that digital technologies can integrate with classical reactions to provide cost-effective, portable, and sustainable solutions for food analysis and quality control.

title: Rapid and accurate PLS-RBF neural networks for multi-constituent prediction in intact fresh maize kernels using NIR spectroscopy
abstract: Developing robust and accurate near-infrared (NIR) neural network calibration models for intact fresh maize kernels remains challenging in fresh maize breeding. In this study, four rapid and reliable PLS-RBF neural networks were established by integrating PLS feature extraction with ridge-regression-optimized RBF neural networks, to predict the contents of amylopectin, protein, crude fiber, and total sugar in intact fresh maize kernels, respectively. Compared with PCA-based models, PLS-based models consistently exhibited superior predictive performance, with RPD improvements of at least 15.89%,72.85%,54.77% and 19.01% for amylopectin, protein, crude fiber, and total sugar, respectively. The optimized PLS-RBF neural networks presented acceptable predictive performance, with R P 2 value ranging from 0.871 to 0.970 and RPD values between 2.799 and 5.836. Overall, the proposed PLS-RBF neural networks provide efficient, nondestructive approaches for multi-constituent assessment of intact fresh maize kernels and demonstrate considerable potential for practical quality control applications within the collected sample population.

title: Matrix-specific design of food-grade probiotic microcapsules: Wall materials, scalable processing, and AI-enabled optimization
abstract: Microencapsulation of probiotics has been widely studied to improve microbial viability during processing and storage, but its performance in real food systems remains inconsistent because protection, controlled release, sensory acceptability, and manufacturing feasibility must be balanced simultaneously. This review examines key encapsulation techniques by linking microstructural characteristics with practical scale-up constraints. It also discusses wall materials, including polysaccharides, proteins, and prebiotic matrices, with emphasis on their interactions governing encapsulation capacity, swelling behavior, and storage stability. The review further analyzes food matrix adaptability by relating the characteristics and constraints of different food systems to probiotic protection and microcapsule performance and highlights an AI-driven optimization framework that integrates material characteristics, process parameters, food-matrix constraints, and probiotic performance within multivariable and multi-objective design. Future progress requires matrix-specific wall materials and preparation methods, regulatory compliance, scalable manufacturing, and AI-assisted optimization, thereby supporting the transition of probiotic microcapsules from laboratory prototypes to industrial production.

title: Differentiation of roselle calyx preparation by hexane-extractable volatile/semi-volatile profiles and sensory aroma characteristics
abstract: This study characterized the volatile/semi-volatile profiles of roselle calyx preparations using GC-MS analysis of n-hexane extractable compounds obtained by maceration, and aroma characteristics by quantitative descriptive analysis. Independent PCA mapping of volatile/semi-volatile and sensory datasets, together with OPLS-DA, differentiated dried and powder samples to fresh roselle calyx. Fresh calyx and dried calyces (dehydrator- and sun-dried) formed distinct clusters to foamed calyx powders (TBM and SP). Thus, sun-dried and dehydrator-dried calyces showed more similar characteristics to fresh calyx under the evaluated conditions. Fresh calyx was characterized by linoleate, palmitate, phytosterols, and alpha-tocopherol. Both dried calyces were characterized by lupeol, hexahydrofarnesyl acetone, hexadecanoic acid methyl ester, beta-sitosterol, and 2,4-bis(1,1-dimethylethyl)phenol. Foamed calyx powders were characterized by stearic acid and (Z)-9-octadecenamide. Although PCA mapping showed consistent clustering across GC-MS and sensory datasets, the hexane-extractable volatile/semi-volatile profiles did not fully account for the observed sensory aroma characteristics.

title: Fingerprinting ochratoxin in white wine using visible/near-infrared spectroscopy, chemometrics and aquaphotomics
abstract: Wine is regarded as the second most significant source of Ochratoxin A (OTA) when considering the mean European total dietary consumption, just behind cereals, among many foods that may be contaminated with fungi and consequently with OTA. This study employed the use of Visible-Near-infrared spectroscopy (Vis-NIRS) in rapidly detecting different concentrations of OTA in three different brands of white wine at three distinct wavelength ranges and multiple sprectral pre-processing techniques. Variations were observed in the aquagrams indicating distinct water matrix interactions for each wine type, suggesting that the intrinsic water structure and its interactions with wine components differ among Wine1 (W1), Wine2 (W2), and Wine3 (W3). Linear discriminant analysis was effective in classifying OTA concentrations depending on wavelength range and the type of pretreatment. It was easier to rapidly predict OTA in W1 with good accuracies, ranging from R 2 CV of 0.85 to 0.92 while recording RMSE C values below 7μg/L at wavelength ranges 450 nm to 1050 nm, 1200 nm to 1800 nm, 1300 nm to 1600 nm and 2050 nm to 2300 nm. W3 recorded moderately good predictions whiles W2 recorded the lowest predictions. NIRS can potentially serve as a rapid and reliable tool for screening OTA in white wines, with its effectiveness being influenced by the wine matrix and wavelength selection, particularly excelling in predicting OTA concentrations in W1 within the 450-1050 nm and 2050-2300 nm ranges with high accuracy.

title: Microbial fermentation-mediated starch modification: Structural evolution, mechanistic insights, traditional application and future perspectives
abstract: Native starch has intrinsic drawbacks, including retrogradation, syneresis, poor shear stability, weak texture, and low viscosity, which restrict its applications in the food industry worldwide. Fermentation is a mild and sustainable modification method that can reduce retrogradation and syneresis, improve rheological, textural, and thermal properties, and modulate starch digestibility. Unlike previous reviews that mainly summarize fermentation-mediated quality changes, this review integrates predominant microorganisms, fermentation strategies, and traditional food applications, with a core focus on starch functionality. It links alterations in multiscale structure, physicochemical properties, retrogradation behavior, and digestibility to microbial species, substrate sources, and fermentation parameters, thereby exploring the underlying structure-property mechanisms and critically discussing inconsistent findings in the existing literature. Based on genetic engineering and synthetic biology, current challenges and future directions are also discussed, highlighting the potential to shift fermentation from an empirical practice to a controlled, precise technological domain, thereby facilitating the development of functional products with a low glycemic index and longer shelf life.

title: Flaxseed oil cake as a functional ingredient of gluten-free bread: impact on antioxidant properties, volatile organic compounds, and bioaccessibility of minerals
abstract: Gluten-free bread (GFB) often exhibits nutritional imbalances compared with conventional wheat-based bread. Flaxseed oil cake (FOC) is a nutrient-rich by-product containing minerals and bioactive compounds with antioxidant properties. This study evaluated the effects of FOC incorporation into GFB formulations on antioxidant properties, the volatile organic compound (VOCs) profile, and mineral bioaccessibility. The increase in FOC in the GFB formulation was accompanied by a significant (p ≤ 0.05) increase in total phenolic content and the enhancement of the antioxidant potential. Its incorporation also markedly increased total mineral content, although the effect on in vitro bioaccessibility depended on the mineral. FOC incorporation at 5% increased the relative VOC content, while this effect was not observed at 15% and 30% FOC additions. Overall, these findings support the potential of FOC as a value-added ingredient for GFB while contributing to the valorisation of an agri-food by-product.

title: A cost-effective and stable paper-based SERS substrate: DFT-guided design for trace perchlorate detection in goat milk
abstract: This study presents a facile and efficient method for fabricating a paper-based surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate for sensitively determining perchlorate, a persistent environmental pollutant. The fabrication of the substrate involved the formation of a homogeneous silver nanoparticle monolayer on thiol-functionalized filter paper through an interfacial self-assembly process driven by the Marangoni effect, with subsequent functionalization using sodium diethyldithiocarbamate (DDTC) for electrostatic adsorption of perchlorate anions into SERS hotspots. Precise identification of specific normal vibrations associated with DDTC was achieved by density functional theory calculations. The prepared substrate exhibits excellent uniformity, reproducibility, and storage stability. When applied to spiked goat milk samples, the method demonstrates applicability in this complex food matrix, with a detection limit of 42.3 ppb, satisfactory recovery rates (90-95%), and good precision (7.3-8.8%). This work provides a promising platform with potential for on-site screening perchlorate in complex food matrices when coupled with portable Raman instrumentation.

title: Structural characterization and release kinetics of gallic acid–corn starch complexes
Targeted metabolomics reveals differential anthocyanin profiles in blueberry juice after thermal versus ultra-high pressure processing
abstract: This study compared thermal processing (TP; 85 °C, 30 min) and ultra-high pressure processing (UHP; 300-600 MPa, 5-15 min) in terms of their impacts on anthocyanin profiles and the metabolic composition of blueberry juice. TP produced significantly higher total anthocyanin, flavonoid, and phenolic contents alongside stronger antioxidant activity than UHP (p < 0.01). Targeted metabolomics revealed that differential metabolites mapped to the phenylpropanoid biosynthesis pathway under TP: three anthocyanin monomers and five proanthocyanidins increased by 19-181%, while three cyanidin-type monomers decreased by 17-20%, indicating concurrent release and degradation. UHP triggered minor metabolic shifts, with anthocyanin species largely unaltered. These outcomes reflect distinct effects: TP liberates anthocyanins through heat-induced release and proposed endogenous enzyme inactivation, while UHP preserves native anthocyanin profiles through mild non-thermal disruption. Collectively, TP and UHP exert opposing impacts on juice anthocyanins, offering practical guidance for selecting processing technologies to produce anthocyanin-rich juices.

title: Corrigendum to “Enhancing bread anti-staling with glucose-derived Maillard reaction products: In-depth analysis of starches, gluten networks, and moisture status” [Food Chem. 455 (2024) 139760]
Water kefir fermentation of mixed plant-based extracts: effects on antioxidant activity and volatile composition
abstract: Water kefir fermentation was applied to a mixture of hydrosoluble plant-based extracts from cashew nut, coconut, and quinoa to investigate fermentation performance and associated chemical transformations. A mixture experimental design evaluated the effects of substrate composition on microbial growth, physicochemical properties, antioxidant capacity, volatile profile, gastrointestinal stability, and sensory response. Fermentation significantly modulated kefir grain growth, organic acid production, ethanol formation, and carbon dioxide release, with quinoa exerting the strongest effect on fermentation dynamics. The selected centroid formulation exhibited balanced fermentation behavior, stable physicochemical characteristics, and relevant protein, lipid, mineral, and antioxidant contents. SPME-GC-MS analysis revealed pronounced changes in the volatile profile, including increased alcohol and ethyl ester formation and reduced aldehyde levels. In vitro digestion revealed differential microbial survival after the intestinal phase, with yeasts showing greater persistence than bacterial groups. Despite increased chemical complexity, the fermented beverage showed lower sensory acceptance, highlighting the need for process optimization.

title: Ultrasound and γ-aminobutyric acid improve quality of Chinese kale sprouts through coordinated metabolic regulation: insights from multi-omics analysis
abstract: Brassica sprouts are valued for their abundant bioactive compounds and strong antioxidant capacity. This study evaluated the effects of ultrasound, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA), and their combination on the growth, nutritional quality, and metabolic regulation of Chinese kale sprouts. All treatments promoted growth and enhanced soluble sugars, proteins, pigments, antioxidant-related compounds, and glucosinolates, although their effects varied among quality attributes. The combined treatment produced pronounced improvements in plant height, soluble sugars and proteins, pigments, and ascorbic acid. Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed coordinated regulation of primary and secondary metabolism, involving carbohydrate and glutathione metabolism, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and glucosinolate biosynthesis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified CAD and COMT as hub genes, along with key transcription factors including WRKY75, GATA22, MYB108, and ERF113. These findings indicate that ultrasound and GABA improve sprout quality through coordinated metabolic and transcriptional regulation, providing a theoretical basis for the application of elicitation strategies in sprout production.

title: Terpenoids in Baijiu: sensory evidence, formation pathways and analytical confidence
abstract: Terpenoids are structurally diverse, isoprene-derived compounds, several of which are volatile and contribute to aroma complexity in fermented foods. In Baijiu, although less abundant than esters and alcohols, low-threshold terpenoids such as β-damascenone, linalool and α-terpineol can shape floral, fruity, herbal and woody notes. Current evidence links their occurrence to raw materials, microbial transformation during solid-state fermentation, and reactions during distillation, storage and aging, but cross-study comparison remains limited by inconsistent flavor types, sampling designs, analytical platforms and identification criteria. This review distinguishes reported occurrence from sensory validation and evaluates formation pathways, application relevance and analytical confidence of Baijiu terpenoids. Key gaps include incomplete annotation, poor quantitative comparability, weak pathway validation and limited sensory confirmation. Addressing these gaps will require targeted and untargeted volatilomics, multi-omics, isotope tracing, controlled fermentation, and odor activity, omission and recombination tests to strengthen the mechanistic basis for flavor regulation and Baijiu quality assessment.

title: Concentration-dependent modulation of the aroma profile of Jiang-flavor Baijiu by isoamyl alcohol through noncovalent interactions with key aroma compounds
abstract: Isoamyl alcohol (IAA), a key higher alcohol in Baijiu, is capable of both enhancing and disrupting aroma balance depending on its concentration. This study investigates its concentration-dependent role using recombination models with quantitative descriptive analysis, molecular dynamics simulations and 1 H NMR spectroscopy. At 200-400 mg/L, IAA enhanced floral and fruity aromas while suppressing acidic and roasted aroma, consistent with reduced compound volatility. Above 600 mg/L, the inhibitory effect on aroma release weakened. These concentration-dependent effects on aroma are driven by changes in compound volatility mediated by hydrogen bond, with van der Waals and Coulomb interactions contributing. 1 H NMR confirmed hydrogen bonding between IAA and aroma compounds via 0.05-0.09 ppm downfield shifts. Notably, the 400-650 mg/L range represents a pivotal transition window for sensory traits, compound volatility and hydrogen bond formation with IAA. However, a limitation remains in fully bridging the nonlinear gap between microscopic molecular interactions and human olfactory perception, as in vivo sensory integration involves complex perceptual mechanisms beyond physical volatility modulation.

title: Corrigendum to “Mechanisms of fructose-to-mannitol conversion in citrus juice fermented by fructophilic Leuconostoc mesenteroides” [Food Chem. 526 (2026) 150844]
Hydrophobic TMCS-modified MIL-101(Fe) for highly efficient and reusable detoxification of Ochratoxin a in edible oil and protein-rich meal
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) contamination poses significant risks to food safety. In this study, TMCS-modified MIL-101(Fe) was synthesized as an efficient adsorbent for OTA removal. The material exhibited excellent structural stability and adsorption performance, achieving 96% OTA removal under optimized conditions (adsorbent dosage: 0.8 mg mL -1 , pH 7.0, and 333 K), with an adsorption capacity of 10.917 mg g -1 . Kinetic analysis revealed rapid adsorption equilibrium within 10 min, while thermodynamic studies indicated a spontaneous and endothermic adsorption process. Molecular docking demonstrated that hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, and electrostatic interactions contributed to OTA binding. Furthermore, TMCS-MIL-101(Fe) achieved OTA removal efficiencies of 87% and 72% in spiked rapeseed oil and peanut meal systems, respectively, highlighting its potential for mycotoxin detoxification in complex food matrices.

title: PUL/HPMC water-in-water Pickering emulsions: A food-grade microculture platform for efficient encapsulation and cultivation of Lactobacillus plantarum
abstract: In this study, pullulan-in-hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (PUL/HPMC) water-in-water Pickering emulsions stabilized by cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were prepared for the encapsulation and cultivation of L. plantarum. Results demonstrated that CNCs were mainly adsorbed at the PUL-HPMC interface, thereby effectively inhibiting the aggregation and coalescence of emulsion droplets. L. plantarum was encapsulated in emulsions and primarily distributed in the PUL phase. It was found that the optimal encapsulation concentration of L.plantarum was 9.67 log CFU/g, and the optimal addition of MRS broth was 1.0 wt%. Finally, the viable counts of L.plantarum increased from 4.44 to 7.42 log CFU/g during 30 h of cultivation. Furthermore, an initial pH 5.5 afforded the optimal cultivation performance for L.plantarum, with viable counts increasing from 4.00 to 7.06 log CFU/g during 24 h of cultivation. This study provides a novel microculture platform for efficient L.plantarum cultivation and fully aqueous emulsion systems with food-grade application potential for probiotics-based functional foods.

title: An all-in-one Zn/Ce-MOF nanozyme: combining ratiometric sensing, oxidase-like activity, and apparent phosphoester hydrolase-like behavior for organophosphorus pesticide monitoring
abstract: The widespread residue of highly toxic organophosphorus pesticides (OPs) poses a serious threat to food safety and human health, underscoring the need for sensitive screening methods. In this work, a ratiometric fluorescence sensor array was constructed based on a trifunctional Zn/Ce-MOF exhibiting intrinsic blue fluorescence, oxidase-like activity, and apparent phosphoester hydrolase-like behavior. LC-HRMS full-scan analysis further showed DDV signal depletion accompanied by a marked increase in a DMP-assigned signal after 90 min. Ce sites promoted o-phenylenediamine (OPD) oxidation to produce yellow-fluorescent 2,3-diaminophenazine (DAP), which attenuated the intrinsic fluorescence through the inner filter effect. Upon addition of OPs, the DAP-associated emission decreased while the intrinsic fluorescence of Zn/Ce-MOF recovered, resulting in a ratiometric response (F 565 /F 440 ). Meanwhile, the fluorescence variation enabled visible color changes and smartphone-assisted signal acquisition based on red, green, and blue (RGB) analysis. The proposed sensor exhibited two linear response regions toward DDV over the final concentration ranges of 0-5 and 5-30 μg/mL, with a detection limit of 0.043 μg/mL. The sensing platform was preliminarily evaluated through post-extraction matrix-spike experiments for DDV in tenfold-diluted tomato and spinach extracts, yielding post-extraction matrix-spike recoveries of 93.5-121.5%. Multivariate analysis of F 565 /F 440 , G/B, and R/G signals revealed characteristic distribution, separation, and clustering patterns for five OP standards, including dichlorvos (DDV), dimethoate (DM), chlorpyrifos (CPF), methyl parathion (MP), and trichlorfon (TCF), in standard solutions. The study therefore provides a Zn/Ce-MOF-based strategy for smartphone-assisted DDV screening in tenfold-diluted tomato and spinach extracts and multichannel response-pattern analysis of five OP standards under controlled conditions. Further studies will evaluate the applicability of the multichannel response patterns to multiple OPs in complex food matrices.

title: Phenolic-focused untargeted ion mobility LC-MS metabolomics reveals season-associated chemical signatures in Scottish honey
abstract: Honey authenticity is compromised by mislabelled origin, blending, and product modification, undermining traceability and consumer trust. To address this, we developed a phenolic-focused, untargeted ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-ion mobility-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UHPLC-IM-QTOF-MS) workflow for profiling Scottish honeys using a low-solvent extraction approach and collision cross section-supported annotation (CCS-SA). Thirty-nine samples, including Scottish heather, spring, and summer honeys together with market-relevant comparators, were analysed to investigate compositional variation linked to origin, season, and product type. The workflow produced a robust, quality-controlled feature set with strong dilution linearity, while integration of accurate mass, retention time, MS/MS, and CCS increased confidence in marker annotation. Paired within-apiary comparison provided robust evidence that spring and summer honeys carry distinct season-associated chemical signatures, and heather honey emerged as a chemically distinct class. Exploratory analyses also indicated differences between Scottish and non-Scottish honeys and compositional shifts associated with blending and infusion. Because several comparator groups were small and unbalanced, these findings are considered preliminary. Overall, the workflow provides a robust platform for characterising seasonal variation and discovering candidate authenticity markers in Scottish honey.

title: Sequential supercritical CO₂ and microwave-assisted extraction for dual valorization of berry pomace
abstract: In this study, redcurrant, blackcurrant, blueberry, and chokeberry pomace were valorized using supercritical CO₂ extraction (SC-CO₂) followed by microwave-assisted extraction of defatted residues. SC-CO₂ yielded 2.75-7.46% lipid fraction, rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, mainly linoleic acid, with β-sitosterol as the predominant phytosterol. Redcurrant lipid fraction showed the highest tocopherol content. Chokeberry defatted pomace exhibited the highest total polyphenols, anthocyanins, and antioxidant capacity. UPLC-MS/MS identified over 40 phenolic compounds, with the highest anthocyanin content in chokeberry. Preliminary biological testing showed mild antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity of chokeberry and blueberry extracts at 0.007-0.014 mg polyphenols/mL, while 0.5 mg polyphenols/mL was associated with cytotoxic effects. No clear genotoxic effects were observed for blueberry, blackcurrant, or redcurrant extracts, whereas chokeberry extract showed genotoxicity at higher concentrations. Overall, berry pomace emerged as a promising source of both lipophilic and hydrophilic bioactive fractions, with concentration- and cell-specific biological effects.

title: Chemometric and ultraviolet-visible spectrometric methods for simultaneous determination of caffeine, trigonelline, and chlorogenic acid in instant coffees
