abstract: New methods for simultaneous determination of caffeine (CAF), trigonelline (TRIG), and chlorogenic acid (CGA) in instant coffees using UV-Vis spectrometry and multivariate calibration (full-PLS, iSPA-PLS, and SPA-MLR) algorithms are presented. Instant coffees were analyzed using the reference HPLC method to determine CAF, TRIG, and CGA concentrations. The dataset, comprising UV-Vis spectra and reference HPLC concentrations, was split into calibration (71 samples) and prediction (47 samples) sets; cross-validation was performed within the calibration set. The proposed methods yielded RPD pred > 3 for TRIG and CAF determinations, indicating excellent performance, and RPD pred ≤ 2 for CGA, suggesting poor performance or suitability for screening. This work offers an innovative, green, fast, and low-cost alternative to HPLC for complementary screening or routine analyses. This alternative requires no organic solvents and generates no waste. Moreover, it uses an inexpensive instrument that records the spectrum in just 1 s, whereas the HPLC run takes 20 min.

title: Coordinated improvement of shrimp Litopenaeus vannamei preservation quality during super-chilling at −3 °C by combination of chitosan coating with vacuum packing: Efficiency and mechanism
abstract: The quality deterioration of Litopenaeus vannamei during super-chilling exerts a critical challenge for shrimp industry. This study proposes a "antibacterial and oxygen removal-dependent coupling" mechanism to address this challenge. The efficacy of chitosan coating (CC) combined with vacuum packaging (VP) on quality indicators was investigated. Remarkably, the highest sensory score, desirable values of hardness and springiness, the lowest TVB-N contents and activities of protease and polyphenols oxidase (PPO), as well as the significant decrease in TVC and Pseudomonas counts were observed in CC + VP group (P < 0.05). Furthermore, scanning electron microscopy revealed the desirable integrity of myofibrils in CC + VP group than in the samples of CC or VP groups and molecular docking visualized the strong affinity between chitosan with the active sites of PPO, serine protease, calpain and cathepsin B/L in shrimp muscle. Taken together, this study highlights the potential of CC + VP for maintaining shrimp quality during super-chilling.

title: Effect of subcritical water-mediated dual-protein conformational reconstruction on texture, digestibility, and release kinetics of curcumin-based meat floss analogue
abstract: The poor stability and bioavailability of curcumin (Cur) limit its application in functional foods. This study employed green subcritical water treatment (SWT) to reconstruct the wheat bran-textured soy protein matrix into an efficient delivery system for Cur. SWT transformed the proteins into a homogeneous porous network that, when applied to a Cur-loaded meat floss analogue, resulted in a high encapsulation efficiency (∼90%) and enhanced digestibility. At the molecular level, this restructuring created a favorable hydrophobic binding pocket for Cur (key residues, Ile48 and Phe12), with an exceptionally strong binding affinity driven by van der Waals forces. Consequently, Cur release followed diffusion-controlled kinetics, resulting in a higher release rate and the retention of more than 80% of its antioxidant activity after simulated digestion. This work demonstrates that SWT effectively engineers plant proteins from molecular conformation to macroscopic functionality, offering a sustainable strategy for designing high-performance functional foods with controlled nutrient delivery.

title: Recyclable magnetic ionic liquid-based aqueous two-phase for rapid extraction of trace quinolones in honey
abstract: A novel aqueous two-phase system based on diimidazolium magnetic ionic liquids (MIL-ATPS) was developed for the extraction and determination of trace quinolones (QNs) in honey. The MIL-ATPS achieved extraction efficiencies over 95% and partition coefficients exceeding 200 under optimal conditions, while maintaining good recyclability over at least five cycles without efficiency loss. The method showed satisfactory sensitivity, with limits of detection (LODs) and quantification (LOQs) of 2.853-3.772 μg/L and 8.647-11.43 μg/L, respectively. Satisfactory analytical results were obtained in honey samples, with spiked recovery rates of 97-104% and a relative standard deviation (RSD) below 3%. The intra-day and inter-day precisions ranged from 0.40% to 2.83% and 0.09% to 3.16%, respectively. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that the MIL could form stable host-guest complexes with the three QNs, providing molecular-level support for the favorable extraction behavior. Our finding provides a rapid, solvent-free, magnetic approach for sensitive antibiotic detection in food.

title: Electrochemical biosensor for rapid quantification of hyaluronic acid using a carbohydrate-binding module as the recognition element
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is increasingly incorporated into functional foods, and its rapid quantification is essential for quality control and process monitoring. Here, an electrochemical biosensor was developed using a carbohydrate-binding module (CBM) as the molecular recognition element. The immobilized CBM selectively binds HA at the electrode interface, forming an insulating complex that modulates electron transfer and generates a concentration-dependent electrochemical signal. The biosensor enables rapid HA determination within 10 min and exhibits a broad working range of 5-10,000 μg/mL. The platform exhibits analytical selectivity toward HA and supports reliable quantification in the evaluated matrices. The method was successfully applied to food samples and fermentation broths, showing good agreement with the conventional carbazole assay. Integration with a portable system supports the feasibility of on-site HA measurement. This CBM-based biosensor provides a rapid and reliable strategy for HA detection, with practical potential in food systems and biomanufacturing.

title: Intelligent packaging for tofu preservation: a comprehensive review of advanced materials and pathways toward integrated AI-driven systems
abstract: Tofu, a highly perishable and increasingly popular global staple, has received limited research attention regarding intelligent packaging. This review systematically consolidates recent advances, spanning molecular spoilage mechanisms to prospective integrated AI-driven systems. It analyzes two main pillars: advanced materials-evolving from controlled-release to stimuli-responsive systems-highlighting development directions for tofu-specific smart packaging; and sensing technologies-including visual indicators and embedded sensors-documenting failure modes and matrix interference. The discussion culminates in a conceptual framework for AI-enabled systems, noting that no fully integrated implementation currently exists for tofu. It identifies integration gaps, hardware constraints, and the absence of tofu-specific datasets. Additionally, IoT and blockchain technologies are evaluated for connectivity and trust throughout the supply chain. Finally, key commercialization challenges-technical, economic, regulatory, and environmental-are synthesized, and a co-design research agenda is proposed. This work provides a roadmap for next-generation intelligent packaging to enhance shelf life, safety, and supply chain efficiency for tofu and other perishable foods.

title: Influence of protein source and polysaccharide structuring agents on water immobilisation and gel properties of fermented high-protein desserts
abstract: The influence of protein source and polysaccharide structuring agents on thermal behaviour, water immobilisation and gel properties of high-protein desserts was investigated. Desserts formulated with whey protein isolate or yeast protein and structured with furcellaran in the presence of inulin or maltodextrin were evaluated using differential scanning calorimetry, rheological measurements, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and texture analysis. Whey protein systems formed more elastic and deformation-resistant gels, exhibiting higher water-holding capacity (93.2-95.2%) and greater yield strain (4.35-4.53) than yeast protein systems (65.2-73.8% and 0.23-1.66, respectively). In contrast, yeast protein systems showed greater variation in freezable water enthalpy (114-251 J/g). Inulin reduced water activity (0.938-0.940) and promoted more cohesive matrices, whereas maltodextrin produced softer gels (hardness 0.06-0.08 N). Overall, protein source and polysaccharide composition significantly affected water organisation, thermal behaviour and gel properties of fermented high-protein desserts.

title: Whey protein isolate as a modifier of texture and digestibility in ready-to-eat corn paste
abstract: Corn paste is widely consumed worldwide, but starch pastes often suffer from poor texture and lumping during hot-water reconstitution. This study introduces whey protein isolate (WPI) to regulate protein-starch-water interactions and improve rehydrated corn paste quality. WPI was added before or after extrusion to evaluate its effects on physicochemical, rheological, and nutritional properties. Pre-extrusion addition of 3% WPI significantly enhanced texture, water and oil absorption, and reduced solubility and bulk density. Microstructural analysis showed smoother surfaces and the disappearance of serrated cross sections. X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirmed A + V-type crystalline structures after extrusion. Rheological results indicated a shift from an elasticity-dominated to a viscosity-dominated system, improving dispersion and reconstitution. Nutritionally, pre-extrusion WPI protected tea polyphenols during digestion and reduced estimated glycemic index (eGI) by 10-15%. These findings support the use of pre-extrusion WPI to develop protein-fortified, relatively low-GI instant corn paste products.

title: pH-switchable multi-enzyme-like activities of Bi12Co0.6O18.8-AuNPs nanozyme: An electrochemical-colorimetric dual-mode aptasensor for ultrasensitive Cd2+ detection in rice
abstract: The severe health risks associated with cadmium-contaminated food necessitate the development of accurate and rapid detection technologies. Herein, a novel pH-switchable multi-enzyme activity Bi 12 Co 0.6 O 18.8 -AuNPs is designed to construct a dual-mode aptasensor for the rapid and reliable detection of Cd 2+ . This nanozyme exhibits pH-modulated catalytic behaviors, demonstrating peroxidase-like activity under acidic conditions (pH 4) to catalyse the H 2 O 2 -mediated oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine for visual colorimetric detection, while switching to catalase-like activity at slightly alkaline conditions (pH 8) to decompose H 2 O 2 into O 2 , thereby generating a measurable electrochemical signal. Benefiting from the collaborative enhancement mechanism of the dual-mode strategy through cross-validation and the high specificity of aptamer recognition, the sensor achieves highly precise and reliable detection of Cd 2+ . The sensor shows ultra-sensitive detection with limits of detection of 9.23 pg/mL (colorimetric) and 0.43 pg/mL (electrochemical). Its successful application in real rice samples confirms its practical utility for food safety monitoring.

title: Discovering new potential in a native fruit byproduct: An unprecedented evaluation of the composition and properties of cambucá seed (Plinia edulis (Vell.) Sobral)
abstract: Cambucá seed is an unexploited native byproduct. To support complete fruit utilization, the nutritional, physicochemical, and technological properties and bioactive potential of cambucá seed were investigated. High carbohydrate content was found (56.28%), with starch predominating within this fraction (27.64%), while dietary fiber accounted for 36.68%, all on a dry basis. The seed showed high potassium content (4.88 mg.g −1 fresh seed), with potentially toxic metals below regulatory limits. Twenty-three volatile compounds and eight organic acids indicated sensory complexity, complemented by four anthocyanins responsible for purple coloration. The phenolic profile showed predominance of insoluble-bound compounds, with gallic acid as the major compound (3373.08 μg.g −1 fresh seed). These bioactive compounds contributed to high antioxidant capacity, especially in the ORAC assay (2643.74 μmo lTE.g −1 fresh seed). The seed composition resulted in high thermal stability and a specific paste-forming profile. Overall, cambucá seed is a sustainable coproduct with potential for developing high-value innovative products.

title: Metabolomic profiling of pumpkin (Cucurbita spp.) male flowers using integrated LC–HRMS, GC–MS and 1H NMR
abstract: Pumpkin ( Cucurbita spp.) male flowers are edible tissues traditionally consumed in several regions worldwide; however, information regarding their metabolite composition remains limited. In this study, four agronomically important pumpkin varieties cultivated in northeastern Brazil were investigated using an integrated metabolomics workflow combining LC–HRMS, GC–MS and 1 H NMR. The complementary analytical platforms enabled the annotation of 151 metabolites spanning amino acids, carbohydrates, phenylpropanoids, flavonoids, terpenoids, fatty acids and other specialized metabolites, while increasing annotation confidence through orthogonal analytical information. Multivariate and univariate analyses revealed clear genotype-dependent metabolic differences, particularly in carbohydrate, amino acid and phenolic metabolism, whereas PCA showed no clear separation according to planting-bed position. The integrated analytical strategy broadened chemical coverage beyond that achievable with any individual platform and provided new insights into the molecular composition of pumpkin flowers. These findings strengthen current knowledge of Cucurbitaceae floral metabolism and support the nutritional, technological and economic valorization of pumpkin flowers as an underexplored edible resource.

title: A metrologically traceable approach for quantifying proteinaceous fining agents by HPLC-HRMS
abstract: Residual proteins from fining agents such as egg albumen and animal gelatin may persist in wine, raising food safety and labelling concerns. This study develops a metrologically traceable HPLC-HRMS workflow for the absolute quantification of proteotypic peptides from ovalbumin, ovotransferrin, lysozyme, and collagen α1/α2, using isotope-dilution mass spectrometry in parallel reaction monitoring mode. Method development, calibration hierarchy, and uncertainty evaluation were fully established in ammonium bicarbonate buffer, achieving good calibration linearity (chi-square values below 1) and LOQs of 0.63 to 1.16 mg/L. Wine was evaluated only as a post-extraction matrix effect, through matrix-matched calibration in a reference red wine. Expanded uncertainties were comparable between buffer (28.6-36.6%) and wine extract (27.8-36.2%), indicating that matrix effects had limited impact despite peptide-dependent signal suppression. This framework offers a solid, SI-traceable analytical foundation, established in buffer, for future validation in fortified wine samples, supporting quantitative allergen assessment in winemaking.

title: Pilot scale, supercritical CO2 extraction of lipids and bioactive compounds from tiger nuts co-products: Green chemistry metrics and life-cycle assessment
abstract: Supercritical CO 2 (scCO 2 ) extraction of food wastes has emerged in the recent decades as a sustainable approach towards valorization and reduction of environmental footprint. We present for the first time an upcycling of tiger nuts co-products enabled by scCO 2 at a pilot level that paves the way for an industrial scale-up. The method demonstrated a great potential, with a noted 77% yield towards a good quality oil rich in oleic acid (71%), linoleic acid (10%), bioactive molecules (tocopherols, 0.114 g/100 g), or minerals (Fe, Mg, P). The post-extraction solid is rich in fibre (50% w/w), suggesting a potential scenario for sustainable food systems. The environmental sustainability of the process was measured by Green Chemistry Metrics (GCPMs) and Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), which revealed that the production of 1 kg of oil at industrial scale could reach an endpoint single score value of 1 Pt under the ReCiPe methodology.

title: Zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (7, 8, 9, and 67) for removal of aflatoxin M1 from raw cattle milk
abstract: This investigation demonstrates the applicability of four synthesized and characterized metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), ZIF-7, ZIF-8, ZIF-9, and ZIF-67, for the removal of aflatoxin M1 (AFM1) from cattle milk. Experiments assessed the removal of AFM1 at different concentrations (100 to 1100 ng L -1 ). The efficiency of ZIFs for adsorbing AFM1 was affected by the adsorbate concentration, indicating that an increase in AFM1 concentrations of milk samples could result in a decrease in AFM1 removal efficiency. The order of removal efficiency was: ZIF-8 > ZIF-7 > ZIF-67 > ZIF-9. ZIF-8 had the highest removal efficiencies. The AFM1 in the milk sample treated ZIF-8 never exceeded the USFDA maximum safety limit (500 ng L -1 ); however, at AFM1 concentrations ≥700 ng L -1 , ZIF-8 was not capable of maintaining the AFM1 concentrations below the limit of the EU and Codex Alimentarius (50 ng L -1 ). Hence, some ZIFs can serve as effective adsorbents for removing AFM1 from real samples.

title: Revealing the influence on nanoparticle formation and antioxidant efficacy from aging in Liupao tea via integrated physicochemical, metabolomic, and elementomic approaches
abstract: Nanoparticles are bioactive carriers with significant application value, and the aging influence on the formation and bioactivity of Liupao tea nanoparticles (LTNs) was investigated in this study. Stable spherical nanoparticles with diameters of 100-500 nm were present in Liupao tea infusions, and polysaccharides as well as proteins were their primary components. Multi-omics analysis showed that glycosylated flavonoids accumulated in LTNs5 and LTNs15, and amino acids and K were enriched in LTNs5, LTNs10, and LTNs15, which were associated with smaller particle size and higher antioxidation. In contrast, methylated flavonoids, methylxanthine alkaloids, Ca, Al, and Mn concentrated in samples with larger particle sizes and lower antioxidation, such as LTNs0, LTNs3, and LTNs8. Interestingly, consistent changes of polyphenols and Cu suggested a potential synergistic role in the formation and bioactivity of LTNs. Overall, these findings enhanced the understanding of the connection between vintage quality and functional value in Liupao tea.

title: Single-drop detection of sulfamethoxazole in milk using MOF@MIP electrochemical sensor with DFT-guided imprinting strategy
abstract: The study presents the development of a disposable electrochemical sensor based on lanthanide metal-organic frameworks (Ln-MOFs) and molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) for detecting the veterinary antibiotic sulfamethoxazole (SMX) in single-drop mode. The Ln-MOF was synthesised using La(NO 3 ) 3 and 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene (H 3 BTB), yielding La-BTB, followed by modification of the screen-printed gold electrode (SPGE) with La-BTB. DFT calculations were used to investigate the formation of the pre-reaction complex prior to the molecular imprinting process, on the basis of which the most suitable functional monomer (FM) was identified and selected. The MIP was formed on the SPGE/La-BTB electrode via electropolymerization using o-phenylenediamine (oPD) as FM. The developed MOF@MIP-based sensor detects SMX over a wide concentration range (1 pmol/L to 11 μmol/L), providing a picomolar detection limit of 0.6 pmol/L. The proposed platform was successfully applied to detect SMX in milk and tap water, confirming its substantial potential for point-of-care implementation in real-matrix analysis.

title: Divergent specificity of PatA, GabT, and IlvE defines the branched transamination of Nε-carboxymethyllysine and its metabolite N-carboxymethylcadaverine in Escherichia coli
abstract: -carboxymethyllysine (CML), a key advanced glycation end product (AGE) and marker of the Maillard reaction in food. Escherichia coli utilizes CML as a nitrogen source. While SpeC initiates degradation by decarboxylating CML to N-carboxymethylcadaverine (CM-Cad), the enzymes liberating the nitrogen remained unknown. Here, we identify PatA, GabT, and IlvE as glutamate-dependent transaminases responsible for CML and CM-Cad transamination. Our results reveal a branched metabolic network, not a linear pathway: PatA shows specificity toward both substrates, while GabT and IlvE selectively process CM-Cad and CML, respectively. We further demonstrate that the carboxymethyl piperideinium ion (CM-Pip) is formed following CM-Cad transamination and tentatively identify the previously unknown carboxymethyl-tetrahydropicolinic acid (CM-THPA) as a novel metabolite in CML metabolism. Combining molecular microbiology, biochemistry, and analytical chemistry, we define a branched transaminase network that integrates dietary CML into bacterial nitrogen metabolism, providing a model for microbial AGE processing via underground metabolism.

title: Cyclodextrin hydrophobic cavity size directs soy protein thermal stability and gelation behavior
abstract: Enhancing thermal stability in high-content soy protein solutions (SPs) is crucial. Cyclodextrins (CDs), with their distinctive hydrophobic cavities, are commonly used as stabilizers in food systems. This study investigates the effects of cyclodextrins with different cavity sizes (α-CD, β-CD, and γ-CD) and preheating on the thermal stability of soy proteins (SPs). The results show that all CDs improved reheating stability, but their effects were cavity-size dependent. Larger cavities enhanced binding to exposed hydrophobic groups and increased electrostatic repulsion; γ-CD reduced surface hydrophobicity from 197.38 to 148.74. CD addition also markedly suppressed gelation by lowering G', delaying gelation, and increasing water mobility, with γ-CD showing the strongest effect. These results identify cavity size as a key structural parameter for CD-mediated stabilization and establish γ-CD as the optimal stabilizer for formulating thermally stable, high-protein soy liquid foods.

title: Cold-gelation-related functionality of hot-air-popped flours from pigmented popcorn (Zea mays var. ‘Everta’), sorghum (Sorghum bicolor), and amaranth (Amaranthus sp.)
abstract: Hot-air popping promotes grain matrix reorganization and may enhance cold-gelation functionality in grain flours. This study evaluated the structural, techno-functional, and rheological properties of pigmented popcorn, sorghum, and amaranth flours after hot-air popping using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, pasting analysis, and rheology. Popping increased β-sheet (56%) in purple popcorn and reduced crystalline order (2.4% and 0%) in red sorghum and amaranth, respectively. Microscopy revealed expanded porous structures. These modifications improved water absorption (6.5%), swelling capacity (572%), and oil absorption (7%), and increased initial viscosity in yellow popcorn and amaranth (1.21 and 1.03 Pa•s, respectively), as well as viscoelastic behavior. Popcorn and sorghum showed pronounced structural reorganization associated with enhanced gel-forming potential. The results demonstrate that hot-air popping is an effective, low-energy process for modifying grain structure and promoting cold-gelation functionality, supporting the development of clean-label ingredients for food formulations requiring viscosity and texture enhancement under mild conditions.

title: Retrospective screening of food contaminants in Total diet study (TDS) samples over more than a decade: Complementarity between LRMS and HRMS systems in food safety
abstract: This study explores the potential of liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) for the retrospective analysis of samples from French Total Diet Studies. Composite babyfoods, sugary products and seafood samples were analysed by LC-HRMS using complementary targeted and suspect-screening approaches. Historical TDS analyses, carried-out using various compound-specific analytical methods, including LC/GC-MS/MS, had previously reported 28 chemicals in these samples. While direct comparisons with historical LC/GC-MSMS data are precluded by strong methodological discrepancies, LC-HRMS analysis provided additional chemical information on the archived samples. Indeed, 18 compounds were detected and confirmed (confidence-level 1), 21 could be annotated with a confidence-level 2a, while >100 features were detected but lacking MS/MS confirmation. LC-HRMS provided complementary data to historical monitoring and demonstrated its potential as an early-warning tool for reporting emerging chemicals. Operating in full-scan mode, HRMS systems generate comprehensive and complementary datasets that can be analysed retrospectively, supporting long-term food safety monitoring.

title: Quercetin attenuates acrylamide-induced damage to largemouth bass myofibrillar protein and associated gut health impairments
abstract: Thermal processing can enhance the nutritional quality and flavor of aquatic products; however, hazardous compounds such as acrylamide formed during the process may exert adverse effects on proteins and intestinal health. In this study, myofibrillar protein (MP) extracted from Largemouth Bass was used as a model to systematically investigate the regulatory effects of quercetin on acrylamide-induced protein damage and intestinal health impairment. The results showed that AA treatment significantly increased the particle size of MP, promoted protein aggregation, and markedly reduced the α-helix content, indicating severe structural disruption. Quercetin pretreatment effectively mitigated these structural alterations, with the most pronounced effect observed at a concentration of 3%, where the particle size decreased to 106.98 μm and the α-helix content increased to 22.42%. Furthermore, results from in vitro digestion and gut microbiota fermentation revealed that AA significantly decreased the digestibility of MP (from 76.68% to 54.87%, p < 0.01), reduced Caco-2 cell viability, and increased the apoptosis rate. Pretreatment with 3% quercetin markedly improved protein digestibility (71.88%), enhanced Caco-2 cell viability, and inhibited apoptosis. Overall, this study elucidates the detrimental effects of acrylamide on MPs and intestinal health and demonstrates the potential of quercetin in alleviating acrylamide-induced damage, providing a theoretical basis for the application of natural bioactives in improving the nutritional quality of aquatic products and controlling hazardous compounds during processing.

title: Time-resolved monitoring of key tea fermentation indicators via Raman–NIR spectroscopic fusion and deep learning-based predictive modeling
abstract: Routine monitoring of black tea fermentation relies on destructive and time-consuming wet chemistry methods. Therefore, a non-destructive analytical strategy combining Raman and near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with deep learning was developed for simultaneously monitoring key fermentation indicators. Fresh Camellia sinensis leaves were fermented for 4 h under controlled temperature and humidity, with samples collected at nine time points. Concentrations of total tea polyphenols, theabrownins, and theaflavins were determined using standard reference methods, while corresponding Raman spectra (400-2500 cm -1 ) and NIR spectra (970-1700 nm) were acquired. The spectral data were integrated via low-level fusion and subsequently modeled using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. The fused LSTM model yielded the best predictive performance, with Rp values of 0.9395, 0.9345, and 0.8596 for total tea polyphenols, theabrownins, and theaflavins, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of Raman-NIR spectral fusion combined with deep learning for non-destructive testing of key quality indicators during black tea fermentation.

title: Generalizable principles for tailoring deep eutectic solvents in alkaloid extraction: Insights from multi scale computational profiling of Piper nigrum and Zanthoxylum bungeanum
abstract: Conventional extraction of bioactive alkaloids relies on volatile organic solvents. This study evaluated 21 deep eutectic solvents (DESs) through experimental screening and multi scale computational profiling to extract piperine (PIP) from Piper nigrum and hydroxy sanshools (HAS and HBS) from Zanthoxylum bungeanum. For rigid PIP, a choline chloride/1,2-butanediol (1:4, 20% water) DES achieved 60.11 mg/g (a 1.53-fold increase over methanol). For flexible sanshools, a urea/acetic acid (1:2, 30% water) DES yielded 59.36 mg/g (HAS) and 14.61 mg/g (HBS). Molecular dynamics revealed that extraction efficiency depends on topological and electrostatic complementarity. Specifically, ChCl/1,2-BD extracts PIP via synergistic hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions, whereas UR/HAc solubilizes sanshools through network reorganization, anchoring polar terminals while accommodating flexible chains. This work establishes three generalizable principles for rational DES design: electrostatic complementarity matching, spatial topology adaptation for rigid frameworks, and van der Waals compensation for flexible chains.

title: Sustainable extraction of apple and pear polyphenols using natural deep eutectic solvents: functional activity, cytotoxicity and sustainability assessment
abstract: Apples and pears are widely consumed, polyphenol-rich fruits, yet whole-fruit extraction using green solvents remains underexplored relative to by-product-focused approaches. Natural deep eutectic solvents (NADES) were investigated as green extraction media for polyphenols from apple and pear. NADES were characterized (FTIR, DSC, viscosity, density) and extracts were evaluated for polyphenol content and profile (HPLC, LC-MS/MS), antioxidant activity (DPPH, ABTS, square-wave voltammetry) and cytotoxicity. Hydrophilic choline chloride-based NADES significantly enhanced polyphenol recovery compared with ethanol and menthol-based systems, with stronger radical-scavenging and electrochemical responses. Fluorescence spectroscopy indicated improved polyphenol solubilization. Cytotoxicity assays in tongue-derived and intestinal cell lines (HSC-3, Caco-2) showed high viability for choline chloride-based systems, whereas menthol-based NADES showed reduced tolerance. Sustainability assessment showed reduced solvent use, waste generation, and processing complexity versus conventional extraction. Solvent polarity and hydrogen-bonding capacity governed extraction efficiency, supporting food-grade NADES-based extraction as a proof-of-concept green alternative for whole-fruit polyphenol recovery.

title: Metabolomic fingerprinting of an artisanal blue-veined cheese: Impact of cave microenvironment and producer
abstract: Artisanal blue cheeses are highly valued products due to their unique quality attributes. This study conducted a large-scale longitudinal investigation into the influence of the producer and natural cave microenvironment on the metabolomic profile of PDO Cabrales cheese during ripening. Cheeses from three producers and ripened in three different caves were analysed for composition, free fatty acids, free amino acids, volatile compounds and biogenic amines using physico-chemical and chromatographic techniques. Distinct producer-specific metabolomic fingerprints emerged under identical ripening conditions, while cave-derived effects were evident on cheese rinds. Variations in lipolysis, proteolysis and secondary pathways were associated with changes in bioactive amino acids such as γ-aminobutyric acid and ornithine and key aroma compounds including methyl ketones and esters. These discriminant metabolites reflected the nutritional and sensory diversity of naturally ripened cheeses. The combined influence of producer practices and cave microenvironment underscores the importance of terroir preservation in maintaining artisanal cheese authenticity.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals that castration improves chicken meat flavor by altering lipid metabolic pathways
abstract: This study elucidated key mechanisms by which castration influences chicken meat flavor. The findings revealed that castration led to decreased serum androgen levels and other hormonal changes. Fourteen key volatile organic compounds (VOCs), including 1-octen-3-ol and (E)-2-nonenal, were identified to be responsible for the flavor differences following castration. Lipidomics analysis revealed that castration primarily altered hydrolyzed fatty acids and triglyceride (TG) content, with no significant changes in phospholipids (PLIPs). Additionally, transcriptomic analysis showed that castration, by reducing androgen levels, induces the reprogramming of pectoral muscle gene expression, which inhibits PLA2G2A/PLA2G2E expression, thereby reducing PLIPs degradation, increasing fatty acid esterification, and promoting TG accumulation. These effects alter flavor precursor supply patterns via glycerol ester metabolism, leading to the characteristic changes in key VOCs, and creating the distinctive flavor profile of castrated chickens. In conclusion, a potential interaction mechanism of "hormones-lipids-VOCs" triggered by castration was established.

title: Hypoglycemic potential of mulberry leaf extract – red palm oil emulsion: extraction, formulation, and bioactivity assessment
abstract: Both mulberry leaf extract (MLE) and red palm oil (RPO) have been reported to help regulate blood sugar levels, attributed to the 1-deoxynojirimycin (1-DNJ) in MLE and tocopherols and carotenoids in RPO. This study aims to investigate the potential hypoglycemic effects of an MLE-RPO emulsion, which have not been previously explored. The results prove that cellulase-assisted ultrasound extraction improved the recovery of 1-DNJ by 6.5-fold to 2.97 ± 0.01 mg/g, and enhanced α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibition activities by 10-20%. Combining MLE and RPO into an emulsion at a ratio of 5.25:1 further increased α-glucosidase inhibition activity to 90.26 ± 0.73%. However, the MLE-RPO emulsion at a 1:1 ratio exhibited superior antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities and was more effective than the 5.25:1 ratio in modulating the pattern of reducing sugar release during rice digestion. This study provides insights into the potential of the MLE-RPO emulsion as a functional food additive for modulating carbohydrate digestion.

title: A robust nanobody-magnetic bead immunoassay for food safety monitoring: Sensitive detection of viral contamination in giant salamander
abstract: The Chinese giant salamander is a valued food source of high-quality protein; however, the prevalence of Giant Salamander Iridovirus (GSIV) poses a significant threat to the safety and stability of the aquaculture food supply chain. Rapid and sensitive screening of viral pathogens in complex food matrices is therefore critical. We developed a bridge-free double-nanobody sandwich ELISA using magnetic beads (MBs) for detection of GSIV. AlphaFold 3 modeling suggested that covalent immobilization via conserved framework lysines may promote an optimal "upright" nanobody orientation, significantly enhancing capture efficiency compared with passive adsorption. The assay achieved a detection limit of 2.2 × 10 5 PFU/mL within 2 h, with sensitivity comparable to that of our previously reported pAb-based assay. The method exhibited exceptional resistance to matrix interference in undiluted tissue homogenates and was adapted to a semi-automated workflow. This work provides a scalable foundation for automated pathogen surveillance in aquatic food supply chains, ensuring food safety.

title: Coupling sugarcane bagasse with chitooligosaccharides for safe and metabolic-balanced fruit preservation
abstract: Postharvest deterioration of fresh fruits and inefficient utilization of agricultural residues remain major global challenges. Polysaccharide-based coatings have attracted increasing attention in recent years as preservation materials; however, most existing systems still rely on chemical modifications or non-renewable components. In this study, we developed a fully bio-based composite coating by mixing sugarcane bagasse (SCB), chitooligosaccharides (COSs), and citric acid. The SCB-COSs coating exhibited well broad-spectrum antibacterial, antioxidant capacity, biosafety, edibility and water-washability. Applied to strawberries, the coating effectively delayed softening and senescence, extending storage time while maintaining texture and sensory quality. Multi-omics analysis revealed that the coating not only functioned as a physical barrier but also mildly regulated key metabolic pathways, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle, abscisic acid signaling, and phenylpropanoid metabolism. This simple strategy for constructing polysaccharide-based coatings from agricultural waste and bioactive oligosaccharides provides a sustainable solution for improving postharvest fruit quality and valorizing waste biomass.

title: Comprehensive evaluation of the nutritional composition of Atlantic chub mackerel (Scomber colias): Influence of cooking methods
abstract: Nutritional composition and the impact of boiling and grilling on nutrient stability of the Atlantic chub mackerel (Scomber colias) were evaluated. Raw fish showed high protein content (22 g/100 g), a profile rich in omega-3 fatty acids (30%), and exceptional vitamin B 12 levels (28 μg/100 g). Thermal processing led to moisture loss, resulting in apparent increases in nutrient concentrations. However, True Retention Values (TRVs) demonstrated that these changes were primarily driven by concentration effects rather than net nutrient synthesis. High retention was observed for proteins (86-89%), lipids (72-80%), essential amino acids (86-102%), and vitamin B 12 (92-105%), indicating limited losses. Lipid quality indices (AI = 0.58-0.62; TI ≈ 0.27) and protein quality further supported the nutritional excellence of this species. Overall, boiling and grilling preserved the key attributes of S. colias, confirming its relevance as a sustainable and nutrient-dense seafood resource.

title: Fabrication and performance study of dihydromyricetin-fortified sodium alginate/konjac glucomannan-activated cling film
abstract: Food packaging is crucial for freshness preservation, with edible films gaining widespread attention. This study prepared sodium alginate (SA)/konjac glucomannan (KGM) composite films containing dihydromyricetin (DMY), with 8% DMY as optimal. Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, molecular docking, and isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) confirmed hydrogen bonding, stabilizing DMY. The film exhibited potent antioxidant activity (88.9% DPPH scavenging), antimicrobial efficacy against both Gram-negative Escherichia coli and Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus (92.05% and 95.20% inhibition, respectively; log₁₀ reduction >2.50 at 12% DMY loading). Fresh-cut apple trials showed it delayed quality loss, inhibited browning (lower PPO activity), and suppressed microbial proliferation (3.97 log CFU/g vs. 5.28 log CFU/g control). The key innovations are: (i) elucidating DMY stabilization in a polysaccharide matrix via hydrogen bonding through docking and ITC; (ii) integrating antioxidant, antimicrobial, and barrier functions in a single edible film; and (iii) demonstrating dual efficacy against enzymatic browning and microbial spoilage in fresh-cut produce.

title: Electroactive MnO2 nanorods-integrated grafted pectic acid nanocomposite for enzyme-free hydrogen peroxide determination in milk and salami samples
abstract: Grafting pectic acid (PecA) is fueled by free radical copolymerization of acrylic acid (AcA) and acrylamide (AAm), [PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA)], embedded with manganese dioxide-nanorods (MnO 2 -NRs) produced an inventive nanocomposite, [PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA)/MnO 2 -NRs]. Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopic analysis, thermal gravimetric (TG) measurement, scanning and transmission electron microscopes (SEM and TEM) analyses, in addition to X-ray diffraction (XRD), alongside cyclic voltametric (CV) measurements with spectroscopic investigation of electrochemical impedance (EIS), were applied for evaluating PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA)/MnO 2 -NRs. Based on the TEM images, MnO 2 -NRs have a width size extent from 9 to 33 nm, PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA) has cluster nanoporous framework shapes with a particle size close to 45 nm, and observative nanorods covered the nanoparticles for PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA)/MnO 2 -NRs with the polymeric particle's diameters between 21 and 50 nm. The MnO 2 -based nanocomposite showed significantly higher electrical capacitance than its grafted copolymer, PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA). Screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) modification using PecA-g-poly (AAm-co-AcA)/MnO 2 -NRs was examined for its ability to detect hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) effectively. Across a range of 0.1 to 1000 μM, it showed remarkable stability, reproducibility, rapid, linear sensitivity, and instantaneous electron transmission. Furthermore, the sensor demonstrated good recovery rates while analysing milk and salami samples. This nanocomposite is thus suitable for detecting hydrogen peroxide as one of reactive oxygen species and its decomposition due to the markedly improved electrical properties.

title: Wireless portable MEMS sensor with mesoporous yolk-Shell SnO2/TiO2 Nanospheres for real-time and nondestructive freshness monitoring of aquatic products
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of trimethylamine (TMA), a key spoilage indicator in aquatic products, is of critical value for real-time freshness monitoring and food safety control. Herein, mesoporous yolk-shell SnO 2 /TiO 2 nanospheres were utilized as sensing materials to construct a wireless and portable microelectromechanical system-based sensing platform for nondestructive aquatic product freshness evaluation. The optimized SnO 2 /TiO 2 -2 sensor exhibited a high response (R a /R g = 53.2@100 ppm TMA), fast response/recovery times (7.7 s/10.8 s), and superior selectivity. The signal of the detection device, which is integrated with this sensor, was positively correlated with total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) content measured via the standard reference method. The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was also performed to determine the optimal classification threshold for discriminating between fresh and spoiled states. These results demonstrate that the proposed platform provides a practical, cost-effective solution for real-time freshness monitoring across the entire aquatic product supply chain.

title: Engineering covalent organic frameworks for tailored encapsulation and controlled release of fragrances
abstract: The inherent volatility of fragrances leads to rapid fading, poor stability, low availability, potential health, and environmental issues, necessitating the development of effective fragrance carriers for stable storage and controllable release. Herein, we presented a strategy for finely tuning the encapsulation and release profiles of fragrant molecules through engineering the pore surface properties of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Three imine-based COFs with variable functional groups (TAPB-DHTP-COF, TAPB-DMTP-COF, and TAPB-DVA-COF) were rationally designed and constructed via solvent evaporation method, which exhibited stable crystallinity, uniform morphology, and tunable surface areas (152-1056 m 2 g -1 ), and pore sizes (2.3-3.9 nm). Notably, the polar COFs demonstrated significantly higher loading capacities for polar aldehyde-type fragrances (anisaldehyde, Ani; and citral, Cit) compared to nonpolar terpene-type (limonene, Lim). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that the superior adsorption of polar fragrances into the COFs was governed by strong hydrogen bond interactions, with adsorption energies of -1.16 eV (Ani) and -1.17 eV (Cit) versus -0.37 eV (Lim). All fragrance-loaded COFs exhibited sustained release profiles over 48 h, in stark contrast to the rapid release of free fragrances. Importantly, the release rate was tunable by modulating host-guest interactions, stronger hydrogen bonding led to more prolonged release. This pioneering research established COFs as a heavy metal-free, designable platform for the encapsulation and controllable release of volatile fragrances, showcasing promising applications in cosmetics and personal care industries.

title: Configurational transformation of dihydromyricetin during thermal processing and its implications for quality evaluation
abstract: Thermal processing is a critical under-evaluated factor influencing the stereochemical stability of bioactive flavonoids. This study demonstrates that natural 2R, 3R-dihydromyricetin (DMY) undergoes a configurational evolution during heating, yielding two previously overlooked non-natural diastereomers (2S, 3R- and 2R, 3S-). The transformation was proposed to proceed through a quinone methide (QM)-mediated pathway. Bioactivity assays revealed differences in antibacterial activity between the natural and non-natural isomers at the tested concentration (32 μg/mL). This disparity in activity suggests that processing-induced isomerization may represent an overlooked factor contributing to variations in biological properties. Consequently, monitoring the emergence of these isomers during thermal processing may complement conventional content-based assays by incorporating stereochemical information, thereby providing a more comprehensive framework for quality evaluation.

title: Mechanisms of acid generation and reduction during Jiangxiangxing Baijiu fermentation: insights from practices of raw materials saccharification regulation
abstract: Elevated total acidity in the first round base liquor is a major challenge in Jiangxiangxing Baijiu production. Production practice has shown that enhanced raw material saccharification effectively reduces total acidity. This study investigated the underlying regulatory mechanism. Enhanced saccharification reduced total acidity, predominantly attributable to acetic acid, to 0.059 mol/L, representing a 14.47% reduction, without altering overall microbial succession. Multi-omics and culture-dependent analyses identified Limosilactobacillus panis, Lactobacillus acetotolerans, and Limosilactobacillus avium as core acetic acid-producing microorganisms, with their relative abundances reduced by 48.43%, 43.01%, and 32.67%, respectively. The acetate kinase-mediated pathway was the dominant route of acetic acid biosynthesis, and enhanced saccharification reduced transcription of the acetate kinase-encoding gene. Fermentation validation showed that elevated reducing sugar promoted yeast growth and ethanol production, thereby suppressing acetic acid formation. Overall, enhanced saccharification reduces total acidity in base liquor by modulating reducing sugar-driven microbial dynamics and suppressing acetic acid biosynthesis.

title: A win-win strategy between carbon reduction and flavor enhancement: Optimized rolling process for large-leaf yellow tea with fresh and flowery aroma
abstract: Conventional large-leaf yellow tea (LYT), made from mature leaves, relies on energy-intensive old-fire roasting to mitigate coarse flavor, thereby posing significant sustainability challenges. This study established a novel "heavy rolling - light roasting" cascaded improvement strategy to LYT, achieving the balance between quality enhancement and energy efficiency. Sensory evaluation combined with chemical analyses revealed that the coarse and green odor was reduced while fresh and flowery aroma was imparted to LYT. Linalool, geraniol and nonanal et al. were identified as key volatile compounds to the novel aroma profile. Tissue-specific aroma contributions were further elucidated, with buds, leaves and stems respectively exhibiting flowery, fresh, and coarse-sweet characteristics, and leaves were identified as the key contributors. Carbon footprint assessment confirmed that the cascaded processing technology for LYT significantly reduced carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. These findings provided a practical pathway for high-quality and low-carbon tea productions, promoting sustainable development in tea industry.

title: Class-selective and highly sensitive detection of β-diketone antibiotics in milk using a Eu(III)-anchored covalent organic framework probe via dual-mode ratiometric strategy
abstract: Developing reliable methods for β-diketone antibiotics detection is significant for food security. Herein, a Eu(III)-anchored COF probe was designed for class-selective and sensitive detection of β-diketone antibiotics via a dual-mode sensor. This Eu(III)@COF probe exhibited inherent fluorescence at 527 nm, served as an internal reference signal. Upon addition of levofloxacin (LVF, a model of β-diketone antibiotics), the resulting LVF-Eu(III)@COF exhibited a markedly enhanced fluorescence at 616 nm due to target-induced "antenna effect". Thus, a ratiometric fluorescent sensor was successfully constructed for LVF detection using the intensity ratio of F 616 to F 527 . Furthermore, a portable smartphone-aided visualization platform was developed for detecting LVF using RGB-based ratio with a LOD of 0.746 μM. The dual-mode ratiometric sensor features self-calibration and cross-verification capabilities, which can minimize interferences from complicated matrices and external fluctuations. This sensor demonstrates a promising approach for class-selective assay of β-diketone antibiotics and accurate detection of LVF in milk samples.

title: Evaluating protein quantification methods in long-life dairy and plant-based milk alternatives
abstract: Routine protein quantification in plant-based milk alternatives is essential for nutritional labelling and quality control. This study compared UPLC-UV amino acid analysis, elemental, Bradford assay, Raman spectroscopy, and ATR-FTIR for protein determination in bovine and plant-based milks. UPLC-UV provided detailed protein measurements but was labor-intensive and time-consuming. Elemental analysis offered rapid and robust estimates but lacked specificity for protein-derived nitrogen. The Bradford assay showed variability depending on the calibration standard, supported by circular dichroism findings indicating inconsistent performance. Raman spectroscopy, using 785 nm excitation, was limited by fluorescence interference in complex milk matrices. ATR-FTIR demonstrated strong potential as a fast, simple, and easy method for protein estimation, achieving high linearity (R 2 = 0.997) with minimal sample preparation. Effective water subtraction and optimised calibration improved its performance despite matrix complexity. Although further matrix-matched calibration and validation are required, ATR-FTIR shows considerable promise for routine industrial protein analysis and food science applications.Keywords: plant-based milk alternatives, amino acid analysis, elemental analysis, Bradford assay, circular dichroism, Raman spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, food quality control.

title: Mechanistic insights into deodorization of Pyropia haitanensis by ultrasound-assisted Lactiplantibacillus plantarum fermentation: Linking key odorants with amino acid metabolism
abstract: The fishy odor of Pyropia haitanensis limits its sensory acceptance and industrial utilization. In this study, ultrasound-assisted fermentation (UAF) combined with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum was employed to investigate the molecular mechanism underlying deodorization of P. haitanensis. Gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS) identified nonanal, 1-octen-3-ol, and trans-β-ionone as the major contributors to the fishy odor. UAF effectively reduced the fishy odor intensity. Furthermore, gas chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS) combined with flavor omission and recombination experiments identified six key flavor compounds associated with odor reduction. Metabolomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of amino acid metabolism during UAF, with L-3-phenyllactic acid showing the greatest increase (17.61-fold). Correlation analysis and metabolite addition experiments demonstrated that UAF activated aromatic amino acid metabolism, promoted the accumulation of pleasant flavor metabolites, and masked undesirable odors. Overall, this study provides new mechanistic insights into UAF-mediated deodorization and supports the high-value utilization of P. haitanensis.

title: Structural characteristics of wheat bran arabinoxylan and its differential effects on the physicochemical properties of A-, B-, and C-type starches
abstract: Arabinoxylan was extracted and purified from wheat bran through alkaline extraction, enzymatic removal of starch and protein, and ethanol precipitation. Its interactions with wheat (A-type), potato (B-type), and pea (C-type) starches were systematically investigated and compared. The purified arabinoxylan exhibited a low degree of substitution, with a weight-average molecular weight of 112 kDa and a backbone mainly composed of →4)-d-Xylp-(1→ linkages. Addition of 0.5% arabinoxylan reduced peak viscosity of wheat, potato, and pea starches by 55.3%, 68.8%, and 49.4%, respectively, and significantly decreased setback viscosity (p < 0.05). Rheological analysis revealed reductions in both of the storage and loss moduli, indicating the formation of weakened starch gel networks. Potato starch exhibited the strongest response, suggesting that crystalline type plays an important role in arabinoxylan-starch interactions. These findings highlight the potential of wheat bran arabinoxylan as a functional polysaccharide for modulating the processing and textural properties of starch-based foods.

title: Exudate-based biomarkers as minimally invasive tools for monitoring meat freshness under refrigerated storage
abstract: This study evaluated whether package exudate can serve as a minimally invasive matrix for freshness monitoring in vacuum-packed beef and pork stored at 2 ± 0.5 °C for 21 days. Physicochemical and microbiological indicators, including pH, color, lipid oxidation, protein carbonyls, total aerobic count, and Escherichia coli, confirmed progressive spoilage during storage (p < 0.05). Exudate pH and microbial loads closely reflected deterioration patterns observed in meat tissue. HS-SPME-GC-MS analysis revealed substantial storage-dependent changes in volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in both tissue and exudate. Exudate VOCs responded earlier than tissue VOCs, with 51.6% of beef-exudate VOCs and 43.8% of pork-exudate VOCs significantly altered by Day 7 relative to Day 1 (p < 0.05). Multivariate analyses identified 12 candidate biomarkers in beef exudate and 14 in pork exudate. These findings demonstrate that package exudate provides sensitive and early spoilage-related signals and represents a promising substrate for freshness-monitoring applications.

title: Current trends in the analysis of mycotoxins in bee products: Occurrence, extraction, and determination
abstract: Bee products, including honey, bee pollen, propolis, and royal jelly, are increasingly valued for their nutritional and bioactive properties. However, these matrices may also be contaminated by mycotoxins, toxic secondary metabolites produced by fungi under inadequate agricultural and storage conditions. Although mycotoxin contamination has been extensively investigated in cereals and animal feed, studies involving bee products remain limited, despite their increasing consumption and commercial relevance. This review is the first to comprehensively compile and critically discuss current methodologies for the extraction and determination of mycotoxins specifically in bee products. Emphasis is placed on advances reported over approximately the last five years, including improvements in sample preparation and the application of chromatographic and mass spectrometric techniques. Additionally, occurrence data are examined in light of analytical performance, limitations, and emerging challenges. The implementation of sensitive and robust analytical strategies is essential to ensure product safety, support regulatory monitoring, and preserve the functional quality of bee-derived foods within the global food system.

title: Integration of HS-SPME-GC–MS and targeted metabolomics to elucidate the regional flavor characteristics and metabolic pathways of ‘Shushanggan’ apricots from core production areas in Xinjiang
abstract: 'Shushanggan' apricots are strongly favored by consumers because of their high nutritional profile and unique flavor. However, their flavor characteristics significantly differ among different production areas, and the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Herein, targeted metabolomics was integrated with HS-SPME-GC-MS to analyze apricot metabolites across seven core production areas. Notably, sucrose (highest in Kashi (KS; 413,029.33 μg·g -1 ), organic acids, including malic acid and oleanolic acid, which were highest in Gongliu (GL), and γ-aminobutyric acid (highest in Tekes (TKS; 1365.06 μg·g -1 ) were the major components. Terpenoids were the main contributors to aroma. Twenty-seven characteristic volatiles were identified via the rOAV. Regional habitat significantly influenced metabolite accumulation, with strong correlations between nonvolatile metabolites and key volatiles. This study elucidates regional variations in apricot flavor and the underlying biochemical mechanisms. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the development of high-value products and industrial optimization.

title: Compositional analysis of commercial milk using combined FTIR and Raman spectroscopy with chemometric techniques
abstract: Rapid and reliable characterization of milk composition is essential for quality control and authentication in the dairy industry. This study evaluates the combined use of FTIR and Raman spectroscopy coupled with chemometric tools for the determination and classification of fat, lactose, and protein in commercial milk. Ninety-five samples from different milk types (whole, semi-skimmed, skimmed, lactose-free, calcium-enriched, and sheep milk) were analysed in liquid and solid states, including freeze-dried, tablet-compressed, and thawed samples. Quantitative analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares regression, while sample discrimination was achieved through supervised classification models. Both techniques provided robust models for fat and lactose quantification, with Raman spectroscopy showing superior performance for fat in solid matrices, and FTIR exhibiting higher sensitivity for lactose. Protein determination was limited due to low compositional variability. Sample processing did not significantly affect model performance. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy offer a rapid, non-destructive, complementary approach for routine dairy analysis.

title: Pulsed electric field-enhanced phenolic release, profiling, and antioxidant enhancement in cold-pressed rapeseed oil
abstract: Cell-wall sequestration intact Brassica napus seeds severely restricts phenolic recovery during conventional processing, thereby limiting cold-pressed oil quality. Fifteen Yunnan winter accessions were screened for total phenolic content, and the three highest-ranking were selected for pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment and profiling using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS-TQD), antioxidant activity, and oxidative markers. Optimal PEF-treatment (7 kV/cm; 10 Hz; 1 min) enhanced phenolic release and migration, increasing from 308.70 to 1204.52 mg GAE/100 g, with rutin and kaempferol showing cultivar-dependent, PEF-exclusive detection. PEF enhanced antioxidant activities while reducing peroxide values by up to 71.2%. Electron spin resonance (ESR) indicated reduced lipid radical signal after PEF, while proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 HNMR) and gas chromatography (GC) showed comparable fatty acid profiles. These results, limited to three accessions and a single time point, require broader validation and storage conditions. PEF is a promising clean-label, non-thermal strategy to enrich phenolic-bioactives in cold-pressed oil.

title: Effects of peroxidase and xylanase treatments on gluten separation efficiency from wheat tailings flour: Insights into batter properties and gluten characteristics
abstract: This study investigated the effect of peroxidase, xylanase and their sequential treatments on gluten separation from wheat tailings flour, aiming to enhance separation efficiency and modify gluten characteristics. The best-performing treatment was 6 U/g peroxidase followed by 10 U/g xylanase, which significantly enhanced separation efficiency, achieving 13.40% yield and 89.34% purity, outperforming the reverse enzyme sequence and single enzyme treatments. Peroxidase followed by xylanase treatment reduced the batter viscosity and weakened arabinoxylan-protein association. This treatment increased glutenin macropolymer to 28.05%, increased the β-sheet proportion, and reduced free sulfhydryl content, resulting in a more ordered gluten network with changed viscoelasticity and tensile strength. In contrast, the xylanase followed by peroxidase sequence may have led to premature arabinoxylan degradation, which impaired gluten aggregation. This study elucidates the mechanism by which peroxidase followed by xylanase sequence enhances gluten separation efficiency, providing a promising approach for improving gluten separation from wheat tailings flour.

title: Mechanistic insights into structural reorganization and quality formation of starch coated pork tenderloin under mechanical pounding
abstract: Pork tenderloin slices subjected to graded pounding were used to clarify how mechanical treatment influences structural reorganization, quality formation, and in vitro digestibility. Moderate pounding, particularly for 120 s, reduced hardness and chewiness while improving water-holding capacity and tenderness. Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance indicated redistribution of water from tightly bound to immobilized fractions, with prolonged relaxation times, suggesting a loosened myofibrillar matrix. Differential scanning calorimetry and vibrational spectroscopy showed reduced protein denaturation temperatures and enthalpy, accompanied by a 36.7% decrease in α-helix content, a 119.7% increase in β-turn content, and surface hydrophobicity increasing to about 67%. Electrophoretic analysis suggested limited protein fragmentation and aggregation. During simulated digestion, moderately pounded samples exhibited higher protein solubility and faster hydrolysis, with overall digestibility increasing to approximately 90%, compared with about 83% in the control. These results provide structural insight into quality improvement and digestibility enhancement in mechanically treated pork tenderloin.

title: A comparative study of emulsifiers for curcumin-loaded emulsion coatings: Enhancing delivery and stability to inhibit heterocyclic amines in air-fried chicken wings
abstract: To overcome the poor solubility and instability of curcumin, an oil-in-water emulsions were prepared using four food-grade emulsifiers (MSP, SC, SSOS, SE). Their physicochemical properties, stability, and antioxidant capacity were characterized. And their inhibition efficacy in heterocyclic amines (HAs) was evaluated by coating chicken wings prior to air-frying (190 °C, 15 min). The SC-stabilized emulsion (Cur-NE-10gSC) exhibited superior stability with droplet size of 164.1 nm and PDI of 0.187, and achieved 93% reduction in total HAs (from 4.59 to 0.30 ng/g, p < 0.05), outperforming its non-emulsified counterpart and other formulations. CLSM analysis revealed that SE-based emulsions possessed the best skin penetration, correlating with their high sensory acceptability. This study demonstrates that emulsification, particularly with SC and SE, is a highly effective strategy for delivering curcumin, significantly enhancing its bioavailability, stability, and functional efficacy in inhibiting HAs formation while maintaining sensory quality, offering a practical solution for safer meat processing.

title: Synergistic co-stabilization of Pickering-surfactant hybrid emulsions using cellulose nanocrystals and chitin-glucan nanofibers for curcumin delivery systems
abstract: To investigate the synergistic co-stabilizers of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) and chitin-glucan nanofibers (CGNFs) in Pickering emulsions for curcumin delivery. CNCs were obtained through sulfuric acid hydrolysis, while CGNFs were prepared using a deep eutectic solvent-assisted esterification. CGNFs were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), displayed an entangled nanofiber network, high crystallinity, thermal stability, and a strong negative surface charge (-40.8 mV). Oil-in-water Pickering emulsions were fabricated using CNCs, CGNFs, and polyglycerol polyricinoleate (PGPR), then loaded with curcumin, resulting in demonstrated high encapsulation efficiency (>97%), pH-responsive release (pH 5.0 and 7.4), and good rheological properties (shear thinning behavior). In vitro digestion demonstrated efficient lipid digestion efficiency. These findings support the synergistic co-stabilizers of CNCs and CGNFs for Pickering emulsions and support their application as robust, natural, and sustainable delivery systems for lipophilic bioactives in food and nutraceutical industries.

title: Oleosome stability: Interfacial mechanisms, destabilisation pathways, and stabilisation strategies
abstract: Oleosomes, or plant oil bodies, are natural lipid storage organelles comprising a triacylglycerol core surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer embedded with oleosins, caleosins, and steroleosins. Their emulsifying properties make them attractive for food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications. However, commercial utilisation is constrained by oxidative degradation, aggregation, and destabilisation during processing and storage, and a mechanistic understanding of oleosome stability remains lacking. This review synthesises current knowledge on the interfacial mechanisms governing physical, oxidative, enzymatic, and microbial stability emphasising how interfacial proteins, phospholipids, and bioactive components control electrostatic interactions, steric protection, interfacial mechanics, and oxidative resistance. Stabilisation strategies, including pH and ionic-strength control, biopolymer incorporation, thermal treatments, homogenisation, drying, and water-activity reduction, are evaluated for their mechanisms and practical limitations. This review identifies key principles for preserving oleosome integrity in structured emulsions, dairy analogues, and delivery systems, and outlines priorities for standardised stability metrics, omics-based characterisation, and predictive modelling.

title: Capillary electrophoresis with diode array detection for the determination of organic acids in fermented food samples
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), branched SCFAs, and their precursors (lactic, succinic, pyruvic acids) are key microbial metabolites relevant to gut function and are present in fermented foods. This study reports the transfer, development, and validation of a rapid capillary electrophoresis method with diode-array detection (indirect UV) for the simultaneous determination of 12 biologically important organic acids in <15 min. Starting from a commercial methodology, background electrolyte composition and separation voltage were optimised. The method was validated according to ICH Q2(R2). Linearity was confirmed from LOQ to 100 μg/mL, with LOQs of 1.53-5.76 μg/mL. Precision and trueness were satisfactory (CV ≤ 7.6%, |RE| ≤ 7.5%), matrix effects ranged from 80 to 121%, and selectivity was adequate. Applicability was demonstrated by analysing 11 fermented vegetable juices. Finally, the RGBfast model benchmarking against literature methods supported the method's suitability for routine profiling of organic acids in fermented foods.

title: Interfacial engineering of zein nanoparticles by phosphatidylcholine and polysaccharide synergy: Enhanced quercetin delivery and improved ultrasonic emulsification stability
abstract: Zein and quercetin (QUE) are limited in food applications due to their poor dispersibility. In this study, an interfacial engineering strategy was developed to tailor the surface structure of zein nanoparticles through the sequential incorporation of phosphatidylcholine (PC) and polysaccharides (dextran or sodium alginate). The addition of PC improved nanoparticle dispersibility and induced a "positive-to-negative shift" in ζ-potential, which influenced subsequent polysaccharide assembly. Nanoparticles coated with sodium alginate (SA) exhibited enhanced colloidal stability, photostability (retention: 90.33%), thermal stability (retention: 71.07%), suppressed premature QUE release during digestion (<1%), and improved bioaccessibility (74.58%). Moreover, these engineered nanoparticles effectively stabilized ultrasound-prepared walnut oil emulsions, resulting in smaller droplet size (∼7 μm) and improved oxidative stability. Overall, this study provides a practical strategy for the encapsulation of hydrophobic bioactive compounds and effective ultrasonic emulsification in food systems.

title: Protective effects of gamma-irradiated ice-nucleating Pseudomonas syringae on quality loss in rainbow trout during freeze-thaw cycles
abstract: This study investigated the protective effects of gamma-irradiated ice-nucleating Pseudomonas syringae, known as P. syringae parabiotics (PBs), on the freezing behavior, physicochemical quality, and microstructural integrity of rainbow trout mince during six freeze-thaw (F-T) cycles. PBs were added to the mince at levels of 2 × 10 2 to 2 × 10 4 inactivated cells/g and compared with the viable cell treatment (2 × 10 3 CFU/g). The results demonstrated a pronounced protective effect of 2 × 10 2 inactivated cells/g (PBs-2) and 2 × 10 3 inactivated cells/g (PBs-3) during repeated F-T cycles. PBs-2 exhibited the lowest thawing loss, delayed color deterioration, reduced particle size, and the highest absolute negative zeta potential (-32.45 mV). While PBs-3 reduced loss of total sulfhydryl groups (35.10%), mitigated formation of protein carbonyls (1.92 nmol/mg protein), and decreased centrifugal loss (39.00%). The use of P. syringae PBs may be a non-viable biotic-based strategy for protecting fish myofibrillar proteins from freeze-thaw-induced damage.

title: Polyphenol-mediated stabilization of myofibrillar proteins: Effects of pomegranate peel extract on freeze-thaw stability and gelation
abstract: This study investigated the cryoprotective efficacy of pomegranate peel extract (PPE; 0.45%, w/w) against commercial cryoprotectant in silver carp myofibrillar proteins during repeated freeze-thaw (FT) cycles (0-4). Compared with the commercial cryoprotectant, PPE effectively mitigated FT-induced protein oxidation, exhibiting 25% lower carbonyl content, 18.96% higher sulfhydryl content, 16.55% lower disulfide bond formation, and maintained 20.24% higher Ca 2+ -ATPase activity. PPE also suppressed protein aggregation, as evidenced by smaller particle size (263 vs. 305 nm, respectively), lower turbidity, and higher absolute zeta potential. Consequently, PPE efficiently preserved the secondary structure and myosin heavy chain integrity, resulting in 15.13% higher protein solubility, 11.37% greater water-holding capacity, and 2.1-times higher gel strength after four FT cycles. SEM further confirmed a denser gel network with finer ice-crystal distribution. These findings highlight PPE as promising multifunctional natural alternative to conventional cryoprotectants for preserving the structural integrity and functionality of frozen aquatic food proteins.

title: Noncovalent interaction-driven self-assembly of β-cyclodextrin-soy protein isolate supramolecular aggregates for cinnamon essential oil microencapsulation: Application in postharvest preservation of garlic scapes
abstract: To overcome the challenges posed by the inherent properties of cinnamon essential oil (CEO) in practical applications, an effective microencapsulation system (CEO@SPI/βCD) was developed using supramolecular aggregates of β-cyclodextrin and soy protein isolate, serving as a natural preservative for garlic scapes. The microcapsules achieved a particle size of 61.333 ± 3.65 μm, while their high negative surface charge (-26.20 ± 0.68 mV) imparted excellent storage stability to CEO@SPI/βCD. Structural characterization confirmed the effective encapsulation of CEO and the noncovalent interactions between the wall materials. Additionally, microencapsulation enhanced the thermal stability, antimicrobial activity (MIC of 0.195-0.781 μg/mL), and sustained-release properties of CEO. Preservation experiments revealed that the CEO@SPI/βCD was superior in maintaining both the appearance and intrinsic quality of garlic scapes, as evidenced by higher nutrient content and enhanced antioxidant levels. These results provide valuable insights into the application of CEO@SPI/βCD for the postharvest preservation of garlic scapes.

title: Washing pretreatment enhances dielectric barrier discharge plasma preservation of fresh goji berries through residual surface water-mediated effects
abstract: Fresh goji berries are highly perishable. Direct dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma benefits postharvest preservation but may cause fruit surface damage. This study investigated the effects of water or plasma-activated water (PAW) washing before DBD on goji berry preservation, surface damage and safety. Both combined treatments reduced weight loss and microbial counts, and better maintained firmness, phenolics, and antioxidant capacity during storage. On day 6, the decay rates in PAW + DBD and H 2 O + DBD were 39% and 41% lower than the control. H 2 O + DBD performed comparably to PAW + DBD, suggesting a simpler option. Representative SEM images showed fewer punctate surface alterations after washing-DBD than after DBD alone. The measured H 2 O 2 and NO 2 - decay was kinetically compatible with a possible ONOOH formation pathway in the residual surface liquid. The combined treatments also improved acetamiprid and carbofuran removal to 82% and 70%, respectively, and reduced Alternaria toxin levels.

title: Thermal loss of phytosteryl/stanyl fatty acid esters during heating: Intramolecular structural susceptibility and intermolecular matrix regulation
abstract: Phytosteryl/stanyl fatty acid esters are widely used as cholesterol-lowering ingredients in functional foods, but the relative contributions of molecular structure and lipid environment to their thermal loss remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify these effects using sitosteryl/stanyl palmitate, oleate, and linoleate as model compounds. Sitosteryl/stanyl ester loss increased with temperature, heating time, and acyl-chain unsaturation, while sitostanyl esters were more stable than sitosteryl esters. Moiety-level and kinetic analyses showed that the dominant degradation site shifted from the steryl skeleton in palmitate esters to the acyl chain in linoleate esters, whereas high temperature promoted synchronized whole-molecule degradation. Oil matrices markedly reduced ester loss, with stronger protection from more unsaturated matrices, suggesting a possible competitive oxidation effect. α-Tocopherol inhibited ester degradation, whereas squalene and β-carotene showed pro-oxidant behavior at 180 °C. These results suggest that thermal stability was governed by intramolecular structural susceptibility and intermolecular regulation by the lipid environment.

title: A dual-phase continuous process for lipid extraction from Litopenaeus vannamei by-products: process performance, lipid quality, and flavor
abstract: Traditional extraction of Litopenaeus vannamei lipids often suffers from oxidation and low yields due to high-temperature and oxygen exposure. This study proposes an innovative, low-temperature, synergistic anaerobic process that combines low-pressure superheated steam drying (LPSSD) with low-temperature continuous phase-change extraction (LCPE). Compared to conventional methods, the LPSSD-LCPE coupling process establishes a dual protective barrier, achieving a significantly higher lipid extraction yield of 95.54% ± 1.39% (an increase of 14.15%). This technology resulted in higher EPA and DHA proportions while successfully enriching bioactive odd-chain fatty acids and nervonic acid (0.38%-0.97%). Furthermore, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analyses demonstrated that this process effectively suppresses off-flavor compounds like trimethylamine and 1-octen-3-ol, with isovaleraldehyde identified as the key aroma contributor. By balancing "deterioration inhibition" and "intrinsic flavor retention, " the LPSSD-LCPE process provides a green, efficient pathway for the high-value recovery of bioactive lipids and precise flavor regulation in aquatic by-products. However, the subsequent valorization of high-value components in the defatted shrimp meal remains to be explored.

title: Thermal conversion profiles of catechins and extractable low-molecular-weight compounds in Camellia sinensis leaves under dry- and wet-heat processing
Non-covalent complexes of Chlorella pyrenoidosa antioxidant peptides with chlorogenic acid: structure-activity relationships and potential synergistic cytoprotection
abstract: Non-covalent complexation with chlorogenic acid (CA) was investigated to remodel complex-level structure-activity relationships of antioxidant peptides (AOPs) from Chlorella pyrenoidosa protein hydrolysates (CPPH) and to evaluate their potential cytoprotective interaction. CPPH-CA complex formation and conformational/microenvironmental changes were characterized by FTIR, intrinsic fluorescence, UV-vis, and interfacial/colloidal measurements. Antioxidant activity and synergy of CPPH-CA and peptide-CA systems were quantified using ABTS, DPPH, and FRAP assays. Representative AOPs were identified by LC-MS/MS and in silico screening, synthesized, and analyzed by quantum chemical parameters (HOMO/LUMO, ESP, ALIE, Fukui functions and IGMH). CA associated with AOPs mainly through hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces, inducing charge redistribution and decreased HOMO-LUMO gaps, consistent with enhanced reactivity and synergy. In H 2 O 2 -injured HepG2 cells, PLR-CA exhibited a potential cytoprotective effect under the tested conditions by improving cell viability, reducing lipid peroxidation, and restoring antioxidant enzyme activities.

title: Preservation of refrigerated tilapia by plasma-activated nitrogen-lactic acid: A lipidomic insight into phosphatidylethanolamine protection and metabolic remodeling
abstract: Maintaining refrigerated tilapia freshness remains challenging. Four plasma-activated solutions, plasma-activated water (PAW), plasma-activated lactic acid (PALA), plasma-activated nitrogen water (PNW), and plasma-activated nitrogen-lactic acid (PNLA), were evaluated for quality preservation and lipid metabolism over 8 d at 4°C.
