PNLA performed best: it maintained texture, minimized cooking loss, and inhibited spoilage. Lipidomics revealed that PNLA was associated with relative preservation of certain phosphatidylethanolamine species and a distinct glycerophospholipid remodeling pattern, whereas other treatments were linked to increased phospholipase markers and phosphatidylcholine oxidation. These associations suggest a potential protective effect on membrane lipids; however, direct measurements were not performed. Thus the proposed mechanisms remain correlational and hypothesis-generating. Although reactive species were not quantitatively measured, PNLA's distinct profile was hypothesized to enable multi-target preservation by reducing lipid oxidation, microbial spoilage, and structural degradation. Further studies are needed to validate these mechanisms, including direct assessment of PE adduction, carbonyl scavenging, and membrane integrity.

title: Ozone treatment of postharvest apricot fruit reveals a pathway to enhanced black spot disease resistance mediated by DNA methylation
abstract: Postharvest apricot fruits are highly susceptible to Alternaria alternata infection, which induces black spot disease and causes considerable economic losses. This study investigated the effect of ozone (O₃) on the resistance of 'Chuanzhihong' apricots to A. alternata using integrated metabolomic, transcriptomic, and whole-genome methylomic analyses. Fruits were inoculated with A. alternata, treated with 46 μL·L -1 O₃ for 10 min, and stored for 6 days. O₃ significantly inhibited disease progression, promoted the accumulation of 11 amino acids, elevated jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA) contents, and activated relevant metabolic pathways. It regulated JA/SA biosynthesis genes (LOX2S, ACX, ACAA1) and the key signal transduction transcription factor MYC2. Dynamic CG/CHG/CHH hypermethylation and hypomethylation triggered by O₃ modulated the transcription of 29 pivotal defense-related genes. Collectively, O₃ enhances postharvest disease resistance in apricots by orchestrating DNA methylation, phytohormone crosstalk, and amino acid metabolic networks.

title: Magnetic dispersive solid-phase microextraction of fourteen rare earth elements (REEs) from herbs, tea, and water using bimetallic spinel magnetic NiZnFe2O4 nanomaterial followed by ICP-OES determination
abstract: In this work, bimetallic spinel magnetic NiZnFe 2 O 4 (BS-M-NZF) nanomaterial was prepared using a sol-gel route. By using BS-M-NZF as an adsorbent, a magnetic dispersive solid phase microextraction (M-D-SPμE) method coupled with ICP-OES was developed to determine 14 REEs in tea, herbs and waters. Parameters affecting M-D-SPμE of 14 REEs have been investigated. They were at pH 6.0; contact times were 1 min and 30 s; volume was 40 mL; adsorbent amount was 100 mg; and the eluent was 1 mol L -1 HNO 3 (4 mL). The LODs and the RSDs% of 14 REEs changed from 0.014 μg L -1 (Yb) to 0.362 μg L -1 (Sm) and 0.96% (Yb) to 2.81% (Lu), respectively. The accuracy of the M-D-SPμE was validated by analyzing a SPS-SW2 Batch 145 (except for Sm). Besides, it was verified by recovery studies in the LGC6016 Estuarine Water, NW-TMDA-54.6 Lake water, tea, herbs, and water, which changed from 89 to 114%. The developed M-D-SPμE-ICP-OES method offers advantages such as fast adsorption/elution kinetics, high sensitivity, low LODs, rapid analysis, selectivity, accuracy, and simplicity.

title: Effects of amyloid fibrils and divalent ions on the structure, rheological behavior, and gel properties of potato protein/carboxymethyl chitosan hydrogels
abstract: Plant protein-based hydrogels have attracted increasing attention, but the poor gel-forming ability of native proteins limits their applications. In this study, potato protein (PP) amyloid fibrils (PFs) with different fibrillation degrees were prepared by regulating the initial protein concentration and incorporated with carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS) and divalent ions (Zn 2+ or Mg 2+ ) to construct composite hydrogels. The results showed that moderately fibrillated PFs promoted β-sheet formation, strengthened intermolecular interactions, and facilitated a denser three-dimensional network, thereby improving water-holding capacity, viscoelasticity, and structural stability. Excessive fibrillation induced PF aggregation and fibril bundle formation, limiting network construction. Compared with Mg 2+ , Zn 2+ promoted stronger crosslinking, resulting in enhanced gel strength, springiness, and thermal stability. These effects were associated with the synergistic interactions among PP, PFs, and divalent ions. This strategy converts PP into structurally reinforcing PFs and enables its integration into high-performance hydrogels, providing a promising approach for the value-added utilization of PP.

title: Molecular simulations of food proteins: Assessing the basis and limits of interpretation
abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are increasingly applied to food proteins, often beyond the systems and conditions where the underlying models are well characterized. This review examines force-field benchmark coverage in food-protein MD and discusses the inferential distance between MD-derived quantities and experimental measurements. It also discusses recurring challenges and approaches beyond conventional atomistic MD. Direct force-field benchmarking remains sparse across food-protein systems and conditions, leaving model-dependent uncertainty incompletely characterized. Beyond model uncertainty, interpretive scope depends on how directly MD-derived quantities relate to the claimed outcome. Cross-scale explanations of higher-level functionality are therefore better treated as hypothesis-generating interpretations rather than direct evidence of mechanisms. Among recurring challenges, limited assessment of sampling reliability, particularly the frequent absence of reported independent replication, appears the most immediately addressable. Overall, this review emphasizes the need to consider both the scope of claims and the adequacy of the simulations supporting them in food-protein MD.

title: Uneven distribution of thiol precursors across red grape berry compartments shapes wine aroma quality: effects of variety, vintage, and skin composition
abstract: Varietal thiols constitute key aroma compounds in wine and occur in grape berries as odorless precursors. This study aimed to characterize thiol precursor diversity in 32 red grape varieties (Vitis vinifera and hybrids) by examining their distribution across berry compartments and assessing the effects of grape variety, vintage, and skin cell wall composition. Significant varietal differences were observed in thiol precursor content among berry tissues (average of 10.08 ± 15.02 μg/kg in skins, 10.22 ± 9.59 μg/kg in pulps and 0.94 ± 0.89 μg/kg in seeds), providing the first evidence of biosynthetic activity in seeds. Vintage strongly influenced precursor levels in all compartments, with a higher effect in skins, underscoring their central role. The lack of correlation between precursor content in berries and musts may indicate a selective extraction maybe due to interactions with cell wall polysaccharide. Furthermore, no correlation was found between must precursors and volatile thiols in wine, highlighting the complexity of thiol formation.

title: Sensomics-guided decoding of key flavor drivers in six new superior table grape cultivars
abstract: Table grapes are high-value global berry crops, whose commercial value relies on cultivar-specific flavor quality. However, critical gaps in systematic flavor characterization of new superior cultivars restrict data-driven quality evaluation and flavor-oriented breeding. Herein, this study conducted comprehensive sensomics-based flavor profiling of six new superior table grape cultivars. The results showed significant inter-cultivar differences in appearance, color, and flavor composition. Electronic sensory analysis identified fruity/floral notes as olfactory markers and sweetness/sourness/saltiness as taste discriminants across six cultivars. Using GC × GC-QTOFMS, 270 volatile compounds were detected and 47 key odorants were screened via GC-O and OAV, with a six-attribute grape aroma wheel constructed. Recombination reproduced cultivar-specific aroma profiles, and omission identified 21 key aroma-active compounds, with (Z)-3-hexenal, (E)-β-ionone, and (E,Z)-2,6-nonadienal as core contributors across several cultivars. These findings reveal the chemical and sensory basis of inter-cultivar flavor differences in table grapes, laying targeted support for flavor-oriented grape breeding.

title: Interfacial soft-hard locking of Pickering emulsions in marine biomass for enhancing fruit and vegetable preservation
Complementary integration of highly sensitive aptasensor and portable hydrogel for colorimetric detection of dhurrin in sorghum based on enhanced laccase-like activity of CuCo-MOFs
abstract: As a cyanogenic glycoside commonly found in grass family plants such as sorghum, dhurrin poses a serious threat to the food safety due to its hydrolysis product, hydrogen cyanide. But the equipment is expensive and the procedures complex, making it difficult to meet the demand for rapid on-site screening. This study develops a colorimetric aptasensor and its hydrogel format for rapid dhurrin detection in sorghum, based on aptamer-enhanced laccase-like activity of copper‑cobalt metal-organic frameworks. Dhurrin binding triggers aptamer detachment, weakening the enhancing effect of the aptamer on the laccase-like activity. The liquid-phase sensor achieves a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.566 μg·mL -1 , suitable for accurate quantitative analysis. The hydrogel sensor, with a higher LOD (200 μg·mL -1 ), provides stable color development within 20 min, offering good portability for on-site screening. This complementary system combines high sensitivity and specificity with operational simplicity, presenting a promising platform for rapid food hazard surveillance.

title: Comment on “Qualitative non-targeted screening by high resolution mass spectrometry of chemicals transference from plastic food contact materials after cooking”
abstract: Recently Bartolomé et al. have published a very interesting paper concerning the transference of various chemicals from plastic food contact materials to the food, after cooking. The authors have analyzed both intentionally and non-intentionally added substances. The results obtained by Bartolomé et al. bring significant elements of scientific innovation in the field of human exposure to chemicals transference through ingestion of foods that are cooked in their plastic packaging. The issues which are disputable in the paper by Bartolomé et al. concern the identification of two polyethylene glycol homologues and a polypropylene glycol homologue, as well as the tentative identification of some compounds by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, as discussed in details in this comment.

title: Sugar selection modulates bread flavor through carbon source-dependent metabolism and transcriptional reprogramming in baker's yeast
abstract: Bread flavor is fundamentally shaped by Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolism during dough fermentation, yet how the type of sugar used as a carbon source identity drives distinct volatile profiles remains poorly understood. By integrating transcriptomics, non-volatile metabolomics, and volatile metabolomics, we characterized the carbon source-dependent metabolic programs of the industrial baker's yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae SPC-SNU 70-1 fermenting glucose, fructose, maltose, and sucrose. Glucose established a baseline metabolic state with the highest relative levels of branched-chain fusel alcohols. Fructose induced a high-flux glycolytic overflow state, accompanied by higher relative levels of acetate esters associated with fruity and floral aroma notes, which appeared to be driven by substrate availability rather than transcriptional induction of alcohol acetyltransferases. Maltose established a balanced, hydrolysis-limited state without overflow metabolite accumulation. Sucrose, despite minimal transcriptional reprogramming, showed a distinct volatile profile, partly reflecting reduced yeast turnover of flour-derived lipid oxidation products. Integration of these datasets showed that fructose and maltose shared similar changes in respiratory and Ehrlich pathway gene expression yet yielded divergent metabolite and volatile profiles, suggesting that volatile biosynthesis is governed primarily by substrate availability rather than transcriptional regulation and providing a basis for bread flavor modulation through strategic carbon source selection.

title: Semirational engineering of glycosyltransferase UGTPg29 enables efficient biosynthesis of rebaudioside M and M2
abstract: Steviol glycosides (SGs) from Stevia rebaudiana are widely used as low-calorie sweeteners. Rebaudioside M (RebM), valued for its superior sensory characteristics, occurs at low abundance in S. rebaudiana, whereas its isomer rebaudioside M2 (RebM2), which features a distinctive β-1,6 glycosidic linkage at the C-19 position, has so far been obtained mainly through enzymatic conversion. Here, semi-rational engineering of the Panax ginseng glycosyltransferase UGTPg29 generated the triple mutant UGTPg29 C41I/A140S/A342L for rebaudioside D biosynthesis. This mutant exhibited a catalytic efficiency (k cat /K m ) 16.5-fold that of the wild type toward rebaudioside A (RebA) and retained 85.18% of its activity after 3 h at 50 °C. When coupled with UGT76G4 or NtUGT F72L/L123P/L157P , and Arabidopsis thaliana sucrose synthase, this enzyme drove one-pot cascades converting abundant RebA into 62.74 mM RebM and 41.01 mM RebM2, with molar yields of 75.8% and 66.1%. These results establish an efficient multi-enzyme strategy for the green production of high-value SGs.

title: A dual-module enhanced YOLO model integrating CSP-PTB for non-destructive freshness grading of Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei)
abstract: Peeled Litopenaeus vannamei is highly perishable during storage and transportation, yet current freshness assessment relies on subjective sensory evaluation or time-consuming destructive tests. We propose YOLO_FreshShrimp, an improved YOLOv8-based deep learning model for intelligent freshness grading. High-resolution shrimp images were paired with physicochemical indicators during 4 °C storage to establish visual-freshness mapping. A dataset with four grades (I, II, III, inedible) was constructed. The model integrates a cross-stage partial partially transformer block (CSP-PTB) feature module and a lightweight shared convolutional separate BN detection head (LSCSBD) to address subtle spoilage features and background interference. Ablation studies verified both modules' individual contributions to performance gains. This work delivers a practical, non-destructive, and rapid solution for automated shrimp freshness grading, offering strong potential for industrial quality control applications.

title: Ester markers of sweet fruit aroma prediction in Xiangning Cabernet Sauvignon dry red wines
abstract: Sweet fruit aroma is characteristic of Cabernet Sauvignon dry red wines from the Xiangning appellation, China Loess Plateau. To identify its volatile markers, 13 consecutive vintages of Xiangning Cabernet Sauvignon were analyzed using sensomics and chemometric approaches. Results indicated that sweet fruit aroma fluctuated inconsistently yet maintained consistently high levels across vintages, with vintage exerting a significant influence (P < 0.05). Moreover, fruity ester content increased and then slightly decreased during storage, among which ethyl acetate, isoamyl acetate, ethyl isobutyrate, ethyl butyrate, ethyl octanoate were identified as sweet fruit aroma markers through omission tests and PLSR. Sweet fruit aroma was attributed to ester marker content and ethyl acetate/ethyl isobutyrate proportion, with sweet fruit flavor intensity prediction model developed using natural logarithm concentrations of markers. This study identifies ester markers that confirm the aging potential of sweet fruit aroma in Xiangning Cabernet Sauvignon, providing data for the optimization of winemaking technology.

title: Shielding effect of d–p orbital hybridized nanozyme sensor array for machine learning-assisted discrimination of phenolic compounds
abstract: It is of great challenge to achieve efficient quantification and identification of phenolic sensors in food. Herein, a novel dual-channel colorimetric sensor array was developed relying on the differential shielding effect of phenolic compounds on the peroxidase-mimicking activity of as-synthesized nickel metal-embedded nitrogen-doped graphene nanozymes (Ni/NG and NiSe x /NG) in TMB-H 2 O 2 system. Moreover, experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrated that selenium element enhanced the d-p orbital hybridization between the nickel active site of the graphene-based nanozyme and the oxygen site of the phenolic hydroxyl group, enhancing the adsorption and shielding effect, which ultimately resulted in a lighter blue color. This colorimetric senor array based on dual-channels of Ni/NG and NiSe x /NG was able to high-sensitively detect and identify six kinds of phenolic compounds from concentrations and mixtures through principal component analysis (PCA). In addition, the integration of artificial neural network (ANN) algorithms with sensor arrays has enabled precise discrimination of six phenolic compounds in distinct plant-based beverages.

title: Aerogel-based oil sorbents derived from pomelo (Citrus grandis L.) peel powder as a fat replacer: effect on physicochemical properties, fatty acid composition and volatile profile of salami
abstract: Fat reduction in salami remains challenging because animal fat contributes substantially to texture and volatile development. This study extends pomelo peel-derived aerogel-based oil sorbents (ABOS) to fermented salami and evaluates their performance during 18 days of fermentation. ABOS reduced fat by 37.5-40.9% and energy by 23.7-25.4% (p < 0.05), while maintaining protein and ash contents (p > 0.05). Fat-reduced salami showed 27.1-32.8% higher final moisture and 23.3-37.7% lower weight loss than the control (p < 0.05), with final pH of 4.64-4.75 and aw of 0.83-0.85. Formulations containing 125 μm ABOS retained hardness and chewiness comparable to the control (p > 0.05), while exhibiting a more favourable PUFA/SFA ratio, lower atherogenicity index, and broadly comparable volatile profiles with reduced aldehyde formation. These findings demonstrate the technological feasibility of ABOS and support sustainable upcycling of pomelo peel into a functional fat replacer for fermented meat products.

title: Dual-mode lateral flow Immunochromatographic assay with Nanobody-functionalized hollow copper sulfide nanoprobe for Salmonella Typhimurium detection in food
abstract: To overcome the limited sensitivity and matrix tolerance of traditional lateral flow immunoassays (LFIA), we developed a nanobody-based colorimetric-photothermal dual-mode LFIA for detecting Salmonella Typhimurium. Hollow copper sulfide (HCuS) nanoparticles served as dual-signal reporters, leveraging a light-cavity effect to achieve a 49.26% photothermal conversion efficiency. To maximize target capture, biotinylated nanobodies were directionally immobilized onto HCuS via a streptavidin-biotin system, effectively preserving antigen-binding activity. Under optimized conditions, this platform enabled reliable quantitative evaluation with a naked-eye screening limit of 1 × 10 3 CFU mL -1 . The assay achieved quantitative detection limits of 129 CFU mL -1 (colorimetric) and 103 CFU mL -1 (photothermal), alongside a linear range of 10 3 -10 7 CFU mL -1 . Validation in spiked milk and juice samples yielded satisfactory recoveries ranging from 88.44% to 112.37%, with low relative standard deviations (<8.77%). Ultimately, this rationally designed immunoprobe provides a robust, rapid, and matrix-tolerant tool for on-site food safety monitoring.

title: Ratiometric fluorescent immunoassay mediated by alkaline phosphatase-catalyzed Eu3+ coordination polymers for the detection of Ochratoxin A
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) contamination severely threatens global food safety. Herein, a ratiometric fluorescent immunoassay method was established for trace OTA detection based on an alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-catalyzed Eu 3+ coordination polymer (Eu-CP). The Eu-CP probe is self-assembled from ciprofloxacin, adenosine monophosphate, and Eu 3+ . Upon activation by the Mg 2+ cofactor, ALP drives the dephosphorylation and subsequent structural disassembly of the Eu-CP framework, which synchronously regulates dual-emission fluorescent signals. In indirect competitive reaction, OTA competes with bovine serum albumin-OTA for limited antibodies, and the bound ALP-labeled secondary antibody is inversely correlated with OTA concentration. Based on the ratiometric fluorescence signal (F 618 /F 418 ), the proposed method exhibited a reliable linear range of 0.4883-62.5 ng/mL (R 2 = 0.9909) and a limit of detection as low as 0.0273 ng/mL. Recoveries in corn, oat and rice were 97.07%-119.11% with inter-batch CV < 10%. This study provides a simple and sensitive method for trace OTA detection.

title: Green synthesis of N-doped carbon quantum dots using Senecio scandens for Cu2+ sensing in tea sample
abstract: In this study, Nitrogen-doped carbon quantum dots (N-CQDs) were synthesized via a one-pot hydrothermal route using Senecio scandens as the carbon source and urea as the nitrogen dopant. The resulting N-CQDs are monodisperse and near-spherical, with an average diameter of 1.6 nm. It possess a partially graphitized core and abundant N/O-containing functional groups at the surface. The N-CQDs exhibits good photostability and disperses readily in water. Fluorescence quenching of the N-CQDs by copper ions follows a static photoluminescence mechanism. The response is linear over the range of 0-3 μmol/L, and the limit of detection is 0.646 μmol/L. The N-CQDs also display favorable biocompatibility which can be used for non-invasive fluorescence imaging of copper ions in live zebrafish larvae as well as in Arabidopsis thaliana roots. These results confirm the method is reliable for real tea sample analysis. Recoveries ranged from 95.64% to 102.44%, with relative standard deviations remaining below 4.79%. Overall, this study has established a practical sensing platform suitable for on-site Cu 2+ monitoring in tea and other agricultural food products.

title: Tea processing shapes the structural characteristics and gut microbiota-modulating potential of polysaccharides from the fresh summer tea
abstract: In this study, fresh summer tea leaves from the same cultivar and batch were processed into green, black, and dark (post-fermented) teas, and the corresponding polysaccharides (GTP, BTP, DTP) were subsequently extracted. Their digestive stability and gut microbial fermentability were evaluated. Simulated digestion of polysaccharides showed their strong resistance to enzymatic hydrolysis. In vitro anaerobic fermentation demonstrated GTP, BTP, and DTP could be effectively utilized by gut microbiota, resulting in increased production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). Microbial analysis revealed that GTP exerted the strongest inhibitory effect on Escherichia-Shigella, while BTP most effectively suppressed Allobaculum. GTP significantly promoted the growth of Lactobacillus, BTP enriched Bifidobacterium, and DTP favored the proliferation of Bacteroides species. Furthermore, cultivation experiments confirmed that BTP significantly promoted the growth of Bifidobacterium. These findings collectively demonstrate that tea processing methods play a critical role in shaping the structural characteristics and prebiotic potential of polysaccharides.

title: Characterization of key odor-active compounds in aged Chinese grain whisky by sensory-directed flavor analysis and simulation
abstract: Chinese grain whisky possesses distinctive flavor owing to the unique raw materials and barrel aging process, yet its aroma chemistry has not yet been fully studied. All the odor compounds of aged whisky were initially determined by two-dimensional gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC × GC-MS) with solid-phase microextraction (SPME) and liquid-liquid extraction (LLE). A total of 43 odor-active compounds were identified by aroma extract dilution analysis (AEDA) with gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS), with 31 compounds (OAV ≥ 1) confirmed. Moreover, the aroma recombination successfully replicated the original sensory profile (fruit, coconut, flower, acid, and vanilla), while the omission experiments demonstrated ethyl 2-methylbutanoate, ethyl octanoate, vanillin, whisky lactone, β-damascenone, 2-phenylethanol and 3-methylbutanoic acid were indispensable. Finally, OR1A1 exhibited the strong binding energy to β-damascenone, vanillin, whisky lactone and 2-phenylethanol through the hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. Therefore, comparing pre- and post-aging profiles confirmed critical odorants, providing a foundation for aroma control and quality standardization.

title: Dynamics of volatile and bioactive compounds in Criollo cocoa during spontaneous and Saccharomyces cerevisiae-inoculated fermentation and drying
abstract: Fermentation is a critical postharvest stage influencing cocoa quality through changes in volatile and bioactive compounds. This study evaluated these dynamics in Criollo cocoa beans from Amazonas, Peru, during spontaneous fermentation (SF), Saccharomyces cerevisiae -inoculated fermentation (SC), and drying. Temperature increased faster in SC than SF, while both treatments reached pH conditions associated with aroma precursor formation. Alcohols had the highest relative abundance among volatile families, whereas esters comprised the largest number of tentatively identified compounds; 2,3-butanediol, 2-heptanol, and 2-phenylethanol were the most abundant volatiles. SC yielded more tentatively identified volatiles at the end of fermentation. Drying increased the relative abundance of pyrazines and ketones, reorganizing the volatile profile during moisture loss. Processing stage and fermentation time were the main factors associated with differences in volatile composition. Theobromine remained the predominant bioactive compound, while SC retained higher catechin and epicatechin concentrations than SF at the end of fermentation.

title: ecent advances in Nanobody-based rapid detection of pesticide residues: A review
In-situ formed selenium-enriched CoSe2–FeSe2/N-doped MWCNT heterostructure for detection of butralin in agricultural food commodities
abstract: The development of reliable electrochemical sensors is essential for monitoring hazardous agrochemicals that threaten food safety. Butralin (BTN), a carcinogenic dinitroaniline herbicide, can migrate from soil to edible crops, raising significant health concerns. In this work, a sensitive voltammetric sensor was developed using an in-situ formed, selenium-enriched CoSe 2 @FeSe 2 (CFS) heterostructure integrated with N-doped multi-walled carbon nanotubes (N-MWCNTs). The CFS heterostructure promotes efficient charge transfer and enhances electrocatalytic activity, while N-doped MWCNTs improve conductivity and provide abundant active sites. The resulting composite (CFS/N-MWCNT) exhibited excellent analytical performance, with a low detection limit (0.013 μM), high sensitivity (3.751 μA μM -1 cm -2 ), and good repeatability. This sensor was successfully applied to determine BTN in real agricultural food samples, including vegetables and legumes, with satisfactory recovery. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed platform for practical determination of BTN in agricultural food matrices.

title: Pellicle-retained roasting enables endogenous polyphenol-mediated covalent remodeling of walnut protein for enhanced gelation and curcumin delivery
abstract: Pellicle-retained roasting was investigated for modifying walnut protein (WP) through endogenous polyphenol release and subsequent reactions during alkaline extraction. WPs from untreated pellicle-removed (K), roasted pellicle-removed (RK), pellicle-retained roasted (RK-P), and in-shell roasted (RK-P-S) kernels were compared. K and RK showed polyphenol grafting contents of 6.41 and 10.13 mg GAE/g and solubilities of 17.54% and 21.42%, whereas RK-P reached 181.46 mg GAE/g and 56.53%, respectively. Hydrophobic interactions and disulfide bonds contributed substantially to RK-P gel stabilization, with hardness reaching 155 g versus 28.4 g for K and 58.8 g for RK. RK-P achieved a curcumin retention efficiency (RE) of 81.02% and cumulative intestinal release of 32.73%, versus 50.87% and 8.27% for K and 59.04% and 11.45% for RK, while limiting gastric release to 2.19%. RK-P-S showed intermediate performance. These results indicate that pellicle retention promotes WP remodeling and gelation and enhances curcumin retention and intestinal-phase release under the tested conditions.

title: Competitive difference-driven Ag@Pt nanozyme on a single gold nanowire sensing platform integrated with machine learning for accurate identification of multiple tetracycline antibiotics
abstract: The wide use of tetracycline antibiotics (TCs) exists serious public safety concern for human health due to their accumulation in foods and environments. Meanwhile, various kinds of TCs are frequently present simultaneously in practical environments, it is vital to come up with innovative solutions for high-sensitivity detection and accurate identification. Herein, a novel strategy of competitive difference-driven Ag@Pt nanozyme on a single gold nanowire (Au NW) sensing platform was developed for accurate identification of multiple TCs. Hollow dendritic Ag@Pt nanoparticles (NPs) with peroxidase-like (POD-like) activity have been synthesized and can decompose H 2 O 2 to produce reactive oxygen species (ROS), which subsequently oxidize 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) into oxidized TMB (ox-TMB). In the presence of both TCs and TMB, a competitive reaction with ROS occurs, attenuating the extent of TMB oxidation. Building on this, this platform integrates surface-enhanced Raman scattering and electrochemical (SERS/EC) techniques and further combines them with machine learning to achieve ultrasensitive quantitative detection and accurate identification of five TCs, including minocycline (MC), tetracycline (TET), oxytetracycline (OTC), chlortetracycline (CTC), and doxycycline (DOX). It enables accurate detection of various targets at low concentrations ranging from 2 × 10 -5 ppm to 2 × 10 -2 ppm, with a detection limit as low as 3.54 × 10 -7 ppm for MC. This study combines efficient catalytic activity of nanozymes, the significant advantages brought by the miniaturization of the single Au NW platform, and the structural differences among various TCs, offering significant application value for the rapid, direct, and simultaneous detection of multiple hazards in the environment and food chain.

title: An antifouling electrochemical aptasensor engineered with zwitterionic terpolymer and gold nanostars for robust analysis of oxytetracycline in food
abstract: Electrochemical sensors still suffer from challenges associated with interference caused by fouling in complex matrices. To address this issue, we designed a tailored high-performance antifouling sensor interface based on a thiol-terminated zwitterionic terpolymer, [P(MPC-CBMA-MAA)-SH, PMCM-SH], by fine-tuning the composition of two zwitterionic moieties, including 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC) and carboxybetaine methacrylate (CBMA), along with methacrylic acid (MAA) for post-functionalization. Highly conductive multi-branched gold nanostars (AuNSs) were introduced to assist sensitive assaying. The precise regulation of PMCM-SH enabled to form a dense and stable hydration layer, endowing excellent antifouling performance, which was validated in simulated solutions and food matrices. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations offered molecular-level insights into its superior hydration capacity. The aptasensor exhibited excellent analytical performance with a low limit of detection (LOD, 2.19 pg·mL -1 ) and high recoveries of 98.9-106.9% for oxytetracycline (OTC) in milk, eggs, and pork, exhibiting great potential in solving the limitation of fouling for sensor interface.

title: Insights into the effects of microscopic fractal features, supramolecular structures on digestibility of retrograded starch gels
abstract: The digestibility of starch gels is closely associated with their microstructure, yet quantitative understanding remains limited. Starch gels prepared from wheat, high-amylose wheat, corn, high-amylose corn, potato, pea, and sweet potato starches were investigated using fractal analysis, DSC, ATR-FTIR, XRD, and digestion kinetic. Six starches were evaluated at 10%, 20%, and 30%, whereas high-amylose corn starch was tested at 15%, 25%, and 35% because it did not form a stable, testable gel at 10%. Increasing starch concentration was generally associated with greater microstructural complexity and structural order. Pore fractal dimension (D f ) was strongly positively correlated with the rapid-phase digestion rate (k₁) and negatively correlated with the slow-phase rate (k₂) and fitted asymptotic hydrolysis extent (C ∞ ). Thus, pore D f represents a structural indicator strongly associated with starch digestibility. These findings clarify relationships between gel structural characteristics and starch digestion, providing a basis for designing starch-based foods with tailored digestibility.

title: Multi-omics comparison of Rhodotus palmatus and Armillaria mellea reveals distinct metabolomic profiles and prebiotic potential of their polysaccharides
abstract: Edible mushrooms are increasingly recognized as sources of bioactive compounds with potential health benefits, yet comprehensive characterization of recently cultivated species remains limited. Herein, multi-platform metabolomics and in vitro fermentation were employed to compare their chemical composition and prebiotic potential. GC-MS and UHPLC-HRMS identified over 4800 differential metabolites between RP and AM. Targeted amino acid profiling revealed significantly higher levels of free and acid-extractable amino acids, including essential amino acids, in RP compared to AM, indicating distinct amino acid profiles between the two species. Lipidomics identified over 1500 differential lipids, providing chemotaxonomic markers for species authentication. In vitro fermentation demonstrated that RP crude polysaccharides significantly modulated gut microbiota, enriching beneficial Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae while suppressing Proteobacteria. Notably, RP and AM polysaccharides exhibited distinct fermentation signatures, suggesting species-specific prebiotic applications. These findings establish RP as a nutritionally superior edible mushroom with promising prebiotic potential.

title: Exploring the potential of enzymatic hydrolysis assisted glycosylation to modify β-lactoglobulin fibrils: Insights into aggregation behavior, functional properties and antibody binding capacity
abstract: This study investigated the effects of enzymatic hydrolysis and glycosylation on the self-assembly and functional properties of β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) amyloid fibrils. Thioflavin T fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed the successful formation of amyloid fibrils from modified β-LG samples. Transmission electron microscopy observations revealed that β-LG, hydrolyzed β-LG, and glycosylated-hydrolyzed β-LG formed relatively long fibrils (Fβ-LG), a coexistence of long and short fibrils (FHβ-LG), and a fibril system that was shorter than Fβ-LG (FGHβ-LG), respectively. FGHβ-LG exhibited significantly enhanced emulsifying properties, antioxidant capacity, and foaming capacity compared to β-LG. Moreover, these aggregates remarkably reduced the IgE and IgG binding to β-LG. Amino groups exposed during enzymatic hydrolysis promoted glycosylation efficiency, while the conjugated glycosyl chains regulated the surface hydrophilicity of the fibrils. In summary, this sequential modification expands the potential applications of β-LG fibrils as functional food ingredients and emulsifiers in food systems.

title: Hydroxyl position of 3 flavonoid isomers modulate gelatin structure-properties relationship: Structural rearrangement, non-covalent binding mechanism and function regulation
abstract: Flavonoid modification is an effective method to improve protein properties. Non-covalent complexes of gelatin and flavonoid isomers with same hydroxyl number but different hydroxyl position (kaempferol-KA, luteolin-LUT and fisetin-FIS) were fabricated. Binding mechanism and their properties were elucidated. Results showed that the ordered α-helix of gelatin was transferred to disordered structures after the addition of flavonoids by lowering the content of hydrogen bonds and enhancing the contents of ionic bonds and hydrophobic interactions. The conformation change of gelatin was correlated with hydroxyl position of flavonoid. KA (3-5-4' OH) endowed gelatin with small particle size. LUT (5-3'-4' OH) endowed gelatin with good emulsifying properties due to high hydrophobic interactions (0.42 ± 0.07) and random coil (39.2%). FIS (3-3'-4' OH) endowed gelatin with optimal foaming capacity and gel properties due to high surface hydrophobicity (302.30 ± 15.78). Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations showed that the main binding ways might be hydrogen bonds, van der Waals forces, and hydrophobic interactions. GE-KA and GE-FIS showed an exothermic interactions, whereas GE-LUT exhibited a pronounced entropy-driven binding mode.

title: Oleanolic acid enhances milk fat synthesis in bovine mammary epithelial cells via antioxidant-lipid metabolism crosstalk: A natural strategy for improving dairy product quality
abstract: This study investigates the effects of rosemary-derived compounds on milk fat synthesis in bovine mammary epithelial cells (BMECs). Using a combination of multi-omics technologies, we evaluated the lipogenic potential of key bioactive constituents, including rosmarinic acid (RA), oleanolic acid (OA), ursolic acid, thymol, and carvacrol. Our findings reveal that OA significantly enhances lipid droplet accumulation and triglyceride synthesis in BMECs, alongside improving antioxidant defenses. Lipidomics analysis identified OA-induced alterations in lipid composition, with marked increases in triglycerides and phospholipids. Transcriptomic profiling highlighted key regulatory pathways such as PPAR signaling and triglyceride homeostasis. OA also upregulated the expression of lipid metabolism-related genes (OLR1, INHBE, and SESN2), suggesting its potential as a natural strategy to promote milk fat synthesis. These results provide a scientific foundation for utilizing rosemary-derived compounds in dairy nutrition.

title: Proteomic insights into the mechanism of atmospheric cold plasma in reducing muscle protein degradation in Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) during cold storage
abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatments at different voltages (10-50 kV) in mitigating muscle protein degradation and maintaining the quality of Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) during refrigerated storage at 4 °C. Shrimp samples were treated with ACP at various voltages, and physicochemical indices, including trichloroacetic acid (TCA)-soluble peptides, acid-soluble nitrogen (ASN), and free amino acid (FAA) contents, were monitored throughout storage. Proteomic analysis was conducted to identify differentially expressed proteins (DAPs), followed by Gene Ontology (GO), KEGG pathway, and protein-protein interaction analyses to elucidate functional alterations. Findings indicated that the 50 kV ACP treatment markedly retarded the buildup of TCA-soluble peptides and ASN, and alleviated fluctuations in FAA levels relative to the control. Over the 0-12-day storage interval, fewer differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) were identified in the 50 kV-treated group than in the untreated control group. Bioinformatic analyses suggested that these DAPs were largely linked to the preservation of protein structure. Correlation analysis suggested that reactive species generated by ACP induced oxidative modification of key endogenous proteases (cathepsins B, L, D, and calpains), leading to conformational changes that inhibited enzyme activity. Consequently, hydrolysis of myosin heavy chains and actin was reduced, preserving myofibrillar integrity, protein solubility, and cytoskeletal stability. Overall, ACP treatment effectively impeded protein degradation through a non-thermal mechanism, offering a sustainable preservation strategy to extend the shelf life of shrimp and other high-protein aquatic products while minimizing quality deterioration and economic losses.

title: Machine learning-assisted dual-channel FeZnCu@CNP nanozyme sensor array for qualitative and quantitative analysis of multiple pesticides
abstract: To fulfil rapid identification and quantification of various pesticide residues, we first synthesized a FeZnCu@CNP nanozyme with dual laccase- and peroxidase-like activities, enabling differential responses to eight pesticides (Gly, Car, Met, TBZ, CBZ, PCNB, ACE, and MCPA) via coordination and hydrogen-bonding interactions. The dual-channel nanozyme sensor array based on machine learning was developed, successfully discriminating these pesticides at 0.1-100 μg/mL for both qualitative and quantitative detection with an LOD of 0.013 μg/mL. Principal component analysis (PCA) and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) confirmed effective differentiation of eight individual pesticides and their mixtures at varied concentrations and ratios. The concentration-independent discrimination model based on the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm demonstrated outstanding accuracy in pesticide detection and differentiation. Importantly, this model demonstrated strong anti-interference and high feasibility for fruit/vegetable and blind sample identification. This sensor array enables concentration-independent qualitative identification and accurate quantitation of eight residues, offering a supplementary rapid-screening strategy for multi-pesticide detection.

title: Proteolysis and peptide release during in vitro digestion at infant conditions of bovine casein ingredients in comparison with human milk
abstract: The present study evaluated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion behavior and peptide generation in infant conditions of simplified milk protein blends composed of micellar casein isolates (MCI) and whey protein concentrate (WPC) blends (40,60, 1.2% w/w total protein). Standard MCI, plasmin-treated (PMCI), and calcium-reduced (CaMCI) forms of MCI were compared, alongside pure WPC and human milk (HM) as references. During gastric digestion, caseins were rapidly hydrolyzed, whereas whey proteins remained largely intact until intestinal digestion. Plasmin pre-hydrolysis generated peptides and exposed additional pepsin cleavage sites, resulting in enhanced gastric hydrolysis and peptide release in PMCI:WPC compared with MCI:WPC. Decalcification also facilitated digestion, but its effect was pronounced most in intestinal phase, where CaMCI:WPC produced a markedly higher level of peptides due to improved protease accessibility. Both treatments yielded higher levels of bioactive peptides than MCI:WPC. HM produced more diverse but less abundant peptides, and bioactive peptides were less than protein mixtures.

title: Rational hapten design enables monoclonal antibody-based immunoassays for class-selective detection of phthalate esters in edible oils
abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs) are frequently detected in edible oils, necessitating rapid detection methods. However, the small molecular size and high structural similarity of PAEs make it challenging to develop antibodies that combine analytical sensitivity with group-selective recognition. Herein, a monoclonal antibody (mAb) with group-selective recognition toward dibutyl phthalate (DBP), diallyl phthalate (DAP), and diethyl phthalate (DEP) was generated through rational hapten design guided by computational analysis. Based on this mAb, an indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ic-ELISA) and a colloidal gold immunochromatographic strip (ICS) were developed for rapid quantitative detection. The optimized ic-ELISA exhibited half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) values of 20.4, 80.1, and 110.4 ng/mL for DBP, DAP, and DEP, respectively, while showing <1% cross-reactivity with other tested phthalate analogues. The ICS enabled visual detection within 15 min, with visual limit of detections (vLODs) of 20, 100, and 200 ng/mL for DBP, DAP, and DEP in edible oils, respectively. By integrating computationally guided hapten design with complementary quantitative and rapid screening formats, this study provides a practical platform for class-selective screening of PAEs in edible oils and a useful strategy for developing group-recognizing antibodies against structurally related small-molecule contaminants.

title: The tea specific pretreatment methods for rapid detection of aflatoxin B1 and ochratoxin A on dark tea samples
abstract: Rapid test strips have been widely used for mycotoxins detection in foods; however, their application in tea is strictly limited by pronounced matrix interference. In this study, tea-specific cleaning methods were developed to enable rapid detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB 1 ) and ochratoxin A (OTA) in dark tea and tea infusions. The proposed methods achieved recoveries ranging from 81.5% to 128.07% for AFB 1 and ranging from 80.05% to 131.48% for OTA. Method validation demonstrated robust accuracy and precision, with AFB 1 recoveries of 83.82%-110.00% (RSDs: 0.46%-12.74%) and OTA recoveries of 82.83%-118.47% (RSDs: 0.69%-11.74%). The limits of detection (LODs) were 1.14-2.52 μg/L for AFB 1 and were 1.13-3.04 μg/L for OTA in tea samples. The tea-specific clean-up effectively minimized matrix interference, yielding extracts compatible with rapid test strips for qualitative and quantitative testing. Overall, this study provides a simple, efficient and cost-effective strategy for improving the reliability of rapid mycotoxins detection in complex tea matrices.

title: Revealing the characteristic aroma compounds and metabolites basis of Yunnan coffee using a combined sensomics and metabolomics strategy
abstract: Yunnan Arabica coffee is renowned for its distinctive sweet caramel aroma and balanced flavor, yet the key aroma compounds and their metabolic basis remain unclear. This study combined sensomics and metabolomics to compare three Yunnan Arabica varieties (Catimor, Typica and Bourbon) with Robusta (RT). Arabica samples exhibited enhanced sweetness and more prominent floral and fruity notes. A total of 102 volatiles were identified via HS-SPME/GC-MS, with furans and pyrazines being dominant. Eight key volatile metabolites (VMs) were selected based on odor activity value (OAV) and variable importance in projection (VIP). Molecular docking demonstrated their binding to olfactory receptors OR1A1/OR1A2 through hydrogen-bonds and hydrophobic interactions (-7.14 to -4.17 kcal/mol). Integrated pathway enrichment and correlation analyses revealed L-phenylalanine as a potential precursor of 2-phenylethanol, and ferulic acid as a potential precursor of 2-methoxy-4-vinylphenol and 2-methoxyphenol. These findings reveal the metabolic and molecular foundation of Yunnan Arabica coffee's distinctive aroma profile.

title: Dual-mode detection of tetracyclines in animal-derived food samples based on MOF-on-MOF heterostructure fluorescent sensor coupled with machine learning algorithms
abstract: Tetracyclines (TCs) that accumulate in food enter the human body through the food chain, leading to drug resistance and health risks. This study synthesized a heterostructure fluorescent sensor, Zn-TCPP-MOF/NH 2 -MIL-53(Al) (abbreviated ZTA) for TCs detection. A dual-mode detection system was established by integrating fluorescence spectroscopy with machine learning algorithms and fluorescence imaging with YOLOv5, enabling precise detection of TCs. The π-π stacking reduced ZTA electron density to promote electron transfer, inducing specific recognition of TCs with a low detection limit of 0.012 μmol/L. Machine learning algorithms of k-means clustering, hierarchical cluster analysis, support vector machine, random forest, logistic regression, and decision tree achieved 100.0%, and YOLOv5 reached 99.8% precision for TCs identification. The ZTA sensor achieved recovery rates between 95.40%-108.50% for TCs detection in animal-derived foods. This study facilitated the design of a MOF-on-MOF heterostructure sensor and provided an intelligent detection strategy for the rapid on-site monitoring of antibiotic residues.

title: Hierarchically porous sodium alginate ultra-fine nanofiber-based aerogel fiber aggregates for enhanced lysozyme separation and purification
abstract: Achieving high throughput without compromising adsorption capacity remains a central challenge in bioprocessing. Herein, we report the rational design and fabrication of hierarchically porous sodium alginate nanofiber-based aerogel fiber aggregates (SANFAFs), prepared by integrating non-solvent-induced phase separation and centrifugal wet-spinning. The resulting material features a dual-scale pore network. Inter-fiber macropores facilitate convective mass transfer, while nanopores provide a large accessible specific surface area for protein binding. Benefiting from deprotonated carboxylate groups along the sodium alginate (SA) polymer backbone, SANFAFs possess inherent cation-exchange functionality. SANFAFs reach a static lysozyme adsorption capacity of 2842.43 ± 60.35 mg/g. Under column operation, they achieve a flow rate of 13.33 ± 1.52 L·h -1 at 0.1 bar and a dynamic binding capacity of 106.19 ± 3.81 mg/mL (10% breakthrough), surpassing commercial cation-exchange microspheres. Selective enrichment of lysozyme from pretreated egg white validates the practical performance of SANFAFs, highlighting their promise as chromatographic media for laboratory-scale protein bioprocessing.

title: Proteomics and lipidomics of a diverse oat (Avena sativa L.) cohort reveal molecular signatures underlying groat oil phenotype
abstract: High oil content in oat grains and flour contributes to aggregate formation, hindering oat milling and fractionation processes. Breeding for low-oil oat varieties presents a cost-effective approach. Using a cohort of ninety Australian oat genotypes, we identified acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2 (ACCase2) protein as a strong determinant of oat oil content. Additional candidates in fatty acid synthesis (FAS) also demonstrated strong, positive correlations with oil content. Comparison of low-, medium- and high-oil oat proteomes highlighted an inverse relationship between fatty acid and protein syntheses, which was reflected in the grain phenotypes. Lipidomic analysis revealed differences in lipid partitioning between triacylglycerols and phospholipids that were associated with oat grain oil content, further highlighting potential targets in the triacylglycerol assembly pathway. This study provides further molecular insights into oat oil synthesis, which may inform future breeding strategies aimed at improving oat processing efficiency and nutritional quality.

title: Integrated virtual screening and experimental validation identify dietary phytochemicals as PI3Kα inhibitors with antiproliferative activity
abstract: The phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT/mTOR pathway is a central regulator of cancer progression, with frequent activation of the PI3Kα catalytic subunit (p110α) in breast cancer. Here, an integrated in silico to experimental workflow was applied to systematically identify dietary phytochemicals capable of inhibiting PI3Kα and suppressing cancer cell proliferation. A curated PhytoHub library comprising 1966 food-derived compounds was screened by molecular docking against the PI3Kα catalytic domain, followed by isoform-specific enzymatic validation and cellular evaluation. Several flavonoids demonstrated strong PI3Kα inhibition at 30 μM, with jaceosidin and luteolin exhibiting the highest potency (IC₅₀ ≤ 0.1 and 0.76 μM, respectively), whereas anthocyanidins delphinidin and petunidin showed weaker activity. In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, myricetin, delphinidin, apigenin, and kaempferol produced the strongest antiproliferative effects (~55-65% inhibition; p < 0.05). These findings identify flavone-type scaffolds as potent PI3Kα inhibitors and highlight dietary flavonoids as promising functional food bioactives targeting oncogenic signaling.

title: The first comprehensive analysis of the flavor of Freekeh: a toasted, smoked, green durum wheat product, by analytical and sensory approaches
abstract: Freekeh, smoked immature durum wheat, has gastronomic significance and attractive nutritional values, fueling increasing global demand. Yet, knowledge regarding its flavor chemistry and sensory properties remains absent, hindering quality control and market expansion. We employed analytical and sensory methods, with multivariate modeling, to study how Freekeh flavor is shaped by agro-technical and processing practices. Freekeh flavor is a mixture of grain-derived metabolites and processing products, yielding >300 volatiles. Twenty volatiles were validated as key-odorants (phenols, pyrazines, aldehydes) via GC-olfactometry; phenols comprising most of the profile. Grain maturity significantly influences flavor: early-harvest Freekeh is more aromatic, sweet, umami and kokumi due to elevated sugars, amino acids, 5'-ribonucleotides and γ-glutamyl peptides. Genotype and toasting intensity similarly play a pivotal role in shaping flavor. This study serves as the inaugural roadmap to freekeh flavor, establishing a predictive chemical/sensory framework uncovering novel cereal flavors, and providing producers benchmarks to fine-tune quality using early-harvest practices.

title: Ratio-dependent co-encapsulation of heptanal and 1-octen-3-ol by V-type starch: Structural characterization and molecular dynamics insights
abstract: The encapsulation and interaction mechanisms of off-odors in aquatic products are crucial for the food industry. In this study, flexible V-type starch was utilized to adsorb heptanal and 1-octen-3-ol as representative binary off-odor compounds related to oyster enzymatic hydrolysate. Although 1-octen-3-ol alone has a higher affinity for V-type starch than heptanal, an appropriate proportion of 1-octen-3-ol enhances the encapsulation and loading efficiency of heptanal in the binary system. Compared with the single system, the binary system exhibited lower relative crystallinity and greater enthalpy, suggesting that co-inclusion of the two guest molecules disturbed the long-range crystalline packing while increasing the extent and/or stability of inclusion complex formation. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that 1-octen-3-ol induced a larger amylose helical cavity and modified the hydrogen-bond network, which may facilitate heptanal accommodation at an appropriate H/O ratio. These findings clarify binary off-odor co-encapsulation by V-type starch and provide a basis for developing starch-based odor-scavenging materials for aquatic foods.

title: Simultaneous determination of eight free- or cross-linked advanced glycation end products in different processed meat products based on UPLC-MS/MS
abstract: A universal ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed for the simultaneous detection of eight free- or cross-linked advanced glycation end products (AGEs), including Nε-carboxymethyllysine, Nε-carboxyethyllysine, N δ -(5-hydro-5-methyl-4-imidazolon-2-yl)ornithine, glyoxal-derived hydroimidazolone, methylglyoxal lysine dimer, glyoxal lysine dimer, pyrraline and argpyrimidine. This method achieved the separation and quantification of the eight AGEs substances within 16 min. All analytes exhibited high correlation coefficients (R 2 > 0.999) within their respective linear ranges. Limits of detection and quantification in reconstituted solution were 0.8-2.5 and 2.5-5.5 μg/L, corresponding to 0.08-0.25 and 0.25-0.55 mg/kg in samples. Respectively. Method validation was performed using crispy fried pork as a blank matrix. The recovery rates ranged from 85.5% to 122.0%, with acceptable intra-day and inter-day precision. This method was successfully applied to the detection of AGEs in 30 different representative meat products, providing technical support for the research on the formation and control of AGEs.

title: A multifunctional WPC-linoleic acid-EGCG complex: structural characterization, bioactivity, and application as a butter substitute in processed cheese
abstract: Developing multifunctional ingredients for fat reduction without quality loss is challenging. This study developed a whey protein concentrate-linoleic acid-epigallocatechin gallate (WPC-LA-EGCG) ternary complex as a butter substitute in processed cheese. Multi-spectroscopy experiments and molecular docking simulations suggested that hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic, and electrostatic interactions reconfigured protein secondary structure. At optimal EGCG levels (<0.1%), the complex showed enhanced molecular flexibility, interfacial adsorption, emulsifying activity, and stability. In vitro, the complex showed synergistic antioxidant activity, reduced IgE-binding (52.5-68.7% by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, ELISA), and modulated glucose consumption and lipid metabolism in 3 T3-L1 adipocytes. However, these findings are preliminary and require in vivo validation. Replacing 30.4% butter, the complex transformed the matrix into a continuous protein-dominant gel, improving texture, viscoelastic moduli (G', G″), and thermal stability. Electronic tongue evaluation detected no notable taste profile deterioration. The tailored complex offers a viable strategy for healthier low-fat dairy products with enhanced functionality and bioactivity.

title: Influence of pea protein on structural modulation of tapioca starch emulsion gels: Vitamin E release behavior and potential as a dysphagia-friendly food matrix
abstract: This study investigated the influence of pea protein (PP) on the structural modulation and vitamin E (VE) release behavior of tapioca starch (TS)-based emulsion gels and evaluated their potential as a dysphagia-friendly food matrix. TS/PP-based emulsion gels were prepared with different PP concentrations. FE-SEM and CLSM suggested a more compact gel network and finer oil-phase dispersion at higher PP concentrations, and FT-IR and XRD indicated structural changes and possible TS-PP interactions, potentially involving hydrogen bonding. The encapsulation efficiency of VE increased from 80.0% to 99.6% as the PP concentration increased from 0% to 10%, respectively. In vitro release studies showed that increasing PP concentration progressively delayed VE release under simulated gastrointestinal conditions. According to the IDDSI test, emulsion gels containing 5.0% and 7.5% PP corresponded to level 4, and those containing 10% PP corresponded to level 5, indicating their potential as a dysphagia-friendly food matrix for VE delivery.

title: Comparative antifungal activity of three essential oils against mycotoxigenic Fusarium graminearum and multi-omics analysis
abstract: This study aims to identify eco-friendly essential oils (EOs) with dual antifungal and anti-mycotoxigenic activity against Fusarium graminearum, a destructive cereal pathogen associated with yield loss and deoxynivalenol (DON) contamination, compare their bioactivity and elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Among the seven tested EOs, carvacrol, cinnamaldehyde and citral were the most effective, markedly inhibiting mycelial growth, conidial germination, and DON production. These EOs showed greater inhibitory activity than sodium diacetate (SDA), which upregulated key TRI genes. Multi-omics analyses revealed that the tested EOs induced cell wall and membrane damage, mitochondrial dysfunction and perturbations in critical metabolic pathways, including terpenoid biosynthesis and energy metabolism. Wheat seedling assays further demonstrated that carvacrol, cinnamaldehyde and their synergistic combinations substantially reduced crown rot and DON accumulation, whereas SDA exacerbated the disease. These findings identify promising EO candidates and provide a robust scientific basis for developing EO-based sustainable biocontrol strategies against F. graminearum in wheat.

title: Construction of dual-mode bimetallic MOF/carbon fiber biosensor and its application in visual detection of L-cysteine
abstract: A bimetallic ZnNi-MOF was grown on carbon fiber via a one-pot hydrothermal method. Compared with single-metal MOFs, the resulting material exhibited enhanced luminescence and electrochemical activity, which enabled the construction of a flexible dual-mode sensor for rapid fluorescence-electrochemical detection of L-cysteine. Electrochemical detection exhibited a linear range of 1 nM-10 μM with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.017 nM, while fluorescence sensing gave a linear range of 1 μM-1 M with a LOD of 0.89 μM. Both modes showed good selectivity and stability. Flexible sensors were also prepared by impregnating filter paper and textiles, wet spinning, and hydrogel microspheres. By combining the sensor with mobile phone software that collects the RGB values of the fluorescence color change, visual detection of L-cysteine can be achieved. The sensor successfully determined L-cysteine in human sweat and milk, with recoveries of 93-114% and RSDs of 2.43-5.32%, demonstrating promising applications in intelligent wearable monitoring, precision medicine, and food safety.

title: The weak gluten paradox: Post-hydrolysis protein reaggregation and glutenin ratio synergistically retard starch digestion
abstract: While intact gluten networks modulate starch digestion, the multiscale regulatory mechanisms of gluten hydrolysates remain elusive. This study explored how gluten hydrolysates, varying in strength and glutenin-to-gliadin ratio, modulate starch digestibility through protein network reconstruction and molecular interactions. We identified a reversal of the strength-dependent pattern: weak-gluten hydrolysates retard starch digestion more effectively than their strong-gluten counterparts. Hydrolysis of weak gluten appears to enhance subsequent protein reaggregation during hydrothermal processing, consistent with a compact protein-starch matrix. Increasing the glutenin ratio raised unextractable polymeric protein from 5.78% to 26.33%. Conversely, elevating the gliadin ratio impaired the structural barrier in weak gluten while altering hydrophobic assemblies in strong systems. These findings support a dual-mechanism framework in which reconstructed protein networks and interfacial protein-starch and protein-enzyme interactions jointly regulate starch digestion, pointing to protein-mediated strategies in wheat-based foods.

title: Construction of gelatin-based rutin delivery systems by ultrasound/pH-shifting pretreatment and polysaccharide modulation
abstract: This study investigated the effects of polysaccharide types (chitosan oligosaccharide (COS), dextran, and soybean soluble polysaccharide (SSPS)) and ultrasound intensity (0, 300, and 500 W) on rutin-loaded gelatin nanoparticles prepared by pH-shifting. Ultrasound-assisted pH-shifting modified gelatin conformation, promoting polysaccharide binding and improving encapsulation and delivery. The results indicate that the sample modified with 500 W ultrasonication combined with pH 12.0 shift and SSPS (U500GS) exhibited optimal performance (p < 0.05), including the smallest particle size, the highest encapsulation efficiency, and the best stability, which may be possibly attributed to the steric hindrance of the SSPS network. In vitro digestion showed that U500GS reduced the burst release of rutin, enhanced bioaccessibility (89.71%, p < 0.05), and exhibited the strongest antioxidant activity (DPPH: 91.23%; ABTS: 86.43%; p < 0.05) and the highest protease hydrolysis resistance (hydrolysis degree: 53.28%; p < 0.05). This work reveals the roles of protein pretreatment and polysaccharide binding in delivery systems, offering a strategy for hydrophobic polyphenol utilization.

title: pH-shifting and high-intensity ultrasound enable the functional design of quinoa protein isolate as a plant-based emulsifier
abstract: Quinoa protein isolate (QPI) derived from dehulling by-products was structurally tailored using a combined pH-shifting and high-intensity ultrasound (HIU) approach to enhance its functionality as a plant-based emulsifier. Alkaline conditions (pH 11) promoted protein unfolding, increasing solubility, surface charge, and exposure of reactive groups, including higher free sulfhydryl content and oil-holding capacity. These changes improved interfacial activity and emulsifying performance. A Box-Behnken design optimized HIU conditions and formulation variables, producing emulsions with minimal phase separation (SI ≈ 0%), small droplet size (0.35 ± 0.02 μm), and dominant elastic behavior (G' > G″). The optimized system also showed high thermal stability (98% at 80 °C). These findings demonstrate that pH-induced structural modification combined with ultrasound enables the functional design of QPI as an effective emulsifier and highlights quinoa by-products as sustainable sources of clean-label ingredients.

title: SOS-HPTLC: second-order spectral high-performance thin-layer chromatography as a sustainable approach for wine discrimination
abstract: An innovative high-performance thin-layer chromatography approach with second-order spectral detection (HPTLC-SOS) integrates multi-wavelength UV-Vis data (286-525 nm) across eight discrete retardation factor (Rf) positions to characterize complex oenological matrices. Seventy-one Argentine wines from three regions and multiple monovarietals (including Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon) were analyzed. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of this compact three-dimensional dataset achieved prominent separation based simultaneously on varietal identity (PC1) and geographical origin (PC2). Cluster-specific loading heatmaps validated the chemical basis of this discrimination. Furthermore, HPTLC-SOS outperformed a reference HPLC-DAD technique in throughput (7.2 vs. 60 min/sample) and greenness, as confirmed by the AGREE metric (0.74 vs. 0.50). This superiority stems from parallel processing, passive capillary development, and over 98% reduction in solvent waste. Consequently, this discrete-sampling strategy represents a reliable, high-throughput, and sustainable analytical platform for wine traceability and quality control.

title: Improved thermal stability of 1,4-α-glucan branching enzyme via the semi-rational design of the flexible loops and disulfide bonds for starch modification
abstract: The industrial application of 1,4-α-glucan branching enzyme in high-temperature starch modification requires enhanced thermostability, yet engineering this enzyme from Aquifex aeolicus is hindered by the absence of a crystal structure. Here, a semi-rational strategy combining flexible loop rigidification and disulfide bond introduction was employed to improve the enzyme thermostability based on the AlphaFold2 prediction model. The combinatorial mutant V155L-V280I-D282N-H408C-W536C exhibited enhanced thermal stability, with a half-inactivation time at 85 °C extended from 25 to 81 min and a half-inactivation temperature increased by 4.15 °C from 83.62 to 87.77 °C. Differential scanning calorimetry showed a 7.29 °C increase in melting temperature relative to the wild-type. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed reduced flexibility at mutation sites and stabilized catalytic triad geometry. When applied to potato starch modification, the mutant increased amylopectin content by 10.5% and cold water solubility by 8.0% relative to the wild-type enzyme, while reducing rapidly digestible starch by 9.75%. This study establishes a workflow for engineering thermostable enzymes without crystallographic data. The resulting mutant shows promise for high-temperature starch modification in food processing applications.

title: Integrated sensory, volatilomic and metabolomic profiling reveals storage-stage-associated quality evolution of raw Pu-erh tea
abstract: During long-term storage, raw Pu-erh tea (RAPT) undergoes substantial sensory and chemical changes. However, the integrated contributions of sensory attributes and metabolites to this process are not well understood. This study applied an integrated multi-omics approach to examine its quality evolution across storage stages. Sensory evaluation indicated a notable shift in aroma profile, from initial floral and fruity notes to matured characteristics dominated by woody, stale, and herbal scents. Metabolomic analysis showed that during storage, total polyphenols (TPs), catechins, theanine, and free amino acids (FAA) decomposed, while total flavonoids accumulated. Additionally, 332 metabolites were identified as potential markers for distinguishing aging/aged RAPT. Eight key aroma markers of the aging process were identified using volatilomics, including 1,2-dimethoxybenzene, 1,2,3-trimethoxybenzene, linalool oxide-related isomers and cedrol. Collectively, this study advances our understanding of the chemical and sensory evolution of RAPT during storage and provides a foundation for optimizing storage strategies to control product quality.

title: Adsorption behavior study of polyphenols and flavonoids in Moringa oleifera Lam. On three macroporous resins
abstract: The adsorption behavior of polyphenols and flavonoids from Moringa oleifera Lam. on three macroporous resins (AB-8, D-101, and NKA-9) were investigated. The AB-8 macroporous resin exhibited the optimal adsorption performance for polyphenols and flavonoids. The adsorption behavior of polyphenols and flavonoids on AB-8 resin conforms to the pseudo-second-order kinetic (R 2 > 0.98) and Freundlich isothermal adsorption models. The AB-8 resin exhibits a typical S-shaped breakthrough curve for the target components. For polyphenols, the breakthrough point and saturation point are reached at an effluent volume of 40 mL and 130 mL with a dynamic adsorption capacity of 0.18 mg/g, respectively. For flavonoids, the breakthrough point and the saturation point occur at 43 mL and 110 mL with a dynamic adsorption capacity of 10.4 mg/g, respectively. This study establishes a theoretical foundation and technical support for the industrial purification and sustainable development of bioactive components in natural product resources from an energy conservation standpoint.

title: Wholegrain pasta: Influence of raw material and drying temperature on product quality
abstract: The present study investigated the effects of wholemeal semolina (WS) type and drying conditions on phenolic compounds, antioxidant activity, volatile profile, sensory attributes, and cooking behaviour of wholegrain pasta. Two WS samples differing in protein, lipid, fibre, and damaged starch content were utilised. Pasta was dried either at a maximum of 50 °C for 21 h or at 85 °C for 6 h. Both WS type and drying temperature affected the polyphenol profile, while antioxidant activity was only moderately influenced. Hexanal and 2-pentylfuran reflected WS lipid content; hexanal decreased and 2-pentylfuran increased at higher drying temperature. Furan compounds and furosine increased in pasta dried at 85 °C and were related to damaged starch content of WS. Caramel and toasted notes intensified with temperature. WS type significantly influenced cooking behaviour, and high-temperature drying slightly improved wholegrain pasta cooking quality.

title: A high performance covalent organic framework material assists metabolomics in the detection of mycotoxin infection in wheat
abstract: Wheat contamination by aflatoxin B 1 (AFB 1 ) poses a serious threat to food security and human health due to its potent carcinogenicity. However, conventional analytical methods are limited by complex sample pretreatment and post-contamination analysis, lacking early warning capability. Herein, we developed a highly crystalline hydroxyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF1) as an interference-free laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) substrate for metabolomics profiling and early monitoring for AFB 1 infection in wheat. Compared with traditional organic matrices and low-crystallinity COF (COF2), COF1 exhibited excellent auxiliary desorption/ionization performance and successfully acquired metabolic fingerprints of 120 wheat samples (60 AFB 1 -infected and 60 healthy controls) without complicated pretreatment, clearly revealing metabolic divergence between the two groups. Furthermore, 11 candidate biomarkers were screened by multivariate statistical analysis and their roles in the metabolic pathway responses under mycotoxin stress were preliminarily elucidated. This work offers a rapid and reliable strategy for early risk screening of mycotoxins in wheat.

title: Curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticle-stabilized pickering emulsions for co-delivery of resveratrol: Synergistic efficacy in strawberry preservation
abstract: Strawberries are nutrient-dense and economically vital fruits with extremely high perishability. They frequently suffer from postharvest losses and safety hazards due to their thin epidermis, active metabolism, and susceptibility to microbial infection. Conventional preservation strategies including refrigeration, chemical fungicides and polymer coatings suffer from chilling injury, health risks and high costs. Herein, we developed a novel Pickering emulsion stabilized by curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticles (Cur-SF NPs) for the co-delivery of resveratrol (Res) to synergistically enhance strawberry preservation. Formulated via a facile eco-friendly route, Cur-SF NPs serve as bifunctional stabilizers to enhance emulsion stability as well as solubility and stability of Res. Physicochemical characterization, antioxidant assays, and microbial tests verified the emulsion's favorable properties, revealing enhanced antioxidant activity and broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy against Aspergillus niger and Escherichia coli. Integrated into chitosan edible coating, the emulsion effectively reduced strawberry weight loss, maintained firmness and inhibited spoilage. This green, sustainable strategy presents a highly viable approach for the postharvest preservation of soft fruits.

title: Thermosonication enhances the antioxidant quality of tomato juice: Enzyme inactivation kinetics, targeted metabolomics of carotenoids and phenolic acids, and multivariate correlation analysis
abstract: Thermosonication (TS) enhances tomato juice antioxidant quality, yet its effects on enzyme activity and bioactive compounds remain unclear. This study compared TS (60 °C, 15 min) and traditional pasteurization (TP; 85 °C, 10 min) regarding color, enzyme inactivation kinetics, and bioactive profiles. Both first-order and Weibull models described enzyme inactivation, with Weibull giving higher R 2 , especially for POD under TP (0.982 vs. 0.891). Targeted metabolomics revealed significant increases in carotenoids (lycopene, +12.8%) and phenolic compounds (chlorogenic acid, +93.7%; rutin, +108.3%; syringic acid, +596.6%). TS better preserved ascorbic acid and color (ΔE = 1.79), with higher DPPH/ABTS activity in lipophilic and hydrophilic fractions. Correlation analysis suggested associations between enzyme activity and color, POD activity and phenolic oxidation, and phenolic acids/lycopene and antioxidant capacity. TS may improve antioxidant quality via oxidative enzyme inactivation, release of bound phenolics, improved extractability, and glycoside hydrolysis, offering a hypothesis-generating framework for high-bioactivity tomato juice production.

title: A dataset-calibrated multi-module model for evaluating plant oil similarity to human milk lipids: single oil ranking, blending optimization, and machine learning assisted cross-checking
abstract: Designing infant-formula lipids requires matching human milk across multiple lipid dimensions, but plant-oil screening lacks a unified objective method. We developed a model to assess similarity and optimize blends. Liposoluble bioactives, phospholipids, and triacylglycerol fatty acids of 20 plant oils were compared with lipid centroids of colostrum, transitional milk, and mature milk. Aitchison distances were converted to module similarities by quantile-logistic calibration and absolute-composition correction and integrated using jackknife-optimized weights. Corylus heterophylla Fisch. ex Trautv. ranked highest in colostrum, whereas Prunus dulcis (Mill.) D.A.Webb performed better in transitional and mature milk, with leading oils remaining stable across stages. Blend optimization showed Glycine max (L.) Merr. dominated phospholipid matching, while Prunus dulcis (Mill.) D.A.Webb, Idesia polycarpa Maxim., and Pistacia chinensis Bunge complemented fatty acid and integrated blends. Robustness analyses supported ranking stability, while PERMANOVA, SIMPER, and machine learning characterized compositional and methodological differences, supporting preliminary, dataset-specific feedstock screening.

title: Structure–function relationships of potato protein–gum arabic–β-cyclodextrin ternary complexes for emulsion stability and suppression of volatile release from Chinese giant salamander oil
abstract: This study investigated how three-component co-assembly of potato protein (PP), gum arabic (GA), and β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) affects complex organization and the performance of Chinese giant salamander oil (CGSO) emulsions. pH regulated PP charge, solubility, and aggregation, with pH 8 providing favorable conditions for PP-GA organization. At this pH, addition of 0.75% (w/v) β-CD altered the molecular environment and colloidal organization of the ternary system, while maintaining favorable emulsifying properties and enhancing thermal stability. Comparisons with controls showed that these effects could not be fully explained by β-CD presence or nonspecific carbohydrate addition. Electronic-nose analysis provided a descriptive characterization of formulation-dependent headspace sensor-response fingerprints, whereas HS-SPME-GC-MS showed lower relative headspace abundances of several aldehydes in the ternary emulsion. These findings link ternary co-assembly with emulsion functionality, while the lower headspace abundance of volatiles may reflect combined effects of lipid oxidation status, volatile partitioning and retention, and possible β-CD-volatile interactions.

title: Synergistic modification of wheat starch by freeze-thaw treatment and fucoidan: Insight into the gel properties, rheological behaviors, multiscale structure, and the application in hot-dry noodles
abstract: The synergistic effects of freeze-thaw treatment (FT) and fucoidan (FC) on the physicochemical and structural properties of wheat starch (WS), alongside its application in hot-dry noodles, were investigated.
