The combined treatment significantly reduced the gel hardness and viscoelastic moduli of WS. Additionally, peak viscosity and swelling power decreased, whereas water absorption capacity increased. Microscopic observations revealed distinct alterations in the surface morphology of starch granules. Furthermore, the structural ordering of the starch was disrupted, as evidenced by significant declines in short-range and long-range molecular order. Specifically, the relative crystallinity was reduced from 12.37% to 7.41%. Upon application in hot-dry noodles, synergistically modified starch significantly enhanced the textural properties, resulting in superior hardness and springiness. These results demonstrated that the synergistic application of FT and FC effectively modulated the multiscale structure and functional characteristics of WS, providing a practical basis for developing clean-label modified starches with enhanced thermal stability.

title: Allergenicity reduction of silkworm pupae allergen Bomb m 6 via ultrasound-assisted xylosylation: Structural disruption and epitope-masking effects
abstract: Silkworm pupae (Bombyx mori) are a promising sustainable protein, but their use is limited by potent allergens like Bomb m 6. This study developed an ultrasound-assisted xylosylation method to mitigate its allergenicity. Ultrasound-assisted xylosylation effectively altered the structure of Bomb m 6 and introduced 8 new glycation sites within known B-cell epitopes, suggesting a potential for epitope masking. These modifications reduced IgE-binding capacity by nearly 2-fold, which remained sustained even after simulated gastrointestinal digestion. In vivo, mice sensitized with ultrasound-xylosylated Bomb m 6 exhibited attenuated allergic symptoms, decreased histamine/MCP-1, suppressed Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-13), and elevated TGF-β1, alongside expanded activated splenic regulatory T cells (Tregs), indicating the induction of a tolerogenic immune environment. This work establishes ultrasound-assisted xylosylation as an effective strategy for protein ingredients with lower allergenic potential.

title: Non-contact smartphone-based colorimetric sensing platform using Si3N4 nanozyme-embedded kudzu starch hydrogel for on-site meat freshness monitoring
abstract: A non-contact colorimetric sensing platform was developed for on-site meat freshness assessment, integrating a Si 3 N 4 nanozyme-embedded kudzu starch composite hydrogel as the sensing element and a smartphone-assisted RGB system for signal readout. The Si 3 N 4 nanozyme with intrinsic peroxidase-mimicking activity catalyzes H 2 O 2 decomposition to produce hydroxyl radicals, which oxidize 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) into blue products. Nonanal, a characteristic volatile biomarker of meat spoilage, is proposed to reduce ox-TMB through a competitive redox process, giving rise to concentration-dependent color fading. The porous hydrogel enables nanozyme immobilization and gaseous nonanal enrichment, realizing label-free non-contact detection. Under optimized conditions, the platform shows two linear ranges of 0.001-0.1 and 0.1-0.35 mmol L -1 with a detection limit of 0.873 μmol/L, along with favorable selectivity and spiked recovery. Practical sample validation confirms its potential for real-time on-site meat freshness monitoring.

title: Deep chemometrics for retrospective auditing of the water-nutrient nexus in olive oil via 1D-CNN and explainable AI
abstract: Transitioning toward high-value functional food markets increases demand for forensic tools capable of verifying the "water-nutrient nexus", the complex agronomic interplay between irrigation and fertilization that shapes olive oil composition and authenticity. Conventional chemometrics often fail to capture synergistic, non-linear cultivation fingerprints within complex chemical matrices. This study introduces a "Deep Chemometrics" framework for retrospective auditing of olive oil history using FTIR spectroscopy and a customized one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). The framework was developed from 324 FTIR spectra representing nine irrigation × fertilization (W × F) regimes and incorporated physics-informed data augmentation to overcome limited sample availability. The optimized 1D-CNN achieved 97.89% validation accuracy (validation loss = 0.0548) and 83% accuracy on a held-out test set (macro-averaged precision = 0.85, recall = 0.83, F1-score = 0.83), representing a 25.8% improvement over the baseline model. Gradient-based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) consistently identified the ester carbonyl stretching vibration (1744 cm -1 ) and CH₂ asymmetric stretching vibration (2922 cm -1 ) as the principal spectral features driving classification. Representative constrained pseudo-Voigt peak deconvolution, together with non-parametric (Kruskal-Wallis) statistical analysis, confirmed significant treatment-dependent differences within these diagnostic bands (1744 cm -1 : p = 0.0076; 2922 cm -1 : p = 0.0025), providing independent spectroscopic validation of the CNN-derived feature importance. By integrating deep learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and spectroscopic validation, the proposed framework provides a transparent, scientifically interpretable, and robust strategy for retrospective authentication of olive oils according to their irrigation and fertilization history, thereby strengthening agricultural transparency and supporting supply-chain authenticity.

title: Measuring wine tannin through pigment subtraction by spectrophotometer
abstract: Red wine is a complex mixture containing thousands of compounds. Anthocyanins and proanthocyanidins (PAs) are among the most important contributors to red wine quality, influencing color, astringency, and long-term color stability. During winemaking and aging, PAs undergo structural modifications that produce wine tannins (WTs) and pigmented tannins (PTs). We demonstrate that the Malvidin-3-O-glucoside molar absorption coefficient (ε) is 4.6× that of (-)-epicatechin at 280 nm. Differences in the ε of WTs and PTs were accounted for by manipulating the Bouguer-Beer-Lambert law and correcting the measured 280 nm absorbance for the contribution of pigments. This correction was applied to 24 commercial red wines spanning a range of pigmentation levels. Highly pigmented wines exhibited greater spectral interference than less pigmented wines, leading to corrections in quantification as high as 19% and as low as 1.7%, respectively. This approach improves WT and PT quantification and advances our understanding of stable color development in red wine.

title: Enzymatic detoxification mechanisms of histamine in fish and fermented aquatic products: research progress and future development strategies
abstract: Histamine is a biogenic amine and a chemical food safety hazard in fish and fermented aquatic products. Prevention and enzymatic degradation are complementary strategies. This review compares the catalytic mechanisms of diamine oxidase, histamine dehydrogenase, multicopper oxidase and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, the latter as a moonlighting enzyme with limited histamine-degrading activity. Building on these mechanisms, we evaluate kinetic limitations from high salinity, low pH, and competing amines in fish and fermented aquatic products, including fish sauce and canned tuna homogenates, although final-product validation remains lacking. Food-grade immobilization and whole-cell biocatalysis are discussed as current or applied approaches, while AI-guided protein design and micro-/nanomotor systems remain at proof-of-concept or early-development stages. Despite progress in understanding histamine-degrading enzymes, application remains hindered by short enzymatic half-lives, process incompatibility, and inhibitor vulnerability. We propose a conceptual multi-hurdle framework centered on enzymatic degradation and complementary supply-chain measures, shifting seafood safety from reactive monitoring toward proactive control.

title: Flavor evolution of Antarctic Krill (Euphausia superba) during thermal processing: insights from GC-IMS, GC-O-MS, and RATA
abstract: Despite its high nutritional value, the application of Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba, AK) is hindered by complex off-odors. This study integrated electronic nose (E-nose), gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS), and headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-O-MS) with Rate-All-That-Apply (RATA) to map AK flavor evolution under various thermal treatments, including steaming (100 °C for 5 min), frying (220 °C for 5 min), and baking (180 °C for 1 min). Based on the screening criteria of relative odor activity values (ROAV >1), and GC-O detection frequency ≥ 3, 29 key aroma-active compounds were identified. While raw and steamed AK exhibited mild, lipid-derived profiles, frying exacerbated fishy odors due to a surge in lipid oxidation markers (e.g., hexanal, 1-octen-3-ol, and 1-penten-3-one). Conversely, baking optimized the balance of Maillard-lipid interaction profiles, generating sufficient pyrazine-mediated nutty and roasty notes while avoiding excessive lipid oxidation. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) modeling confirmed that baking achieved the highest consumer acceptability, correlated with fruity, meaty, and caramel attributes associated with markers such as trans-2-cis-6-nonadienal, 2-propylfuran, and 5-ethyl-2,3-dimethylpyrazine. These findings provide molecular-level insights for developing sensory-optimized krill products, facilitating the high-value utilization of AK resources.

title: Phytohormonal and metabolomic responses to Lysinibacillus sp. TT41 and lactic acid during drought stress in kimchi cabbage (Brassica rapa L. subsp. pekinensis)
abstract: Drought-stress severely disrupts plant metabolism and nutritional quality. We investigated the metabolic and hormonal mechanisms underlying drought tolerance in kimchi cabbage treated with Lysinibacillus capsici TT41 and its metabolite, lactic acid (LA). Comprehensive profiling revealed 84 metabolites and 9 hormones, distinguishing drought-stressed plants from surviving plants. Notably, 10 mM LA treatment effectively maintained metabolic homeostasis, resulting in profiles comparable to those of controls. This finding demonstrates that LA modulates the accumulation patterns of nitrogenous metabolites, thereby enhancing drought tolerance while preserving the crop's nutritional quality. A strong correlation between these metabolites and key stress hormones (abscisic acid, jasmonic acid, and salicylic acid) suggests that LA is closely associated with the coordinated modulation of an integrated metabolic-hormonal network that maintains chemical homeostasis. These findings highlight LA as a promising chemical elicitor for preserving the nutritional quality of cruciferous vegetables and provide a sustainable strategy to maintain food quality under environmental-stress.

title: Editorial Board
The threat of climate change to anthocyanin content in black wolfberry fruit
abstract: Climate associations with wild-fruit quality remain incompletely quantified. This study assessed climate-anthocyanin associations in black wolfberry (Lycium ruthenicum) and projected changes. Anthocyanins in 200 samples collected across seven regions in 2017 were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography and modeled using random forest. Regional differences were significant (P 2 = 0.84; mean temperature of the warmest quarter had the highest predictive importance (percentage increase in mean squared error, 44%). This pattern, high contents in Qaidam and Hexi but low contents in Turpan, persisted during 2005-2020. Under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 5-8.5, conditional projections indicated a 30% decline in the Qaidam Basin during 2081-2100. These findings suggest that warming may threaten black wolfberry quality and underscore the need for climate-adaptive cultivation strategies.

title: A time-dependent study of volatile compounds formation driven by mild heating and photooxidation in virgin olive oils, avocado oils and pure fatty acids
abstract: Studying incipient rancidity in oils, a stage where sensory recognition remains challenging, requires examining early volatile formation under moderate conditions. This study characterized early-stage volatile profile changes in virgin olive and avocado oils under mild heating and photooxidation and evaluated fatty acid standards as simplified reference systems. Headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS) was used to characterize and monitor the volatile compounds generated under mild heating and photooxidation incubation (17,000 lx and 35 °C). After 264 h, avocado oils generated higher amounts of volatile compounds than virgin olive oils, indicating lower oxidative stability. Similar volatile trends were observed in oils and fatty acid standards, although greater formation in standards reflected the absence of natural antioxidants. Six compounds -octane, (E)-2-heptenal, heptanal, butanal, formic acid, and hexanoic acid- increased at least threefold over time across all systems. Characterizing volatile formation under mild conditions may aid the identification of early oxidation markers.

title: Multi-omics analysis revealed oil accumulation and compositional remodeling in Rhodosporidium toruloides under nitrogen limitation
abstract: Microbial lipids from oleaginous yeasts are promising sustainable alternatives for biofuel and food applications. However, rational engineering requires a comprehensive understanding of both lipid yield and molecular composition, together with their regulatory basis. In this study, high-coverage lipidomics integrated with stage-resolved transcriptomics was applied to Rhodosporidium toruloides under nitrogen limitation. Lipidomic analysis revealed a two-phase pattern characterized by rapid triacylglycerol accumulation followed by compositional remodeling. During the accumulation window, fatty acid class distribution and derived oil parameters showed palm-oil-like compositional features, particularly in terms of saturation balance and unsaturation-related indices. Transcriptomic analysis linked these phenotypic changes to distinct regulatory modules associated with lipid assembly and turnover. These findings suggest that lipid quantity and composition are differently regulated and may be modulated through cultivation-stage control, providing a phenotypic and regulatory basis for rational engineering of microbial oils with defined functional profiles.

title: Reassessing the link between soluble solids and sugars in melon: FTIR models as an alternative tool
abstract: Soluble solids content (SSC, °Brix) is widely used to estimate melon sugar content. However, in a diverse set of Ibericus melons, it correlated moderately (R 2 ≈ 0.60) with total sugars and sucrose, and not with hexoses content or the hexose-to-sucrose ratio. Moreover, the sensitivity of SSC under high selection pressure for high sugar (10%-20%) remained low (55%-60%). In contrast, FTIR trial specific models predicted sucrose (s), hexoses (h), citric acid (not malic), total sugars, sucrose equivalents, and the h to s ratio with mean prediction R 2 ranging 0.73-0.88 and errors ranging 3.5-8.9%. A general model, performed similarly to the weakest specific one, strongly affected by low fructose levels, resulting in mean prediction R 2 of 0.63 (external validation). Externally validated specific models achieved prediction R 2 values of 0.79-0.94 (mean 0.84) and errors ranging 3.6-28.7% (mean 11%). FTIR represents a good alternative to SSC for high-throughput phenotyping.

title: Insight into the improving on physicochemical and functional properties of corn starch by dielectric barrier discharge low-temperature plasma
abstract: This study explored the influences of dielectric barrier discharge low-temperature plasma (DBD-LTP) operating at 40 kHz for 10 min with different power on corn starch structures, physicochemical and functional properties. Structural analyses showed that DBD-LTP treatment maintained the A-type crystal structure of starch. However, the treatment decreased molecular chain order, relative crystallinity, and gelatinization temperature. Regarding functional properties, the 75 W treatment increased cold-water solubility over 3-fold, improved water-holding capacity by 21.4%, and enhanced gel hardness to 965.95 g. It also improved transparency and DPPH radical scavenging ability. Moderate power treatment reduced rapidly digestible starch and increased resistant starch content. Overall, 75 W DBD-LTP effectively optimizes starch physicochemical and functional properties with well-preserved granular integrity, offering theoretical support for starch non-thermal modification.

title: Editorial Board
Fermentation-induced molecular remodeling in African indigenous tubers: cassava and cocoyam
abstract: Cassava and cocoyam are major dietary staples in sub-Saharan Africa, commonly processed by natural fermentation before consumption. Although fermentation reduces antinutritional compounds and improves food quality, its molecular effects remain poorly characterized. We used untargeted mass spectrometry-based metabolomics with a computational annotation pipeline to compare fermentation-induced molecular remodeling in the two tubers, which showed distinct responses. In cassava, 718 of 773 significant features (92.9%) were decreased, indicating a predominantly catabolic process. In cocoyam, the response was more balanced, with 385 of 1013 features (38.0%) enriched, including di- and tripeptides consistent with proteolytic processing. Class analysis, molecular networking, and pathway enrichment against reference microbial models revealed tuber-specific signatures: in cassava, purine metabolism was the most enriched pathway and fatty acids were the chemical class that decreased the most relative to its overall metabolome, whereas cocoyam showed stronger enrichment of amino acid pathways. Cyanogenic glycoside-related features were decreased, consistent with detoxification. Biotransformation prediction also suggested putative fermentation products absent from current databases, highlighting the under-characterized chemistry of these tubers.

title: Factors affecting the size, distribution, and number of fat globules in sheep milk
abstract: This study presents a detailed characterization of the native fat globule size, distribution, and number in 275 raw ovine milk samples, utilizing advanced laser diffraction particle size analysis. Milk samples were collected from two indigenous Italian sheep breeds (Comisana and Massese) originating from three farms in the Tuscany region. Statistical analysis was conducted using a linear mixed-effects model, followed by a parametric bootstrap approach. Parity was significant on all globule size traits, with a non-linear reduction in diameter as parity increased. Days in milk had a marginally negative effect on globule diameter and significant negative effect on number of globules normalized per unit mass of fat. Breed x Fat interaction was significant, with Comisana ewes exhibiting a sharp increase in globule number and a decrease in size with higher fat content. Increasing Mg levels correlated with smaller, more diverse globules. Elevated Cl levels were associated with larger globules, decreased specific surface area, and reduced globule number.

title: Development and validation of a rapid RP-HPLC-UV method for lactose quantification in milk and its application in lactose hydrolysis monitoring
abstract: The increasing prevalence of lactose intolerance necessitates reliable analytical methods for lactose detection and effective strategies for lactose reduction in dairy products. In this study, a reverse-phase HPLC-UV method was optimized and validated for the detection and quantification of lactose in milk. As lactose lacks a UV chromophore, samples were derivatized using para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and sodium cyanoborohydride, followed by ten-fold dilution with methanol: water (70:30) before injection onto an RP-C18 column. The method provided good chromatographic resolution, with retention times of 6.0, 6.9, and 9.1 min for lactose, glucose, and PABA, respectively. Excellent linearity was obtained (R 2 = 0.9952), with limits of detection and quantification of 0.002 M and 0.008 M, respectively, and precision below 2%. Application of the method revealed that lactase treatment reduced lactose concentration to below 1 g/100 g within 4 h, achieving low-lactose milk, whereas dahi culture and Kluyveromyces lactis showed slower lactose hydrolysis. The method demonstrated applicability for monitoring lactose reduction during hydrolysis and for analysis of low-lactose milk within the validated analytical range.

title: Fabrication of ultrasensitive ciprofloxacin electrochemical aptasensor based on AuNPs decorated MWCNTs@GO@CS film
abstract: A highly sensitive electrochemical aptasensor (BSA/Apt/MWCNTs@GO@CS/. AuNPs/SPCE) was fabricated for the efficient detection of ciprofloxacin (CIP). The complementary structural and physicochemical properties of MWCNTs and GO provide a conductive and functionalized platform for aptamer immobilization, while the excellent film-forming property of CS ensures stable and uniform deposition of the nanomaterials on the limited SPCE surface. The sensor displayed excellent linearity by the DPV method from 0.03 to 100.00 nM with a detection limit of 0.01 nmol/L. Spiked recovery tests in lake water and river water achieved 97.98-103.98% recovery with relative standard deviations below 10%, indicating acceptable precision. Moreover, results from chicken samples analyzed by the proposed sensor were consistent with HPLC-MS, with only 0.9% relative error, confirming the sensor's reliability and practical applicability for real-world CIP monitoring.

title: Effects of ultrasonic treatment on the quality of dough enriched with whole soybean pulp: insights from starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties
abstract: This study investigated the impact of ultrasonic treatment on the processing characteristics of dough containing 40% whole soybean pulp (WSP) by analyzing starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties. Results showed that ultrasonic treatment enhanced dough rheological properties and formed a stabilized starch-gluten network. It also disrupted starch granules, causing a decrease in molecular weight alongside increases in apparent amylose content and A-chain content of 16.07% and 17.60%, respectively. SAXS, XRD, and FTIR analyses revealed that ultrasonic treatment promoted the formation of V-type complexes and enhanced the structural order of starch molecules. Additionally, starch disintegration and recombination enhanced thermal stability, swelling capacity, and gelatinization properties. Correlation analysis and principal component analysis further confirmed a significant association between starch structural modifications and dough quality improvement. Overall, ultrasound offered an effective way to improve WSP dough quality by modulating starch multi-scale structure and physicochemical properties.

title: Astaxanthin-zein-polysaccharide nanoparticles via intelligent microfluidics: Ionic-type polysaccharides differentially regulate stability and intestinal sustained release
abstract: Astaxanthin (AST), a potent lipophilic antioxidant, suffers from poor water solubility, environmental instability and low bioavailability, severely restricting its application in functional foods. In this study, six AST-Zein-polysaccharide ternary nanoparticles were precisely fabricated via an advancedcomputer-integrated intelligently controlled microfluidic platform. Different from conventional thermal bulk methods, this non-thermal microfluidic technique achieves confined self-assembly and precise laminar mixing for efficient, reproducible fabrication of homogeneous nanoparticles. Six food-grade polysaccharides (gum arabic (GA), pectin, HPMC, chitosan, guar gum, and xanthan gum) were systematically compared, and AST-GA-NPs were screened as the optimal delivery system. These nanoparticles exhibited superior comprehensive performance with a small particle size (80.8 ± 2.6 nm), low PDI (0.116 ± 0.054), and excellent antioxidant activity (DPPH: 87.17 ± 1.13%; ABTS: 90.51 ± 1.76%), as well as good morphological regularity, hydrophilicity and stability under variable pH, salt and light conditions. Gastrointestinal simulation tests showed that the cumulative AST release rate of AST-GA-NPs reached 86.62 ± 0.39%, 7.94 times higher than that of free AST. Multispectral analysis verified that hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions drove the stable self-assembly of nanoparticles. The unique highly branched structure and anionic characteristic of GA further optimized the interfacial characteristics and structural stability of the ternary system. This study proves the great superiority of computer-integrated microfluidics in constructing high-performance bioactive delivery systems, providing a feasible strategy for improving the stability and intestinal bioavailability of AST in functional foods.

title: An NIR fluorescent probe for dynamic monitoring of β-lactoglobulin: from milk quality analysis to biological imaging
abstract: Dynamic monitoring of β-lactoglobulin (β-LG) stability plays a crucial role in evaluating dairy product quality and understanding its biological functions. While some fluorescent probes are capable of real-time β-LG monitoring, achieving reliable long-term detection requires a probe that possesses intrinsic stability and can overcome severe background interference and high light scattering in complex matrices. Herein, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probe, DDT, was specifically designed for the dynamic monitoring of β-LG. The probe exhibited high selectivity and sensitivity toward β-LG. Dual-mode quantification of β-LG in liquid milk was achieved using DDT via a fluorescence assay and a smartphone-based colorimetric platform. Furthermore, DDT enabled long-term monitoring of milk stability by accurately tracking β-LG degradation. Additionally, DDT served as a reliable tool for dynamically monitoring β-LG uptake and distribution in living cells and in vivo. DDT demonstrates significant potential as a versatile tool for food safety diagnostics and biological research.

title: Function-transitioning supercritical fluid extraction: a novel approach to improve tea quality
abstract: The tea industry constitutes a substantial segment of the food sector, making the continuous advancement and innovation of its processing technologies essential. A systematic methodology was developed, employing a Function-Transitioning Supercritical Fluid Extraction (FT-SFE) to improve tea quality. This approach enabled the creation of a controlled sample library, which was used to establish proof-of-concept predictive models that quantitatively correlate flavor composition with sensory quality. FT-SFE reduced bitter and astringent compounds-particularly total esterified catechins (TETCs), a major astringent-resulting in improved infusion taste while maintaining the physical integrity of the dry tea leaves. The PLS-DA model identified total catechins, total polyphenols (TPPs), TETCs, and (-)-epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) as the major chemical indicators of sensory quality. The by-products from the FT-SFE provided preliminary evidence of anti-inflammatory potential. This study developed a reproducible food processing approach whose application may affect resource utilization and provide potential economic benefits for tea production.

title: Integrated Mn-doped ZIF-67 derived hollow heterojunction sensors with enhanced electrocatalytic activity for sensitive detection of methyl parathion in fruits and vegetables
abstract: Methyl parathion (MP) is a highly toxic organophosphorus pesticide and poses a serious threat to food safety and public health. Herein, an integrated sensing platform combining hollow Mn-doped ZIF-67 with carboxylated carbon nanotubes to form a heterojunction (H-Mn/ZIF-67@COOH-CNTs) was successfully fabricated for sensitive recognition and ultrafast removal of MP. The constructed sensing platform demonstrated excellent analytical performance for MP under optimized conditions, featuring a broad linear range of 0.3-100 μM and a low detection limit of 0.024 μM. Furthermore, H-Mn/ZIF-67@COOH-CNTs achieved rapid removal of MP. The Langmuir fitting yielded a theoretical maximum adsorption capacity of 584.8 mg·g -1 , while a removal efficiency of 92.52% was achieved within 5 min. This research provides a reliable platform for the sensitive detection of MP in fruits and vegetables and its rapid removal from aqueous solutions, while offering novel insights for designing high-performance electrocatalysts in environmental monitoring and food safety testing.

title: Precise prediction of amino acid content and geographical origin tracing of lotus seeds based on multimodal data fusion and Bayesian optimization
abstract: This study established a three-tiered framework of feature characterization, information coupling and modeling mapping to correlate multi-source coupled information with the geographical origin and quality of lotus seeds. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features and amino acid profiles were acquired, and Bayesian optimization was adopted. Dual-modal (amino acid + NIRS; amino acid + GLCM) and tri-modal (amino acid + NIRS + GLCM) models were constructed. These multimodal combinations outperformed single-modal counterparts in most cases instead of universally, and Bagged Trees achieved the optimal overall performance balance. Key NIRS-GLCM features for amino acid prediction were screened via feature-target association visualization. For L-carnosine, γ-aminobutyric acid and phosphorylethanolamine, the amino acid-free NIRS-GLCM non-destructive model yielded R 2 p ≥ 0.92209. A MATLAB-based GUI integrating preprocessing, multi-model prediction and result analysis was built as a conceptual prototype to illustrate the workflow for quality assessment of lotus seeds and other foods.

title: Encapsulation of cinnamaldehyde into V-type starch derived from different sources: structural characteristics and emulsifying properties
abstract: This study establishes a clear structure-function relationship linking starch botanical origin-indica rice (IRS), japonica rice (JRS), quinoa (QS), lentil (LS), and pea (PS)-to the formation and emulsifying performance of V-type starch/cinnamaldehyde (CA) complexes. Structural features directly dictated the ability of V-type starch to encapsulate CA, with V-QS exhibiting the highest CA loading (38.86 mg/g) due to its large specific surface area, despite relatively low amylose content. CA incorporation further modulated particle hydrophobicity and interfacial activity, enhancing contact angles and reducing interfacial tension across all complexes. The resulting structure-driven interfacial behaviors led to distinct emulsifying performances among five V-type starch/CA complexes. V-IRS/CA and V-JRS/CA, characterized by smaller particle sizes and efficient interfacial adsorption, produced emulsions with the smallest droplets (4.67 μm and 6.90 μm) and highest emulsifying activity (14.61 m 2 /g -1 and 13.57 m 2 /g -1 ). In contrast, V-LS/CA and V-PS/CA generated larger droplets and weaker stabilization due to limited adsorption kinetics.

title: Integrating instrumental analysis and computational simulation to elucidate the effect of dual-enzyme hydrolysis combined with γ-glutamylation on the flavor characteristics of soybean meal
abstract: To improve soybean meal's flavor, this study explored the effect and mechanism of dual-enzyme hydrolysis combined with γ-glutamylation on the flavor characteristics of soybean meal. Sensory evaluation revealed dual-enzyme hydrolysis significantly enhanced umami, saltiness and sweetness, while γ-glutamylation further strengthened umami and kokumi sensations. Specifically, γ-glutamylation increased umami amino acid (18.23 mg/100 mL), reduced bitter amino acids (26.94 mg/100 mL). Meanwhile, it also elevated esters and heterocyclic compounds (P < 0.05). Correlation analysis showed umami/sweet amino acids were positively correlated with umami/kokumi (P < 0.05), with ethyl formate, 2,6- and 2,5-dimethylpyrazine as potential contributors Besides, γ-Glutamylation increased potential umami peptides by 16.70%, with 7-13 amino acid peptides dominating. Molecular docking identified key interaction modes (hydrogen bond, hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions) and residues (Asp216, Ser147, Ala302 for T1R1/T1R3; Asp215, Gln179, Ser147 for calcium-sensing receptor). This strategy effectively improves soybean meal's flavor, providing theoretical support for novel flavor base materials development.

title: Hydrophobic modified starch reinforced chitosan/lignosulfonate composite film for cherry tomatoes preservation
abstract: To address the environmental pollution caused by petroleum-based plastic packaging, the development of high-performance biodegradable films has become a key research focus in the field of food packaging. In this study, hydrophobically modified starch (AKDSC) was prepared via the esterification reaction of alkyl ketene dimer and subsequently introduced into a chitosan/sodium lignosulfonate (CH/SL) composite system, successfully constructing a multifunctional composite film (CH/SL-AKDSC). The structural characterization results indicated the formation of a denser hydrogen bond network between the phenolic hydroxyl/amino groups in CH/SL and the hydroxyl groups in AKDSC. The performance tests showed that the film exhibited a water contact angle of 105.9°, an oxygen transmission rate as low as 1.18 g/(m 2 ·d), and an ultraviolet shielding rate of over 99%. In a 10-day cherry tomato preservation experiment, the CH/SL-AKDSC film demonstrated good preservation effects, highlighting its practical application potential in green and efficient food packaging.

title: Decoding jujube aroma: Integrated extraction, advanced analytical strategies, formation mechanisms, influencing factors, and future perspectives
abstract: Jujube is a characteristic fruit of China with distinctive aroma and high nutritional value. This review summarizes advances in the extraction and analysis of free and glycosidically bound volatile organic compounds (VOCs), odor-active compounds, aroma formation mechanisms, and influencing factors. More than 300 VOCs have been identified, including esters, ketones, aldehydes, acids, and pyrazines. Esters, particularly ethyl decanoate, are important contributors to fruity aroma and are formed through alcohol and fatty acid metabolism, followed by acyl-CoA formation and alcohol acyltransferase (AAT)-catalyzed esterification. The lipoxygenase-hydroperoxide lyase-alcohol dehydrogenase pathway and β-oxidation also contribute to precursor supply. Multi-omics and enzymology facilitate the identification of key genes, enzymes, and pathways. Emerging approaches, including stable isotope tracing, molecular docking, machine learning, neuroimaging, and olfactory cell-based biosensors, offer new opportunities to elucidate aroma formation and perception and enable aroma prediction and quality control. This review provides insights into jujube aroma formation and quality improvement.

title: Pigment-associated metabolic signatures and processing stability in color-diverse carrot accessions: a chemometric and functional analysis
abstract: This study assessed compositional, antioxidant, and sensory variation in color-diverse carrot (Daucus carota L.) accessions (orange, yellow, purple) under different processing conditions. Significant accession and product effects (P < 0.05) were observed for sugars, phenolics, flavonoids, anthocyanins, β-carotene, and DPPH activity. Purple accessions contained higher phenolic and anthocyanin levels with higher antioxidant potential, while orange accessions showed higher β-carotene and sucrose contents. Yellow accessions exhibited a moderate compositional profile. Processing method influenced bioactive levels in a compound-dependent manner, with higher phenolic values observed in juice and relatively stable β-carotene levels across products. Multivariate analysis separated accessions based on variation in compositional and morphological traits. Sensory evaluation showed higher acceptability scores for orange carrot-derived products, while purple and yellow products showed moderate scores. This study provides a comparative assessment of compositional, processing, and sensory variation in color-diverse carrot accessions and derived products, supporting evaluation of their performance in different food matrices.

title: Ternary interactions of polyphenols, polysaccharides, and gluten proteins: molecular mechanisms and strategic regulation of flour-based product quality: a review
abstract: As a major staple, wheat supplies 18% of global dietary energy and 19% of protein. Wheat flour-based foods constitute complex matrices wherein gluten, starch, non-starch polysaccharides, polyphenols, and water undergo dynamic interactions during sequential processing. Integrating findings from binary and ternary systems, this comprehensive review identifies hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, water competition, macromolecular crowding, and covalent cross-linking as key driving mechanisms. Depending on formulation, these interactions govern gluten network development, starch transitions, and water mobility, thereby shaping product volume, texture, sensory quality, and glycemic response. Reversible association dominates mixing, thermal aggregation dictates baking, and moisture migration coupled with retrogradation governs storage stability. Overall, non-covalent, water-mediated effects predominate over the formation of distinct ternary complexes in intact dough. This review establishes a structure-processing-quality framework linking molecular-level interactions across sequential processing stages to the macroscopic quality and nutritional functionality of flour-based foods.

title: Positional-isomer composition of palm-kernel-stearin diacylglycerols regulates cooling-induced interfacial crystallization and whipping performance of partially crystalline emulsions
abstract: Interfacial crystallization influences both the stability and aeration of partially crystalline emulsions, yet its dependence on diacylglycerol (DAG) positional-isomer composition and cooling history remains unclear. We compared palm-kernel-stearin-based DAG systems with sn-1,3/sn-1,2 ratios of 9:1 and 2:1, alongside a triacylglycerol control. The DAG systems had comparable solid fat content but differed in cooling-dependent interfacial rheology, projected birefringent patterns, and crystal organization. The 9:1 formulation cooled at 10 °C min -1 reached a viscosity of 562.0 mPa·s and 14.2% partial coalescence after ten temperature cycles. In whipping tests, it achieved an overrun of 289.3%. Whipping emulsions after the 21-day distribution challenges yielded 250.0-270.1% overrun. Boundary-associated birefringence, increased interfacial elasticity, and preserved globule morphology support crystal-associated interfacial organization as a basis for this combination of stability and whippability. These findings establish a link between DAG isomer composition, cooling history, and emulsion functionality, providing a strategy for balancing distribution stability with subsequent aeration performance.

title: Aqueous radical modification of cellulose enables antioxidant Pickering emulsion coatings for fruit preservation
abstract: Postharvest fruit losses remain a major challenge, and many preservation coatings still rely on solvent-intensive processing or non-renewable additives. We report all-aqueous, ball-milling-assisted radical grafting of propyl gallate (PG) onto cellulose, producing nanofibrillar stabilizers for antioxidant Pickering coatings, avoiding organic solvents and multistep processing while integrating nanofibrillation, interfacial regulation, and antioxidant functionalization. The optimized C-PG achieves a three-phase contact angle of 87.5° and stabilizes soybean-oil emulsions with a mean droplet size of 6.41 μm and minimal growth over 30 days. Quercetin loading achieved high encapsulation efficiency (95.48%) and sustained radical-scavenging activity. As edible coatings, the emulsions delayed spoilage and mass loss in strawberries and fresh-cut apples; compared with untreated controls, QPE-C-PG6 delayed the 50% strawberry decay threshold from day 4 to 9, reduced microbial counts, preserved firmness, soluble solids, titratable acidity, and sensory quality. This fully biobased, solvent-free platform offers a scalable route to food-contact coatings for postharvest preservation.

title: Molecular interactions of fiber-rich banana blossom powder during the structuring of mung bean protein-based high-moisture meat analogs
abstract: Fiber-rich banana blossom powder (BBP; 63% dietary fiber) was evaluated as a structuring ingredient in mung bean protein (MBP)-based high-moisture meat analogs. Blends containing 0–10% BBP were characterized before twin-screw extrusion; extrudates were assessed for structure, texture, anisotropy, and spectroscopic changes. BBP increased water-holding capacity from 3.2 to 4.6 g water/g and median particle diameter (Dx50) from 38.5 to 61.3 μm, while bulk density decreased from 0.59 to 0.40 g/cm 3 . EM-7.5 showed the highest mechanical anisotropy, whereas hydration continued to increase at 10%, demonstrating endpoint-specific responses. Docking and 300 K molecular dynamics predicted persistent noncovalent associations between native MBP 8S globulin and cellulose-, hemicellulose-, and galactose-based motifs under simplified aqueous conditions. These simulations suggest a plausible interaction contribution but do not reproduce 140 °C extrusion or isolate dietary-fiber effects from other BBP constituents. These results support BBP as a formulation-dependent structuring ingredient, with the highest observed anisotropy at 7.5%.

title: Evolution of aroma profiles and key aroma compounds associated with pleasantness in Baihao Yinzhen during aging
abstract: This study investigates aroma evolution and pleasantness changes in Baihao Yinzhen (YZ) white tea during aging. Using sensory evaluation, GC-MS analysis, aroma reconstitution and omission experiments, and molecular simulations, this study found that fresh aroma decreased during aging, whereas aged and cocoa aromas intensified. Pleasantness was strongly correlated with fresh aroma (r = 0.83), peaking in the unaged control sample (YZ0) and declining to a minimum in the 6-year-aged sample (YZ6). Phenylethyl alcohol, phenylacetaldehyde, and citral were identified as potential aroma compounds associated with pleasantness, with phenylethyl alcohol showing the strongest contribution. Molecular simulations suggested that these compounds may interact with the ADORA2A receptor, with a predicted binding free energy of -77.73 kcal/mol, and that PHE168 may contribute to complex stability. These findings provide valuable insights into the relationship between aroma evolution and pleasantness and offer a reference for white tea quality evaluation, storage optimization, and product development.

title: Cocoa bean shell as a novel substrate for kombucha: fermentation dynamics and bioactive potential
abstract: Fermented beverages have gained attention as functional foods for valorizing agro-industrial by-products rich in bioactive compounds. Cocoa bean shell (CBS), a by-product of cocoa processing, is rich in phenolics and methylxanthines. However, its behavior as a substrate in kombucha and its contribution to bioactivity remain unclear. This study aimed to develop and monitor kombucha prepared from CBS infusions (0.5-5.0% w/v) and evaluate its bioactive properties. Fermentation with SCOBY at 25 ± 1 °C for 7 days was monitored by pH, titratable acidity, soluble solids, and total phenolic content (TPC). Phenolics and methylxanthines were quantified by HPLC, and antioxidant and antimicrobial activities were assessed. Fermentation decreased pH and soluble solids, and increased titratable acidity. TPC was governed by CBS concentration and remained stable. (+)-Catechin and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid predominated, while theobromine was the main methylxanthine. The beverages showed concentration-dependent antioxidant and antimicrobial activity, partially preserved after neutralization, indicating bioactivity beyond organic acids.

title: Design and fabrication of a preconcentration-free Mg-doped hydroxyapatite based electrochemical sensor for simultaneous determination of cadmium, lead, and mercury in seafood and plant-derived foods
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in certain food remains a major public health concern due to the persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity of cadmium, lead, and mercury. In this study, we report the design and fabrication of a preconcentration-free electrochemical sensor based on magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite (Mg-HAP) nanoparticles for the simultaneous determination of Cd 2+ , Pb 2+ , and Hg 2+ in food matrices using a non-stripping voltammetric approach. Mg-doped HAP ((Ca 9 Mg)(PO 4 ) 6 (OH) 2 ) nanoparticles were synthesized via microwave irradiation and characterized using powder XRD, XPS, and HRTEM. The Mg-HAP modified glassy carbon electrode exhibited wide linear ranges of 1-1770 μM (Cd 2+ ), 1-995 μM (Pb 2+ ), and 0.25-995 μM (Hg 2+ ), with corresponding lowest detection limits of 0.874 μM, 0.132 μM, and 0.257 μM, respectively. The fabricated sensor demonstrated good selectivity along with satisfactory repeatability and stability. The sensor was validated in seafood (trevally, mullet and crab) and plant-derived foods (turmeric, mushrooms, peanuts), confirming its suitability for food safety monitoring.

title: A green pH-shifted cottonseed protein-shellac complex for improved solubility and curcumin delivery
abstract: This study developed a pH-shifting assisted assembly strategy to construct soluble cottonseed protein isolate (CPI)-shellac complexes (CPS), achieving remarkable improvements in both protein functionality and nutraceutical delivery. First, a dramatic enhancement in solubility was accomplished: the CPS system reached a near-complete solubility of 94.5% at neutral pH, compared to only 6.8% for native CPI. Furthermore, the underlying solubilization mechanism was systematically deciphered through a multi-scale approach: physicochemical characterization confirmed effective shielding of hydrophobic regions by shellac; proteomics revealed a more homogeneous and stable protein state; and molecular dynamics simulations visually demonstrated that shellac molecules selectively patch key hydrophobic residues, thereby inhibiting aggregation. Notably, the CPS exhibited excellent performance as a curcumin delivery vehicle, achieving a high encapsulation efficiency (EE) of 75% and significantly improving the photothermal stability, cellular uptake, and anti-migration bioactivity of curcumin. This work provides a green, scalable, multi-scale strategy for developing high-performance nutraceutical carriers from plant proteins.

title: Simultaneous enantiomeric separation and analysis of dimpropyridaz and its two major metabolites in plant-origin foods by UHPLC-MS/MS
abstract: A rapid and efficient method using UHPLC-MS/MS for the simultaneous enantioselective determination of dimpropyridaz and its two major metabolites (M550I002 and M550I006) in plant-origin foods has been established. Successful simultaneous enantioseparation of six enantiomers was obtained within 12 min on a chiral MZ(2)-RH column. A sample preparation procedure based on reversed-dispersive solid phase extraction with multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) was established. Good linearity (r ≥ 0.997) is achievable in the range of 0.5-100 μg/L for all the analytes. The limit of detection (LOD) ranged from 0.07 to 0.48 μg/kg, and the limit of quantitation (LOQ) was established at 5 μg/kg for all six enantiomers across all matrices. At spiked levels of 5, 50, and 500 μg/kg, mean recovery rates across different matrices ranged from 74.4% to 95.3%, with relative standard deviations (RSDs) below 6.4%. This validated approach provides an efficient strategy for monitoring enantiomeric residues of dimpropyridaz in cereals, vegetables, and fruits.

title: Reduction in bovine milk fat globule size is characterized by remodeling of membrane-associated lipids in milk
abstract: Milk fat globule (MFG) size is closely linked to milk lipid interfacial organization, but its association with membrane-associated lipid remodeling remains unclear. Here, milk composition, MFG size distribution, fatty acid profiles, and whole-milk lipidomics were analyzed in conjugated linoleic acid (CLA)-supplemented cows. CLA supplementation reduced milk fat content and shifted MFGs toward smaller sizes. Whole-milk lipidomics showed that the small-MFG phenotype was accompanied by remodeling of membrane-associated lipid classes, particularly sphingolipids. Among major sphingolipids, hexosylceramides (HexCer) showed the most consistent associations with MFG structural traits and were characterized by increased lower-carbon molecular groups and reduced abundance-weighted carbon number and double bond number. These findings identify HexCer as a prominent sphingolipid structural marker associated with MFG size reduction.

title: Bioinspired chitosan-xanthan gum self-assembled nanosponge incorporating natural deep eutectic solvent: batch adsorption, mechanism, sustainability, and selective non-nutritive sweetener elimination
abstract: A bio-inspired self-assembled nanosponge, constructed from a binary chitosan-xanthan gum (CX) gelling network incorporating a [betaine]:[tannic acid] natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES), is introduced as an innovative platform for the selective tracing of emerging non-nutritive sweeteners (NNSs) in waters and non-alcoholic beverages, due to their growing environmental relevance. The molar ratio of NADES precursors, CS-to-XG weight proportion, and NADES fraction within the CX network were optimized. Physicochemical characterization corroborated that the nanosponge possesses a porous, channel-like configuration, with outstanding aqueous stability and controlled swelling while preserving structural resilience. An adsorption capacity of 103.492-117.281 mg g -1 was achieved via synergistic electrostatic, hydrogen-bonding, and π-π interactions, ascribable to multiple crosslinking and high density of accessible active sites. The nanosponge was implemented in a one-step micro-solid-phase extraction (μ-SPE) method, affording selectivity (α, 102.50-554.00), LOQ (0.05-0.07 μg L -1 ), precision (RSD, 2.09-3.84%), and recoveries (RR, 93.82-107.16%), with minimal matrix effect (ME, 2.29-4.02%) and desirable re-usability ( five cycles). The BAGI (75/100), AGREE (0.74/1.0), and AES (81/100) tools validated the practicality and sustainability of the procedure.

title: Lactic acid bacteria fermentation of Undaria pinnatifida: microbial dominance, metabolic remodeling, and quality formation
abstract: Undaria pinnatifida, a representative brown macroalga, has limited high-value food applications due to its dense cell wall structure, pronounced marine odor, and inefficient conventional processing. In this study, we established a controlled fermentation strategy using different lactic acid bacterial (LAB) starters with Undaria pinnatifida slurry as the substrate. Kimchi starter fermentation was characterized by a predominance of Lactiplantibacillus, whereas milk starter fermentation showed a predominance of Streptococcus. The distinct LAB community profiles were associated with differential patterns of carbohydrate metabolism, amino acid turnover, and lipid-related metabolism, together with changes in flavor profiles and textural properties of fermented Undaria pinnatifida slurry. These findings indicate that starter-dependent microbial community composition was associated with distinct metabolic and quality profiles during fermentation. This study characterizes LAB-associated metabolic patterns and their relationships with quality attributes, providing a basis for the controlled bioprocessing and high-value utilization of brown macroalgae.

title: The sodium hyaluronate/sodium caseinate complex improves the emulsifying stability of EPA algae oil by forming an interface network
abstract: Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)-rich algal oil is widely used in functional dairy products due to its favorable functional properties. However, its limited restricts broader application in the food industry. In this work, sodium hyaluronate (SH) was combined with sodium caseinate (SC) to form an aqueous network as an emulsifier for EPA. The binding mechanism between SC and SH was investigated via fluorescence spectroscopy and thermodynamic analysis, revealing that van der Waals forces and hydrogen bonds dominate the SC-SH interaction. When used as an emulsifier, the SC/SH complex effectively encapsulated EPA-rich algal oil. The resulting emulsions exhibited significantly enhanced stability against environmental stresses-including storage, ionic, and oxidative stresses-with more uniform droplet size distribution. The SC/SH complex thus demonstrates potential as a stabilizer for functional lipid-delivery systems.

title: Dual-mode electrochemical and colorimetric detection of propyl gallate in food samples using a tungsten carbide anchored rGO aerogel nanocomposite modified SPCE
abstract: The wide-ranging use of artificial antioxidants in processed foods has generated growing concerns about food safety and quality assurance. Propyl gallate (PGT) is frequently utilized as an additive to prevent lipid oxidation and prolong the shelf life of food items; yet, excessive consumption may pose health hazards. Consequently, the advancement of quick and sensitive analytical techniques for the detection of PGT in food matrices is important. This study constructed a highly sensitive electrochemical sensor and colorimetric detection utilizing a tungsten carbide/reduced graphene oxide aerogel nanosheet (WCs/rGOANs) nanocomposite-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) for the detection of PGT. The WCs/rGOANs nanocomposite was prepared via a solvothermal method, followed by composite integration, resulting in a conducting and catalytically efficient electrode interface. The physicochemical characterization validated the effective synthesis of the hybrid nanocomposite, while electrochemical analyses revealed improved electron transport characteristics and significant electrocatalytic activity for PGT oxidation. Under optimal conditions, the sensor demonstrated an extensive linear detection range of 0.039 μM to 1490.264 μM, while the linear range of colorimetric sensing was about 0.99 μM to 356.65 μM with a low detection limit of 2.4 nM, a limit of quantification of 0.008 μM, and a sensitivity of 35.48 μA μM -1 cm - 2 for electrochemical sensing, and the LOD obtained for the colorimetric analysis was 0.0173 μM. The superior analytical performance is due to the synergistic interaction between WCs and rGOANs framework, which offers several active sites and enhances efficient charge transfer. Moreover, the developed sensor exhibited excellent selectivity, stability, and reproducibility, and was effectively utilized for the quantification of PGT in real food samples, including edible oils, noodles, and cookies. The nanocomposite facilitated dual-mode electrochemical and colorimetric sensing, providing a dependable platform for the assessment of antioxidant compounds in food matrices.

title: High-pressure homogenization for food protein modification: Structural mechanisms, functional regulation, and combined processing strategies
abstract: High-pressure homogenization (HPH) is a promising non-thermal technology for modulating food protein structure and techno-functional properties, including solubility, emulsifying activity and foaming capacity in food-processing systems. During HPH, protein dispersions pass through narrow valves or microchannels, where shear, turbulence, cavitation and localized heating collectively disrupt aggregates, reduce particle size, expose hydrophobic/sulfhydryl groups and rearrange protein structures, enhancing solubility, emulsification, foaming and interfacial performance. However, HPH-induced modification is non-linear. Moderate treatments drive deaggregation and partial unfolding, while excessive pressure or repeated cycles trigger hydrophobic association, reaggregation and functional decline. This review summarizes recent advances in HPH modification of food proteins, focusing on processing-structure-function relationships. Combined strategies coupling HPH with heating, ultrasonication, enzymatic hydrolysis, glycation or protein-polyphenol conjugation are discussed to overcome limitations of single HPH treatment. Finally, challenges regarding mechanism elucidation, process standardization, complex matrices, equipment clogging and industrial scale-up are evaluated, providing a process-structure-function perspective for developing high-functionality protein ingredients.

title: Development of lignocellulosic hydroxyethyl cellulose composite films for fruit antimicrobial packaging
abstract: The nonbiodegradability of conventional petroleum-based packaging materials and associated health concerns have increased interest in developing more environmentally friendly alternatives for food preservation. As a renewable candidate, cellulose lacks intrinsic antimicrobial capacity, and cotton-based hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) suffers high production costs. Herein, lignocellulose-based hydroxyethyl cellulose (Lig-HEC) was fabricated and formulated into composite films. The obtained film delivered 6.1 MPa tensile strength and 6.19 × 10 -10 g m -1 s -1 Pa -1 water vapor permeability, together with pronounced inhibitory activity against Penicillium oxalicum. Moreover, two flexible application strategies, tape casting and liquid dip-coating, were adopted for different berry fruits. The composite film mitigated weight loss and mold growth of cherries/strawberries, achieving a 29.3%-46.9% reduction in fruit weight loss relative to the untreated control, outperforming commercial polyethylene films. The results indicate that Lig-HEC can be used to develop high-performance and cost-effective antimicrobial packaging materials for food preservation.

title: Beyond the red carolina reaper: capsaicinoid variability across colour morphs revealed by HPLC-validated SWV deconvolution
abstract: Strongly overlapping voltammetric signals limit the individual determination of capsaicin (CAP) and dihydrocapsaicin (DHC) in pepper extracts. This study evaluated square-wave voltammetry (SWV) combined with Lorentzian signal deconvolution using HPLC as a reference method. Eleven commercially available Carolina Reaper-derived colour morphs were represented by one pooled sample each. Reliable deconvolution was achieved for nine samples, with the resulting individual CAP and DHC contents showing good agreement with HPLC measurements. Separately, total CAP and DHC contents determined by SWV and HPLC were strongly correlated (R 2 = 0.992). Among the analysed samples representing different colour morphs, Stinger and Rustic had the highest combined CAP and DHC contents, whereas Cream, Olive, Mustard, and Yellow had lower levels. These findings support the feasibility of the deconvolution approach for the successfully resolved extracts and provide an exploratory chemical comparison of the sampled commercial morphs.

title: Harnessing silk proteins for advanced food preservation: a review of materials, mechanisms, and multifunctionality
abstract: Silk proteins are natural protein biomaterials with broad application prospects in food preservation. Although recent studies have explored silk protein applications in food preservation, a systematic review of preparation strategies, functional mechanisms, and suitability for different food types is lacking. In this review, the structural characteristics, extraction methods, functional properties, and modification strategies of silk proteins are outlined, and various materials developed using silk proteins are introduced. Furthermore, the key strategies for using silk protein-based materials in food preservation and their effects on food systems are highlighted. Despite their promising benefits in food preservation, the large-scale application of silk proteins is limited by high extraction costs and incomplete safety evaluations. Future research should involve green extraction process development, smart responsive system construction, and life cycle assessments to provide new pathways for sustainable food packaging systems.

title: High-voltage prick alternating electric field maintained the freshness of Litopenaeus vannamei during partial freezing storage via inhibiting spoilage bacterial growth and modulating lipid metabolism
abstract: This study applied 3 kV high-voltage prick alternating electric field (HPAEF) to assist partial freezing storage of Litopenaeus vannamei. The potential mechanism was systematically explored by integrating microbial inhibition analysis and lipidomics. Compared with the control group, HPAEF reduced melanosis degree, the total viable count by 0.33 log CFU/g, the count of Pseudomonas spp. by 0.41 log CFU/g, and thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances by 24.71%. The growth of Pseudomonas fluorescens was inhibited through promoting intracellular content leakage and decreasing alkaline phosphatase activity. Lipidomics analysis indicated that HPAEF exerted significant regulatory effects primarily on glycerophospholipid metabolism, manifested as elevated phosphatidylcholine (18,1/22:1) level and reduced lysophosphatidylcholine level. Moreover, HPAEF effectively retarded lipid oxidation by reducing the activities of lipoxygenase and peroxidase. This study confirmed that HPAEF could retard phospholipid degradation by inhibiting the proliferation of Pseudomonas, and further mitigate lipid oxidation via inactivating lipoxygenase, thereby efficaciously maintaining the freshness of partially frozen shrimp.

title: Evaluation of the effect of catechin on the Maillard reaction based on model systems: a chemical insight
abstract: The Maillard reaction (MR) strongly affects food quality and sensory properties by generating desirable and undesirable products. Herein, catechin reactivity toward reducing sugars and amino acids was systematically investigated under conditions mimicking thermal food processing to assess its impact on early-stage MR. Catechin effectively reduced browning and suppressed furosine-associated signal formation through the formation of covalent catechin-sugar adducts identified by LC-UV-MS and NMR analysis. Antioxidant capacity of the reaction mixtures exceeded the theoretical value calculated based on the amount of residual catechin, indicating a contribution from catechin-derived products. Reduced browning and enhanced antioxidant properties were observed even in complex food systems (e.g., milk, egg white, flour) when catechin was present. Similar effects were observed using polyphenol-rich apple samples in place of catechin. Overall, these results highlight the dual role of natural polyphenols in modulating MR progression and enhancing antioxidant properties in food systems.

title: Dual-signal fluorescent–colorimetric aptasensor for tobramycin detection in milk based on fluorescent magnetic nanoparticles and AuNPs
abstract: Tobramycin (TOB) is an aminoglycoside antibiotic employed in human and veterinary medicine whose residues in food raise safety concerns. To resolve this issue, we developed a dual-mode aptamer-based sensor for sensitive TOB detection via fluorescence and colorimetric signals. The platform utilizes fluorescent magnetic nanoparticles (FMNs) conjugated with anti-TOB aptamers and gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). In the absence of TOB, AuNPs associate with FMN-Apt, causing fluorescence quenching. Upon TOB binding, aptamer-target recognition interrupts the complex, restoring fluorescence. Concurrently, magnetic separation and enhancer treatment reduces matrix interference and promotes AuNPs growth, causing a color change from red to blue-gray. The fluorescent and colorimetric modes attained detection limits of 1.03 nM and 2.45 nM, respectively, exhibiting enhanced sensitivity relative to previously documented techniques. The sensor was validated using TOB-spiked milk varieties and human serum without pretreatment, with recoveries of 94.05-106.42%, highlighting its potential for practical preliminary TOB monitoring in food safety and clinical applications.

title: Rapid fluorimetric determination of glyphosate in beer and fruit juices using a chitosan-coated magnetic–fluorescent molecularly imprinted sensor
abstract: Glyphosate is the most widely used herbicide in the world and is frequently detected in food. Magnetic and fluorescent molecularly imprinted polymers (MFMIP) were developed for rapid, selective GLY detection in food matrices. Two systems, MFMIP and chitosan-coated MFMIP-CS, were synthesised and characterised by FTIR, thermogravimetry, zeta potential, N₂ adsorption–desorption isotherms, and electron microscopy. Chitosan coating was introduced to mitigate matrix effects and surface fouling, enabling reliable fluorescence readout directly in complex beverages. The MFMIP-CS sensor showed matrix-specific nominal interaction times of 1 min for beer, 2 min for strawberry juice, 3 min for orange juice, and 4 min for grape juice; detection limits of 0.0016–0.0066 mg L −1 ; linearity between 0.005 and 0.50 mg L −1 ; recoveries of 86.96%–106.90%; and intraday precision ≤5.74%. GLY residues were found in beer, grape, and strawberry juices. The proposed method combines sensitivity, speed, and environmental sustainability, offering a promising alternative for routine glyphosate monitoring in food samples.

title: Pickering emulsions stabilized by zein and polysaccharide composite nanoparticles and their application in food preservation
abstract: In response to the demand for natural, safe, and sustainable food preservation, zein-polysaccharide Pickering emulsions have attracted increasing attention for their biocompatibility, interfacial stability, and bioactive loading capacity. This review examines polysaccharides with different charge properties, zein-polysaccharide binding mechanisms, preparation methods, emulsion fabrication, stabilization mechanisms, and food-preservation applications. The available evidence indicates that polysaccharide structure and charge, zein-polysaccharide interactions, and processing conditions collectively determine the interfacial architecture and physicochemical stability of the resulting emulsions, thereby affecting their bioactive loading, protection, and preservation performance. Tailoring polysaccharide characteristics and processing strategies therefore provides opportunities to regulate emulsion properties for specific food-preservation applications. A key innovation of these systems is the integration of interfacial stabilization with bioactive protection and delivery, providing a multifunctional platform for food preservation.

title: Effect of interface structures on myofibrillar protein-trehalose based emulsion delivery systems: Stability and β-carotene bioaccessibility
abstract: Four emulsion carriers with different interface structures based on myofibrillar protein-trehalose (MP-Tre) complexes: single-layer emulsions (SE, monolayer emulsifier adsorption), layer-by-layer emulsions (LBL-E, double interface via electrostatic and hydrogen bonding), double network emulsion gel (DNEG, double cross-linked gel network) and high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs, stacked structure by droplets accretion), were constructed to explore the effect of interface structure on emulsion stability and β-carotene bioaccessibility. HIPEs and DNEG exhibited superior storage and thermal stability due to dense networks, while SE was the least stable. These stability differences led to the worst protection of SE on β-carotene, whereas HIPEs loaded and retained the most β-carotene. Moreover, HIPEs effectively resisted digestive enzymes, delayed lipid digestion, and yielded the highest β-carotene bioaccessibility, implying the protection and controlled release of β-carotene. Release kinetics illustrated diffusion-dominated Fickian I release in SE, whereas non-Fickian release controlled by both diffusion and erosion in the rest emulsions. This study offers innovative strategies for lipophilic bioactives delivery by regulating emulsion interfacial structures.

title: Quercetin in Foods: Sources, Bioavailability, and nanoencapsulation Strategies
abstract: Bioactive compounds are naturally occurring food constituents with recognized antioxidant properties and potential health benefits. Among these compounds, quercetin, a flavonoid widely distributed in fruits and vegetables, stands out. However, its practical use is limited by low bioavailability, influenced by its chemical structure, physicochemical properties, and food matrix interactions. The objective of this study was to evaluate extraction technologies, bioavailability limitations, and nanoencapsulation strategies associated with quercetin. To identify gaps, an analysis of peer-reviewed articles published between 2015 and 2025 was conducted across major scientific databases (such as Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed). A total of 962 records were identified, of which 186 underwent full-text assessment and 29 met the inclusion criteria for the final review. The results showed that extraction efficiency depends on the plant matrix, solvent, and extraction technology. Compared with non-encapsulated quercetin, nanoencapsulation generally improved stability, solubility, controlled release, and bioaccessibility. However, only a few studies have incorporated nanoencapsulated quercetin into food systems, and among those, only a limited number have evaluated sensory acceptance and industrial applicability. Therefore, despite promising technological advances, additional studies addressing food applications, large-scale production, safety, and in vivo validation are essential for the successful implementation of quercetin-based delivery systems in the food industry.

title: Balancing aroma development and chemical safety in smoked chicken breast: Effects of smoking duration on aroma compounds, hazardous compounds, and precursors
abstract: This study investigated how smoking duration (0-12 h) shaped aroma development and hazardous-compound accumulation in smoked chicken breast. Fifty-seven volatile compounds were identified. Smoke-derived phenols dominated early, whereas several Maillard-derived pyrazines appeared mainly after 6 h and lipid oxidation-related aldehydes declined. Hazardous compounds followed different accumulation patterns. The advanced glycation end products N ε -carboxymethyllysine (CML) and N ε -carboxyethyllysine (CEL) increased markedly during late-stage smoking. Norharman showed the greatest increase among the detected heterocyclic amines (HAs), whereas the four priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH4) accumulated rapidly and exceeded the European Union maximum level from 2 h onward. Changes in reducing sugars, amino acids, creatine/creatinine, and free fatty acids were consistent with ongoing Maillard, HA-forming, and lipid-related reactions. Thus, characteristic aroma development did not coincide with a single low-hazard stage, highlighting the need to control smoke exposure, particularly to limit early PAH4 accumulation.

title: Mechanisms of low-temperature acclimation in alleviating muscle quality deterioration during the cold-chain transport of live Asian swamp eel (Monopterus albus)
abstract: An integrated molecular biology and metabolomics approach was employed to investigate the effects of low-temperature acclimation, including linear cooling (LC) and gradient cooling (GC), on muscle quality, energy metabolism, and apoptosis in Asian swamp eel during transport. Low-temperature acclimation markedly improved muscle quality, with GC exhibiting superior protective effects, as evidenced by enhanced chewiness, increased IMP content, reduced lactic acid levels, and improved whiteness, water-holding capacity and muscle microstructure. These improvements were accompanied by changes in biochemical indicators, including cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose, lactate dehydrogenase, hexokinase, and pyruvate kinase. Furthermore, low-temperature acclimation may involve AMPK/SIRT3/PGC-1α-mediated energy metabolism and PI3K/AKT-related apoptotic responses. Metabolomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of purine, amino acid, and glycerolipid metabolism pathways, suggesting their potential contribution to energy homeostasis and muscle quality preservation under cold conditions. These findings suggest that AMPK and PI3K/AKT pathways may regulate muscle quality under low-temperature conditions, providing insights for optimizing cold-chain transport strategies.

title: High resolution NMR and mass spectrometry to evaluate the metabolome of novel strawberry advanced breeding selections and correlate it with the fruit quality
abstract: The adverse climatic conditions are causing increasing concern across the Mediterranean region, driving strawberry producers toward alternative and effective strategies, including the selection of new and resistant cultivars. In this work, three new strawberry selections, derived from intraspecific crossings, were compared with five commercial cultivars. The aim was to characterize these cultivars by using both traditional methods (pH, TA, DW, TPC, TAC, vitamin C and TEAC) and advanced analytical techniques, including high resolution liquid-state NMR and Mass Spectrometry (FT-ICR and LC-MS/MS). The latter techniques, associated to chemometrics, enabled the identification of a unique molecular profile for each cultivar, in terms of primary and secondary metaboloma. Moreover, an innovative NMR-based method was proposed to appreciate the strawberry freshness. Concluding, the new selection AN 165354 resulted as excellent alternative to the commercial strawberries under greenhouse, exhibiting high nutritional and nutraceutical quality (48 and 163.2 mg/100 g FW for Vitamin C and total phenols, respectively) and an enhanced resistance to the degradation when stored at 4 °C (S/F ratio lower than 67% 7 days after the harvest).

title: Quantitative prediction of freshness of fish muscle tissue by machine learning coupled with MALDI-TOF MS
abstract: This study developed a prediction model for freshness analysis of fish muscle tissue based on MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry (MS) combined with machine learning (ML) algorithms. Dorsal muscle samples of large yellow croaker (Larimichthys crocea) stored at 4 °C for different periods were analyzed as models. The sensory quality of the samples was evaluated at 0, 1, 3, 5, and 7 days of storage using a 10-point scale. Sensory evaluation results show that the overall acceptability scores decreased from 9.8 at day 0 to 3.3 at day 7 during refrigerated storage, falling below the acceptance threshold (5.0) between day 3 and 5. The mass spectral data of protein extracts of dorsal fish muscle samples were obtained by MALDI-TOF MS. Six ML models were constructed based on 315 mass spectra, and compared. The XGBoost model shows the superior performance for predicting the freshness of large yellow croaker fish dorsal muscle tissue, with a coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.978, and residual predictive deviation (RPD) of 6.742. An 8:2 train/test split of mass spectral data is appropriate for constructing the models. The impact of data partitioning on the models' performance was evaluated using a leave-one-fish-out cross-validation (LOFO). XGBoost remains the optimal performing model (R 2 = 0.905 ± 0.074) under LOFO. A model performance ranking keeps consistent with that under the 8:2 split. SHAP analysis, combined with tryptic digestion and peptide mass fingerprinting searching, identified four proteins that can serve as potential biomarkers for monitoring freshness change during storage of the analyzed fish muscle tissue. During the single-blind validation using commercial samples, 29 predictions among the 30 analyzed samples remain within the model's error tolerance of 0.5 d, with an overall prediction accuracy of 96.67% (n = 30). It provides a valuable methodological reference for the laboratory-based quality assessment of aquatic products.

title: Characterization of covalent conjugation between rosmarinic acid and soybean proteins with different 7S/11S globulin ratios and its impact on conjugate structure and functionality
abstract: Polyphenol-driven protein modification is an effective strategy for developing functional food materials. This study investigated rosmarinic acid (RA) conjugation with soybean proteins differing in 7S/11S globulin ratios and evaluated the resulting structural, functional, and digestive changes. SP-80 and SP-96 showed the highest apparent RA-binding levels, whereas SP-115 did not increase further despite having the highest 7S/11S ratio. RA conjugation induced fraction-dependent structural reorganization, enhanced antioxidant activity and emulsifying properties across all samples, and produced distinct rheological responses among protein fractions. In vitro digestion showed that RA conjugation increased the apparent gastric digestibility of SP-22 by 24.65% and altered apparent intestinal digestibility in a sample-dependent manner. Peptidomic analysis further revealed a shift toward shorter soluble peptides in most RA-conjugated samples, accompanied by a shift toward greater local hydrophobicity around cleavage sites. These findings provide a composition-informed basis for developing RA-modified soybean protein ingredients with tunable structural, functional, and digestive characteristics.

title: A review on recent advancement in lactulose: From synthesis to application
abstract: Lactulose is a nondigestible disaccharide widely used in functional foods and pharmaceuticals. This review links advances in lactulose production with purification requirements and applications. Alkaline isomerization remains the most mature chemical route, while complexation and electrochemical methods modify product equilibria or regulate reaction conditions. Enzymatic routes involve transgalactosylation or cellobiose 2-epimerase-catalyzed lactose isomerization, with distinct substrate requirements and product profiles. These differences guide enzyme engineering and immobilization to improve selectivity, stability, and catalyst reuse. Reaction mixture composition also determines the roles of membrane separation, ion exchange, decolorization, and crystallization in product recovery. Product composition and quality subsequently influence pharmaceutical and food applications, discussed alongside physiological effects, matrix interactions, and processing and storage behavior.
