This process-wide perspective integrates catalyst and reactor development with purification and application-specific requirements, using productivity, catalyst lifetime, resource consumption, waste generation, and lactulose recovery to evaluate industrial feasibility and guide scale-up.

title: Exploring the functionality of chickpea flour fermented by lactic acid bacteria: a multidisciplinary approach for ingredient development
abstract: The use of chickpea flour as a substitute for animal-derived products is a well-established choice, offering advantages in terms of environmental sustainability and nutritional benefits, but presenting certain limitations related to sensory aspects and allergenicity. This study explores the potential of fermentation to overcome these limitations by fermenting a chickpea-based batter with different lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains: Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. lactis, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, Lacticaseibacillus casei, and Leuconostoc spp. A holistic research approach allowed the assessment of significant changes in physical and chemical parameters: rheological behavior, water-holding capacity (WHC), protein structure, volatile compound composition, functional properties such as allergenicity, antioxidant capacity, (poly)phenolic profile, and biopreservative effects. All strains enhanced batter structure, with different dynamics. Protein content remained stable, while allergenicity was moderately reduced. Fermentation led to increase total phenolic content and antioxidant capacity, and modified the (poly)phenolic and volatile profiles in a strain-dependent manner. Additionally, a biopreservative effect was observed.

title: Rational construction of an electrophoretic system for the determination of flaxseed lignans by capillary electrophoresis
abstract: A rational strategy was developed for constructing a capillary electrophoretic system for the separation of structurally related flaxseed lignans. Electrophoretic selectivity was sequentially optimized through background electrolyte composition, dynamic capillary modification, and organic modifier content using multivariate experimental design. The selected system consisted of 20 mmol L -1 borate, 7.5 mmol L -1 phosphate, and 2.5 mmol L -1 citrate (pH 11.0), containing 0.20% (w/v) PDADMAC and 20% (v/v) methanol, with separation at -20 kV. The method separated pinoresinol, lariciresinol, matairesinol, secoisolariciresinol, and secoisolariciresinol diglucoside. Quantitative validation was established for secoisolariciresinol and secoisolariciresinol diglucoside, determined at 0.87 ± 0.05 mg g -1 after sequential alkaline-acid hydrolysis and 6.6 ± 0.3 mg g -1 after alkaline hydrolysis, respectively. Field-amplified sample injection was additionally explored for improving detectability, although signal enhancement was accompanied by loss of selectivity for the lariciresinol-matairesinol pair.

title: SAGT-Net: A multi-scale Transformer embedded with GCN based on FT-NIR for Vitis ‘Shine Muscat’ maturity classification
abstract: Vitis 'Shine Muscat' remains green when fully ripe, making visual maturity identification unreliable. Traditional judgment methods depend on growers' experience, which is subjective and error-prone. This study proposes the Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer Network (SAGT-Net), a multi-scale Transformer combined with Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), to achieve rapid and non-destructive maturity classification of Vitis 'Shine Muscat' using Fourier Transform Near-Infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy. First-derivative Savitzky-Golay (SG-1st) smoothing was selected as the optimal spectral preprocessing method. After dataset partitioning and data augmentation, the model integrates one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), spectral attention and adaptive multi-scale GCN. It achieves a test accuracy of 95.16% and F1-score of 95.15%. Key spectral bands were further identified via t-SNE and SHAP analyses. The results show that the SAGT-Net model achieves high-precision maturity classification of Vitis 'Shine Muscat', providing a methodological framework and technical support for near-infrared nondestructive testing of this cultivar.

title: Antioxidant mechanisms of polyphenols in the storage and preservation of marine foods: a comprehensive review
abstract: Marine foods deteriorate during frozen storage, driven by protein and lipid oxidation and manifesting as colour browning, texture softening, and flavour loss. Polyphenols, multi-target natural antioxidants, offer considerable potential for preservation. The review summarises deterioration patterns, emphasising oxidation mechanisms, evaluates current preservation technologies, and examines advances in polyphenol application. Polyphenols act via radical scavenging, metal chelation, enzyme modulation, and target protein protection, and exert synergistic effects when combined with packaging or physical methods. However, polyphenol application remains constrained by inadequate stability, fragmented data, and unclear structure-activity relationships. Future priorities include stabilised polyphenol release via encapsulation or grafting, AI-driven construction of standardised datasets, and machine learning-based elucidation of preservation patterns to enable intelligent prediction and targeted formulation optimisation.

title: The advantages of radio frequency-assisted oven heating on thermal efficiency and meat quality of beef loin steak
abstract: Radio frequency-assisted oven heating (RF-OV) exhibits deeper thermal penetration, more uniform heating, and lower energy consumption than conventional heating methods. Nonetheless, its application to large food materials, such as beef loin steak, remains limited. Therefore, the effects of RF-OV on thermal efficiency, physicochemical quality, and sensory attributes of beef loin steak were evaluated by comparison with other heating methods: conventional oven heating (OV), microwave-assisted oven heating (MW-OV), and sous-vide heating (SV). The heating rate of RF-OV was significantly higher than that of OV (3.11 °C/min vs 1.63 °C/min). RF-OV resulted in improved physicochemical properties, including lower cooking loss (19.46% vs 28.87%) and shear force (50.00 N vs 58.55 N), along with more uniform heat distribution compared to MW-OV. Additionally, RF-OV produced a low level of burnt aroma intensity similar to SV (p > 0.05). Overall, RF-OV was effective in cooking beef steak due to its thermal efficiency, uniformity and desirable meat quality.

title: Cold plasma-activated lactic acid ice improved myofibrillar protein gel properties in tilapia fillets: A synergistic preservation mechanism
abstract: The quality of refrigerated tilapia fillets rapidly declines due to microbial spoilage and oxidative degradation of proteins and lipids. To address this, we developed plasma-activated lactic acid ice (PALAI) as a synergistic preservation method and evaluated its efficacy against tap water ice (TWI) and plasma-activated ice (PAI) over 7 days at 4 °C. PALAI outperformed controls by more effectively inhibiting microbial growth, delaying lipid oxidation, and suppressing protein oxidation. It better preserved myofibrillar protein (MP) integrity, maintaining higher carbonyl content (3.16 ± 0.50 nmol/mg) and Ca 2+ -ATPase activity (0.096 ± 0.02 U/mg prot). Consequently, PALAI-treated MP formed gels with superior strength (45.15 ± 3.70 g·mm), whiteness, and water-holding capacity. High-throughput sequencing showed PALAI selectively suppressed Gram-negative spoilage bacteria. Correlation analysis linked freshness indicators to MP properties (P < 0.05), demonstrating PALAI as a multi-target technology for maintaining tilapia quality during storage.

title: Comparative evaluation of high-performance aptamers to construct aggregation-induced emission-based DNA hydrogels for sensitive tetrodotoxin detection
abstract: Ingestion of the highly toxic tetrodotoxin (TTX) poses a serious threat to human health, making the development of sensitive and accurate analytical methods urgently necessary. Recognition molecules are critical for achieving high-sensitivity detection. Here, we aimed to rationally evaluate aptamers with high affinity, stability, and specificity for TTX using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. High-brightness fluorescent probes (TBTZNPs) were prepared via self-assembly to restrict intramolecular motion. By integrating high-performance aptamers with these probes, composite DNA hydrogels encapsulating TBTZNPs were constructed, which could be cleaved in response to TTX for sensitive detection. The sensor exhibited excellent application value, with a detection limit of 21.7 pg/mL, high specificity, reproducibility, and stability. Recoveries from real samples ranged from 91.52% to 110.20%, consistent with standard methods. These results demonstrate that highly sensitive TTX detection can be achieved using high-performance aptamers, providing new strategies for aptamer evaluating, and food safety monitoring.

title: Influence of processing on star anise quality: Appearance, chemical composition, and bioactivity
abstract: Star anise has been used as a spice for thousands of years, yet the effects of processing on its appearance and quality remain unclear. In this study, we systematically evaluate the effects of pretreatment (pre-blanching) and drying methods (sun, shade, and hot-air drying) on the appearance, phytochemical composition, antioxidant activity, and quality formation mechanism of star anise. The key finding is a temperature-dependent trade-off: low-temperature drying (sun, shade, and hot air drying ≤60 °C) produced brown samples with low brightness (L*) and yellowness (b*), accompanied by markedly lower levels of total flavonoids, phenolics, tannins, and epicatechin. In contrast, high-temperature treatments (pre-blanching and hot-air drying ≥80 °C) yielded yellowish-brown samples with substantially higher bioactive compound contents, along with correspondingly stronger antioxidant activity. In addition, odor was unaffected by pre-blanching but was absent in hot air dried samples, indicating that drying method governs volatile retention. Mechanistically, high temperature inactivated peroxidase while releasing bound phenolics, thereby suppressing enzymatic browning and promoting phenolic accumulation. Correlation analyses confirmed that L* and b* positively correlated with phenolic content and antioxidant activity. Overall, processing temperature, rather than pretreatment, is the primary determinant of star anise quality. High temperature processing (pre blanching or hot air drying ≥80 °C) is an effective strategy to produce star anise with superior phenolic profiles and antioxidant capacity, albeit at the cost of characteristic odor loss.

title: Characterization of flavor profiles and key discriminant compounds in citrus essential oils via metabolomics combined with sensory analysis
abstract: Citrus essential oils (EOs) are widely valued for their distinctive flavor and versatile functional properties. Existing single analytical approaches carry inherent limitations. Chromatographic techniques can profile metabolite compositions but fail to link chemical profiles to sensory perception, whereas sensory analysis alone cannot reveal the molecular basis underlying flavor variations. This study established an integrated strategy combining HS-SPME-GC-MS, UHPLC-MS/MS, electronic sensing, multivariate analysis and molecular docking to explore flavor differences across three citrus EOs. Overall, 49 volatile organic compounds were identified, and 1459 non-volatile metabolites were tentatively annotated. Thirteen key aroma-active compounds were screened out based on OAVs, and molecular docking suggested that they may bind to olfactory receptors through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Meanwhile, Pearson correlation confirmed close associations between metabolites and sensory responses. This work provides comprehensive chemical and sensory characterization for citrus EOs.

title: Corrigendum to “A new strategy to generate nanobodies for the coumaphos based on the synthesized nanobody libraries” [Food Chem. 455 (2024) 139684]
Identification of kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside as a characteristic marker and bioactive profile of Gentiana macrophylla pall. monofloral honey
abstract: As a medicinal plant-derived honey, Gentiana macrophylla Pall. monofloral honey (GH) remains insufficiently characterized in terms of botanical authentication and characteristic chemical markers. The objective of this study was to identify a marker compound for GH and to evaluate the physicochemical characteristics and bioactive properties. The botanical origin of GH was verified by SEM observation, revealing that Gentiana macrophylla Pall. pollen grains are monad, isopolar, radially symmetrical, with a tricolporate aperture system. Kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside was identified as a potential characteristic compound by UHPLC-DAD-QTOF-MS/MS, with a content of 331.06 ± 19.96 μg/kg in GH. Due to the abundant total flavonoid (34.98 ± 0.31 mg Rutin/kg) and total phenolic contents (283.68 ± 3.07 mg GAE/kg) compared with other common commercial honeys, GH exhibited significant antioxidant capacity and antibacterial activity against E. coli MG1655 and S. aureus 23,923. Consequently, kaempferol-3-O-sophoroside, as a potential authentication marker for GH, contributes to the improvement of bioactivity.

title: Generation of cyclic peptides with improved anti-Photoaging activity during the thermal processing of collagen peptides
abstract: This study explored the structural changes of collagen peptides during heat treatment under different conditions that might affect their anti-photoaging activities. Results showed that the matrix metalloproteinase-1 (MMP-1) inhibition rate of collagen hydrolysates significantly increased after heat treatment at various pH values, and its contents of Hyp (O)-containing and Gly-Pro-Xaa tripeptides significantly reduced, while cyclic dipeptides such as cyclo(LO), cyclo(FO), and cyclo(GP) were formed. Specifically, cyclo(LO) and cyclo(GP) displayed stronger MMP-1 inhibition (64.12% and 52.81%, respectively) than the linear di- and tripeptides LO, LOG, GPI and GPM (35.86%, 22.03%, 21.28% and 41.14%, respectively). This might be due to their increased conformational rigidity and strengthened hydrophobic interactions with MMP-1. Additionally, the cyclic dipeptides cyclo(PO), cyclo(LO), cyclo(AO), cyclo(SO), cyclo(FO) and cyclo(GP) significantly enhanced the viability of fibroblasts damaged by UVA. The results highlighted the cyclic form of Hyp-containing dipeptides with improved anti-photoaging activity generated upon heat treatment and its potential application in skin health.

title: Computation-assisted design and aqueous synthesis of magnetic molecularly imprinted polymers for trace detection of cephalosporins in aquatic products
abstract: The illegal use of ceftriaxone (CEF) and cefotaxime (CTX) in aquaculture threatens food safety and the environment. Conventional cephalosporin-imprinted magnetic molecularly imprinted polymers (MMIPs) are mainly synthesized in organic solvents, which limits their compatibility with aqueous food matrices and typically requires tens of minutes to hours to reach adsorption equilibrium. We report a quantum-chemistry-guided aqueous synthesis of a cephalosporin-selective magnetic molecularly imprinted polymer (MMIP). Theoretical analysis revealed that 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole (ATA) binds CEF through synergistic bidentate hydrogen bonds and π-π stacking interactions. Using water as the sole solvent and porogen eliminates toxic organic solvents and aligns with green chemistry principles. The resulting MMIP exhibited superparamagnetic properties, ultra-fast adsorption (equilibrium within 40 s, considerably faster than most reported cephalosporin MMIPs), an imprinting factor of 2.11, and two distinct binding site populations. An elution strategy combining hydrogen-bond disruption and electrostatic shielding achieved quantitative recovery (>95%). Combined with HPLC-MS/MS, the MMIP-based magnetic dispersive solid-phase extraction achieved a linear range of 1-400 ng/mL, a detection limit of 1.3 μg/kg, and recoveries of 71.0-93.1%. From 15 commercial aquatic samples, one was found positive at 18.2 μg/kg, corresponding to a positive rate of 10% for sea cucumber. This study offers a theory-guided, efficient, sensitive approach for detecting prohibited drug residues in seafood.

title: Transfer and processing fate of pesticide residues from feed to milk and dairy products: Kinetics, transformation and precision control
abstract: Pesticide residues in dairy products present a growing food safety concern, as residues originating from feed, water, soil, and veterinary applications of pesticide-active compounds may enter the dairy chain, undergo metabolic or processing-induced transformations, and partition among milk and dairy products. Unlike plant-derived foods, milk is a structurally heterogeneous matrix in which fat globules, proteins, phospholipid-rich interfacial layers, and an aqueous phase create distinct microenvironments that influence residue partitioning and analytical recovery. This critical narrative review examines the fate of pesticide residues across the dairy value chain, integrating feed-to-milk transfer, deposition in animal body, processing factors, mass-balance approaches, transformation products, analytical advances, and decontamination technologies within a food-chemistry framework. Across the available evidence, pesticide transfer along the dairy value chain is governed by the physicochemical properties of the pesticide, the composition of the dairy matrix, and the processing conditions. Under the specific mild pasteurization conditions examined in dairy studies, many residues show limited concentration change, whereas cream separation, coagulation, fermentation and water loss can redistribute or enrich selected compounds in particular product fractions. Consequently, a decline in parent-residue concentration should not be interpreted as degradation or detoxification without consideration of product yield, fraction-specific mass balance, transformation products and analytical recovery. Recent targeted MS/MS, high-resolution mass spectrometry and suspect-screening approaches have improved quantification of current-use pesticides, polar residues and metabolites in dairy products; however, the characterization of transformation-product and the availability of matrix-resolved mass-balance data remain limited. Upstream prevention, risk-based feed control and matrix-specific monitoring therefore remain central to residue management, while biological, enzymatic and oxidative interventions require direct validation in the intended dairy matrix. To organize such evidence, this review proposes a six-gate decision framework encompassing validated quantification of parent-residue, yield-corrected mass balance, characterization of transformation-products, assessment of residual-toxicity, preservation of dairy quality, and industrial feasibility. This framework provides a structured basis for evaluating pesticide-residue fate and intervention effectiveness beyond apparent reductions in parent compounds, thereby supporting robust risk assessment and safer dairy.

title: Deamidation-enabled fabrication of tough, stretchable, and transparent plant protein hydrogels
abstract: Plant protein hydrogels are promising for food structuring and nutrient delivery, yet conventional soybean protein systems suffer from weak mechanical strength due to particulate aggregation. Enzymatic deamidation can dissociate dense aggregates and improve homogeneity, but limited intermolecular connectivity still restricts mechanical performance of soybean protein hydrogels. Here, a sequential strategy involving protein-glutaminase (PG)-induced deamidation and transglutaminase (TGase)-mediated crosslinking was developed. PG promoted protein unfolding and aggregate reorganization, generating a transparent and designable network precursor, while TGase enhanced intermolecular connectivity via ε-(γ-glutamyl)lysine bonds. This led to denser, more homogeneous and ordered gel networks without compromising transparency. Multiscale analyses revealed increased network compactness, stronger protein-water interactions, and more uniform water distribution. Consequently, the hydrogels exhibited improved viscoelasticity, elasticity, deformation resistance and cyclic stability, with optimal performance at moderate TGase levels. This study provides a feasible and sustainable approach for fabricating tough and transparent soybean protein hydrogels for food and bioactive delivery applications.

title: Mild oxidation- and L-Cysteine-mediated disulfide bond modulation restores gelation performance of freeze-damaged myofibrillar protein
abstract: Freeze-thaw-induced protein oxidation and aggregation detrimentally compromise myofibrillar protein (MP) gelation. This study systematically elucidated the regulatory role of L -Cysteine ( L -Cys, 0-450 μmol/g) in the gelation behavior of native and freeze-thaw-damaged MP (FMP) under both non-oxidative and oxidative conditions. L -Cys treatment elicited extensive, concentration-dependent structural remodeling, culminating at 300 μmol/g, as evidenced by markedly elevated fluorescence intensity, surface hydrophobicity, and disulfide bond formation, insinuating enhanced thiol-disulfide exchange and intermolecular interactions. Notably, these effects were further potentiated under mild oxidative stress. Consequently, L -Cys supplementation, especially when combined with mild oxidation, accelerated gelation kinetics and triggered a favorable secondary structural transition from α-helix to β-sheet, while driving disulfide bonds toward a highly stable g-g-g conformation. This structural realignment facilitated the construction of a more compact, interconnected, and homogenous gel network with superior water-immobilizing capacity. Ultimately, the resultant gels exhibited markedly improved viscoelasticity and mechanical strength, effectively counteracting freeze-thaw-induced functional deterioration.

title: Decoding quality and metabolic shifts in truss tomato during ripening and cold storage for precision harvesting
abstract: Whole-truss harvesting is complicated by asynchronous ripening, which can decouple external maturity from internal quality. Truss tomato 'Qingfan No. 3' was evaluated at green (GS), turning (TS), mature (MS), and short-term cold storage stages (SS3 and SS6) by integrating harvest-related traits, internal quality, and sensory assessment. Ripening was characterized by softening, increased soluble solids content (SSC), sugars, lycopene, antioxidant capacity, and umami-related amino acids, together with decreased L-malic acid and titratable acidity. Cold storage further altered color and metabolism and increased weight loss and cracking. A non-color partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) model discriminated preharvest maturity, whereas an exploratory partial least-squares regression (PLSR) model linked firmness and SSC to a multivariate internal-quality score and defined an empirical MS harvest boundary (SSC ≥ 6.975 + 0.133 × firmness). These findings provide a preliminary cultivar-specific framework for maturity classification, harvest-readiness assessment, and precision harvesting of truss tomato.

title: Cross-scale effects of micro- and nanoplastics on nutritional composition, structural properties, and sensory quality in food systems
abstract: Despite growing concerns about micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) in food, the primary focus of most existing studies is on occurrence, human exposure, and detection methods, while providing limited understanding of how MNPs directly impact food quality. In contrast to the literature, this review focuses on the connection between structure, interaction, and food quality, emphasizing how surface chemistry, reactivity, and nanoscale dimensions of MNPs drive nutrient loss, off-flavor formation, textural changes, and oxidative degradation in foods. This review demonstrated that the dominant MNPs, biomolecule interactions occur through hydrophobic, electrostatic interactions, and surface adsorption processes. Among food macromolecules, the most susceptible to MNPs interaction is led by lipids, while proteins show a moderate risk and less risk for carbohydrates. Such interactions collectively contribute to food quality deterioration. Overall, the study highlights the need for method standardization, mechanistic and toxicological studies, which are meant to protect the global food supply against growing MNP pollution.

title: Decoding the quality changes of blunt snout bream (Megalobrama amblycephala) muscle under post-harvest cold stress
abstract: Rapid cooling during transportation triggers stress in fish, but its impact on muscle quality remains unclear. This study exposed blunt snout bream to four temperature drops (5 °C, 10 °C, 15 °C, and 20 °C). Mild cold stress (10 °C drop) enhanced quality: it preserved texture and color, increased inosine monophosphate and betaine, and suppressed bitter histidine. Severe cold stress (20 °C drop) caused softening, darkening, increased bitterness, and reduced betaine. Mechanistically, mild cold stress lowered levels of cortisol, glucose, lactate, and malondialdehyde, maintained low caspase-3 activity and apoptosis rate, and thereby protected myofibrils. Severe cold stress upregulated calpain, cathepsin B, and caspase-3 activity, leading to apoptosis, protein hydrolysis, and myofibril rupture. This study provides the first demonstration of an optimal cold stress in fish, showing that mild stress improves flavor and texture.

title: Top-down strategy for discovering bioavailable and bioactive natural compounds targeting aging and obesity: A human-to-cellular investigation
abstract: Obesity and aging are major global health challenges, both characterized by oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and metabolic dysfunction. Plant extracts provide promising sources of bioactive compounds, but traditional bottom-up strategies often encounter translational limitations because they assess biological activity before confirming compound bioavailability. This study implemented a top-down approach, beginning with a randomized, placebo-controlled human trial in which volunteers ingested lemon verbena ( Lippia citriodora ), olive leaf ( Olea europaea ), or milk thistle ( Silybum marianum ) extracts. Bioavailable circulating metabolites were identified through targeted mass spectrometry annotation by HPLC–ESI–QTOF–MS and subsequently evaluated in cellular models. Six major metabolites were selected and tested in stress-induced senescent fibroblasts and hypertrophic adipocytes to evaluate effects on cell proliferation, oxidative status, and lipid accumulation. Antioxidant capacity was assessed by TEAC and FRAP assays, and molecular docking simulations were used to explore potential protein targets. Verbascoside, gardoside, oleuropein, hydroxytyrosol 3-glucuronide, silybin, and myricetin 3-glucoside were consistently detected in human plasma after extract intake. After determining their cytotoxicity on the different cellular modeles, non toxic doses of these metabolites restored proliferation and reduced reactive oxygen species in senescent fibroblasts, decreased intracellular triglycerides in hypertrophic adipocytes, and modulated protein markers including SIRT1, Nrf2, and LC3. Docking analyses supported interactions with metabolic and stress-response pathways, consistent with the observed cellular effects. The “human-to-cellular” strategy identified bioavailable metabolites with protective effects against cellular hallmarks of obesity and aging. By ensuring bioavailability before functional screening, this approach may enhance translational predictability and help identify potential candidates for future nutraceutical research based on a multicomponent formulation enriched in these bioavailable compounds. These findings support the value of the top-down approach in natural product research, intervention studies and nutraceuticals developments. Future studies should test these combinations in intervention trials to evaluate synergy, dosage, and long-term benefits modulating the negative effects of obesity and aging on human health.

title: In-situ VT-NMR and VT-CLSM reveal water-gluten interaction dynamics during freeze-thaw: From post-thaw inference to real-time monitoring
abstract: Freeze-thaw (FT) cycles cause frozen dough quality deterioration. This study employed in-situ variable-temperature NMR (VT-NMR) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (VT-CLSM) to monitor water state and gluten network evolution at -30 °C in doughs with 40%, 46%, and 50% hydration during FT cycling. VT-NMR captured increases in T 2 relaxation time and decreases in unfrozen water content, corresponding to changes in water mobility and phase redistribution. VT-CLSM visualized concurrent structural disruption of the gluten network, including increased porosity and reduced protein continuity. Frozen-state T 2 showed a strong correlation with microstructural damage (r = 0.92), while unfrozen water content was moderately associated with thawing loss (r = -0.58). Optimal hydration (46%) exhibited the greatest FT stability. These results indicate that in-situ VT-NMR, complemented by VT-CLSM structural evidence, can provide information associated with gluten network integrity that is not directly obtainable from conventional post-thaw analysis.

title: Low-conjugation carbonized polymer dots enable rapid dual-mode detection of nitrite via diazotization–coupling and synergistic inner filter effect/static quenching
abstract: Herein, we report a fluorescence/colorimetric dual-mode probe for NO 2 - detection based on blue-emissive carbonized polymer dots (b-CPDs), rapidly synthesized from m-phenylenediamine and phosphoric acid via a one-step solvent-free thermal route. The probe enabled rapid and sensitive detection of NO 2 - within 3 min, with fluorescence and colorimetric detection limits as low as 30 and 5 nM, respectively. This performance may arise from low background absorption due to limited conjugation and stable dispersion at relatively high concentrations enabled by abundant hydrophilic surface groups. Smartphone readout enabled a portable quantitative platform for on-site analysis. Real-sample recoveries were 98.20%-105.67%, with RSDs ≤ 4.79% and no significant difference from the results obtained by ion chromatography. Structural characterization and quantum chemical calculations suggested that the colorimetric response may originate from a diazotization-coupling reaction involving surface amino groups, whereas fluorescence quenching may arise from the combined contributions of the inner filter effect (IFE) and static quenching.

title: Physicochemical properties and antioxidative stability of curcumin-loaded oleogel made with ethyl cellulose enhanced by soy lecithin
abstract: Curcumin-loaded liposome-ethyl cellulose (CLE) complexes are developed to overcome curcumin degradation and weak gel networks in PUFA-rich oleogels. Curcumin liposomes, prepared with soy lecithin and cholesterol, are combined with ethyl cellulose (EC), and the optimal CLE formulation (13 wt% lecithin/EC, 40% ethanol) is selected by encapsulation efficiency and stability. When incorporated into linseed oil, CLE enhances oil binding (91.88%) and hardness (352.47 g) vs EC-only oleogels, indicating reinforced network. CLE oleogels exhibit lower peroxide value (PV) and p-anisidine value (p-AV) than those containing free curcumin, reflecting reduced primary hydroperoxides and secondary aldehydes, along with higher ABTS radical scavenging, confirming improved antioxidant retention during processing and storage. FTIR and molecular dynamics reveal that van der Waals and electrostatic interactions, especially EC-glycerol trilinolenate (-26.46 kcal/mol) and glycerol trilinolenate-lecithin (-26.27 kcal/mol), govern complex stability. These results support CLE as a viable trans-fat-free oleogel system for delivering natural antioxidants in oxidatively sensitive lipid matrices.

title: Rapid visual detection of DNA-traceable barcodes for food authentication using saltatory rolling circle amplification (SRCA)
abstract: DNA-traceable barcodes have shown potential for food traceability and anti-counterfeiting; however, rapid and user-friendly detection methods are still needed for practical deployment. In this study, a rapid authentication strategy for a DNA-traceable barcode system was developed using saltatory rolling circle amplification (SRCA) combined with fluorescence-based visual detection. Under optimized conditions, the visual SRCA method achieved an empirical visual detection limit of 5.4 fg/μL recombinant plasmid DNA, representing a 1000-fold improvement in sensitivity compared to conventional PCR-capillary electrophoresis (PCR-CE) under the tested conditions. The applicability of the system was demonstrated using Citrus sinensis samples labeled with DNA-traceable barcodes. Notably, the DNA-traceable barcodes remained detectable after 90 days of storage, and Sanger sequencing confirmed complete sequence identity of the recovered barcode. Therefore, the developed SRCA-based visual assay, characterized by rapid operation, high sensitivity, and simple readout, provides a practical tool for detecting DNA-traceable barcodes and holds significant potential for food traceability and anti-counterfeiting applications.

title: Insights into glycidyl ester formation during single- and two-stage deodorization of medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols: mitigation behavior and potential mechanism
abstract: Medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs) are nutritionally valuable structured lipids, but they face a severe deodorization challenge due to glycidyl ester (GE) formation. This study investigated the changes in FFA composition, acylglycerol distribution, GE formation, and distillate composition during single- and two-stage deodorization of MLCT oil. For single-stage deodorization, FFA removal followed an asymptotic first-order kinetic model, and medium-chain fatty acids were preferentially stripped owing to higher volatility. Temperatures above 220 °C, FFA removal was significantly enhanced, but also promoted GE formation and intensified neutral lipid loss via co-distillation. Based on these findings, two-stage deodorization was developed to balance deacidification and hazard mitigation. Under the optimal conditions (180 °C for 30 min followed by 220 °C for 20 min), FFAs were reduced to 0.94% while GEs remained at 0.85 mg/kg. These findings provide an effective refining strategy for producing safer MLCT oil and promoting its application in food processing.

title: Formulation of alginate-based edible films blended with encapsulated plum seed oil, and application for grape tomato preservation
abstract: Food packaging plays a crucial role in preserving quality, safety, and shelf life. This study developed alginate-based edible films incorporating plum seed oil in free and encapsulated forms and evaluated the effects of encapsulation on their physicochemical, mechanical, color, antioxidant, antimicrobial, thermal, microstructural, and biodegradability characteristics. The applicability of the films was assessed using grape tomatoes by monitoring weight loss and color changes during refrigerated storage. Encapsulated plum seed oil improved the physical stability of the films, reduced water activity and moisture content, and preserved mechanical properties at intermediate encapsulation levels. Encapsulation also protected phenolic compounds, significantly enhancing antioxidant and antimicrobial activities. SEM and FT-IR analyses indicated that the chemical structure was preserved, with predominantly physical interactions among the components, while TGA demonstrated enhanced thermal stability. All films exhibited high biodegradability. Overall, alginate-based edible films effectively reduced quality deterioration in grape tomatoes, highlighting their potential as an environmentally friendly approach to extending the shelf life of fruits and vegetables.

title: Construction of functionalized covalent organic framework for the efficient enrichment of neonicotinoid insecticides from leafy vegetables prior to HPLC-MS analysis
abstract: Trace residues of neonicotinoid insecticides (NIs) in food may pose great risk to human health. In this study, an amino and triazine co-functionalized covalent organic framework (Tp@tr-COF) was fabricated and it exhibited enhanced adsorption performance for NIs compared with that of un-functionalized counterpart. The mechanism investigation revealed that hydrogen bond interactions and π-π stacking were the main adsorption forces. With Tp@tr-COF as solid phase extraction adsorbent, a sensitive high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry method was established for the determination of NIs in leafy vegetables. The accuracy and precision of the established method were verified, achieving low limits of detection (0.18-0.60 ng·g -1 ) and satisfactory recoveries (88.0%-110%) with RSD ≤ 7.7%. Furthermore, the extraction recovery of Tp@tr-COF remained unchanged after 30 regeneration cycles. These data suggest that the proposed method is a promising alternative for quantifying NIs in leafy vegetables, while this study sheds light on the rational design of functionalized COFs.

title: Immobilized enzyme-catalyzed preparation and characterization of artificial Antarctic krill oil analogs from egg yolk lecithin
abstract: Antarctic krill oil (AKO) serves as a vital natural source of phospholipid-bound EPA/DHA, but its large-scale industrial application is limited by unstable supply chains, poor oxidative stability, and potential food safety risks. This work established an enzymatic strategy for the synthesis of artificial AKO analogs (AAKOs). A dual-functionalized hollow mesoporous silica carrier (HMSP-N 3 /C 8 ) was engineered to immobilize phospholipase B (PLB). Synergistic hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions significantly enhanced the catalyst's stability and reusability. The transesterification reaction between EPA/DHA-rich oils and egg yolk lecithin was optimized under solvent-free conditions, achieving high incorporation efficiency. Comprehensive characterization revealed that the prepared AAKOs possessed physicochemical features and oxidative stability comparable to natural AKO. This work provides a sustainable, controllable, and cost-effective platform for the enzymatic production of AKO analogs, offering a promising solution to overcome the current limitations associated with the utilization of natural AKO.

title: Selective enrichment of milk phospholipids via cryo-crystallization: application to various dairy matrices and elucidation of sphingomyelin crystallization mechanisms
abstract: Milk sphingomyelin (SM) is a bioactive phospholipid involved in infant neurodevelopment and gut health; however, its proportion in dairy by-products is around 20% of total phospholipids, compared to over 30% in human milk, limiting its application in infant formula products. The molecular mechanisms underlying the selective enrichment of SM during cryo-crystallization were elucidated. Cryo-crystallization increased total phospholipid content by 2.12-fold, while the SM proportion increased from 27% to 41%. Lipidomics revealed preferential enrichment of very-long-chain fatty acid-containing phospholipids. Structural analyses showed enhanced molecular ordering and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Differential scanning calorimetry identified ~70% ethanol as a thermodynamic window favoring SM crystallization over glycerophospholipids. For raw buttermilk, low initial phospholipid content limited direct cryo-crystallization, requiring ethanol pre-extraction optimized at 100% ethanol, a 1:20 solvent-to-material ratio, 55 °C, and 90 min; phospholipid recovery decreased at 70 °C. The strategy was applicable to multiple dairy matrices for producing SM-enriched phospholipids.

title: Effects of different plant growth regulators on the fruit quality and characteristic aroma of ‘Summer Black’ grapes for juice production
Melatonin regulates protein structures of wheat under shading for cookie crack ratio and digestibility modifications
abstract: The crack ratio and nutritional value of cookies depend on wheat protein structures, yet how melatonin modifies these attributes under shading remains unclear. This study evaluated the effects of melatonin (200 μmol L -1 ) on protein structure and cookie-making quality in shaded wheat. Under shading, melatonin increased glutenin, gliadin, total protein, and small polymeric protein content, and raised β-sheet and α-helix proportions by up to 14.4% and 13.2%, respectively, strengthening non-covalent interactions into a more cross-linked gluten network. Melatonin also elevated sulfur-containing and aromatic amino acids, improving nutritional value and digestibility. A SegFormer-based machine learning model showed melatonin reduced the cookie crack ratio by 18.8-30.7% and improved homogeneity. Protein content, γ-gliadin, and small polymeric proteins governed the crack ratio, whereas digestibility was primarily associated with small polymeric proteins. Collectively, melatonin regulates crack ratio and digestibility by modulating amino acid profiles and protein structures, offering a promising approach to enhance cookie-making quality.

title: Synergistic effects of micro wet milling and thermosonication on microstructure, rheology, polyphenol profiling, and quality attributes of Flacourtia jangomas juice
abstract: This study investigated the effects of micro-wet milling (MWM), ultrasonication (US), and thermosonication (TS) on the microstructure, rheological behavior, bioactive recovery, and microbial quality of underutilized Flacourtia jangomas juice. MWM-assisted treatments significantly reduced particle size, with MWM + TS achieving the lowest D50 (37.24 μm) and improved morphological uniformity. MWM + US exhibited the highest measurable bioactive compounds and antioxidant activity, including total phenolic content (73.73 mg GAE/100 mL), total flavonoid content (25.35 mg QE/100 mL), and DPPH inhibition (85.28%). Color analysis revealed treatment-dependent changes in visual attributes. MWM + TS enhanced microbial quality by reducing peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase activities and microbial loads. FTIR combined with second-order derivative analysis indicated treatment-induced variations in functional group environments without major changes in the chemical profile. LC-MS tentatively annotated phenolic compounds, while partial least squares analysis suggested treatment-related phytochemical variations. Overall, MWM-assisted acoustic processing improved the structural, functional, and quality attributes of F. jangomas juice.

title: Deciphering the effect of sugar-to-water mass ratios on key aroma formation in roasted ducks: Insights from volatilomics, lipidomics, and Maillard reaction
abstract: Sugar-coating is a pivotal step in roasted duck processing, yet its optimization has relied on artisanal experience rather than standardized protocols. This study explored how varying sugar-to-water mass ratios affect the aroma formation. The 1:6 sugar-to-water mass ratio produced the richest aroma compounds in roasted ducks compared with the ratios of 1:5, 1:7 and 1:8. This optimal condition likely facilitated the glucose penetration from the skin into the meat, enhancing Maillard reactions with arginine and alanine for pyrazine formation. It also promoted the contribution of triglycerides, ceramides, and phosphatidylcholines containing C 18 -acyl chains to the formation and retention of key odorants. Variations in the consumption of arginine, alanine, phospholipids, and triglycerides mainly caused aroma differences in roasted ducks with different sugar-coating ratios. Interestingly, (E)-2-nonenal and (E, E)-2,4-nonadienal emerged as potential markers discriminating roasted ducks with various sugar-coating ratios. These findings provided new insights into the standardized processing of sugar-coated roasted duck.

title: Unveiling the structural evolution and molecular assembly in ethanol-induced gelation of tamarind seed polysaccharide
abstract: Tamarind seed polysaccharide (TSP) can form gels in the presence of ethanol, yet the underlying structural mechanism remains unclear. Here, ethanol-induced TSP gelation was investigated by combining rheology, micro-differential scanning calorimetry, atomic force microscopy, synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering, and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance. The results reveal that TSP undergoes a four-stage structural evolution during a heating-cooling cycle. At ambient temperature, ethanol reduced solvent quality and chain hydration, promoting chain association and partial precipitation. Upon heating, these initial aggregates progressively reorganized into weak, locally correlated associations that were further destabilized at elevated temperatures, yielding loosely connected structures. During cooling, reduced thermal motion and closer chain proximity promoted the reorganization of short-range associations and the formation of mechanically effective junctions, resulting in a stable gel network. These findings reveal a multistage, solvent-regulated assembly pathway for ethanol-induced TSP gelation.

title: Multi-omics analysis elucidates the impacts of anthocyanins from various fruit pulps on bacterial communities, metabolites and proteins in yogurt
abstract: Fruit pulp fortification improves the nutritional profile and bioactive functionality of yogurt. In this study, we adopted 16S rRNA gene sequencing, UHPLC-MS-based metabolomics and DIA (data-independent acquisition)-based proteomics on raw milk, plain yogurt and five different anthocyanin-rich fruit yogurts. The work intended to clarify how anthocyanins in fruit pulp reshape yogurt composition and identify signature microbes and substances to each group. Besides Streptococcus, the dominant genera in plain, mulberry and grape yogurt were respectively Lactococcus, Lacticaseibacillus/Lactobacillus, and Bifidobacterium. β-D-fucose accumulated abundantly in plain yogurt. Abscisic acid exhibited higher levels in strawberry yogurt. It was positively correlated to Lactobacillus acidophilus and L. delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus. Furthermore, it downregulated α S1 -casein, a major milk allergen. Grape yogurt contained elevated levels of astilbin, eriocitrin and glucosylxanthone. In conclusion, yogurt microbiota, metabolites and proteins could be modified by fruit anthocyanins. Our findings advance a deeper understanding on the unique health-promoting effects of various fruit yogurt.

title: Aptamer-functionalized solution-gated graphene transistor for rapid detection of trace scandium
abstract: The growing exploitation of rare earth resources has led to the migration and accumulation of Scandium (Sc) within food systems, giving rise to emerging food safety concerns. Conventional techniques for Scandium (III) ions (Sc 3+ ) detection are limited by labor-intensive sample preparation, high instrumentation costs, and poor suitability for rapid on-site screening. Here, we report a highly sensitive and selective biosensor for Sc 3+ that integrates a Sc 3+ -specific nucleic acid aptamer (Sc-1) with a solution-gated graphene transistor (SGGT). The sensing mechanism relies on aptamer conformational changes induced by Sc 3+ binding, which modulate the interfacial charge distribution and electric double-layer properties at the gate electrode, producing a quantifiable shift in the graphene channel current. The optimized aptamer-functionalized Sc-SGGT (Scandium-specific solution-gated graphene transistor) biosensors exhibit a wide dynamic range from 1 pM to 100 nM and an excellent sensitivity with a limit of detection (LOD) calculated to be 0.736 pM. They also demonstrate robust anti-interference capability against common coexisting ions and rare-earth analogs. Moreover, spike recovery experiments in real food samples yield excellent recoveries, confirming the method's practicality for complex matrix analysis. Together, these results establish a rapid, sensitive, and reliable strategy for Sc 3+ detection, presenting a promising platform for food safety surveillance of rare-earth contaminants.

title: A stage-dependent mechanism of high-amylose starch gelation: amylose-associated early differentiation and botanical-origin-dependent later maturation
abstract: High-amylose starch gels are widely used in applications requiring firm texture, and structural stability, yet gelation is often interpreted primarily by amylose content. Herein, fifteen starches from maize, rice, wheat, barley, and potato were compared to determine whether gel evolution is governed solely by amylose level or by stage-dependent structural pathways. At 1 h, high-amylose maize, wheat, barley, and potato starches generally exhibited stronger rheological properties, accompanied by finer microstructures, higher short-range order, reduced SAXS correlation length (ξ), and early water redistribution, indicating rapid scaffold formation. Rice was an exception, with normal starch exhibiting stronger rheological properties. After 7 days, maturation no longer followed a simple amylose-dependent pattern. While nanoscale and crystalline features were largely established early, microstructural development and water redistribution became increasingly source-dependent. These findings support a two-stage model in which amylose drives early network formation, whereas botanical origin governs subsequent gel maturation.

title: Sequence-based database mining and characterization of cutinases for efficient synthesis of aromatic esters
abstract: The discovery of cutinases with desirable catalytic properties is important for expanding their applications in the synthesis of value-added food and pharmaceutical molecules, particularly for the aromatic esters. However, many efficient enzymes remain hidden within the growing sequence data. We used sequence-based database mining to identify an uncharacterized cutinase, NlCut, and investigated its structural features, biochemical properties and catalytic performance. NlCut was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) at 55.92 mg protein L -1 culture and exhibited a specific activity of 198.26 U/mg toward p-nitrophenyl butyrate. Notably, immobilization on Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 -NH-CHO magnetic nanoparticles markedly enhanced its stability in organic solvents. In toluene, the immobilized NlCut catalyzed the transesterification of benzyl alcohol with vinyl acetate, affording benzyl acetate in 96.11% yield within 1 h. Moreover, the yield remained above 80% after eight consecutive reuse cycles. This work highlights the potential of immobilized NlCut as an efficient biocatalyst for non-aqueous synthesis of aromatic esters.

title: Dual-action preservation of Selenicereus megalanthus by Leonurus japonicus extract: direct antifungal activity and host resistance elicitation
abstract: Selenicereus megalanthus is an economically important tropical fruit highly susceptible to postharvest soft rot. Fusarium equiseti was isolated from diseased fruits and identified as a new pathogen causing soft rot. Leonurus japonicus extract (YMC) showed potent in vitro activity (EC₅₀ = 0.943 mg mL -1 ). LC-MS profiled 83 compounds; five major markers were validated. YMC disrupted hyphal ultrastructure, increased membrane permeability, suppressed ergosterol biosynthesis, and induced oxidative stress. Molecular docking, MD simulations, and expression analyses confirmed downregulation of ergosterol synthesis enzymes (ERG7, CYP51) and virulence proteins. In vivo, YMC at 2 × EC 50 reduced lesion expansion and soft-rot incidence, matching 80 μg mL -1 prochloraz and outperforming carvacrol. YMC also upregulated host defense enzymes (PAL, POD, PPO, CHI, SOD, CAT) and genes (HuPAL, HuPOD, HuCHI), maintaining fruit quality and extending room-temperature shelf life by 12 days. Caenorhabditis elegans toxicity assays confirmed its high biological safety. YMC acts through direct antifungal action and host defense activation, showing strong potential as a sustainable green biopreservative for postharvest tropical fruit.

title: Drying-driven quality differentiation of rhubarb rhizomes: a multi-level metabolomics analysis of microstructural damage and bioactive compound attenuation
abstract: Pithiness is one of the most common quality defects occurring during the drying process of Rhubarb (Rheum palmatum L.), yet its effects on quality characteristics and metabolic profiles remain poorly understood. In this study, fresh Rhubarb (X), normally dried Rhubarb (NK), and pithy Rhubarb (K) were systematically compared using sensory evaluation, microstructural observation, physicochemical analysis, and untargeted metabolomics. Compared with NK, K exhibited lower bitterness, darker color, more pronounced tissue collapse, and extensive cavity formation. X showed the highest total phenolic (TPC) and total flavonoid (TFC) contents. TPC in X was 26.21% and 48.03% higher than in NK and K, respectively, while TFC was 24.5% and 24.2% higher. K exhibited lower DPPH and FRAP antioxidant activities, whereas ABTS activity did not differ significantly among groups. Compared with NK, K exhibited markedly lower levels of major anthraquinones, including emodin, chrysophanol, aloe-emodin, physcion, and rhein. Untargeted metabolomics identified 1607 metabolites, with 199, 158, and 261 differentially accumulated metabolites in NK_vs_X, NK_vs_K, and K_vs_X, respectively. KEGG analysis revealed marked alterations in glycerophospholipid metabolism and phenylpropanoid-flavonoid biosynthesis. NK showed higher levels of several aromatic precursor- and polyketide-related metabolites and anthraquinones, whereas K exhibited distinct lipid-related and secondary metabolic profiles. These findings provide a basis for understanding post-drying quality deterioration and optimizing Rhubarb processing.

title: Effects of a Hofmeister kosmotropic salt and protein thermal denaturation on bovine serum albumin–lutein binding, complex stability, and the in vitro biological activities of the carotenoid
authors: Bruno Ricardo de Castro Leite Junior
abstract: Fluorescence, FTIR, and UV–Vis spectroscopy, combined with in vitro antioxidant (ABTS and DPPH) and antidiabetic assays, were used to evaluate the interaction between bovine serum albumin (BSA) and lutein (LUT), as well as carotenoid dispersion and functional responses at pH 7.4, under defined Na 2 SO 4 conditions (0.01–0.05 M) and thermal denaturation of BSA. Fluorescence analysis revealed a static quenching mechanism with 1:1 stoichiometry and binding constants on the order of 10 4 L/mol that increased with temperature (298–313 K). Binding affinity followed the order BSA–LUT < BSA (0.01M Sulfate) –LUT < BSA den –LUT < BSA (0.05M Sulfate) –LUT. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔH° > 0, ΔS° > 0) indicated that hydrophobic interactions were the predominant driving force for complex formation. FTIR indicated BSA structural rearrangements, particularly increased β-sheet content. Na₂SO₄ (0.05 M) and thermal treatment improved LUT dispersion and enhanced its antioxidant and α-glucosidase inhibitory activities, demonstrating that BSA environment modulation can improve the functional performance of LUT-containing systems.

title: Retraction notice to “Colorimetric and fluorometric nanoprobe for selective and sensitive recognition of hazardous colorant indigo carmine in beverages based on ion pairing with nitrogen doped carbon dots” [Food Chem. 349 (2021) 129160]
Ligand-based prediction of novel sweetener candidates
abstract: Artificial sweeteners raise health concerns due to disrupted appetite regulation and potential cardiometabolic risks. Discovering novel, high-intensity, low-calorie sweeteners remains a significant challenge. In this study, we present a robust ligand-based machine learning framework using our in-house Iterative Stochastic Elimination (ISE) algorithm to distinguish between sweet and bitter compounds. By screening three vast chemical libraries; Enamine HTS, Enamine REAL, and ZINC Druglike, we identified a diverse set of potential sweeteners. Our models showed high accuracy and specificity, minimizing false positives and maximizing enrichment of true actives. To refine these hits, we integrated molecular docking targeting the T1R2 Venus flytrap domain and filtered for PAINS/BRENK liabilities, resulting in a prioritized set of 92 candidate molecules. Tanimoto similarity analysis confirmed that the majority of these hits represent novel chemotypes, distinct from known modulators. This workflow demonstrates the power of combining physico-chemical-based models with structural filtration to accelerate the discovery of novel sweeteners.

title: Polysaccharide-metal ion chelation-mediated regulation of anthocyanin stability and molecular interactions
abstract: Anthocyanins are widely recognized as natural colorants with diverse bioactive properties, but their poor thermal stability restricts their application in food systems. In this study, high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS) characterizes the anthocyanin (ACN) profile of Lycium ruthenicum Murr.. The effects and underlying mechanisms of Lycium barbarum polysaccharides (LBPs), Zn 2+ /Ca 2+ , and their combined interactions (ACN-LBPs-Zn 2+ /Ca 2+ ) on the thermal stability of anthocyanins were systematically investigated. The results showed that the ACN-LBPs-Zn 2+ /Ca 2+ systems significantly enhanced anthocyanin thermal stability, with the ACN-LBPs-Zn 2+ system increasing the half-lives of total anthocyanins and total petunidin by 3.49- and 2.53-fold, respectively. Mechanistic investigations indicated that LBPs interacted with Zn 2+ /Ca 2+ to form compact cross-linked networks, while hydrogen bonding and coordination interactions stabilized ACN molecules, inhibiting thermal degradation. These findings provide a theoretical basis for improving the color stability of anthocyanin-containing foods and offer a promising strategy for developing highly stable natural anthocyanin pigments for food applications.

title: Effects of modified β-lactoglobulin on in vitro digestion and absorption characteristics of algae oil emulsion
abstract: In this study, β-lactoglobulin (β-Lg) was modified by sequential glycation, high-pressure microfluidization (HPM), and conjugation with (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG). The effects of this modified protein on the in vitro digestive and intestinal uptake of algae oil emulsions were investigated. It was found that the interfacial film formed by multi-modified β-Lg (EHG 48 β-Lg) at the water-oil interface resisted pepsin hydrolysis. In intestinal digestion, it was readily and effectively displaced by bile salts, which facilitated the adsorption of lipase. This effect endowed the algae oil emulsion stabilized by EHG 48 β-Lg with the highest free fatty acid release rate and a 329.2% increase in DHA bioaccessibility. Furthermore, compared with pure algae oil, the DHA uptake rate and apparent permeability coefficient of the EHG 48 β-Lg-stabilized algae oil emulsion increased by 54.4% and 85.0%, respectively. These results demonstrated that EHG 48 β-Lg can significantly improve the delivery and absorption efficiency of DHA by optimizing the interfacial structure of the emulsion.

title: Persimmon peel polyphenols modulate the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway to exert prebiotic effects: implications for high-value utilization
abstract: Persimmon (Diospyros kaki 'Fuping Jianshi') peel is a by-product of persimmon processing, which is rich in polyphenols. In this study, the ultrasound-assisted ethanol extraction and purification of persimmon peel polyphenols (PPP) were optimized, and the PPP with yielding a final total phenolic content (TPC) of 287.52 ± 4.10 mg GAE/g of 287.52 ± 4.10 mg GAE/g was obtained. Using UPLC-MS/MS, 796 compounds were identified from PPP, which were primarily phenolic acids. PPP significantly promoted the growth of Lactobacillus acidophilus NCFM and exhibited prebiotic activity. In vitro colonic fermentation showed that PPP promoted Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, inhibited Proteobacteria and Escherichia-Shigella, and significantly increased Short-Chain Fatty Acids (SCFAs) production. Multi-omics analysis elucidated that the biotransformation of PPP is closely associated with a reciprocal feedback loop with gut microbiota, potentially modulated by the specific enrichment of flavonoid biosynthetic pathways. These results indicated that PPP possesses strong antioxidant and gut regulatory properties, supporting its value as a functional food ingredient or nutritional component, and promoting the valorization of persimmon peel.

title: Aroma chemical signatures of wine geographical origin: rationalizing the chemical drivers of red wine terroir expression
abstract: Expression of the link between a wine and its place of origin is highly sought after in wine, in particular in relation to aroma composition. The aim of this study was to explore the existence, in wine, of volatile chemical patterns reflecting the place of origin of the grapes. Wines were produced from grapes coming from five vineyards during three consecutive vintages, and their volatile composition was analyzed. We identified specific volatile patterns uniquely associated with each vineyard, clearly indicating the existence of terroir factors specific of each the different vineyard sites. Grape-derived metabolites such as linalool and α-terpineol, damascenone, vitispirane, dimethyl sulfide (DMS), as well as fermentative metabolites such as isoamyl acetate and ethyl hexanoate were the main drivers of pattern differences. Further investigation indicated that the grape content of aroma precursors, yeast nitrogen nutrients, and must pH are key drivers to the development of terroir-related aroma signatures of red wine.

title: Pre-harvest cold treatment enhances the flavor quality of green tea: Insights from metabolomics, volatilomics, and sensory analysis during processing
abstract: Pre-harvest cold treatment enhances tea flavor, yet the chemical mechanisms during processing remain elusive. This study investigated the impact of cold treatment on green tea quality using metabolomics, volatilomics, and sensory evaluation. Cold treatment significantly reduced astringency and enhanced umami, chemically attributed to a reprogrammed "high-amino acid, low-ester catechin" profile. Crucially, GC × GC-O-Q-TOF-MS revealed a dramatic enrichment of floral and fruity volatiles in the cold-treated group. Odor activity value (OAV) analysis identified trans-β-ionone as the critical impact odorant, exhibiting an over 1800-fold increase compared to the control. Integrated analysis suggested this aroma surge was closely associated with the priming of jasmonic acid (JA) and abscisic acid (ABA) signaling pathways, which upregulated key structural enzyme genes particularly during the spreading stage. These findings demonstrate that cold treatment effectively primes metabolic precursors for superior aroma formation, offering a novel strategy for high-quality green tea production.

title: Destabilization of monoglyceride-structured oleogel emulsions by secondary surfactants for enhancing crystal morphology-driven saltiness perception
abstract: Water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions can enhance saltiness perception through localized sodium release. This study investigated how secondary surfactants affected microstructure, sodium release and saltiness in oleogel-based emulsions structured with glycerol monopalmitate (GMP) or glycerol monolaurate (GML) crystals. In GMP systems, the addition of surfactants weakened the oil-phase crystal network, promoting droplet coalescence and Na + release. In contrast, GML-based systems exhibited interfacial crystal displacement and a "bubble effect", which synergistically promoted rapid Na + release. Low-molecular-weight surfactants enhanced saltiness perception more effectively than the protein-based surfactants, increasing saltiness intensity by up to 40% in GMP emulsions. Moreover, several surfactants improved Na + migration in lingual mucin, which was beneficial for enhancing the saltiness perception. Although GML emulsions showed greater in vitro Na + release, their rapid oral breakdown minimized perceptual differences among the samples. Overall, these findings provide a robust structure-release-perception framework for the design of salt-reduced food products.

title: Physicochemical properties, storage stability, and cell viability of bread supplemented with encapsulated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of whey protein isolate (WPI)-based binary systems with maltodextrin (MTX) or octenyl succinic anhydride-modified starch (OSA) for spray-drying microencapsulation of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and its incorporation into bread. This approach addresses a key limitation in probiotic bakery by enhancing cell survival under thermal and gastrointestinal stresses. Microcapsules exhibited low moisture ( 6 log CFU/g). Although encapsulation modified dough rheology, reduced loaf volume, and increased firmness, sensory acceptance remained moderate to high. These findings demonstrate the potential of WPI-polysaccharide systems to enable probiotic delivery through bread, supporting the development of functional bakery products.

title: From seeds to sprouts: micronutrient profiling across edible chia forms highlights dried dark-grown seedlings as ingredients with a broad compositional profile
abstract: Chia seeds and sprouts are known for their nutritional value, but other forms remain underexplored. To evaluate micronutrient content across edible chia forms, dark-grown seedlings and sprouts were grown from seeds and compared. Light and methyl salicylate treatments were applied to biofortify sprouts. Dried dark-grown seedlings displayed the greatest micronutrient density (vitamin C [435.6 mg/100 g], together with high contents of magnesium, calcium, iron, phosphorus, zinc, sulfur, manganese, and molybdenum) and radical scavenging activity. Seeds were rich in minerals and γ- and δ-tocopherol, whereas sprouts had the highest pro-vitamin A content [5.4 mg/100 g]. A chia-only mixture of 185 g sprouts, 130 g dark-grown seedlings, and 60 g seeds reached micronutrient reference values on a theoretical compositional basis. Biofortification produced slight light-dependent effects, with selected minerals increasing 1.3-1.6-fold. These findings position edible chia forms as complementary micronutrient sources and highlight dried dark-grown seedlings as a nutrient-dense ingredient for food applications.

title: Valorization of tomato pomace to produce lycopene-enriched chia and poppy seed oils: Effects on nutritional quality, oxidative stability, and volatile aroma profile
abstract: Tomato by-products are rich in bioactive compounds but remain largely underutilized. In this study, tomato pomace (1, 5, and 10%, w/w) was incorporated into chia and poppy seeds prior to screw-press oil extraction to obtain functional oils enriched with tomato-derived compounds. Extraction yield, quality parameters, oxidative stability, fatty acid composition, sterol content, lycopene concentration, and volatile profile were evaluated. Pomace addition reduced oil yield by 3.5% in chia oil and 23.3% in poppy oil at 10% incorporation, without compromising oil quality. Oxidative stability increased by 29.6% in chia oil and 15.0% in poppy oil, while fatty acid profiles remained unchanged. Lycopene reached 64.52 mg/kg in chia oil and 66.41 mg/kg in poppy oil at 10% incorporation. Tomato pomace modified the volatile composition by enhancing tomato-derived aldehydes and esters and reducing heat-derived furans. These results demonstrate the potential of tomato pomace for sustainable production of nutritionally and sensorially improved seed oils.

title: Structure-dependent effects of laccase-mediated phenolic acid incorporation into starch nanoparticles on starch retrogradation
abstract: This study investigated the structure-dependent effects of laccase-mediated incorporation of ferulic acid (FA), caffeic acid (CA), gallic acid (GA), and tannic acid (TA) into starch nanoparticles (SNPs) on the retrogradation of maize starch (MS). Phenolic acid (PA) incorporation increased with increasing structural complexity, with TA-SNPs exhibiting the highest phenolic loading (128.48 mg/g). Spectroscopic and X-ray diffraction analyses supported PA incorporation and revealed disruption of the original A-type crystalline structure of SNPs, limited formation of V-type inclusion-like structures, and reduced relative crystallinity. In MS gels, PA-SNPs inhibited both short- and long-term retrogradation, with inhibitory efficacy positively correlated with the number of phenolic hydroxyl groups. Compared with MS gel, MS/PA-SNP gels exhibited lower retrogradation-associated enzymatic resistance and reduced hardness after 21 days of storage. These findings demonstrate that the PA molecular structure shapes the physicochemical properties of SNPs, thereby modulating their ability to inhibit starch reassociation and recrystallization during storage.

title: Dialdehyde cellulose-l-lysine Schiff base conjugate synergistically modulates water status, texture, and antibacterial activity of wheat gluten
abstract: To address poor water retention, texture deterioration, and microbial contamination in gluten-based products, a dialdehyde cellulose-l-lysine Schiff base conjugate (DAC-Lys) was synthesized. DAC-Lys-2 (12 h oxidation, 4-6% addition) densified the network with more regularly distributed pores, increased tightly bound water from 6.93% to 8.32% and reduced mobile water from 82.91% to 80.75%, indicating significantly restricted water mobility. Baked gluten containing 6% DAC-Lys-2 exhibited 44.61% lower hardness and 39.13% higher elastic force than unmodified gluten, a "soft yet elastic" texture. DAC-Lys-2 showed antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli (12.42 ± 0.24 mm), Staphylococcus aureus (12.49 ± 0.17 mm), Salmonella (12.26 ± 0.09 mm), and Bacillus cereus (14.36 ± 0.46 mm), with free aldehyde residues (50.03-67.36 μg/g). The mechanism involves Schiff base crosslinking and hydrogen bonding that pre-structure the gluten network and directionally convert mobile water to bound water. DAC-Lys has been demonstrated to be a promising modifier for gluten-based foods, providing synergistic improvements in water retention, texture, and antibacterial functionality.

title: Integrative quality evaluation of tea raw material uniformity using sensory analysis, metabolomics, GC–O, and principal component analysis
abstract: Although mechanical harvesting reduces labor costs, non-selective picking decreases fresh leaf uniformity, increasing the difficulty of sorting and high-value processing. This study used sensory evaluation, metabolomics, gas chromatography-olfactometry, and principal component analysis (PCA) to investigate the effects of raw material uniformity (U1 ~ U5) on tea flavor. The results show that high uniformity materials (U1 ~ U2) have floral and green aromas, with a fresh and full-bodied taste, while low uniformity materials (U4 ~ U5) are enriched with mature woody, roasted, sweet aromas and sweetness. Bitterness, astringency, and umami decrease as uniformity declines. A total of 23 key flavor compounds were identified, and their content changes were mainly related to differences in leaf maturity and drying time. In addition, PCA revealed distinct distribution patterns between U1 ~ U3 and U4 ~ U5, supporting "one bud with three leaves" as the sorting threshold between medium- and low-grade mechanically harvested fresh tea leaves.

title: Mitigation of EGCG-induced bitterness and astringency by soy protein hydrolysates: an integrated in silico and electronic tongue study
abstract: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), one of the most abundant polyphenols in tea, is challenging to utilize due to its strong astringency and bitterness. The current study used an in silico and experimental strategy to determine whether soy protein isolate hydrolysates (SPIHs) could modulate the perception attribute associated with EGCG. Firstly, an in-silico digest of the soy protein with subsequent molecular docking showed that several peptides generated had significant affinity to EGCG. Using an E-tongue, these hypotheses were confirmed: the addition of SPIHs did result in a reduction in bitterness and astringency. This effect was particularly noted with the EGCG mixture preparations P1.3 and P2.5 (0.5). Physicochemical characterization data (particle size, FTIR, UV-vis, fluorescence, and CD) have equally validated the potential for forming stable complexes of SPIH with EGCG. Overall, SPIHs are able to reduce the bitterness and astringency of EGCG, making way for protein-fortified functional tea drinks with more pleasant attributes.

title: Early-warning evaluation of pasteurized milk spoilage during storage and distribution
abstract: Hidden temperature deviations within the cold chain are a major contributor to global food waste, yet existing quality assurance methods predominantly rely on lagging indicators that fail to capture early-stage spoilage. Here, we integrate high-resolution foodomics with machine learning approaches to identify a biomarker for pasteurized milk freshness: N-((4-amino-2-methylpyrimidin-5-yl)methyl)formamide (AMF). Through structural elucidation and isotope tracing, we revealed that AMF is formed via a specific hydrolytic ring-opening pathway of thiamine. Importantly, perturbation experiments using sterile UHT milk, NaOH, and formic acid further suggested that alkaline microenvironments and spoilage-associated biochemical activity may facilitate this transformation. Validated on datasets from diverse geographic regions and processing methods, we established a quantitative spoilage warning threshold at 1.7 ng/mL, and the early-warning sensitivity allows detection of transient high-temperature exposures as brief as 6 h. This promising molecular indicator enables a shift in milk quality control from retrospective rejection to prospective prevention, acting as an indicator of thermal history and allowing precise, early detection of temperature abuse in complex dairy supply chains.

title: Integrated metabolomic fingerprinting and machine learning for the discrimination of geographical origin and regional flavor profile differences of Zanthoxylum bungeanum
Maillard conjugate-engineered nanostructured lipid carriers for enhancing bioaccessibility of cinnamaldehyde and pyrroloquinoline quinone by synchronized co-delivery
abstract: Cinnamaldehyde (CA) and pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ) face co-delivery challenges due to instability, poor solubility, and conflicting hydrophilic-hydrophobic properties. A dual bioactive-loaded nanostructured lipid carrier (NLC) was developed using a whey protein isolate-chia seed polysaccharide (WPI-CSP) Maillard conjugate as a stabilizer. The optimal NLC displayed spherical morphology, achieving encapsulation efficiencies of 89% for CA and 83% for PQQ at a 2:1 mass ratio. Lyophilized CA/PQQ@NLC exhibited high bioactive retention (86%) over 60 days at 4 °C. NLC encapsulation significantly enhanced UV-C photostability, as the half-life of CA and PQQ increased. In vitro digestion presented pH-responsive biphasic release (<10% in gastric fluid and efficient intestinal release), with cumulative release of 84% for CA and 88% for PQQ. NLC encapsulation enhanced the in vitro bioaccessibility by 7.3-fold for CA and 1.6-fold for PQQ. Zebrafish toxicity assays confirmed the preliminary biocompatibility of CA/PQQ@NLC, highlighting it as a promising oral delivery system for dual bioactives.

title: IS-embedded core–shell SERS for precision pesticide quantification in foods: a review
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) offers sensitive molecular fingerprinting for rapid pesticide-residue detection, but quantitative reliability remains limited by hot-spot heterogeneity, substrate variation, analyte adsorption, and complex food matrices. Internal-standard (IS)-embedded core-shell nanostructures enable ratiometric correction of common-mode fluctuations, while their shells can regulate analyte transport, resist fouling, sieve molecules, and promote selective enrichment. This review summarizes recent advances in IS-embedded core-shell SERS, with particular attention to IS location, shell chemistry, local electromagnetic fields, and mass transport. Reported systems are further evaluated in terms of limit of quantification (LOQ), recovery, precision, matrix effects, reproducibility, uncertainty, regulatory relevance, and comparison with established reference methods. Current evidence positions IS-SERS as a calibratable platform for rapid screening and near-site quantification, complementary to LC-MS/MS or GC-MS/MS confirmation. Future priorities include MRL-relevant and validated LOQ, interbatch and interinstrument reproducibility, storage stability, and scalable manufacturing.

title: Spectroscopic evidence supporting micelle-mediated molecular transfer in oil-in-water emulsions revealed by Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET)
abstract: Mass transport in oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions has been gaining attention. Among the proposed mechanisms, micelle-mediated transfer has emerged as a key pathway, but direct evidence remains limited. In this study, Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) was employed to investigate mass transport through emulsifier micelles in O/W emulsions. FRET between fluorescein (FL)-loaded and octadecyl rhodamine B chloride (RB)-loaded emulsions was confirmed by decreased FL emission (524 nm) and increased RB emission (582 nm) once mixed. To further elucidate the action of micelles, FL-loaded emulsions were mixed with RB-loaded cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) solutions below and above the critical micelle concentration (CMC) of CTAB. Results showed a simultaneous decrease in relative FL emission (up to 48.85%) and increase in RB emission (up to 1402.12%) with increasing CTAB concentration, confirming FRET. However, only limited changes were observed above the CMC. These spectroscopic findings support the contribution of micelles to molecular transfer in emulsions.

title: Detection of residues of chlorine-containing pesticides on tomato fruits by machine learning evaluation of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy data
abstract: In this pilot analytical study, we propose the machine learning evaluation of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) data as a new, fast screening methodology for the detection of pesticides on tomato fruits. Five pesticides (acetamiprid, chlorpyrifos, λ-cyhalothrin, tebuconazole, tefluthrin) at three concentration levels down to 0.01 m/v% corresponding to their real application (spraying) concentrations were tested on fully ripe fruits of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum cv. Money maker). Direct (on the fruit peel) and indirect (sampling-based) analytical approaches were both tested. Linear discriminant analysis and classification tree machine learners, coupled with data normalization were applied to the LIBS data collected.
