It was found that the proposed method can provide a fairly robust classification with up to about 90% balanced accuracy. The results indicate that LIBS-based qualitative discrimination analysis is a promising candidate for further development towards the detection of hazardous pesticide residues.

title: Microencapsulated silymarin nanoparticles prepared by atomized instantaneous solidification: Structural characterization, molecular interactions, improved solubility and bioavailability
abstract: To enhance the solubility and bioavailability of silymarin (SLM), SLM nanoparticles (SLM-NP) were prepared using sunflower phospholipid (SPL), Tween 80, and sodium alginate (SA); subsequently, redispersible microencapsulated silymarin nanoparticles (SLM-NMP) were obtained via atomized instantaneous solidification. SLM-NMP retained 97.86 ± 0.33% and 99.15 ± 0.27% of SLM after storage at 60 °C for 24 h followed by storage at room temperature for 28 days, with no significant changes in particle size and PDI during the 28-day period. Characterizations confirmed amorphous SLM encapsulation and rounded shape of SLM-NMP. Molecular dynamics simulations aligned with experimental results. In vitro, SLM-NMP achieved >80% cumulative release rate within 0.5 h in pH 1.2, 4.0 and 6.8, significantly outperforming SLM and silymarin liposome (SLM-LIP). In vivo studies confirmed enhanced bioavailability and safety of SLM-NMP. This approach combined solubilizers and electrolytes in NP offering a promising strategy for hydrophobic bioactives delivery, with microencapsulation further improving stability.

title: Degradation patterns and risks quantification of chlorfluazuron, chlorfenapyr and metabolite in chives by multi-model comparison
abstract: Elucidating the degradation fate and risk characteristics of chlorfluazuron, chlorfenapyr, and its metabolite in chives in both open-field and greenhouse cultivations is crucial for safeguarding the ecosystem and humans from their hazardous effects. This study shows that the dissipation pattern and concentration variations of these pesticides are governed by multiple factors, including cultivation patterns and climatic conditions. A biexponential model revealed that the half-lives of chlorfluazuron and chlorfenapyr were 5.4-11.8 d and 3.3-11.6 d in chives, respectively, as indicated by lower akaike information criterion values and the residual mass closer to zero. Additionally, tralopyril was detected at concentrations up to 0.02 mg/kg after chlorfenapyr application. A novel risk assessment framework was developed by integrating deterministic modeling with probabilistic Monte Carlo simulation. The deterministic model showed that the chronic dietary risks of chlorfluazuron and chlorfenapyr in chives were 4.731%-12.969% and 0.523%-1.434%, respectively. Children aged 2-6 years were identified as the most significantly exposed group, with risk levels approximately 1.4-1.8 times higher than other groups. Furthermore, rural residents exhibited markedly greater exposure risk than urban counterparts. Notably, chlorfluazuron accounted for 90.04% of the cumulative risk, thereby being prioritized in risk management strategies. Although the exposure risks were acceptable, the potential health hazards of chlorfluazuron to vulnerable groups should be taken into account, given its widespread presence and high contribution to combined risks.

title: A carbon dot-hydrogel-based dual-response platform for adsorption, detection of Cr(VI) and NO2−, and monitoring and preservation of aquatic products‐
abstract: Hexavalent chromium Cr(VI) and nitrite (NO 2 - ) pose threats to environmental safety and food quality; therefore, their rapid and sensitive detection is critical. In this study, a multifunctional sensor based on nitrogen‑phosphorus co-doped carbon quantum dots/agarose-gelatin hydrogel (NPAH) was developed. NPAH exhibits excellent mechanical and optical properties and permits the separate fluorescence detection of Cr(VI) and NO 2 - under their respective experimental conditions. It features a linear range for Cr(VI) of 10-100 μM, a detection limit of 0.21 μM, high selectivity, portability, visual detection, and a maximum Cr(VI) adsorption capacity of 213.29 mg/g. It can effectively detect Cr(VI) in real water and is used to monitor the spoilage of aquatic products, outperforming pure N-CD and P-CD solutions and exhibiting higher recovery rates.

title: Structural characteristics, processing stability, and antioxidant activity of peptide-zinc chelates from pumpkin seed protein hydrolysates
abstract: Protein-rich pumpkin seed meal is often discarded or used as low-value feed, wasting resources. To valorize protein resources from this by-product, five types of novel pumpkin seed peptide‑zinc chelates (PSPHs-Zn) were synthesized in this study. The zinc chelating capacity, structural characteristics, processing stability, and antioxidant activity of PSPHs-Zn were systematically compared. Among them, PSPH-Aci (from acidic protease hydrolysate) exhibited the highest zinc chelating capacity (134.88 mg/g), an antioxidant amino acid (Trp, Arg, etc.) content of 28.38%, and a DPPH radical scavenging rate of 72.57%. This chelate retained over 90% of zinc after pasteurization and showed little change in zinc retention under high salt conditions (≤ 6% NaCl) and at pH 3.0-6.0. Moreover, the thermal stability of PSPH-Pro-Zn (zinc chelate from composite protease hydrolysate) (ΔH = -135.42 J/g) was superior to that of the conventional supplement zinc glycinate. These findings offer a viable strategy to valorize pumpkin seed meal as a by-product.

title: Comparative influence of cellulose nanofiber variants on the structural properties and digestion of traditional tofu
abstract: This study evaluated the effects of different cellulose nanofibers (CNF) on the structure and digestion of MgCl 2 - and CaSO 4 -coagulated tofu. CNF exhibited rod-like fibrous structures. The mean particle sizes for Polygonati rhizoma CNF (P-CNF), okara CNF (O-CNF), and TEMPO-oxidized okara CNF (TO-CNF) were 538-781 nm. O-CNF incorporation led to a 17%-32% increase in tofu yield. P-CNF addition resulted in no significant difference. This aligns with the increased semi-bound water within the gel network. Microstructure indicated that CNF reduced aggregation, with O-CNF producing a continuous microstructure with micropores. Alterations in the β-sheet suggest interactions between amino acid residues, contributing to a more ordered conformation. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed a direct interaction between soy protein and O-CNF, stabilized by approximately 10 hydrogen bonds. The hydrolysis rates of tofu incorporating O-CNF or TO-CNF were lower than those observed for P-CNF tofu. These findings support the development of dietary fiber-reinforced tofu.

title: Untargeted metabolomics integrated with explainable machine learning reveals processing biomarkers for camellia oil adulteration detection
Identification of key floral odorants in Jiang-flavor baijiu via a source-backtracking assisted flavor integration approach
abstract: Floral aroma is a hallmark of premium Jiang-flavor Baijiu, yet its molecular foundation remains unclear. We observed that perceived floral intensity does not always correlate with the absolute concentrations of typical odorants, indicating a sensory-chemical discrepancy. To decode this complexity, aroma-active compounds were systematically characterized using GC-O-MS, AEDA and GC × GC-TOF-MS. Via a source-backtracking-assisted flavor integration approach, we constructed an "Extended Floral Aroma" model. Aroma recombination experiments showed that adding the six-component non-floral mixture increased floral intensity compared with the model containing floral odorants alone. Feller's additive model analysis supported synergistic enhancement at the mixture level. The omission tests revealed a layered contribution within the EFA model: 11 compounds (including both floral and non-floral compounds) function as primary drivers for aroma integrity. This study proposes a conceptual compositional principle for deconstructing complex aromas and provides a scientific basis for flavor regulation in traditional spirits.

title: Acid–thermal responses and co-gel performance of konjac flours from Amorphophallus bulbifer and Amorphophallus rivieri in κ-carrageenan systems
Ultrasound-assisted glycation reduces the IgE cross-reactivity of yellow mealworm protein with conformational modification
abstract: Edible insects, particularly yellow mealworm (Tenebrio molitor) protein (YMP), are promising sustainable protein sources, yet their cross-reactivity with allergens from other arthropods (e.g., crustaceans and house dust mites) raises safety concerns. This study investigated the effects of ultrasound-assisted glycation with xylo-oligosaccharides (XOS) on the IgE reactivity and conformational structures of YMP. Using serum pools from crustacean-allergic, dust mite-allergic, and co-allergic individuals, we showed that ultrasound-assisted glycation reduced the cross-reactive IgE-binding capacity of YMP by up to 53.9% and suppressed basophilic degranulation, with glycation as the main contributor and ultrasound providing an additional benefit in the crustacean-allergic pool. Structural analyses showed modest secondary structure changes, including increased α-helix and decreased random coil contents, and reduced surface hydrophobicity. Correlation analysis indicated these parameters were associated with IgE binding. Collectively, ultrasound-assisted glycation reduced YMP IgE cross-reactivity, possibly through conformational changes altering epitope accessibility, offering preliminary insights for insect protein ingredients with reduced allergenicity.

title: Ethanol-alkaline modulation enables mild-temperature egg white protein gelation with tunable rheological and textural properties for vitamin D3 delivery
abstract: Conventional egg white protein (EWP) heat-set gelation requires temperatures above 80 °C, limiting its use as a carrier for heat-labile bioactives. Here, we report that low-concentration ethanol (5-15%, v/v) combined with alkaline pH effectively lowers EWP gelation onset by up to 30 °C, enabling gelation at 50-60 °C and pH-dependent tuning of the gel network. Differential scanning calorimetry confirmed additive thermal destabilization by each factor, with ethanol promoting conformational unfolding and hydrophobic exposure at mild temperatures. At pH 9.3, ethanol progressively increased the storage modulus of EWP gels by 3-6-fold, building a stiffer network. At pH 11.0, despite lower storage modulus, pronounced strain-stiffening under large deformation yielded elevated yield strain and stress. Scanning electron microscopy confirmed distinct network topologies between pH conditions. This dual-factor modulation strategy raised vitamin D 3 encapsulation efficiency to >90% with controlled release during simulated digestion, demonstrating a mild, tunable platform for heat-sensitive bioactive delivery.

title: Unveiling the inhibitory effect of curcumin on phycocyanin glycation, with insights into its application in spirulina biscuits
abstract: Studies on the glycation of phycocyanin (PC) and its inhibition mechanism are scarce. This study aimed to explore the glycation of PC during thermal processing and elucidate the potential inhibitory effect of curcumin (Cur) on this process. The results demonstrated that Cur (1 mg/mL) significantly inhibited the formation of fructosamine (73.9%), dicarbonyl compounds (44.6%-59.3%), and advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) (50.6%). Cur also effectively prevented protein oxidation (>50%) and sulfhydryl depletion (89.8%). Moreover, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) and molecular docking demonstrated the weak binding affinity between Cur and PC. The antiglycation mechanism of Cur mainly relied on trapping active carbonyl intermediates and enhancing antioxidant capacity rather than substantial binding to PC. Furthermore, Cur dose-dependently inhibited the accumulation of AGEs, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural, and dicarbonyl compounds in spirulina biscuits and markedly elevated the antioxidant capacity. These findings offer theoretical insights into the inhibition of AGE formation during the thermal processing of microalgae-based food products.

title: A novel mass-deficit-based method for the rapid determination of diacylglycerols in edible oils
abstract: Diacylglycerols (DAGs) are valued for their nutritional benefits, driving the need for effective quality control. Current chromatographic methods are time-consuming and impractical for routine analysis. Accordingly, we have developed a rapid mass-deficit-based analytical strategy that capitalizes on the inherent structural disparities between DAGs and triacylglycerols, facilitating accurate quantification through selective derivatization and precipitation. Systematic optimization of critical parameters, including sample mass, water bath duration, precipitation separation, and precipitation formation time, yielded a robust and reliable analytical protocol. The method exhibits a wide linear range (0-70% (w/w), R 2 > 0.997), low detection (1.42% w/w) and quantitation (4.75% w/w) limits, and high precision. Accuracy was confirmed by strong agreement with a standard method and recoveries of 96-104%. This approach provides an accurate and efficient alternative for routine DAG analysis in edible oil quality control.

title: Design, characterization and evaluation of gallic acid incorporated carboxymethyl cellulose based composite films for postharvest fruit preservation
abstract: The persistent environmental problems related with petroleum-based packaging has encouraged the development of sustainable active food packaging systems. In this study active biocomposite film composed of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and PVA-PEG graft copolymer (PC) was developed by using solvent casting method. The optimized formulation CMC (3.69%) and PC (7.68%) predicted by the CCD model demonstrated strong model fit with R 2 = 0.9325 (TS) and 0.9492 (WCA). Furthermore, the incorporation of GA (16% w/w), in the film demonstrated improved tensile strength (16.77 MPa), surface hydrophobicity (94.2 o ). Additionally, GA incorporated film exhibited high antioxidant activity (90% DPPH scavenging) and antibacterial efficacy for E. coli and S. aureus. The film demonstrated great potential in preservation of fresh-cut pineapple for 7 days and physical disintegration within 14 days. Overall, these findings highlight the developed film's potential as a sustainable post-harvest packaging solution for fruit shelf-life extension and quality preservation.

title: Longitudinal metabolomic profiling of rosehips from six wild Rosa species grown under common-garden conditions: ripening dynamics, taste-associated metabolites, and antioxidant profile
abstract: H NMR spectroscopy and LC-DAD-ESI-MS/MS characterized rosehip development in six individuals, each representing a wild Rosa species grown under common-garden conditions. Longitudinal NMR profiling was complemented by LC-MS comparison of the initial and final ripening stages. Ripening generally involved increased sugars and organic acids and decreased amino acids, alongside marked individual-specific trajectories. Among-individual variation was also observed in nitrogen-related metabolites, particularly arginine and asparagine. LC-MS revealed differentiated phenolic profiles, with R. gallica showing the widest range of detected flavonoids. OPLS-DA separated immature and mature samples and indicated changes in flavonoid conjugation and ellagic acid-related constituents. Complementary DPPH, TEAC, FRAP, and ORAC assays showed the highest in vitro antioxidant capacity in the investigated R. gallica material. These findings reveal shared ripening-associated changes alongside substantial phytochemical diversity and provide a framework for evaluating wild rosehip materials for food applications.

title: Contrasting grain-quality and starch structure–function responses of double-cropping rice to elevated CO2 and warming
abstract: Rice starch functionality under concurrent elevated CO 2 and warming remains unclear in double-cropping systems. We conducted a two-year field experiment to assess the effects of elevated CO 2 (ECO 2 , +110 μmol mol -1 ) and warming (+1.5 °C) on yield and grain quality. Detailed analyses of starch molecular order, relative crystallinity, thermal properties, and pasting properties were conducted using 2019 samples. The relative importance of the two climate drivers differed between the two cultivar-season systems. In early-season rice, warming was the dominant factor, enhancing molecular order and relative crystallinity; gelatinization enthalpy and setback increased by 39.7% and 40.0%, respectively, while starch swelling was restricted. In late-season rice, ECO 2 was the main driver, increasing gelatinization enthalpy and setback by 11.0% and 23.2%, respectively. These coordinated responses were associated with greater chalkiness and less favorable pasting functionality, indicating a partial decoupling between productivity gains and preservation of starch-based grain quality under experimentally elevated CO 2 and warming.

title: Interfacial behavior of oat protein hydrolysates and its regulatory mechanism on emulsion stability
abstract: This study investigates how enzymatic hydrolysis affects oat protein hydrolysate structure and relates these changes to oil-in-water emulsion stability. Interfacial behavior was characterized by surface tension, adsorption kinetics, interfacial protein content, and adsorption rate. Results show that moderate hydrolysis at enzyme-to-substrate ratios (E/S) of 0.125%-0.50% shifts the droplet size to smaller values, increases ζ-potential, and reduces the Turbiscan stability index (TSI). Optimal stability occurs at E/S of 0.25% and 0.50%, while higher concentrations (E/S ≥ 1.00%) cause aggregation and decreased stability. Interfacial analysis reveals that at 0.25% E/S, oat protein exhibits favorable diffusion and adsorption rates, higher interfacial protein content, and thicker interfacial films. At 0.50% E/S, a significant increase in rearrangement rate, along with decreased protein content and adsorption rate, leads to a more densely rearranged interfacial film. Thus, protein structural characteristics such as molecular weight dictate distinct interfacial layer properties at the oil-water interface.

title: Development and validation of an analytical method for the comprehensive profiling of tryptophan-derived compounds in pistachio (Pistacia vera L.)
Integrated chemical profiling for honey authentication and origin discrimination
abstract: This study presents an integrative analytical approach for honey authentication by combining physico-chemical parameters, stable carbon isotope ratios, and detailed profiles of sugars and organic acids to differentiate honeys according to floral origin. The high-performance anion-exchange chromatography with pulsed amperometric detection (HPAEC-PAD) method for sugar analysis was optimized and validated for the simultaneous separation of 9 saccharides within a 35-minute run time. Additionally, nine organic acids were quantified using an optimized ion chromatography method with conductometric detection (IC-CD). Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA)) revealed that minor saccharides (trehalose, raffinose, maltose, erlose, isomaltose), dominant sugars (fructose and glucose) and their ratios, organic acids (citric, malic, succinic, maleic, and isocitric), as well as key physico-chemical parameters (electrical conductivity, free acidity) are critical discriminative markers of botanical origin. Within the pre-screened dataset, the optimized PLS-DA models successfully classified Robinia pseudoacacia and Honeydew honeys with zero misclassification errors (class error = 0.00; R 2 pred > 0.86; RMSEP ≤0.14). Although differentiating closely related floral groups and utilizing multiple analytical platforms can be resource-intensive, this innovative, derivatization-free approach demonstrates strong discriminatory potential. Ultimately, integrating targeted chemical profiling provides a robust proof-of-concept framework for botanical authentication, offering a reliable tool to prevent mislabeling and adulteration of honey.

title: Retraction notice to "Biodegradable film of carboxymethyl cellulose modified with red onion peel powder waste and boron nitride nanoparticles: Investigation of physicochemical properties and release of active substances" [Food Chem. 445 (2024) 138721]
Engineering a smart bionic hydrogel powered by V2C MXene nanozymes for self-driven antibacterial and fruit preservation
abstract: Postharvest decay of fresh fruits, driven by water loss and microbial colonization, remains a critical global challenge. Herein, we engineered a microenvironment-responsive biomimetic hydrogel featuring a physical-chemical dual-defense mechanism for zero-additive fruit preservation. This dynamic polymer network (Poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/cationic chitosan/glycerol) securely anchors two dimension Vanadium carbide (2D V 2 C) MXene nanozymes. Macroscopically, a glycerol-driven hydrogen-bonding network endows the hydrogel with dynamic morphological adaptability, conforming to fruit shrinkage to lock moisture and eliminate bacteria-invading micro-cracks. Microscopically, the V 2 C nanozymes act as an intelligent H 2 O 2 -responsive system, capturing trace endogenous H 2 O 2 from microbial metabolism to trigger localized, lethal reactive oxygen species (ROS) storms without exogenous chemicals. In vivo evaluations on cherries and mandarins demonstrated that the P 90 VC 10 G coating maintained weight loss below 10% and total viable counts below 3.43 Lg CFU/g after 9 days of storage at ambient temperature. This work provides a promising protective strategy for sustainable postharvest management.

title: Differential regulation of flavor metabolism in “Xiahui No. 8” firm-melting peaches and “Yuhua No. 3” soft-melting peaches under low-temperature storage: analysis of sugars, acids, and aroma metabolic pathways
abstract: This study systematically compared the changes in quality, flavor-related metabolites, and their enzyme activities and gene expression levels in 'Xiahui No. 8' (XH) and 'Yuhua No. 3' (YH), during the storage at 4 °C for 35 d. Results showed that XH maintained better storage quality with firmness reduction of 60.6% and retaining 87.9% of initial sucrose content on day 35, and slight chilling injury (CI) symptoms. XH retained stable sugar-acid balance by maintaining high activities, along with strong transcriptional activation of synthesis genes and low basal expression of degradation genes. YH exhibited severe CI, rapid firmness loss (94.7% reduction), and pronounced flavor deterioration, characterized by rapid sucrose degradation (depletion to 70.5% of initial), and extensive loss of volatile aroma compounds. These degradation characteristics in YH were associated with high expression of degradation genes, insufficient activation of synthesis genes. This study provides insights into elucidating flesh texture-flavor molecular mechanisms in peaches.

title: Hierarchy-dependent mechanical reinforcement in gelatin–whey protein composite hydrogels and high internal phase emulsions
abstract: Protein composite hydrogels (PCHs) and high internal phase emulsion gels (HIPEs) are widely used as fat mimetics, yet their reinforcement mechanisms across hierarchical structures remain unclear. Here, gelatin (GEL)-whey protein isolate (WPI) composites were used to systematically compare the effects of thermal treatment, enzymatic cross-linking, and Hofmeister salting-out on PCHs and corresponding HIPEs. Identical compositions and treatments produced distinct structure-mechanics coupling in the two systems. In PCHs, mechanical performance was governed by the continuous GEL network, with WPI acting as a dispersed, particle-like modifier. In contrast, emulsification redistributed proteins between the continuous phase and oil-water interface in HIPEs, forming load-bearing continuous phase networks. Our findings demonstrate that the strengthening behavior of GEL and WPI follows quasi-orthogonal responsibility, attributable to their intrinsic structural differences. This mechanistic insight provides a rational basis for structuring cultured fat scaffolds and fat analogues with tough mechanical properties suitable for practical applications.

title: Bioinspired laccase-like nanozyme with high-density histidine‑copper site for efficient juice clarification in beverage systems
abstract: Residual phenolic compounds in beverages cause turbidity and negatively affect sensory quality. Although natural laccase has been widely used for phenolic oxidation and juice clarification, its industrial application is limited by high cost and poor stability. Herein, a bioinspired nanozyme with histidine‑copper (His-Cu) catalytic centers was developed for efficient laccase-like degradation of phenolic compounds. By changing the acetic acid concentration during synthesis and introducing ligand vacancies into the metal-organic framework, a higher density of His-Cu catalytic centers can be anchored, mimicking the active sites of natural laccases. Remarkably, the catalytic performance strongly depended on the density of His-Cu sites. The optimized nanozyme achieved up to 80% phenolic removal in apple juice with a turbidity reduction of 36.33%, and exhibited broad applicability in orange and tangerine juices, consistently outperforming natural laccase. These results demonstrate that bioinspired nanozyme with a His-Cu site is a sustainable strategy for improving beverage quality and value.

title: Dynamic changes in volatile profiles of fu brick tea during storage and a predictive model for aging year
abstract: This study investigated the dynamic evolution of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in Jingyang Fu brick tea during storage. Using GC-IMS and HS-SPME-GC-MS, we characterized the VOC profiles, identifying 291 volatiles, among which 36 key compounds (including α-ionone, trans-β-ionone, and methyl salicylate) were pinpointed as responsible for the distinctive fungal-floral aroma that intensified with storage time. Sensory evaluation revealed a progressive shift from fresh to mellow fungal and aged characteristics. Key fungal-floral compounds exhibited synchronous variations with processing-derived metallic elements. Based on the identified VOCs, we developed the first predictive model for determining storage year using machine learning (PLSR and SVM). The model achieved a classification accuracy of 0.889 and high regression precision (R 2 > 0.87). This work provides fundamental insights into the aroma evolution of Fu brick tea during aging and offers a robust tool for quality control.

title: The molecular properties and potential interactions with TMC4 of salt taste-enhancing peptides derived from spent hen meat
abstract: Salt taste-enhancing peptides (STEP) are promising alternatives for sodium reduction in food systems. 27 peptides from spent hen hydrolyzates exhibited significant salt taste-enhancing activity (STEA). Dipeptides containing Arg/Asp residues displayed higher STEA, particularly for DE, DR, and AR. Partial least squares regression analysis identified fractional partial positive surface area, charge, and conformational flexibility as important characteristics associated with the activity of STEP. STEA increased with increasing pH, suggesting that the ionic form of peptides may influence their saltiness perception. Molecular simulation analysis of DE, DR, and AR indicated that the potential interactions with TMC4, primarily involving hydrogen-bond and electrostatic interactions with key residues Arg294, Arg580, Arg583, Glu319, and Glu323. Furthermore, density functional theory calculations revealed differences in electrostatic potential distribution among DE, DR, and AR, which may be related to their different interaction patterns with TMC4 and differences in STEA. These results provided insights into the relationships between peptide structure, interaction with TMC4, and STEA, and provided a basis for further experimental investigation of the molecular mechanisms underlying salt taste enhancement of STEP.

title: Cellulose nanofibers enhance the binding of pea protein amyloid fibrils with 2,5-dimethylpyrazine via regulating protein conformation and microstructure
abstract: In this study, the effects of cellulose nanofibers (CNF) on the structural characteristics, physicochemical properties, and aroma-binding performance of pea protein amyloid fibrils (PAFs) toward 2,5-dimethylpyrazine were investigated. Compared with pea protein isolate (PPI), acid-heat fibrillation markedly altered the surface charge, secondary structure, and microstructure of pea protein, thereby increasing the binding ratio toward 2,5-dimethylpyrazine from 8.95% to 16.50%. CNF incorporation further reorganized the PAFs network, improved microstructural compactness, and enhanced the thermal stability of aroma binding. Notably, the binding ratio of the PAFs + CNF composite reached 30.30%, indicating that CNF incorporation markedly enhanced the aroma-binding performance of PAFs. This improvement may be associated with CNF-mediated conformational regulation and local microstructural confinement of PAFs. These findings provide insight into the role of CNF in regulating the structure and aroma-binding behavior of PAFs, offering a potential strategy for designing protein-based composite flavor carriers.

title: UHPLC-HRMS quantitative analysis of monoglycosylated aroma precursors in grape must using factorial design for extraction protocol optimization
abstract: Wine aromas precursors are of utmost importance in the winemaking process, as they release volatile compounds pivotal for wine flavour and taste, after hydrolysis during fermentation. Several analytical methods are present in literature for glycosylated wine aromas, almost limited to identification and characterization, while accurate quantitative data are still difficult to be collected. In this work, we developed a protocol for aroma glycosides quantification in grape musts by UHPLC-ESI-HRMS. Design of Experiment was used to optimize the extraction and pre-concentration method of three classes of glycosylated aromas, as well as the ESI source parameters to increase their ionization efficiency. The performance of the method was validated on synthetic musts in terms of linearity (r 2 > 0.994), precision (RSD ≤ 9%), accuracy, recovery and matrix effect (71–102%). The method was further tested in real samples to quantify aroma precursors in 10 samples of Italian and French musts, highlighting phenolic and aliphatic glycosides as the most abundant classes.

title: Taste-modulating properties of N-fumaryl-L-phenylalanine: Sensory evaluation, enzymatic preparation, and molecular insights
abstract: N-Fumaryl amino acids were explored as taste-modulating molecules by integrating microspecies prediction, virtual screening, synthesis, sensory evaluation, and molecular modeling. pH-dependent microspecies analysis and docking against taste-related receptor/protein models prioritized N-fumaryl-L-phenylalanine (Fum-Phe), which was chemically synthesized and confirmed by NMR and high-resolution mass spectrometry. A commercial enzyme-based route was further established, with FP-G giving an optimized yield of 12.04%. Quantitative descriptive analysis showed that Fum-Phe enhanced umami, saltiness, and sweetness in single-taste model solutions while showing weak intrinsic taste and no significant bitterness enhancement. Time-intensity analysis further demonstrated that Fum-Phe increased peak intensity and prolonged taste persistence in a simulated chicken broth matrix. Docking, electrostatic potential analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested that the carboxylate, amide, and aromatic groups of Fum-Phe contributed to receptor/protein-model-dependent polar and hydrophobic/aromatic contacts. These results identify Fum-Phe as a promising multi-taste modulator and support N-fumaryl amino acids as candidates for flavor-enhancement design.

title: SPME GC–MS-based volatile profiling of three cardamom species via chemometric tools: Uncovering aroma and bioactivity changes following gamma irradiation and autoclaving
Biomass cellulose-supported CuO-based molecularly imprinted photoelectrochemical sensing platform for highly sensitive and selective detection of lincomycin in food
abstract: The presence of lincomycin (LIN) residues in animal-derived foods presents a potential threat to human health. A sensitive photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor was developed for LIN detection using a water bamboo cellulose-supported copper oxide (CuO@WBC) composite as photoactive substrate. CuO particles with visible-light PEC activity were uniformly anchored onto the cellulose framework to form a stable and improved photoactive layer. A molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) with tailored binding sites was further constructed on the electrode surface to achieve selective recognition of LIN. A wide linear detection range spanning 0.1 nM to 100 μM was achieved, and the limit of detection was 36 pM. Selectivity tests demonstrate good anti-interference against food matrix interferents, while control experiments verify the necessity of molecular imprinted cavities for specific LIN recognition. The fabricated MIP-PEC sensor achieves reliable practical detection, offering a novel sensitive and eco-friendly strategy for antibiotic residue assay in food samples.

title: A tailored strategy for 4D-printed surimi gel: modulating myofibrillar protein disulfide bonds via starch and its acetylated derivative to control thermal-driven deformation
abstract: Controlling thermal deformation of 4D printing gels remains a significant challenge for achieving 3D structural stability of printing products. This study focused on the regulation of tapioca starch (TS) and its acetylated derivative (ATS) on thermal deformation (4D) of 3D-printed "crown" models based on surimi inks. The 4D printing images showed that the "crown" underwent a "flowering" deformation during steam heating. The COMSOL simulation revealed that greater thermal deformation on inner side than on outer one of model, resulted from heat and stress accumulation on inner side near the base of model. Both TS and ATS (particularly ATS) hindered the thermal deformation degree (from 27.8% to 16.5% and 11.7%), due to the improvement of heat conduction uniformity as evidenced by heat maps. Additionally, compared with single surimi gel, the TS/ATS-incorporated surimi gels exhibited higher gel strength and denser structure, suggesting an increasing resistance to thermal deformation. Analysis of protein secondary and tertiary structure and molecular force indicated that TS/ATS promoted the transformation from α-helix into β-sheets, exposing more hydrophobic amino acid residues and forming more disulfide bonds in proteins. In case of ATS, hydrophobic interactions formed between its acetyl groups and the hydrophobic residues of proteins promoted protein to unfold and cross-link, thus suppressing moisture evaporation and thermal deformation. Overall, disulfide bond promoted by starch was the key for regulating network strength, and further thermal deformation of surimi gel. This study offered a new insight into regulating the thermal deformation of 4D-printed products via molecular forces by incorporating starch materials.

title: Polysaccharide structure influences the functional and allergenic properties of β-lactoglobulin conjugates: A comparative study of inulin, chitosan oligosaccharides and yeast β-glucan
abstract: This study investigated the heat-induced glycosylation of β-lactoglobulin (BLG) with inulin (BLG-I), chitosan oligosaccharides (BLG-C), and yeast β-glucan (BLG-G) to elucidate structure-function relationships. BLG-C underwent the most pronounced structural rearrangement, with α-helix increasing from 25.1% to 38.7% and β-sheet decreasing from 41.6% to 21.8%. All conjugates exhibited enhanced thermal stability and solubility, with BLG-G reaching 36.9% solubility. BLG-C showed the lowest zeta potential (-2.6 mV) and strongest antioxidant activity (DPPH scavenging: 65.2%; FRAP value: 640.3 μM/AAE, 3 mg/mL). Mass spectrometry revealed distinct glycosylation patterns: high-density multi-site coverage for BLG-I, electrostatic-driven C-terminal anchoring for BLG-C, and branch-induced network modifications targeting lysine clusters for BLG-G. Glycosylation significantly altered volatile profiles, enriching hexanal and acetone. In RBL-2H3 cells, all conjugates reduced IgE, histamine, and β-hexosaminidase release, suppressed Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13), and upregulated IL-10, with BLG-G exhibiting the strongest immunomodulatory effects.

title: Evaluation of the preservation of strawberries by exopolysaccharides composites loaded with g-C₃N₄ and Ag
abstract: This study investigated a novel exopolysaccharide-graphitic carbon nitride‑silver (EPS-C 3 N 4 -Ag) composite antibacterial material for its potential application in strawberry preservation. The composite showed good in vitro cytocompatibility and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity. Silver migration analysis indicated limited Ag transfer from the coating to strawberry tissues during storage, supporting its potential safety for direct-contact fruit preservation. When applied to strawberries stored at room temperature, the EPS-C 3 N 4 -Ag composite delayed quality deterioration by reducing weight loss rate, pH, spoilage rate, total bacterial count, and malondialdehyde (MDA) accumulation, while maintaining vitamin C (Vc), soluble solids content (SSC), and titratable acid content. Microbial community analysis revealed that EPS-C₃N₄-Ag inhibited spoilage fungi such as Colletotrichum spp. (anthracnose) and Botrytis cinerea (gray mold), and reduced pathogenic bacteria such as Pantoea, Pseudomonas, and Erwinia. These findings support EPS-C₃N₄-Ag as a promising preservation coating, providing both new material options and a theoretical foundation for developing advanced preservation technologies for perishable fruits and vegetables.

title: Multi-scale interactions in whey protein-dual polyphenol complexes: Structure characterization, interfacial behavior, and antioxidant activity
abstract: While individual polyphenol-whey protein isolate (WPI) interactions are partially understood, how dual-polyphenols regulate WPI colloidal properties remains unclear. This study elucidated the combined interaction of resveratrol (RES) and epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) with WPI. RES-EGCG bind to WPI via hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces. Multi-spectroscopy showed that EGCG in the dual-polyphenol complex reduced α-helix and increased β-sheet. The ternary complex, prepared at an initial RES:EGCG molar ratio of 1:1, showed optimal interfacial and antioxidant performance. Lipid hydroperoxide (ROOH) formation and decomposition kinetics in emulsions showed that RES-EGCG jointly controlled lipid oxidation: suppressing ROOH formation and minimizing its decomposition. Quantum chemical calculations indicated that the ternary complex exhibited a smaller HOMO-LUMO gap, suggesting enhanced electron-transfer tendency. Correlation analysis linked α-helix to interfacial activity (r = 0.74-0.93) and β-sheet to antioxidant activity (r = 0.71-0.90). This work clarifies the combined interaction and provides a strategy for designing complex WPI-based colloidal ingredients.

title: Mechanistic insights into lipid-driven structural evolution of cod protein soft gels: From interfacial reconstruction to protein conformational migration
abstract: Lipids can modify the texture of protein-based foods, but how the type of lipid added regulates protein conformation and gel-network formation through interfacial reconstruction remains unclear. Therefore, this study compared the effects of incorporating egg white microgel-stabilized high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) or soybean oil into cod protein soft gels prepared by high-pressure homogenization. The aim was to clarify texture-regulation mechanisms. Both systems, but particularly soybean oil, increased hardness, and promoted disulfide bonding while weakening hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Lipid addition enlarged structural units and increased fractal dimensions. HIPEs formed a more complex interfacial structure and elastic interfacial film than soybean oil, as indicated by higher surface fractal. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed cooperative and competitive adsorption among HIPEs components, forming a denser composite interfacial layer (G' > G″). Thus, lipid incorporated determines controls protein conformational migration, network reorganization, and gel texture through distinct interfacial reconstruction pathways.

title: A systematic study on the role of amylose-to-amylopectin ratio in governing starch-amino acids interactions and in vitro digestibility
abstract: This study investigated how the amylose-to-amylopectin ratio and amino acid functional groups modulate starch-amino acid interactions and digestibility. Complexes were characterized by Fourier-transform-infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, solid-state NMR, and molecular docking. High-amylose starch (HAMS) exhibited stronger interactions with amino acids than normal and waxy starches due to its higher amylose content. The incorporation of amino acids enhanced the structural order, crystallinity, and thermal stability of starch, with histidine (His) showing the most pronounced effects, increasing relative crystallinity to 24.87±0.52% and gelatinization enthalpy to 28.33 ± 1.21 J/g for HAMS-His complex. Solid-state NMR and docking confirmed hydrogen bonding as the primary interaction mechanism, with HAMS-His complex displaying the strongest binding affinity (-4.4 kcal·mol -1 ). In vitro digestion revealed that HAMS-His achieved the highest resistant starch content (48.82 ± 0.68%). This study preliminarily explores starch-amino acid interactions, which may offer guidance for low-glycemic-index food development.

title: A dual-mode fluorescence sensing platform based on reversible i-motif switching and FRET for reliable pH detection
abstract: A dual-mode fluorescent sensing platform based on reversible i-motif DNA conformational switching and fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) was developed for pH detection using complementary fluorescence outputs. Two cytosine rich probes, a single stranded turn-on probe and a double stranded turn-off probe, generated complementary fluorescence responses through pH dependent i-motif folding and unfolding. Both probes showed sensitive responses around the i-motif transition region near pH 6.5. The platform was applied to monitor storage associated pH changes in bass fish and minced mutton and to detect urease activity. For urease detection, both modes showed good linearity over 1-4 U/L, with detection limits of 0.02 and 0.11 U/L, respectively. The opposite fluorescence outputs provide complementary evidence for cross-checking pH-related signals, offering potential to improve analytical reliability. However, further validation is needed to establish the effectiveness of this approach in complex food matrices.

title: Surface-engineered magnetic shellac microcapsules as recyclable Pickering interfacial biocatalysts for enzymatic synthesis of partial Acylglycerols
abstract: Enzymatic synthesis of partial acylglycerols from glycerol and free fatty acids is often limited by poor interfacial mass transfer and low product selectivity. Herein, surface-engineered lipase-loaded magnetic microcapsules were fabricated using natural shellac as recyclable Pickering interfacial biocatalysts. Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles imparted magnetic responsiveness, while the hydrophobic/hydrophilic fumed silica ratio tuned surface wettability and interfacial behavior. Results show that optimal surface wettability yielded uniform Pickering emulsion droplets. The optimized sample M5 exhibited 3.26-fold higher apparent activity than Novozym 435. In glycerol-fatty acid esterification, M5 achieved comparable fatty acid conversion to Novozym 435 while significantly suppressing triacylglycerol formation and enhancing partial acylglycerol selectivity, reaching 86.09% total yield. The catalyst retained high activity after six magnetic recycling cycles. This study establishes a wettability-controllable Pickering biocatalysis platform, offering a promising green strategy for selective enzymatic production of functional lipids rich in partial acylglycerols for food and nutraceutical applications.

title: Multifunctional value of table grapes: Advances in nutrition, flavor, health benefits, consumer preferences, and industrial valorization
abstract: Over the past decade, global consumption of table grapes has risen steadily due to their flavor and nutritional value. This critical narrative review evaluates the nutritional composition and bioactive compounds of table grapes. The roles of flavor compounds in sensory perception and consumer acceptance are critically discussed. Global consumer preference trends reveal a decisive shift toward seedless varieties, crisp texture, distinctive aroma profiles, and health-oriented attributes. Intervention studies indicate that regular grape or grape product consumption may positively influence vascular function, metabolic parameters, cognitive performance, gut microbiota composition, and skin photoprotection. However, much of this evidence derives from small, short-term trials using freeze-dried grape powders, juices, or extracts, and long-term population-level validation remains limited. Industrial applications have expanded beyond traditional juices and raisins to include bakery, dairy, and grape seed valorization. This review highlights table grapes as a versatile, multifunctional food and identifies critical knowledge gaps for future research.

title: Formation of heat-stable egg white protein aggregates as emulsifiers for ready-to-drink beverages
abstract: Native egg white protein (EWP) is heat-labile; therefore, it cannot be used as a protein ingredient in oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion based ready-to-drink (RTD) nutraceutical products. This study aimed to manufacture EWP aggregates (EWP-A) with superior heat stability and acceptable emulsification properties. EWP dispersions (4%, w / v ) with different pH levels ranging from 9.5 to 12 were heated at 85 °C for 10 min to 120 min resulting in 24 EWP sols. Thirteen of 24 EWP sols obtained from the heat treatment exhibited excellent heat stability (90 °C for 15 min). Interfacial property analysis showed that EWP-A had poorer interfacial adsorption behavior compared to untreated EWP control (EWP-C). However, EWP-A showed acceptable emulsification properties and the EWP-A emulsions exhibited superior heat stability (90 °C, 30 min). The outcomes of this work may be implemented for processing ready-to-drink beverages using EWP-A as the primary protein and emulsifying ingredient.

title: Molecular and sensory insights into mung bean aroma in mung bean-flavor Baijiu: Key aroma compounds and potential formation pathways
abstract: Mung bean-flavor Baijiu (MBF) incorporates mung bean to develop a distinctive mung bean aroma (MBA), yet its key aroma compounds and formation mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, through aroma extract dilution analysis (AEDA), quantitative measurements, and aroma addition and omission, 22 key aroma compounds were identified that define the flavor profile of MBF. Among these, 2-isopropyl-3-methoxypyrazine, 1,1-diethoxy-3-methylbutane, 1-hexanol, furfural, furfuryl ethyl ether, and dimethyl trisulfide collectively shape the characteristic MBA. Furthermore, integrated analyses of metabolic pathways and raw material composition showed that mung bean contained higher levels of linoleic acid, valine, glycine, leucine, and methionine, which may contribute to formation of six key aroma compounds. Specifically, valine and glycine may be associated with IPMP formation, whereas leucine may contribute to the formation of 1,1-diethoxy-3-methylbutane. These findings establish a molecular basis for MBA and advance the understanding of raw material-driven regulation of characteristic aroma formation.

title: Changes in furfural compounds and the formation pattern of HMF during the processing of Chinese hickory nut (Carya cathayensis Sarg.) kernels
abstract: The furfural formation in thermally processed Chinese hickory nuts was investigated. Four furfural compounds were identified, with high-temperature baking identified as the primary stage of their formation. Single-factor experiments and correlation analysis revealed that both sugar content and processing conditions significantly influenced furfural formation. Among the compounds detected, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) exhibited the highest concentration (22.69 μg/g) and was further investigated using a simulated in vitro system to characterize its formation kinetics and potential formation pathways. Under the tested conditions, rosemary extract (RE) at 0.22 g/kg significantly inhibited HMF formation (p < 0.05) while exerting minimal effects on sensory properties. These findings highlight RE as a potential natural inhibitor of HMF formation in thermally processed Chinese hickory nuts, although further research is required to validate its effectiveness and broader applicability.

title: Roasting-driven transformation of triacylglycerols and trace bioactive components in camellia seed oil: A cascade evolution
abstract: This study investigated the effects of roasting temperature (80-180 °C) and time (30-120 min) on the quality of camellia seed oil, focusing on the thermal behavior of triacylglycerols (TAGs) and the dynamic evolution of trace bioactive compounds (squalene, phytosterols, polyphenols, and α-tocopherol). Results showed that moderate roasting (120-140 °C) largely preserved TAG structural integrity, promoted the release of squalene and phytosterols, and maintained high oil extraction yield, particularly for roasting time of 60 min or less. Intense roasting (≥ 160 °C) induced pronounced TAG polymerization, accompanied by significant degradation of trace bioactive components and substantial accumulation of total polar compounds, free fatty acids, and characteristic aldehydes (nonanal and 2,4-decadienal). Collectively, an optimal temperature window (120-140 °C) with a processing duration of ≤60 min was identified to balance oil yield and nutrient retention. These findings support the application of precision roasting to maximize nutritional retention in camellia seed oil.

title: Synergistic inhibitory mechanism of peptide and β-glucan from oat on α-glucosidase was explored by molecular docking and spectroscopy analyses
abstract: Natural hypoglycemic active substances have attracted extensive attention. A novel hypoglycemic peptide was identified from oat bran. The 50 ) of 531.90 ± 5.23 μg/mL against α-glucosidase. The synergistic α-glucosidase inhibitory effect and mechanism when combined with oat β-glucan were investigated in vitro. The combination of 800 μg/mL RELGGFF and 50 mg/mL oat β-glucan produced the strongest synergistic effect, achieving an enzyme inhibition rate of 71.14 ± 1.52% and a combination index (CI) value of 0.71. Molecular docking and spectral analysis indicated that RELGGFF and oat β-glucan could tightly bind to α-glucosidase and synergistically inhibit its activity by influencing its conformational stability. This study established a theoretical foundation for the synergistic application of RELGGFF and oat β-glucan in the management of type 2 diabetes (T2D).

title: Decoding the characteristic aroma of air-fried potato strips and its evolution patterns during processing
abstract: This study aimed to identify characteristic aroma compounds of air-fried potato strips using molecular sensory science and examine their evolution patterns during processing through the Maillard reaction and lipid oxidation. A total of 53 volatile compounds were identified. Methional, dimethyl disulfide, 2,3-dimethylpyrazine, 2,6-dimethylpyrazine, 3-ethyl-2,5-dimethylpyrazine, nonanal, and phenylacetaldehyde were the major contributors to aroma. Aldehydes and sulfur-containing compounds accumulated with increasing air-frying time, while pyrazines increased during the later stage (10 min). Meanwhile, reducing sugars and free amino acids (methionine, cysteine, glutamic acid, and lysine) were progressively consumed, whereas lipid oxidation products increased markedly. Air-frying for 10-15 min was a critical stage for forming golden-colored potato strips with a rich aroma. This study provides insight into the aroma formation of air-fried potato strips, offering guidance for the aroma regulation and product development.

title: Linking phenolic composition, cultivar and ripening stage to oxidative stability and shelf-life prediction of EVOO using accelerated aging and NIR-based chemometrics modeling
abstract: The reliable prediction of extra virgin olive oil (EVOO) shelf-life remains a challenge for producers and regulators. This study proposes an approach combining accelerated aging with near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy and feature selection to monitor physicochemical and sensory stability. A total of 132 samples from Arbequina, Manzanilla, Hojiblanca, Picual, and Picudo cultivars, harvested at two ripening stages and classified by phenolic content, were stored under accelerated (40 °C, 12 h/day light) and ambient conditions for up to 12 months. Physicochemical, sensory, and spectral data were analyzed using stepwise variable selection (SELECT) and ordinary least squares regression. The models showed high predictive performance for free acidity (R 2 = 0.97), peroxide value (R 2 = 0.95), rancidity (R 2 = 0.94), and fruitiness (R 2 = 0.96). Phenolic-rich oils, particularly early-harvest Picual and Picudo, exhibited greater oxidative stability. The results demonstrate that accelerated aging combined with NIR-based modeling enables rapid, non-destructive, cultivar-specific shelf-life prediction.

title: Oil–water interfacial adsorption and rheology of pea protein isolate nanoparticles in high internal phase pickering emulsions
abstract: This study investigated the interfacial behavior of pea protein isolate nanoparticles (PPINs) at the oil-water interface and their ability to stabilize HIPPEs. Results showed that PPINs alone stabilized HIPPEs containing an internal phase fraction of 80% at concentrations as low as 0.5 wt%. As colloidal particles, PPINs formed interfacial layers whose properties were governed not only by adsorption but also by interfacial packing and rearrangement. Increasing PPIN concentration did not further reduce the equilibrium interfacial tension, but generally promoted interfacial rearrangement and enhanced interfacial elasticity and resistance to large deformation. Lissajous analysis revealed strain softening during extension and strain hardening during compression. Increasing PPIN concentration reduced droplet size, produced denser microstructures, and improved viscosity, viscoelasticity, and storage stability. All HIPPEs retained gel-like behavior after 30 days of storage. These findings deepen our understanding of pea protein particle adsorption at the O/W interface and the rheological implications for HIPPEs applications.

title: Preparation of silkworm pupae protein hydrolysate–curcumin–chitosan nanoparticles and their protective effects on alcohol-induced gastric mucosal injury
Comparison of antioxidant activities and antibacterial properties of polyphenols from tropical fruits based on targeted quantification and molecular docking
abstract: To make high-value use of tropical fruits and by-products, in this study, polyphenols were extracted from four tropical fruits, and the molecular mechanism underlying the difference in activity was revealed by combining targeted quantification and molecular docking technology. UV-Vis and FT-IR verified the structural integrity of the polyphenols. The in vitro activity results indicate that the polyphenol extracts from different sources exhibit different antioxidant and antibacterial activities. The mango peel inhibited Staphylococcus aureus with an MIC of 0.19 mg/mL. Targeted quantification revealed higher polyphenol contents in peels than in flesh: chlorogenic acid was dominant in jackfruit peel, gallic acid was dominant in mango peel. Molecular docking further showed that isoquercitrin targeted the σA subunit of S. aureus RNA polymerase, while chlorogenic acid and neochlorogenic acid bound to Keap1, clarifying the differences in activity. This work reveals the differences in polyphenol profiles and bioactivities between peel and flesh of four tropical fruit by-products.

title: Comparative ganglioside profiling of human milk and six animal milks via UPLC-Q-TOF-MS and UPLC-QQQ-MS/MS
abstract: Gangliosides in mammalian milk are critical for infant neurodevelopment and gut maturation, yet their molecular diversity across populations and lactation stages remains poorly characterized. Using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS and UPLC-QQQ-MS/MS, we profiled GM3 and GD3 in human milk from four Chinese regions (Heilongjiang, Shanxi, Zunyi, Qingdao) across three lactation stages and six animal milks (camel, cow, buffalo, sheep, yak, horse). We identified 26 GM3 and 12 GD3 species in human milk, revealing extensive diversity in fatty acyl chains (C12-C26). Longitudinal analysis showed dramatic remodeling: colostrum exhibited high heterogeneity, while mature milk enriched very-long-chain species (C22:0, C24:0). Geographic comparison identified 25 differential biomarkers, with GD3 most sensitive to regional factors. Strikingly, human milk was qualitatively distinct from all animal milks showing 10-20 fold higher GM3 and unique C22-C24 enrichment, whereas ruminant milks featured shorter-chain (C16:0)-dominant GD3 profiles. These findings provide a benchmark for optimizing infant formula to replicate human milk's functional lipidome.

title: Dual-functional active-indicator biomass-based films based on lignin and cationic guar gum for maintaining and monitoring food freshness
abstract: The application of biomass-based packaging films is often hindered by their single functionality and their poor long-term stability. Herein, a dual-function composite film (CLA-III) was simply solution-cast from sodium lignosulfonate (LS), cationic guar gum (CGG), and alizarin red S (ARS). The film exhibited rapid colorimetric responses to pH buffers and ammonia vapor (0.8 and 0.08 M), with ΔE = 18.14 within 6 min at 0.08 M. It also demonstrated excellent reusability and durability, maintaining consistent chromatic performance after 180 days of storage and three consecutive acid-base cycles. Additionally, the film showed complete biodegradation within 10 days, ensuring environmental safety, while its ARS release kinetics followed a Fickian diffusion mechanism. In practical applications, CLA-III not only effectively extended the shelf-life of strawberries as a fresh-keeping packaging but also served as a reliable, real-time visual indicator for monitoring shrimp spoilage. This work offers a robust and sustainable strategy for intelligent food packaging.

title: Coupled airflow, heat, and moisture transport in static magnetic field assisted pork precooling based on multiphysics simulation analysis
abstract: Static magnetic field (SMF) assisted precooling may improve pork water retention, but its coupled thermal and moisture transfer remains unclear. A multiphysics model coupling airflow, heat transfer, moisture transport, and an empirical SMF dependent correction to liquid water mobility was developed for pork longissimus dorsi. Under 2.5 mT SMF and 95% relative humidity, the predicted time for center temperature to decrease from 25 to 2 °C was 42.50 min, compared with 43.55 ± 2.26 min experimentally, the relative deviation was 2.41%. Core temperature differences between magnetic and non-magnetic conditions remained below 0.5 °C. Drip loss decreased by 45.65%, and the model predicted a 43.60% reduction in total net moisture transfer rate magnitude at 42.50 min. Relative humidity mainly affected surface evaporation, the SMF term reduced internal water mobility. These results indicate that the combined precooling method can effectively enhance the water retention capacity during the pork cooling process.

title: Egg white protein-high-acyl gellan gum composite emulsion gels: Structural design and mechanistic insights for fat substitute in emulsified meat systems
abstract: Emulsified sausages often contain high fat levels, increasing energy density and potential health risks. This study evaluated modified egg white protein (EWP) and high-acyl gellan gum (HAGG) complexes as fat substitutes in emulsified sausages. HAGG promoted EWP-HAGG assembly through hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic association, and local electrostatic contributions, increasing particle size, absolute zeta-potential value, surface hydrophobicity, and emulsifying ability. In emulsion gels, storage modulus exceeded loss modulus across testing, confirming elastic viscoelastic behavior, with thixotropic recovery reaching 93.33%. During gelation, EWP and HAGG formed an interpenetrating network, producing a denser structure with improved texture and water retention. When applied to sausages, the EWP-HAGG emulsion gel improved water-holding capacity, texture, and sensory attributes, especially at 75% pork back-fat replacement. These findings suggest that EWP-HAGG complexes can reduce fat in emulsified meat products while maintaining desirable quality.

title: Effects of storage time on protein structure properties in spicy strips
abstract: This study investigated the hardening mechanism of spicy strips during 180 days of storage. Protein network markers (glutenin macropolymer, free sulfhydryl groups, and sodium dodecyl sulfate-soluble proteins), molecular forces, zeta potential, and moisture distribution, as determined by low-field nuclear magnetic resonance, were analyzed. Hardness increased by 45.2%, whereas the glutenin macropolymer content decreased by only 3.17% (P > 0.05). Oil addition reduced moisture loss by 28.7% and the increase in hardness by 42.3%, with the zeta potential increasing from -2.54 mV to -15.35 mV. These findings demonstrate that protein oxidation is not the primary driver of hardening; rather, moisture migration and starch characteristics are the key targets for quality preservation in starch-protein-oil composite foods.

title: Enterocin-capped CuZn bimetallic nanoparticles as an innovative strategy to control Salmonella in food safety systems
abstract: Salmonella remains one of the leading causes of foodborne infections worldwide, and the increasing dissemination of antimicrobial resistance has intensified the demand for alternative control strategies applicable to food systems. Bacteriocin-mediated green synthesis has emerged as a promising approach for producing multifunctional nanomaterials with antimicrobial potential. In this study, enterocin-capped copper‑zinc bimetallic nanoparticles (Bio-CuZnNPs) were synthesized through a one-pot green approach using the cell-free supernatant of Enterococcus durans MF5 as both reducing and stabilizing agent. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited spherical morphology, negative surface charge, homogeneous size distribution, and prolonged colloidal stability, indicating effective nanoparticle formation and stabilization by bacteriocin-associated biomolecules. Bio-CuZnNPs showed concentration-dependent antimicrobial activity against Salmonella serovars, with MIC values ranging from 0.5 to 32 mg mL −1 and reductions of up to 6 log CFU mL −1 during time-kill assays. The nanoparticles also reduced biofilm formation and induced membrane disruption, as confirmed by fluorescence microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and intracellular leakage assays, suggesting that cell envelope damage is a major mechanism associated with bacterial inactivation. In addition, Bio-CuZnNPs exhibited antioxidant activity and maintained antimicrobial efficacy in food-derived test systems, including coconut water and chicken thawing drip. These findings demonstrate that enterocin-mediated CuZn bimetallic nanoparticles combine structural stability with antimicrobial and antioxidant functionalities, supporting their application as multifunctional nanoplatforms for food preservation and mitigation of foodborne pathogens.

title: Cavitation jet treatment-assisted glycosylation of hemp seed protein: Structural regulation and emulsion stability
abstract: This study employed cavitation jet treatment to facilitate the effective glycosylation of hemp seed protein (HSP) with chitosan (CS). Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%. Consequently, the secondary structure of HSP was reorganized from an ordered state into a more relaxed, disordered configuration. The subsequent covalent attachment of hydrophilic CS chains effectively shielded exposed hydrophobic regions, significantly enhancing the complex's water affinity. Therefore, overall functional performances were markedly improved: solution properties were enhanced through increased solubility and decreased turbidity, while emulsion performance was optimized, evidenced by a superior EAI (55.89 m 2 /g), an extended ESI (84.35 min), and improved apparent viscosity and viscoelasticity. This approach provides a practical strategy for the high-value utilization of hemp by-products.

title: A systematic literature review on resistant starch type 5 (RS5) in rice products: Formation factors, approaches to enhancement and impact on starch digestibility
Ratiometric fluorescence determination of furfural in Chinese baijiu via schiff base formation and glutathione-triggered nucleophilic addition on N-CDs surface
abstract: Reliable methods for furfural (FUR) determination are significance for ensuring the food safety and quality control of Chinese baijiu. In this work, nitrogen-doped carbon dots (N-CDs) were synthesized via a hydrothermal method using p-phenylenediamine (p-PD) as the precursor. Taking advantage of the sequential reaction between the surface amino groups of N-CDs, FUR, and glutathione (GSH), a novel ratiometric fluorescence sensor was constructed. In the presence of FUR and GSH, the sensor exhibits a new blue emission peak at 433 nm, while the intrinsic red emission of N-CDs at 605 nm remains essentially unchanged, thereby generating a self-calibrated ratiometric signal (I 433 /I 605 ). In particularly, this ratio increases linearly with FUR concentration increase, showing good linearity over two ranges (1.0-10 μmol/L and 10-140 μmol/L), with a detection limit as low as 80.75 nmol/L. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the sensing process involves Schiff base formation between FUR and the amino groups on N-CDs, followed by thiol nucleophilic addition of GSH to the C=N bond, these two steps together account for the emergence of the blue fluorescence. The method was successfully applied to the analysis of real baijiu samples, with spike recoveries ranging from 96.6% to 109.9%, and showing good prospects for practical application in alcoholic beverage analysis.

title: Moisture determination in Cyperus esculentus by using visible/near-infrared transmission spectroscopy coupled with sample distribution optimization
abstract: Transmission spectroscopy is being increasingly employed for nondestructive evaluation of agricultural product quality. However, the predictive performance of this technique largely depends on the representativeness of the selected calibration and validation samples. A self-designed transmission spectroscopy device was developed for evaluation of Cyperus esculentus, and a sample selection algorithm was employed to optimize dataset partitioning. The device enabled stable spectral acquisition, while the algorithm effectively reduced sample redundancy and improved model generalization. The experimental results demonstrated that in comparison with conventional methods, the proposed method achieved superior predictive performance for measurement of the moisture content in Cyperus esculentus (coefficient of determination for the calibration set [R c 2 ] = 0.9701, root mean square error of calibration [RMSEC] = 0.0158; coefficient of determination for the validation set [R v 2 ] = 0.9554, root mean square error of validation [RMSEV] = 0.0174). This study highlights the potential of combining device innovation with advanced sample selection strategies to improve spectral modeling in agricultural and food research.

title: Structural rearrangement of β-lactoglobulin induced by preheating and high hydrostatic pressure: Comparative effects on salt–thermal stability
abstract: β-Lactoglobulin (β-lg), the predominant whey protein fraction, is highly susceptible to aggregates under combined salt and thermal stresses, limiting its application in electrolyte-rich beverages. This study compared the preheating and high hydrostatic pressure (HHP) on improving the thermal stability of β-lg in systems containing NaCl and CaCl 2 . Both treatments may modify β-lg, characterized by enhanced sulfhydryl oxidation, disulfide bond formation, carboxyl group exposure, and surface charge. The absolute ζ-potential increased from 17.3 to 20.3 mV after HHP at 600 MPa and to 21.9 mV after preheating at 120 °C, accompanied by decreases in sulfhydryl content from 48.2 to 36.0 and 19.0 μmol/g protein, respectively. These properties increased the thermal stability of β-lg and enhanced its resistance to ion-promoted aggregation. This work provided mechanistic insights into the regulation of salt and heat-induced aggregation of β-lg and offered a clean-label strategy to improve protein stability in electrolyte-rich beverage formulations.

title: Feeding substrate and extraction technique-dependent variations in Tenebrio molitor larval oil and protein composition
abstract: Interest in insect-based foods reflects the need for sustainable sources of lipids and proteins. However, the extent to which feeding substrate and extraction technique shape insect-derived products remains insufficiently understood. Here, mealworm larvae reared on wheat bran and bran supplemented with pumpkin or sunflower seed pressed cakes were subjected to Soxhlet and supercritical fluid extractions. The results revealed that extraction significantly influenced abundance of carotenoids, phenolics, N-acyl amino acids, monoacylglycerols, and glycerophospholipids as well as in vitro antioxidant activity and peroxide value. On the other hand, both feeding and extraction influenced protein fractions. Contrary, oil yield (20.0-25.7%), linoleic acid, and in vitro protein digestibility were primarily affected by variations in feeding substrate. Overall, the findings demonstrate that the composition and quality of mealworm-derived products are governed by the combined effects of larval feed and extraction, providing valuable insights for the development of insect-based ingredients with tailored nutritional and functional properties.

title: Differential sensitivity of myofibrillar proteins from Litopenaeus vannamei and Parapenaeopsis hardwickii to long-term frozen storage and freeze-thaw cycles: structural destabilization and functional deterioration mechanisms
abstract: This study compared the structural and functional responses of myofibrillar proteins (MPs) from Litopenaeus vannamei (LV, farmed species) and Parapenaeopsis hardwickii (PW, wild species) to long-term frozen storage (-20 °C, FG) and freeze-thaw cycles (FC), aiming to reveal species-specific freezing sensitivity mechanisms and guide differentiated preservation strategies. Results indicated that FC induced more severe damage than FG, leading to greater oxidation (PW: hydrophobicity +29.12%, carbonyl +2.53 nmol/mg), structural unfolding (LV: α-helix -4.96/-5.21%, β-sheet +2.82/+6.93% in FG/FC; PW: α-helix -7.10/-8.17%, β-sheet +8.15/+9.27%), aggregation, and loss of solubility and emulsifying functionality. PW MPs demonstrated higher freezing sensitivity compared to LV MPs, characterized by less stable secondary/tertiary structures, faster oxidation and aggregation, and consequently a more pronounced decline in functional properties. These findings not only clarify the molecular damage pathways of shrimp MPs under frozen stress but also provide actionable guidance for industrial preservation, facilitating the quality maintenance of different shrimp products.

title: Corrigendum to “Design of metastable peanut protein–polyphenol complex particles for tunable flow, interfacial, and gelation properties” [Food Chem. 525 (2026) 150611]
Editorial Board
Protein composition governs soy yogurt gelation: Role of relative proportions of 7S and 11S globulins
abstract: This study systematically investigated the soy protein composition (i.e., the relative proportions of 7S and 11S globulins) and soy yogurt gelation. Molecular dynamics simulations predicted that 11S-11S complexes had the strongest binding at pH 4.6, while 7S-7S interactions exposed more hydrophobic regions. These findings were consistent with intermolecular force analyses in soy yogurt. At low 7S proportion ( 4,3 > 30 μm), maintaining high water retention but reducing uniformity and surface smoothness. Principal component analysis confirmed that gel properties of soy yogurt were primarily governed by protein composition via modulation of intermolecular interactions, independent of pH.

title: Dy-MOF-based electrochemiluminescence probe regulated by ACQ inhibition and Ti2AlC conductivity for targeted detection of sulfadiazine
abstract: Sulfadiazine (SDZ) residues in animal-derived foods posed a potential risk to human health. We constructed a molecularly imprinted electrochemiluminescence sensor (MIECLS) for selective detection of SDZ based on the framework confinement effect of a dysprosium-based metal-organic framework (Dy-MOF) luminophore and the electron transfer acceleration effect of Ti 2 AlC. A Dy-MOF with eight-coordinate Dy 3+ centers was synthesized under microwave assisted coordination between Dy 3+ and 9,10-di(p-carboxyphenyl)anthracene (DPA). The rigid Dy-MOF framework suppressed π-π stacking by spatially isolating DPA ligands and reduced nonradiative relaxation by restricting intramolecular motion of DPA, thereby mitigating aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ). Ti 2 AlC suppressed Dy-MOF aggregation via electrostatic interactions and facilitated electron transfer through its good conductivity, thereby enhancing ECL intensity. By employing molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) as specific recognition elements, the developed MIECLS exhibited linear range of 1-500,000 nmol/L with a limit of detection of 0.552 nmol/L, providing a promising strategy for rapid food safety monitoring.

title: Country and varietal influences on the nutritional quality and protein digestibility-corrected amino acid scores of groundnuts across six countries
Screening of potential estrogen disruptors of food additives based on a framework for predicting estrogenic activity combined with bioassays
Sequential ultrasound-assisted enzymatic extraction optimization, partial purification, and characterization of proteins from red seaweed (Gracilaria corticata)
abstract: Gracilaria corticata (GC; protein: 12.20%) has potential as an alternative protein source. However, conventional extraction resulted in low protein yield (PY). Moreover, partial purification of extracted proteins is limited. Therefore, this study focuses on optimizing the sequential ultrasound-assisted enzymatic conditions to improve PY, followed by partial purification and characterization. The maximum PY (33.69%) was obtained at 4.4% cellulase concentration, 2.7 h time, and 47.0 °C temperature. The ultrasound-assisted enzymatic protein extract (UEPE) contained 70.47% protein, 76.44 mg/100 g iron, and 74.49% in vitro protein digestibility. Q Sepharose Fast Flow chromatography (QFF) yielded four fractions. Fluorescence spectroscopy, sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed chromophores, distinct protein profiles, and secondary structure variations. UEPE and QFF fractions showed essential amino acid contents (32.64-47.71 g/100 g) and bioactivities. Furthermore, UEPE demonstrated high protein solubility (91.69%), emulsifying, and foaming properties across pH 7-12, suggesting its potential as a food protein ingredient.

title: Machine learning-enabled discrimination and key feature identification of functional whey protein ingredients based on multidimensional compositional, physicochemical, and structural properties
abstract: Commercial functional whey protein ingredients are highly heterogeneous, making reliable classification challenging. In this study, 16 commercial whey protein ingredients, including microparticulated (MWP), thermostable (TWP), and gel-forming whey proteins (GWP), were characterized using 41 compositional, physicochemical, functional and structural variables. Eleven machine-learning algorithms were evaluated using repeated nested group-based cross-validation. XGBoost showed the strongest overall performance, achieving a mean accuracy of ~0.972 and a macro-F1 score of ~0.970, while permutation testing supporting above-chance discrimination (p = 0.001). Feature-importance and SHAP analyses consistently identified β-lactoglobulin, α-lactalbumin and secondary-structure-related variables as important contributors to classification. XGBoost retained high classification performance when only four features were retained within each outer training fold, suggesting that fewer measurements could suffice for preliminary classification. Although larger sample sets and further external validation are required before industrial application, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of identifying multivariate signatures associated with predefined functional whey protein classes.

title: Self-assembled particles in tea infusions: Chemical-structural interplay enables enhanced flavor
abstract: Infusion systems contain three distinct phases. While the flavor contributions of the true solution phase are well characterized, the roles of the colloidal and suspended phases remain largely underexplored. Here, particles isolated from tea buds, leaves, and stems by utilizing differences in metabolite abundance despite similar composition exhibited distinct structures and flavor attributes. Stem-derived particles exhibited mild sweetness, whereas bud/leaf-derived particles imparted pronounced bitterness and roughness; the former were porous, irregular, low surface potential, while the latter, enriched in esterified catechins and caffeine, formed larger regular octahedral aggregates. These results indicate that particle composition determines flavor potential, while assembled structures contribute to oral interfacial behavior and sensory expression. Notably, particles accounted for about 20% of the total flavor intensity by comparing sensory scores before and after removal.
