Collectively, this work identifies particles as critical flavor contributors in infusion systems and provides a basis for particle-driven optimization of mouthfeel and aftertaste.

title: Structural characterization and modification of a novel fucosylated heparan sulfate from the pleopods of whelk Volutharpa ampullacea perryi
Structural and functional properties of alkaline protease-treated yeast protein hydrolysates and their application as egg substitutes in pound cake

Mechanisms of flavor quality enhancement in mechanically harvested flake-shaped raw tea materials via light shaking: An integrated analysis of intelligent sensory evaluation, metabolomics, and enzyme activities
abstract: Non-selective mechanical harvesting yields flake-shaped raw tea materials with uneven maturity and poor integrity, thereby constraining the flavor quality of finished tea. This study applied light shaking to improve flavor and used multi-omics to uncover the underlying regulatory mechanisms. The results showed that shaking decreased the ratio of tea polyphenols to total free amino acids by 13.91% and catechin content by 12.73%, while increasing total volatiles by 84.86%. Bitterness, astringency, and green aroma were significantly reduced, whereas umami, floral, fruity, and sweet aromas were markedly enhanced. A total of 60 non-volatile and 90 volatile metabolites were identified, with 21 key compounds driving the flavor profile shift. Mechanistically, shaking, as an abiotic stress, increased phenylalanine and tryptophan levels by 64.07% and 23.16%, respectively, and enhanced the activities of 13 key flavor-related metabolic enzymes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for improving the quality of flake-shaped fresh tea leaves.

title: Permselective-antipathogenic-buffering ternary synergy: A grapefruit-inspired biomimetic pericarp for advanced strawberry preservation
abstract: Inspired by the integrated defense system of grapefruit pericarp, we developed a ternary biomimetic packaging that couples permselective gas regulation, confined antimicrobial activity, and moisture buffering. The trilayer architecture consists of a dense polyamide barrier with selective O 2 /CO 2 permeability (2.7/3.6 Barrer), an in-situ-generated Ag nanoparticle layer for broad-spectrum antimicrobial protection, and a sulfonated polyethersulfone matrix enabling water-vapor modulation (143 g/(m 2 ·h)) and controlled Ag + diffusion ( 2 /high-CO 2 atmosphere (8.4% O 2 , 17.1% CO 2 ), reduced respiration by 65%, and retained ~80% firmness and ~ 85% springiness after 15 days at 4 °C. It inhibited the tested bacterial strains by >86%, preserved chelator-soluble pectin at 1.2-fold control levels, suppressed pectinase activities and minimized malondialdehyde accumulation. This design effectively mimics natural pericarp mechanisms, offering a mechanism-driven strategy for extending the shelf life of perishable fruits.

title: Multichannel chemical fingerprinting and exploratory chemometric analysis for Taiwanese tea traceability
abstract: This study explored a multichannel analytical framework for characterizing chemical differentiation among Taiwanese oolong teas. HPLC-UV, electrochemical detection (ECD), high-resolution ESI-MS/MS, and HILIC-based amino acid profiling were integrated to provide complementary chemical information. ECD contributed selective responses to electroactive constituents, particularly catechin-related compounds, complementing UV and mass-spectrometric signals. Thirty-six secondary metabolite- and amino acid-related features were characterized. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed exploratory group-associated patterns, while quantitative K-means validation supported three clusters. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and Random Forest (RF) were evaluated using Tea-ID-grouped validation to prevent information leakage between duplicate measurements; both correctly classified all nine independent teas in the held-out test subset. Feature-importance analyses indicated contributions from amino acid-, polyphenol-, UV-, and electrochemical-response features. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating detector-specific chemical information for tea characterization, while larger independent cohorts are required to establish its applicability to authentication and traceability.

title: An interpretable machine learning approach for process optimization and characterization of key model-derived parameter effects in sunflower oil diacylglycerol synthesis
abstract: Diacylglycerol (DAG) has potential metabolic and cardiovascular health benefits. An interpretable machine learning framework was developed to predict and optimize enzymatic DAG synthesis from sunflower oil. Among 16 model configurations, XGBoost-GS was numerically top-ranked under repeated exact-condition-grouped cross-validation (overall R 2 = 0.910, RMSE = 2.942 pp., and MAE = 2.175 pp). Through process parameter optimization using differential evolution, the optimal conditions were determined to be 11.53 h, 72.11 °C, 8.29 wt% lipase loading, and a weight ratio of 8.93, with a predicted relative DAG content of 54.22% (ensemble predictive dispersion: 1.06%). Experimental verification at the optimization-selected condition yielded 54.68 ± 0.20% relative DAG content. Interpretation of the final fitted model indicated that time had the highest permutation importance, temperature had the largest averaged perturbation sensitivity, and the time-weight ratio pair had the largest positive pairwise interaction metric. This framework supported model-assisted process optimization within the investigated domain.

title: Constructing restructured jujube using blackened jujube pulp and carrageenan to resolve Peel-induced rough mouthfeel
abstract: Blackened jujube offers improved nutritional value, while its peel-induced coarse mouthfeel limits its broader use in snack-style products. To address this limitation, this study proposes restructuring blackened jujube pulp into self-supporting composite gels using κ-carrageenan (KC). While neither 0.5% KC nor the pulp alone formed a self-supporting gel, composite gels containing 0.5% KC were observed to be self-supporting, indicating that the pulp matrix facilitates gelation at a lower KC level. Increasing KC from 0.5% to 2.5% progressively strengthened the network, increasing hardness from ~2.5 N to 16.7 N, water-holding capacity from 53.45% to 77.01%, and freeze-thaw syneresis from 68.94% to 26.69%, alongside network densification and T₂₂ shortening (75.8 to 37.0 ms). Sensory evaluation also confirmed that restructuring markedly reduced grittiness and improved overall mouthfeel. Overall, this work offers a practical strategy for converting fruit pulps into self-supporting composite gels, thereby enabling blackened jujube products with tunable texture and improved mouthfeel. The authors contributed equally to this work.

title: Identification of a putatively novel heat-induced glyceride derivative in goji berries via thermal processing and structural analysis
abstract: This study compared the effects of three methods tetrahydrofuran extraction (C1), subcritical-fluid extraction (C2), and supercritical carbon dioxide extraction (C3) on the carotenoid profile of Lycium barbarum using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS) coupled with multivariate analysis. C3 showed a higher relative representation of long-chain esterified carotenoids, particularly zeaxanthin dipalmitate (ZDP), though absolute extraction yields were not directly comparable due to differing scales and conditions. Heating a matrix-containing carotenoid extract at 110 °C generated a previously unreported compound, P1 (C₅₉H₁₀₆O₆). P1 was identified as a glyceride derivative formed via oxidative cleavage of the polyene chain followed by skeletal rearrangement. Inverse time-dependent changes in ZDP and P1 were consistent with, but did not establish, a precursor-product relationship. Oxidative cleavage, glycerol incorporation, and skeletal rearrangement are presented as a putative thermo-oxidative pathway. This finding demonstrates that thermal processing of goji berries can drive specific, structure-directed chemical transformations rather than mere degradation.

title: Isothiocyanate-targeted submetabolome characterization in edible Brassicaceae and Moringaceae plants
abstract: Isothiocyanates (ITCs) are widely distributed in Brassicales vegetables and exhibit promising anticancer benefits. However, in-depth mass spectrometric characterization of ITCs remains scarce. Here, we characterized the MS 1 and MS 2 features of five representative ITC standards and established a four-step screening workflow. Twelve free ITCs and seven ITC-derived adducts were captured and tentatively annotated. More importantly, we discovered a previously unreported class of covalent ITC-derived adducts. The sulforaphane-goitrin and iberin-goitrin adducts were structurally justified via matching full exciting energy ramp-MS 3 spectra and chemical synthesis. Nineteen ITC-related compounds were relatively quantified crossing 76 batches of edible plants from 25 Brassicaceae species and one Moringaceae species. Noteworthily, broccoli seeds were found to be a rich source of ITCs. Together, this study revealed a new class of covalent ITC-derived adducts and the distribution patterns of ITCs in edible plants, providing a chemical basis for future anticancer studies and translational studies on ITCs.

title: Iron-mediated assembly of lactoferrin-alginate composites for iron encapsulation and structural stabilization
abstract: Ternary composite systems formed by lactoferrin (LF), sodium alginate (Alg), and Fe(II) were designed to investigate their potential as an iron delivery platform with enhanced protein stability. The ternary LF-Alg-Fe (LAF) composites demonstrated distinct structures depending on the LF to Alg ratio and the Fe(II) concentrations. At an LF to Alg ratio of 8:2 and final Fe concentrations between 20 and 30 mM, the system formed complexes stabilized by electrostatic interactions. Alg-rich formulations formed hydrogels stabilized by Alg-Fe(II) egg-box cross-linking. Rheological analysis and swelling behavior indicated a higher mechanical strength in LF-rich complexes and stronger network integrity in Alg-rich hydrogels. Thermal studies indicated that these ternary systems improved LF stability, evidenced by preserved secondary structure after heating using circular dichroism (CD), and an increased denaturation temperature. In addition, in LF-rich formulations the Fe(II) release in aqueous solution was ~50% while in Alg-rich formulations it was much lower (< 10%).

title: Covalent modification of α-cyclodextrin with L-glutamic acid for synergistic delivery of calcium and vitamin D3: Formation mechanism, stability, and digestion behavior
abstract: Calcium (Ca 2+ ) and vitamin D 3 (VD 3 ) synergistically maintain bone health. However, traditional non-covalent Ca 2+ /VD 3 co-delivery systems, such as emulsions and nanoparticles, can be easily dissociated and released prematurely during digestion because of their reliance on reversible hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions, and other weak forces. This study aimed to develop a stable covalent co-delivery system (α-CD-VD 3 -L-Glu-Ca 2+ , CV-LC) by coupling L-glutamic acid (L-Glu)-Ca 2+ chelate (LC) with α-cyclodextrin (α-CD) encapsulating VD 3 (CV). The CV-LC complex had a monodisperse average particle size of 439.70 nm and a zeta potential of -24.26 mV. Multispectral analysis further confirmed the formation of the covalent co-delivery structure. The CV-LC complex demonstrated excellent physicochemical stability. In vitro digestion experiments revealed synchronized intestinal release of both nutrients, with final release rates of 73.81% for Ca 2+ and 80.39% for VD 3 . These findings provide new insights into the rational design of cyclodextrin-based composite nutrient delivery systems.

title: Development of an efficient β-N-acetylhexosaminidase with elevated transglycosylation activity: A synergy of experimental validation and computational simulations
abstract: In this study, a hydrophobic and substrate-binding amino acid scanning (HSaaS) strategy was applied to enhance the transglycosylation activity of β-N-acetylhexosaminidase (SmNag86) from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, using N-acetyl chitobiose [(GlcNAc) 2 ] as the substrate to produce N-acetyl chitotriose [(GlcNAc) 3 ]. Following three rounds of computational screening, alanine scanning and hydrophobic amino acid saturation mutation, the final positive mutant (SmNag86-S436V) was obtained. The space-time yield and final product concentration of SmNag86-S436V reached 174.0 g/L/h and 29.0 g/L, representing 3.0-fold and 1.5-fold increases, respectively. Concurrently, the hydrolytic k cat /K m value of SmNag86-S436V decreased 3.1-fold, thereby favoring transglycosylation reactions. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that SmNag86-S436V improve catalytic groove hydrophobicity and conformational stability, thereby underpinning the enhanced transglycosylation activity. Density functional theory calculations further confirmed that SmNag86-S436V reduced the activation energy barrier at the rate-limiting step, thereby enhancing its transglycosylation activity. The strategy created a mutant with boosted transglycosylation activity and revealed its mechanism, facilitating food-industry enzyme engineering.

title: Encapsulation of Eriobotrya japonica polyphenols in soybean protein isolate-dextran conjugate nanogels: A strategy to enhance stability and bioactivity
abstract: Loquat defective fruit polyphenols (LDFP) and loquat old leaves polyphenols (LOLP) were encapsulated in soybean protein isolate-dextran conjugate nanogels (SDCNGs) via co-assembly method, with encapsulation efficiencies of 77.10% and 79.81%, and with loading capacities of 26.53% and 33.09%, respectively. FTIR, UV-vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions promoted the encapsulation of polyphenols in SDCNGs. XRD and DSC demonstrated that LDFP-SDCNGs and LOLP-SDCNGs could improve the thermal stability of LDFP and LOLP. Micromorphology revealed that SDCNGs had a typical core-shell structure and good dispersion to protect the polyphenols. After encapsulation, the antioxidant activity, hypoglycemic activity, and environmental stability of LDFP and LOLP were significantly improved. In vitro digestion trial revealed that the polyphenol retention rates of LDFP-SDCNGs and LOLP-SDCNGs reached 63.68% and 66.71%, about 1.24 and 1.56 times that of free polyphenols. Therefore, SDCNGs have the potential to encapsulate polyphenols to develop value-added healthy foods.

title: The effects of L-arginine on the storage stability of low-salt sturgeon surimi gels prepared by microwave heating
abstract: This study investigated the effects of L-arginine (L-Arg) on the storage stability (4 °C) of low-salt (0.3% NaCl) sturgeon surimi gels prepared with microwave heating. Gels with 0-2.0% L-Arg were stored for 35 days. The addition of 2.0% L-Arg inhibited lipid oxidation (thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), 0.38 vs. 0.70 μg MDA/g) and protein degradation (total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), 7.93 vs. 16.57 mg/100 g). Compared with the total viable count (TVC) of 6.03 log CFU/g observed in the control group on day 10, the first sampling point at which the TVC exceeded 6.0 log CFU/g was delayed to day 25 in both C-0.5 A and C-1.0 A groups, and to day 30 in the C-2.0 A group. Furthermore, L-Arg increased pH and promoted a compact gel network, improving water-holding capacity and textural properties. This research provides a theoretical basis and practical reference for improving the storage stability of low-salt protein-based products.

title: Identification of potential regulators of caffeine biosynthesis in shading- and nano‑selenium–treated tea leaves based on integrated bioinformatics and AlphaFold3 analysis
abstract: Caffeine is an important flavor and bioactive compound in tea, yet external stimuli-induced regulatory networks of caffeine biosynthesis remain largely unclear. Our study showed that shading and nano‑selenium (SeNPs) treatments respectively increased caffeine content in tea leaves from 35.96 mg/g to approximately 43 mg/g, whereas their combined treatment exerted a synergistic effect, raising it to 51.12 mg/g. Correlation of transcriptome with caffeine content and treatment factors via WGCNA and Mantel tests identified 4 key gene modules and 64 transcription factors (TFs). To accelerate TF screening, we established a rapid and high-throughput screening strategy by integrating AlphaFold3 with JASPAR motif prediction, resulting in 10 candidate TF-DNA complexes. Subsequent validation in yeast and tobacco systems confirmed that CsTSO1 directly binds to the promoter of CsSAMS. Our study uncovers how shading and SeNPs modulate caffeine biosynthesis in tea plants, and provide an AI-assisted framework for efficient TF screening in plant metabolic network.

title: Decoding condensed tannins in faba bean (Vicia faba L.) seed coats: Tannin structural diversity across spring- and winter-type varieties revealed by UHPLC-DAD-MS/MS and phloroglucinolysis
abstract: The faba bean seed coat represents a polyphenol-rich co-product of legume protein extraction, with tannin levels varying widely among varieties. Residual tannins persist after dehulling and may negatively affect protein techno-functional properties. Gaining insights into tannin structure could help minimize these interactions or, alternatively, exploit them for innovative applications. We discriminated twelve varieties of faba bean (Vicia faba L.) for their seed coat composition and content in condensed tannins. Methanolic extraction and phloroglucinolysis coupled with liquid chromatography and UV-Visible and mass spectrometry detection provided complementary data on faba bean condensed tannins. Phloroglucinolysis enabled their quantification and detailed structural characterization, including the determination of procyanidin and prodelphinidin subunits. Spring-type varieties presented a higher total condensed tannin content (81.7 ± 7.0 g·kg -1 DW), smaller chains (mDP = 9.7 ± 0.8) and lower proportion of prodelphinidin subunits (59.4%) than winter-type varieties (70.8 ± 5.8 g·kg -1 DW, 10.6 ± 0.5, 64.8%, respectively).

title: Characterization of exopolysaccharide/chitosan/TiO2 composite film and its application in preservation of chilled meat
abstract: Biodegradable food packaging films are essential for preserving chilled meat. A novel composite film of exopolysaccharide (EPS) from Pediococcus acidilactici J1, chitosan (CS), and titanium dioxide (TiO 2 ) nanoparticles was developed and evaluated. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed favorable film morphology at 1%TiO₂, whereas higher TiO 2 loading caused particle aggregation. Zeta potential analysis indicated optimal film-forming solution stability at 1%TiO₂. Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction (XRD) provided evidence for TiO 2 incorporation. After 8-day storage at 4 °C, EPS/CS/1%TiO₂-packaged chilled meat exhibited reductions compared with control of 5.52 percentage points in weight loss, 1.96 log CFU/g in total viable count (TVC), 0.59 mg MDA/kg in thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), and 11.18 mg/100 g in total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), respectively. On day 8 of storage, total Ti migration in chilled meat was 0.85 mg/kg. The EPS/CS/1%TiO₂ composite film shows potential for chilled meat packaging.

title: Carbohydrate transformation and gluten immunoreactivity in bread-based amazake: carbohydrate and protein profiling with electronic eye colour analysis
abstract: This study examined the valorisation of stale bread in amazake production. Carbohydrate transformation, gluten degradation and colour development were assessed in products prepared with rice or wheat bread koji. Bread supplementation increased mono- and oligosaccharide concentrations, with wheat bread yielding the highest levels of trehalose, kojibiose, nigerose and isomaltose. Amazake produced with wheat bread koji showed higher levels of free amino acids. Principal component analysis revealed distinct sugar composition patterns. Among bread containing variants, wheat bread koji with rice addition resulted in the lowest gluten levels, remaining close to, but slightly above the low-gluten threshold. Colour analysis differentiated the samples according to bread type and process conditions. Overall, both koji type and saccharification substrate influenced amazake properties across all analysed parameters. Stale bread proved to be a suitable substrate for koji-mediated processing, enabling the production of amazake with enhanced carbohydrate complexity and reduced gluten levels.

title: A novel heteropolysaccharide from Lentinula edodes residue: Structural characterization and anti-inflammatory properties
abstract: In this study, a novel heteropolysaccharide, designated LEHP, was purified from Lentinula edodes residue, and its structure was characterized by modern instrumental analysis methods. The average molecular weight of LEHP was 21.7 kDa and LEHP was composed of (1,2), (1,3)-α-Araf, (1,2), (1,3), (1,2,4)-α-Xylp, (1,2)-α-Glcp, (1,6)-β-Glc p, (1,3)-β-Galp, and (1,3,4)-β-Manp units, branched with (1,4)-β-Xylp and (1,4)-β-Manp units. LEHP attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory injury in RAW264.7 macrophages by reducing levels of inflammatory mediators including NO, TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6. LEHP inhibited JNK/MAPK and JAK1/STAT1 signaling pathway by modulating JNK phosphorylation and STAT1 expression. Animal experiments showed that LEHP markedly attenuated inflammation and histopathological damage in TNBS-induced zebrafish by reducing neutrophil numbers and promoting goblet cell proliferation in the neuromasts of caudal lateral line. Overall, LEHP has anti-inflammatory activity and may serve as a natural anti-inflammatory agent in the development of functional foods and dietary supplements.

title: Polyethylene glycol–based polymeric supramolecular solvent for solid–liquid microextraction of neonicotinoids from vegetables
abstract: This study established a new polymeric supramolecular solvent (Poly-SUPRAS) for the effective solid-liquid microextraction of neonicotinoids from vegetables, with subsequent determination by high-performance liquid chromatography with diode array detection. Biocompatible polyethylene glycols were used as low-toxicity coacervation agents to prepare the Poly-SUPRASs for the first time. The method achieved wide linear ranges with good determination coefficients (R 2 ≥ 0.9971). The detection and quantification limits were 0.01-0.06 and 0.05-0.20 μg g -1 , respectively. The method was then used to analyze neonicotinoids in seven vegetables. Extraction recoveries ranged from 87.4% to 103%. Density functional theory calculations showed that the extraction driver was noncovalent interactions between the Poly-SUPRAS and neonicotinoids. The method achieved an Analytical GREEnness preparation metric of 0.67 and a Blue Applicability Grade Index score of 77.5. Thus, the Poly-SUPRAS-based method was validated as a robust tool for the routine detection of neonicotinoid residue in vegetables.

title: Effects of different factors on antioxidant activity of tragacanth gum grafted glutamic acid
An efficient ester-type catechin-degrading tannase from a screened Aspergillus aculeatus: Heterologous expression, characterization, and application in tea beverages
abstract: Ester-type catechins cause bitterness and sedimentation in tea beverages, but tannases with high hydrolytic activity toward them remain scarce. Here, a tannase-producing strain, Aspergillus aculeatus LS06, was isolated from fermented sour tea. Its tannase gene was codon-optimized and expressed in Pichia pastoris KM71. The recombinant enzyme TanBT had a molecular weight of 63.4 kDa and optimal activity at 30 °C and pH 5.0. TanBT showed high hydrolytic activity toward four ester-type catechins, with the activity for (-)-epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) being 5.44-fold higher than that for methyl gallate. TanBT efficiently hydrolyzed the four major ester-type catechins in tea infusion, 1.44-fold more efficiently than a commercial tannase (CE). TanBT treatment also enhanced antioxidant capacity and overall sensory score. Molecular docking suggested stronger binding of TanBT to EGCG, (-)-epicatechin gallate, and (-)-gallocatechin gallate than CE. Therefore, TanBT shows promising prospects for improving the flavor and quality of tea beverages based on the present study.

title: Unraveling soymilk glycoproteome. New insights into O-glycosylation in plant glycoproteins
Dually oxidized starch: Effect of combining ozone with chemical agents on in vitro digestibility and morphostructural and thermorheological properties
authors: Aldira Oliveira de Carvalho e Silva Neta
abstract: ), sodium hypochlorite (SNa), hydrogen peroxide (SH2), and their combined applications (SNaO3 and SH2O3), on the structural, thermal, gelatinization, and functional properties of red rice starch. The treatments were performed under identical concentration and time conditions to evaluate the influence of different oxidizing systems on starch modification for potential food applications. Carbonyl and carboxyl groups reduced the hydrodynamic radius and degree of polymerization of amylopectin, indicating a shift toward shorter chain fractions. This increased rapidly digestible starch (RDS) and reduced resistant starch (RS), attributed to greater enzymatic accessibility. The combined treatments promoted an increase in gelatinization temperatures, indicating greater thermal stability. The gelatinization properties reflected molecular depolymerization and weakening of granular integrity, as evidenced by the reduction in peak, break, and final viscosities. The combination (SNaO3 and SH2O3) intensified the structural and functional degradation of starch.

title: Food applications of pulsed electric field combined with other non-thermal technologies: progress and perspectives
abstract: Pulsed electric field (PEF), a non-thermal technology, is applied in microbial inactivation and potato processing industry. It mainly disrupts microbial cell membranes via electroporation, yet its independent application suffers from uneven treatment and limited efficacy against spores and some enzymes. The combination of PEF with other non-thermal technologies can overcome these shortcomings, improve treatment uniformity, and enhance inactivation efficiency. This review introduces that combining PEF with high-pressure processing (HPP), ultrasound (US), cold plasma (CP), ultraviolet C (UV-C), pulsed light (PL), plasma-activated water (PAW), and ozone can enhance microbial inactivation, extraction efficiency, and certain food quality attributes. Their synergistic effects vary with processing parameters, treatment sequence, and food matrix characteristics. Key knowledge gaps in the combination mainly include insufficient understanding of synergistic mechanisms, inconsistent evaluation methods, complex food matrices, and limitation in industrial applications. This review provides a theoretical reference and guidance for the combination of non-thermal technologies in food applications.

title: Preparation of emulsion for encapsulating compound cinnamon essential oils and their application in plant-based meat analogs preservation
A widely targeted metabolomics comparison of processing methods for nutritional and flavor profiles of ‘Huozhouheiyu’ grape juice
abstract: A systematic comparison has been made among whole fruit juice (WP), cloudy juice (CJ), and clarified juice (CLJ) derived from the 'Huozhouheiyu' grapes, a distinctive variety from Turpan, Xinjiang. Physicochemical analysis indicates that total phenolics, anthocyanins, proanthocyanidins, and antioxidant activities in WP prepared by ultrafine grinding are significantly higher than those of CJ and CLJ. The relative headspace abundance of volatile compounds in CLJ was higher than that in WP, suggesting differences in volatile release and distribution among processing routes. Polyphenolic metabolomics has identified 1073 polyphenolic metabolites,with WP exhibiting a broader polyphenolic profile and higher relative abundances of numerous polyphenolic metabolites. In contrast, the levels of anthocyanins and flavanols in CJ and CLJ decrease significantly during the clarification process. Through this comprehensive comparative analysis, this study provides a theoretical foundation and scientific data for the high-value utilization and product development of grape resources.

title: Molecular-size-dependent cryoprotection of thaw exudate fractions in frozen pork batter: Effects on myofibrillar protein stability and gelation
abstract: Frozen storage impairs pork myofibrillar protein (MP) re-gelation by disrupting protein conformation, redox stability and protein-water interactions. This study evaluated whether thaw exudate fractions with different molecular sizes could protect freeze-damaged MP during subsequent heating. Two ultrafiltration fractions, UF1 (>10 kDa) and UF2 ( 2 ). DIA proteomics revealed changes in redox- and energy-metabolism-related proteins. Overall, UF1 mainly supported structural stabilization, whereas UF2 showed stronger hydration-related and antioxidant-associated responses with distinct metabolism-related proteomic changes.

title: Unraveling the synergistic inhibition mechanism of hyperin, isoquercitrin, and their aglycone quercetin on α-amylase: Insights from flavonoid-enzyme binding and flavonoid-starch interaction
abstract: This study explored the synergistic inhibitory effects of hyperin (H), isoquercitrin (I), and quercetin (Q) against α-amylase (α-AMY) and starch hydrolysis. The ternary combination (TC: H + I + Q), constructed based on mass ratio identified in previously characterized polyphenol extract, exhibited synergistic inhibitory activity. For flavonoid-enzyme interactions, Q exerted a prominent influence on α-AMY conformational alterations, as indicated by enzyme kinetics, and spectral measurements. Regarding starch interactions, H and I bound more strongly to starch than Q via hydrogen bonding, revealed by starch-iodine binding and FT-IR, SEM, and CLSM characterizations. Analysis of starch-degradation products (G1-G7) verified that TC markedly reduced the generation of malto-oligosaccharides. Molecular docking indicated that multi-site binding of H, I, and Q toward α-AMY together with plausible complementary interactions with starch chains collectively contribute to the superior inhibitory capacity of TC against α-AMY-mediated starch hydrolysis. These findings provide a framework for evaluating synergistic actions within complex natural-product systems.

title: Roasting-time dependent aroma development in sesame oil: time-resolved VOCs evolution revealed by deconvolution-assisted HS-SPME-GC–MS
abstract: Roasting is essential for developing sesame oil's color, aroma, and texture. This study investigated the effects of roasting time on key volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and sensory profiles. An optimized HS-SPME-GC-MS coupled with DEMCR-ALS-based deconvolution (AntDAS-GCMS) was established to profile VOC dynamics during roasting at 150 °C for 0-40 min. Among 731 resolved differential features, 94 VOCs changed significantly across 30 samples. Volatile composition changed markedly during the first 20 min, when the characteristic roasted aroma emerged. However, odor activity values (OAVs) of key aroma-active compounds continued to change with prolonged roasting, particularly those associated with caramel-sweet and smoky notes. Hydrocarbon-associated signals progressively decreased, whereas nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compounds increased. Sensory and OAV-based analyses showed a shift from fresh, seed-like profile toward a thermally derived flavor system. Roasting for 20-30 min enhanced desirable aromas, whereas longer roasting increased smoky notes and reduced aroma balance.

title: Valorization of agro-industrial beetroot peel waste (Beta vulgaris L.) as a natural colorant: chemical characterization and consumer-oriented sensory perception
authors: Patricia Daniele da Silva dos Santos
abstract: The increasing demand for clean-label foods has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives to synthetic colorants, highlighting agro-industrial residues such as beetroot peel ( Beta vulgaris L . ), as promising sources of natural pigments and bioactive compounds. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of oven drying (OBP) and freeze-drying (FBP) on physicochemical, phenolic, betalain, antioxidant, and technological properties of beetroot peel flour, addressing a gap in studies that rarely integrate processing effects with performance in real food systems. FBP preserved total phenolics (78.31 mg GAE g −1 ) and betalains (8.72 mg g −1 ), while OBP showed greater oxygen radical absorbance capacity (605.14 μM TE g −1 ), color intensity, and processing viability. OBP was incorporated into gummies, resulting in best color and sensory balance at 3%, while 5% showed highest sensory acceptance. These findings demonstrate processing conditions strongly influence functional performance and highlight beetroot peel as an effective clean-label colorant for food applications.

title: Proteome-metabolome remodeling reveals changes in nutritional and bioactive components of mastitis-affected sheep milk
Low-phosphate myofibrillar protein emulsions stabilized by fractionated fava bean protein fibrils: Interfacial synergy between amorphous and fibrous fractions
abstract: The amorphous fraction (AF, mainly containing peptides <6000 Da) and fibrous fraction (FF) of fibrillated fava bean protein (FFP) synergistically compensate for the decrease in stability of pork myofibrillar protein (MP) emulsions under reduced phosphate conditions. AF significantly increased the emulsifying activity index (EAI) by rapidly adsorbing to and covering the interface, while FF, containing 34.1% hydrophobic amino acids, slowly rearranged at the interface and enhanced the interfacial dilatational modulus. With FFP, the droplet size was reduced to 32.23 ± 0.92 μm and the creaming index decreased (P < 0.05). Under simulated processing (heating at 75 °C followed by storage at 4 °C), when phosphate was halved or removed, 1-2% FFP restored water-holding capacity to over 85% of that of the normal-phosphate control, increased oil-holding capacity by up to 21.8%, and reduced water-oil separation. These findings reveal an interfacial synergy mechanism, providing a plant-based strategy for clean-label emulsified meat products.

title: Coffee brew quality approved by photoionization mass spectrometry: Predicting sensory perception of coffee beverage during the roasting process in real-time
abstract: Real-time monitoring of coffee roasting is essential for consistent quality, but current methods are slow, labor-intensive and largely post-roast. We applied photoionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (PI-TOFMS) using complementary resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization (REMPI) and single-photon ionization (SPI) to continuously analyze roast gas during Arabica coffee roasting on an industrial scale. The roast degree for beans dropped at different roast stages were evaluated by Colorette, while brews were assessed by a human sensory panel and electronic tongue. Partial least squares regression models built from PI mass spectra predicted six sensory attributes with errors comparable to human panelists (RMSE P 10–17%) and six taste attributes from the electronic tongue (RMSE P 1.3–7.8%). Variable importance analysis identified key contributors, including furfuryl alcohol and furfurylthiol. Coupling PI-TOFMS with PLS enables prediction of coffee sensory attributes with one-second time resolution during roasting, offering a rapid, in situ tool for process control and quality optimization.

title: Integration of vibrational spectroscopies and synthetic samples in the chemometric prediction of Ciprofloxacin in lyophilized milk powder
Fruit pretreatment and extraction method govern macadamia protein functionality and ACE2 inhibitory peptides: A flag-ACE2 pull-down study
abstract: This study examined the combined effects of fruit pretreatment (fresh, air-dried, and roasted) and extraction method (alkaline versus salt) on the structure, physicochemical properties, and function of macadamia protein. Roasting increased protein recovery but decreased water-holding capacity. In contrast, salt extraction improved water-holding capacity and surface hydrophobicity despite lower recovery. Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed that emulsifying properties were primarily determined by the extraction method rather than by the pretreatment method. Simulated gastrointestinal digestion (SGID) significantly enhanced both DPPH radical-scavenging and ACE2 inhibitory activities. Following SGID, the roasted samples (both alkaline- and salt-extracted) exhibited stronger DPPH scavenging activity. Meanwhile, the roasted alkaline-extracted samples showed higher ACE2 inhibition (84.67%). A novel strategy was then established: Flag-ACE2 affinity pull-down coupled with peptidomics to identify ACE2-inhibitory peptides from the most active gastrointestinal digest. Using this method, a total of 37 novel ACE2-binding peptides were identified across three independent experiments. Among them, three peptides (AAYQVAALPK, GGGGFGGGGFGGGGIGGGGF and YYHKPSVF) with relatively low binding energies to ACE2 were selected for functional validation. The synthetic peptides inhibited ACE2 in a concentration-dependent manner, with respective IC₅₀ values of 40.21, 9.14, and 152.5 μM. The glycine-rich peptide GGGGFGGGGFGGGGIGGGGF exhibited the strongest inhibitory activity. These results illustrate the critical role of the method of fruit pretreatment and extraction in determining the techno-functional and bioactive properties of macadamia protein. Furthermore, the target protein affinity pull-down strategy effectively bypasses conventional fractionation workflows, enabling the direct identification of ACE2-inhibitory peptides in complex food digests. This offers a platform for screening bioactive peptides against other protein targets.

title: Corrigendum to “Matrix-dependent modulation of chemical composition, volatile profile, and biological activity of kombucha beverages from different tea types” [Food Chem. 514 (2026) 149160]
Hierarchical geographical origin discrimination and adulteration detection of white tea using UV–vis and NIR spectra
abstract: Fuding white tea, particularly premium silver needle, is a high-value Geographical Indication product increasingly vulnerable to cross-regional mislabeling, substitution, and blending. This study developed a dual-modal ultraviolet-visible diffuse reflectance and near-infrared spectroscopic strategy combined with chemometrics for hierarchical authentication. At the macro-geographical level, optimized UV-Vis and NIR PLS-DA models achieved accuracies of 100% and 97.54%, respectively, and correctly classified external Fujian and Yunnan samples. At the town scale within Fuding city, UV-Vis outperformed NIR in predictive ability (Q 2 = 0.70 vs. 0.37), indicating greater sensitivity to subtle local origin variation. Earlier-year Panxi samples were also correctly assigned, suggesting preliminary temporal transferability for town-scale authentication. Colorimetric analysis showed limited visual separability between authentic Fuding and non-Fuding silver needle samples, whereas spectroscopic models correctly identified all blended samples. Variable importance in projection analysis revealed complementary contributions from UV-Vis chromophore-related features and NIR matrix-related information, while low-level UV-Vis-NIR fusion further improved blending detection.

title: Beeswax-constructed O1/W/O2 double emulsion gels: Stabilization mechanism, 3D printability, and co-delivery of nutrients
abstract: O 1 /W/O 2 double emulsion gels (DEGs) are promising food matrices, and tailoring their properties is essential for practical application. Here, DEGs were fabricated from CNC/β-LG-stabilized inner emulsions and PGPR-containing outer oil phases structured with beeswax. Beeswax concentration was found as a key regulator linking stabilization mechanism, microstructure, rheological/textural behavior, printability, and nutrient delivery. Increasing beeswax concentration strengthened the outer crystalline network, decreased droplet size, and enhanced oil holding capacity and structural retention. All DEGs exhibited shear-thinning behavior, whereas viscosity, modulus, and hardness varied with beeswax content, demonstrating that their overall performance could be customized through simple compositional adjustment. Notably, beeswax concentration had little effect on the encapsulation efficiencies of Cur and EGCG, whereas increasing beeswax content enhanced their UV and thermal stability and modulated gastrointestinal release behaviors. These findings provide an effective design strategy for printable and customizable gel systems capable of multifunctional nutrient delivery.

title: Flavor differences and key odorant identification in boiled breast meat of three duck breeds: Muscovy, Cherry Valley, and Sheldrake
Highly stretchable sodium alginate/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel films incorporating cinnamaldehyde/tannic acid/zinc acetate nanoparticles for strawberry preservation and humidity regulation
Foodomics of garlic organosulphur compounds: Analytical challenges and implications for product-specific quality assessment
abstract: Garlic organosulphur compounds contribute to product composition and sensory properties, but their interpretation depends on the garlic matrix and the quality attribute being assessed. Allicin is informative for tissue-disruption-dependent thiosulfinate formation and selected product specifications; its reactivity also makes measured concentrations sensitive to sample preparation, processing and storage. This review examines how enzymatic reactions following tissue disruption and subsequent chemical transformations affect the interpretation of allicin and related compounds. Evidence from targeted analysis, metabolomics, volatilomics and chemometrics is evaluated in relation to the questions each approach can answer. Existing studies establish compositional differences and, in some cases, discrimination of garlic samples or associations with measured attributes. These findings do not alone establish reaction pathways or transferable predictors of product quality. A product- and endpoint-specific framework is proposed for evaluating candidate sulphur markers against independently measured outcomes and simpler alternatives. Progress towards practical quality assessment will require reliable compound identification and quantification, independent biological or production samples, and external validation for each intended use.

title: Grape stalk valorisation: Effects of grape stalk extract on the chemical and sensory properties of Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, and Chenin Blanc wines after bottle ageing
abstract: Grape stalks are a phenolic-rich winemaking by-product with potential antioxidant applications. This study evaluated the effects of grape stalk crude extract (CE), at 0.2 and 0.4 g/L, on the chemical, mineral, and sensory properties of Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, and Chenin Blanc wines under SO 2 -treated and SO 2 -free conditions after 14 months of bottle ageing. CE addition significantly increased total phenolic content (TPC) and ABTS antioxidant capacity across all varieties. Although tannin concentrations declined during ageing, increases in TPC and antioxidant activity were maintained, suggesting structural rearrangement or depolymerisation of condensed tannins into lower-molecular-weight phenolics with enhanced reducing capacity. Mineral responses were variety-dependent and reflected matrix-specific redistribution. Sensory outcomes were strongly modulated by SO 2 regime: in the absence of SO 2 , higher CE intensified bitterness, astringency, and browning, whereas SO 2 presence preserved balance and varietal typicality. Therefore, grape stalk extract is a promising phenolic and antioxidant enrichment ingredient for white wines, although its application should complement appropriate SO 2 management rather than serve as a direct substitute.

title: Bioinspired fluorinated zwitterionic peptide-based electrochemical biosensors for highly sensitive and antifouling detection of chloramphenicol in food samples
abstract: Accurately detecting chloramphenicol (CAP) residues in animal-derived foods remains challenging primarily due to severe electrode biofouling. Inspired by shark skin's antifouling properties, a biomimetic antifouling peptide (FUZP) was designed by covalently grafting a perfluorocarboxylic acid moiety onto a U-shaped zwitterionic peptide scaffold, combining hydration layers with low surface energy to reduce nonspecific adsorption synergistically. By leveraging FUZP, an antifouling electrochemical biosensor was fabricated on a conductive poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)/gold nanoparticles (PEDOT/AuNPs) platform for aptamer immobilization. This biosensor demonstrated a broad linear detection range for CAP spanning from 10 -15 to 10 -11 M, with an ultralow limit of detection (LOD) of 0.343 fM in PBS. Notably, it enabled ultrasensitive detection of CAP in milk and honey matrices without the need for extensive sample pretreatment. It also exhibited high selectivity, stability, and strong resistance to matrix interference. This work offers a robust and generalizable antifouling strategy for reliable electrochemical biosensing in complex food samples.

title: Tyrosinase-catalyzed phenolic acid modified fish collagen film enhanced physicochemical and functional properties for sea bass (Lateolabrax maculatus) packaging
abstract: To alleviate the pollution and harm caused by non-biodegradable packaging materials, a tyrosinase-catalyzed oxidation of phenolic acid-modified fish protein-based film was developed. The modification effects of different phenolic acids were evaluated. The structure, morphology, mechanical, optical, water sensitivity, barrier, thermal stability, antimicrobial and antioxidant properties, and preservation effects on sea bass were characterized. The results showed that gallic acid (GA) modified fish collagen exhibited the most stable antimicrobial and antioxidant properties at low concentrations. FT-IR and SEM results indicated good compatibility between the components of the films. Furthermore, GA also endowed the film with enhanced various properties, including mechanical performance, barrier properties, and bioactivity. Finally, compared with commercial PE films, the modified film prolonged the shelf life of sea bass by at least 6 days. Therefore, the GA-COL/PVA film has been proven to be a preservation material with enhanced properties and holds great potential for application in the preservation of aquatic products.

title: High internal phase Pickering emulsions stabilized by pH-shifting modified egg white/pea protein isolate: Oral tribological evidence for fat replacement in whipped cream
abstract: This study aimed to address the high saturated fatty acid content of conventional whipping cream and the challenge of balancing structural properties and whipping performance during fat replacement. An 8% (w/w) composite of egg white protein (EWP) and pea protein isolate (PPI) modified by pH-shifting was used to stabilize high internal phase Pickering emulsions (HIPPEs), which replaced 30% of the coconut oil in whipped cream. Increasing the PPI proportion reduced droplet size and viscosity while improving oral lubricity, whereas higher EWP content enhanced network rigidity, freeze-thaw stability and centrifugal stability. Notably, the EWP/PPI ratio of 1:3 showed favorable whipping performance, with a shorter whipping time of 161 s, a high overrun of 57.05%, and a more uniform oil-air structure. Overall, this study provides a theoretical basis for designing protein-stabilized HIPPEs as structured fat replacers in low-fat whipped products.

title: Identification and characterization of umami-enhancing peptides from soybean fermented by Aspergillus cristatus CB10002 using sensory-guided and computational approaches
Effects of lychee puree with pasteurization or induced electric field pretreatment on fermentation characteristics and dynamics of purines, folate vitamers, and amino acids in craft beer
A hierarchical contrastive learning-based framework for enzyme function prediction and its application value in Avena sativa protein research

Comprehensive characterization of processing-induced changes in finger millet (Eleusine coracana): Integrating physicochemical, structural, metabolomic, multivariate, in vitro, and in silico approaches to assess its potential antidiabetic functionality
Potential covalent masking of an immunoreactive Jug r 2-derived epitope (DFLAGQNNIINQLER) by EGCG: A molecular mechanism contributing to reduced walnut protein antigenicity under alkaline conditions
abstract: This study evaluated the efficacy and molecular mechanisms of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) in attenuating the allergenicity of walnut protein (WP) under alkaline conditions. Covalent conjugation triggered the formation of high-molecular-weight aggregates and a significant reduction in free amino and sulfhydryl groups. Structural characterization indicated that EGCG-induced unfolding of the WP structure, specifically the conversion of α-helices to β-sheets, was directly linked to diminished IgG-binding capacity. In vivo assays demonstrated that WP-EGCG conjugates effectively alleviated systemic anaphylaxis and restored Th1/Th2 balance by modulating cytokine profiles (IL-4, IL-13, and IFN-γ). Proteomic analysis showed that EGCG affected multiple walnut allergens. The Jug r 2-derived peptide DFLAGQNNIINQLER was strongly associated with IgG-binding capacity (R 2 = 0.7872, P < 0.0001), supporting its relevance as one EGCG-responsive epitope. These findings provide mechanistic evidence for reducing walnut protein antigenicity, although validation in whole-walnut and food-processing systems is required.

title: Mechanistic insights into the cascade from dynamic hierarchical structure changes to digestion kinetics and in vitro satiety-related hormone secretion in proteins
abstract: This study investigated structural variations and digestive kinetics of potato (PP), yeast (YP), and whey protein (WP) during gastrointestinal digestion, along with their effects on satiety-related hormone secretion. Results indicated that PP and YP showed lower digestibility, forming gastric aggregates in the gastric phase and retaining >10 kDa peptides after the intestinal phase. All protein digests revealed that aromatic and hydrophobic amino acids were predominant in the gastric phase, whereas basic and branched-chain amino acids in the intestinal phase. Structural analysis suggested that higher molecular weight, surface hydrophobicity, and β-sheet content of PP and YP were associated with lower gastric digestibility. High α-helix content of WP was associated with higher conformational flexibility and intestinal digestibility. Notably, a lower gastric digestibility correlated with cholecystokinin secretion, whereas a higher digestibility correlated with glucagon-like peptide-1 release. Overall, these findings provide preliminary in vitro insights for designing protein-based foods to influence satiety-related hormone secretion.

title: Anti-radiation activities of crayfish shell peptides and the radioprotective effects of their derived film material
abstract: Ionizing radiation threatens human health and food systems, and anti-radiation bioactives are attracting attention. Herein, crayfish shell peptides (CSPs) were prepared via enzymatic hydrolysis, analyzed for amino acids, and screened for bioactive segments. When an in vitro 60 Co γ-ray irradiation experiment was performed using Escherichia coli as the model organism, CSPs scavenged hydroxyl radicals (·OH) and suppressed irradiation-induced oxidative stress damage. For two CSP-derived peptides, FLPVY and PEFPHPIPDF, molecular docking predicted their possible binding to the Keap1 Kelch domain, whereas quantum chemical calculations analyzed their electron-rich reaction-prone sites that may participate in ·OH neutralization. A chitosan/sodium alginate/CSP composite film was developed and characterized for structure and barrier properties. Using film-covered strawberry and white mushroom slices, irradiation (0-3 kGy)-induced changes in appearance, color, and NO, H 2 S, and H 2 O 2 were evaluated. The composite film significantly mitigated irradiation stress, alleviating aging and browning. CSPs are a biomass-based radioprotective material, and their derived films mitigate irradiation-induced oxidative damage in foods.

title: Thermal aging of microplastics during food processing: microplastic release and food safety implications
Saltiness-enhancing peptides derived from goat liver via transglutaminase-catalyzed glycosylation: a comparative study of chitosan oligosaccharides and glucosamine as saccharide donors
abstract: Long-term high-salt diets increase the risk of cardiovascular diseases. Transglutaminase-catalyzed glycosylation enables peptide glycosylation under mild conditions and enhances the saltiness-enhancing effect. In this study, goat liver protein was hydrolyzed using Flavourzyme, and the optimal hydrolysis time was determined. Transglutaminase-catalyzed glycosylation reactions of goat liver peptides were conducted using glucosamine and chitosan oligosaccharide as sugar donors, followed by sensory evaluation and mechanistic investigation. The optimal conditions were enzyme concentration of 1.0% and reaction time of 3 h. The saltiness-enhancing rate of COS-derived glycopeptides (63.33%) was higher than that of GlcN-derived ones (55.47%). UV and fluorescence spectroscopy confirmed a low extent of glycosylation. LC-MS/MS identified glycopeptide sequences with glycosylation at Gln residue. Molecular docking revealed that glycopeptides bound to salt receptors ENaC, TRPV1, and TMC4, with TRPV1 showing the highest affinity, followed by ENaC, and TMC4. Overall, this study provides a theoretical basis for development of salt-enhancing peptides from goat liver.

title: Effects of ultrasonic treatment and incorporation of carboxymethyl chitosan-gallic acid conjugate on pea protein isolates on the rheological properties, stability and 3D printing performance of high internal phase emulsion
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI)-stabilized high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) are promising clean-label systems for food 3D printing, but limited self-supporting ability and stability restrict their application. This study examined the effects of ultrasound pretreatment and carboxymethyl chitosan-gallic acid conjugate (CG) incorporation on interfacial, rheological, stability, and printing properties of PPI-based HIPEs. Moderate ultrasound treatment and appropriate CG addition improved the complexes' amphiphilic wettability and interfacial activity. HU60%-PPI-CG4:1 showed a contact angle near 90° and reduced interfacial tension to approximately 7 mN/m, promoting oil-water interfacial adsorption. The resulting HIPEs exhibited a denser gel network, shear-thinning behavior, solid-like viscoelasticity, and good thixotropic recovery. After 7-day accelerated storage, the peroxide and MDA values of HU60%-PPI-CG4:1-stabilized HIPEs decreased to 12.37 μmol/g oil and 117.64 nmol/g oil, respectively. Moreover, HU60%-PPI-CG4:1-stabilized HIPEs showed smooth extrusion, strong self-supporting ability, and high shape fidelity, providing a basis for expanding PPI-based HIPEs in 3D printing and functional food development.

title: Evaluation of full-bodied mouthfeel in Jiangxiangxing baijiu based on multimodal profiling and machine learning
Metabolic mechanisms underlying the enhanced sensory quality of Sangzhi white tea under red and far-red light during withering
abstract: White tea withering depends heavily on weather conditions, making LED-assisted light regulation a promising for processing stability. However, the effects of red light and far-red light on white tea quality formation remain unclear. In this study, Camellia sinensis cv. Bixiangzao was subjected to natural withering (CK), RL, FRL, and RL + FRL treatments. Sensory evaluation, quality component analysis, and untargeted metabolomics were performed to investigate light-induced metabolic changes. RL + FRL achieved the highest overall sensory quality, whereas FRL significantly increased free amino acids and theanine. Untargeted metabolomics revealed distinct alterations in both non-volatile and volatile metabolite profiles under different light treatments. FRL and RL + FRL treatments showed partially overlapping metabolic patterns. KEGG enrichment and metabolomics-based pathway analyses highlighted changes in amino acid, flavonoid, phenylpropanoid, and terpenoid-related metabolism. These findings provide a theoretical basis for optimizing LED-assisted withering under variable weather.

title: Analysis of the effect of dynamic fermentation treatment on the quality of congou black tea using nontargeted metabolomics
abstract: Fermentation critically shapes black tea flavor. Although dynamic fermentation offers potential for quality improvement, its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we combined nontargeted metabolomics, electronic tongue analysis, and chemometrics to investigate the effects of dynamic and traditional static pile fermentation on the sensory profile and nonvolatile metabolites of Ninghong Congou black tea. Dynamic fermentation increased tea infusion lightness (L*) and yellowness (b*) by 2.65% and 1.88%, respectively, while significantly reducing bitterness and astringency. These sensory changes were associated with decreased bitter compounds including polyphenols, caffeine, and ester catechins and increased levels of key quality components, including theaflavins and thearubigins. Nontargeted metabolomics revealed 63 differential metabolites, primarily flavonoids, catechins, and phenolic acids. Dynamic fermentation accelerated the oxidative degradation of these compounds, which may contribute to improved flavor quality. This study provides a theoretical and technical basis for optimizing fermentation to produce high-quality black tea.

title: Synergistic effects of chlorogenic acid and konjac glucomannan on physicochemical properties and metabolic health benefits
Bacteria-derived particle-stabilized Pickering emulsions reinforce chitosan active films for salmon headspace preservation
Mono- and disaccharides in insects: potential dietary relevance
abstract: This study aimed to quantify selected mono- and disaccharides in 19 insect samples using HPAEC-PAD. The sum of quantified mono- and disaccharides ranged from 49 to 1675 mg/100 g of lyophilised insect matter. Trehalose predominated in most species, reaching 495 mg/100 g in Hermetia illucens larvae (approximately 100 mg per 20 g serving). Glucose showed interspecies variability, with the highest concentration in Locusta migratoria subadults (1328 mg/100 g in powder). Lactose was generally absent or present at trace levels (<5 mg/100 g), except in Musca domestica larvae. Insect species, developmental stage, and sex significantly affected saccharide profiles ( p < 0.001). Most species had low lactose and sucrose contents, indicating potentially low dietary exposure. The levels of trehalose were variable and highlight the need for further investigation. The data provide a baseline for nutritional assessment and for future physiological or clinical studies investigating the tolerance of specific insect-derived foods.

title: Targeted flavor stabilization of tea beverages via hydrolat addition: Dynamic chemical profiling and correlation analysis
Miniaturized UAE–SPE-d-SPE–HPLC–UV method for trace determination of triazine herbicides in corn tortillas
abstract: An analytical methodology was developed for simultaneous extraction and determination of triazine herbicides atrazine and simazine in maize tortillas. This method combined ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) using a methanol:water mixture followed by simple and rapid miniaturized solid-phase extraction-dispersive solid-phase extraction (SPE-d-SPE) concentration and a clean-up step using C18/PS-DVB sorbents. Only 100 μL of the extract was obtained through effective matrix simplification. This allowed determination of herbicides using HPLC–UV with good linearity (R 2 > 0.99) (range of 50–250 ng g −1 ) and limits of detection and quantification in the ranges of 20–50 and 20–60 ng g −1 for atrazine and simazine, respectively, enabling monitoring at the maximum residue limit (MRL) established for maize (250 ng g −1 ). Precision was less than 7.5%, and recoveries were 71% for simazine and 76% for atrazine. The proposed method proved robust across tortillas prepared from maize of different varieties and origins in Mexico. This approach provides a reliable and miniaturized tool for trace-level determination of triazine herbicides, supporting food safety monitoring of maize-based products.

title: Tuning rheological behavior and 3D printability of a thermoreversible agar-corn starch-microfibrillated cellulose emulsion gel
Flavor characteristics and key compounds of jasmine tea prepared by one-step yellowing-scenting strategy: insights from sensory evaluation, metabolomic analysis and molecular docking
abstract: Jasmine tea is highly sought after by consumers but its traditional production is time-consuming and costly. To address these issues, this study developed a one-step yellowing-scenting (NS) strategy by directly incorporating jasmine flowers into yellow tea during the yellowing stage. Sensory evaluation and metabolomic analysis showed that NS improved aroma quality via enriching characteristic aroma compounds (e.g., benzyl alcohol, linalool, methyl salicylate, 3-hexen-1-ol benzoate) and optimized taste by increasing mellow taste-related non-volatile components, including theobromine, myricetin 3-O-beta-D-galactopyranoside, and 3,4-dihydroxybenzaldehyde. Dynamic analysis confirmed the yellowing-scenting stage as critical for flavor development. Compared with the latest single-cycle temperature-controlled scenting (TS), NS yielded significantly higher levels of these characteristic components, showing superior accumulation efficiency. Furthermore, molecular docking indicated that tea non-volatiles bind to aroma molecules, potentially explaining enhanced aroma retention in NS teas. Collectively, these findings clarify the flavor formation mechanism of NS jasmine tea and provide theoretical and technical support for scented tea quality upgrading.

title: Label-free dual-target electrochemiluminescence aptasensor based on interdigitated electrodes for rapid on-site detection of mycotoxins in grain
Systematic sampling and machine learning reveal the mechanisms of climatic cascades driving high-temperature Daqu ripening dynamics and liquor quality
Molecular competition between chain degradation and ordered rearrangement governs the digestibility of extruded highland barley starch-β-glucan complexes
abstract: The regulation mechanism of extrusion on the multiscale structure of starch-non-starch polysaccharide systems was still unclear, especially how moisture balanced molecular degradation and recrystallization remained to be elucidated. In this study, the effects of extrusion water on the multiscale structure and digestibility of highland barley starch-β-glucan complexes were investigated. The results showed that water dominated the competition between degradation and ordered reconstitution of starch chains by regulating the degree of plasticization. At 55% moisture content, the starch chains were broken significantly, which promoted amylose rearrangement and enrichment of single-helices, and the content of resistant starch reached the highest value (23.25%). β-glucan and water exhibited cooperative regulation: at the molecular level, hydrogen bonds inhibited excessive chain breakage and induced single helix enrichment, while at the macroscopic level, they enhanced compactness of gel network to form physical barrier. This controlled degradation offers a green strategy to produce slow-digestion foods from highland barley.

title: Chemometric-assisted quantitative SERS detection of okadaic acid using paper-based MoS2 nanoflower–Au nanoparticle substrate
Chemistry-informed AI for food toxicant and adulterant detection: matrix-aware validation and auditable decision support
abstract: Food toxicants and adulterants pose interconnected safety, authenticity, and regulatory challenges across complex food matrices. This review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) converts spectra, images, chromatographic-mass-spectral fingerprints, biosensor outputs, and portable-device signals into screening decisions. Toxicant detection is treated primarily as a threshold-based task, whereas adulteration is addressed as an authenticity or anomaly-detection problem. Evidence is evaluated using AI performance and classical analytical criteria, including selectivity, recovery, precision, robustness, limits of detection and quantification, measurement uncertainty, matrix effects, independent validation, and agreement with reference methods. The review distinguishes direct analyte evidence from correlated proxy signals and separates experimentally demonstrated methods from author-proposed chemistry-informed concepts. A matrix-aware framework links field screening with confirmatory laboratory analysis through calibration transfer, drift monitoring, uncertainty-based decisions, and traceable model records. Emerging tools, including conformal prediction, generative augmentation, digital twins, and secure ledgers, remain promising but are not yet fully validated for regulatory use in foods.

title: Interaction mechanism between loach protein and chlorogenic acid and emulsion properties of their complex: a study based on multispectral technology and molecular simulation
abstract: This study investigated the binding features, conformational changes, and emulsifying properties of loach protein (LP) with chlorogenic acid (CGA) using multispectral techniques, molecular simulation, and in vitro assays, aiming to clarify aquatic animal protein-polyphenol interactions and promote high-value utilization of LP. LP and CGA spontaneously formed stable non-covalent complexes, with hydrophobic interactions as the main driving force (ΔH = 14.55 kJ/mol, ΔS = 137.40 J/(mol·K), ΔG = -25.51 to -29.89 kJ/mol). CGA induced LP conformational rearrangement, optimized surface charge distribution, and improved dispersibility. The emulsifying and foaming properties of LP were enhanced by CGA in a dose-dependent manner. Specifically, the LP-CGA complex (1:0.1) increased EAI to 268.30 ± 4.73 m 2 /g and FC to 72.67 ± 3.06% (98.2% increase). ESI peaked at 48.00 ± 2.65 min (1:0.05). After 14 days of storage, the 1:0.1 group maintained a CI of 91.00 ± 3.61%, significantly higher than that of LP (64.67 ± 1.53%). Rheological parameters (n,K) were governed by mechanisms distinct from those of emulsifying properties, reflecting the mechanical strength of the protein network rather than interfacial adsorption behavior. This study elucidates the LP-CGA interaction mechanism, providing theoretical support for LP-based functional food development and stable emulsion system construction.

title: A Pt@Z8P-based electrochemiluminescence aptasensor with T7 exonuclease-assisted amplification for ultrasensitive deoxynivalenol determination in cereals
Aeration rate regulates organic acid metabolism during cereal vinegar solid-state fermentation: Insights from quantitative metagenomics and targeted metabolomics
Bacterial cellulose – chia seed mucilage dry formulation: A fully natural stabilizer and texturizing agent for food and cosmetics
abstract: A new, clean-label, and functional additive was developed using mucilage extracted from chia seeds (ChM) as co-drying agent for bacterial cellulose (BC). Dried and rehydrated mixtures of BC:ChM (ratios of 1:0.5 and 1:1) retained their original properties, as validated by visual and microscopic observation, and rheological analysis. Rheological studies revealed a shear thinning behaviour, predominantly elastic, with BC:ChM 1:1 reaching a yield stress of 1.63 Pa, compared to 1.08 Pa for the 1:0.5 ratio (at 0.5% w /w). The rheological properties of 0.5% BC:ChM (1:1) remained stable across a wide range of ionic strength (5–150 mM), pH (2.7–7.7) and temperature (6–80 °C). Finally, the BC:ChM dry formulation effectively stabilized isohexadecane-in-water emulsions (characterized by optical microscopy, laser diffraction and rheology) preventing both creaming and oil separation at a concentration of 0.4%. These results suggest promising applications of BC:ChM as a natural additive in various industries, including food and cosmetics.

Multi-platform fingerprinting analysis of UV-C-assisted maturation in light-flavor Baijiu by E-nose, UV–Vis/EEM fluorescence and HS-GC-IMS
Characterization of tocopherols, Δ7-sterols, and triterpenoids in shea kernels from a field preservation trial in Burkina Faso
abstract: West African shea kernels from Vitellaria paradoxa (family Sapotaceae) contain isoprenoid-derived lipophilic metabolites, including triterpene alcohols and esters, Δ 7 -sterols, and tocopherols, all of which are associated with beneficial properties. This study investigated the effects of traditional preservation methods, such as parboiling, boiling, smoking, fermenting, sun-drying, and storage, on the contents of lipophilic shea metabolites and free fatty acids in 21 shea samples. Unsaponified triterpene esters and the corresponding alcohols released after saponification were quantified by GC–MS, using either native standards or ion-intensity-corrected analogue standards. Lipid deterioration through hydrolysis to free fatty acids decreased linearly with increasing sun-drying time and was lower in boiled than in parboiled kernels. Triterpene acetates and cinnamates accounted for more than 99% of Σ triterpenoids, while the free alcohols represented only 0.3–0.6%. The high triterpenoid content (3.6 ± 0.4 g/100 g kernels) and consistent distribution of triterpene esters across treatments highlight their relevance for functional applications.

title: Ultrasonic degradation of sulfonamide antibiotics in cow milk: efficiency, kinetics, and mechanisms
abstract: Sulfonamide residues in milk pose food safety risks and are difficult to remove without affecting milk quality. This study evaluated ultrasound (US) as a nonthermal method to degrade six sulfonamides-sulfadiazine (SDA), sulfathiazole (STZ), sulfamerazine (SMR), sulfamethazine (SMN), sulfachloropyridazine (SCP), and sulfamethizole (SML)-in cow milk. Sonication promoted continuous degradation following pseudo-first-order kinetics, with removal efficiencies up to 93.7%. The degradation rate inversely correlated with hydrophobicity (log K ow ), and the calculated activation energies indicated cavitation-controlled, diffusion-driven processes. Mechanistically, ultrasound first desorbed antibiotics bound to casein micelles and fat globules, then oxidized them mainly via hydroxyl radicals, while aqueous electrons played a minor role, facilitating dechlorination of SCP. Response surface modeling revealed temperature and frequency as dominant factors. Nutritional analysis confirmed negligible changes in macronutrient contents and only a slight riboflavin loss (4.2%). Overall, ultrasound effectively degraded sulfonamides in milk, offering an efficient and safe approach for antibiotic mitigation in dairy processing.

Release mechanism of potent angiotensin-I converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptides from soybean protein: A peptidomics insight into protease specificity and site accessibility
Structural modification and reduced in vitro immunoreactivity of shrimp tropomyosin by dual-enzyme cross-linking systems

In vitro digestion and colonic fermentation characteristics of free and bound phenolics from Radix Puerariae Thomsonii and their effects on gut microbiota
Covalent polyphenol modification of collagen from jellyfish wastes toward high-value utilization as multiple performance-improved packaging film
Enzyme-catalyzed oxidative crosslinking for the fabrication of zein–chitosan conjugate film in multifunctional food preservation
High-throughput quantification of multiple human milk oligosaccharides by ion mobility-mass spectrometry: From standard addition to single-point calibration
abstract: Quantifying human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) in breast milk is challenging due to structural isomerism, matrix effects, and the lack of a true blank milk. Here, a multiplexed standard-addition strategy was proposed to quantify simultaneously nine HMOs in breast milk using ion mobility-mass spectrometry with single ion mobility monitoring (SIM²)-stitching acquisition on a TIMS-Tof instrument. Although, both ordinary (OLS) and weighted (WLS) least squares regressions yielded comparable results in terms of precision and accuracy, the WLS method accounted for heteroscedastic response variance and reduced dependence on the calibration range for endogenous concentration estimates. This method enabled the HMO determination in breast milk samples ranging from 0.06 to 0.92 g L⁻¹. As a simplified alternative to multi-point calibration, the performance of a single-point standard addition strategy was evaluated. This provided HMO levels very similar to those determined by multipoint standard addition, demonstrating the potential of this simple quantification strategy for high-throughput applications.

title: Strain-specific complementarity in a minimal synthetic community reshapes the phenolic and aroma profiles of white wines during malolactic fermentation

Effects of 4,5-dicaffeoylquinic acid on the physicochemical properties of ultrasound-glutaminase treated myofibrillar protein of tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) and its potential application prospects in curcumin encapsulation
Origin and mitigation of catechins-induced discoloration during pea protein isolation while inhibiting off-flavor formation
abstract: This study elucidates the mechanisms of catechin-induced discoloration during pea protein isolation via alkaline solubilization–isoelectric precipitation, where catechins are applied to inhibit off-flavor formation. Catechins were also combined with various mitigation strategies, including reduced protein solubilization pH, sodium bisulfite (SB), gallic acid (GA), Duralox®, and their effects were evaluated using untargeted metabolomics, lipid-oxidation markers (HODE, MDA) and volatile compounds. Untargeted metabolomics identified extractable catechin-derived oxidized dimers ( m / z 570–610) as compounds strongly associated with brown color development. Lowering solubilization pH reduced pigment formation but diminished catechins retention and increased free-radical signals. Catechins–SB combinations most effectively suppressed discoloration, lipid oxidation and formation of volatile off-flavors which was consistent with improved sensory attributes. GA offered additional protection but caused concentration-dependent darkening, whereas Duralox® showed limited efficacy. Overall, targeted antioxidant systems, particularly catechins–SB combinations, offer an effective strategy to control oxidation and improve sensory quality in pea protein.

title: Effects of ultrasound-assisted Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentation on Dunaliella salina flavor: Insights from GC × GC–MS and metabolomics
Effects of lactic acid bacteria fermentation on bioactive constituents and volatile profiles in Siraitia grosvenorii: a combined HS-SPME-GC–MS and HS-GC-IMS approach
Covalent organic framework quantum dots with structurally adaptive dual-functional surfaces for ultra-fast d-μSPE of five bisphenols in milk products
Integrated multi-omics analysis of sulfadiazine-induced oxidative stress and its impact on catechin biosynthesis and tea quality in Camellia sinensis
AIE-enhanced glutathione-stabilized CuNCs/SA hydrogel for dual-mode fluorescence-colorimetric Immunosensing of aflatoxin B1 in foods
Matrix design and pre-processing drive carotenoid and chlorophyll bioaccessibility in broccoli baked snacks
abstract: Understanding how pre-processing and matrix assembly influence the stability and release of plant-derived compounds is important for food design. Potato-based baked snacks containing 25% broccoli were formulated using fresh, frozen, freeze-dried, or air-dried broccoli to determine how pre-processing and matrix incorporation affect carotenoid and chlorophyll-related compound retention, digestive stability, and in vitro bioaccessibility. Snacks were evaluated using simulated gastrointestinal digestion followed by anaerobic fecal fermentation. Pre-processing and formulation affected compound recovery in a compound-specific and digestion-phase-dependent manner. Air-dried broccoli had the highest β-carotene and lutein contents at the ingredient level, whereas freeze-dried broccoli snacks showed the highest small-intestinal bioaccessibility for β-carotene and pheophytin a. Fresh broccoli snacks showed the highest 48 h fermented bioaccessibility for selected compounds, including lutein and pheophytin a. These findings indicate that broccoli pre-processing and snack formulation jointly influence in vitro compound persistence and bioaccessible recovery.

title: A volatile aldehyde-based rancidity score index for robust hazelnut quality monitoring
abstract: Reliable monitoring of hazelnut ( Corylus avellana L. ) oxidation is a critical challenge. Traditional indices have limited specificity and dynamic range, while single markers approaches lack robustness. This study introduces the Rancidity Score Index (RSI), a data-driven metric based on the combined quantification of four aldehydes (hexanal, heptanal, octanal, and nonanal) using Headspace Solid-Phase Microextraction Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC–MS). The RSI (0–100 scale value) was developed and validated on 416 industrial samples collected over four crop years (2020−2023) from Turkey and Italy, encompassing multiple cultivars and storage conditions monitored for 24 months. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) showed that the four aldehydes co-varied along a dominant axis explaining ~80% of total variance, while K-means clustering enabled the translation of the continuous RSI into a three-cluster framework. Preliminary agreement between MS- and FID-derived RSI values ( r = 0.974, n = 30) supports potential transferability to portable GC platforms for industrial rapid monitoring, pending validation.

L-proline-trehalose natural deep eutectic solvent as a functional cryoprotectant for quick-frozen pork patties: improving oral processing and digestibility
Formation of a chestnut-like aroma by blending fresh-scented and bean-scented green teas
Discovery of α-glucosidase inhibitory peptides from hemp seed protein via integrated peptidomics and molecular dynamics simulation
